One major limitation in our knowledge of sonoporation biophysics is that the membrane is often assumed to be a homogeneous lipid bilayer. Consequently, important mechanisms like lipid order dynamics during sonoporation have not been studied. Here, using giant unilamellar vesicles (GUV) as an organelle-free cell model, we investigate how the membrane lipids would switch between ordered (LO) and disordered (LD) phases during sonoporation. We found that LD fluorescence increased at the pore region after US. Outside the pore region, LD fluorescence remained relatively stable. Across multiple GUVs, generalized polarization analysis showed a transient decrease in membrane order (33.9±2.9% decrease in GP; N = 8) at pore regions after US, followed by recovery after 60 s. In contrast, the GP away from the sonoporation site had no significant change. These results indicate reduced lipid packing and increased membrane fluidity at the sonoporation site, highlighting the role of membrane lipid organization in sonoporation and its resealing.

papers.title: Nanobubble-Mediated BBB Opening Using a Clinical Imaging Array
papers.abstract: Focused ultrasound-mediated blood-brain barrier opening (BBBO) typically relies on dedicated therapeutic transducers, while clinical imaging arrays may offer a more scalable platform by combining therapy, image guidance, electronic steering, and cavitation monitoring. This study establishes nanobubble (NB)-mediated BBBO using a standard imaging array. NB acoustic emissions were first characterized in vitro with a 1.5 MHz P4-1 phased-array transducer using passive cavitation detection across peak negative pressure and pulse length. Harmonic cavitation increased with pressure and pulse duration, whereas broadband cavitation remained low across most conditions and rose mainly under selected high-pressure conditions, identifying an operating range favoring stable cavitation. A selected condition of 1100 kPa PNP and 10 cycles was then tested in vivo, where tracer extravasation and fluorescence microscopy confirmed localized BBBO. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of NB-mediated BBBO using a standard imaging transducer and provide a cavitation-guided framework for future optimization.

sessions.title: MEL: Skeletal Muscle and Brain Tissue Characterization

papers.title: Three-Dimensional Ultrasound Shear Strain Imaging for Chronic Lower Back Pain Classification
papers.abstract: The diagnosis of chronic myofascial pain (MP) or lower back pain (LBP) is still challenging due to lack of quantitative imaging modality and poor understanding of the fundamental mechanism. This study uses three-dimensional (3D) ultrasound imaging to assess the shear strain in thoracolumbar fascia (TF) tissue during well-controlled back flexion. Shear deformations of TF tissue were quantified by 3D Green-Lagrange strain tensors. The strain tensors were generated from deformation gradient tensors derived by 3D ultrasound speckle tracking. The ultrasound images were acquired from 150 bilateral lower back multifidus muscle locations (participant n = 75). Among all trials, 65 are labelled to have MP points (35 have radiating MP points, known as “Trigger” points; 30 are non-radiating, known as “Tender” points) and 85 are labelled to have no MP points (control). The 3D strain image suggests a reduced shear strain magnitude for MP group. The observation is confirmed by statistics. The results demonstrated an encouraging 3D ultrasound shear strain imaging to classify LBP conditions.

papers.title: Characterization of Shear and Tensile Anisotropy in in Vivo Skeletal Muscle Using 3D-Rotational Shear Wave Elasticity Imaging (3D-RSWEI): Dependence on Applied Stretch
papers.abstract: Previous work has shown the characterization of skeletal muscle as an incompressible transversely isotropic (ITI) material. Herein we extend this analysis to reconstruct shear moduli and tensile anisotropy across multiple stretch states in in vivo vastus lateralis using volumetric 3D-RSWEI data. In-plane muscle fiber tilt was estimated using B-Mode Fourier analysis. Shear moduli parallel and perpendicular to the fibers and a weighted modulus-like term related to tensile anisotropy were estimated by minimizing the RMSE between experimentally measured SWS and analytical calculations of SWS in an ITI material. Shear moduli parallel and perpendicular to the fibers increase in the vastus lateralis with increasing knee flexion, as does the tensile anisotropy modulus. This work indicates feasibility for 3D-RSWEI to estimate ITI material parameters in in vivo skeletal muscle, towards the development of clinical biomarkers for disease monitoring in skeletal muscle.

papers.title: Growing Indenter Anisotropy Imaging (GIAnI) Enables Two-Dimensional in Vivo Assessment of Skeletal Muscle Activation
papers.abstract: Growing Indenter Anisotropy Imaging (GIAnI) is a novel acoustic radiation force–based ultrasound elastography technique for two-dimensional, point-wise assessment of shear anisotropy. Skeletal muscle activation increases longitudinal relative to transverse stiffness via actomyosin cross-bridge formation, suggesting anisotropy as a potential biomarker of neuromuscular function. This study evaluated whether GIAnI-based anisotropy measurements relate to muscle activation and force generation in vivo, tested in the biceps of two participants. GIAnI was implemented on a Verasonics Vantage 256 system using confocal ARF excitations (F/1.5 and F/5.0), with anisotropy quantified as the sum of absolute differences (SAD) between displacement profiles. Data were acquired at rest and during sustained isometric contractions using a Biodex dynamometer with simultaneous surface electromyography (EMG). GIAnI-derived SAD showed strong positive correlations with torque (R²=0.97) and EMG (R²=0.90), indicating that GIAnI-based spatially resolved anisotropy imaging tracks muscle activation and force generation, supporting its potential for noninvasive muscle function assessment.

papers.title: Reconstructing Direction-Dependent Shear Wave Phase Velocity Maps from Rotationally Sampled Wave Fields in in Vivo Skeletal Muscle
papers.abstract: To characterize transversely isotropic (TI) tissues with SWEI, measurements of multiple shear wave velocities (SWVs) at multiple trajectories relative to the tissue's axis of symmetry are required. The SWVs for a TI material model as a function of trajectory can be represented in terms of the direction dependent group velocity (gSWV) or phase velocity (pSWV). gSWV measurements can be more robust as they use larger kernels and lower order SWV estimation algorithms, but require more assumptions and complicated fitting routines to accurately relate these measurements back to underlying TI material models. pSWV measurements can be less robust as they use smaller kernels and higher order SWV estimation algorithms, but can be more directly fit to the underlying TI material model. Further, previous high resolution SWV algorithms are not compatible with rotationally sampled wave fields. This proof-of-concept study demonstrates a high resolution algorithm that estimates both SWV magnitude and trajectory, and how its application to rotationally sampled wave fields from in vivo skeletal muscle allows direct estimation of pSWV.

papers.title: Phase Structure Tensor-Based Directional Filtering for Volumetric Transcranial Ultrasound Shear Wave Elastography
papers.abstract: Volumetric transcranial ultrasound shear wave elastography (VTU-SWE) enables three-dimensional assessment of brain tissue mechanical properties, but skull-induced distortion and lesion-related propagation disturbances can degrade wavefield quality and reduce the reliability of shear wave speed (SWS) reconstruction. This study proposes a phase structure tensor-based directional filtering (PST-DF) method to adaptively preserve locally coherent shear wave components. PST-DF extracts a single-frequency complex wavefield, estimates local propagation directions using phase structure tensors in overlapping blocks, and applies direction-selective filtering in the three-dimensional wavenumber domain. Experimental results show that PST-DF suppresses incoherent fluctuations and preserves locally curved propagation features more effectively than global directional filtering, providing more reliable inputs for SWS reconstruction.

papers.title: Shear Wave Elasticity Imaging of Human Brain Through Sonolucent Covers
papers.abstract: This abstract demonstrates the ability to generate and track shear waves through Sonolucent covers created by Longeviti. Shear wave speed can be related back to tissue stiffness, which is an important physiological parameter that can be altered by many intracranial pathologies, like elevated intracranial pressure. The work involves characterizing the acoustic properties of the cover, followed by characterization of phantoms with and without the cover. Additionally, preliminary results from an IRB-approved human subject study are shown. The cover was found to have a speed of sound of 2302 m/s. In the subject shown in the abstract, shear wave propagation is shown, and characterized to have a shear wave speed of 1.63 m/s. Across all experimental repeats, the average shear wave speed in this patient as imaged through the cover is 1.67 +- 0.29 m/s.

sessions.title: TMI: Wearable Ultrasound for Biomedical Imaging and Sensing

papers.title: A PMUT-Based Wearable System for Real-Time Horizontal Gaze Detection
papers.abstract: This work presents a wearable ultrasonic eye-tracking system based on four 1.27 MHz 2D PMUT arrays integrated into an adjustable 3D-printed frame. The arrays operate in a bistatic pulse-echo configuration and are positioned bilaterally around the eye for Time-of-Flight-based gaze estimation. An FPGA-based platform drives the PMUTs and transfers conditioned receive signals to a PC, where real-time cross-correlation is used to estimate gaze direction. In vivo experiments on a human subject demonstrated real-time horizontal gaze tracking from −15° to +15°, with sufficient mechanical stability for dynamic operation. The results confirm the potential of PMUT-based wearable ultrasound for low-power, light-insensitive gaze tracking, while highlighting challenges related to airflow sensitivity and initial alignment. Future work will exploit 2D array beam steering for electronic alignment and full two-dimensional gaze estimation.

papers.title: High-Uniformity PMUT Array with Enhanced Acoustic Output and Broad Bandwidth for Wearable Deep-Organ Imaging
papers.abstract: Aluminum nitride (AlN)-based piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducers (PMUTs) are attractive for wearable ultrasound imaging, but deep-organ applications are still limited by low transmit acoustic pressure, narrow bandwidth, and nonuniform channel responses. Here, we present a high-performance 64-channel AlN-PMUT array designed to improve acoustic output, bandwidth, and channel uniformity. Structural optimization enabled more uniform vibration of micro-elements within each channel, as verified by amplitude and displacement measurements. The silicone-covered array operated at a center frequency of 2 MHz, with a −6 dB fractional bandwidth of 62% and a gain-corrected pulse-echo sensitivity of 54.5 μV/V. Interfaced with a Verasonics system and driven by a 30 V single-cycle sinusoidal pulse, the array achieved phased-array imaging at depths up to 150 mm. Clear cardiac and bladder images demonstrate its potential for wearable deep-organ ultrasound imaging.

papers.title: A Pilot Study of Wearable Ultrasound for Tremor Frequency Monitoring During Functional Hand Motion
papers.abstract: This pilot study evaluates wearable ultrasound (WUS) for tremor-frequency monitoring during functional hand motion and compares it with wrist-mounted IMU sensing. A custom dual-array WUS system with two 64-element, 6-MHz linear arrays was used to image forearm muscle regions in two essential tremor subjects during postural-hold and finger-to-nose tasks. WUS-derived muscle-region echogenicity signals and IMU magnitude signals were analyzed using Welch power spectral density to estimate dominant tremor frequency within 3–8 Hz. During postural hold, WUS and IMU produced comparable tremor-frequency estimates. During finger-to-nose motion, IMU estimates deviated more from the postural-hold reference, while WUS estimates remained closer to baseline. Across two subjects, WUS showed smaller mean reaching deviations than IMU, supporting its potential as a motion-tolerant wearable sensing modality for tremor monitoring during functional hand tasks.

papers.title: Fully Wearable A-Mode Ultrasound for Real-Time-Compatible Torque Estimation During Weighted Elbow Flexion
papers.abstract: This proof-of-concept study investigates a fully wearable, single-element A-mode ultrasound approach for real-time-compatible torque estimation during weighted elbow flexion. Data were collected from one healthy participant across three 10-s trials using a wearable ultra-low-power ultrasound system placed over the biceps, an IMU on the hand, and dynamometer-measured elbow torque as the reference target. A Hilbert-envelope centroid from the muscle-depth ROI was extracted from each A-mode frame as a tissue-motion feature, while IMU gyroscope data were integrated to estimate joint angle. Compact two-layer neural networks were trained using IMU-only, WUS-only, and combined IMU+WUS inputs. WUS-only performance was comparable to IMU-only, while the combined model achieved the lowest average error. The results support single-element wearable A-mode ultrasound as a lightweight sensing pathway for torque-related muscle-performance monitoring and future embedded real-time inference.

papers.title: Effect of Wrist Posture on the Accuracy of Wearable Ultrasound-Based Blood Pressure Monitoring
papers.abstract: Continuous cuffless and unobtrusive blood pressure (BP) monitoring is essential for long-term cardiovascular management, yet its robustness under varying wrist postures remains unclear. This study presents a wrist-worn radial artery ultrasound system based on piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducers, enabling continuous vessel diameter measurement across three postures: resting flat, half fist, and full clenched fist. A synchronized cuff sphygmomanometer was used for one-to-one calibration between diameter and BP, with B-mode imaging for validation. The semi-clenched posture served as a normalization reference, and systolic/diastolic pressures were derived from averaged peak and trough values over multiple pulse cycles. Results show that despite posture-dependent variations in vessel diameter and signal amplitude, reconstructed BP remains stable, with inter-posture errors below 6 mmHg after calibration and within 5 mmHg after normalization. Compared with wrist cuff-based measurements, the proposed method demonstrates improved robustness, supporting its feasibility for continuous BP monitoring in daily use.

papers.title: Wearable Ultrasound-Informed Prediction of Volitional Torque During Walking
papers.abstract: Accurate estimation of human-generated torque is critical for robotic assistance-as-needed control for gait therapy. Ultrasound can be used to obtain this information, but conventional probes are not body-conforming. This work seeks to validate the ability of wearable ultrasound sensor (WUS)-derived features to enhance volitional torque prediction accuracy relative to predictions informed by kinematics and EMG features. Four participants, including one with spinal cord injury, walked on an instrumented treadmill while EMG, WUS, and motion capture data were collected. Neural networks (NNs) were created to map normalized joint torques from kinematics alone or kinematics plus WUS and/or EMG features. All physiologically-informed NNs improved torque prediction accuracy relative to the kinematics-only-informed NN, with the WUS–EMG-informed NN yielding the best performance. These findings confirm that WUS-extracted features can enhance volitional torque prediction accuracy relative to kinematics-only-informed and EMG-informed predictions, including in people with disabilities.

sessions.title: ASE: Simulation and Evaluation Technqiues

papers.title: * INVITED * Demystifying Berlincourt and IEEE Electromechanical Coupling Definitions for Bulk Acoustic Wave Resonators
papers.abstract: Abstract—The effective electromechanical coupling 𝒌𝒆𝒇𝒇𝟐 of a one-dimensional piezoelectric resonator is derived from the exact Foster-1 modal expansion of the input impedance 𝒁𝟏𝟏(𝝎) about the open-circuit Sturm–Liouville spectrum. The single-mode formula 𝒌𝒆𝒇𝒇𝟐=𝝌 ⋅𝒌𝒕𝟐⋅ 𝜞𝒐𝒗 is shown to be the naive truncation of this expansion, obtained by discarding all higher branches. Retaining those branches through their static contribution — a quasi-static closure implemented as a perturbed clamped capacitance computed from the free capacitance of the stack — yields a quasi-static single-mode formula, 𝒌𝒆𝒇𝒇𝟐=𝝃𝟏/(𝟏−𝝉). The two formulas agree at leading order in 𝒌𝒕𝟐, but at the elevated couplings characteristic of AlScN thin films, the naïve formula develops errors of several percent to approximately 10%—errors that the quasi-static formula reduces by more than an order of magnitude in the free-plate benchmark, positioning it as the accurate single-mode expression for high-coupling piezoelectric resonators.
keywords: Demystifying Berlincourt and IEEE Electromechanical Coupling Definitions in a Multilayer Bulk Acoustic Wave Resonator

papers.title: Intermodulation Distortion Simulation of Surface Acoustic Wave Resonator Based on Nonlinear Extended Coupling-Of-Modes Theory
papers.abstract: With the advancement of mobile communications, the suppression of nonlinearity in RF front-end modules is becoming increasingly important. Predicting nonlinear responses from the filter design stage is in high demand. Nonlinear simulation technique has been reported that 3rd-harmonic simulations of Surface Acoustic Wave (SAW) resonators were performed by Coupling-Of-Modes (COM) theory. It is also indicated that this method can be applicable to Intermodulation Distortion (IMD). The IMD responses can be modeled by expressing the nonlinear terms using the sum of linear responses at two frequencies. The result illustrates COM simulations and measurements of admittance and IMD response of an LT POI SAW. We assumed a two-port setup, with two signals having equal power and a constant frequency difference applied to one port, and IMD response is observed at the other port. We focused on the lower frequency IMD response near main response. The result shows a moderate degree of reproducibility. This method is also applicable to circuit simulation and is usable in actual filter design. This report will detail the results of applying the technology to filters.

papers.title: A Cylindrical Transmission Line Matrix Method for Efficient Simulation of Curved BAW Resonators
papers.abstract: This work develops and validates an efficient simulation framework for curved BAW resonators. It reformulates the Transmission Line Matrix method in cylindrical coordinates, incorporates precomputed Lamb wave dispersion, and constructs a nodal Y-matrix to model lateral wave propagation. The approach is implemented and benchmarked against 3D FEM by comparing impedance responses and mode shapes. It is evaluated across multiple geometries (circular, ellipsoidal) and supports different resonator types (SMR, FBAR), demonstrating significant reductions in computation time and memory usage for rapid design iterations.

papers.title: Evaluation of Shear Wave TCV in Piezoelectric and Metal Thin Films Using a GHz pulse-Echo Technique
papers.abstract: The temperature stability of SAW and BAW filters is critical. However, extracting the intrinsic TCF of individual thin films remains difficult. This study evaluates the shear wave TCV, which is essential for optimizing temperature-compensated SAW filters because SAW contains both longitudinal and shear wave components. The measurement structure uses c-axis tilted Sc0.4Al0.6N ultrasonic transducers on a sapphire substrate. An approximate 35° c-axis tilt maximizes the shear mode coupling coefficient (k35). Target films (10-20 µm) are deposited on the opposite side. Shear wave velocity is derived from the time delay between acoustic echoes, and TCV is estimated from velocity changes during heating. According to the results, the metal thin films (Pt, Ti) exhibited a severely poor shear wave TCV compared to longitudinal waves. In ScAlN films, the TCV decreased as Sc concentration increased for both wave modes. However, ScAlN exhibited a superior shear wave TCV compared to its longitudinal wave TCV.

papers.title: Low-Data OOD Prediction of SAW Resonators with Simulation-Compensated Transfer Learning
papers.abstract: This work addresses out-of-distribution (OOD) prediction for surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators under scarce experimental data. Standard machine learning models frequently struggle with OOD scenarios, leading to high prediction errors. This work proposes a simulation-compensated transfer learning framework that leverages noise-free simulation data to calibrate predictions for physical resonators exhibiting authentic fabrication non-uniformity. The model generalizations are benchmarked across three OOD dimensions: geometry, frequency, and material. Results demonstrate that simulation-compensated regularization enables reliable forecasting with limited measurements, achieving significant reduction in OOD prediction error versus baseline methods. This data-efficient methodology provides a scalable solution for optimizing microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) where high-fidelity experimental data acquisition is cost-prohibitive, effectively bridging the prediction-fabrication gap without expensive tape-out iterations. The framework advances robust performance estimation in undersampled design spaces, supporting accelerated RF front-end development.

sessions.title: NSH: Nonlinear, Dispersive, and Structured-Guided Wave Methods in Complex Systems
sessions.chair: Acharya Shashidhara, Mauricio Pereira da Cunha

papers.title: Qualitative Defect Detection in Corrugated Pipes Leveraging Periodic Structure Bandgaps and Non-Dispersive T-Modes
papers.abstract: Through theoretical analysis and finite element modeling, the non-dispersive torsional T-mode was selected as the optimal wave mode for inspection. A four-sensor circumferential phased array was designed to selectively excite this mode, effectively suppressing interference from flexural modes. By analyzing phase and group velocity curves, the optimal excitation frequency was determined, significantly enhancing the signal-to-noise ratio by leveraging periodic bandgap properties. Computational evaluation results demonstrate that the method possesses high sensitivity and robustness, successfully identifying micro-cracks as short as 2 to 3 mm and clearly detecting cracks with various orientations, including those with a 30° inclination. Time-frequency analysis further revealed characteristic energy concentration patterns for different types of defects, specifically inclined external cracks and non-inclined internal cracks. The study confirms that utilizing the bandgap characteristics of periodic structures provides a feasible and efficient solution for the health monitoring of complex elastic components.

papers.title: Sub-Sampling Time Delay Estimation for Guided-Wave Stress Detection
papers.abstract: Monitoring structural stress is vital for aerospace safety. Stress induces nanosecond-level Time-of-Flight (ToF) shifts in ultrasonic guided waves via the acoustoelastic effect, typically necessitating GHz-level sampling and high hardware costs. This study proposes a high-precision sub-sampling time delay estimation (TDE) method using Parabolic Interpolation (PI) to achieve accurate stress extraction at significantly lower sampling rates. By analytically modeling the Discrete Cross-Correlation (DCC) peak via second-order Taylor expansion, ToF precision is elevated from the sampling period level to the sub-nanosecond level. Validated through FDTD simulations and uniaxial tensile tests on 3 mm aluminum alloy plates (S0 mode), the PI algorithm effectively eliminates quantization errors, maintaining sub-nanosecond precision even at 10 MHz. Compared to traditional envelope peak-tracking, this method significantly enhances the linearity and stability of stress inversion, providing a low-power solution for structural health monitoring.

papers.title: Contact-Induced Nonlinear Lamb-Wave Residual Enhancement via Phase-Reversal Modal Decomposition for Early-Stage Bolt Preload Loss Monitoring
papers.abstract: Quantitative ultrasonic monitoring of bolt preload is important for bolt-joint structural health monitoring, but early preload loss is difficult to detect when the interface remains macroscopically closed. This work proposes a phase-reversal modal decomposition framework to enhance contact-induced nonlinear Lamb-wave residuals. For each preload state, paired 0°/180° phase-reversed 200 kHz Lamb-wave responses are decomposed into odd and even branches. The S0-odd packet provides a stable linear reference, while the A0-even high-frequency lobe captures contact acoustic nonlinearity. At 21 N·m, corresponding to 30% torque reduction, the A0-even feature deviates by 53.2% from the reference state, compared with 14.7% for S0-odd, giving a 3.61-fold early-stage response gain. Time-frequency consistency is supported by Pearson r = 0.958. ARSF-Net further enables quantitative preload regression and M10-to-M5 transfer, achieving R² = 0.9694 on M10 and R² = 0.9274 after one-epoch transfer.

papers.title: Compact Three-Element Temperature-Compensated Guided-Wave Imaging for Cryogenic Structural Health Monitoring of Plate-Like Structures
papers.abstract: This work presents a compact three-element guided-wave imaging framework for cryogenic structural health monitoring of plate-like structures. A triangular piezoelectric array is used as a low-sensor-count SHM unit, where sequential transmission from each element provides six pitch-catch channels from only three actuation events. To mitigate temperature-induced baseline drift, a target-temperature healthy response is reconstructed before residual extraction through guided-wave packet time-axis alignment. The compensated residuals are then processed using ToF-difference-guided sector selection and weighted TFM, where measured inter-channel ToF-difference signs reject geometrically infeasible pixels and the six channels are fused into a damage-intensity map. At 25 °C, two defects were localized with errors of 1.0 mm and 2.8 mm. At −160 °C, uncompensated imaging produced a 69.8 mm error, whereas compensation reduced the error to 14.9 mm, demonstrating a 78.7% reduction in cryogenic localization bias and practical low-sensor-count guided-wave SHM capability under extreme thermal environments.

papers.title: Simultaneous SOC and Temperature Estimation for LFP Batteries at Low Temperatures via Guided Ultrasonic Waves and Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.abstract: This study proposes a novel ultrasound-assisted sensing method using Guided Ultrasonic Waves (GUW) and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to simultaneously estimate the State of Charge (SOC) and temperature of LFP batteries in sub-zero environments. Bypassing the limitations of traditional electrical methods at low temperatures, the CNN directly processes raw ultrasonic waveforms to detect internal physicochemical changes without relying on external thermal sensors. The model achieved a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.92% for SOC and 0.11°C for temperature, providing a robust, thermocouple-free monitoring solution for Battery Management Systems.

papers.title: Dual-Focusing Shear-Horizontal Surface Acoustic Waves for High-Throughput Microparticle Manipulation
papers.abstract: Conventional SAW-based acoustofluidic systems rely on leaky shear-vertical (SV) SAWs to excite fluid acoustic fields, but often suffer from PDMS energy dissipation and weak channel resonance. In contrast, SH-SAWs radiate inefficiently into liquids and have therefore been mainly used for sensing rather than fluid actuation. Here, we demonstrate a dual-focusing SH-SAW acoustofluidic mechanism. A single parabolic reflector transducer (SPLUS) first focuses SH-SAW energy from a large x-polarized PZT onto the substrate surface without mode-conversion loss. A concave fluidic channel then creates a local slow-phase-velocity region, further confining the focused SH-SAW energy near the channel. Numerical results show that SPLUS concentrates energy from a 10-mm-wide PZT into a 2.5-mm focal region with an amplification ratio of 4. The confined vibration generates a half-wavelength standing wave across a 375-μm-wide, 100-μm-high channel, producing a dominant x-direction acoustic radiation force that focuses microparticles toward the central nodal plane. This dual-focusing mechanism enables efficient acoustic energy delivery for scalable acoustofluidic particle manipulation.

sessions.title: MEL: Wave Physics, Advanced Actuation, and Material Characterization

papers.title: A Comprehensive Physics-Based Finite-Element Framework for End-to-End Shear Wave Elastography Simulation: the Cornea As a Test Case
papers.abstract: Quantitative interpretation of acoustic radiation force (ARF)-induced shear wave elastography (SWE) in anisotropic tissues, such as the keratoconic cornea, is limited by the absence of a simulation framework that captures the full physics of the measurement. Existing models rely on simplified solid formulations (e.g., k-Wave) that break down in realistic tissues. We therefore developed a 3D finite-element (FEM) framework for end-to-end ARF-SWE simulation, demonstrated on a corneal geometry with nearly incompressible transversely isotropic (NITI) material behavior as the test case. Results show that although k-Wave agreed with FEM under purely elastic assumptions, it deviated from experiment even in a weakly viscoelastic medium; the viscoelastic FEM framework matched the measurements most closely, confirming its accuracy and exposing the limits of k-Wave for tissue-mimicking media. The framework also reproduced the NITI guided-wave behavior. The time-resolved fields showed coherent propagation in the healthy cornea but a distorted, dispersed wavefield in the keratoconic case. These results validate the framework as a generalizable platform for ARF-SWE simulation in complex tissues.

papers.title: Focused Shear Wave Transient elastography Using an Annular Piston Reduces Artifact Due to Compressional Waves in Vivo
papers.abstract: An annular (ring-shaped) piston design in focused shear wave transient elastography (fTE) reduces compressional wave artifacts and improves signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) compared to concave designs, demonstrate fTE feasibility to improve reliability in liver stiffness measurements for patients with obesity. In proof-of-concept tests, the annular piston maintained high success rates in a volunteer and improved performance in a patient with a BMI of 40 kg/m² relative to traditional concave focused piston methods. These results demonstrate fTE feasibility for patient obesity.

papers.title: In Situ Shear Wave Focusing via Patterned Push Pulses
papers.abstract: Recent work shows focused shear waves improve transient elastography, but require a physical source. Here, we propose focusing shear waves via a shaped push pulse to enhance particle velocity and improve tracking SNR for SWE.

papers.title: 3D Shear Wave Elastography for Volumetric Visualization of Proton Dose Distribution and Bragg Peak Localization in NIPAM Gel Dosimeter
papers.abstract: This study investigates the feasibility of using 3D shear wave elastography (3D-SWE) to visualize proton-induced dose distributions in NIPAM polymer gel dosimeters. NIPAM gel phantoms were irradiated with a 110 MeV proton beam using a 1 cm diameter field at dose levels from 0 to 10 Gy. SWE measurements were performed 24 hours after irradiation, and volumetric data were acquired with a 0.2 mm sampling interval to reconstruct the elasticity distribution along the beam path. The reconstructed 3D elasticity volume showed a localized high-elasticity region at the distal beam end, corresponding to the expected Bragg peak region. Maximum-intensity-projection elasticity maps further depicted the spatial extent of dose deposition and showed a slight proximal shift compared with water-based simulations, suggesting that NIPAM has a higher stopping power than water. In addition, the mean elasticity increased linearly with dose, indicating a quantitative dose-stiffness relationship. These findings support the potential of 3D-SWE as a volumetric readout technique for polymer gel dosimetry in proton range verification and dose distribution assessment.

papers.title: Characterization of Crosslinking-Dependent Elasticity in Soft Hydrogels with Acoustic Force Elastography Microscopy
papers.abstract: Polyacrylamide (PAAm) hydrogels regulate cell behavior through tunable mechanics. Current methods provide bulk values, require contact, and destroy samples, which limits longitudinal studies. Transparent and thin hydrogels further restrict conventional elastography. This study applies acoustic force elastography microscopy (AFEM) for non-contact quantification of hydrogel elasticity across crosslinking densities. A 5 MHz transducer generated acoustic radiation force to induce longitudinally polarized shear waves. A spectral-domain OCT system measured particle displacement at 30 kHz. PAAm hydrogels (12% acrylamide) were prepared with three crosslinking densities (φ_c = 0.00088, 0.0044, 0.0088). Elastic modulus was estimated from wave velocity and compared with mechanical testing. Measured moduli followed expected trends and agreed with mechanical testing (11.55–36.90 kPa reference; 12.42–29.56 kPa AFEM). AFEM provides localized, non-contact, and non-destructive elasticity mapping. The method supports longitudinal monitoring of mechanical evolution in living hydrogels and establishes a quantitative framework for tissue engineering and biomaterial systems.

papers.title: Differentiation of Microplastic-Containing Fluids via Capillary Wave Dispersion Measured by Acoustic Radiation Force Optical Coherence Elastography
papers.abstract: Microplastics alter fluid mechanical properties and remain difficult to detect with sufficient sensitivity and standardization. Capillary waves depend on interfacial mechanics and provide a direct measure of surface tension. We hypothesize that microplastic contamination modifies capillary wave behavior and can be identified through its mechanical signature. An acoustic radiation force optical coherence elastography system generated and detected capillary waves. A 5 MHz transducer induced waves and OCT tracked propagation. Three samples were tested: tap water, bottled water, and the same water after 50 hours of sunlight exposure. Surface tension was estimated from k-space dispersion analysis. Surface tension was 74.26 ± 1.22 mN m for tap water, 65.60 ± 1.07 mN m for bottled water, and increased to 70.30 ± 1.34 mN m after exposure. Phase velocity at 500 Hz decreased from 0.72 m/s to 0.66 m/s after exposure. These shifts indicate modified interfacial mechanics. The results support that ARF-OCE resolves microplastic-induced changes and provides a label-free approach for fluid assessment.

sessions.title: MIS: Speed of Sound & Inverse Problems

papers.title: Reconstruction-Aware Measurement Refinement for Imaging Sound-Speed
papers.abstract: Speed-of-sound (SoS) is a quantitative biomarker and crucial for ultrasound modalities via beamforming. Speckle-shift-based methods estimate SoS by solving an inverse problem relating SoS to measured shifts. These approaches typically assume straight-ray propagation, neglect refraction, and rely on heavy postprocessing (requiring RF data), yet remain sensitive to motion and low SNR in vivo. We propose a framework that enables accurate SoS imaging using simplified straight-ray imaging models by denoising and refining measurements.

papers.title: Impact of Windowing on Full-Waveform Inversion for Ultrasound Tomography
papers.abstract: Full-waveform inversion (FWI) is widely used in ultrasound tomography (UST) but suffers from non-convexity, making it prone to cycle-skipping when initialized with high-frequency data. This work proposes a dynamic windowing approach guided by Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) time-of-flight (TOF) estimates to mitigate this issue. The method aligns a temporal window with the first arrival and initially restricts it to early signals, emphasizing low-frequency phase information for stable, large-scale sound-speed updates. As inversion progresses, the window expands to include later scattered waves, enabling higher-resolution reconstruction. Validation on in-vivo breast and ex-vivo transcranial datasets shows that this strategy effectively extends usable bandwidth below the transducer’s nominal limit. Compared to static windowing, which limits resolution, and no windowing, which causes instability, dynamic windowing balances robustness and detail, reducing cycle-skipping while improving fine-scale imaging accuracy.

papers.title: Improving Speed-of-Sound Reconstruction with Physics-Guided Reverse Time Migration Representations
papers.abstract: Accurate reconstruction of the spatial distribution of the speed of sound (SoS) in ultrasound imaging is a challenging inverse problem due to its strong nonlinearity and inherent ill-posedness. Existing deep learning approaches often rely on end-to-end frameworks that directly map measurement data to SoS distributions; however, these methods typically exhibit limited robustness and poor generalization to variations in medium properties. To address these limitations, we propose a physics-guided reconstruction framework that leverages reverse time migration (RTM) to generate intermediate representations. A ConvNeXt-based network is then trained to map these representations to the final SoS distribution.

papers.title: Sound Speed Imaging Based on Image Autocorrelation Tracking
papers.abstract: Sound speed is an intrinsic acoustic biomarker closely related to tissue density and elasticity, serving as a key indicator of ultrasound clinical diagnosis. This work presents a novel practical sound speed imaging (SSI) framework capable of estimating global average speed and mapping local speed distributions. The raw radiofrequency (RF) data were beamformed at different sound speeds, and a two-dimensional (2D) spatial autocorrelation function (ACF) was adopted to evaluate each beamformed image. Full width at half maximum (FWHM) was calculated for both axial and lateral peaks to determine the globally optimal sound speed that minimizes the FWHM. For local speed reconstruction, we implemented regional calculation using a sliding-window strategy to generate a 2D distribution map, with the window size determined by the smallest unit to be resolved. Phantom and in vivo results demonstrated excellent consistency with the reference, indicating the feasibility of ACF tracking-based SSI.

papers.title: Bayesian Cramér–Rao Bound for Quantifying Speed-of-Sound Imaging Limits
papers.abstract: Speed-of-sound (SoS) imaging provides quantitative information related to tissue properties and has potential value for ultrasound tissue characterization. However, existing SoS reconstruction methods are commonly evaluated using empirical metrics, such as mean squared error, that depend on the simulated or experimental dataset, noise level, and reconstruction algorithm. These metrics do not distinguish fundamental limits imposed by the forward model, imaging geometry, noise, and prior assumptions from errors introduced by specific reconstruction algorithms or datasets. To address this limitation, this work investigates the Bayesian Cramér–Rao bound (BCRB) as a theoretical lower bound for SoS estimation error and as a tool for comparing and optimizing SoS imaging strategies. In this work, SoS estimation is formulated as a Bayesian inverse problem incorporating prior knowledge of medium SoS variations and the noise model. The resulting BCRB map is derived from the Bayesian Fisher information matrix associated with the inverse problem, which provides spatially resolved lower bounds on SoS estimation uncertainty.

papers.title: Fourier Neural Operator-Enhanced Physics-Embedded Full Waveform Inversion for Transcranial Ultrasound Sound-Speed Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Transcranial ultrasound sound-speed reconstruction is challenging because the skull causes strong refraction, scattering, attenuation, and phase distortion. Conventional full waveform inversion (FWI) uses rich wavefield information but requires repeated wave-equation solutions. This work introduces a Fourier neural operator (FNO) forward surrogate into a physics-embedded FWI framework for fast frequency-domain transcranial ultrasound inversion. The FNO maps a 250 × 250 sound-speed image to a 64 × 64 × 2 complex-valued data matrix and is embedded into the inversion network after training. Conventional FWI, FCNN-FWI, and FNO-FWI were compared using RMSE, relative error, SSIM, error maps, reconstruction time, and model size. FNO-FWI achieved the best result, with RMSE = 0.0228, relative error = 0.0146, SSIM = 0.9947, and 0.0080 s reconstruction time. It also used only 5.9% of the FCNN-FWI parameters. This result shows that FNO is a compact and efficient surrogate for transcranial ultrasound inversion.

sessions.title: MCA: Clinical Diagnostics and Organ-Specific Imaging

papers.title: Quantitative and Noninvasive Evaluation of Portal Hypertension in Pediatric Patients Using Subharmonic-Aided Pressure Estimation (SHAPE)
papers.abstract: The objective of this study was to provide a retrospective analysis of 21 subharmonic-aided pressure estimation (SHAPE) studies performed on pediatric patients to determine its utility for diagnoses of pediatric portal hypertension. There does not currently exist a quantitative, noninvasive measure of pediatric portal hypertension, and this study aims to pose SHAPE as a viable tool.

papers.title: Comparison Between Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound and Magnetic Resonance Imaging in the Evaluation of Uterine Fibroid Vascularity Prior to Uterine Artery Embolization
papers.abstract: Uterine fibroids are the most common type of benign uterine tumor affecting approximately 30% of all women in the USA. Uterine artery embolization (UAE) is a nonsurgical therapy that blocks arterial blood flow to the fibroids causing selective ischemic necrosis and fibroid shrinkage. Gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the current standard imaging modality for vascularity characterization of uterine fibroids prior to UAE. Contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) offers a low cost, noninvasive, and readily available approach, which can characterize both structural and functional features of tumor vascularity from its earliest stages. The objective of the study was to assess fibroid microvascularity prior to UAE using CEUS and to compare the results with the clinical standard MRI. The results indicate that CEUS prior UAE can accurately evaluate fibroid microvascularity and, thus, can be a noninvasive and accurate alternative to MRI for uterine fibroid diagnoses and characterization. The utilization of CEUS prior to UAE would be beneficial for patient care, since it is easily accessible, less expensive, and is a real-time imaging modality.

papers.title: In Vivo Lymphatic Flow Imaging Using Lymphatic Contrast Enhanced Ultrasound (CEUS)
papers.abstract: The lymphatic system is clinically vital but difficult to image. Existing modalities suffer from poor resolution, lack of flow dynamics, or invasive procedures. Lymphatic CEUS (contrast-enhanced ultrasound) uses subcutaneous microbubble (MB) injections as tracers and has proven effective for lymphatic system imaging. However, previous work has not demonstrated lymphatic flow imaging capabilities. We demonstrate lymphatic flow imaging using CEUS combined with 2D cross-correlation-based speckle tracking. Definity MBs were injected around the ankle of a rabbit. Data were acquired at 19 fps using a Siemens Sequoia system. Lymphatic tissue was identified via high-intensity regions unique to CEUS images. Speckle tracking was implemented with the MATLAB Ultrasound Toolbox and bulk tissue motion compensation was compensated for. Vector field calculations for the lymph node and vessel system revealed regions of coherent flow. Average flow speeds of 0.25 mm/s were calculated, aligning with reported physiological rates for rabbits. While some noise persists, CEUS imaging shows promise as a non-invasive alternative for characterizing lymphatic flow.

papers.title: Effect of Bubble Size Distribution on Multiparametric Dynamic Contrast Enhanced Ultrasound (mpDCE-US) of Pancreatic Tumors
papers.abstract: While widely understood that UCA acoustic response depends on cross-sectional diameter and shell composition, few studies rigorously examine bubble size impact on agent dynamics in tumors. In this work, we investigate tumor kinetics for bubbles of different sizes and identical composition to examine how size distribution impacts DCE-US parameters. Agents were prepared via mechanical amalgamation driven self assembly. Nanobubbles (NBs) were isolated via centrifugation and MBs from remaining fraction after NB removal. Mid-size bubbles (MsB) were prepared with an identical protocol without centrifugation. Gas volume matched agents were administered IV, imaged with concurrent B/nonlinear contrast mode. Parametric maps were produced from time intensity curves. In vivo, NBs showed significantly higher AUC versus MsB, MB. Parametric maps are distinct for each agent and show vasculature delineation (MB), smaller capillaries (MsB), and extravascular enhancement with vascular component obscured (NB). The data suggest that agent size distribution affects in vivo dynamics and parametric maps provide critical physiological information which can be interpreted differently based on agent size.

papers.title: Rapid High Frequency Imaging of Breast Cancer Tumors Expressing Gas Vesicles
papers.abstract: The introduction of acoustic reporter genes (ARGs) into mammalian cell line raises the question of how and what optimized tools can be provided to researchers to detect the presence of gas vesicle (GV) with ultrasound. We have developed dual frequency (DF) transducers for X-wave imaging of GV. An 8/30 MHz configuration was used to obtain measurements such as signal-to-noise and contrast-to-tissue ratios for GV detection in LM2-4_ARG cell line. Imaging was performed in agar phantoms with cells embedded in low melting agarose and mouse subcutaneous xenograft model. The DF configuration improves linear scatter signal suppression, frame rates (kHz), and resolution of GV detection. The contrast sequence is reduced to a Tx pulse in DF mode because Rx harmonics are separated from the tissue by the frequency gap between the Tx and Rx transducers. Uninduced and induced GV expression in LM2-4_ARG cells show little variation in echogenicity in B-mode, but a 17 dB contrast in DF mode, and ~30 dB contrast-to-noise ratio in phantoms. Contrast signals difference between uninduced vs induced cells was also observed in vivo. This DF imaging offer a useful approach for the detection of GVs.

papers.title: Ultrasound Contrast Imaging with Truncated Hadamard-Encoded Transmission for Suppression of Tissue Motion Artifacts
papers.abstract: Coded excitation with Hadamard-encoded multipulse (HEM) transmission is widely used in ultrasound contrast imaging to enhance nonlinear microbubble echoes while suppressing tissue background. However, its performance is highly sensitive to tissue motion, which introduces temporal misalignment among echoes from multiple transmissions and degrades HEM decoding, resulting in residual tissue signals after pulse subtraction. In this study, a truncated HEM transmission is proposed to mitigate motion-induced artifacts by removing pulses most affected by motion. Using a 4th-order Hadamard sequence, the first and last bits are eliminated, and amplitude modulation (AM) is applied to the remaining pulses to enhance nonlinear signals. The decoding framework remains unchanged, preserving the original signal gain. Experimental results demonstrate improved performance of contrast-enhanced imaging with motion robustness. The CTR is consistently higher than that of the conventional method at physiological reasonable speed of motion with a maximum improvement of approximately 7 dB.

sessions.title: PNL: Nonlinear Physical Acoustics II

papers.title: Fourier Neural Operator Modeling of Ultrasound Intensity Fields in Heterogeneous Scattering Media
papers.abstract: This work proposes a Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) to accelerate wave propagation modeling in heterogeneous multiple-scattering media. Full-wave simulations can generate pressure and intensity fields, but they are computationally demanding, and acquiring the full-field experimental data is often infeasible. To address this challenge, k-Wave was used to generate a dataset of 2000 cases, treating the scatterer number density, speed of sound, and density as input variables, and the target output was the log of the normalized intensity at several time frames. An FNO was then trained with an RMS/L2-based error metric, in which input maps were Gaussian-smoothed on a coarser grid, and spatial coordinates were added as channels. After 80 epochs, train/validation errors dropped below 5%, and predicted intensity maps agreed closely with corresponding k-Wave at multiple times. The proposed framework can be extended to predict full Rf response matrices for adaptive beamforming, imaging, and QUS-based inverse problems and tissue characterization. It also enables rapid parameter sweeps and inverse-problem pipelines and offers a practical alternative to repeated k-Wave simulations.

papers.title: Two-Dimensional Transcranial Ultrasound Simulations with a High-Order Discontinuous Galerkin Solver
papers.abstract: Simulations of ultrasound propagation through the skull are important for transcranial focused ultrasound, neuromodulation, and other HIFU-based applications, where heterogeneity, impedance mismatch, refraction, aberration, and nonlinear waveform distortion can substantially alter the transmitted field. Such simulations are computationally demanding because realistic skull models require large three-dimensional domains, fine spatial resolution, and robust treatment of material interfaces. To reduce computational cost, some solvers use frequency-domain approaches such as angular spectrum and mixed-domain methods. Although such methods provide useful approximations, the associated simplifications can limit predictive accuracy.

papers.title: Two-Dimensional Discontinuous Galerkin Modeling of Shear Waves Generated by an Acoustic Radiation Force
papers.abstract: Shear wave elastography estimates tissue mechanical properties from shear waves generated by an acoustic radiation force. The shear wave field depends on the spatial distribution of the excitation and the mechanical response of the medium, motivating numerical models to study how focusing, transducer configurations, and tissue-like properties influence shear wave generation and propagation. Fully three-dimensional simulations are computationally demanding, which motivates two-dimensional formulations that preserve essential wave behavior while remaining practical on personal computers. Discontinuous Galerkin methods, which are well suited for these simulations, provide a high-order, energy-stable framework for time-domain elastic wave propagation with localized body-force excitation.

papers.title: Efficient Mini-Batch Full Waveform Inversion for Transcranial Ultrasound Computed Tomography Using Adam Optimization
papers.abstract: Stroke is a time critical disease where rapid and accurate imaging is essential. Ultrasound Computed Tomography (USCT) combined with Full Waveform Inversion (FWI) enables high resolution imaging and has shown strong promise in breast cancer diagnosis. More recently, FWI has been extended to brain imaging for estimating tissue sound speed, but its application is limited by high computational cost, as each iteration requires solving both forward and adjoint wave equations for all sources. To address this challenge, we propose a mini-batch FWI framework that integrates Adam optimization with spatially diverse source selection to approximate the data misfit and gradient efficiently. Compared with the conventional full batch method, demonstrations on a hemorrhagic stroke model show faster convergence, near linear reductions in computational cost, and improved image quality. Reconstructions with moderate batch sizes achieve higher structural similarity (SSIM) than the full batch baseline, underscoring the potential of mini-batch FWI to reduce computational burden while enhancing brain imaging performance.

papers.title: An Analytic Solution for Laser Heating in Laser Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Modeling laser ultrasound with FDTD requires the combination of a laser heating simulation with an elastic wave propagation simulation. Because of the different scales of the simulations, it is difficult to couple the heating simulation to the elastic wave propagation simulation. Fortunately, by formulating the laser heating via an analytical solution, the need to combine two FDTD simulations that take place at different scales is avoided. An analytic solution for three-dimensional laser heating is derived by inserting the Green’s function for diffusion in the Fourier heat equation. The laser spot is formulated as an infinite line source whose energy decays exponentially into the material. We compare laser heating, simulated with an FDTD simulation to the results obtained with the proposed analytic solution. The analytic solution predicts a higher maximum surface temperature and slightly faster decay than the FDTD simulation. Both methods produce wave fields which are virtually the same.

papers.title: Audible Focal Spot Generation via a Metasurface-Enabled Parametric Array Loudspeaker
papers.abstract: Parametric array loudspeakers (PALs) produce highly directional sound beams but are constrained by poor low-frequency performance and unwanted low-path attenuation. Here, we present a passive acoustic metasurface (AMS) lens that enables broadband focusing of the audible beam generated by an ordinary PAL. The AMS is constructed from Fabry-Pérot-based annular unit cells, whose width is smaller than the carrier ultrasound wavelength, allowing fine spatial phase control for achieving tight focusing. Both simulations and experiments confirm the generation of strongly localized audible focal spots, with measured full-width at half-maximums below 30 mm axially and 6 mm laterally across a wide frequency range from 500 Hz to 4 kHz. Furthermore, the proposed metasurface lens achieved a 46.6 dB enhancement in the sound pressure level at the focal point at 500 Hz, effectively delivering strong low-frequency output. Ultimately, our passive AMS design significantly reduces unwanted acoustic spillover and provides steeper path attenuation than conventional PALs, supporting privacy-preserving audio delivery in public installations, vehicles, healthcare, and immersive environments.

sessions.title: MTH: Neuromodulation and Brain Circuit Control with Focused Ultrasound

papers.title: Frequency-Dependent Bidirectional Control of Dopamine Release by Transcranial Focused Ultrasound Targeting of the Substantia Nigra
papers.abstract: Focused ultrasound (FUS) can non-invasively target deep brain structures, but how stimulation parameters shape neurotransmitter release remains unclear. We investigated how pulse repetition frequency (PRF) controls striatal dopamine release in transcranial FUS targeting the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) in awake, freely moving mice. Dopamine dynamics were monitored using GRAB-DA3m with fiber photometry. FUS trains (550 kHz, 5 s, 20% duty cycle, 0.76 MPa) were delivered at PRFs of 1, 2.5, 5, 10, 20, and 100 Hz in a within-subject design. PRF determined response polarity: low PRFs (1–2.5 Hz) evoked dopamine increases, while medium-high PRFs (10–20 Hz) produced sustained suppression. Peak responses occurred at 2.5 Hz (Z-score: 5.97±0.75). Post-stimulation analysis of spontaneous dopamine release revealed increased transient amplitude, prolonged duration, and reduced event rate, indicating lasting effects beyond the FUS window. These results demonstrate PRF-dependent bidirectional control of nigrostriatal dopamine release, suggesting that FUS can be selectively tuned to alter dopaminergic signaling in therapeutic applications targeting movement and psychiatric disorders.

papers.title: Acoustic Vagus Nerve Stimulation Modulates Basolateral Amygdala Activity in Chronic Restraint Stress Mice
papers.abstract: This study investigated whether acoustic vagus nerve stimulation (aVNS) modulates basolateral amygdala (BLA) activity and alleviates stress-induced emotional abnormalities. A noninvasive aVNS platform was established to stimulate the cervical vagus nerve, with acoustic characterization showing a ~1.8 mm ultrasound spot at −3 dB and 3 MPa pressure. Fiber photometry showed that aVNS evoked robust calcium responses in BLA neurons. In chronic restraint stress (CRS) mice, 7 days of daily aVNS improved anxiety-like behaviors in the OFT and EPM. LFP analysis further showed that CRS reduced BLA oscillatory power, whereas aVNS selectively restored δ and high-γ power. These results suggest that aVNS alleviates CRS-induced anxiety-like behaviors by modulating BLA activity.

papers.title: Bayesian-Enhanced closed-Loop Optimization of Ultrasound Protocols for Targeted and Precise neuromodulation
papers.abstract: Low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU) is an emerging non-invasive neuromodulation technique whose translational potential is currently limited by a poorly understood parameter space and by high intra- and inter-subject response variability. Identifying effective stimulation protocols at the subject level requires closed-loop methods that adapt the choice of parameters to an observed neural response, ideally with a small number of evaluations and an explicit stopping rule. Here we developed and validated in vivo a closed-loop optimization framework, Bayesian-enhanced adaptive control of ultrasound neuromodulation (BEACUN), that combines real-time functional ultrasound imaging (fUSI) feedback with Bayesian optimization.

papers.title: Sonogenetic Control of a Prefrontal cortex-Hypothalamus Circuit for Heart Rate Control in non-Human Primates
papers.abstract: TRPV1-mediated sonogenetics is an emerging neuromodulation tool which uses focused ultrasound (FUS) mild warming to noninvasively activate genetically defined neuron populations overexpressed with TRPV1 ion channel, enabling cell-type specific and temporally precise interrogation of brain circuits. However, its feasibility in the primate brain remains unexplored. The primate ventral lateral prefrontal cortex (area 47/12; a12) is involved in many decision-making processes and may influence heart rate regulation through its projections to lateral hypothalamus (LHA). This positions a12 as a promising target for treating disorders related to cognition-heart dysfunction. Here, we showed that sonogenetics can modulate heart rate dynamics via primate a12 brain circuitry, providing a scalable tool for human brain intervention.

papers.title: Peripheral Focused Ultrasound neuromodulation for the Reduction of Chronic Pain in Neurofibromatosis Type 1 Patients
papers.abstract: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) causes nerve sheath tumors that often lead to chronic pain, with limited effective treatments. This study explored peripheral focused ultrasound (FUS) as a noninvasive method to reduce pain in NF1 patients. Eight participants were recruited. In the first phase, the ability of FUS to reduce NF-related pain was investigated with six subjects who received mechanical pain stimuli paired with FUS. Pain ratings were reduced with FUS compared to sham stimulation, while active control subjects receiving off-target FUS reported increased pain. In the second phase, two subjects underwent weekly FUS treatments over 4 and 9 weeks. Both showed meaningful reductions in pain intensity and interference, along with improvements in quality of life measures such as anxiety, depression, and sleep quality. When treatments were missed, pain returned to baseline, suggesting ongoing therapy is needed. Overall, displacement-guided FUS appears to safely reduce NF1-related pain and improve quality of life, with effects dependent on precise nerve targeting and consistent treatment.

papers.title: Optimizing Focused Ultrasound Parameters for Sterile Inflammation and T-Cell Recruitment in the Healthy Murine Brain
papers.abstract: The efficacy of immune therapies in the brain is restricted by the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and the brain’s immune-privileged status. Focused ultrasound and microbubble (FUS+MB) treatment offers a non-invasive approach to open the BBB and trigger transient sterile inflammation. This process induces vascular expression of intracellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1), a key mediator of leukocyte trafficking. This study characterized the kinetics of this inflammatory response and evaluated how specific FUS parameters influence T-cell recruitment and microglia density (brain resident antigen presenting cells). Our objective was to establish a parametric framework to optimize FUS+MB as a priming tool for treatment cell and immune therapies. These results demonstrate that FUS parameters can be precisely tuned to temporarily modulate the brain’s immune environment and provides a foundational framework for enhancing delivery and efficacy of adoptive cell therapies in the brain with FUS+MB.

sessions.title: MTN: Immunotherapy and Cancer Theranostics

papers.title: * INVITED * Ultrasound Therapy Paradigms for Precision Cancer Treatment
papers.abstract: Immunotherapy has revolutionized cancer treatment, but significant limitations remain across solid tumor indications. This talk will highlight advances in the use of image-guided focused ultrasound (FUS) as a non-invasive, multi-pronged interventional tool for potentiating multiple classes of immunotherapy, including vaccine adjuvants, checkpoint inhibitors, and CAR T cells. We will showcase integration of non-invasive surveillance approaches such as positron emission tomography (PET) and liquid biopsy with FUS to inform precision, adaptation, and de-intensification of combinatorial treatment regimens. We will also showcase development of novel image-guided ultrasound instrumentation toward these objectives. Applications spanning high-risk breast cancer and adult/pediatric brain cancers will be discussed. Finally, this talk will overview clinical translation and insights from first-in-human trials investigating FUS for immuno-oncology applications.

papers.title: Membrane-Bound Gold nanoassemblies for Longitudinal ultrasound-Guided Photoacoustic Monitoring of Car T Cells Against Heterogeneous Solid Tumors
papers.abstract: Noninvasive monitoring of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell activity in heterogeneous solid tumors remains a major challenge for understanding and improving therapeutic response. To address this, we developed membrane-bound gold nanoassemblies composed of plasmonically coupled gold nanospheres in an anisotropic framework for longitudinal ultrasound-guided photoacoustic imaging of CAR T cells. These nanoassemblies exhibit ~90% absorption efficiency and high photostability under laser fluences exceeding 20 mJ cm-2, enabling robust photoacoustic signal generation over repeated imaging cycles. Surface anchoring of nanoassemblies preserves key CAR T cell functions while conferring strong photoacoustic responsiveness upon laser excitation. In heterogeneous HER2-expressing breast tumor models, longitudinal imaging enabled early stratification of tumors by correlating CAR T cell trafficking dynamics with therapeutic outcomes. Collectively, this approach provides a strategy for noninvasive, functional monitoring of CAR T cell activity in solid tumors.

papers.title: Nanobubble-Mediated Ultrasound Mechanotherapy Potentiates Immunotherapy for Noninvasive Cancer Ablation
papers.abstract: This work explores nanobubbles as efficient cavitation nuclei for low-frequency ultrasound histotripsy, enabling tumor ablation at significantly reduced energy levels. Beyond ablation, this approach may modulate the tumor microenvironment and enhance immune responses. The study proposes a theranostic strategy combining nanobubbles, low-frequency ultrasound, and systemic antibody therapy, aiming to both destroy tumors mechanically and improve immunotherapy efficacy by increasing antigen release and antibody accessibility. In vitro, breast cancer cells were treated using optimized ultrasound parameters, showing reduced viability (21.6%) and increased apoptosis (61.0%) and necrosis (16.9%). In vivo, nanobubbles combined with ultrasound in a HER2-positive mouse model achieved effective noninvasive tumor ablation. When paired with HER2-targeted antibodies, the treatment further slowed tumor growth and led to complete regression in some cases, demonstrating synergistic therapeutic effects and improved outcomes.

papers.title: Engineering a US/Pa Imaging Strategy to Guide and Inform αvβ3 Car T Cell Therapies
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapies have demonstrated success in hematological malignancies. However, their translation to solid tumors remains limited, largely due to the complex tumor microenvironment, which restricts T cell infiltration and can suppress their effector function. Efforts to overcome these barriers are hindered by a lack of noninvasive methods to monitor CAR T cell delivery, distribution, and persistence within tumors in real time, limiting our ability to identify where and why therapies fail. Ultrasound and photoacoustic (US/PA) imaging provide a clinically translatable platform to address this challenge. While prior studies have demonstrated the feasibility of tracking T cells using PA imaging in preclinical models, these approaches have been limited to murine cells. Here, we investigate the potential of an imaging-enabled approach to track αvβ3 CAR T cell trafficking and tumor infiltration in a clinically relevant solid tumor model. Ultimately, this approach seeks to improve our understanding of CAR T cell behavior in solid tumors and inform the development of more effective cancer treatment strategies.

papers.title: Super-Resolution Ionizing Radiation Acoustic Beam Localization During Proton Beam Therapy
papers.abstract: Proton beam therapy (PBT) can improve outcomes by concentrating dose in the tumor while sparing healthy tissue, but delivery accuracy is limited by range uncertainties and anatomical changes during treatment. This work develops and validates ionizing radiation acoustic beam localization (iRABL), a real-time method to localize proton beam spots with high sensitivity, resolution, and accuracy. A specialized high-speed, high-resolution iRABL system was built and evaluated in soft-tissue phantoms and with clinical prostate treatment plans, then demonstrated in the first human study of prostate cancer patients receiving PBT. The system achieved submillimeter displacement resolution (0.1 mm lateral, 0.2 mm axial), single-pulse temporal resolution with tracking above 1 kHz using GPU acceleration, and accurate tracking of pencil-beam scanning trajectories and temporal dose accumulation; for an M-shaped plan it reached a 92.8% gamma index with 3 mm/3% criteria, supporting its feasibility for real-time monitoring of clinical proton beam delivery.

sessions.title: TPM: Piezoelectric Materials and Transducers

papers.title: * INVITED * Recent Development of Textured Piezoelectric Ceramics for Electromechanical Applications
papers.abstract: In this talk, the recent progress of textured piezoelectric ceramics will be introduced, including the design of new microplatelet templates, sintering aids, material compositions and texturing process. Based these new developments, some textured piezoelectric ceramics currently show comparable piezoelectricity to that of single crystal counterparts.

papers.title: Sonofibers: a Flexible Textile for Low-Ultrasound Absorption
papers.abstract: Sound-absorbing textiles are critical materials across different applications, ranging from civil infrastructure to more advanced mechanical systems. Inorganic fibers, despite their higher absorption performance, are limited by processing costs, health hazards, recyclability, and material stiffness. In this work, we present flexible orghanic sonofibers, made of polyamide-6 (PA6) hollow fibers, filled with a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) matrix and stainless steel microbeads. The microbeads convert mechanical energy into heat, upon ultrasound interrogation. We demonstrate experimentally this concept, in the low ultrasound regime (100 kHz–200 kHz). The modal displacement is recorded via laser doppler vibrometry, and the real and imaginary parts of the wavenumber are evaluated with the inhomogeneous wave correlation (IWC) method to compute the dispersion relation. The sonofibers show sharp resonances at ~150 kHz and ~190 kHz, attributed to the localized microresonator modes, which are not visible in the control fibers, with attenuation differences respectively of ~40 dB and ~20 dB at the corresponding frequencies.

papers.title: Characterization of the Complete Database of Piezoelectric Ceramic from a Single Sample and Single Impedance Measurement Using Deep Learning
papers.abstract: Accurate characterization of (cE, e, EpsS) tensors is vital for ultrasound transducer design. Traditional IEEE standards often yield inconsistent results by requiring multiple samples. While single-sample methods exist, they typically rely on Levenberg-Marquardt optimization, which requires a precise initial guess. This work proposes a characterization method using a Residual Neural Network (ResNet) that eliminates the need for an initial solution, enabling rapid and robust analysis of diverse piezoelectric materials. A ResNet was developed to characterize a Pz26 ceramic block. The approach uses a single electrical impedance measurement featuring 80 resonance modes. To enhance sensitivity, an optimized electrode pattern was designed. Validation on FEM test data shows high precision for elastic tensors and e31 (error < 5%), while e33 and e15 remain within 10%. Experimental application demonstrates that the ResNet successfully identifies constants consistent with the CTS supplier database. This proves the network's ability to provide near-instantaneous, accurate characterization from a single sample.

papers.title: Physics-Guided AI-Assisted Data-Driven Design Exploration of High-Frequency 1–3 Composite Ultrasound Transducers Using Interpretable Surrogate Modeling
papers.abstract: This study develops a physics-guided, AI-assisted surrogate modeling framework for high-frequency 1–3 composite ultrasound transducer design. Simulation data from 29 unique design combinations were used to map structural variables, including pillar diameter, kerf, composite thickness, and parylene coating thickness, to bandwidth, center frequency, and sensitivity. Multiple regression models were benchmarked using leave-one-out cross-validation, and the quadratic surrogate achieved the best overall performance while preserving interpretability. The selected model predicted normalized bandwidth, center frequency, and sensitivity with LOOCV R² values of 0.851, 0.976, and 0.916, respectively. The surrogate then screened 640,000 candidate designs under target frequency, bandwidth, and sensitivity constraints, identifying 23,757 feasible candidates and revealing a narrow favorable pillar-diameter/kerf region. The results demonstrate rapid, interpretable design-space down-selection and highlight the trade-off between bandwidth and frequency constraints.

papers.title: Customized UV Nanosecond Laser Micromachining for Fabrication of PZT Ultrasonic Transducer Arrays
papers.abstract: Miniaturized and application-specific ultrasonic arrays are increasingly required for endoscopic and wearable imaging. Conventional mechanical dicing can introduce mechanical stress and limit geometric flexibility, while commercial laser micromachining systems are often costly and less adaptable for process optimization. This work presents a customized 355 nm UV nanosecond laser micromachining platform for rapid prototyping of PZT ultrasonic transducer arrays. With synchronized laser emission and motion control, key parameters were optimized to obtain narrow, well-defined kerfs (~10 μm) with reduced edge damage. Using the optimized process, 64-element PZT linear arrays with a 10 MHz design frequency and 0.16 mm pitch were fabricated. Pulse-echo and Doppler experiments showed an average center frequency of 9.09 MHz, a 67% bandwidth, and a power Doppler SNR of 27.9 dB in flow phantoms. The array was further integrated into a dual-modal endoscopic probe for combined optical guidance and ultrasound imaging. These results demonstrate a flexible and cost-effective route for application-specific PZT array fabrication.

sessions.title: MTC: Speed-of-Sound, Nonlinearity & Head Imaging

papers.title: Cryoablation Temperature Monitoring with Dense Ultrasonic speed-of-Sound Shift Imaging
papers.abstract: Cryoablation destroys pathological tissue via extreme cooling, but accurate temperature monitoring remains challenging. This work presents a dense speed-of-sound shift imaging method for non invasive, spatially resolved temperature monitoring using ultrasound. The approach estimates speed-of-sound changes from temperature-induced pixel displacements using Farnebäck optical flow and a regularized inverse problem to reconstruct slowness maps. Experiments were performed in agar phantoms and ex vivo turkey breast during cryoablation, with thermocouples as reference. A strong relationship was observed between temperature drop and slowness changes: linear in agar (-20.70 ns/m·°C; R²=0.99) and exponential in turkey (34.04×exp(0.075(-ΔT)-1) ns/m·°C; R²=0.95). Temperatures were tracked down to -39.4±5.6°C. RMSE was 1.7°C in agar and 4.0°C in turkey. Bland-Altman analysis showed biases of 1.48°C in agar and -2.91°C in turkey, with limits of agreement of -3.37 to 6.34°C and -8.11 to 2.28°C, respectively. These results demonstrate the feasibility of real-time, noninvasive ultrasound thermometry for cryoablation.

papers.title: Plane-Wave-to-Line-by-Line Transfer Learning for Speed-of-Sound Estimation Using Synthetic Focusing
papers.abstract: Most deep learning-based quantitative ultrasound (QUS) models are trained on plane-wave (PW) data, causing performance degradation on line-by-line (LBL) acquisitions due to domain shift. Direct LBL training is limited not only by the prohibitive simulation cost but also by the inflexibility of fixed transmit parameters. To address this issue, we propose an efficient data generation and PW-to-LBL transfer learning strategy for deep learning speed-of-sound (SoS) estimation on most commercially available ultrasound machines. Synthetic focusing generates LBL data with various transmit configurations from a single acquisition sequence, and a deep learning backbone pretrained on 4,500 PW samples is fine-tuned with only 30 synthetically focused LBL samples. The framework is validated on simulated breast data to confirm the acoustic equivalence between synthetic and conventional LBL ultrasound, and on in vivo breast scans to demonstrate qualitative lesion delineation under clinical conditions. Our approach achieves an RMSE of 12.37 m/s on simulated breast data, comparable to 12.33 m/s from conventional LBL simulation.

papers.title: Sound Speed Estimation via Multi-Depth Aberration-Corrected Focused Beams
papers.abstract: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease is a major cause of diffuse liver disease, and ultrasound sound speed estimation (SSE) may serve as a key quantitative tool for assessing hepatic steatosis. In this work, we propose a multi-depth SSE method with aberration-corrected focused beams, which enables liver’s SSE without the need for manual segmentation of muscle and fat layers. The proposed method adopts a two-stage framework. First, a depth-dependent effective sound speed, representing the cumulative propagation speed through a superficial layer and the underlying target medium, is estimated using van Cittert–Zernike theorem. To enhance estimation accuracy, phase aberration correction is incorporated to improve beam focusing. Second, the target-medium slowness is recovered via linear regression between depth and effective travel time under a two-layer model. Phantom and in vivo experiments indicate that the proposed approach can effectively estimate the liver’s sound speed without manual segmentation.

papers.title: 3D Characterization of Human Skull Geometry and speed-of-Sound Using refraction-Corrected Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: Previous studies have shown that these aberrations can be corrected when the skull geometry and acoustic wave speed are known. However, such approaches typically rely on CT or MRI to obtain this information. The objective of this study is to characterize the 3D geometry and acoustic wave speed of the human skull using refraction-corrected ultrasound imaging with a matrix array. From homogenized 3D CT images of the human skull, a full matrix capture (FMC) of ultrasound imaging with single-element emissions was simulated using the k-Wave MATLAB toolbox and a 32 × 8 matrix array operating at a center frequency of 1.5 MHz.Three-dimensional image reconstruction was performed using a dedicated delay-and-sum algorithm with compensation for refraction at skull interfaces. The ultrasound wave speed was estimated using a volumetric autofocusing approach that accounts for refraction at bone surfaces. Skull geometry was obtained from segmentation of reconstructed ultrasound images.

papers.title: Nakagami-Based Quantitative Ultrasound Imaging for Noninvasive Intracranial Pressure Monitoring
papers.abstract: Noninvasive monitoring of intracranial pressure (ICP) remains a critical unmet need in neonatal neurocritical care, particularly in conditions such as hydrocephalus. This work investigates quantitative ultrasound (QUS) using Nakagami statistical modeling to detect ICP-induced microstructural changes in brain tissue. In a neonatal porcine model, ICP levels (baseline, 20, 30, 40 mmHg) were established via intracranial fluid infusion and verified using invasive catheter measurements. Radiofrequency ultrasound data were acquired using a research system and analyzed to estimate Nakagami shape (m) and scale (Ω) parameters within a thalamic region of interest. Results demonstrated a monotonic increase in m and decrease in Ω with increasing ICP, with strong correlations (m: r=0.861; Ω: r=−0.702). These findings suggest that Nakagami-based QUS provides a sensitive, noninvasive biomarker for ICP assessment in neonatal hydrocephalus without the need for contrast agents or ionizing radiation.

papers.title: Extension of the Depletion Method in Nonlinearity Parameter Imaging for Arbitrary Power-Law Attenuation Coefficient
