papers.abstract: This project extends the pulse-echo depletion method for nonlinearity parameter (B/A) imaging to media with arbitrary power-law attenuation. The original depletion method estimates B/A from fundamental-band depletion but assumes quadratic frequency-dependent attenuation, which can bias estimates in soft tissues. A new closed-form expression for fundamental-band incident pressure was incorporated into an extended depletion model, while preserving the same low/high-pressure acquisition workflow and reference-phantom compensation. The method was validated using matched simulations and physical phantom experiments, including two uniform sample/reference pairs and one nonuniform inclusion phantom. Across uniform cases, the extended model reduced B/A bias from above 10–15% with the original model to below 1–4%. In the nonuniform case, inclusion bias decreased from 29% to 7% in simulation and from 29% to 5% in the phantom. These results suggest that accounting for arbitrary power-law attenuation improves the accuracy of depletion-based pulse-echo B/A imaging.

sessions.title: ANA: Novel Acoustic Devices

papers.title: High-Sensitivity Tactile Sensor Based on S1-Mode Lamb Wave Resonator
papers.abstract: This work proposes a high-sensitivity tactile sensor based on a first-order symmetric (S1) mode Lamb wave resonator (LWR) for the first time, which achieves exceedingly high sensitivity of 1000 MHz/N at the mN level. A high-sensitivity tactile sensor was implemented based on X-cut single-crystal lithium niobate (LN) thin film with interdigital transducers (IDTs). The S1 mode was selected because of its high Q and stress sensitivity. By properly designing the Euler angle and the suspension structure, localized forces applied via an insulating contact pin directly shift the parallel resonant frequency (fp). The extremely sensitive frequency response can be attributed to the induced large structure deformation. Specifically, the variation of electric field distribution modulates the static capacitance C0 in the modified Butterworth-Van Dyke model, thereby resulting in the change of fp. The S1 mode LWR exhibits parallel quality factor (Qp) of 350 and electromechanical coupling coefficient (k2) of 7.2% at 6.5 GHz. Loading of 50 mN force results in a Δfp of 50 MHz, indicating a sensitivity as high as 1000 MHz/N, making it suitable for next-generation tactile interfaces in robotics.

papers.title: Receiver (Rx) Filter co-Design for Optimized Module Performance
papers.abstract: Conventionally, filters are designed with 50Ohm input and output impedances. Phone makers use matching circuits to shift the impedance to the desired operating point to optimize system performance. In recent years, however, major smartphone makers have increasingly adopted Front-End Module, where filters, Low Noise Amplifiers (LNA), matching networks, Power Amplifiers (PA), and switches are integrated into one module. This integration creates opportunities for co-design and module-level optimization, allowing the filter and surrounding components to be jointly tuned. A non-50Ohm impedance may yield a better overall performance than the 50Ohm design. Two examples illustrate the benefits of non-50Ohm design. (1) The total Rx chain Noise Figure (NF) is determined by the front-end loss combined with the LNA NF, which depends on the noise circle. Compared with a 50Ohm Rx design, using a 70Ohm can yield a lower overall NF. As Double Mode SAW (DMS) can be used as impedance transformer. This allows a SAW filter to bridge the gap between a 50Ohm antenna and a non-50Ohm LNA input impedance. (2) By modifying the Rx filter topology, module-level Tx leakage performance can be improved.

papers.title: Self-Aligned Piezoelectric Nanorod Resonators with Exceptional FoM and Low TCF
papers.abstract: In this work, a new kind of self-aligned nanorod bulk acoustic wave (SN-BAW) resonators has been proposed. By innovating on the core device structure design using a silicon substrate, this novel design successfully breaks the inherent trade-off between high electromechanical coupling (wide bandwidth) and thermal stability. The SN-BAW resonator operates at 1.89 GHz, with a k2 of 29.2%, quality factor at series resonance (3dB_Qs) of 103 and quality factor at parallel resonance (3dB_Qp) of 1053. Besides, the Qmax is measured to be 1235, resulting in an exceptional figure of merit (FoM = k2 × Qmax) of 361. Thanks to the SiO2 layer, the SN-BAW resonator exhibits a TCFp of -23 ppm/°C, approximately one-fourth that of conventional LN based resonators (-80 ppm/°C). In this way, the SN-BAW technology provides a highly scalable, high-performance, and low-cost filtering solution for next-generation space-air-ground integrated wireless networks.

papers.title: Vertically Excited A1 Mode Resonator Using X-124°Y LiTaO3 with 8.7% Bandwidth and Frequency Tunability via Lateral Geometry
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduced a new vertically excited first order antisymmetric mode (A1) resonator employing X-cut LiTaO3 (LT).The device uses LT film sandwiched by top IDT(Interdigital Transducer) and bottom electrode.The Euler angle of (90°,90°,124°) is selected, where piezoelectric constant e35 is maximized. The electric field is oriented in z direction while the displacement distributes in the xz-plane, characterizing the mode as a vertically excited A1 mode.The measured frequency response shows a Z-ratio of 53 dB and BW as high as 8.7%. The device shows a high Qa of 355 although the electrode quality is not well controlled, potentially indicates a high performance after optimization. Significant frequency shifts can be realized by simply tuning the lateral IDT geometry.

papers.title: Polarity Control of Epitaxial Sc0.4Al0.6N Films Using Ion Beam irradiation-Enhanced Sputtering with Anode Magnetron Circuit
papers.abstract: Polarity-inverted multilayer resonators enable high-frequency operation of BAW filters through overtone-mode while keeping the film thickness. We previously reported extraordinary N-polar growth of polycrystalline Sc0.20Al0.80N films using the ion beam irradiation during the sputter-deposition [1]. However, N-polar growth through both epitaxial growth and high Sc concentation films is still challenging. In this study, we present the N-polar growth of epitaxial ScAlN thin films with Sc concentration of 40%. Sc0.40Al0.60N film was grown on (111)Pt / sapphire substrate by RF magnetron sputtering. The substrate was placed on the anode with a magnetron circuit. Ion beam irradiation on the substrate during the film growth can be enhanced by the magnetic fields of magnetron circuit. Six symmetry in the in-plane scan XRD result indicates that the ScAlN film was epitaxially grown. From HBAR conversion loss electromechanical coupling coefficient kt2 of the films was measured to be 8.8%. The film grown with anode magnetron exhibited a positive electrical response when compressive pressure was applied using oscilloscope probe and was therefore identified as extraordinary N-polar.

sessions.title: MIM: Transcranial Ultrasound for Functional and Microvascular Brain Imaging

papers.title: Speed of Sound Aberration Correction for transcranial Dynamic Ultrasound Localization Microscopy Using a Row-Column Array
papers.abstract: Skull-induced speed of sound heterogeneities cause aberrations that limit transcranial ULM (tULM) vascular network reconstruction. We adapted Fermat's beamformer as a self-calibrating SoS correction for row-column array (RCA) based 3D-tULM and evaluated it in the mouse brain. Fermat's beamformer was formulated as a local coherence optimizer for effective SoS, adapted to orthogonal plane wave compounding (42 angles, 21 per dimension). Experiments were performed in n=5 mice (aged 1 to 7 months) transcranially at 12 MHz, 750 fps. Microbubble tracks were attributed to arterial or venous flow from their along-track acceleration sign, producing separate 3D vascular maps. SoS correction increased vessel density by 17±6% and track count by 26±13%, with visibly improved reconstructions in both networks. The higher track count may benefit dynamic measurements such as pulsatility, and results across ages suggest compatibility with longitudinal neuropathology studies.

papers.title: Acoustic Transparency Enables Transcranial Functional Ultrasound Imaging in Mice and Nonhuman Primates
papers.abstract: The skull poses a fundamental barrier to ultrasound-based brain imaging by strongly attenuating and aberrating acoustic waves, preventing functional ultrasound imaging (fUSI) from achieving its broad adaptation and translation. Overcoming this limitation has remained a central challenge for ultrasound neuroimaging. Here, we present an acoustic transparency strategy for transcranial microscale fUSI, based on the hypothesis that the Ca²⁺-chelating agent EDTA can modulate the acoustic properties of the skull. A topical application of a chelating agent (EDTA) restores trans-skull transmission comparable to that of the free-field level. EDTA treatment increased transcranial power Doppler signal by 10-fold in mice, reaching a level comparable to craniotomy (95.8 ± 3.5%); and we further demonstrated that acoustic transparency enhanced transcranial fUSI in nonhuman primate, achieving over 6-fold signal increase. In summary, EDTA-mediated acoustic transparency can safely and effectively enable transcranial fUSI without microbubbles, addressing a fundamental barrier to the translation and broad application of fUSI.

papers.title: Transcranial Ultrasound Aberration Correction via Cascaded Residual Networks and Online Differentiable Beamforming
papers.abstract: Transcranial ultrasound localization microscopy (tULM) suffers from skull-induced phase aberrations. Standard deep learning speed-of-sound (SoS) predictions lack patient generalization. We propose DART-net, a two-stage framework combining offline SoS estimation with online residual fine-tuning via differentiable beamforming (DB). Stage 1 uses a Res-UNet to estimate a baseline SoS from 11-angle IQ data. Stage 2 uses an identical Res-UNet to predict SoS residuals. During test-time optimization, the combined SoS drives DB to recalculate wavefronts. An unsupervised loss of multi-angle coherence and phase error backpropagates through DB to dynamically fine-tune Stage 2, iteratively aligning phases. Compared to SVD and AutoSoS baselines, DART-net achieved highest precision, reducing axial and lateral localization errors to 0.113λ and 0.209λ. With a 1.5301λ FWHM and 31.60 dB contrast ratio, it suppresses skull artifacts, enabling robust, high-fidelity phase correction for tULM.

papers.title: Arbitrary Wave Compounding for Contrast-Free 3D Transcranial Functional Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: This work presents a wavefront-agnostic beamforming approach for contrast-free 3D transcranial functional ultrasound imaging, addressing skull-induced aberration and signal loss. A simulation-informed pipeline was developed to reconstruct arbitrary transmit wavefronts and evaluated in vivo in mice without contrast agents or surgery. A conventional 5-angle plane wave compounding sequence was compared to a 25-angle partial focusing strategy optimized for transcranial imaging, both operating at 500 volumes/s. Power Doppler signals were extracted using SVD filtering and temporal integration. Partial focusing achieved over 9 dB improvement in vascular contrast-to-noise ratio, demonstrating that arbitrary wave compounding enables high-frame-rate, contrast-free functional imaging through the intact skull.

papers.title: Single-Capillary-Reporters in Whole-Brain 3D ULM
papers.abstract: This work benchmarks single-capillary-reporter (SCaRe) classifiers for capillary-resolved 3D ultrasound localization microscopy without in vivo ground truth. Four methods (velocity threshold, fractional-region split, Gaussian HMM, and quadratic U-fit) were evaluated on ~933k microbubble tracks using a physiology-informed scoring framework incorporating velocity profile shape, transit-time plausibility, and smoothness. Classifiers were optimized via F1 score and compared on detection performance and estimated transit times. Rankings depended on scoring strictness: fractional-region split performed best under strict criteria, while velocity threshold dominated under loose criteria, driven by sensitivity to U-shape features. Estimated capillary transit times (5–30 ms) were substantially shorter than prior expectations, likely reflecting acquisition limits. The framework provides guidance for selecting SCaRe classifiers in ULM studies.

papers.title: Can Sure Detect stroke?
papers.abstract: Super-resolution ultrasound imaging using erythrocytes (SURE) enables contrast-free visualization of the microvasculature, but its ability to detect ischemic stroke remains unclear. In this study, SURE was applied in a rat model of microsphere-induced stroke to assess its sensitivity to perfusion changes. SURE imaging performed before and during stroke revealed a clear reduction in blood flow within the affected hemisphere using only 5 s of data. A marked decrease in vessel visibility was observed, and intensity profiles confirmed attenuation or loss of peaks corresponding to at least 5 perfused vessels. These results demonstrate that SURE can detect and localize ischemic regions, highlighting its potential as a rapid, non-contrast imaging tool for stroke detection and monitoring in vivo

sessions.title: MIS: Microvascular & Functional Imaging

papers.title: Fast End-to-End Contrast-Free Microvessel Imaging Using Deep Learning
papers.abstract: Ultrasound microvessel (MV) imaging enables visualization of tissue microvasculature and extraction of quantitative biomarkers. Conventional pipelines rely on computationally intensive steps such as SVD-based clutter filtering, background suppression, and vessel enhancement, requiring manual tuning and limiting real-time use. We propose a fully data-driven end-to-end framework for fast contrast-free MV reconstruction from high-framerate IQ data. The method introduces a two-stage pipeline. In Stage 1, pixel-wise clutter removal and power Doppler estimation use a Casorati representation with a 1D encoder–decoder network with spatial-channel attention, residual connections, and wavelet-enhanced loss, compressing 1680 frames into a compact latent space while preserving blood flow signals. In Stage 2, a 2D U-Net refines vessel continuity and suppresses noise, producing MV images without handcrafted steps. Evaluated on 324 subjects (29 test), the method achieves Dice 0.900 ± 0.037, PCC 0.956 ± 0.015, and SSIM 0.802 ± 0.031. It reduces computational cost by ~900× compared to conventional pipelines while maintaining strong fidelity and enabling near real-time reconstruction.

papers.title: Short-Ensemble Functional Ultrasound (fUS) Imaging with Deep Interpolation
papers.abstract: Functional ultrasound (fUS) imaging is limited by Doppler sensitivity, requiring large ultrafast ensembles to detect subtle hemodynamic changes and constraining temporal resolution. We propose a deep learning–based denoising framework to enable reliable power Doppler (PD) imaging from substantially shorter ensembles. The method employs a deep interpolation network trained via consistency with noisy references, eliminating the need for noise-free ground truth. Experiments were performed in awake mice under single-whisker stimulation (30 s ON/30 s OFF) using a Verasonics NXT system (15.625 MHz, 5-angle compounding, 1000 Hz frame rate, 250-frame ensembles). The proposed approach enables robust functional activation detection using only 30-frame ensembles, approaching the performance of standard 250-frame acquisitions. Correlation maps show improved activation localization in the contralateral SSp. Temporal traces exhibit reduced noise and more distinct stimulus-locked responses, indicating enhanced Doppler sensitivity. These results demonstrate that the method supports high-sensitivity fUS imaging with reduced ensemble size and improved temporal resolution.

papers.title: Depth-Varying Deconvolution for Uniform Volumetric Micro-Angiography of Adult Zebrafish
papers.abstract: Densely sampled ultrafast, high-frequency ultrasound enables volumetric micro-Doppler imaging (μPDI) with remarkable detail, offering strong potential for contrast-free micro-angiography in developing adult zebrafish. However, accurately resolving fine vascular structures requires addressing the inherent anisotropy of μPDI volumes, which degrades spatial fidelity. We propose a depth-varying anisotropic compensation framework via deconvolution using a 3D UNET model. Validation was conducted on the diameter of the registered vessel obtained from the other orthogonal scanning direction. We found that deconvolution were generally achieves uniform and natural vessel distribution with increasing diameter as deeper region, validated via the orthogonal scan direction. Without assuming uniform PSF, our depth-varying deconvolution achieves larger uniform volume particularly near the probe. The proposed method enhances uniformity, facilitating detailed studies of vascular development of the adult zeberafish.

papers.title: An Anatomically Realistic Simulation Framework for Cerebral Blood Flow Imaging Based on Ultrasound Localization Microscopy Data
papers.abstract: Accuracy of Cerebral blood flow (CBV) imaging using ultrafast Doppler (uDoppler) is limited by spatio-temporal resolution and skull-induced attenuation and aberration. Multiple strategies have been proposed, however, their systematic evaluation requires realistic controllable ground truth data. We propose an anatomically realistic simulation framework for uDoppler CBV imaging. The approach combines experimental Ultrasound Localization Microscopy (ULM) data with numerical simulation. Experimental acquisitions of uDoppler and ULM were performed on a wild type mouse. Assuming microbubbles flow like red blood cells (RBC), ULM tracks were used to estimate RBC positions over time and accumulated to obtain a blood-like density. The uDoppler acquisition at these RBC positions was simulated in 2D using k-Wave, including brain tissue properties. We found qualitative agreement between the experimental and simulated images. Comparison of the experimental and simulated uDoppler images via correlation indicate strong structural agreement, with differences mainly in intensity and noise, supporting the framework’s feasibility for physically accurate simulations.

papers.title: Nanobubble-Enhanced in Vivo Vascular Imaging Within a Single Breathing Cycle Using High-Frame-Rate Plane-Wave Imaging
papers.abstract: Microbubble-based super-resolution ultrasound imaging typically requires minutes-long acquisitions for localization and tracking of sparse individual bubbles. In contrast, the much higher achievable concentrations of nanobubbles (NBs) enable ensemble-based vascular imaging from much shorter data segments. This work investigated whether NB-enhanced in vivo vascular imaging could be achieved from high-frame-rate single-pulse plane-wave imaging (PWI) data acquired within individual breathing cycles. NBs were injected in mice for renal imaging on the Vevo F2 system using a customized PWI sequence. NB-enhanced signals were extracted per breathing cycle using singular value decomposition, followed by power Doppler reconstruction. Peak-density imaging was generated by accumulating detected NB signal peaks. Before NB injection, SVD-based power Doppler from a 0.64 s segment showed limited vascular visibility. After NB injection, power Doppler from 0.6 s revealed richer vasculature, while peak-density imaging from a 0.43 s segment resolved vessels down to ~67 μm versus ~140 μm for matched power Doppler. These results support NB-enhanced vascular imaging within a single breathing cycle.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal Signal Separation Using eigen-Image changepoint Detection for Dual Mode Molecular and Vascular Imaging in Deep Tissue
papers.abstract: This study introduces Eigen-CPD which is an automated spatiotemporal signal separation method designed for dual-mode molecular and vascular imaging in deep tissue. By combining SVD-based decomposition with spatial statistics and changepoint detection, the method partitions data into tissue clutter, gas vesicle (GV) signals, and red blood cell (RBC) flow. Each eigen-image is evaluated using a composite pattern score that captures sparsity, gradient, and structural features, enabling robust subspace classification even in low SNR tumor environments. The approach was validated in a mouse tumor model using acoustically collapsible GVs and high-frequency ultrasound imaging. Compared to conventional covariance-based SVD, Eigen-CPD reduced RBC interference and improved GV signal isolation, leading to a higher GV-to-RBC signal ratio. Extracted subspaces were used to generate super-resolved GV localization and microvascular maps, which were co-registered to reconstruct a 3D representation of the tumor microenvironment.

sessions.title: MCA: Molecular imaging and cancer therapy monitoring

papers.title: Acoustically Switchable Cellular Tags for T Cell Therapy Monitoring
papers.abstract: Non-invasive localization of therapeutic T cells after adoptive transfer remains a major challenge in cancer immunotherapy. Existing imaging modalities are limited by poor spatiotemporal resolution, ionizing radiation, or lack of accessibility. Here, we present acoustically switchable cellular tags based on phase-change perfluorocarbon nanodroplets (PFCnDs) for ultrasound-based T cell tracking. PFCnDs were functionalized with a maleimide-modified lipid shell and covalently conjugated to surface thiols on T cells, enabling stable labeling while preserving acoustic responsiveness. Upon pulsed focused ultrasound (FUS) exposure, cell-bound PFCnDs underwent acoustic droplet vaporization (ADV), generating localized contrast for contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) imaging. The resulting signal is titrated with PFCnD loading and correlated with cell numbers, supporting estimation of labeled cell concentration at the target site. In murine tissue, labeled T cells were distinguished from the background tissue. These results establish acoustically switchable cellular tags for image-guided and longitudinal monitoring of adoptively transferred T cells.

papers.title: Dual-Frequency Amplitude Modulation for High-Contrast Ultrasound Imaging of Acoustic Bacteria
papers.abstract: Acoustic reporter genes (ARGs) encoding gas vesicles (GVs) have been developed and expressed in bacteria, i.e., acoustic bacteria, enabling ultrasound visualization of cells in vivo. However, their weak scattering signals are easily obscured by tissue echoes, resulting in limited imaging contrast. Existing imaging strategies can improve contrast but often sacrifice imaging field of view or frame rate, or require more complex transmission schemes. To address this limitation, we developed a dual-frequency amplitude modulation (dAM) method to enhance acoustic bacteria image quality without increasing transmission complexity.

papers.title: Fibrin-Targeted Contrast Imaging: Peptide-Loaded Microbubbles Yields Higher Efficacy Than tPA-Loaded Microbubbles
papers.abstract: Early detection of clots can greatly improve treatment outcomes. Ultrasound as the current workhorse for clot detection struggle at times with poor clot echogenicity or comorbidities that impede imaging. Potential targeting strategies using PPACK inhibited tPA (itPA) or peptide (e.g. CREKA) have distinct advantages in enabling a targeted CEUS solution yet a comparison in performance between these strategies has not been made. Here, a systematic comparison is made between itPA and a peptide representative. Despite a general increase in microbubble (MB) retention for both ligands, we observed that retention performance of itPA-MBs on fibrin decreased in the presence of plasminogen when compared to the peptide-MB alternative. This observation suggests that the peptide strategy is more suitable for fibrin-targeted contrast while itPA-MB targeting was sensitive to plasminogen.

papers.title: Monitoring Response of Pancreatic Cancer Patients Undergoing Chemotherapy with Adjuvant Sonoporation Treatment Using Subharmonic-Aided Pressure Estimation (SHAPE) and Shear Wave Elastography (SWE)
papers.abstract: Sonoporation is a novel method that can enhance the therapeutic efficacy of co-administered chemotherapy. A Phase II clinical trial aims to improve standard of care (SoC) chemotherapy treatment of pancreatic cancer by adding sonoporation. As part of this study, subharmonic-aided pressure estimation (SHAPE) was used to acquire intra-tumoral pressure measurements, while shear wave elastography (SWE) was used to evaluate tumor stiffness. The objective of this study was to use SHAPE and SWE after the chemotherapy with sonoporation treatment to evaluate treatment response. Comparison between first and last cycles for responders showed decrease in SHAPE values (indicating a pressure increase; p = 0.11) and SWE increase in tumor stiffness (p = 0.13), while for non-responders showed increase in SHAPE intra-tumoral measurements (indicating a pressure decrease; p = 0.01) and SWE decrease in tumor stiffness (p = 0.01). In conclusion, the results suggest that SHAPE and SWE may be used to indicate chemotherapy of pancreatic cancer responses.

papers.title: Real-Time Ultrasound Molecular Imaging Using Targeted Microbubbles: a New Paradigm for Early Detection and Monitoring of Breast Cancer
papers.abstract: Cancer is highly heterogeneous, yet standard imaging methods such as MRI and PET-CT are limited by cost, radiation exposure, and insufficient resolution to capture tumor dynamics. Ultrasound molecular imaging (UMI) uses targeted microbubbles (MBs) to bind cancer biomarkers, but real-time quantitative detection remains challenging, as existing approaches either destroy MBs, are computationally intensive, or cannot distinguish bound from circulating MBs. This work proposes a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based method for real-time MB detection integrated into an ultrasound system. Data were collected from 36 breast cancer mouse models using targeted (B7-H3, PD-L1) and nontargeted MBs, yielding 114 scans. Microbubble signals were extracted using robust principal component analysis (RPCA), and background noise was reduced through differential targeted enhancement. These served as ground truth to train a lightweight CNN. The pipeline achieves real-time imaging at up to 30 frames/s and shows strong agreement with ground truth (AUC = 0.94, Dice = 0.7). It enables continuous imaging without destroying MBs and shows strong potential for early cancer detection and treatment monitoring.

papers.title: Sonoporation for Augmenting Pancreatic Cancer treatment: a Clinical Trial
papers.abstract: This multi-center, IRB approved, Phase II clinical trial (NCT04821284) enrolled 97 patients with pancreatic cancer.(≥ stage 2) prior to starting their chemotherapy. Neither PFS nor OS curves showed any significant differences between groups with and without sonoporation (p > 0.36), but the median OS for subjects that received Gemcitabine/Nab-Paclitaxel with sonoporation was markedly greater than in the control group (407.5 days vs 234 days, respectively; an improvement of almost 75%). These results are somewhat encouraging and suggest that sonoporation treatment of pancreatic cancer may improve treatment outcomes.

sessions.title: MSR: Dysfunctional subunits

papers.title: Super-Resolution Ultrasound Imaging of Vasa Vasorum in Rabbit Atherosclerotic Plaque Using Adaptive Local SVD-Based Clutter Filtering
papers.abstract: Super-resolution ultrasound (SRU) enables in vivo visualization of microvasculature such as vasa vasorum (VV), an important marker of atherosclerotic plaque (AP) progression and vulnerability. However, imaging VV near large vessels is limited by strong, spatially varying tissue clutter that obscures weak microbubble signals. We propose an adaptive local SVD-based clutter filtering approach with spatially adaptive threshold selection to improve tissue–flow separation. A rabbit AP model was imaged at 8 and 12 weeks using ultrafast plane-wave ultrasound. Local SVD filtering enhanced VV visualization, particularly near the vessel wall. SRU-derived VV density increased significantly from week 8 to week 12 (p = 0.041), consistent with progressive neovascularization. Histological analysis confirmed plaque formation and VV proliferation, and showed strong agreement with SRU measurements (R² = 0.87). These results demonstrate that adaptive local SVD improves VV detection and enables reliable quantitative assessment for SRU-based characterization of AP progression.

papers.title: Fast 3D Ultrasound Localization Microscopy via Projection-Based Processing
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) enables volumetric microvascular imaging and offers improved robustness over 2D ULM by reducing dependence on user-selected imaging planes. However, its intensive computational cost remains a major barrier to real-time and clinical translation. In this work, we propose a projection-based framework for fast 3D ULM reconstruction, among the first to achieve near real-time performance.

papers.title: Ultrasound Localization Microscopy Reveals Pre-Albuminuric Renal Microvascular Alterations in Type 2 Diabetic Kidney Disease
papers.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) requires early detection before irreversible damage to enable timely therapeutic intervention, yet sensitive non-invasive biomarkers remain limited. This study investigates whether renal microvascular alterations precede albuminuria using ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM). Longitudinal imaging was performed in db/db mice and db/m controls at 4, 6, and 8 weeks. Hemodynamic (mean velocity, skewness) and morphological (fractal dimension, tortuosity) metrics were extracted from cortical microvascular maps. Results show that mean velocity was significantly reduced in diabetic mice as early as 4 weeks, preceding the divergence of urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) by two weeks. Skewness differentiated groups at later stages, while structural metrics revealed dynamic vascular remodeling. These findings demonstrate that ULM enables non-invasive detection of early renal microvascular dysfunction prior to albuminuria, supporting its potential as an early imaging biomarker for DKD.

papers.title: Whole-Organ Renal Microcirculation Mapping in Humans
papers.abstract: This work addresses the challenge of imaging the human renal microvasculature, a key marker of kidney disease progression. While Doppler ultrasound lacks sufficient spatial resolution, ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) has enabled microvascular imaging in animal models. However, translation to whole-organ human imaging remains limited by restricted field of view, respiratory motion, and non-standardized microbubble (MB) protocols. Here, we present a platform for high-resolution, whole-organ imaging using 3D ULM. The method combines a custom 1MHz multi-lens probe, a 4D ultrafast imaging sequence, controlled MB injections, and advanced processing, including multi-layer beamforming, motion correction, multi-threshold SVD filtering, and MB tracking. In vivo acquisitions in three volunteers enabled full kidney imaging (150 cm³) and hemodynamic analysis, resolving vessels from arteries to arterioles (153 μm dynamic resolution). Vessel radii ranged from 131±22 μm to 2.85±0.65 mm, with separation of arterial and venous flow. These results demonstrate the potential of 3D ULM with a multi-lens probe as a clinical tool for whole-kidney imaging and renal pathology assessment.

papers.title: Super Resolution Ultrasound Localization Microscopy of Bladder cancer: a Clinical Feasibility Study
papers.abstract: Current clinical imaging techniques lack the sensitivity to reliably detect a pathologically complete response prior to radical cystectomy (RC) in patients, limiting the potential for bladder preservation. Ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) is a super-resolution imaging technique that uses intravascular microbubble contrast agents to break the diffraction limit while maintaining imaging penetration depth. We conducted the first in-human study of ULM that evaluates its safety and feasibility for detecting residual bladder cancer prior to RC. This is a prospective, single-arm pilot study of patients undergoing RC for muscle invasive or high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer.

papers.title: Ultrasound Localization Microscopy (ULM) for Non-Invasive Assessment of Kidney Transplant Rejection in Non-Human Primates
papers.abstract: Kidney xenotransplantation offers a potential solution to the organ shortage, but rejection remains a major barrier. Current noninvasive monitoring detects injury late, and biopsy is invasive. Whether ULM-derived microvascular markers can discriminate rejection in vivo is unknown. Four pig-to-NHP kidney xenografts were imaged at POD1 (baseline) and rejection (POD7–9) after IV Lumason bolus (GE 9L-D, 5.25 MHz). Parallelized writes to a 4-drive NVMe SSD array enabled continuous dual-mode AM/fundamental imaging at 500 Hz across the full bolus, with AM for glomerular signal and co-registered fundamental for motion correction. Glomeruli were identified via HMM and DBSCAN, then binned by cortical depth (0–2, 2–4, 4–6 mm). Longitudinally (N=2), superficial cortex showed perfusion loss at rejection (GPI −47 to −74%; velocity −11 to −46%), and mid cortex showed flow disorganization (tortuosity +14 to +43%). Across all four subjects, superficial GPI and weighted velocity at all depths reached AUC=1.00. Dual-mode continuous ULM detects rejection-associated microvascular changes, supporting noninvasive graft monitoring.

sessions.title: MTH: Blood–Brain Barrier Modulation & Drug Delivery

papers.title: Low-Boiling Perfluorocarbon Mixture Nanodroplets Enable Sub-Focal Blood Brain Barrier Opening with Translational Feasibility in Non-Human Primates
papers.abstract: Focused ultrasound (FUS) blood brain barrier opening (BBBO) with phase change contrast agents can confine bioeffects below the conventional −6 dB focal area, but decafluorobutane droplets require elevated activation pressures. We developed low-boiling octafluoropropane/decafluorobutane mixture nanodroplets to reduce acoustic droplet vaporization pressure while preserving sub-focal BBBO. Mixtures were characterized in vitro using 1 MHz FUS and passive cavitation detection, then evaluated in mice, rats, and nonhuman primates. The mixtures vaporized at significantly lower pressures than decafluorobutane alone. In mice, nanodroplets produced axial BBBO as small as 250 µm, below the theoretical 1 mm −6 dB focal zone. In rats, treatment produced pressure-dependent, sub-focal Evans blue extravasation that corresponded with acoustic emissions and histology. Early primate studies demonstrated safe transcranial BBBO with MRI and PCD-guided pressure escalation. These data support low-boiling mixture nanodroplets for lowering activation pressure while maintaining spatially confined BBBO.

papers.title: FUS-Mediated BBB Opening Preferentially Enhances Delivery Efficiency of Larger Agents
papers.abstract: Focused ultrasound–mediated blood–brain barrier opening (FUS-BBBO) enables delivery of large therapeutics to the brain, but prior single time-point studies paradoxically reported higher delivery of smaller agents, possibly missing dynamic pharmacokinetic effects. We performed longitudinal in vivo pharmacokinetic profiling via cerebral open-flow microperfusion (cOFM) to evaluate size-dependent delivery after FUS-BBBO. Mice underwent implantation of a cOFM cannula and a baseplate enabling reversible coupling of a 1 MHz ring-shaped FUS transducer. Interstitial fluid was collected over 280 min under four conditions: IV 10 or 500 kDa fluorescein-dextran, with or without FUS-BBBO (n = 6 per condition). Two-way ANOVA revealed significant size × FUS interactions for delivery rate, total AUC, and post-peak AUC. Under FUS-BBBO, the 500 kDa tracer showed ~5- to ~18-fold higher delivery than 10 kDa, with a longer apparent half-life (3.8-fold). These findings demonstrate that FUS-BBBO acts as a size-dependent modulator of delivery kinetics, favoring larger macromolecules over the full pharmacokinetic profile, highlighting the value of longitudinal characterization for optimizing FUS-BBBO.

papers.title: Molecular-Level Insight Into the Safety of Blood-Brain Barrier Opening Dependent on Instantaneous Cavitation Intensity
papers.abstract: Different instantaneous cavitation intensity (ICI) levels caused differential neurovascular damage. However, how ICI affects BBBO under same total cavitation dose (TCD) remains unclear. This work aims to build an ultrafast closed loop system for ICI regulation and to study the effect of ICI on BBBO at the molecular level. Mouse right hippocampi were exposed to short pulsed ultrasound. the harmonics per pulse was defined as ICI. An ultra fast controller (<300 μs) adjusted PNP to keep ICI near target (high/medium/low). After RNA extraction and library prep, DESeq2 identified different genes for GO/KEGG analysis. In ultra fast controller, under same TCD, real time PNP adjustment maintained ICIs at target H/M/L levels. GO/KEGG analysis revealed that HICI and MICI triggered strong inflammatory responses (acute inflammation, cell migration, activation), which were greatly reduced in LICI. Pro inflammatory pathways (IL 17, TNF, JAK STAT) were upregulated in HICI/MICI but not in LICI. Heatmaps confirmed upregulation of inflammatory mediators (Cxcl1, Ccl11, Tnf, Sele) by HICI/MICI, while gene expression in LICI resembled controls, showing safe BBBO.

papers.title: Vortex-Focused Ultrasound Enables Precise Control of Endothelial Angiogenesis via Shear-Driven Calcium Signaling
papers.abstract: Angiogenesis is vital for tissue repair, yet current therapies lack spatial precision. To address this, we developed vortex-focused ultrasound (VFUS), which utilizes a spiral wavefront to generate unique rotational torque and shear stress, precisely modulating calcium signaling in endothelial cells. Using a 2-MHz transducer, PIV revealed VFUS generates substantially higher peak shear stress (84.2 vs. FUS: 39.8 mPa) and flow velocity (85.8 vs. 28.4 μm/s). Optimized VFUS (1.25 MPa, 30% duty cycle, 10 s) safely activated calcium ion influx in >80% of HUVECs. Mechanistic assays confirmed this was driven by stretch-sensitive channels, without thermal or cavitation effects. Ultimately, VFUS markedly enhanced angiogenesis, outperforming FUS by upregulating VEGF secretion (3.2-fold vs. 1.3-fold) and increasing tube length (160% vs. 96%). Thus, VFUS emerges as a highly precise, noninvasive tool for vascular regeneration, paving the way for future in vivo ischemic stroke therapies.

papers.title: The Role of Cell Death Morphology in Brain Cancer Treatment Monitoring Using Focused Ultrasound-Enhanced Liquid Biopsy
papers.abstract: Effective noninvasive monitoring of brain cancer treatment with liquid biopsy remains a major challenge due to the blocking of biomarkers by the blood-brain barrier. While combining it with focused ultrasound (FUS) offers a promising approach to enhance biomarker detection, the impact of therapeutics on biomarker release remains poorly understood. In vivo experiments included blood collection before and 24h after FUS sonication, with doxorubicin infusion administered immediately after FUS sonication. Doxorubicin+FUS group had an increase in ctDNA concentration of 2300% while the FUS-only group had a reduction in ctDNA by 26%. Immunofluorescent staining of brain tissue indicated that, compared to the FUS-only group, doxorubicin-only and doxorubicin+FUS groups increased the expression of RIP3 protein by 61% and 5,600%, respectively. We observed that cfDNA increased significantly for groups with overexpression of RIP3 protein, where necroptosis and cell membrane rupture were induced. This was further observed with in vivo experiments, highlighting the impact of therapies on liquid biopsy protocols.

papers.title: Dual-Frequency Bifocal Lens for Multi-Target Ultrasound
papers.abstract: This work presents a dual-frequency bifocal lens system for generating two closely spaced independent focused ultrasound targets for multi-site neuromodulation. Conventional single-frequency multifocal lenses can suffer from mutual interaction between foci, limiting target separation and focal control. To address this, we use spatial orthogonality between two frequency components to improve independence between focal spots. The system combines a dual-frequency focused ultrasound transducer with two concentric elements and an SLA-fabricated bifocal lens. The lens is designed so that the 350 kHz wave preserves the natural transducer focus, while the 700 kHz wave is steered to a second target. Performance was evaluated using 3D k-Wave simulations, and hydrophone-based field mapping is underway. Simulations show two distinct focal targets separated by 3 mm, with intensity between targets reduced to -6.73 dB. Compared with a single-frequency 700 kHz design, the proposed lens provides improved focal confinement and target separability. This platform may enable controlled multi-site ultrasound neuromodulation and studies of distributed neural circuits relevant to therapeutic applications.

sessions.title: MSD: Emerging Ultrasound Platforms

papers.title: * INVITED * Transforming Ultrasound imaging: the Impact of Microelectronics from the 80s to Today
papers.abstract: Medical ultrasound (US) imaging technology is experiencing a new Renaissance, marked by the continuous emergence of innovative methods and instruments. This talk explores the origins of the growing interest in the field from both industry and academia, with particular attention to the close interplay between advances in microelectronics and developments in medical US. The impact of novel microelectronic devices (including AFEs, FPGAs, and GPUs) and computing systems (from personal computers to open scanners) on US technology will be critically assessed. Practical examples will illustrate how key building blocks of US instruments—such as the beamformer—have evolved over the past four decades, enabling real-time imaging at frame rates of several kilohertz. The talk will emphasize the crucial role of adequate hardware in supporting the real-time implementation of of transformative methods, including AI-based approaches. Finally, perspectives on potential future advancements will be discussed, highlighting the expected trajectory of US technology in the coming years.

papers.title: Open-Source Live-Reconfigurable Multi-Mode Wearable Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Wearable ultrasound (WUS) enables continuous physiological monitoring, but most systems use fixed modes or need offline reprogramming, preventing in-session switching between anatomical and flow protocols. We present a software control stack for automated runtime reconfiguration of a 32-channel WUS platform, enabling live multi-modal operation. The stack is evaluated on a probe integrating FPGA, AFE, pulser, and Wi-Fi 6 MCU. Typed hardware models and Hardware Access Layers connect to a session layer that tracks register changes and emits only required writes. Batched RPC commands sync with a separate raw-data streaming path. Modality flows define setup, acquisition, and teardown; a scheduler precomputes block sequences and transitions. Validation uses phantom vascular measurements combining Pulsed-Wave Doppler and A-mode imaging. Two strategies are shown: coarse 4 s Doppler / 4 s A-mode switching, and fine interleaving of 70 Doppler shots with one A-mode shot. A-mode estimates lumen diameter from wall echoes. Mode-switching overhead is 80 ms, enabling time-multiplexed flow and structural measurements in one WUS session.

papers.title: A Programmable Wireless Ultrasound Patch Platform for Sonodynamic Therapy
papers.abstract: We developed a programmable wireless ultrasound patch (WUP) designed as a universal platform for multi-scenario therapy. The platform features a highly integrated, ultra-lightweight (<10 g) architecture comprising a 1.0 MHz PZT-4 transducer and miniaturized control circuitry. This work establishes a wearable paradigm for autonomous and personalized ultrasound therapy.

papers.title: Estimation of Lower Limb Joint Angle and Torque via Wearable Ultra-Low-Power Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Measuring kinematic and kinetic parameters such as joint angles and torques during locomotion is important for the understanding of movement. This study investigates the feasibility of using a wireless ultra-low-power wearable ultrasound probe to make such measurements. We collected US data using a wearable acquisition platform and two 3.8 MHz single-element transducers. The system was strapped to the right shank of one subject and transducers were placed on the tibialis anterior and gastrocnemius muscles. US signals were recorded at a frame rate of 15 Hz per transducer while the subject walked on an instrumented treadmill at speeds ranging from 0.68 to 1.68 m/s. Ground truth ankle angle and torque were recorded with a marker-based motion capture system. A 2D convolutional neural network (CNN) was then used to estimate the ankle angle and torque from sliding windows of M-mode images. The CNN achieved mean absolute errors of 2.99o and 0.19 Nm/kg for the ankle angle and normalized ankle torque, respectively. The low errors suggest that wearable US sensors can potentially measure these quantities in real-world environments without specialized motion capture systems.

papers.title: A Wearable Modular Ultrasound and Photoacoustic Platform for Longitudinal Neonatal Brain Monitoring in Intensive Care
papers.abstract: In neonatal intensive care, point-of-care ultrasound plays an important role in identifying life-threatening neurological emergencies. In this work, we propose wearable ultrasound and photoacoustic modules for longitudinal monitoring of the neonatal brain. We demonstrate a proof-of-concept prototype for optically-tracked synthesis of disjoint modular aperture that consists of acoustic/optical pulse-echo events. A custom module was designed using a 1.2-MHz PVDF receive element and a 1.35MHz ceramic piezoelectric transmit element, optically trackable using infrared LEDs. Ultrasound and photoacoustic imaging feasibility was shown through linear scans of a graphite rod phantom and volumetric imaging of a neonatal head phantom with metal rod inclusion. We aim to further develop our modular ultrasound and photoacoustic framework to expand applicability across a broad range of clinical settings.

sessions.title: THF: Front-end Electronics and Ultrasound Systems

papers.title: First-Silicon Validation of Temporal Compressed Sensing for Ultrasound RF Acquisition Using a Switched-Capacitor SAR ADC
papers.abstract: Portable, wearable, and 3D ultrasound systems require high-channel-count RF acquisition with lower power, wiring, and data throughput. Compressed sensing can reduce data rate, but ultrasound RF data are not sparse in time and hardware validation remains limited. This work demonstrates a first-silicon TSMC 65 nm ASIC for temporal compressed ultrasound acquisition. The prototype uses a switched-capacitor two-stage SAR ADC with inter-stage gain of 16 and 6+8-bit conversion with 2-bit redundancy. The RF input is multiplied by a programmable PRBS and accumulated before digitization. With a 10 MS/s ADC rate, the effective rates are 10, 5, and 2.5 MS/s for 1×, 2×, and 4× modes, with compressed modes below Nyquist. Field II wire-phantom RF data from a 64-element, 2 MHz probe were applied through an AWG. ASIC outputs were reconstructed offline using a probe-dependent RF model and elastic net recovery before plane-wave compounding. Beamformed images show that the main wire targets remain visible at 2× and 4× compression. Higher compression increases noise and reduces sharpness, but the results validate temporal CS acquisition in silicon.

papers.title: Integrated 2D PMUT-ASIC Module for Programmable Air-Coupled Ultrasonic Sensing
papers.abstract: This work presents a compact integrated module for air-coupled ultrasonic sensing based on a 600 kHz 5×5 PZT PMUT array stacked on a dedicated multichannel front-end ASIC in an open-cavity package. The system targets applications such as human–machine interfaces and robotics, where discrete ultrasonic implementations are limited by size, power consumption, and cost. Each PMUT element consists of a single 420 µm membrane connected to one ASIC transceiver. The ASIC integrates 25 V pulsers with damping for ringdown reduction, TX/RX switches, LNAs, programmable TX delays for 2D beamforming, and flexible RX summation or multiplexing into five acquisition chains. Each chain includes PGA with TGC, filtering, 10-bit ADCs up to 6 MS/s, on-chip memory, and QSPI communication. Prototypes were packaged, mounted on custom boards, and controlled through an STM32 board with custom firmware and GUI. Electrical tests confirmed correct ASIC operation, while air pitch-catch measurements at 5 cm showed clear ultrasonic pulses at the expected time-of-flight. The module demonstrates end-to-end PMUT–ASIC operation and provides a scalable platform for compact 2D air-coupled ultrasonic sensing.

papers.title: EchoButton - a Miniature Wireless Ultrasound System with Pulse-Echo and Doppler Capability for Wearables and Industrial Monitoring
papers.abstract: Button is a single-channel, button-size wireless ultrasound platform for wearable and industrial monitoring applications requiring small, lightweight, low-power, low-cost, and easily deployable ultrasonic devices. The self-contained device measures 22 mm in diameter and 8 mm in height, with an additional 2 mm for the antenna, and weighs 6 g including the housing and CR2032 battery. It integrates a top electronics PCB, middle coin cell, and bottom in-house fabricated polymer-based capacitive micromachined ultrasonic transducer. The electronics provide up to 30 V excitation, 18 dB receive amplification, 12-bit digitization, and Bluetooth communication. The polyCMUT is rapidly customizable and currently offers a 0.5 mm profile, 1.8 MHz center frequency, and 120% fractional bandwidth. Hardware-separated transmit and receive elements reduce switching components and artifacts while improving signal integrity. Experiments demonstrated pulse-echo detection from an aluminum reflector in isopropyl alcohol and Doppler flow measurement with a clear spectrogram. The device consumed 21 mW at 120 Hz, enabling over 30 h of CR2032 operation.

papers.title: A CMUT-Based Ultrasound Receiver Front-End with Triple-Mixer Architecture for Real-Time Harmonic Envelope Extraction
papers.abstract: Focused ultrasound (FUS) combined with microbubbles (MBs) offers a non-invasive alternative for targeted drug delivery by opening the blood–brain barrier, yet its safety depends on precise cavitation control to prevent tissue damage from bubble collapse. To address this, we propose a CMUT-based receiver architecture that monitors MB activity by extracting f0, 1.5f0, and 3f0 envelopes through a TIA-PGA front-end and a triple-mixer stage. A single master clock synthesizes three synchronous reference signals to ensure phase-coherent detection, where f0 tracks kinetic behavior and the higher harmonics indicate the cavitation regime. Fabricated in 180-nm BCDMOS, the receiver occupies a compact 960 μm × 90 μm per channel and consumes 10.3 mW at 1.8 V. The TIA achieves a gain of 91–114 dBΩ over a 3–14 MHz bandwidth with an input-referred noise of 4.7 pA/√Hz. System verification using emulated cavitation spectra demonstrates that while 1.5f0 levels remain negligible during stable cavitation, a significant amplitude surge occurs during the pre-collapse stage, confirming the system's potential for real-time pre-collapse detection in Broadband Bubble Oscillation environments

papers.title: A Low-Noise Ultrasound Receiver with Bandpass Response Matched to PMUT Transducers for Biomedical Imaging Applications
papers.abstract: Ultrasound biomedical imaging requires low-noise receiver (RX) to achieve wider dynamic range. Conventional RXs adopt a wideband low-noise amplifier (LNA) followed by a bandpass filter. As noise is amplified by LNA, power-consuming high-order bandpass filter is required for noise rejection. The bandpass nature of PMUT is not yet fully exploited to optimize RX performance. This paper presents a RX LNA with bandpass response which can be tuned to matched with PMUT for optimum integrated noise with low power consumption.

papers.title: Low-Cost Wearable Ultrasound Development Platform - Single Plane Wave Multiplexed Acquisition System
papers.abstract: Wearable ultrasound patches can measure signals like fetal heart rate, bladder volume, and continuous blood pressure, often needing less image quality by leveraging AI. This work presents SIGMA (Single plane wave multiplexed acquisition system), a low-cost portable platform: a 28 g skin-adherable probe head connects via a flexible cable to a readout unit for raw RF capture. It achieved 0.35 mm axial/1.1 mm lateral resolution at 4 cm, up to 150 Hz, and costs <€1000 (excluding transducer/laptop).

sessions.title: ANC: Acoustics on Non-conventional Substrates

papers.title: * INVITED * The Golden Age of Acoustic Resonators & Filters
papers.abstract: Early on, filters in RF systems were large and bulky. Even with the SAW filter in the early 1990s and FBAR in 2000, the potential seemed small. This changed dramatically starting in 2007 with the launch of Smartphones and the subsequent explosion of small high-quality filters. One of the most expensive components in Smartphones are the 10+ RF Radio Front End modules. The most expensive components inside these modules are the 3 to 50 filters collectively (per module). Filters define the cost. Filters define the size. And Filters define the performance of these modules. All 3 of these orthogonal demands from the customer can be solved with better filters. Currently, there are two competing technologies for high performance filters: Low band modules are dominated by TCSAWs, In the mid band (1.4 to 2.7 GHz), both Guided Wave Surface Acoustic Wave Devices and Free-Standing Bulk-Wave Devices compete. The ‘new frontier’ for acoustic filters are now radio bands above 4 GHz. Two new technologies are emerging; XBAR and RSBARs. Filters are also becoming commoditized Navigating our way through both the challenges of innovation and the horrors of commoditization will be the theme of my talk

papers.title: High Electromechanical Coupling SAW Resonators Based on Al0.6Sc0.4N-on-Diamond
papers.abstract: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators are critical for compact RF front-end filters, where strong electromechanical coupling is needed for wide-bandwidth operation. AlScN-on-diamond is a promising platform because diamond’s high acoustic velocity and elastic modulus support high-frequency Sezawa modes with larger coupling than Rayleigh modes, although diamond roughness and highly-oriented AlScN film growth remain key challenges. Here, we demonstrate a 4.9 GHz Al₀.₆Sc₀.₄N-on-diamond SAW resonator with 8.42% electromechanical coupling. Resonators with 1.38 μm wavelength were fabricated using e-beam lithography and Al liftoff. Measurements showed Rayleigh and Sezawa resonances at 3.3 and 4.9 GHz, with kₜ² values of 1.53% and 8.42%, respectively. MBVD fitting confirmed strong Sezawa coupling with extracted kₜ² of 7.46%. This work achieves Qp = 367 and the highest reported kₜ² among comparable Sezawa mode AlScN SAW resonators on diamond and SiC, highlighting its potential for frequency-scaled RF communication filters.

papers.title: Design of Near-Zero TCF SAW Filters Based on LiTaO₃/SiO₂/Si Substrate
papers.abstract: SAW filters play an essential role in radio-frequency (RF) front-ends for frequency selection and interference suppression. With the development of mobile communication technology, frequency spectrum are becoming increasingly crowded, requiring filters to have steep roll-off and small temperature coefficient of frequency (TCF). Traditional TCF optimization for resonators is typically restricted to a single frequency point, which only allows for the optimization of either the upper or lower passband edge of a filter. This study introduces in-plane rotation as a novel design dimension to simultaneously minimize the TCF at both passband edges. By precisely tuning the in-plane orientations of the series and parallel resonators, near-zero TCF is achieved at the anti-resonance and resonance frequencies, respectively, ultimately enabling simultaneous TCF optimization across both edges of the passband.

papers.title: IDT-Less Transversal SAW Filter Using Solid Flat Electrode on Periodically Polarization Inverted ScAlN Structure
papers.abstract: By utilizing an in-plane periodically polarization inverted ScAlN structure on a sapphire substrate and replacing conventional IDTs with a solid flat electrode (Au), this study demonstrates an IDT-less transversal SAW filter that addresses the low power handling capability caused by narrow IDT pitch in high frequency applications. The Sc0.4Al0.6N layer was grown on a Pt/sapphire substrate, and polarization inversion was achieved through DC bias application using temporary IDEs which were subsequently removed by chemical etching. FEM simulations confirmed that the proposed structure excites Rayleigh SAW with resonant frequencies nearly identical to conventional devices, while experimental impedance characteristics revealed a maximum K2 of 7.0%. The transversal type SAW filter design successfully demonstrated SAW generation and detection with a low insertion loss of -10.7 dB, suggesting that this structure improves device reliability since only a DC electric field is applied to the functional layout, thereby mitigating the thermal failure typically associated with RF application on fine IDT electrodes.

papers.title: Resilience of Langasite SAWRs in High Temperature Nuclear Reactor Environments
papers.abstract: High-temperature (HT) small modular nuclear reactors (SMRs) are gaining considerable interest due to their high thermal-to-electrical conversion efficiencies and operational flexibility for rapid deployments. Since these reactors function at temperatures > 300°C with intense core-level neutron fluxes > 10¹² n/cm²·s, new advanced sensors are needed for real-time monitoring of in-core operations. In this work, we investigated the resilience of seven one-port langasite (LGS)-based surface acoustic wave resonator (SAWR) devices with Pt/Ni and Pt/Al₂O₃ electrodes that were subjected to both intense nuclear irradiation and HT within a research-grade nuclear reactor over a five-day test period. After an initial stabilization period between Day 1 (pre-irradiation) and Day 2 (post-exposure), all SAWR devices produced stable S₁₁ responses with respect to their resonant frequencies (± 1 kHz for Pt/Al₂O₃ devices), with virtually no changes in peak amplitude and baseline responses. These results highlight the excellent resilience and reproducibility of the LGS SAWR devices to intense reactor powers and HT conditions present in SMRs.

sessions.title: NMC: Material & Defect Characterization

papers.title: Quantitative Characterisation of Defects in Pipes Using Guided Wave Testing with Geometrical Full Waveform Inversion
papers.abstract: Guided wave testing is widely used for long-range pipeline inspection, enabling detection and localisation of defects over tens of metres from a single measurement location. However, accurate geometric characterisation remains limited, as reflection amplitude alone cannot reliably distinguish between defects with different morphologies and structural implications. This work proposes, for the first time, a Geometrical Full Waveform Inversion (GFWI) framework for guided wave inspection, exploiting the full information content of the measured wavefield. A finite element model of the pipe is iteratively fitted to observations using an adjoint-state optimisation scheme, updating nodal geometry to reconstruct defect profiles. Validation using simulated and experimental corrosion-like defects demonstrates quantitative reconstruction with depth errors below 10% of wall thickness. The results establish a practical route to recovering wall thickness and defect shape from standard guided wave measurements, providing a significant advance in pipeline integrity assessment.

papers.title: High-Resolution Acoustic Metal Loss Mapping for Pipelines
papers.abstract: Quantifying remaining wall thickness is essential for pipeline integrity. Amplitude-only or single-ray time-of-flight measurements are often unreliable when corrosion and pitting create irregular surfaces and strong diffuse scattering. Phased-array in-line inspection yields dense data from rough inner and outer boundaries, but converting those responses into quantitative spatial metal-loss maps remains challenging. Wall loss is estimated in two stages: interface candidates from Total Focusing Method (TFM) images constrained by known nominal thickness, then a global cross-sectional wall model with a fine spline surface for local departures. Normal separation between the fitted surfaces defines metal-loss relative to the reference wall. Normal-incidence plane-wave data were acquired in a water-immersed 16 in. pipe (9.52 mm wall) with a 256-element array; inner and outer laser scans provide independent comparison. Results compare photography, laser metal loss, acoustic intensity, and acoustic metal-loss maps for outer-wall corrosion/pitting and inner-wall corrosion, with peak metal loss agreeing closely with reference specifications and laser mesh data (~0.5 mm sampling).

papers.title: In Situ Full-Lifespan Fatigue Characterization of 316L Stainless Steel Using Nonlinear Ultrasonic Adaptive Weighted Spectral Integral
papers.abstract: Accurate characterization of fatigue damage from early microstructural evolution to macroscopic crack initiation remains challenging for structural health monitoring. This study proposes an in situ nonlinear ultrasonic framework for full-lifespan fatigue characterization of 316L stainless steel under asymmetric cyclic loading. A Rayleigh wave and Digital Image Correlation monitoring system is combined with an Adaptive Weighted Spectral Integral (AWSI), which uses dynamic moving thresholds and discrete confidence weighting to quantify broadband nonlinear spectral features while reducing dependence on discrete peak amplitudes. Experiments show that the AWSI captures multi-stage fatigue evolution. Under the high-stress condition, it exhibits an abrupt increase at about 8,000 cycles, indicating the onset of irreversible microstructural evolution, followed by changes associated with damage localization and crack initiation. Under the lower-stress run-out condition, the index remains comparatively stable. The results demonstrate that broadband spectral integration provides a robust single-metric approach for in situ fatigue assessment across different damage stages.

papers.title: Defect-Driven Acoustoelastic Amplification in Two-Dimensional Periodic Structures for Stress Sensing
papers.abstract: High-sensitivity stress sensing in two-dimensional periodic structures requires accurate characterization of prestress-dependent dispersion behavior. This study develops an acoustoelastic framework combining nonlinear hyperelasticity, the semi-analytical finite element method, and Floquet–Bloch periodic conditions. Spatially nonuniform initial stress and deformation fields are incorporated into the incremental elastic coefficients to evaluate dispersion curves under prestress. A smooth circular-hole periodic structure is used as the reference configuration, while localized notches are introduced to construct defect-engineered configurations. Results show that uniaxial prestress causes clearer branch separation and local dispersion reconstruction, whereas biaxial prestress mainly produces systematic frequency shifts while largely preserving in-plane symmetry. The notch features intensify local stress concentration and increase the prestress sensitivity of selected dispersion branches. These results demonstrate that controlled geometric defects can enhance the acoustoelastic response of periodic structures for ultrasonic stress sensing.

papers.title: Non-Destructive Ultrasonic Estimation of Ice Crystal Orientation Fabric: Multi-Frequency Experimental Validation and Failure Mode Characterisation
papers.abstract: Pulse-echo reflection ultrasound provides a non-destructive route to estimating crystal orientation fabric (COF) in glacial ice, which controls ice-sheet mechanical anisotropy. Five laboratory-grown ice disk specimens were scanned at 1, 2.5, and 5 MHz over 180 azimuthal positions. A second-order harmonic model was fitted to the azimuthal P-wave velocity to recover the predominant crystal orientation. Three failure modes are identified and characterised: weak fabric (FSR < 0.5), grain-boundary scattering at high frequency in coarse specimens, and systematic coordinate-frame registration offset. A combined criterion of FSR >= 0.5 and inter-frequency azimuth consistency < 10 degrees correctly classifies all five specimens. For accepted specimens, orientation errors range from 2.9 to 14 degrees, with the best results approaching the theoretical Cramér-Rao lower bound of 1.7-2.2 degrees.

papers.title: Exploration of Commercially Available Medical Adhesives As Acoustic Coupling Materials for Wearable Ultrasound Applications
papers.abstract: This study evaluates commercially available medical adhesives as acoustic coupling materials for wearable ultrasound devices, aiming to find alternatives to conventional gels that dehydrate quickly and lack long-term usability. Seventeen materials were tested for acoustic transmission efficiency between 5 and 12 MHz, identifying four top candidates with over 70% efficiency and double-sided adhesion, which were further assessed in phantom and human studies alongside standard ultrasound gel. Results showed these materials, particularly AG625 and MED 6513SI, provided high transmission efficiency and improved wear comfort, indicating their potential as practical, biocompatible, and medical-grade alternatives for continuous wearable ultrasound applications .

sessions.title: SPT: Ultrasound Neural Stimulation and Guidance - From Mechanisms to Applications

papers.topicName: Spotlight Session: Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Devices & Applications
papers.title: * INVITED * Neuroplasticity in Human Brain Circuits Following Low Intensity Ultrasound Neuromodulation
papers.abstract: This talk will present recent evidence demonstrating that Transcranial Focused Ultrasound Stimulation (TUS) can induce transient, targeted neuroplastic changes in the human brain, with implications for both mechanistic research and therapeutic development. I will highlight TUS’s precision in targeting deep brain structures, its value in probing neural circuits underlying decision making and learning, and its emerging clinical potential in psychiatric disorders where these neural signals are dysfunctional. Drawing on recent human studies; I will present evidence of TUS’s effects on task-related neural changes, behaviour and symptoms demonstrating its promise as a transformative neuromodulation tool.

papers.topicName: Spotlight Session: Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Devices & Applications
papers.title: * INVITED * Focused Ultrasound for Neurological Disorders: From Incisionless Surgery to Neuromodulation
papers.abstract: Focused ultrasound (FUS) is transforming the treatment of neurological disorders by enabling precise, noninvasive targeting of deep brain structures without incisions, implanted devices, or radiation. Now the most commonly performed surgical treatment for medication-refractory essential tremor, FUS has demonstrated strong clinical success in movement disorders, including Parkinson disease. This presentation reviews current applications of FUS ablation, patient selection, outcomes, and safety strategies. It also explores emerging uses of blood-brain barrier opening for biomarker discovery, liquid biopsy, and targeted drug delivery. Advances in neuromodulation, histotripsy, and other ultrasound technologies highlight the expanding potential of incisionless neurosurgery.

papers.topicName: Spotlight Session: Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Devices & Applications
papers.title: A Validated tFUS Neuronavigation Platform for Deep-Brain Modulation in Behaving Non-Human Primates
papers.abstract: We combined acoustic modeling with neuronavigation to significantly improve certainty of brain target engagement during neuromodulation studies performed in awake and behaving non-human primates. We tested this system in 2-animals for 23 sessions per animal.

papers.topicName: Spotlight Session: Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Devices & Applications
papers.title: TRPV4-F617L As an Ultrasound-Sensitive Actuator for in Vivo Sonogenetic Neuromodulation
papers.abstract: This study characterizes TRPV4-F617L as an ultrasound-sensitive actuator for in vivo sonogenetic neuromodulation. AAV vectors encoding TRPV4-WT, TRPV4-F617L, or control were injected into the left striatum of mice, followed by repeated transcranial focused ultrasound stimulation through a wearable device. Rotational behavior and GCaMP6s fiber photometry were recorded simultaneously, and post-stimulation histology was used to assess Fos induction and tissue safety. At 1.47 MPa and 40% duty cycle, tFUS induced significant contralateral rotation and increased striatal calcium activity in TRPV4-F617L mice, while TRPV4-WT and control groups showed no significant motor responses. Fos mRNA expression was increased in the stimulated TRPV4-F617L-expressing striatum, and safety staining showed no significant tissue damage. These results support TRPV4-F617L as a parameter-dependent actuator for focused-ultrasound-based neuromodulation in vivo.

sessions.title: MEL: Cardiac and Vascular Elastography

papers.title: Integrated in vitro and in silico Modeling of Cardiac Natural Shear Wave elastography: Impact of Excitation Properties on Shear Wave Propagation
papers.abstract: Left ventricular (LV) myocardial stiffness is elevated in many cardiac diseases. Natural shear wave (SW) elastography offers a non-invasive approach for stiffness assessment by tracking SWs generated by intrinsic cardiac events, such as mitral valve closure. However, the mechanisms governing natural SW excitation and propagation remain incompletely understood. Computational models are powerful tools for studying SW physics and have been applied to acoustic-radiation-force elastography, but translation to natural cardiac SW elastography is limited by the difficulty of characterizing valve-closure excitation. To address this gap, we combined in vitro LV phantom experiments with matched in silico finite-element models to investigate how excitation-force magnitude and orientation affect SW speed and frequency content. By reproducing experimentally observed SW propagation under controlled excitation conditions, this framework is a first step toward a simple yet high-fidelity valve-closure model for realistic natural SW generation. Future work will extend the approach to more realistic myocardial material behavior and anatomies representative of both sexes and broader age groups.

papers.title: New Biomarkers for Myocardial Viscoelasticity Evaluation of Hemodialysis Patients Based on Natural Mechanical Waves
papers.abstract: Hemodialysis (HD) usually causes an acute deterioration of left ventricular diastolic function (LVDF). This study thus proposed novel biomarkers and validated their ability to assess myocardial viscoelasticity in various loading conditions.The results show that a hemodialysis session can acutely increase myocardial stiffness, indicating a rapid deterioration of LVDF. This trend is consistent with the changes observed in global longitudinal strain. Interestingly, the reduction in end-diastole volume (i.e., pre-load) after dialysis not decreased natural mechanical wave velocities but elevated them, as well as the attenuation. Moreover, the dispersion slop decreased, suggesting a post‑dialysis viscosity reduction.

papers.title: Guided-Wave Dispersion of Natural Cardiac Waves: the Influence of Myocardial Thickness on Stiffness Estimation
papers.abstract: Assessing myocardial stiffness using naturally generated cardiac waves offers significant diagnostic value, but the low-frequency nature of these waves makes their propagation velocity highly dependent on myocardial wall geometry. To address this confounding factor, this study utilized seven realistic, variable-stiffness polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) heart phantoms with varying septal wall thicknesses (10 mm to 18 mm). Using a transverse actuator to simulate natural mechanical waves and 3D ultrafast ultrasound imaging to estimate shear-wave velocities, researchers observed significant frequency-dependent dispersion, with low-frequency wave velocities deviating from intrinsic shear wave velocities by up to 30%. Crucially, by normalizing the experimental data into dimensionless variables, the dispersion curves for all thicknesses and stiffnesses collapsed onto a single, unified master curve that aligns with theoretical tube-wave models. These findings confirm that guided-wave effects dominate septal shear-wave propagation, thereby validating a dimensionless ventricular model as a robust, thickness-independent method for accurate in vivo myocardial elastography.

papers.title: 3D Myocardial Shear Wave Elastography Discriminates ATTR Cardiac Amyloidosis in Patients with Left Ventricular Hypertrophy
papers.abstract: ATTR cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR‑CA) causes myocardial amyloid deposition, increased stiffness, and diastolic dysfunction. This study assessed whether myocardial stiffness measured by transthoracic 3D shear‑wave elastography (3D‑SWE) can improve ATTR‑CA screening in patients with LV hypertrophy referred for suspected amyloidosis. A custom 3D‑SWE system generated and tracked shear waves at 3,000 volumes/s, measuring shear‑wave velocity (SWV) in three myocardial segments during diastasis. Among 107 patients, 49 had ATTR‑CA. Conventional echocardiography failed to distinguish them from non‑ATTR cases, whereas SWV was significantly higher in ATTR‑CA in the septal and RV walls. A diagnostic model combining age, NT‑proBNP, and SWV achieved 98% sensitivity and 100% specificity. Real‑time 3D‑SWE thus shows strong potential as a non‑invasive tool for targeted ATTR‑CA screening and follow‑up.

papers.title: A Novel Shear Wave Speed Estimation Method to Reduce Interobserver Variability in Cardiac Shear Wave elastography
papers.abstract: Cardiac shear wave speed (SWS) measured by high-frame-rate imaging is a promising marker of myocardial stiffness. However, interobserver variability remains high due to manual M-mode placement. This study proposes an adaptive approach to reduce variability while providing a confidence metric. A total of 62 shear waves were estimated in the interventricular septum from 11 healthy volunteers and 7 patients, by two observers. Three methods were compared: (i) conventional Mmode line; (ii) thickness-based Mmode (5 mm IVS, fixed 3 cm); and (iii) adaptive Mmode with variable lenghts (1.5–5 cm). For the latter, SWS values were retained based on ≥3 frames and high R², and averaged with the coefficient of variation (CoV) as a reliability metric. The adaptive method reduced variabilitycompared to conventional approuch (LoA −0.80 to 0.55 m/s vs. LoA 1.18 to -1.76m/s, resp.) while preserving SWS values (Δ0.11 m/s, p=0.663). This approach improves robustness and supports clinical implementation.

papers.title: Acoustic Radiation Force Induced Arterial Circumferential Waveform Extraction Using the Apex-Shifted Radon Transform (ASRT)
papers.abstract: Circumferentially propagating waves in acoustic radiation force (ARF)-based arterial elastography encode valuable biomechanical information but are often obscured by overlapping modes. We propose an apex-shifted Radon transform (ASRT) to selectively extract these waveforms by accounting for curved propagation geometry. A total of 23 vessel-mimicking tube phantoms were studied using ARF excitation and ultrafast imaging to generate spatiotemporal particle velocity maps. ASRT demonstrated high similarity between original and extracted signals (correlation ≈ 0.91, range: 0.70–0.97), low error (MSE ≈ 0.019), and preserved structure (SSIM ≈ 0.76). Group and circumferential velocities were strongly correlated (r = 0.92, p < 0.01). Representative in vivo carotid data showed similar extraction behavior. These results demonstrate that ASRT provides a robust framework for isolating circumferential guided waves for vascular elastography.
keywords: Acoustic Radiation Force (ARF) Circumferential Guided Waves Vascular Elastography Radon Transform Apex-Shifted Radon Transform (ASRT)

sessions.title: MIS: Doppler Ultrasound & Hemodynamic Assessment

papers.title: Benchmarking Venous Doppler Envelope Extraction from Displayed Umbilical Vein Doppler Spectrograms for Preeclampsia Prediction
papers.abstract: This work benchmarks envelope extraction methods on displayed pulsed-wave Doppler spectrograms when upstream IQ data or raw spectra are unavailable, using LRSP-based umbilical venous biomarker estimation for preeclampsia prediction as the downstream validation task. Seven methods were evaluated: five cumulative-power-based approaches (RotatePeak, TwoTangent, MGM, SNSI, and MSNSI) and two image-processing approaches (WhiteContour and BiggestGap). Robustness was tested using controlled simulations of adjacent umbilical arterial (UA) contamination, in vivo-derived background noise, UA aliasing, and Field II raw-RF white Gaussian noise. In vivo performance was assessed on 459 umbilical vein Doppler images from 66 subjects, including 30 with subsequent preeclampsia. Extracted envelopes were analyzed in the spectral domain to compute the log ratio of spectral power (LRSP) and evaluate preeclampsia discrimination. Results identify methods that better preserve subtle venous features and characterize method-specific failure modes under realistic artifacts and noise.

papers.title: Doppler co-Pilot for Vascular Imaging Optimization via Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Spectral Doppler ultrasound is a central tool for cardiovascular assessment. Still, quantitative measurements depend strongly on user-selected settings, such as beam-flow angle and sample volume placement, thereby limiting reproducibility. Here, we propose an automated reinforcement-learning-based approach to optimize acquisition parameters during scanning. Doppler tuning is formulated as a sequential decision-making task. A deep Q-learning agent analyzes acquired spectrograms, extracts signal-quality and flow-related features, and iteratively updates Doppler angle, gate size, and gate depth. We trained this model using a large carotid and jugular dataset simulated with Field II pro, including random geometry and flow parameters, tissue motion, and noise. Preliminary results show reliable convergence to high-quality settings across heterogeneous simulated cases, while avoiding invalid parameter selections and generalizing to unseen profiles. These findings support autonomous Doppler tuning as a route to more reproducible and standardized vascular ultrasound.
