The acoustic forces underlying this clustering have conventionally been modeled using pairwise approximations, but pairwise additivity is known to break down in dense particle configurations. Numerical methods such as finite element analysis can account for multibody effects, yet their computational cost limits application to systems with many particles. Here, we apply a coupled multibody scattering potential to compute the forces on individual particles in levitated clusters. We adopt a generalized interaction potential that solves the coupled multibody scattering problem for N particles via a 4N-dimensional linear system, enabling force computation in diverse external acoustic fields. The interaction force map shows that the cluster attracts nearby particles, and that near the vacancy the force field directs the probe particle toward it, consistent with experimentally observed cluster growth.

papers.title: Solid-Liquid Separation with Acoustic Radiation Force Generated by ELIPS-SAW
papers.abstract: Solid-liquid separation is essential for applications such as blood-cell isolation and microplastic removal. Conventional methods, including centrifugation and filtration, are often limited by batch operation, particle damage, and environmental burden. SAW-based separation offers a contactless and noninvasive alternative, but conventional devices are constrained by substrate size and high operating frequencies, limiting throughput. To address these challenges, we propose solid-liquid separation using ELIPS-SAW, a substrate-flexible platform for high-throughput operation. ELIPS-SAW generates Rayleigh waves by mode-converting longitudinal waves from an attached PZT plate, enabling SAW excitation on substrates of arbitrary material, size, and geometry. Particle separation was demonstrated using a silicone-rubber chamber mounted on ELIPS-SAW. The acoustic radiation force (ARF) was evaluated theoretically from hydrophone-measured acoustic pressure and experimentally from PTV. Results showed size- and frequency-dependent transitions between acoustic streaming- and ARF-dominated motion and highlighted the potential of ELIPS-SAW for high-throughput acoustofluidic solid-liquid separation.

papers.title: Numerical Simulation of Acoustic Radiation Force for Microparticle Manipulation in Travelling Wave Acoustofluidic Systems
papers.abstract: Finite element modelling is commonly used for simulating standing-wave acoustofluidic devices. However, particle-trajectory simulation in travelling-wave devices dominated by acoustic radiation force (ARF) remains limited. This work develops a two-dimensional (2D) simulation model for a travelling surface acoustic wave (TSAW) device using a user-defined ARF expression and evaluates its ability to reproduce the experimental trapping results for 10 µm particles. The simulation results show agreement with the experimental trends across different applied voltages and flow rates. Quantitative accuracy remains limited by uncertainties in material properties, device losses, and modelling assumptions. With further validation, the model could support design optimization by identifying the optimal operating frequency, applied voltage, flow rate, and channel height for selective particle trapping.

sessions.title: MPA: Clinical and Interventional Photoacoustic Imaging

papers.title: * INVITED * Diagnostic and Interventional Applications of Spatial Coherence in Ultrasound and Photoacoustic Imaging
papers.abstract: This talk will overview applications and use cases of short-lag spatial coherence in breast mass characterization to determine the presence of breast cancer, sound speed estimation to improve delay-and-sum beamforming, flexible array shape estimation, skin tone bias reduction in non-invasive photoacoustic imaging, and interventional photoacoustic image guidance during surgery, biopsies, and cardiac catheterization procedures. Early adoption of our real-time system by breast radiologists at the Johns Hopkins Hospital will additionally be discussed. This expansiveness of applications represents a gold mine of untapped potential to revolutionize our standards for equity in ultrasound-based patient care.

papers.title: Assessing Intestinal Fibrosis Using a Translational Endoscopic Photoacoustic/Ultrasound Balloon Catheter
papers.abstract: Assessing fibrosis in intestinal strictures in Crohn’s disease is critical for clinical decision-making between medical therapy and surgical intervention. We developed a photoacoustic (PA)/ultrasound (US) balloon catheter that is fully compatible with the instrument channel of a clinical colonoscope. The catheter can quantify collagen and hemoglobin content as surrogates for fibrosis and inflammation, and assess the relative stiffness, which increases as fibrosis progresses. Using the catheter, we observed a significant difference between human intestinal strictures and normal margins ex vivo, and the collagen content and relative stiffness correlated with fibrosis conditions in human subjects.

papers.title: Blind Spectral Unmixing for Characterizing Cartilage Damage in Osteoarthritis
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis involves progressive and irreversible cartilage degeneration, highlighting the need for early and reliable damage assessment. Unfortunately, current diagnostic methods are not suitable for early diagnosis. Ultrasound imaging captures structural changes, and spectroscopic photoacoustic imaging provides complementary compositional information related to collagen spectral features. In this study, blind spectral unmixing based on a piecewise convex multiple-model endmember detection approach is applied to spectroscopic photoacoustic data of human osteoarthritic cartilage to extract endmember spectra and abundance maps, which are correlated with histological grading. The extracted endmembers reproduce osteoarthritis-related spectral trends, including increased heterogeneity and loss of collagen spectral features with OA progression, while separating tissue signal from background and artifacts. These findings demonstrate that blind spectral unmixing improves spatially resolved assessment of cartilage composition and may enable earlier and more robust characterization of cartilage damage.

papers.title: Multimodal Photoacoustic–OCT Platform for High-Resolution 3D Monitoring of Choroidal Neovascularization in a Clinically Relevant Pigmented Rabbit Model
papers.abstract: Wet age-related macular degeneration is a major cause of vision loss, driven by choroidal neovascularization (CNV). Early detection and longitudinal monitoring remain challenging due to limited 3D resolution of conventional imaging. This study investigates CNV progression in a laser-induced pigmented rabbit model using multimodal imaging with emphasis on three-dimensional characterization. Six Dutch Belted rabbits received laser photocoagulation to induce CNV and were followed for 4 months using fundus photography, fluorescein angiography, photoacoustic microscopy (PAM), and optical coherence tomography (OCT). PAM and OCT enabled 3D visualization of CNV morphology. Indocyanine green (ICG) enhanced PAM contrast, allowing differentiation of CNV from melanin and surrounding vasculature. PAM at 700 nm quantified CNV location and density, with immunohistochemistry validating neovascular formation. PAM showed up to 59-fold signal increase in CNV regions, with strong agreement across imaging modalities. This approach enables accurate 3D assessment of CNV progression and provides a robust platform for studying disease mechanisms and evaluating therapies.

papers.title: Theranostic Nanoconstruct–Tagged Macrophages for Longitudinal Photoacoustic Monitoring and Enhanced Antitumor Activity
papers.abstract: Enhancing macrophage antitumor activity by improving their ability to phagocytose cancer cells and secrete inflammatory cytokines is a promising strategy for treating solid tumors. For example, CAR-macrophages show strong preclinical results. However, reliable methods to track cells and monitor therapeutic effects over time are lacking, where monitoring the localization and persistence of therapeutic cells can provide data-driven therapy adjustments. Specifically, imaging techniques to enable noninvasive tracking of macrophages in tumors are needed. In this study, we present therapeutic macrophages tagged with hyperbranched gold nanoconstructs (HBGNCs) functionalized with a macrophage-stimulating cytokine, IFNγ. These theranostic IFNγ-HBGNCs are both immunomodulatory and can be visualized by ultrasound-guided photoacoustic (US/PA) imaging. In mouse model of solid cancers, IFNγ-HBGNCs-tagged macrophages were tracked real-time non-invasively, and allowed for data-driven therapy adjustments, leading to complete remission cases.

sessions.title: MBB: Refraction, Aberration, Speed of Sound Estimation

papers.title: Fast Approximate Refraction Correction (FORCE) for Ultrasound Imaging in Layered Media
papers.abstract: We propose an efficient approximate refraction correction method for beamforming in known layered media. The method selectively targets strongly refracting interfaces via local boundary linearization and a closed-form Snell's law approximation, while treating remaining boundaries as in straight ray tracing (SRT). Validation using a 3D-printed silicone aberrator on a wire target phantom shows that the proposed method matches full ray tracing in both FWHM (within 0.1%) and peak amplitude (within 0.01 dB), while SRT and standard beamforming show FWHM increases of 20%/300% and peak losses of 0.9/7.5 dB. The computational cost is less than 1.5 times that of SRT, while full ray tracing is orders of magnitude more expensive.

papers.title: Implant-Aware diverging-Wave Imaging for trans-Implant Brain Imaging
papers.abstract: Transcranial ultrasound is degraded by skull-induced attenuation, refraction, and phase aberration. Although a sonolucent cranial implant can provide an acoustic window, implant-induced steering loss and path error can still reduce image quality. This study evaluated implant-aware diverging-wave imaging (DWI) through k-Wave simulations and experiments using a 3-MHz P4-2 phased-array transducer. Angle-dependent transmission at the implant interface was analyzed, and a feasible steering-angle range was derived for each imaging point by accounting for refraction. Ray-tracing-based transmit and receive delays were then incorporated into beamforming. The proposed method reduced implant-induced image distortion in point-target and cyst-phantom simulations and showed similar improvements in experiments. Quantitatively, experimental SNR increased from 22.33 to 24.9 dB and |CR| from 8.09 to 12.50 dB, supporting the feasibility of wide-field trans-implant DWI through a limited implant window.

papers.title: High-Quality Divergent-Wave Cardiac Imaging and Speed-of-Sound Estimation by Optimizing Virtual Source Loci
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose a general approach framework for computing the set of optimal Virtual Sources required to fulfill an objective application according to the imaging conditions. By backtracking the rays from the points in an ROI and translating the problem to solve (ie. insonification angle coverage, angle disparity, total coverage, etc), problems like SoS estimation, Maximizing image quality and Flow estimation can be approached with optimal insonification conditions

papers.title: Improved Sound Speed Estimation Using a Wavefield Correlation Approach to Autofocusing
papers.abstract: Ultrasound autofocusing simultaneously estimates sound speed while applying aberration correction. While autofocusing shows significant aberration correction, the estimated sound speed can be incorrect due to the straight-ray model used for the delay-and-sum beamformer, which ignores refraction and diffraction, thereby introducing errors in the sound speed estimation. In this work, the straight-ray model is replaced by a wave-equation propagation model, accomplished using the wavefield correlation (WFC) approach to beamforming, which improves sound speed estimation. Here, the WFC beamformer incorporates refraction and diffraction in the autofocusing model. The WFC model was tested in simulation, phantom, and in vivo experiments and is shown to produce more spatially accurate sound speed estimation compared to the straight-ray model. In simulations, the mean absolute error (MAE) of the sound speed estimation for the straight-ray and WFC models were 30.1 and 20.3 m/s, respectively. In phantoms, the MAE across all targets was 53.5 and 20.5 m/s for the straight-ray and WFC models, respectively.

papers.title: Pixel Decoupling to Stabilize Differentiable Beamforming for Pulse-Echo Speed of Sound Estimation Without Regularization
papers.abstract: Differentiable beamforming is an emerging tool for optimizing DAS parameters, including the medium speed-of-sound (SoS). However, the gradients for speed-of-sound estimation are unstable and lead to local minima. We propose that pixel decoupling, separating the speed-of-sound grid from the beamforming grid, can stabilize pulse-echo SoS estimation without regularization. By updating the pixel positions based on equal travel time principles, similar samples are extrated from the channel radiofrequency data. We assessed the benefit of pixel decoupling using an arbitrary N-layer differentiable beamformer. We used 10 transmits from steered plane waves (-15:15 range) and a coefficient of variation loss function. Our validation sets were two-layer agar phantoms and human quadriceps in longitudinal view containing the subcutaneous adipose tissue and the muscle below. Pixel decoupling resulted in lower mean absolute error and standard deviation in both layers of the phantom scenario. Pixel decoupling also showed a significant difference (p < .0001) between the subcutaneous adipose and the muscle tissue, while no decouple resulted in no significant difference between the two (p = .07)

papers.title: ENR-DBUA: Physics-Informed Implicit Neural Representations for Aberration Correction
papers.abstract: We present a method for aberration correction in ultrasound using a physics-informed implicit neural representations of time-of-flight (ToF) fields. The representation is optimized to obtain physically consistent ToF fields by maximizing common-midpoint coherence while enforcing isotropic eikonal propagation. This formulation eliminates the need for straight-ray assumptions and yields an eikonal-consistent sound speed distribution. In physical phantom experiments, ENR-DBUA produces realistic sound speed estimates and achieves effective aberration correction. In vivo, the method improves image contrast and outperforms baseline methods (DBUA and CUTE) in terms of speckle brightness and coherence factor. Additionally, we demonstrate the value of integrating SoS priors from other methods: including the SoS map estimated by the CUTE method in our initialization, the resulting image focus improves even further. This allows us to combine the advantages of accurate global estimation from priors, with the strong local focusing qualities provided by iterative optimization with differential beamforming.

sessions.title: TMU: Capacitive and Piezoelectric Micromachined Ultrasonic Transducers

papers.title: Broadband Hybrid 96-RX/7-TX Ultrasound Array (CMUT and PMN-PT) for MIMO Imaging: Fabrication and End-to-End Characterization
papers.abstract: Conventional ultrasound transducer arrays use the same elements for transmit and receive, forcing a single-material trade-off: piezoelectric elements offer high transmit pressure but limited receive sensitivity and bandwidth, while CMUTs provide broadband, sensitive reception but weak, nonlinear transmission. Element sharing also imposes a dead zone — reception is blocked during transmit — limiting SNR via short transmit signals. MIMO imaging with cyclic coded continuous excitation and dedicated TX/RX elements would lift both constraints: each technology operates at its strength, and SNR scales with signal length. The resulting transducer-level requirements — broadband response, low TX to RX crosstalk, and high sensitivity — must be met simultaneously, which is unproven for hybrid arrays at the device level. We present the first realization and end-to-end characterization of an array integrating 7 PMN-PT single-crystal TX elements with 96 CMUT RX channels, fabricated as two silicone-bonded stacked PCBs with windows in the upper TX PCB. Combined transfer functions across 64 TX/RX pairs and crosstalk measurements indicate the architecture meets MIMO imaging requirements.

papers.title: A Compact 10-MHz BEOL-Embedded CMUT Array with Deep-Submicron Transduction Gap in Standard 0.18 µm CMOS
papers.abstract: Capacitive micromachined ultrasonic transducers (CMUTs) are attractive for biomedical ultrasound due to their CMOS compatibility. However, high-frequency applications such as IVUS and ICE require lateral scaling, which reduces active transducer area and degrades receive sensitivity. This work presents a high-frequency CMUT prototype in TSMC 0.18 µm CMOS, integrating one receiver (RX) array, four transmitter (TX) linear arrays, and a sub-mW low-noise transimpedance amplifier with 96 dBΩ gain at 10 MHz. A metal-insulator-metal (MIM) capacitor structure and post-CMOS etching were used to realize a 150 nm effective capacitive gap. In RX mode, acoustic pulse excitation produced a 22.45 mVpp output, with a center frequency of 10.6 MHz, a 6-dB bandwidth of 10.1 MHz, and a 95.1% fractional bandwidth. The receive sensitivity reached 7.11 mVpp/kPa at 35 V, close to the FEM-predicted 8.8 mVpp/kPa. In TX mode, four linear arrays driven by a -10 V short pulse generated approximately 5 kPa pressure at 3.5 mm, with a center frequency of 11.2 MHz and a 64.3% fractional bandwidth. These results demonstrate the feasibility of MIM-based CMOS-MEMS CMUTs for miniaturized high-frequency ultrasound.

papers.title: Non-Invasive Flow Velocity Monitoring in Millimetric Tubes Using a Single-Chip PMUT Array
papers.abstract: Precise hemodynamic monitoring in small-diameter vessels is critical for cardiovascular diagnostics, yet conventional ultrasonic flowmeters suffer from rigid alignment requirements and bulky integration. This study proposes a minimalist, single-sided sensing approach using a single chip PMUT array to detect low-velocity flow (cm/s level) within a 3.175 mm tube. The device features 24 channels with an optimized arrangement of multi-sized elements, enabling reconfiguration of the incident angle without mechanical adjustment. By leveraging interpolated cross-correlation to resolve sub-nanosecond Time-of-Flight (ToF) shifts, the system achieves high temporal resolution. Experimental results demonstrate a proportional stepwise response as flow velocity transitions from 0 to 4.21 cm/s. This research bypasses the spatial alignment and synchronization complexities inherent in multi-sensor systems, paving the way for monolithic PMUT-on-CMOS integration for miniaturized diagnostic platform that can monitor subtle hemodynamic fluctuations in clinical settings.

papers.title: Fabrication and Characterization of Linear CMUT Arrays with TiSi₂ Bottom Electrodes via Ultra-Thin Titanium Film Bonding
papers.abstract: This study presents the fabrication and characterization of 15 MHz linear CMUT arrays utilizing low-resistivity titanium disilicide (C54-TiSi₂) bottom electrodes to mitigate the distributed RC delay lines that fundamentally limit array scaling. To overcome the silicide-induced stress and delamination typically associated with standard fusion bonding, an ultra-thin titanium film bonding process was successfully employed. Wafer-level characterization demonstrated robust mechanical stability through backend processing without delamination. Electrical testing confirmed the targeted low-resistivity performance of the electrodes alongside hysteresis-free electromechanical operation and a resonance peak at 26 MHz in air. These results establish ultra-thin titanium film bonding as a highly viable platform for integrating silicide electrodes, paving the way for the future development of large-aperture, low-RC-delay CMUT arrays.

papers.title: Wideband Liquid-Coupled Epi-PZT PMUT Arrays for Ultrasonic Doppler Flow Measurement
papers.abstract: Piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducers (PMUTs) offer a promising route toward compact ultrasound systems but are often limited by narrow bandwidth and strong ringing, particularly in liquid operation. This work investigates how array geometry and electrical interfacing jointly influence performance in linear epi-PZT PMUT arrays. A 64-element dual-electrode array is developed on SOI, and both finite-element simulations and RC network modeling are used to capture acoustic coupling and interconnect effects. Experimental validation includes impedance, laser-based displacement, and hydrophone measurements, along with Doppler flow testing. The results show that array pitch and kerf design critically control transverse ringing, while two-sided electrical feeding improves phase uniformity. The array demonstrates wideband performance with a one-way −3 dB bandwidth of 7–27 MHz and up to 55% pulse-echo fractional bandwidth at 8.75 MHz. The findings provide practical design guidelines for achieving broadband, low-ringing PMUT arrays suitable for flow sensing.

papers.title: A Dual-Mode ScAlN-Based PMUT Array for Integrated Respiratory Health Monitoring
papers.abstract: In this work, we demonstrate a dual-mode ScAlN-based PMUT array for smart nasal patches, integrating an active ultrasonic mode (AUM) for diagnostics/therapeutics and a passive sensor mode (PSM) for continuous snore detection. To mitigate inter-element crosstalk, deep trench isolation and a differential drive scheme are implemented. The device achieves high-SNR pulse-echo operation, with outer electrodes for transmission and inner electrodes for reception. Furthermore, successful snore acquisition is demonstrated via acoustic coupling to the nasal exterior of multiple volunteers, requiring no external excitation. This single-transducer approach provides a low-power and compact solution for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) management, advancing next-generation wearable health monitors.

sessions.title: MTN: Advanced Technologies for Cancer Therapy

papers.title: Checkpoint immunotheranostic Agents Enable ultrasound-Guided Photoacoustic Imaging of T Cell Antitumor Activity for Early Prediction of Response
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has transformed cancer treatment, yet 60 to 90% of patients with solid tumors fail to respond, while responders often exhibit atypical response patterns such as pseudoprogression that confound conventional imaging. Noninvasive, nonionizing methods to longitudinally monitor intratumoral immune cell activity and predict therapeutic response at early timepoints do not exist. We developed Checkpoint ImmunoTheranostic Agents (CITAs), bifunctional nanosystems that couple ICB antibodies with cytotoxic T cell protease-responsive plasmonic nanosensors, enabling ultrasound-guided photoacoustic (US/PA) imaging of antitumor immune activity. Upon T cell activation and target cell killing, CITAs undergo protease-triggered aggregation that enhances plasmon coupling and amplifies near-infrared photoacoustic signals. In murine tumor models, CITAs enabled noninvasive visualization of intratumoral T cell activity concurrent with anatomical imaging. This platform integrates ICB therapy with functional imaging to enable early assessment of immunotherapy response, addressing a key limitation in current cancer imaging.

papers.title: A Multifunctional Dendritic Cell Platform for Photoacoustic Tracking and Magnetic Targeting
papers.abstract: Dendritic cell (DC)-based immunotherapy has strong potential to induce durable antitumor immunity, but its efficacy is limited by inability to track DC delivery and monitor therapy progress and inefficient homing. We propose a multifunctional DC platform integrating ultrasound/photoacoustic (US/PA) tracking and magnetic guidance to enable real-time monitoring and enhance trafficking. We synthesized gold nanorods (AuNR) and iron nanospheres (FeNS) to enable PA imaging and magnetic delivery, respectively. DC cells were dual labeled with both nanoparticles for photomagnetic properties. In vitro cell viability study showed high viability, confirming safe dual labeling. Magnetic separation study demonstrated increasing magnet-responsive cells with increasing FeNS, showing feasibility of using magnet to guide DCs. US/PA imaging confirmed a strong PA signal, while magnet-guided imaging showed directional PA signal displacement toward the magnet, confirming photomagnetic properties. Together, these in vitro results demonstrate the feasibility of a first-in-kind, safe DC dual labeling strategy for PA tracking and magnetic guidance, supporting future in vivo studies.

papers.title: Acoustically Activatable Drug-Loaded Nanodroplets for Mechanochemical Therapy in Solid Tumors
papers.abstract: Our goal is to develop and evaluate ultrasound-activated NDs for simultaneous tumor disruption and targeted drug delivery, addressing barriers in solid breast cancer treatment. We synthesized ultra-small, lipid-based NDs (<200 nm) via microfluidics, encapsulating 5-FU, STING agonist, or fluorescent molecules. These NDs demonstrated long-term stability and strong acoustic responsiveness (>10 dB enhancement, MI up to 1.9). Upon high-frequency ultrasound-induced vaporization, low-frequency cavitation caused mechanical tumor fractionation and localized drug release. In vitro, ultrasound-activated 5-FU NDs achieved a ~3-fold release increase; STING agonist NDs achieved ~20-fold. In vivo, NDs extravasated into tumors with ~3-fold higher fluorescence vs. controls at 24 h and liver clearance to baseline. Ultrasound with 5-FU NDs prolonged survival by ~74% vs. untreated and ~70% vs. NDs alone. STING agonist NDs with ultrasound suppressed tumor growth 2-fold vs. untreated. This dual-action theranostic platform integrates mechanical ablation with site-specific drug delivery, offering a promising noninvasive strategy for solid tumor treatment.

papers.title: Repeated Blood Brain Barrier Opening in Glioblastoma Multiforme Using a Novel Transcranial MR-Guided Focused Ultrasound System
papers.abstract: This study evaluated a new in-house clinical prototype transcranial MR-guided focused ultrasound (TcMRgFUS) system for repeatedly opening the blood–brain barrier (BBB) in patients with glioblastoma during standard temozolomide chemotherapy. Seven GBM patients underwent up to six monthly sessions in which focused ultrasound, delivered during microbubble infusion, targeted large tumor volumes and surrounding margins to temporarily increase BBB permeability. Contrast-enhanced MRI immediately after each session confirmed successful BBB opening in all treatments, while imaging one day later showed that the BBB had returned to normal, demonstrating reversibility. Minor T2*-weighted MR imaging changes were observed following a subset of treatment sessions but were less pronounced than those reported with commercial TcMRgFUS systems. Overall, the results suggest that repeated, large-volume BBB opening with this prototype TcMRgFUS system is feasible, safe, well tolerated, and capable of enabling enhanced drug delivery during chemotherapy in GBM patients.

papers.title: Clinical Pilot Study of Ionizing Radiation Acoustic Imaging for Mapping Radiation Dose Deposition Deep Into Patient Abdomen During Radiation Therapy
papers.abstract: This clinical pilot study evaluated ionizing radiation acoustic imaging (iRAI) as a real-time, volumetric technique to map delivered radiation dose onto patient anatomy during external beam radiation therapy, with the goal of closing the gap between planned and delivered dose. Patients with intra-abdominal cancers were enrolled in a prospective trial and treated with stereotactic body radiotherapy using standard methods (3D-CRT, IMRT, and VMAT), while volumetric iRAI was used to map three-dimensional dose deposition in real time. Real-time visualization was achieved in 10 patients with liver tumors and 8 with pancreatic tumors on a clinical linear accelerator, and iRAI-measured dose distributions closely matched treatment plans based on isodose lines, dose–volume histograms, gamma index analysis, and structural similarity. These findings indicate that iRAI can provide a practical, cost-effective approach for real-time visualization and quantification of 3D dose delivery, supporting adaptive radiotherapy with improved efficacy and safety.

papers.title: Real-time, Volumetric Dose Mapping During Electron Beam Flash Radiation Therapy
papers.abstract: This study evaluated ionizing radiation acoustic imaging (iRAI) as a real-time method for volumetric dose mapping to support safe clinical translation of ultra-high dose rate (FLASH) electron radiation therapy. Using a 2D matrix-array volumetric iRAI system, experiments were performed in a solidified oil phantom and in vivo in a rabbit liver model, delivering FLASH beams from a modified Varian Clinac (6 MeV, >250 Gy/s, microsecond pulses) under varied beam parameters and validating 3D dose distributions against GAFchromic film, with additional in vivo testing using an IntraOp Mobetron (9 MeV, 1600 cGy/pulse). iRAI dose maps agreed well with film (90% gamma pass at 5%/5 mm), showed strong repeatability (<1% variation across repeated pulses), and achieved single-pulse, real-time volumetric measurements in rabbit liver with SNR > 8, demonstrating accurate, stable dosimetry with microsecond temporal resolution and highlighting iRAI’s potential to enable precise and safe FLASH-RT delivery.

sessions.title: NAS: Acoustic Sensors

papers.title: * INVITED * Augmenting Ultrasound for Continuous Glucose Monitoring via a Wearable Acoustically Readable Microneedle Patch
papers.abstract: We introduce an enzyme-free, wearable microneedle patch (ARMPatch) for continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) using standard ultrasound. The ARMPatch features glucose-responsive hydrogel microneedles that minimally penetrate the skin, swelling in response to glucose levels in interstitial fluid. Embedded silica microspheres enhance ultrasound contrast, enabling accurate, non-enzymatic glucose detection. In vitro and in vivo results demonstrate a strong, reversible correlation between microneedle swelling and glucose concentration, with stable and sensitive readings maintained for up to 56 days. Serving as an accessory to conventional ultrasound probes, the ARMPatch provides a minimally invasive, cost-effective, and durable solution for wearable CGM.

papers.title: Microwave Acoustic Vibration Sensor Glass Mounted on Metallic Structures for Operation Up to 600oC
papers.abstract: Detection of vibration is an important diagnostic tool for monitoring the health of structures and equipment, identifying when maintenance is needed, and to ensure a safe work environment. This is particularly true for high temperature and harsh environments where traditional sensors can’t be placed such as in power plants, nuclear reactors or aerospace applications. SAWRs are a versatile platform that can be placed in many environments that more traditional sensor designs can’t operate in and can measure multiple parameters. To measure vibration through dynamic strain, the sensor needs to be solidly mounted to metallic components. In this work a SAWR was mounted on a Kovar butterfly cantilever beam using a glass epoxy which has similar coefficient of thermal expansion to LGS and Kovar. The butterfly cantilever design allowed for consistent acceleration measurements over tens of hours in the 1g up to 15g’s range, under vibration frequencies in the 100Hz-500Hz range, and from room temperature up to 600C, thus revealing to be an attractive solution for HT HE vibration sensor applications.

papers.title: Three-Dimensional Droplets Sensing System Using High-Frequency Ultrasound Induced by Surface Acoustic Wave
papers.abstract: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices have been widely used for chemical detection and gas sensors due to their ability to transmit and receive high-frequency elastic waves. However, conventional gold-standard designs of SAW sensors have been inherently confined to two-dimensional sensing. In this study, we proposed a three-dimensional droplet sensing system using non-coplanar two SAW devices conclude a SAW transmitter and a SAW receiver. A droplet of pure water was used to connect the transmitter and receiver. The received waveform was acquired without a droplet to obtain the noise, with a droplet, and with a droplet containing 1 wt% of 100 μm diameter microsize particles (MP), whose maximum amplitudes were 0.80×10^-2 V, 3.20×10^-2 V, 2.16×10^-2 V, respectively. These results indicated that this three-dimensional droplet sensing system successfully transmitted and received the ultrasound, detecting amplitude attenuation due to the presence of the MP in the droplet. This system is expected to enable tracking of changes in the physical properties of droplets and contained particles, contributing to the real-time evaluation of chemical synthesis at the microscale.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Airborne Ultrasonic Sensing for Robust Non-Contact Respiration Monitoring
papers.abstract: Non-contact respiration monitoring is needed when contact sensors disturb natural breathing or prove impractical. Airborne ultrasonic sensing is low-cost and unobtrusive, but multipath propagation causes fading and channel interference, making single-channel extraction unreliable. This work proposes a lightweight self-supervised convolutional neural network (CNN) for respiration enhancement using three reflected 40 kHz ultrasonic signals. The signals were envelope-demodulated and filtered in the respiration band (0.15-1.5 Hz), while a chest force-sensing resistor was used only for validation. The 689-parameter CNN learns adaptive channel-frequency weighting from unlabeled 30-s windows through a spectral concentration loss. On the FSR-verified test set, the method achieved 21.80 dB SNR and 0.60 bpm error, outperforming ICA (17.29 dB SNR, 1.67 bpm). DAS beamforming (13.37 dB SNR, 5.67 bpm) confirmed that blind spatial combination degrades performance below single-channel extraction. These results support lightweight self-supervised ultrasonic respiration monitoring for embedded non-contact sensing.

papers.title: Spatially Resolved On-Chip Viscosity Sensing Using a GHz Ultrasonic Imager and a Printed Cantilever
papers.abstract: This work presents a compact on-chip viscosity sensing approach using a GHz ultrasonic imager integrated with aluminum nitride transducers. The method enables spatially resolved measurements (~50 µm) of printable inks and low volume fluids (~50 pL). At GHz frequencies, the acoustic response is sensitive to viscosity dependent damping and interfacial effects, allowing detection of small variations in fluid properties. Acoustic impedance is extracted from time resolved echoes and correlated to viscosity. High viscosity extrusion printed inks (1–100 Pa·s) are measured directly, while low viscosity fluids such as polyethylene glycol solutions (mPa·s range) are characterized using a printed and released silver cantilever that creates a confined sensing region to enhance sensitivity. The system resolves spatial variations in printed features and demonstrates viscosity sensing across a wide range of regimes. This approach provides a scalable platform for in situ monitoring of printed electronics and low volume biomedical fluids, with ongoing work exploring data driven methods for improved analysis.

sessions.title: MIM: Ultrasound Biomarkers and Sensing

papers.title: A High-Resolution Pule-Echo Tomographic Ultrasound System for Volumetric Breast Imaging
papers.abstract: This work presents a real-time, high-resolution pulse-echo tomographic ultrasound system for volumetric breast imaging. A 1024-element, 20-cm-diameter, 2.5-MHz half-ring array acquires multi-view sparse synthetic-aperture data over a large breast field of view. A coupling gel with <100 mL water enables seated or upright imaging without painful compression. Four synchronized Verasonics NXT systems, each with a dedicated host PC and GPU, perform local partial beamforming and transfer beamformed I/Q data to a primary host for real-time image formation. B-mode images are reconstructed using coherence-factor-modulated delay-and-sum beamforming with sound-speed-map-based delay correction for gel, water, and breast tissue. Volumetric scanning translates the array with a motorized stage, acquiring 200 frames over 60 mm in 13 s. Healthy-volunteer imaging visualized fibrous and glandular breast structures over a large field of view, and 3D rendering highlighted hyperechoic structures beyond a single plane. The system achieved 8 frames/s, supporting real-time, posture-flexible volumetric breast ultrasound.

papers.title: Hadamard-Encoded Synthetic Aperture Acoustoelectric Imaging for High-Volume-Rate Current Source Imaging
papers.abstract: Acoustoelectric (AE) imaging has the potential to provide high-resolution imaging of cardiac and neural biocurrents, addressing spatial or temporal limitations of scalp EEG, 12-lead ECG, and fMRI. However, high-volume-rate (HVR) 3D AE imaging faces a tradeoff between volume rate and field of view (FOV), as conventional focused-beam scanning requires many scan lines for a large FOV. We present Hadamard-encoded synthetic beamforming (HSB), in which ultrasound transmissions are spatially encoded using Hadamard matrices. Decoding provides signal averaging and improves SNR over conventional synthetic aperture imaging. The method was validated through an ex vivo human skull in 0.9% NaCl using a 16×16 2D array transducer at 0.6 MHz, a Verasonics Vantage 256 system, and a multichannel recording system. Full-order 16×16 HSB used fewer transmissions than focused-beam scanning, while achieving a wider FOV and an 8.3 dB SNR gain under matched peak pressure. Reduced-sequence 16×4 HSB increased volume rate fourfold over full-order HSB while maintaining image quality over a reduced elevational FOV, achieving 234 Hz volume rate with 64 transmissions at 15 kHz pulse repetition frequency.

papers.title: INTRAOPERATIVE Electromechanical Wave Imaging at Reduced Frame Rates in Pediatric Tachycardia Patients Using Deep Learning
papers.abstract: Electromechanical Wave Imaging (EWI) non-invasively maps cardiac electromechanical activation but requires high frame rates (FRs) incompatible with clinical ultrasound systems. This limitation is particularly constraining in supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) patients, where elevated heart rates demand high temporal resolution. We trained a dedicated 1D convolutional neural network (CNN) at each FR to estimate per-pixel activation time from intraoperative EWI strain waveforms, acquired in 15 pediatric SVT patients (13.8±4.1 yo, 9F) undergoing catheter ablation. RF data acquired at 2000 Hz were decimated to 500, 250, and 125 Hz; manual 2000 Hz isochrones served as ground truth. Evaluated on 3 held-out patients, the model achieved MAE = 22.8 ms and 58.8% ATD ≤ 20 ms at 2000 Hz, remaining robust at 500 Hz (24.9 ms, 55.6%), with progressive degradation at 250 Hz (31.9 ms, 45.3%) and 125 Hz (34.5 ms, 43.6%). The hallmark SVT activation pattern was preserved across all FRs, supporting strain-based deep learning as a viable framework for operator-independent EWI at clinically accessible frame rates.

papers.title: Longitudinal Stem Cell Tracking for Regenerating Retinal Tissues in Living Rabbits
papers.abstract: This study addresses a key limitation in regenerative therapies for age-related macular degeneration (AMD): the inability to reliably track transplanted stem cells in vivo. We developed a multimodal imaging platform combining photoacoustic microscopy (PAM), optical coherence tomography (OCT), and fluorescence imaging (FI) for long-term, selective visualization of transplanted human iPSC-derived RPE cells. In a rabbit model of laser-induced RPE damage, labeled cells were delivered subretinally and monitored for 6 months. Fluorescence imaging showed initial cell distribution and short-term survival up to 28 days, while OCT provided structural localization. PAM enabled clear distinction of transplanted cells from surrounding vasculature based on optical absorption. Multimodal image fusion confirmed migration toward damaged RPE regions. Histology and immunofluorescence validated in vivo findings, showing engraftment and melanin formation. This approach enables long-term tracking of stem cell viability and migration, supporting evaluation and optimization of stem cell therapies for retinal degeneration.

papers.title: End-to-End Transformer for in Vivo Dosimetry Using Quantitative Radiacoustic Imaging
papers.abstract: Accurate in vivo dosimetry is critical for advanced radiotherapy, where radiacoustic imaging (RAI) offers a promising non-invasive solution. Current RAI frameworks rely on a heavy two-step time-reversal (TR) reconstruction process, hindering real-time use. We propose a direct-inversion, end-to-end hybrid Convolutional-Swin Transformer. This network directly maps raw spatio-temporal sinograms to 3D volumetric pressure fields, completely bypassing TR. We trained and evaluated our model on 1,356 simulated and experimental samples, and it achieved comparable performance to the two-stage 3D U-Net baseline. Eliminating TR dramatically reduces inference time, enabling instantaneous, online dose verification.

papers.title: Feasibility of dual-Modality Electromechanical Activation and Mechanical Deformation in Humans for Monitoring Ischemic Conditions in the Heart
papers.abstract: Repeated interruption of blood flow to the myocardium affects both mechanical and electrical function. In this study, the clinical translation of ME-EWI is assessed in chronic ischemia patients diagnosed with Myocardial Fibrosis. Transthoracic scans were acquired using a P4-2 array and a research ultrasound. Short-axis left-ventricular views were acquired using a combined sequence with an ME 300-Hz frame rate, and EWI at 2000 Hz; both at 16-cm depth and 2s acquisition time. Patients were recruited from the Intracardiac Coronary Angiography (ICA) schedule based on recent Cardiac MRI (CMR) with Late Gadolinium Enhancement (LGE) studies. ME and EWI maps of each left-ventricular (LV) annulus at the apex and papillary muscle were generated. Patient 1 (54, M) underwent both CMR-LGE and ICA imaging and was diagnosed with MF and ischemia. EM delays are 30 ms larger in the apex level and 31 ms larger in the papillary level than the regions without MF. Radial strain is 3% lower in affected regions than other segments. ME and EWI provide a full assessment of effects of ischemic conditions on mechanical and electromechanical function to better inform clinical decisions for complex patients.

sessions.title: MEL: Armen Sarvazyan Memorial Session: Advances in Medical Elastography

papers.title: A Neo-Hookean Shear Wave Model for Hepatic Venous Pressure Gradient Estimation
papers.abstract: This study investigates the influence of the hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) on shear wave (SW) propagation to improve the diagnosis of portal hypertension. While HVPG is a key clinical index, its physical impact on SW velocity (SWV) remains unclear. We developed a finite-difference time-domain simulation incorporating Neo-Hookean (NH) body forces to model nonlinear deformation under varying HVPG. In-vivo measurements were conducted on two healthy volunteers using an external vibrator and a LOGIQ E10 system, with SWV estimated via the phase gradient method. Simulation results demonstrated that SWV in tissue surrounding the fluid phase increased from 1.9 m/s to 4.6 m/s as applied HVPG rose from 0 to 10 mmHg. Based on simulation-derived regression, in-vivo peri-vascular SWVs (1.9 ± 0.4, 2.3 ± 0.5 m/s) corresponded to 1.8 and 3.1 mmHg HVPG, within normal range (< 5 mmHg). SW morphological maps indicate that the NH restoring force induced by HVPG causes localized phase distortions and an extension of the apparent wavelength. These findings enable quantitative HVPG estimation, potentially enhancing the reliability of non-invasive PH screening.

papers.title: Multi-Frequency Acoustic Radiation Force Displacement Imaging (MARDI) Detects Kidney Mechanics Before Biomarker Changes in a Preclinical Model of Diabetic Kidney Disease (DKD)
papers.abstract: Multi-Frequency Acoustic Radiation Force Displacement Imaging (MARDI) is investigated for early detection of Diabetic Kidney Disease, a major cause of chronic kidney failure where conventional biomarkers often detect damage late. This study evaluates MARDI’s ability to identify renal mechanical changes in a preclinical rat model. A total of 45 male Sprague–Dawley rats were studied, with diabetes induced using a high-fat diet and streptozotocin. MARDI acquisitions were performed on the left kidney, and peak-to-peak displacement ratios were computed across kidney regions. Results show reduced medullary displacement relative to cortical regions in diabetic kidneys, indicating increased stiffness. Several regional ratios significantly differentiated diabetic and control groups at multiple time points. In contrast, serum cystatin C did not clearly distinguish groups during this early stage. These findings suggest that MARDI can detect heterogeneous renal mechanical changes before conventional biomarkers, highlighting its potential for early DKD monitoring. Ongoing work includes extended longitudinal analysis and histological validation.

papers.title: Multi-Frequency Acoustic Radiation Force Imaging (MARDI) Detects Early Treatment Response Beyond Tumor Volume in a Murine Breast Cancer Model
papers.abstract: Early assessment of breast cancer treatment response is limited by reliance on tumor volume changes that lag underlying structural remodeling. To address this, we applied MARDI, a frequency-resolved on-axis displacement imaging method to monitor chemotherapy and immunotherapy response in a 4T1 murine breast cancer model. Fifteen BALB/c mice were assigned to control, paclitaxel, or combination (paclitaxel + anti-PD-1) groups, with longitudinal imaging from Day 6 to Day 36 using a Verasonics Vantage NXT ultrasound system and L11-5 transducer. The peak-to-peak displacement (P2PD) ratio across 100–1000 Hz quantified mechanical changes. By Day 36, treated groups showed reduced P2PD ratios indicating tumor softening with significant differences at select frequencies (p<0.05) despite non-significant volume changes. Average reductions in P2PD (−71.6%, −45.2%) exceeded those in volume (−6.3%, −12.5%) for paclitaxel and combination therapy, demonstrating that MARDI captures therapy-induced biomechanical alterations earlier than volumetric imaging and supports its potential as a noninvasive biomarker with ongoing histopathological validation.

papers.title: Relating VisR Derived Viscoelastic Anisotropy to Collagen Organization in Malignant and Benign Human Breast Lesions, in Vivo
papers.abstract: Breast cancer is associated with collagen remodeling, causing changes in tissue mechanics. Thus, imaging methods sensitive to collagen organization may improve lesion characterization. Viscoelastic Response (VisR) ultrasound measures viscoelastic degree of anisotropy (DoA). We hypothesized that VisR DoA reflects microscopy-derived collagen organization in malignant and benign lesions. In vivo VisR imaging was done on BI-RADs 4 or 5 lesions at four angles. Relative elasticity (RE), relative viscosity (RV), and peak displacement, were obtained, and DoA of each was calculated. Biopsy specimens were stained and imaged for collagen. Structure tensor analysis obtained collagen orientation interquartile range and coherence. Wilcoxon rank sum tests and Cliff's delta compared characterization. Malignancy was determined via histopathology. Within lesions, RE DoA, RV DoA, and collagen alignment, were higher in malignant cases. Differences did not reach statistical significance. In background tissue, collagen alignment was largely isotropic, and no trends were observed. Although limited by size, this suggests VisR DoA may be sensitive to lesion specific collagen organization in malignancy.

papers.title: Coherence-Based Traveling-Wave Selection for Reliable Shear Wave Speed Estimation in Penile Elastography
papers.abstract: Penile elastography wavefields are dominated by standing (57%) and reflected (11%) waves, with traveling wave energy absent in 59% of acquisitions across N=1,244 measurements from two independent cohorts. A Standing Wave Index (SWI = E_backward/E_forward) quantifies this reverberant regime. Unexpectedly, the erect state shows significantly lower SWI than flaccid (1.06 vs. 1.79, p<0.0001), consistent with reduced impedance mismatch as tissue stiffness increases. Coherence-based traveling-wave selection via LPVI-WBF extracts repeatable wave speed estimates from the sparse traveling-wave subset (4–17% of ROI), with CV decreasing from 0.20 to 0.18 across 100–200 Hz and substantially below unfiltered estimates. LPVI-WBF was the only method yielding physiologically consistent erect > flaccid wave speed; unfiltered methods produced the opposite due to reflected-wave contamination. Wavefield quality, governed by tissue state and anatomy, is the primary determinant of measurement reliability

papers.title: 3D Strain Imaging for Quantification of Uterine Contractions in IVF Patients
papers.abstract: This study proposes a 3D transvaginal ultrasound (TVUS) strain imaging framework to characterize uterine contractions in IVF patients, overcoming out-of-plane artifacts and restricted spatial coverage of 2D speckle tracking. Data were acquired from 13 IVF patients (5 pregnant, 8 non-pregnant) at 1 Hz before embryo transfer. After endometrium segmentation, radial tracking markers are placed in the subendometrial region, and radial strain rate signals are derived via 3D optical flow. Extracted features include contraction frequency, standard deviation, coordination, multi-directional propagation velocities, and longitudinal/circular energy ratios. Non-pregnant patients exhibited higher contraction frequency, while pregnant patients showed higher strain variability and slightly lower coordination, consistent with 2D literature. Circular velocity variability and energy ratios also differed between groups. The 3D framework enables full spatial coverage and multi-directional propagation analysis, supporting its potential for uterine receptivity assessment in IVF.

sessions.title: MTH: Therapeutic Ultrasound Systems, Histotripsy and Imaging-Guided Interventions

papers.title: A Fully Acoustic Stand-Alone Transcranial Histotripsy System
papers.abstract: Precise targeting and monitoring remain major barriers to transcranial ultrasound therapy. Current systems often require MRI or neuronavigation, increasing cost, complexity, and registration error. We developed a fully acoustic stand-alone transcranial histotripsy system integrating skull localization, treatment planning, aberration correction, therapy delivery, cavitation monitoring, and lesion mapping without MRI or neuronavigation during treatment. A 750 kHz 360-element hemispherical array localized ex vivo human skulls via pulse-echo skull surface mapping registered to CT-derived skull surfaces. Two-step CT raytracing and cavitation-based aberration correction were applied before treatment. Passive acoustic mapping (PAM) monitored cavitation and reconstructed lesion geometry. PAM corresponded closely with post-treatment MRI lesions. Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), where 1 indicates perfect volumetric overlap, exceeded 0.80 after manual PAM-to-lesion alignment. These findings support a simplified, lower-cost frameless workflow for integrated transcranial histotripsy targeting, monitoring, and lesion visualization.

papers.title: In-Vivo Handheld Histotripsy of Porcine Thyroid
papers.abstract: The current standard of care for treatment of symptomatic thyroid nodules is surgical resection. There is a significant unmet clinical need for non-invasive approaches to treat thyroid nodules. The objective of this study was to characterize the safety and feasibility of targeting and treating thyroid tissue in-vivo using a handheld image-guided histotripsy probe. A prototype handheld histotripsy system was used to treat thyroid tissue in 6 juvenile pigs (4 acute-terminal and 2 chronic-recovery). Approximately 25-50% of the thyroid was homogenized with no detectable acute adverse effects. The ablation zone was visualized post-treatment via ultrasound and contrast enhanced CT. Acute histological analysis showed large ablation regions within the thyroid with minimal signs of tissue damage beyond the margins of the thyroid. Two pigs were monitored to 28 days post-treatment with no adverse clinical effects. The ablated region appeared smaller in CT images at 7 and 28 days, and histology at 28 days demonstrated signs of healing. These findings demonstrate that miniaturized handheld histotripsy has the potential to be used as a non-invasive option to treat thyroid nodules.

papers.title: Pulse Sequence Affects Cavitation Persistence and Histotripsy Liquefaction in a Fibrous Tissue Mimicking Phantom
papers.abstract: Histotripsy uses cavitation bubble activity to mechanically liquefy tissue, but efficient treatment of fibrous, mechanically robust tissues remains challenging. This study examined how pulse sequence affects cavitation behavior and liquefaction in a fibrous tissue mimicking polyacrylamide+alginate double network hydrogel. Five pulse parameter sets were tested with a 1-MHz (f#0.75) transducer while maintaining a constant 1% duty cycle, with PRF varied across four orders of magnitude and pulse duration varied inversely. High-speed photography quantified bubble cloud dynamics, persistence, cumulative cavitation distribution, and directional bias, while microscopy, B-mode ultrasound, and shear wave elastography assessed treatment outcome. Short-pulse, high-PRF exposures produced broader and more persistent cavitation but resulted in sparse lesion morphology and minimal fully liquefied volume. Longer-pulse, lower-PRF exposures generated more localized cavitation and contiguous liquefaction. Intermediate pulse conditions produced the greatest liquefied volume and highest volumetric treatment rate, showing that cavitation extent alone does not predict treatment efficacy in fibrous media.

papers.title: Noninvasive Photoacoustic Monitoring of Tumor Antigen Trafficking Following Boiling Histotripsy
papers.abstract: Focused ultrasound therapies such as boiling histotripsy (BH) are gaining traction as non-invasive tools for cancer treatment. When BH mechanically disrupts a tumor, it releases antigens that can recruit immune cells and drive an anti-tumor response. However, current monitoring strategies and dose modeling approaches — such as passive cavitation detection — provide limited real-time feedback on therapy efficacy and direct measurement of antigen release, leaving a critical gap in guiding optimal and consistent BH dosing. To address this, we propose a noninvasive, longitudinal monitoring approach centered on combined ultrasound (US) and photoacoustic imaging (PAI). PAI works by detecting acoustic waves generated when tissue absorbs pulsed laser light, and is particularly well-suited for detecting melanin, a naturally occurring chromophore in melanoma tumors. By tracking melanin with PAI, we can monitor antigen trafficking to draining lymph nodes, the key hubs where immune responses are initiated. With this, we aim to ultimately facilitate improved prediction of treatment response, guide BH dosing, and inform combination strategies with PA-active immunotherapies.

papers.title: Transcranial Photoacoustic Guidance for Laser Interstitial Thermal Therapy
papers.abstract: Laser interstitial thermal therapy (LITT) is a minimally invasive treatment for brain pathologies but requires accurate applicator localization and controlled ablation. MRI is the clinical standard yet is costly, non-portable, and limited in real-time flexibility. Ultrasound (US) and photoacoustic (PA) imaging offer a point-of-care alternative, though transcranial imaging is degraded by skull-induced wave aberrations. This work presents a CT-assisted transcranial US/PA framework for real-time LITT fiber-tip localization. Pulsed laser excitation generates PA signals at the fiber tip as a localized acoustic source, detected by a 256-element, 400 kHz ring-array transducer. Skull CT data are registered to the US coordinate system, and CT-derived sound speed maps enable travel-time correction via fast-marching-based reconstruction. Validation with a human skull showed large localization errors without compensation. After correction, accuracy improved to ≤2 mm across all five positions, demonstrating the feasibility of low-frequency US/PA imaging as a practical alternative to MRI for LITT guidance.

papers.title: Feasibility, Safety and Performance of a Non-Invasive Ultrasound Clinical Device for Deep Vein Thrombosis Treatment in a Porcine Model
papers.abstract: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a major clinical challenge due to invasive treatments or thrombolytic reliance. This study validated a real-time image-guided thrombotripsy device using a 1.5 MHz multi-element transducer on a UR3 robotic arm, combining electronic and mechanical steering to fragment clots via acoustic cavitation. In vitro tests (3D-printed vein phantom, PVA gel phantoms) confirmed sub-millimeter accuracy (mean error: 0.027 mm) and recanalization in 31.97±5.47 min (centrality score: 0.955±0.007). In vivo trials (porcine DVT model, N=5) achieved 6.5–15.3 min recanalization for 22.05–50.82 mm clots, with no hemodynamic changes, stable vital signs, and no complications at 14 days. Ongoing histological analysis supports a favorable safety profile. Results demonstrate feasible, safe, high-performance non-invasive venous recanalization with persistent 2-week outcomes.

sessions.title: MBF: Cardiovascular and Neurovascular Flow Imaging

papers.title: Large-Scale Whole-Organ Imaging Platform for Coronary Hemodynamics: a Preclinical Tool for No-Reflow Investigation
papers.abstract: Advanced imaging of the coronary microvascular network is essential for studying left anterior descending (LAD) ischemia and the no-reflow phenomenon, yet remains limited by the inability of conventional modalities to provide whole-organ flow information in large animal models. Recently, we developed a large-aperture 252-channel multi-lens probe enabling 4D whole-organ imaging of coronary hemodynamics. Porcine LAD ischemia-reperfusion was induced (N=3), followed by Langendorff perfusion and microbubble (MB) infusion. 3D ultrafast ultrasound imaging was performed using diverging waves, with multi-layer beamforming and MB tracking for flow velocity estimation, combined with 3D motion correction. This approach enabled volumetric visualization (10×8×12 cm³) of the coronary microcirculation and detection of no-reflow regions. MB quantification showed a 23±2-fold reduction in the no-reflow region, with maxmium velocities (250±5 mm/s). This method enables whole-organ mapping of microvascular flow, linking large arteries to small vessels and supporting preclinical evaluation of therapies for no-reflow.

papers.title: Regurgitant Orifice Shape Modulates the Doppler Ultrasound Spectrum
papers.abstract: High-frame-rate diverging-wave ultrasound captures transient mitral regurgitation (MR) jets at high temporal resolution but only captures local mean within a given voxel, sacrificing intra-voxel velocity spread. Doppler bandwidth mapping (DBW) can recover this velocity spread, which may carry diagnostic information regarding jet geometry or severity, but it remains unvalidated. Here, we establish the physical basis of DBW as a hemodynamic biomarker for mitral jet diagnosis through cross-modal validation against optical particle image velocimetry (PIV) across four clinically representative orifice geometries. Concurrent diverging-wave DBW and PIV were performed on four PVA-based left heart phantoms with different orifice geometries, and PIV variance was compared with DBW. Per-frame Pearson and partial correlation were performed across all four orifice geometries for three different flow rates (10, 15, 20 mL/s). Both DBW and PIV variance scaled monotonically with flow rate. Across all conditions, DBW tracked PIV variance within the jet, median rp = 0.65. These results demonstrate that DBW can server as a mitral jet biomarker and complement color Doppler in MR diagnostics.

papers.title: Early Detection of Cardiac Dysfunction Using Ultrafast Vector Doppler Imaging in a Murine Model of Dilated Cardiomyopathy
papers.abstract: Ultrafast vector Doppler imaging (VDI) enables high-frame-rate quantification of intraventricular blood flow dynamics, providing functional information beyond conventional echocardiography. In this study, we apply VDI to longitudinally assess cardiac function in a murine model of dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and evaluate its ability to detect early dysfunction. Imaging was performed at 2, 3, 4, and 7 months in Tafazzin knockout (TAZ-cKO) mice and controls (n = 5–6 per group). Velocity vector fields derived from multi-angle, staggered PRF acquisitions were used to compute systolic total intraventricular acceleration, a flow-based metric related to intraventricular hemodynamic forces. At 3 months, acceleration detected significant differences between groups (p = 0.045), while shortening fraction showed no difference (p = 0.83). At later time points, both metrics were significantly different, with larger separation at 7 months. These results demonstrate that VDI-derived acceleration provides a sensitive marker of early cardiac dysfunction and enables detection prior to conventional echocardiographic measures.

papers.title: 4D single-Trial transcranial Functional Ultrasound Imaging Reveals brain-Wide Differences During Skilled Motor Behavior in awake, head-Fixed Mice
papers.abstract: Whole brain neuroimaging at single-trial resolution is essential for linking brain network dynamics to variability in skilled behavior. Here, single-trial transcranial 4D functional ultrasound imaging (fUSI) enables trial-specific analysis of skilled behavior in awake animals at high spatiotemporal resolution. Six head-fixed mice performed a reach-to-grab task. Power Doppler and ultrasound localization microscopy images were created. Analyses included activation, connectivity, ICA, PCA, blood velocity, and diameter. Five reach conditions were compared (success, fail, no pellet, spontaneous reach, and multiple consecutive reaches). Unlike fMRI, single-trial activation patterns can be extracted. Successful reaches showed high activation in cortical areas 1.5 s after reach start, closely matching the average across 6 successful trials. Conversely, failed reaches showed high subcortical activation at reach onset (paw lift) that decreased by 1.5 s, with no cortical activation. A linear decoder predicted success vs fail with 73% accuracy and reach detection with 86% accuracy, demonstrating that single-trial fUSI captures behaviorally meaningful circuit dynamics.

papers.title: Microbubble-Enhanced Cerebral Flow Imaging Using a Photoacoustic-Optimized Semi-Ring Ultrasound Array in Mice
papers.abstract: Semi-ring arrays provide broad angular coverage that is well suited to photoacoustic tomography, but their curved aperture and relatively large element pitch are not readily compatible with conventional ultrafast blood-flow imaging schemes developed for linear arrays. Here, we investigated whether a photoacoustic-optimized semi-ring array could support high-frame-rate cerebral blood-flow imaging. A sparse synthetic-aperture sequence was implemented on a 7.5-MHz, 256-element semi-ring array, with eight spatially distributed elements transmitting sequentially. Element-position calibration, synthetic-aperture delay-and-sum reconstruction, and singular value decomposition (SVD)-based clutter filtering were combined to generate microbubble-enhanced power Doppler images. With only eight transmit events per compounded frame, a frame rate of approximately 500 Hz was achieved. In vivo imaging in a craniectomized mouse visualized continuous flow-related structures across the cerebral cross-section and resolved multiple closely spaced vascular signals.

papers.title: Intraventricular Pressure Difference Estimation Using Euler-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Intraventricular flow vector mapping reconstructs blood flow velocity fields in the left ventricle from color Doppler. Recent work using physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) with spatiotemporal fluid-dynamic constraints has improved reconstruction accuracy, while enabling direct relative pressure estimation. Our study benchmarks a PINN-based approach optimizing Euler equations against a B-spline framework on computational fluid dynamics simulations. We also evaluated PINN-derived intraventricular pressure differences (IVPD), a diastolic function marker, in vivo on pediatric data against Blood Speckle Tracking (BST). Both approaches demonstrated high coefficients of determination for velocity and pressure reconstruction on simulated data. IVPD from PINN-predicted pressure maps showed moderate agreement with BST-derived estimates. While both methods produced similar trends across the cardiac cycle, PINN tended to underestimate pressure. This may be due to suboptimal hyperparameter tuning or limited spatiotemporal resolution of color Doppler. Further work will refine PINN optimization and validate against catheter-based measurements to enhance IVPD quantification accuracy.

sessions.title: MCA: Microbubble Physics, characterization, and imaging

papers.title: An accelerated, Differentiable Framework for microbubble Modelling
papers.abstract: Microbubble dynamics underpin both ultrasound imaging and therapy, typically modelled via a 1D radial ODE such as the Rayleigh-Plesset equation. Existing community tools like BubbleSim and APECSS provide standardised solvers but share two limitations: they are not optimised for modern hardware acceleration, and they are not differentiable—precluding the use of gradient-based methods that have transformed adjacent scientific computing fields. We present an open-source Python framework for radial microbubble dynamics built on JAX, providing native hardware parallelisation and automatic differentiation. The framework supports multiple equations of motion with composable shell, gas, and medium models, and includes implicit ODE solvers for the stiff dynamics of inertial cavitation. The framework can run 2000 Keller-Miksis simulations per second (200k ODE steps/s) on a consumer CPU. We demonstrate how differentiability unlocks new capabilities: gradient-based waveform design for target dynamic responses, direct fitting of full radial dynamics for parameter estimation (replacing brute-force search), and analysis of parameter identifiability itself.

papers.title: Multi-Stage Singular Value Decomposition for 3D Ultrafast Nonlinear Ultrasound Microbubble Imaging
papers.abstract: Microbubble-based contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) is highly sensitive for microvascular imaging, but conventional clutter filtering often suppresses slowly moving microbubbles. To address this limitation, we propose a multi-stage singular value decomposition (MS-SVD) framework that jointly exploits angular, pressure, and temporal coherence to improve 3D microbubble signal extraction and ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM).In vivo rat brain experiments demonstrated that the corresponding 3D ULM reconstructions revealed a denser microvascular network and finer capillary details, particularly in transverse slices, where MS-SVD results more closely matched optical reference images. In addition, MS-SVD better preserved low-frequency content associated with slow microbubble flow, indicating enhanced sensitivity to slowly moving contrast agents. By combining angular, pressure, and temporal SVD filtering, MS-SVD improves clutter suppression, microbubble preservation, and volumetric vascular visualization in 3D ultrafast ultrasound. These results support MS-SVD as a powerful front-end for 3D CEUS and ULM.

papers.title: Broadband Microbubble Characterization with Synchronized Swept-Sine Method
papers.abstract: Narrowband CEUS cannot deliver the broadband, harmonic-resolved microbubble (MB) characterization that multicolor ultrasound molecular imaging requires. We use the synchronized swept-sine (SSS) method with a hybrid TX/RX transducer (2.5 MHz transmit, 6 MHz receive), driven by an RFSoC FPGA, to transmit a 10 ms, 1–4 MHz chirp cyclically at up to 100 fps through a flow phantom perfused with water or SonoVue®. Inverse-filter deconvolution, local FFT on time-separated harmonics, and Chebyshev decoupling yield the Hammerstein kernels Hₙ(f); normalization against water gives harmonic-resolved CTRₙ(f). CTR₃ peaks at ≈52 dB near 1.8 MHz and CTR₂ reaches ≈37 dB between 1–3 MHz, matching the reported SonoVue low-MI resonance and confirming that bubble-intrinsic nonlinearity is recovered independently of transducer and tissue response. This establishes SSS as the measurement basis for resonance-based separation of size-isolated and receptor-targeted MB populations toward simultaneous, receptor-specific imaging in a single scan.

papers.title: Ultrasonic Activation of Liquid nanodroplets Created from Uniform lipid-Coated gas-Filled microbubbles
papers.abstract: Phase change contrast agents (PCCAs) are ultrasound-activated nanodroplets that transform into microbubbles, enabling intravascular pressure sensing since their activation threshold depends linearly on ambient fluid pressure. However, depth-related variations in ultrasound pressure cause inconsistent activation, limiting quantitative accuracy. This study quantifies how activation thresholds shift with depth and shows that using depth-scaled transmit control (multifocal activation) achieves consistent PCCA activation across varying tissue depths. Uniform microbubbles were prepared, condensed, and ultrasonically activated using programmable sequences. Pressure sweeps and hydrophone calibrations confirmed that single focus ultrasound causes depth-dependent threshold variations, while multifocal transmit sequences eliminate this issue, yielding stable activation curves regardless of depth. Thus, multifocal US improves pressure estimation reliability in ultrasound-based sensing.

papers.title: Dense Speed-of-Sound Shift Imaging for in Vivo Quantitative Monitoring of Microbubble Dynamics
papers.abstract: This work presents dense speed-of-sound (SoS) shift imaging as a novel ultrasound-based framework for quantitative monitoring of microbubble (MB) presence and dynamics. The method reconstructs MB-induced propagation changes from conventional pulse-echo data by estimating apparent axial displacements and solving an inverse problem for slowness deviations. Unlike prior studies relying on transmission or hydrophone measurements in controlled media, this approach enables noninvasive in vivo estimation of SoS changes using standard imaging systems. The method was validated in tissue-mimicking phantoms, tumor-bearing models, and rat kidney imaging. Results demonstrate clear localization of MB inclusions, sensitivity to concentration and size, and the ability to capture temporal dynamics from arrival to clearance. These findings establish SoS-shift imaging as a complementary propagation-based biomarker beyond conventional intensity-based contrast imaging, with potential applications in therapeutic monitoring and quantitative ultrasound.

papers.title: Characterization of Post-Activation Dynamics of Phase-Change Nanodroplets in Tissue Under Repeated-Burst Activation
papers.abstract: Phase-change nanodroplets (PCNDs) have shown great promise for ultrasound-based extravascular therapeutic and diagnostic applications. Their effectiveness depends critically on post-activation dynamics in tissue, which determine detectability under ultrasound monitoring. However, these dynamics remain insufficiently understood, particularly under clinically relevant repeated-burst activation schemes. Therefore, characterization of the post-activation dynamics of PCNDs in tissue-like environments under repeated-pulse sequences excitation, is essential for enabling effective extravascular imaging and monitoring.

sessions.title: MIS: Computational Imaging & Sparse Acquisition

papers.title: Coherence-Weighted Synthetic Aperture Focusing for Angular Upsampling in High-Speed Intravascular Near-Infrared Fluorescence-Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: Hybrid intravascular near-infrared fluorescence (NIRF) and ultrasound (IVUS) imaging enables co-registered assessment of inflammation and vascular morphology in atherosclerosis. Blood displacement with saline improves NIRF detection but requires pullback speeds above 10 mm/s, which is far beyond conventional rates of 0.5-1 mm/s. At high speeds, sparse angular sampling causes resolution loss, structural distortion, and motion artifacts, which is a critical barrier to clinical translation. We introduce coherence factor-weighted synthetic aperture focusing (CF-SAFT) as an angular upsampling method for rapid-pullback IVUS. CF-SAFT reconstructs missing angular samples using inter-A-line phase coherence while suppressing motion and rotational distortion artifacts. Validated through simulation, coronary stent phantom imaging, and in vivo NIRF-IVUS of rabbit iliac plaques, CF-SAFT enables high-speed hybrid NIRF-IVUS without hardware modifications, which is an important step toward clinical assessment of coronary artery disease.

papers.title: Minimum Transmit Sampling for Resolution Preservation in Ultrasound Tomography
papers.abstract: Reflection ultrasound computed tomography (RUCT) enables high‑resolution full‑view imaging but typically requires dense transmit sampling, limiting achievable frame rate. This work investigates the minimum number of transmit events required to preserve spatial resolution within a region of interest (ROI) in ring‑array USCT. A physics‑based criterion is derived by considering Rayleigh‑regime scattering and transducer directivity, which together limit the detectable scattered field to an effective angular sector. Combined with the angular span of the ROI, this defines the effective angular sampling step and the minimum number of transmit events required to avoid resolution loss. The model was validated using a 512‑element ring array (R=4 cm, 5 MHz). For a hex‑key phantom with R_ROI/R = 0.5, the predicted requirement is ~32 transmit events; fewer transmissions lead to resolution degradation. For an in‑vivo rat dataset with R_ROI/R = 0.25, the predicted requirement decreases to ~16. Experimental reconstructions agree with the predictions, supporting the proposed criterion for sparse‑TX RUCT imaging.

papers.title: Diffusion Posterior Sampling with Ultrasound Channel Data
papers.abstract: This work proposes a new approach for cognitive ultrasound that combines image-domain priors with raw channel data to improve image reconstruction under limited transmit conditions. The problem is formulated as Bayesian inference, using a prior learned from B-mode images while treating channel data as measurements. A key contribution is a differentiable ultrasound pipeline that enables computing the adjoint of delay-and-sum beamforming, allowing integration with diffusion posterior sampling (ChannelDPS). This makes it possible to generate images that are consistent with both the measured channel data and the learned prior. Results show that ChannelDPS produces high-quality images when using few transmissions, achieving improved generalized contrast-to-noise ratio.

papers.title: Robust Full-Waveform Inversion Sparse-Array USCT: Overcoming Sparse-Sampling Artifacts with Phase-Enhanced Metric and Frequency-Wise Virtual Element Modeling
papers.abstract: Sparse-array ultrasound computed tomography (SA-USCT) reduces hardware and acquisition costs. However, insufficient angular sampling degrades frequency-domain full-waveform inversion (FWI), causing phase errors, ring-like artifacts, and unstable sound-speed and attenuation reconstructions. We propose a sparse-array USCT FWI method integrating a phase-enhanced waveform metric and frequency-wise virtual elements for joint sound-speed and attenuation reconstruction. The phase-enhanced metric mitigates phase errors, while virtual elements compensate for angular undersampling throughout the inversion. Virtual receiver elements are inserted between real elements and corrected by geometric propagation delays. Their offsets and weights are adjusted with frequency to preserve low-frequency angular compensation while limiting high-frequency interpolation errors. Simulations and open-source breast USCT experiments show improved stability and artifact suppression. In simulation, fixed-ROI PSNR increased from 42.36 to 47.54 dB for sound speed and from 17.56 to 23.08 dB for attenuation; the corresponding SSIM increased from 0.973 to 0.987 and from 0.667 to 0.918.

papers.title: Orthogonal Convolution Recovery Network in Sparse Ultrasound Imaging with Joint Transmit–Receive Channel Subsampling
papers.abstract: Sparse ultrasound acquisition can reduce RF data volume and hardware burden, but simultaneous angular and transmit–receive channel loss can degrade B-mode image quality. This work presents a deep learning framework for RF data recovery and angular synthesis under joint sparse acquisition. Missing angular views are first estimated by a flow-guided synthesis module to provide structurally meaningful initialization. RF data are then reconstructed using a patch-based recovery network with adaptive amplitude scaling for weak echoes. Experiments on in vivo plane-wave ultrasound data were conducted with controlled transmit-aperture reduction and receive-channel subsampling. The proposed method improved RF reconstruction and beamformed image fidelity across angular and joint transmit–receive channel downsampling settings. In challenging joint subsampling cases, recovered images restored major anatomical structures, reduced artifacts, and improved PSNR and SSIM compared with direct beamforming from sparse RF data. These results support RF-domain recovery as a feasible strategy for maintaining ultrasound image quality under aggressive multi-dimensional sparse acquisition.

papers.title: Coded Ultrasound Imaging with Pulser Frontend vs. Linear Frontend
papers.abstract: This work evaluates the benefits of linear transmit frontends compared to simple pulser-based architectures for coded ultrasound imaging. Maximum Length Sequences (MLS) and Zadoff–Chu (ZC) sequences were transmitted either as binary pulser-modulated waveforms or as linearly amplitude-modulated signals. Simulation results based on ambiguity function analysis predict significant SNR gains for both coding schemes, with ZC sequences particularly benefiting from linear transmission due to reduced sidelobe levels. Measurements on wire phantoms confirm these trends: binary MLS transmission achieves sufficient pSNR and resolution using a pulser frontend, whereas amplitude-modulated ZC excitation combined with a linear frontend yields the highest pSNR and improved sidelobe suppression.
