The results indicate that linear frontends are advantageous for high-performance coded imaging, while pulser-based solutions remain attractive for cost- and power-efficient ultrasound systems.

sessions.title: TMI: 2D Arrays and Novel Imaging Techniques

papers.title: mRCA: a Matrix Row-Column Array Design Strategy for Ultrafast 3D Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: This study proposes a matrix row–column array (mRCA) design and beamforming method for ultrafast 3D ultrasound imaging that improves image quality or frame rate while maintaining scalable hardware complexity. By subdividing the long row and column elements of a row–column array into K1×K2 matrix subapertures, mRCA exploits directional receive sensitivity to suppress artifacts outside the effective receive sensitivity region. This reduces artifacts caused by insufficient angular sampling, enabling either improved image quality at a given frame rate or higher frame rates at comparable image quality. The performance of mRCA is evaluated through simulations, in vitro phantom experiments, and in vivo carotid artery imaging. In point-target experiments, mRCA suppresses grating lobes by up to 20.6 dB in simulation and 15.9 dB in vitro. In tissue-mimicking phantom experiments, mRCA improves the contrast ratio (CR) by up to 18.5 dB in simulation and 8.17 dB in vitro. In vivo carotid imaging further demonstrates CR improvements of up to 5.88 dB.

papers.title: Multiplexed 1536-Element 2D Array Transducer for Monitoring Intracranial Pressure
papers.abstract: Elevated intracranial pressure (ICP) is a critical condition associated with traumatic brain injury, stroke, and hydrocephalus that affects over 1.3 million patients annually in the U.S. ICP is currently assessed using invasive probes, CT, or MRI, however, these approaches have limited accuracy for quantitative ICP assessment. Alternatively, ICP can be monitored by integrating a passive microfluidic pressure sensor into the burr hole cover that is already implanted in post-surgical patients. A multiplexed 7.3 MHz, 1536-element 2D array transducer was developed to provide 3D imaging of the serpentine microfluidic channel in the ICP sensor with isotropic resolution in both lateral and elevational directions. The array achieved a 99.18% yield, with an SNR of 49.01 dB and a -6 dB bandwidth of 52.98%. At an imaging depth of 10 mm, the measured resolution was 0.591 x 0.738 x 0.106 mm (lateral x elevation x depth). The ICP sensor was imaged in 3D with the developed array, and the serpentine microfluidic channel was resolved. This approach could provide non-invasive pressure measurement in post-surgical patients with reduced user dependence.

papers.title: Rotary Aperture Phased-Transducer Operation & Readout (RAPTOR) for Ultrafast Volumetric Imaging with Partitioned Tobe Arrays
papers.abstract: Bias-switchable top-orthogonal-to-bottom-electrode (TOBE) arrays have attracted significant interest due to their ability to reduce the channel count from N×N to 2N while maintaining full element-level addressability comparable to that of fully wired Matrix probes. Advanced 2D and 3D imaging schemes implemented on TOBE arrays have demonstrated high image quality. However, imaging speed remains constrained by the settling time required for each bias pattern, typically 200–300 µs, and even with improved electronics, 50–100 µs delays persist for each transmit/receive event. Partitioned TOBE arrays composed of 2×2 subapertures have been introduced to reduce the number of required biasing patterns and improve frame rate, but still suffer from idle time between acquisitions due to sequential bias loading. In this work, we introduce Rotary Aperture Phased-Transducer Operation & Readout (RAPTOR), implemented on a 2×2 partitioned TOBE array. RAPTOR minimizes idle time by alternating roles between subapertures: while two subapertures actively transmit and receive, the other two simultaneously load the next bias pattern.

papers.title: 3D Super Resolution IVUS Catheter for in Vivo Imaging of Vaso Vasorum
papers.abstract: We propose 3D Super-Resolution IVUS (SR-IVUS) to map the vasa vasorum, a key marker of vulnerable atherosclerotic plaques. As opposed to previous IVUS "pull-back" techniques for 3D volume imaging, the device utilizes a 15 MHz 2D array to perform simultaneous volume acquisition, which is essential for tracking microbubbles in 3D space and eliminating out-of-plane artifacts. The device architecture comprises a custom high-voltage multiplexer ASIC, designed in a 0.35 µm BCD process, which employs plane-wave imaging and synthetic receive aperture (SRA) to acquire data for volumetric beamforming. Simulations of the ASIC demonstrate 57 mW power consumption and minimal switching glitch noise. The fabricated demonstration acoustic array achieved a 14.7 MHz center frequency with 32% fractional bandwidth. Imaging tests on wire targets and phantoms validate the acoustic array capability to operate at target frequencies necessary for in vivo micro-vessel characterization, providing a path toward better identification of risks for coronary heart disease and stroke.

papers.title: Development of High Frequency Ultrasound 2D Array for Brain Imaging Applications
papers.abstract: Ultrasound imaging is an essential diagnostic modality, offering real-time, non-invasive anatomical and physiological assessment. However, conventional 1D linear arrays are fundamentally limited to two-dimensional imaging and typically require handheld operation, constraining their use in continuous or long-term monitoring. In contrast, two-dimensional (2D) ultrasound arrays enable true volumetric (3D) imaging, providing sufficient spatial information. Herein, we report the design and fabrication of a 10 MHz 2D ultrasound array featuring a fine 300-µm pitch (2λ), representing a high-frequency implementation for volumetric imaging applications. This newly-developed 2D array with flexible-PCB enables potential wearability and continuous 3D visualization of tissue structures and dynamics, and holds promise as a portable, non-ionizing radiation alternative to conventional imaging modalities such as MRI and CT in selected use scenarios.

papers.title: Differentiable Calibration for Mechanically Scanning Synthetic Aperture Using a Matrix Array Ultrasound Transducer
papers.abstract: Matrix array transducers offer flexible beam control for volumetric ultrasound imaging, however, the transmission field-of-view and spatial resolution are limited by the small aperture. Extending aperture size with more elements brings fabrication challenges, increased system cost and power consumption. Instead, for static targets, an alternative is to synthesize a virtual larger aperture by mechanically shifting the matrix array. However, any misalignment between the desired and virtual matrix array will degrade the final synthetic aperture (SA) imaging performance. Instead of using hydrophone, electromagnetic or optical tracking instruments, we propose a high-precision differentiable calibration method based on two-way ultrasound localization. Our method has less than 0.5% error with the hydrophone calibration, but does not require additional equipment associated with hydrophone measurements.

sessions.title: NAI: Acoustic Imaging and Microscopy

papers.title: Morphological Analysis of Soil Blocks by Acoustic Impedance Imaging Using a High-Frequency Ultrasonic Transducer
papers.abstract: Soil health monitoring is essential for environmental and agricultural sustainability. Conventional X-ray-based methods require soil crushing and often struggle to distinguish organic matter (OM) from inorganic components. This study evaluates morphological indices using 80 MHz ultrasonic acoustic impedance (Z) imaging. Resin-embedded blocks of sandy soil (Ss), Andosol (An), stagnogley soil (Sg), and red-yellow soil (Ry) were measured using an 80 MHz ultrasonic transducer. Z was calculated from near-surface reflection intensity obtained by cross-correlating pulse-echo signal A with reference echo signal, and 2 × 8 mm² Z maps were constructed. The average impedance Zave of An, Sg, and Ry was comparable (2.5–3.2 MRayl), whereas Ss showed a higher Zave of 7.5 MRayl due to quartz. To classify the remaining OM-rich soils (An, Sg, and Ry), porosity p and coefficient of variation CV were calculated for 50 × 50-pixel regions. Ry showed the highest p (36%) and lowest CV (13%), while An and Sg lay between Ss and Ry in the p–CV plot. These results indicate that morphological analysis using p and CV, alongside Zave, can provide useful indices for classifying OM-rich soils.

papers.title: Wafer Bonding Defect Mapping Using High-Frequency Ultrasound Arrays with Spectral Coherence Factor and Null Subtraction Beamforming
papers.abstract: We investigate high-frequency ultrasound array imaging to overcome the throughput‑resolution trade‑off in scanning acoustic microscopy (SAM) for silicon wafer bonding defect detection. Using a high-frequency linear array (L38‑22v) with single‑angle plane‑wave transmission and mechanical elevation scanning, we adapt frequency‑domain coherence factors (FCF, FGCF) and combine them with null subtraction imaging (NSI). Spectral analysis identifies defect‑specific frequency bands to guide these methods. Simulations and experiments on bonded copper‑layer wafers show that NSI+FCF and NSI+FGCF suppress sidelobes and grating lobes, achieving ~60% lateral resolution improvement and a 2–3 dB reduction in sidelobe‑to‑mainlobe energy ratio versus DAS, with robust noise immunity. The linear array’s single‑pass coverage significantly enhances throughput over conventional SAM. Despite a slight axial resolution loss, defect detectability and speed are substantially improved, demonstrating strong potential for industrial wafer inspection.

papers.title: Single-Sided Detection of Subsurface Welds in Steel Plates
papers.abstract: This work addresses the challenge of detecting subsurface welds in steel plates when only one side is accessible, a common constraint in industrial settings. Traditional radiographic methods are limited by material thickness, access requirements, and safety concerns, motivating the need for a practical single-sided solution. Two complementary techniques are proposed. The first uses a bonded ultrasonic transducer to excite the plate while a scanning Laser Doppler Vibrometer (LDV) measures surface vibrations; spatial variations in stiffness, linked to welds, are identified through frequency response analysis based on Kirchhoff-Love plate theory. The second employs an electromagnetic acoustic transducer (EMAT), which generates and senses ultrasonic waves via induced eddy currents without direct contact. By raster scanning and analyzing reflected signals, subsurface geometry variations are mapped. Experiments on a steel plate with known weld features show that both methods successfully resolve hidden weld locations, demonstrating reliable, non-destructive, single-sided detection capability.

papers.title: Preliminary Study on Soils’ Attenuation and Inhomogeneity Analysis Based on B-Mode Image in MHz Range
papers.abstract: Nondestructive evaluation of soil microstructure is important for ground health. Soil texture affects water retention and mechanics; however, ultrasonic measurements below 100 kHz have limited capability for imaging local texture variations. In contrast, 80 MHz impedance imaging visualizes organic/inorganic components. We used 1.5 MHz B-mode imaging to evaluate attenuation (att) and heterogeneity indices for sand and fine-fraction distributions. Sieved sand (La), red soil (Re), and black soil (Bl), with particle sizes of 0.07–0.17 mm and moisture contents of w = 5–15%, were pressed into 1 cm-thick specimens. B-mode images of 2.5 × 80 mm were acquired with a 1.5 MHz linear probe. The images were divided into 40 strips; att and SNR in a 2 × 2 mm ROI were calculated for each strip. SNR was high in La at 4.9, whereas Re and Bl showed 1.6 and 0.9. La was close to a homogeneous single-grain structure, whereas Re and Bl contained clay particles and organic matter, enhancing internal scattering. Higher-SNR samples tended to show lower att, and similar attenuation trends held across moisture contents. MHz-range B-mode imaging may help evaluate texture-dependent soil structures.

papers.title: Ultrasonic Microscope Using Planar Fresnel Lens with in-Plane Selectively polarization-Inverted KNaNbO3 Epitaxial Films
papers.abstract: High-resolution ultrasonic imaging requires a highly focused beam. Standard acoustic lenses require machining a spherical curvature, making it difficult to array the transducers and mass production. To overcome this, acoustic Fresnel zone plates (FZPs) using in-plane selectively polarization-inverted plates are proposed, which allow adjusting the focus point by switching the inversion pattern via DC bias. As previous phase-reversal zone plates were limited to 10 MHz using bulk ceramics, we propose an 80 MHz ultrasonic FZP based on selectively polarization-inverted ferroelectric thin films for higher-resolution imaging. FEM simulations indicated that an uninverted film generates a plane wave whereas the inverted FZP generates a focused wave. A KNaNbO3 epitaxial film was grown on a La-SrTiO3 substrate. After electrode patterning, polarization was inverted by a high-voltage triangular wave. In-situ S11 measurements showed a temporary vanish and recovery of piezoelectricity, confirming successful inversion. Finally, ultrasonic imaging of a coin in water was performed. Comparing images before and after the inversion clearly showed an improvement in spatial resolution.

papers.title: 3D Ultrahigh-Resolution and Low-Sidelobe Airborne Ultrasound Imaging Using Sparse Array Hyper-Beamformation
papers.abstract: Airborne ultrasound offers a compelling solution for non-contact imaging, providing privacy, immunity to electromagnetic interference, and robustness in challenging optical conditions, making it an emerging technology in robotics, industrial inspection, and smart environments. However, poor spatial resolution and contrast, due to the diffraction limit and high sidelobe levels, hinder the performance of airborne ultrasound across various applications. In this work, an ultrahigh-resolution hyper-beamformation method for 2D sparse arrays is proposed to improve spatial resolution and sidelobe suppression in 3D airborne ultrasound imaging using our homemade 2D sparse-phase-array system.

sessions.title: MIM: Ultrafast Methods for Microvascular Imaging

papers.title: Transcostal 3D Ultrafast Ultrasound Imaging of the Heart with a Large Aperture Probe
papers.abstract: We introduce a large-aperture 3D ultrafast ultrasound framework for cardiac imaging that overcomes rib-induced limitations via SVD-based rib detection and adaptive transmit/receive aperture selection. Using a 256-element (1 MHz, 10 cm) array, ultrafast imaging (up to 786 Hz) was achieved with sub-synthetic compounding. The approach was validated through PSF analysis, shear wave imaging (20–100 Hz) in a phantom, and in vivo transthoracic ULM in three volunteers. Robust rib detection enabled accurate aperture optimization. Shear waves were reliably tracked (1.72–2.51 mm/s), and 3D ULM provided successful microbubble localization in cardiac cavities over large volumes. These results demonstrate the feasibility of transcostal large-aperture ultrafast imaging for whole-heart 3D assessment.

papers.title: Coded Excitation-Assisted Null Subtraction Imaging for High-Resolution Contrast-Free Deep Vascular Power Doppler
papers.abstract: Contrast-free power Doppler imaging is limited in deep organs because weak flow echoes approach the noise floor, making small-vessel separation difficult. Null subtraction imaging (NSI) improves lateral resolution through zero-mean apodization, but low-SNR signals can reduce the reliability of its subtractive beamforming. This study combines 13-bit Barker-coded excitation with NSI to improve pulse-compressed SNR and recover vessel separation. In vivo kidney data were acquired using a Verasonics Vantage 256 system with a 5.2-MHz GE 9L-D probe, 9-angle plane-wave imaging, 4000-Hz PRF, and 400 frames. Barker-coded RF data were pulse-compressed using a mismatched filter with range sidelobes below -40 dB. Barker coding increased SNR from 11.81 to 20.68 dB for DAS and from 11.47 to 20.10 dB for NSI. Barker-coded NSI achieved the lowest peak-normalized background noise power of -31.48 dB and reduced FWHM from 738 to 401 μm and from 656 to 387 μm. These results suggest that coded excitation stabilizes NSI subtraction and enables clearer high-resolution contrast-free deep vascular power Doppler imaging.

papers.title: Contrast-Free high-Resolution Ultrasound Microvascular Imaging for Quantitative Assessment of Kidney Transplant
papers.abstract: Microvascular alterations are closely associated with kidney allograft injury progression, yet current clinical imaging modalities lack sufficient sensitivity and spatial resolution for reliable assessment. High frame-rate ultrasound has significantly improved the sensitivity of power Doppler (PD) imaging to small vessels without contrast agents, but its limited resolution constrains microvascular depiction and quantification. In this pilot study, we introduce an advanced high-resolution power Doppler (HRPD) strategy to enhance microvascular visualization and quantification in kidney transplants (KTs).HRPD-derived metrics showed consistently higher correlations with histological scores (up to |r| = 0.87) than PD-derived metrics (up to |r| = 0.54).

papers.title: Perioperative and 28-Day Cerebral Perfusion Variations Assessed by Ultrafast Power Doppler in Neonates with Congenital Heart Disease Versus Healthy Controls
papers.abstract: Transposition of the great arteries (TGA) is a congenital heart disease which exposes the neonatal brain to hypoxemia and perioperative vulnerability, while bedside tools for repeated cerebral hemodynamic assessment remain limited. This study used transfontanellar ultrafast power Doppler imaging to longitudinally assess cerebral blood volume changes (ΔCBV) during the first 28 days of life and around surgery in 18 TGA neonates and 28 healthy controls. The main finding was a significant increase in ΔCBV in healthy controls (+0.06/day, p=0.03), whereas TGA neonates showed a non-significant negative trajectory (−0.04/day, p=0.06). Similar trends were observed across several brain regions and arterial, and venous analyses. In paired perioperative scans acquired within 48 h before and after surgery, TGA neonates showed a significant postoperative decrease in ΔCBV (median change −0.25, p=0.016). These findings suggest altered cerebral hemodynamic adaptation in TGA neonates, associated with an early postoperative reduction in cerebral blood volume. UPD may support longitudinal and perioperative bedside monitoring of neonatal cerebral hemodynamics.

papers.title: Enhanced Mean-Shift Super Resolution (eMSSR) Method for Row-Column Array Based 3D Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: Row-column addressed (RCA) arrays offer an efficient solution for ultrafast three-dimensional (3D) ultrasound imaging by substantially reducing the number of required electronic channels. Nevertheless, their imaging performance, especially image contrast and lateral spatial resolution, is often degraded by pronounced sidelobe artifacts, mainly due to the limited focusing capability of the array. To overcome this limitation, we proposed an enhanced mean-shift super-resolution (eMSSR) method specifically developed for RCA imaging to improve spatial resolution while remaining robust in the presence of strong sidelobe artifacts and non-Gaussian point spread function (PSF) patterns. The performance was evaluated through simulations and in vivo imaging of a rat kidney.

papers.title: 4D Cerebral Microvascular Imaging Platform During Ischemia-Reperfusion in a Mouse Stroke Model
papers.abstract: This study presents a platform for continuous 4D (3D + time) imaging of whole-brain hemodynamics in a mouse model of ischemia and reperfusion, where rapid changes occur within seconds. Ischemia and reperfusion were induced via filament insertion and withdrawal in the carotid artery, while contrast-enhanced high-speed 3D ultrasound imaging (5 s per volume) was performed at 30-second intervals. RF data were processed using SVD filtering and 3D registration to visualize and quantify blood flow dynamics. The results showed a 6.7 dB decrease in blood flow in the right cortex during ischemia and a 12.2 dB increase after reperfusion. These findings demonstrate that the proposed framework enables rapid, continuous assessment of whole-brain hemodynamics and provides a powerful tool for investigating dynamic cerebrovascular responses in small-animal models.

sessions.title: MTC: Liver, Abdominal & Special Tissue Applications

papers.title: Towards End-to-End Learning-Based Liver Fat Quantification from Volumetric Ultrasound Radio Frequency Data
papers.abstract: Early detection and accurate staging of hepatic steatosis are critical for effective monitoring and intervention of MALSD. MR-PDFF provides reliable liver fat quantification, but availability is limited. Quantitative ultrasound methods are an accessible alternative, but phantom calibration and intensive optimization are required. We propose a learning-based approach to estimate liver fat content directly from volumetric US RF data, and to generate 3D fat-quantification maps comparable to MR-PDFF. The method was trained on 248 spatially aligned 3D MR-PDFF and US acquisitions from 36 subjects. Each MR-US pair was rigidly registered with expert-validated liver segmentations. RF data was processed using overlapping axial windows from each 2D plane to preserve local signal structure. A factorized CNN was trained with liver-masked PDFF supervision labels to estimate volumetric liver fat maps. Leave-one-subject-out validation showed strong agreement with MR-PDFF, achieving r = 0.84, R² = 0.70, and mean absolute error = 3.08%, outperforming 3D ACE on the same RF data.

papers.title: Liver Steatosis Assessment in Bariatric Surgery Patients via Multiparametric Quantitative Ultrasound
papers.abstract: In bariatric surgery patients, noninvasive follow-up evaluation of obesity-associated liver steatosis remains challenging. Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) characterizes tissue using attenuation coefficient slope (ACS), backscatter coefficient (BSC), and speed of sound (SoS). Given grade overlap and limited biopsy-referenced QUS studies, this work evaluates whether multiparametric QUS (MP-QUS) features improve liver steatosis grade classification. An in vivo study included 50 patients spanning non-steatotic to severe steatosis. Steatosis grades were derived from biopsy histology using automated steatotic parenchymal area quantification. Liver RF data were acquired using a Verasonics Vantage NXT, C5-2v probe at 3 MHz and walking-aperture strategy. Universal REFoCUS recovered synthetic-aperture data to estimate SoS, ACS, and BSC. G0-referenced patient-wise deviations were evaluated individually and combined using OOB random forests for grade classification. The MP-QUS model achieved the highest macro-averaged AUC (0.85) compared to ACS (0.76), BSC (0.66), and SoS (0.61).

papers.title: Microvessel Orientation Biomarkers for Detecting Hepatocellular Carcinoma Using Contrast-Free Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common primary liver cancer, and early detection is important for effective treatment. Ultrasound is widely used for liver screening, but its diagnostic performance remains limited. This study introduces microvessel orientation biomarkers from contrast-free ultrasound microvessel imaging to differentiate HCC from benign liver lesions. Contrast-free microvessel imaging was performed in 22 subjects with 29 hepatic lesions, including 10 benign and 19 malignant lesions. Among the malignant lesions, 11 were HCC, 7 were cholangiocarcinoma, and 1 was metastatic adenocarcinoma. Twelve orientation features were extracted, including penetrating and circumferential vessel counts, penetration-density metrics, vessel diameter ratios, and polar-domain features. Each feature was assigned a binary score, and the scores were combined into an orientation score ranging from 0 to 8, where higher scores indicated more penetrating vascularity. The orientation score was significantly higher in malignant and HCC lesions than in benign lesions. The highest AUC was 0.97 for lesions smaller than 30 mm, supporting its potential for early HCC detection

papers.title: Noninvasive Quantitative Ultrasound Assessment of Placental Microstructural Changes in the Preeclamptic Dahl SS/Jr Rat
papers.abstract: Conventional ultrasound is widely used during pregnancy for fetal and maternal monitoring because it is noninvasive, inexpensive, and easy to operate. However, the tissue information provided by conventional ultrasound is limited. Quantitative ultrasound (QUS), based on B-mode ultrasound, processes the raw RF B-mode data to detect subtle microstructural changes in tissue. Numerous studies have demonstrated that preeclampsia (PE) is associated with abnormal placental structure. Insufficient maternal blood supply and placental hypoxia lead to incomplete placental development. QUS analyzes and computes parameters from raw RF B-mode data to monitor microstructural dysfunction in placentas affected by PE.

papers.title: Assessment of Ocular Choroidal Melanoma Lesions from Nevus Lesions Using Wavefield-Aware Ultrasound Elastography
papers.abstract: Purpose: Differentiating ocular choroidal melanoma from nevus is challenging due to overlapping features. Single-frequency shear wave speed (SWS) shows limited separability, and the eye's curved geometry and impedance mismatches promote reflections and interference that compromise conventional estimators. Methods: Using ultrasound elastography with harmonic excitation at 100, 150, and 200 Hz, SWS was measured in lesion-confined ROIs in 10 patients (5 melanoma, 5 nevus; IRB-approved). LPVI-WBF suppressed standing waves via k-space filtering and retained propagation-consistent pixels. Two metrics were evaluated: dispersion slope (DS) and frequency-domain heterogeneity index (Hf). Results: ROI-mean SWS overlapped between groups at individual frequencies. Melanoma exhibited significantly stronger dispersion (DS: 0.0161 vs. 0.0088 m/s/Hz, p<0.01; AUC=1.00) and greater heterogeneity (Hf: 0.187 vs. 0.111, p<0.01; AUC=1.00). Leave-one-out cross-validation confirmed consistent separability despite the small cohort. Conclusion: Multifrequency dispersion and heterogeneity in wavefield-aware elastography provide sensitive biomarkers for melanoma-nevus differentiation beyond absolute SWS.

papers.title: A Preclinical Investigation of Oral Tissues Using Quantitative Ultrasound: Inflammation Tracking and Buccal-Lingual Analysis
papers.abstract: In the USA, 46% of adults aged ≥30 years suffer from periodontal diseases, a spectrum of inflammatory conditions. Currently, standards of care in clinics for inflammation assessment are subjective, qualitative or invasive, presenting a gap in timely and accurate diagnosis. Application of ultrasound imaging in dentistry has become an emerging area recently and quantitative ultrasound (QUS) approaches are largely unexplored for periodontology. Here, we present one of the early implementations of QUS techniques for in vivo oral inflammation characterization in a porcine cohort (N=8). Inflammation was induced in gingival tissues of third premolars through weekly injection of inflammation-inducing bacteria and ligature placement around teeth. Ultrasound scans were acquired at baseline and three inflammation timepoints (24 MHz). QUS parameters of attenuation coefficient and backscatter intensity were considered. We also compared oral tissues at the buccal versus lingual-palatal sides to investigate if the two oral sides are distinct. Our findings showed that QUS have potentials to serve as non-invasive, quantitative biomarkers to complement current standard of care in dentistry.

sessions.title: MSD: Advanced Ultrasound Systems for Imaging, Guidance and Therapy

papers.title: Toward a New Paradigm in Surgical Guidance: Real-Time Multimodal Non-Contact Ultrasound and Photoacoustic Imaging
papers.abstract: We introduce a multimodal non-contact imaging paradigm for surgical guidance by integrating ultrasound (US), photoacoustic (PA), and fluorescence (FL) imaging into a unified platform. Conventional US and PA systems require physical contact, limiting their utility in minimally invasive procedures. Our approach leverages laser Doppler vibrometry (LDV) for remote acoustic detection, enabling volumetric non-contact US/PA imaging. A dual optical architecture with synchronized galvo scanning supports multispectral excitation, while sparse synthetic aperture focusing and adaptive beamforming reduce sampling and suppress artifacts. The system achieves 0.5 Hz imaging over a 1.5 cm² field-of-view, targeting >10 Hz. Ex vivo porcine vagus nerve imaging through overlying fat demonstrated high-contrast spectral PA signatures up to 5 mm depth, with a 7±0.8 dB improvement over conventional methods. Robotic FL microscopy resolved stained tumor cells at microscopic scale. This work establishes a pathway toward real-time, co-registered structural, functional, and molecular imaging for precision surgical intervention.

papers.title: Optical-Guided Automatic Ultrasound multiparametric Imaging for Carotid Artery Screening
papers.abstract: To overcome the operator dependence of traditional carotid ultrasound, we developed an autonomous system integrating optical 3D localization, robotic precision scanning, and ultrafast ultrasound. This system enables operator-independent, multi-parametric assessment of carotid health to facilitate standardized screening. An optical module performs 3D localization of the carotid artery, guiding a 6-DOF robotic arm to execute cardiac-gated scanning via a conformal neck-coupling interface. High-frame-rate plane-wave data are processed on a GPU using spatiotemporal SVD filtering to extract dynamic flow signals. This pipeline reconstructs vessel morphology and simultaneously derives functional metrics, including angle-independent blood flow velocity, wall shear stress (WSS), and local pulse wave velocity (PWV). Validation demonstrates automated 3D imaging with 0.3-mm resolution and velocity measurements (0.2–2 m/s) free of Doppler angle constraints. By providing comprehensive, operator-free carotid profiling including WSS and PWV, this robotic platform enables standardized high-throughput cardiovascular screening in community settings.

papers.title: An Augmented Reality-Based Navigation System for Focused Ultrasound Spinal Stimulation via the Integration of Multi-Modal Image Fusion and Fast Acoustic Field Simulation
papers.abstract: This study presents an augmented reality (AR)-based real-time navigation system for focused ultrasound (FUS) integrating multi-modal image fusion and acoustic field simulation. Conventional ultrasound guidance, such as B-mode imaging, cannot directly visualize acoustic energy distribution or focal location, while simulation-based approaches are typically offline. To overcome these limitations, the proposed system combines CT-derived anatomical models, real-time B-mode ultrasound imaging, and simulated acoustic fields into a unified coordinate framework. CT data are processed using 3D Slicer and aligned with the physical environment via marker-based registration. The FUS transducer is modeled in k-Wave to generate the initial pressure field, which is propagated using the angular spectrum method (ASM) to estimate acoustic distribution. These results are fused and dynamically rendered in AR according to probe motion. The system enables intuitive visualization of acoustic energy propagation, improving spatial awareness and offering potential to enhance targeting accuracy and safety in ultrasound-guided interventions.

papers.title: Noncontact Laser Ultrasound (NCLUS) Clinical Prototype
papers.abstract: We are developing a laser-based medical ultrasound (US) data acquisition system that operates 15 – 30 cm from the patient’s targeted skin region without contact. NCLUS is designed to eliminate probe pose variability seen with handheld transducers and to bypass the need for a sonographer. NCLUS employs a pulsed laser to generate US waves (photoacoustics) consistently within 0.5 mm of the skin surface. A laser Doppler vibrometer array receives returning US echoes at the skin surface. Transmit and receive laser positions are steered by fast scanning mirrors into desired array patterns. NCLUS is a new imaging technique with many advantages, including (1) programmable excitation and receive geometry eliminates fixed transducer geometry, allowing the creation of a near-unlimited range of acquisition array shapes and sizes from a single system; (2) robustly localized transmit and receive locations allow image data to be represented as low-variability spatially localized anatomic “slices,” as with CT and MRI; (3) programmability allows automated large field of view imaging. We are now conducting human subject imaging test trials in a clinical setting.

papers.title: Standardizing Ultrasound Acquisition: Automatic Probe Incidence Angle Tracking for Echocardiography
papers.abstract: Echocardiography maintains a highly operator-dependent procedure where the probe-tissue incidence angle needs to be accurately and robustly controlled to obtain diagnostically meaningful image. To address this problem, this work presents a robotic ultrasound system featuring real-time probe incidence angle tracking using multimodal sensing feedback. The system enables automated probe orientation control for subcostal four chamber (S4C) imaging where the probe is titled to a large angle from the inferior of xiphoid towards the heart. This is achieved by a dual rgb-depth camera mechanism attached to the probe that tracks the local contact surface and thereby a target probe angle with respect to the skin surface normal. The proposed system is validated in three experiment. First, the angular tracking accuracy was calibrated on a flat surface. Next, a phantom study was perform to confirm the feasibility of S4C imaging of a cardiac ultrasound phantom. Finally, the same imaging procedure was performed on a human volunteer under continuous chest motion, further confirming its clinical adaptability

papers.title: A Modular Ultrasound System for Image-Guided Low-Power Therapy
papers.abstract: This work presents a modular ultrasound system for image-guided low-power therapy research. The system is built around a Modular Backplane Board with four configurable slots for 64-channel Transmit/Receive Boards, supporting one to four boards according to the required channel count. Each board provides programmable five-level bipolar excitation with flexible control of amplitude, number of cycles, polarity, duration, and duty cycle. The platform also integrates ultrasound imaging, probe adaptation, system control, clock synchronization, PCIe data transfer, and GPU-based processing. In 64-channel mode, the system can deliver 8 W per channel for 100 μs at up to 600 Hz PRF, or for 10 μs at up to 6667 Hz PRF. Preliminary results demonstrated interleaved B-mode and power Doppler imaging of mouse cerebral microvasculature, hydrophone-measured focal-plane peak-to-peak pressure of approximately 1 MPa, and visible single-droplet ejection under focused pulsed transmission, supporting its feasibility for image-guided low-power therapeutic ultrasound studies.

sessions.title: MPA: Quantitative and Functional Photoacoustic Imaging

papers.title: Photoacoustic Imaging of Evoked Cortical and Subcortical Responses in the Brain of free-Moving Mice
papers.abstract: The mouse is a versatile system for neuroscience research because it allows manipulations that are infeasible in humans. To capture hemodynamic responses in the mouse brain without the interference of anesthesia or restraint, we developed a photoacoustic (PA)/ultrasound (US) imaging system for freely moving mice. We validated the feasibility of capturing evoked hemodynamic responses in anesthetized mice with established visual deficits, and compared the performance of CMUT and piezoelectric US arrays. A prototype head-mount PA/US imaging probe was fabricated and tested in freely moving mice.

papers.title: Automated Assessment of Photoacoustic Breast Image Features to Differentiate Benign from Malignant Lesions
papers.abstract: This work presents the first known automated framework to extract and score photoacoustic biomarkers from multimodal breast images from 42 patients scheduled for ultrasound-guided breast biopsy. Automated scoring reduced assessment time by a factor of 20, while achieving similar sensitivity and specificity. Results are promising for more rapid, objective, and clinically scalable photoacoustic-based breast cancer assessment.

papers.title: A High Frame Rate multi-Perspective Photoacoustic Imaging System Using CMUTs
papers.abstract: Photoacoustic (PA) imaging enables tissue characterization but suffers from limited contrast. A multi-aperture CMUT-based ultrasound (US) /PA system with time-multiplexed shared data channels can improve CNR while preserving low channel count, and boost sensitivity to broadband PA signals. Such a system was presented before but was limited by crosstalk and a low switching rate preventing moving target imaging. We present a solution where time-multiplexing is enabled by fast analog switches and noise is suppressed using a low-noise amplifier (LNA), enabling fast multi-aperture US/PA imaging. The system consists of 3 CMUT modules and a diode laser. US/PA signals are received by CMUTs, time-multiplexed by analog switches, amplified by an LNA, sampled by a Verasonics Vantage system, and reconstructed on a shared grid. Phantoms were imaged to evaluate imaging quality and frame rate. Single and multi-aperture US plaque phantom images demonstrate system gCNR, which is higher for multi- (0.89) than single-aperture imaging (0.41–0.49). Also, multi-aperture US/PA wire phantom images were acquired at 30 Hz, showing potential for real-time moving target imaging, like plaques, in future work.

papers.title: Spatially Regularized Spectral Unmixing for Dual-Wavelength Photoacoustic Breast Oxygenation Imaging
papers.abstract: This work evaluates hemoglobin oxygen saturation (sO2) estimation using spatially regularized spectral unmixing with fluence matching for dual-wavelength photoacoustic breast imaging. Results demonstrate that fluence matching reduces depth-dependent estimation bias, while spatial regularization enhances sO2 map stability, showing promise to improve in vivo oxygenation measurements.

papers.title: A Novel Label-Free Intensity-Independent Differential Spectral Photoacoustic Approach for Nerve Imaging
papers.abstract: Nerve preservation during cancer resection is critical, yet conventional fluorescence imaging requires contrast agents and has limited depth. While photoacoustic (PA) spectroscopy enables label-free tissue identification, it is time-consuming and noise-sensitive. This study proposes a nerve detection technique using only 5 wavelengths by estimating multi-order spectral derivatives. PA spectra analysis of animal-extracted nerve and fat tissues revealed a distinctive peak at 980 nm unique to nerves. The spectrum around this region was modeled as a polynomial function, and coefficients representing multi-order derivatives were estimated, excluding the absolute intensity term for intensity independence. Logistic Regression was applied to derive a classification metric, which was fused with PA images for noise suppression. Results demonstrated high detection reproducibility with an AUC of 0.961 (p < 0.001), confirming excellent discriminative ability between nerve and fat tissue.

papers.title: An All Optical Photoacoustic Imaging Needle for Assessing Microscopic Tissue Morphology
papers.abstract: We developed an interstitial photoacoustic (PA) imaging needle that delivers optical illumination and acquires the generated signals in the close vicinity of the regions of interest, with the purpose of capturing high-frequency PA signals encoding microscopic tissue architecture. The needle includes a fiber optic diffuser for PA illumination and a microring-resonator array for multi-channel PA signal detection. The imaging needle shows an imaging depth of at least 5mm in human prostate ex vivo. By quantifying image texture using PA spectral analysis, we can differentiate normal from cancerous regions (p < 0.005, n=11). We also detected a significant difference between normal and cancerous mouse prostates (p<0.05, n=12,12).

sessions.title: MIS: Clutter Suppression & Image Enhancement

papers.title: High Frame Rate CPWC Denoising via Denoising Diffusion Implicit Modeling
papers.abstract: Coherent plane-wave compounding (CPWC) enables ultrafast ultrasound imaging, but image quality degrades when only a few plane waves (PWs) are used, leading to strong speckle and angular undersampling artifacts. Diffusion models have served as powerful denoising backbones, also in the context of CPWC, however, largely relying on the assumption of Gaussian (GA) corruption model. This work investigates the noise statistics of low-PW CPWC, observing that they are often non-GA, and aims to develop a diffusion denoiser better matched to the observed degradation, enabling higher frame rates without sacrificing contrast. First, we analyze the beamformed compounded RF residual between low-PW CPWC and a 75-PW reference using PICMUS in vivo carotid data. The QQ plots and histogram fits in Fig. A show that the residuals are better described by a Laplacian (LAP) than by a GA distribution, motivating a heavy-tailed noise prior. We therefore formulate a novel LAP denoising diffusion implicit model (DDIM) in which the forward process is defined by direct marginal corruption and train the noise predictor with an L1 objective, which also follows from the LAP noise distribution.

papers.title: SVD-SN2N: Self-Inspired Noise2Noise Learning for Denoising log-Compressed SVD-Filtered Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: Singular value decomposition (SVD) is the reference clutter-rejection strategy for ultrafast ultrasound microvascular imaging, but SVD-filtered images retain a residual speckle-like noise floor that masks contrast signals, especially at depth. Supervised deep denoising is impractical here because clean references are unavailable, training sets are short, and most physics-based ultrasound denoisers operate on radio-frequency or in-phase/quadrature data not exposed by clinical scanners. This study proposes SVD-SN2N, a self-supervised Noise2Noise framework that operates entirely at image level, requires neither clean targets nor RF/IQ access, and trains from a single short ultrasound acquisition.SVD-SN2N was validated on 4 datasets in total, including a public contrast-enhance rat-brain imaging dataset, a clinical human breast tumor CEUS acquisition exported only as DICOM frames, a contrast-free rat brain imaging dataset, and a 3D RCA rat brain image dataset. SVD-SN2N improves SNR by 10.6 dB over conventional SVD across deep regions and reduces vessel full-width-at-half-maximum by 34–59 % in both axial and lateral directions.

papers.title: Noise Characterization of Ultrasound Data with Simulation-Based Inference
papers.abstract: Ultrasound signals are degraded by reverberation and aberration. While each noise source has been separately studied and removed before, they confound each other. In this work, we present a method to jointly infer reverberation and aberration levels using a simulation-based inference (SBI) framework. This approach overcomes the limitations of sequential processing and enables spatially resolved inference of physical noise parameters. SBI trains a neural posterior estimator on simulated data-parameter pairs to yield a multivariate posterior. In this work, we used Field II to simulate diffuse scattering channel data under a near-field phase screen with additive reverberation. The parameters are the root-mean-square (RMS) and full-width-half-max (FWHM) of the phase screen, and the signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR). We compared the mean of the learned posterior over SCR, RMS, and FWHM with baseline and validated SBI with k-Wave abdominal simulations. SBI demonstrated better ability to estimate RMS in the presence of reverberation, and achieved consistent estimates with baseline methods in k-Wave and in vivo data without being trained on those datasets.

papers.title: The Effective Contrast Ratio: a Robust Performance Metric for Pulse-Echo Ultrasound
papers.abstract: In ultrasound B-mode imaging, traditional quality metrics such as the contrast ratio are designed for linear beamformers and may be misleading for modern nonlinear beamformers. There is therefore a need to develop more robust contrast metrics. Here, we present the effective contrast order, a metric that is signed, unbiased, simple to implement, invariant to strictly monotonic dynamic range transformations, and equal to the contrast ratio for Rayleigh speckle imaged with a linear beamformer (thus providing an interpretation familiar to the ultrasound community). We verify through simulations the different properties of the proposed metric and compare it to the contrast ratio.

papers.title: Adaptive, Constrained, and Interpretable Clutter Suppression with Deep Learning
papers.abstract: Color flow imaging relies on clutter filtering to separate blood from tissue. High-pass filters fail under spectral overlap, eigen-based methods are unstable at short ensembles, and end-to-end deep learning (DL) is flexible but hard to validate. We here constrained an adaptive DL-based filter to predict a positive semi-definite filter matrix per slow-time ensemble from in-phase and quadrature signals at packet size N=6, parameterized as orthonormal basis vectors and weighting coefficients. This matches the degrees of freedom of subspace filters like singular value decomposition (SVD), enabling per-ensemble inspection of filter attributes. Training used 20,250 cardiac frames from 37 patients, supervised against polynomial regression at N=12. At N=6, our method reached 0.06 ± 0.01 m/s mean absolute velocity difference in flow regions against the N=12 reference, outperforming end-to-end DL (0.10 ± 0.02), SVD (0.11 ± 0.03), and polynomial regression (0.20 ± 0.04) on 5,120 frames from 9 patients. It generalized to abdominal imaging without retraining. This enables higher frame rates, larger ROIs, and improved slow flow detection and visualization of rapid hemodynamic events.

papers.title: RF-Domain Temporal-Median Residual Low-Rank Stripe Suppression for Transcranial Power Doppler Imaging
papers.abstract: In vivo transcranial power Doppler (PD) imaging acquired in clinical settings is often degraded by structured stripe-like contamination embedded in multi-angle channel RF data, likely related to electrical interference. We propose an RF-domain temporal-median residual low-rank stripe suppression method as a preprocessing front-end for standard PD formation. For each transmit angle, a local temporal median template is estimated from channel RF data and subtracted from the raw frame to form a residual, in which stripe contamination becomes more separable. Singular value decomposition is then used to identify and suppress dominant stripe components before DAS beamforming, angle compounding, clutter filtering, power integration, noise normalization, and dB display. In a representative in vivo transcranial dataset, the method reduced background contamination, improved vessel conspicuity, and revealed deeper vascular structures that were faint or obscured in the raw PD images.

sessions.title: MSR: CapilHarry Spotter

papers.title: Microbubble Tracking Through Cluster Analysis for Super-Resolution Ultrasound Localization Microscopy
papers.abstract: Ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) has emerged as a powerful technique for visualizing microvascular structures by localizing and tracking individual microbubbles (MBs) over time. Previous MB tracking studies have mainly relied on frame-to-frame association strategies, such as nearest-neighbor or bipartite matching, which might become unreliable under limited frame rates and high MB concentrations, thus lengthening the acquisition duration. For the first time, a MB tracking through cluster analysis (TCA) framework is developed that incorporates local flow orientations and anisotropic spatiotemporal constraints. Furthermore, improved matching accuracy, high-quality super-resolution vascular and velocity imaging results demonstrate its advanced performance.

papers.title: Integrated super-Resolution Ultrasound Imaging of Cerebrovascular and Cerebrospinal Fluid Dynamics in the Mouse Brain
papers.abstract: We developed an integrated three-dimensional super-resolution ultrasound platform for concurrent imaging of cerebrovascular structure and ventricular cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics in the mouse brain. The framework combines ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) with ULM-based ventricular CSF imaging, using transcranial matrix-array imaging and cisterna magna microbubble delivery. Sequential volumetric acquisition was tailored to the distinct flow regimes of vascular and CSF signals, enabling unified localization, tracking, and reconstruction of vascular maps and CSF flow pathways within the same session. In healthy mice, the method enabled simultaneous co-visualization of vascular architecture and ventricular CSF pathways. In a hydrocephalus model, it further detected reduced ventricular CSF velocity patterns together with decreased cortical microvascular density relative to sham controls.

papers.title: Longitudinal Awake Mouse Brain Imaging Using Functional Ultrasound and Functional Ultrasound Localization Microscopy
papers.abstract: This study establishes the long-term stability and baseline variability of integrated functional ultrasound (fUS), ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM), and functional ULM (fULM) imaging in awake mice. Using a 5-month longitudinal design with repeated monthly imaging in the same animals, we quantified vascularity, blood flow velocity, fUS-derived cerebral blood volume responses, and fULM-derived microbubble flow responses. No imaging metric showed a significant longitudinal trend, supporting the stability of the multimodal ultrasound framework over time. Structural and flow-based measurements were more reproducible than functional responses, with mean flow velocity showing the highest consistency and lowest detection threshold. Chronic awake imaging did not induce memory impairment or persistent neuroinflammation. These findings provide reference variability ranges and detection thresholds for future longitudinal studies using fUS, ULM, and fULM to investigate disease-related neurovascular changes in awake animal models.

papers.title: An Open Benchmarking Framework for Standardized Functional Ultrasound Localization Microscopy (fULM) Evaluation
papers.abstract: Functional ultrasound localization microscopy (fULM) enables brain-wide hemodynamic imaging at microvascular resolution, but its functional readouts depend critically on microbubble (MB) localization and tracking accuracy. Existing benchmarks address only structural microvascular imaging and cannot guide fULM toward high temporal fidelity, since transient hemodynamic responses make missed detections and broken tracks directly bias functional estimates. To address this gap, we develop a benchmarking framework tailored to functional imaging, comprising four components: a simulation strategy with time-varying hemodynamics for ground-truth-known evaluation; an open in vivo fULM dataset from awake mice under whisker stimulation, with manually curated, multi-pass verified annotations; an evaluation workflow that pairs fULM-specific metrics with parameter-tuning guidance to support cross-operator standardization; and an interactive GUI that lowers the barrier to high-fidelity reconstructions and makes the interplay between localization and tracking parameters more intuitive to explore. Collectively, these contributions move fULM toward a more reproducible neuroimaging modality.

papers.title: Volumetric Ultrasound Localization Microscopy (3D ULM) of Neonatal Cerebral Microcirculation in Intensive Care
papers.abstract: The neonatal brain is highly vulnerable to microvascular injury. Currently, neurovascular imaging relies on MRI, which necessitates high-risk patient transport, or conventional ultrasound, which lacks microcirculatory resolution. To address these limitations, this study presents the first bedside application of volumetric (3D) Ultrasound Localization Microscopy (ULM) in a neonatal intensive care unit. The procedure was performed on an intubated neonate suffering from perinatal asphyxia. A matrix array probe (3.2 MHz) positioned over the fontanelle, combined with an intravenous microbubble injection, enabled ultrafast acquisition (1,000 volumes/s for 90 seconds). Following advanced signal processing—including spatiotemporal tissue filtering and 3D microbubble tracking—the cerebral microvasculature was non-invasively reconstructed at an unprecedented resolution. Over 7.2 million trajectories were successfully accumulated. This approach demonstrates the significant clinical potential of 3D ULM for continuous, bedside neurovascular monitoring, thereby safely circumventing the logistical challenges and inherent risks of patient transport.

papers.title: Point-Cloud Processing Pipeline for 3D Functional Ultrasound Localization Microscopy
papers.abstract: In ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM), functional data is typically analyzed on rasterized voxel grids, introducing grid artifacts and substantial computational overhead especially in three dimensions. We present a continuous-domain pipeline for 3D functional ULM that bypasses rasterization by operating directly on the point-cloud representation of the data, retaining full localization precision throughout the analysis. We demonstrate the pipeline on a rat visual task dataset: our point-cloud skeletonization algorithm extracts centerlines of the brain-wide vascular network in continuous space, not bounded by any rasterization grid. Vessel radius is estimated from the radial distribution of microbubble detections, enabling accurate vascular surface reconstruction. Microbubble flux and velocity are then analyzed along each vascular segment, with spatial smoothing applied along vessels to improve signal-to-noise ratio while preserving vascular boundaries. Correlating hemodynamic signals with the stimulation paradigm yields 3D correlation maps revealing activation in the superior colliculus with strong correlations up to 0.7.

sessions.title: TTT: Therapeutic Transducers and Systems

papers.title: * INVITED * System Development and Integration for Therapeutic Ultrasound Applications: the Pathway to Portability
papers.abstract: The application of ultrasound technology to medical therapeutics, which has been in development for decades, is now seeing a massive increase both in pre-clinical and clinical uptake across a wide variety of applications. This vast increase brings with it pressure for the commercialization of existing research systems as well as the development of new systems capable of rapidly pivoting based on clinical need. To fully address these new challenges, solutions are needed which combine the high integration levels of modern diagnostic systems with larger apertures, higher output powers, better thermal handling and more novel pulsing and focusing control, while also addressing regulatory and safety requirements.

papers.title: Forward-Treating catheter-Based Transducer with Coded Piezoelectric metasurface for Precision Thrombolysis
papers.abstract: Large vessel occlusion stroke causes approximately 90% of all stroke-related deaths. These occlusions are traditionally removed through thrombectomy. However, only 55% of clots are successfully removed on the first attempt. We propose a miniature endovascular therapy transducer with varying beam width to dissolve clots of varying sizes while minimizing acoustic output to the vessel wall. Conventional transducers can only produce 1 beam pattern. By poling different regions of a single piezoelectric material in alternating directions (i.e., phase shift of π), the same device can produce two unique beams at two different frequencies. A 3 mm transducer was fabricated with two resonance frequencies and the described metasurface coding. The coding was performed by isolating surface electrodes, then alternating the poling direction within specific regions by applying 500 V for 5 minutes. When the transducer is excited at 400 kHz, most of the acoustic energy remains towards the center of the field to dissolve a smaller clot in a narrower artery. When the frequency is increased to 2300 kHz, the spatial extent of the acoustic energy increases to dissolve a larger clot in a larger artery.

papers.title: Fermat-Spiral Submillimeter Spherical Phased-Array Transducer for Precision Ultrasound Therapy
papers.abstract: A 104-element spherical phased-array ultrasound transducer based on a Fermat spiral layout was designed, fabricated, and experimentally characterized for precision ultrasound therapy. Acoustic simulations were performed using the MATLAB-based FOCUS toolbox to optimize the element distribution, operating frequency, and focal performance while suppressing grating lobes. The array has a 60 mm radius of curvature, 4 mm element diameter, and operates at approximately 1.43 MHz. A high-precision 3D-printed shell was used for assembly, and impedance measurements confirmed consistent resonant behavior across all elements. Acoustic fields were measured in a water tank using a 0.2 mm needle hydrophone and compared with simulations. The simulated −6 dB focal spot dimensions were 0.63 mm laterally and 1.73 mm axially, while experimental results showed 0.66 mm laterally and 2.00 mm axially. The agreement between simulated and measured pressure profiles validates the design model. The achieved submillimeter lateral focal spot demonstrates the potential of Fermat spiral spherical phased arrays for high-precision focused ultrasound therapy and drug delivery applications.

papers.title: Ultrasound Array with Suppressed Backing Dissipation and Imaging Capability for Tumor Perfusion Enhancement
papers.abstract: Tumor hypoperfusion can reduce the efficacy of chemotherapy and radiotherapy. Ultrasound-stimulated microbubble-mediated perfusion enhancement offers a potential strategy to address this limitation, but requires an ultrasound array with both effective power output and real-time imaging capability. Conventional imaging arrays suffer from backing dissipation, reducing transmit efficiency. In this study, a dual anti-matching-layer (AML) structure was designed to suppress backing dissipation while preserving imaging capability. A 128-element ultrasound array was fabricated using a 2–2 piezoelectric composite and front-side dual matching layers. The proposed array reduced backing power leakage by approximately 30dB, achieved 1.38 times higher electroacoustic efficiency, maintained a fractional bandwidth above 60%, and increased pulse–echo amplitude by approximately 40%. Acoustic field mapping and preliminary biological experiments supported its feasibility for imaging-guided tumor perfusion enhancement.

papers.title: 6-DOF Pose-Aware Flexible Transcranial Focused Ultrasound System
papers.abstract: This work presents a 6-DOF pose-aware flexible transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) system designed to improve targeting accuracy under skull-induced aberrations. By integrating magnetic sensing, CT-based image registration, and K-Wave acoustic simulation within a unified coordinate framework, the system enables precise mapping between physical transducer positions and simulation space. A flexible 8+1 elements array is developed to conform to curved skull surfaces, while nine magnetic sensors provide real-time pose tracking. Using rigid-body transformation based on fiducial markers, transducer alignment is accurately registered with sub-millimeter error. Time-reversal methods are applied to compute phase delays for focus correction, and experimental validation using hydrophone measurements confirms effective focusing with predictable distortion. The approach demonstrates improved adaptability over conventional rigid systems and provides a foundation for future closed-loop, real-time optimization in dynamic tFUS applications.

sessions.title: AHV: High Velocity Devices

papers.title: * INVITED * RF and mmWave Acoustic Resonators and Filters Based on Ferroelectric ScAlN Thin Films
papers.abstract: Recent advances in scandium-doped aluminum nitride (ScAlN) have opened new opportunities for high-performance RF and mmWave acoustic devices through the exploitation of its enhanced piezoelectricity and ferroelectricity. This talk presents the latest progress in ferroelectric ScAlN thin-film engineering and its application to resonators and filters targeting next-generation wireless systems.

papers.title: A Low Loss 8.3 GHz Sezawa SAW Delay Line Based on Al0.6Sc0.4N-on-SiC
papers.abstract: This work demonstrates an 8.3 GHz Sezawa-mode surface acoustic wave (SAW) acoustic delay line (ADL) based on a thin-film Al0.6Sc0.4N-on-SiC platform. ADLs are attractive for true-time-delay systems because they provide passive and high-delay-density signal delay, but scaling them beyond 6 GHz while maintaining low loss and useful delay remains challenging. The device uses a 250 nm Al0.6Sc0.4N film on 4H-SiC with a designed wavelength of 0.83 um, corresponding to hAlScN/lambda ~ 0.3. Bi-directional IDTs with 40 pairs and a 50lambda aperture were defined by e-beam lithography and lift-off with 55 nm Al after AlScN co-sputtering. Devices with delay lengths from 40lambda to 600lambda were fabricated for propagation extraction. After conjugate matching and time-gated IL extraction, the ADLs exhibit ILs from 10 to 23.7 dB and group delays from 9 to 86 ns at 8.32 GHz with 1.8% fractional bandwidth. The extracted propagation loss and group velocity are 28.6 dB/mm and 6042.7 m/s, corresponding to a propagation Q-factor of 1314. These results establish AlScN-on-SiC as a promising solidly mounted SAW platform for high-frequency, low-loss acoustic delay elements.

papers.title: Third Harmonic Acoustic Boundary Wave Excited by Buried IDT in LiNbO3 with Velocity Higher Than 11 km/S
papers.abstract: Acoustic wave devices operating above 7 GHz are increasingly required for mobile communication systems. However, in conventional surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices, the wavelength (λ) of interdigital transducers (IDTs) must exceed ~1 μm due to power-handling limitations, restricting the operating frequency to 3–4 GHz. To overcome this, third-harmonic excitation using buried IDTs (BIDTs) in 26°YX-LiNbO₃ (LN) has enabled devices in the 8–9 GHz range. In this study, we propose an acoustic boundary wave (ABW) device based on a SiN-covered BIDT-in-LN structure and investigate its third-harmonic operation. The proposed structure exhibits a large coupling factor (k² ≈ 17%), about four times higher than that of a conventional IDT-on-LN (~4%) and comparable to BIDT-in-LN. It also achieves a higher effective anti-resonance velocity of ~11 km/s. Experiments using Al-embedded BIDT-SAW devices on 64°YX-LN with a SiN film show that the velocity becomes nearly constant for SiN thicknesses above 0.6λ. In addition, no frequency shift is observed after resin coating, confirming boundary-wave propagation along the SiN/LN interface. This structure enables cavity-less packaging.

papers.title: Towards Ku-Band Longitudinal Leaky SAW Devices Utilizing LiTaO3/SiC Substrate
papers.abstract: With the ongoing development of 5G and the evolution toward 6G, there is a growing demand to extend acoustic filter technologies into the FR3 band. Conventional acoustic filtering solutions, such as surface acoustic wave (SAW) and bulk acoustic wave (BAW) devices, are widely used in sub-6 GHz. Further scaling them to the X- and Ku-band (8-18 GHz) remains challenging due to the degradation of quality factor (Q) and increased fabrication cost. In this work, Ku-band SAW filters on a low-loss X-LiTaO3/SiC hetero-substrate are demonstrated by utilizing high-velocity longitudinal leaky SAW (LLSAW). Besides, a tilted IDT is adopted to suppress transverse modes. By optimizing the tilt angle and length of dummy fingers through simulations, acoustic energy is effectively confined within the IDT region, enabling a high Q factor. The fabricated LLSAW resonators operating at 10-15 GHz exhibit spurious-free responses with an extremely high Q of 1220. The fabricated filters achieve center frequencies up to 14 GHz, with decent bandwidth and high out-of-band rejections. With further optimization, the proposed LLSAW filter shows strong potential for compact cmWave signal processing applications.

papers.title: Ultra-Wideband Surface Acoustic Wave Delay Lines Utilizing 500 nm Al_0.58Sc_0.42N on 4H-SiC
papers.abstract: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices are attractive due to their high performance, small size and ease of manufacturing. Delay lines are one of the most common SAW topologies with applications in radar, oscillators, equalizers and interference suppression. Achieving large bandwidth, low insertion loss delay lines at high frequencies are desirable for many of these applications. This work focuses on an AlScN on SiC material stack that takes advantage of the impedance mismatch of the two to propagate the high velocity Sezawa mode, while mitigating internal reflectivity with a 5-finger pair split finger aluminum interdigitated transducer (IDT) topology designed for a 1 µm wavelength. Apertures of 75, 100, and 125 λ are studied with delay distances swept from 250 to 400 µm in 25 µm steps. A fractional bandwidth over 18%, corresponding to 1.2 GHz at a 6.6 GHz center frequency is observed, with a minimum insertion loss of 15.9 dB achieved when conjugate matched. The propagation loss is found to be 15.8 dB/mm with a 0.17 ns/µm propagation delay. The simplicity and performance of this design make it ideal for high frequency, wide bandwidth, miniature delay lines.

sessions.title: NMC: Ultrasonic Characterization of Multiphase Media, Structures, and Biological Systems

papers.title: Guided Wave Mode Identification and Eccentricity Angle Characterization for Non-Axisymmetric Acoustic Fields in Liquid-Filled Double-Layered Pipes
papers.abstract: Double-layer liquid-filled pipes are widely used in energy transportation, offshore engineering, and wellbore structures, but eccentricity complicates guided-wave analysis because of non-axisymmetry, fluid–structure coupling, and difficulties in dispersion-curve identification. This study proposes a unified post-processing method for guided wave mode identification and eccentricity angle characterization in non-axisymmetric acoustic fields. Dispersion modes are identified by constraining the circumferential order from the Fourier transform of structural maximum displacement. A mirror-error function based on displacement-amplitude distribution is used to determine the symmetry axis of each mode, and a statistical consistency criterion is introduced for eccentricity angle characterization. The method is validated for concentric and 0°, 45°, and 90° eccentric pipes, and the identified symmetry axes agree with the structural eccentric orientation.

papers.title: Ultrasonic Metamaterial Filters for Enhanced Microbubble Harmonic Imaging
papers.abstract: Acoustic metamaterials with engineered band gaps enable frequency-selective control of ultrasonic waves, offering a passive alternative to conventional filtering. In contrast-enhanced ultrasound imaging, weak nonlinear emissions from microbubbles (e.g., subharmonic and ultraharmonic components) are often masked by strong fundamental responses, while digital filtering is limited by reduced dynamic range. We propose a metallic acoustic metamaterial filter based on a periodic array of steel pillars in water. Band structure and frequency-domain simulations identify operating regimes and transmission loss characteristics. To address fabrication challenges at sub-millimeter scales, the structure is realized using CNC-etched steel plates stacked to form a three-dimensional metamaterial. Experimental and numerical results show strong attenuation (~40 dB) over 430–620 kHz, consistent with predicted band gaps arising from Bragg scattering. The results demonstrate effective suppression of targeted frequencies while preserving transmission in the passband, highlighting the potential of acoustic metamaterials for ultrasound signal filtering.

papers.title: Oil Droplet Size Influences Speed-of-Sound and Acoustic Attenuation of Oil-in-Water Emulsions
papers.abstract: Oil-in-water (O/W) emulsions are a core component of the food and pharmaceutical industries. Made by dispersing oil droplets in aqueous media, O/W can enhance food texture and control drug delivery. However, there is a lack of understanding on how the oil droplet size would affect SoS and AC in O/W, so the efficacy of SoS and AC measurements in milk has remained nebulous. To address this gap, we have investigated O/W of different oil droplet sizes to test the reliability of SoS and AC measurements.

papers.title: Multi-Modal Ultrasound Characterization of 3D Bioprinted Liver Constructs
papers.abstract: 3D bioprinted liver constructs offer a promising solution to donor organ shortages, but noninvasive quality assessment during culture remains an unmet need. This study evaluates multimodal high-frequency ultrasound — combining 3D B-mode, quantitative ultrasound (QUS), and shear wave elastography (SWE) — for nondestructive characterization of bioprinted liver constructs. Constructs were fabricated using a BIONOVA X bioprinter with hepatocytes at 30 and 70 M cells/mL, with ex vivo mouse liver as reference. 3D B-mode resolved internal channel architecture with high fidelity (measured vs. designed inlet diameter: 0.41 vs. 0.40 mm). Attenuation and backscatter coefficients both increased with cell density, while SWE distinguished live (1.78 kPa), fixed (39.7 kPa), and ex vivo (10.64 kPa) constructs. Together, these complementary acoustic metrics spanning structural, compositional, and mechanical properties demonstrate the potential of high-frequency ultrasound as a real-time, nondestructive quality monitoring platform for bioprinted liver constructs.

papers.title: Temperature-Enhanced Acoustic Contrast for Tumor Detection: a Computational Study of Ultrasound Response in Skin Tissue
papers.abstract: Skin cancer detection relies on visual inspection and biopsy, which are limited in subsurface sensitivity and are invasive. Ultrasound sensing offers a non-invasive alternative, but distinguishing subtle tissue differences remains challenging. This work introduces non-invasive temperature-enhanced acoustic sensing, where temperature-dependent variations in tissue properties (e.g., stiffness, attenuation, and scattering) amplify contrast between healthy and tumor tissues. A 3D COMSOL model (40 × 40 × 20 mm) of skin tissue, with and without a 2 mm tumor, was developed and evaluated at 30 °C, 37 °C, and 44 °C using a Peltier-controlled boundary. Two angled piezoelectric transducers were used for through-transmission analysis. Results show temperature-dependent spectral variations near ~100 kHz, with increased separation between tumor and healthy responses at higher temperatures. Time-domain signals exhibit higher received amplitudes in tumor cases, with contrast further enhanced as temperature rises. This work demonstrates that temperature modulation can magnify acoustic differences between tissues, enabling improved tumor detectability.

papers.title: Nonlinear Ultrasound Detection of Hydrogen Embrittlement in Aluminum
papers.abstract: Early indications of material degradation such as precursors to fatigue cracks is evident nondestructively from nonlinear ultrasound, whereby the waveform is distorted by the microstructural changes associated with degradation. At the continuum level the waveform distortion is related to the acoustic nonlinearity parameter, which is defined in terms of the third order (and second order) elastic constants. Fatigue cracks are initiated by dislocation dynamics, which can be modelled to predict the relation between the microstructure and the acoustic nonlinearity parameter. However, hydrogen embrittlement is a degradation mechanism that has received far less attention. The objective of this presentation is to show that first principles can be used to model hydrogen embrittlement in an aluminum alloy as well as to show supporting experimental second harmonic generation results.

sessions.title: SPT: Ultrasound Neural Stimulation and Guidance - Enabling Technologies - I

papers.topicName: Spotlight Session: Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Devices & Applications
papers.title: * INVITED * Ultrasound Neuromodulation and Sonogenetics
papers.abstract: Noninvasive and precise control of neuronal activity in the deep brain is essential for probing brain function and developing treatments for neurological disorders. Transcranial low-intensity ultrasound has emerged as a promising neuromodulation modality because of its noninvasiveness, deep tissue penetration, and high spatiotemporal precision. However, the focal volume of an ultrasound beam remains substantially larger than a small neuronal population, limiting its ability to selectively target specific neurons, manipulate defined neural circuits, and elicit desired behaviors. In this talk, I will present evidence supporting ultrasound neuromodulation and highlight the critical role of mechanosensitive ion channels as key mediators of this process. In addition, I will also describe our efforts to develop and refine sonogenetics, beginning with initial in vitro proof-of-concept studies, followed by in vivo validation in the deep striatum, and extending to the modulation of higher-order behaviors through pathway-specific targeting. Finally, I will discuss the potential utility of sonogenetics across a range of neurological disease models.

papers.topicName: Spotlight Session: Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Devices & Applications
papers.title: * INVITED * Computational Approaches to transcranial Ultrasound Brain Imaging in Adults
papers.abstract: Transcranial ultrasound brain imaging has a broad range of potential applications, including intracerebral hemorrhage detection, brain perfusion assessment, cerebrovascular disease diagnosis, and functional imaging of neural activity. Despite this promise, transcranial ultrasound imaging in adults remains limited because the human skull introduces severe attenuation, phase aberration, and reverberation of ultrasound waves. This talk presents recent efforts in computational imaging to address these challenges and to advance transcranial ultrasound brain imaging. Specifically, we will introduce methods for correcting skull-induced phase aberration; evaluate the accuracy and computational efficiency of different aberration correction strategies; describe progress in skull acoustic property characterization and modeling; present the development and validation of a new numerical simulation framework for realistic skull modeling; and discuss technical innovations to improve full-waveform inversion for transcranial brain imaging.

papers.topicName: Spotlight Session: Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Devices & Applications
papers.title: In Vivo Neuromodulation of the Mouse Cortex via a 4V-Driven Focused Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Focused ultrasound (FUS) enables non-invasive neuromodulation. Piezoelectric Micromachined Ultrasonic Transducers (PMUTs) provide a miniaturized, low-power platform uniquely suited for integrated in vivo systems. This study demonstrates a custom, ultra-low-voltage (4V) PMUT array designed to precisely elicit and quantify parameter-tunable neural responses in mice medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) using real-time calcium imaging as a reference.

papers.topicName: Spotlight Session: Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Devices & Applications
papers.title: A Miniature Ultrasound System to Stimulate Peripheral Neural System
papers.abstract: A system to use ultrasound to generate sense of touch at fingertips with high spatial and temporal resolution is designed, implemented and characterized through psychometric experiments. The system improves over existing systems in terms of size and lateral resolution by increasing operation frequency by about an order of magnitude and can enable multi-finger and spatial mapping studies.

sessions.title: MIM: Methods for Volumetric Ultrasound Imaging

papers.title: Free-Hand 3D Ultrasound Imaging via Dual-Plane Motion Estimation with a Zipper Array
papers.abstract: Free-hand 3D ultrasound is clinically attractive, but its accuracy has been bottlenecked by single-plane speckle decorrelation, which loses reliability beyond a fraction of a millimeter in practice. We propose the use of a zipper array — two linear sub-arrays with diagonally cut elements — that produces two closely spaced imaging planes with a known left–right (L/R) separation, enabling direct dual-plane motion estimation. This work develops a robust 6-DOF free-hand 3D framework on a zipper array. A 6-DOF model parameterizes probe motion as in-plane (x, z, α) and out-of-plane (y, β, γ) components. Paired L/R cyst-phantom sequences were acquired with a zipper-array probe on a programmable array system, with a six-axis platform supplying ground-truth motion. The algorithm combines Kabsch with Lucas–Kanade (LK) optical flow on the two planes. Note that dual-plane speckle tracking improves y, and the improved y directly improves β and γ. Phantom experimental results show the y-displacement map with R² = 0.93, matching the physical L/R separation, and volumetric error stayed below 5%, demonstrating free-hand 3D ultrasound beyond decorrelation limits.

papers.title: High-Frequency Power Doppler 3D Vascular Mapping for Pre-Transplant Surgical Planning in Ex-Vivo Livers on Normothermic Machine Perfusion
papers.abstract: Variant donor liver vascular anatomy is common and can complicate transplant surgery. High-frequency power Doppler (HFPD) enables non-invasive, contrast-free vascular visualization with superior resolution over conventional systems. On normothermic machine perfusion (NMP), ex-vivo livers can be imaged without intervening tissue, enabling pre-transplant 3D vascular mapping. Freehand 15 MHz HFPD sweeps were acquired in 17 ex-vivo liver allografts on NMP, with IMU-based motion tracking enabling geometrically accurate 3D reconstruction and active contour segmentation applied to isolate vascular structure. Minimum detectable vessel diameter was 400–450 µm, resolving overlapping vessels within a single imaging plane. HFPD signal was preserved in severely steatotic livers despite degraded B-mode resolution, suggesting robustness across donor liver quality. This work demonstrates a portable, contrast-free pipeline for high-resolution 3D vascular mapping of liver allografts, with potential to support surgical planning and intraoperative decision-making.

papers.title: Fully Volumetric Cross Amplitude Modulation (VxAM)
