papers.abstract: Cross-amplitude modulation (xAM) is the gold-standard pulse sequence for non-destructive detection of gas-vesicle (GV) ultrasound contrast agents, but has been restricted to 2D imaging on 1D linear arrays. We present the first implementation of xAM on a fully sampled 2D matrix array, generalizing the half-aperture splitting of conventional xAM to three primary 2D bisection strategies (X-axis, Y-axis, diagonal) on a 32×32-element Vermon probe (7.81 MHz) driven by four synchronized Verasonics Vantage 256 scanners (1024 channels, fully addressed). The optimal partition was determined in silico by jointly maximizing peak positive pressure (PPP) and along-beam field homogeneity. The Y-split won on both metrics; in simulation, asymmetric beam steering caused xAM bisector incoherence beyond ±2.4 mm, motivating automated robotic translation of the probe. Agarose phantoms loaded with purified, stripped Ana GVs were imaged using only the Y-split with an α-sweep that peaked at α = 6°; CTR at α = 6° was 16.5 dB. These results motivate an extension to transcranial simulation and transcranial imaging.

papers.title: Null Subtraction Imaging for Improved Resolution in 3D Row-Column Addressed Ultrasound: a Phantom Study
papers.abstract: Row-column addressed (RCA) arrays enable 3D ultrasound imaging of volumetric microvasculature with a low channel count. However, conventional delay-and-sum (DAS) beamforming for RCA’s orthogonal geometry yields anisotropic point spread functions and heavy sidelobe artifacts, limiting spatial resolution and contrast. Null subtraction imaging (NSI), a receive-apodization scheme, has been proposed to improve the spatial resolution. Nevertheless, existing NSI formulations are not directly applicable to RCA geometry. In this work, we proposed a 3D RCA-NSI framework, which synthesizes voxel-projected sub-apertures across the two orthogonal transmit-receive pathways to improve spatial resolution and contrast.

papers.title: Wide Composite Volumetric Imaging of the Human Liver
papers.abstract: Expanding the imaging aperture improves lateral resolution by lowering the f-number and also enlarges the field of view (FOV), both of which are valuable when evaluating entire organs. Broader volumetric acquisition can further reduce reliance on operator technique. In this study applied to the adult liver, we acquire and reconstruct large volumes from angular scans obtained with a wide 1D phased array (88-mm aperture, 384 elements, 2.5 MHz center frequency). We combine multiple volumetric scans to survey more than 70% of the adult liver (surveyed volume of 22×15×13 cm3 ). Visualization and automatic extraction of vascular landmarks (Inferior vena cava, hepatic and portal veins) is demonstrated.

papers.title: Generalized Transmission Modeling for Matrix Imaging with Flexible Acquisition Schemes
papers.abstract: Matrix imaging enables ultrasound aberration correction and quantitative tissue analysis, but its current implementations are largely formulated for plane-wave transmissions with linear arrays. This limits its use in more general imaging settings, where diverging or focused transmissions are commonly used. This work proposes a generalized transmission model that separates transmit delay encoding from acoustic wave propagation, allowing a unified model to accommodate plane-wave, single-element, diverging-wave, and focused transmissions. The proposed model extends matrix imaging and matrix-imaging-based techniques, such as aberration correction, to more flexible acquisition schemes and transducer geometries. The proposed framework was validated on phantom and human placental studies using a convex probe, where it improved image quality in terms of spatial resolution and contrast.

sessions.title: MEL: Kevin Parker Memorial Session: Innovations in Ultrasound Elastography

papers.title: Ultrasound Shear Wave Speed Estimation with Regularized Transfer Functions
papers.abstract: This work introduces a robust framework for estimating shear wave speed in ultrasound elastography by addressing limitations of conventional time-of-flight methods, including noise, signal distortion, and false peak detection. Results promise to enable more reliable and clinically viable stiffness estimation.

papers.title: Short-Time Fourier Transform-Based Motion Magnification for High-Sensitivity Shear-Wave Elasticity Imaging
papers.abstract: This study proposes short-time Fourier transform-based motion magnification (STFT-MM) to enhance weak and transient shear-wave motion before velocity reconstruction in shear-wave elasticity imaging (SWEI). STFT-MM is applied to beamformed IQ data, where each pixel-wise temporal signal is decomposed by STFT, shear-wave-related components are selected, and their phase variations are amplified. The enhanced signal is reconstructed by inverse STFT and processed using a conventional SWEI pipeline. Phantom experiments were conducted in a homogeneous region and two different-sized inclusions, and in-vivo thyroid imaging was performed in a healthy volunteer under IRB approval. Compared with conventional SWEI, STFT-MM broadened the phase-velocity bandwidth from 642 to 787 Hz under 16-fold magnification. It also improved inclusion visibility, produced more circular inclusion boundaries, reduced velocity errors, and increased thyroid imaging SNR from 24.55 to 29.49 dB. These results suggest that STFT-MM can strengthen shear-wave-specific motion and improve SWEI reliability under weak-excitation or low-SNR conditions.

papers.title: Fast Volumetric Phase-Gradient Elastography for 3D Ultrasound Shear-Wave Imaging
papers.abstract: This work presents a fast volumetric phase-gradient elastography method for 3D ultrasound shear-wave imaging. The approach processes complex shear-wave fields in 3D k-space using bandpass filtering and 12 directional filters to isolate propagating wave components. For each harmonic component, the local wavevector is estimated from finite-difference phase gradients along the three spatial directions, enabling 3D phase-velocity reconstruction without local blockwise spectral estimation. The method was validated in pseudo-spectral elastodynamic simulations and in a commercial elasticity phantom containing a stiff spherical inclusion, with experimental volumes acquired by translating the imaging plane using motorized axes. For the analyzed datasets, 10 frequencies between 400 and 900 Hz were compounded. Volumetric PGE recovered consistent background and inclusion velocities in simulation and experiment, with a mean absolute error of 5.6%, CNR above 14 dB, and slice-to-slice variability below 6.3%. Results support 3D PGE as a practical block-free strategy for quantitative spectral volumetric SWE.

papers.title: Diffraction-Corrected Shear Wave Attenuation Measurement in Focused Shear Wave Transient elastography
papers.abstract: Transient elastography (TE) is widely used to assess chronic liver disease via liver tissue stiffness measurement but suffers from high exam failure rates in subjects with obesity and can yield false positive results due to inflammation. Focused shear wave TE (fTE) was introduced to improve exam reliability in subjects with obesity. Recent studies suggest that liver tissue viscosity measurement (LVM) is specifically related to inflammation. We propose a diffraction-corrected approach to estimate shear wave attenuation (SWA) using fTE. Simulations (n=40) of focused shear wave propagation to the deep human liver were employed. Parameters were randomly assigned based on measurements in subjects with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Diffraction bias was estimated from n=20 simulations with no viscoelasticity included, and SWA measurement was validated in n=20 separate simulations that included liver viscoelasticity (RMSE = 1.6 dB/cm). Feasibility of the approach in vivo was investigated by retrospective analysis of fTE data in one human subject with MASLD and obesity, where attenuation followed expected diffraction bias and numerical value in MASLD.

papers.title: A VoxelMorph Based Pretrain-plus-Test-Time-Adaptation (PTTA) Pipeline for High Frequency Ultrasound Elastography
papers.abstract: High‑frequency ultrasound has been used to characterize ocular tissue deformation in vivo. Normalized cross‑correlation (NCC) speckle tracking (ST) on ultrasound radiofrequency data is the standard for displacement estimation, but it is computationally intensive and sensitive to speckle noise. Learning‑based registration methods such as VoxelMorph enable fast, unsupervised deformation estimation with smoothness regularization, but their application to high‑frequency ocular ultrasound remains underexplored. In this study, we developed an unsupervised Pretrain-plus-Test-Time-Adaptation (PTTA) pipeline to rapidly adapt a pretrained model to subject-specific speckle and deformation characteristics and produce displacement estimates comparable to conventional NCC-ST. Our results showed the feasibility of the proposed pipeline.

papers.title: Direct Continuous Strain Estimation via Regularized Optimization for Ultrasound Elastography
papers.abstract: Ultrasound strain elastography estimates tissue deformation from pre- and post-compression RF data, yet conventional pipelines rely on displacement reconstruction followed by differentiation to obtain strain. This indirect formulation imposes a fundamental limitation: displacement regularization suppresses fine-scale deformation, while differentiation amplifies noise, leading to loss of spatial fidelity and reduced strain quality. To address this, we introduce DRESS, a continuous optimization framework for direct strain estimation from RF image pairs. The method enforces RF signal consistency through a unified cost function in which displacement is implicitly defined as the cumulative sum of strain. Regularization is applied directly to the strain field, enabling spatial coherence without introducing intermediate smoothing of displacement. This formulation preserves fine structural details while improving robustness to noise. Evaluations on simulated and phantom datasets demonstrate improved strain quality and clearer inclusion delineation compared to SOUL (Second-Order Ultrasound Elastography), while providing a simplified elastography pipeline.

sessions.title: MTC: Breast & Lymph Node Assessment

papers.title: Evaluation of Backscatter Coefficient Metrics for Assessing Breast Tumor Treatment Response Using an in Vivo Reference Target
papers.abstract: QUS parameters such as ESD and EAC are promising for noninvasive monitoring of breast tumor response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC), but their accuracy is limited by attenuation compensation errors in conventional backscatter coefficient (BSC) calibration. This pilot study evaluated an in situ reference method using an implanted gold bead, which inherently accounts for attenuation and transmission losses, and compared it with a standard external tissue-mimicking phantom in 17 patients. Ultrasound data were collected at baseline and weeks 2, 4, 8, and 12. Changes in ESD and EAC were analyzed to assess parameter stability. The bead-based method significantly improved early-stage stability, reducing generalized variance by 7.7× and total variance by 3.8× at week 2 (p = 0.039), consistent with minimal tumor response at this stage. Larger parameter changes were observed at later weeks for both methods. However, bead visibility degraded over time as tumors responded, limiting its long-term use. Overall, the in situ reference is advantageous for early response assessment, while the external phantom remains essential for consistent longitudinal monitoring.

papers.title: Heterogeneity of Quantitative Ultrasound Parameters Improves Lymph Node Metastasis Classification
papers.abstract: Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) provides a noninvasive approach for characterizing lymph node (LN) tissue microstructure. This study evaluates whether QUS heterogeneity improves benign versus metastatic LN classification compared with mean QUS values alone. N=42 patients with confirmed primary cancers were enrolled, with one LN imaged per patient. QUS parameters and morphologic features were extracted from segmented LNs, including mean values and heterogeneity descriptors such as standard deviation and interquartile range. Models were evaluated using repeated 5-fold stratified grouped cross-validation with patient-level separation and highest-suspicion-frame aggregation. Frame-level ESD standard deviation was significantly higher in metastatic than benign LNs (p<0.001). A linear SVM using short-axis length and ESD standard deviation achieved a patient-level AUC of 0.820±0.027, compared with 0.789±0.019 when ESD mean was used. These results suggest that using QUS heterogeneity can improve noninvasive LN metastasis classification.

papers.title: Preclinical Use of Quantitative Ultrasound Imaging for the Detection of Circadian disruption-Induced Changes in Breast Tissue
papers.abstract: The circadian clock is the timekeeping system in humans that coordinates biological processes with the natural cycle of daylight and darkness. Many professions require prolonged circadian rhythm disruption (CRD) like night shift workers. Irregular shift work increases the incidence of breast cancer, suggesting a role of CRD in disease development. However, the mechanisms of mammary gland response to CRD remain poorly understood and are difficult to monitor. The objective of this study was to explore the use of quantitative ultrasound (US) imaging of mammary glands of mice exposed to control (12 h light, 12 h dark, LD) or CRD conditions. Results revealed no difference between B-scan or H-scan US measures. However, a difference was found between US attenuation coefficients from the mammary gland of animals exposed to LD or CRD conditions (p = 0.03). Specifically, attenuation coefficients were found to be -0.53 ± 0.22 and -0.95 ± 0.27 dB/cm/MHz for the LD and CRD groups. Histology revealed a considerable increase in collagen content in the CRD group mice. Overall, quantitative US imaging can be used for detection of changes in breast tissue that increase risk of cancer development.

papers.title: Assessment of Mammographic Breast Density and Impact on Quantitative Ultrasound Images
papers.abstract: Ranging from category A (fatty) to D (dense), mammographic breast density (MBD) can obscure cancer detection. This study assessed whether MBD affects quantitative ultrasound (US) imaging by analyzing multiparametric images including B-scan echogenicity, H-scan frequency, H-scan dispersion, and Burr speckle statistics from 19 breast cancer patients across all MBD categories. Radiofrequency data was processed to extract quantitative parameters from tumors, grouped by MBD, and compared using statistical tests. No significant differences were found across MBD categories for any US parameter (p > 0.05). Thus, quantitative US measurements appear consistent regardless of MBD, supporting their clinical usefulness for tumor assessment and treatment monitoring.

papers.title: Region-of-Interest Quality Assessment Using sub-region-of-Interest Pixel Statistics for Quantitative ultrasound-Based Tissue Characterization of Breast Tissue Components
papers.abstract: In this study, we develop a region-of-interest (ROI) quality metric (QM) using sub-ROI pixel statistics of ultrasound (US) envelope values of breast scans. The QM is used to quality-assess envelope values in rectangular ROIs that are used in quantitative ultrasound-based (QUS) tissue characterization for windowing the US signal. We study this problem in the context of characterization of breast white adipose tissue (WAT) regions corrupted with Cooper’s ligaments, since the latter will provide an unwanted backscattering contribution to the US signal.

papers.title: Multimodal Ultrasound for Axillary Lymph Node Classification Using Attention-Enhanced Deep Learning
papers.abstract: Ultrasound is widely used to assess axillary lymph node (ALN) status, crucial for breast cancer staging. Combining B-mode morphology, shear wave elastography (SWE) stiffness, and color Doppler (CD) vascularity can enhance diagnostic accuracy, yet most deep learning methods rely on single modalities or limited fusion. We propose a lightweight multimodal DL framework for classifying metastatic versus reactive ALNs using B-mode, SWE, and CD. The framework combines a pretrained MobileNetV2 backbone for feature extraction with a custom network comprising convolutional and mixed pooling blocks, followed by a weighted sum mixed pooling layer and squeeze-and-excitation attention for enhancing relevant features. This design enables effective modality-aware feature fusion while preserving both global and local information with low computational cost. Evaluated on 174 patients with five-fold cross-validation, the method achieved 0.91 accuracy, 0.93 sensitivity, 0.91 specificity, F1-score of 0.93, and cvAUC of 0.92, outperforming single-modality baselines. The framework shows promise for real-time clinical deployment and improved preoperative staging.

sessions.title: PGP: General Physical Acoustics II

papers.title: Feature-Level Validation of a Physics-Based Acoustic Model for Respiratory Sound Synthesis Against Multi-Dataset Clinical Benchmarks
papers.abstract: This work presents a physics-based framework for synthesizing respiratory sounds and validating them against clinical data at the feature level. It addresses a key limitation of prior models; the lack of multi-feature validation across independent datasets; by introducing a reproducible evaluation pipeline. A simplified 3D acoustic model (implemented in COMSOL) simulates sound propagation through lung compartments and the trachea. Wheezes are modeled as frequency-modulated signals (170 ± 35 Hz) with breathing-driven amplitude variation, while crackles are represented as Gaussian-envelope transients (140 Hz). Feature extraction is applied consistently to synthetic and clinical signals, focusing on reproducing clinically relevant acoustic properties rather than anatomical detail. The model was evaluated against 730 clinical segments from two datasets. Results show that 11 of 12 features (91.7%) were validated, with a mean error of 8.9% and run times of 1.5–3 hours. Overall, the framework demonstrates that simplified physics-based models can achieve strong acoustic fidelity and provides an interpretable baseline for controlled studies and future multi-physics model extensions.

papers.title: Acoustically Localized Chemotherapy of magnesium-Gallate Metal Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: Conventional chemotherapy lacks spatial selectivity. We developed a magnesium-gallate (Mg-Gal) MOFs combined with single-beam acoustic tweezers (SBAT) for site-specific drug accumulation in breast cancer cell. Mg-Gal was synthesized hydrothermally (120 °C, 24 h) from MgCl₂ and gallic acid, and characterized by XRD, FT-IR, DLS, TGA, FE-SEM, and TEM. It showed Mg–O coordination, ~43.83 nm crystallites, ~2,875 nm hydrodynamic size, ~28 mV zeta potential, >40% mass retention at 800 °C, and a porous morphology with uniform elemental distribution. A custom 7 MHz focused transducer driven by a 50 dB amplifier on a motorized stage manipulated the particles. Upon beam activation, Mg-Gal converged at the focal region within 7 s into reversible 100–150 μm clusters, redispersing on termination and tracking the transducer in 50 μm steps. In MDA-MB-231 cells, MTT yielded IC₅₀ ≈ 79.18 μg/mL with dose-dependent viability loss. Live/Dead assay showed higher dead-cell counts inside versus outside the focal zone (p < 0.001), confirming spatially confined cytotoxicity. Mg-Gal/SBAT thus offers a versatile platform for spatially addressable cancer therapy.

papers.title: The impact of shear elasticity on the performance of acoustic holograms
papers.abstract: Shear waves are often neglected in ultrasound hologram simulations, however these can often lead to discrepancies between simulations and experimental data if not accounted for. This study evaluates how shear elasticity affects two common design methods: single-plane (SP) and phase-matching (PM). Shear velocities were estimated by fitting simulations to experiments for rigid (cL = 2456 m/s) and soft (cL = 969 m/s) lenses at 30, 60, and 90 mm focal distances. Estimated shear speeds were cS = 1018 m/s (rigid) and 441 m/s (soft). Including shear reduced focus position error in simulation with respect to experimental field scans from 1.7±1.6 mm to 0.5±0.4 mm (72.8% decrease). Furthermore, this validation allowed us to compare the SP and PM methods using Comsol Multiphysics and experimental scans. PM outperformed SP in focal accuracy, with shifts of 0.5±1.0, 0.8±0.4, and 5.7±0.7 mm versus 1.8±0.6, 3.2±0.5, and 6.6±0.6 mm (30, 60, 90 mm). PM also increased pressure by 7.0% and 6.5% at 30 and 60 mm, with only a 1% loss at 90 mm. For soft lenses, differences were ~1%.

papers.title: Co-Culture of Heterogeneous Cells in a Flow Path Using microbubbles and an Interferential Acoustic Field
papers.abstract: Functional artificial blood vessels require the spatially controlled co-culture of multiple cell types, but controlling the placement of each cell type at the same site remains difficult. Cells coupled to cRGD-modified microbubbles (BSCs) can be retained on a flow path wall by acoustic radiation force. This study examines the retention and co-culture of two cell types using an interferential acoustic field. Bovine carotid endothelial (HH) and human hepatocellular carcinoma (HepG2) cells were used. A PDMS flow path (2 mm × 1 mm) was coated with polydopamine and collagen. HH cells were seeded at 300 cells/mm² and cultured for 72 h to form a monolayer. Two transducers at a degassed water tank bottom were driven with phase sweeping to generate an interferential acoustic field. A suspension of 5×10⁴ HepG2-BSCs was injected at 10 mm/s, irradiated for 60 s, and incubated for 24 h. Fluorescence microscopy showed HepG2 cells captured on the HH monolayer in a striped pattern matching the acoustic field, with adherence preserved after 24 h, confirming successful co-culture. These results establish initial conditions for layered co-culture toward multi-cell-type vascular constructs.

papers.title: Study on Nanoemulsion Generation Device Using Acoustic Flow Stirring
papers.abstract: Recently, anticancer drug therapies using nanoemulsions have attracted attention. Nanoemulsions contain droplets of a dispersed phase with a nanoscale diameter within a continuous phase. There is a need to generate fine, uniform, and high-concentration nanoemulsions. In this study, a batch-type ultrasonic vibration device capable of droplet stirring by acoustic streaming has been proposed. The proposed device consists of some plates. The two drive patterns are switched by switching the voltage application to the electrodes on the surface of the piezoelectric element. The structure and dimensions have been determined by using FEM. The fabricated device has been evaluated by the emulsion generation experiment. The experimental results show that stirring treatment promoted the miniaturization of large-diameter droplets. We have successfully formed finer nanoemulsion by the device to switch between two driving states: nanoemulsion generation and acoustic streaming stirring.

papers.title: A Numerical Study on Global Optimization of Axisymmetric Reflector Shapes for Airborne Ultrasonic Levitation
papers.abstract: This study presents a field-first inverse design method for axisymmetric reflectors in airborne ultrasonic levitation. Conventional shape-first optimization is costly because each candidate reflector requires a new acoustic-field computation. To avoid this, the proposed method expresses fields as Green's-function superposition from an artificial boundary. A semidefinite program then optimizes the artificial-boundary pressure coefficients to maximize restoring stiffness before any reflector shape is selected. This global field optimization reduces dependence on initial shapes and makes it possible to judge whether the target levitation condition is feasible. After the optimal field is obtained, rigid-wall reflector candidates are extracted from particle-velocity streamlines. Numerical validation confirmed that the extracted reflector can provide restoring force in both the vertical and radial directions, supporting stable particle trapping.

sessions.title: MBB: Coherence

papers.title: CRISP: Coherence Recovery Imaging with Spatially Varying Apertures
papers.abstract: This work introduces Coherence Recovery Imaging with SPatially Varying Apertures (CRISP) to resolve outstanding limitations with short-lag spatial coherence (SLSC) imaging, particularly with respect to poor performance in shallow regions and outside of the focal zone. Results demonstrate that CRISP can improve near-field SLSC image quality, which promises to improve shallow breast mass diagnoses (and assessments of other near-field structures).

papers.title: Stability‑Guided Pixel‑Wise Correlation (SG-PWC) Beamforming for Clutter Suppression in Echocardiography
papers.abstract: Acoustic clutter and incoherent echoes often obscure myocardial structures in cardiac ultrasound, reducing contrast and anatomical visibility. Conventional DAS preserves speckle but is highly susceptible to clutter, while nonlinear or coherence‑based beamformers such as DMAS and SLSC improve cavity contrast but often distort speckle or detail. To overcome these trade‑offs, we propose Stability‑Guided Pixel‑Wise Correlation (SG‑PWC) beamforming, which enhances coherent tissue responses by evaluating the stability of spatial correlations across receive channels. For each pixel, normalized cross‑correlations are computed over multiple short spatial lags, and their dispersion around the mean is analyzed. A stability factor penalizes large deviations, emphasizing echoes with consistent lag‑wise correlations while suppressing unstable, clutter‑dominated signals. Applied to in‑vivo echocardiography, SG‑PWC yields cleaner ventricular cavities, sharper myocardial borders, and preserved speckle. Quantitatively, it achieves superior contrast (gCNR ≈1.00, CNR 4.2) over DAS, DMAS, and SLSC.

papers.title: Adaptive Scaled Subarray Coherence Based Postfilter for Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: The subarray coherence based postfilter (SCBP), which demonstrated improvement in contrast ratio, has been proposed. However, improvements in terms of resolution and contrast ratio acquired by it is not enough. To go further, an adaptive subarray coherence based postfilter (ASCBP) was proposed. Nevertheless, there exist black artifacts beside the point targets and ASCBP degrades the speckle brightness. We propose a novel adaptive scaling factor using subarray zero-cross factor (SZF) with a dynamic subarray length, and normalized reciprocals of amplitude standard deviations for subarray coherence based postfilter, which is termed as adaptive scaled subarray coherence based postfilter (ASSCBP). We verified the proposed method on experimental point and cyst phantom datasets. The proposed ASSCBP can improve the resolution by 42.9% compared with SCBP. Furthermore, ASSCBP achieves average improvements of 74.7%, and 9.5% regarding CR, and gCNR in comparison to SCBP, and obtains improvement of 14.9% in terms of sSNR. Results demonstrates that the proposed method can effectively enhance the imaging performance of SCBP.

papers.title: Adaptive Regional Spatiotemporal Smoothing Coherence Factor for Ultrasound Beamforming
papers.abstract: The Coherence Factor enhances ultrasound resolution and contrast, but its strict coherence criteria often lead to excessive suppression of low-coherence speckle, especially under low-SNR conditions. Although the spatiotemporal smoothing strategy introduced in the Spatio-temporally smoothed coherence factor (STS-CF) method significantly improves speckle patterns, its reliance on a fixed subarray length introduces a fundamental trade-off. Specifically, increasing the subarray length enhances speckle quality, whereas image contrast and resolution benefit from shorter subarray lengths. Thus, a fixed subarray length is inadequate for effectively distinguishing signals from targets with varying echo characteristics. To address this limitation, this study proposes the Adaptive Regional Spatiotemporal Smoothing Coherence Factor (RStS-CF) method, which dynamically selects the subarray length based on regional echo characteristics to balance speckle preservation and clutter suppression. Simulation studies demonstrate that the RStS-CF achieves substantial background speckle improvement without sacrificing spatial resolution or noise suppression, significantly enhancing overall image quality.

papers.title: Physics-Guided Gradient Coherence Weighting for contrast-Enhanced Plane Wave Compounding Imaging
papers.abstract: Ultrasound plane wave compounding (PWC) enables high-frame-rate imaging, but contrast enhancement remains limited without optimal angular weighting. This study proposes a data-driven, physics-guided angular weighting framework that combines all-pair normalized cross-correlation (NCC) with derivatives of the van Cittert-Zernike (VCZ) coherence curve. The method computes NCC across all steering-angle pairs to estimate local angular coherence, while VCZ-based reliability weighting provides a depth-dependent metric that accounts for f-number effects. The resulting weighted coherence map is applied to PWC images to suppress incoherent components while preserving amplitude and speckle texture. Simulation and in vivo thyroid experiments using 10 plane waves from −10° to 10° demonstrated improved performance over conventional PWC. In simulation, CNR and CR improved from 1.87 and 24.56 dB to 1.93 and 31.18 dB, respectively. In vivo thyroid imaging showed improvements from 1.24 and 9.51 dB to 1.45 and 15.31 dB. Compared with SLAC, the proposed method better preserved speckle characteristics while improving lesion conspicuity and background uniformity.

papers.title: Exploiting Multi-Dimensional Coherence in Coherent Multi-Transducer Ultrasound Using HOSVD-Based Tensor Beamforming
papers.abstract: Coherent Multi-Transducer Ultrasound (CoMTUS) enables large effective apertures by combining multiple transmit–receive datasets, but conventional delay-and-sum (DAS) beamforming does not exploit their multi-dimensional structure. We propose a tensor-based beamforming framework using Higher-Order Singular Value Decomposition (HOSVD) to preserve acquisition diversity and enforce coherence across channel, receive, transmit, and plane-wave dimensions. Mode-wise coherence factors are derived and combined into a unified metric to weight DAS reconstruction. The method was validated in a dual-array CoMTUS system using simulations and experiments. Results show improved axial resolution (0.3 vs 0.45 mm), sidelobe reduction (−3.8 dB), and lower noise floor compared to DAS. Lesion detectability is enhanced, with higher gCNR and contrast, and improvements are confirmed in vivo. This demonstrates that tensor-based beamforming effectively exploits multi-dimensional coherence in CoMTUS, with potential for advanced imaging and system calibration.

sessions.title: MIS: 3D & Volumetric Ultrasound Imaging

papers.title: AI-Enabled Quality Control for Bedside 3D Ultrasound Musculoskeletal Imaging
papers.abstract: More than 8.5 million U.S. patients present annually to emergency departments with distal extremity trauma. X-ray is standard of care, but fewer than 40% of cases are fractures, contributing to backlog and bottlenecks. Bedside ultrasound could expedite MSK injury assessment, but is operator-dependent. We developed an AI-enabled quality control (QC) pipeline for rapid 3D MSK ultrasound imaging by novice ED users. The pipeline quantifies artifacts and assesses anatomic placement in reconstructed scans. Volumes are converted to bird’s-eye views, and a U-Net model generates tissue maps for region-of-interest gating. Scan-level edge detection and curve fitting estimate tissue boundaries, alignment, and valid regions. A YOLOv11-nano model detects artifacts on selected tissue-containing frames; detections are filtered and aggregated into scan-level QC metrics. Training included 3,200 frames from 268 clinical scans across seven sites. On 75 test scans, the gated pipeline maintained 81% sensitivity, improved specificity to 89%, and reduced false positives by 16.2%. The system provides Good/Okay/Bad feedback, flags angulation exceeding limits, and recommends reacquisition.

papers.title: Directional Filtering for Angle-Adaptive Transverse Oscillations in Sparse-Array 3D Ultrasound Motion Estimation
papers.abstract: Accurate 3D motion estimation remains challenging, particularly for oblique and large displacements where conventional Transverse Oscillations (TO) lose accuracy due to fixed lateral orientation. Sparse arrays enable flexible 3D imaging but inherit these limitations. This work introduces TO-directional filtering (TO-DF), an angle-adaptive method that aligns oscillations with the motion direction to improve accuracy. TO-DF first estimates the motion angle (θ) using 3D speckle tracking, then applies filtering in a rotated frequency domain aligned with θ. The filter is defined as the product of two orthogonal Gaussians: one selects frequencies along the motion direction, while the other enforces directional selectivity. Combined with axial oscillations, this enables 3D displacement estimation from phase shifts. Validation on a PVA phantom with controlled multidirectional motion shows improved accuracy and precision. Errors remain below 9% for unidirectional motion (vs. up to 40% with TO) and below 15% for combined motion, where conventional TO fails. Improvements are strongest for diagonal motion, confirming enhanced robustness for 3D motion estimation with sparse arrays.

papers.title: Riemannian Deep Learning for Covariance-Based Fiber Orientation Estimation in 3D Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Myocardial fiber orientation plays a critical role in cardiac mechanics, but current imaging modalities still face limitations in clinical settings. This work introduces a geometry-aware deep learning approach to estimate fiber orientation directly from 3D ultrasound RF data. Sample covariance matrices from a 16×16 transducer array are treated as points on the Riemannian manifold of symmetric positive-definite (SPD) matrices and analyzed using SPDNet, a network adapted to this type of data. A sin–cos output representation is used to handle angular periodicity, and Monte Carlo Dropout provides confidence estimates for each prediction. The model was trained on 30,000 synthetic RF covariance matrices covering angles from −90° to +90° with noise augmentation, and validated on experimental phantom data at eight fiber orientations. SPDNet achieved a mean absolute error of 5.52°, improving over backscatter tensor imaging (BTI) by 24%. Confidence-based tractography resulted in more spatially complete fiber reconstructions compared to BTI. These results suggest that Riemannian deep learning on covariance matrices is a promising direction for myocardial fiber mapping from ultrasound.

papers.title: View-Wise Spatially Varying Richardson–Lucy (RL) Deconvolution for Refraction-Corrected 3D Ultrasound Reflection Tomography
papers.abstract: Breast 3D ultrasound tomography (UST) reflection imaging is degraded by acoustic refraction and spatially varying blur. The historical reconstruction workflow compounds all 60 views first and then applies Richardson–Lucy deconvolution using a single constant point spread function (PSF), which cannot fully model the view-, depth-, and array-dependent blur of the system. This work evaluates a new reconstruction approach in which each refraction-corrected reflection view is deconvolved separately using a spatially varying PSF calibrated from 0.4 mm bead phantom measurements, followed by multi-view compounding and log compression. Refraction correction is performed using a 3D UST transmission-based speed-of-sound map and ray tracing based on the eikonal equation. Phantom results demonstrate progressive PSF narrowing with Richardson–Lucy iteration count, while noise increases with iteration, motivating practical stopping-rule optimization. In a 30-case clinical visual grading analysis, an experienced breast radiologist demonstrated consistent image-quality improvement with the view-wise spatially varying method, with mean regional score gains of approximately 16% using L40 GPUs

papers.title: Freehand 3D Ultrasound Reconstruction of the Infant Brain Using Trajectory Estimation and Implicit Neural Representation
papers.abstract: 3D cerebral reconstruction from 2D freehand acquisitions in neonates is clinically important and technically challenging. Clinical constraints prevent sensor-based probe tracking, leaving its trajectory unknown. Furthermore, 3D volumes acquired with matrix probes suffer from their limited field of view and resolution, making them impractical. Trajectory inference from 2D slices is therefore required prior to volumetric reconstruction. We demonstrate that Implicit Neural Representations (INR) show strong promise for this task, with speckle control achievable via positional encoding frequency adjustment.

papers.title: Speckle-Tracking Slam for Low-Cost Freehand 3D Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: A common problem with point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is that it is operator dependent. One solution to overcome this problem is for the operator to capture a 3D volume from a sequential set of 2D images. However, low-cost tracking sensors are too inaccurate on their own to track the probe for high resolution 3D reconstruction. We present a Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) formulation for constructing a high-resolution 3D ultrasound volume while simultaneously estimating its position within that map. We estimate the optimal set of probe poses by formulating trajectory estimation as a pose graph optimization (PGO) problem. In this probabilistic graphical model, nodes represent probe poses and edges represent uncertain constraints from electromagnetic (EM) tracking, ultrasound speckle-based odometry, and loop closure. A 3D volume is reconstructed from the optimized pose estimates. For phantom data, the average mean absolute error for the lateral and elevational pose estimates is 0.29 mm and 0.11 mm respectively, compared with 0.44 mm and 0.12 mm for the EM sensor alone. Results from this method show promise for future implementation of SLAM in 3D ultrasound imaging.

sessions.title: TPF: Novel Piezoelectric Devices and Applications

papers.title: Contact Lens-Integrated Dual-Ring Ultrasound Transducer for Retinal Stimulation
papers.abstract: Retinitis pigmentosa and age-related macular degeneration cause irreversible blindness due to photoreceptor degeneration, while inner retinal neurons remain intact. Electrode-based retinal prostheses require invasive surgery and bulky hardware. This work develops a flexible contact-lens-integrated dual-ring ultrasound transducer array for non-invasive wearable precise retinal stimulation. The array was fabricated using thin PZT with a custom 3D-printed mold and PDMS coating for conformal ocular contact and acoustic matching. The design includes a central hollow window to preserve natural vision and a concentric dual-ring geometry for efficient retinal focusing with rapid post-focal decay. It integrates with a low-power 64-channel wearable neuromodulation platform. Field II simulations and hydrophone/pulse-echo measurements confirm effective beamforming and adherence to ophthalmic safety guidelines (MI and Ispta). The contact-lens form factor offers a lightweight portable solution for precise steerable focal stimulation. This demonstrates the feasibility of a non-invasive daily-wearable ultrasound retinal prosthesis for vision restoration in photoreceptor degenerative diseases.

papers.title: Effect of Ultrasound Stimulation Duration on trpa1-Mediated Gene Expression
papers.abstract: Sonogenetics is an emerging approach for manipulating cellular functions using ultrasound stimulation. This technique has attracted considerable attention due to the high tissue penetrability of ultrasound. Recent studies have demonstrated that the mechanosensitive ion channel TRPA1 is activated by ultrasound stimulation, which increases intracellular Ca²⁺ concentration. However, it remains unclear whether ultrasound-induced TRPA1 activation can regulate gene expression via Ca²⁺-responsive promoters. In this study, we evaluated gene expression driven by a Ca²⁺-responsive promoter in TRPA1-expressing cells under various ultrasound stimulation conditions by monitoring AcGFP fluorescence intensity. Fluorescence intensity increased over time only in TRPA1-expressing cells. Notably, within TRPA1-expressing cells, a greater increase in fluorescence intensity was observed after 60 s stimulation compared with 300 s stimulation over an 8 h period. Despite the longer stimulation duration, gene expression was not enhanced, indicating that gene expression efficiency is not simply increased by prolonging stimulation duration but may instead be reduced by excessive stimulation.

papers.title: Comparing Massive Electrostrictive Tobe Arrays with Conventional Row-Column Arrays
papers.abstract: Fabrication of large-aperture two-dimensional arrays remains a significant challenge with existing probe technologies. Row–Column Arrays (RCAs) and the recently proposed bias-sensitive Top-Orthogonal-to-Bottom-Electrode (TOBE) arrays have mitigated issues related to wiring complexity. Nevertheless, there remains an unmet need for even larger arrays capable of imaging entire organs or the full abdominal region using fully electronic scanning.

papers.title: A Wearable Flexible Ultrasound Patch for Dual-Acupoint Stimulation in Obesity Intervention
papers.abstract: This study presents a wearable flexible dual-acupoint ultrasound patch for obesity intervention. The patch was designed using COMSOL simulations and consists of two 1 MHz transducers with a center-to-center spacing of 14 mm, enabling simultaneous stimulation of bilateral target regions in mice. Acoustic field characterization was performed using a hydrophone, and thermal safety was evaluated in ex vivo porcine tissue using a thermocouple. Without phase control, the focal region reached a depth of 5 mm with a surface width of approximately 4 mm. Both transducer regions generated measurable acoustic pressure responses under different input voltages. Thermal tests showed that the tissue temperature rise increased with voltage amplitude, number of cycles, and duty cycle. Under 150 mVpp, 10 cycles, and 10% duty cycle, continuous stimulation for 15 min increased the tissue temperature by approximately 1 °C. These results support the feasibility of the proposed patch for acupoint stimulation and provide a basis for future in vivo validation in mice and further application in human obesity intervention.

papers.title: A 1.5-mm 48-ElementPhased-Array Catheter for Rapid Mechanical-Sweeping Volumetric Imaging
papers.abstract: we developed a ultra-miniaturized phased-array catheter system capable of rapid, volumetric imaging, providing real-time 3D guidance for complex interventional procedures. The core of the system is a 12-MHz phased-array probe with a record-breaking outer diameter of 1.5 mm, featuring 48 high-density elements. Experimental results demonstrated a high spatial resolution of better than 0.20 mm and an effective imaging depth exceeding 30 mm with developed system.
keywords: Phased array transducer，interventional ultrasound，Mechanical-Sweeping volumetric imaging

papers.title: Ultrathin Silicon-Based Piezoelectric MEMS Micropump Array for High-Performance Active Cooling
papers.abstract: The increasing power density of compact electronic systems requires efficient thermal management within limited form factors. Conventional synthetic jet-based piezoelectric MEMS cooling devices require a jet-to-surface distance exceeding 3 mm, limiting their integration into ultrathin systems. This work presents an ultrathin piezoelectric micropump operating at ultrasonic frequency (>22 kHz), enabling efficient cooling at sub-millimeter working distances (<1 mm). A cantilever-dominated vibration mode replaces the fully clamped diaphragm to enhance displacement and airflow. A coupled electro-mechanical-fluid model is used to optimize the unit, and array configurations are implemented to scale performance. The single device achieves 10 m/s airflow at 3 mW, reducing a 460 mW heat source by 29 °C. Comparable cooling is maintained under direct contact, with only a 1 °C deviation from optimal distance. Array devices deliver >1.5 L/min flow rate and >240 Pa pressure at <100 mW, achieving a 36 °C reduction for a 2 W heat source. These results demonstrate efficient, distance-insensitive cooling within sub-millimeter spacing for ultrathin electronic systems.

sessions.title: AHO: Higher Order Mode Devices

papers.title: Thermal Stability and Enhanced Power Handling of 14-GHz Bulk Acoustic Wave Resonators and Filters Using SMR and SiC Substrates
papers.abstract: With the development of periodically poled piezoelectric film (P3F) technology, bulk acoustic wave (BAW) resonators operating above 10 GHz have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation RF front ends, while their reduced device dimensions and increased power density impose increasingly stringent requirements on thermal stability and power handling. In this work, the thermal stability and power durability characteristics of 14-GHz bulk acoustic resonator (FBAR) and the solidly mounted resonator (SMR) were experimentally investigated, and further investigate the influence of substrate selection on SMR temperature stability. Compared with the FBAR, the Si-based SMR reduces the magnitude of the first-order temperature coefficient of frequency by approximately 50% and increases the 1-dB power-handling threshold from 31.4 to 37.1 dBm. Replacing the Si substrate with SiC further improves the temperature stability, reducing the first-order TCF by up to 62.6%. These results demonstrate that the SMR architecture combined with SiC substrate engineering provides an effective approach for improving the thermal robustness and high-power capability of Ku-band BAW devices.

papers.title: 13 GHz Periodically Poled AlN Lamb Wave Resonators with Enhanced Temperature and Power Stability
papers.abstract: This work demonstrates a 13 GHz periodically poled AlN Lamb wave resonator with improved temperature and power stability for SHF RF front-end applications. Periodically poled piezoelectric film (P3F) technology enables high-frequency mode excitation without extreme thickness scaling, helping to avoid the degradation in quality factor, coupling, and thermal robustness commonly seen in conventional SHF Al(Sc)N BAW resonators. The device uses a bilayer P3F AlN stack composed of two oppositely polarized 180-nm AlN films, together with 80-nm Mo IDTs and a 100-nm Mo floating bottom electrode. XRD confirms strong c-axis orientation with a (0002) rocking-curve FWHM of 0.55°, while PFM verifies the polarity-engineered bilayer with a reduced d33 of 1.99 pm/V. The resonator operates near 13 GHz, achieving k2eff = 1.55% and Qmax = 214. From 25 °C to 85 °C, it maintains nearly constant Qmax, with TCFs of −17.24 ppm/°C at fs and −20.15 ppm/°C at fp. Stable impedance responses from −5 to 9 dBm further indicate initial power-handling capability, demonstrating its potential for thermally robust and frequency-stable SHF acoustic resonators.

papers.title: 10th Overtone Mode BAW Resonator with 10-Layer polarization-Inverted AlN Films
papers.abstract: By employing 10th order overtone mode in a 10-layer polarization-inverted mutilayer, the film thickness can be increased tenfold compared to using fundamental-mode operation at same frequency in a single-layer resonator. Thicker piezoelectric stack results in a larger electrode area and allows to reduce the ratio of outer edge area. This prevents the degradation of electromechanical coupling and Q factors. Furthermore, the thicker stack is less likely to fail under high power RF application. Last year, we demonstrated the polarization of AlN film can be changed only by adjusting the gas ratio during sputter deposition. In this study, 10-layer polarization-inverted AlN resonator were fabricated using this technique. No clear boundaries were observed between the layers from the cross-sectional SEM image of 10-layer polarization-inverted AlN resonator. By comparing with the theoretical curves AlN HBAR with and without polarization inversion, the experimental results clearly shows the 10th overtone mode resonance. This polarization control technique is promising, as it enables the polarization inverted multilayer without major change to the current BAW resonator fabrication process

papers.title: Polarity Inheritance Between MOCVD-AlN Layer and sputter-ScAlN Layer in double-Layer polarization-Inverted BAW Resonators
papers.abstract: To overcome the design bottleneck of single-layer BAW resonators, a polarization-inverted double-layer structure is used to maintain resonance frequency while increasing volume. This study investigates the polarity inheritance between N-polar MOCVD-AlN underlayers and subsequent sputtered piezoelectric layers in polarization-inverted double-layer BAW resonators. Initial experiments with Al-polar sputter-AlN on N-polar MOCVD-AlN revealed unexpected fundamental mode excitation caused by a 300 nm transition layer due to polarity inheritance. While inserting a SiO2 blocking layer suppressed the transition layer formation, it caused significant kt2 degradation. In contrast, the combination of Al-polar sputter-ScAlN and N-polar MOCVD-AlN successfully eliminated polarity inheritance and demonstrated strong second mode excitation without kt2 degradation. This is attributed to the energetic preference of Al-Sc bonds (-3.836 eV) over Al-N bonds (-3.568 eV), which induces self-reversal to Al-polarity in ScAlN even on N-polar underlayers.

papers.title: A Sub-100 nm Layer Periodically Poled Sub-Terahertz Acoustic Resonator
papers.abstract: Within the last ten years, advances in thin-film transfer and acoustic design have rapidly improved the performance of piezoelectric acoustic resonators operating in the millimeter wave regime (30 GHz – 300 GHz). Recent demonstrations have pushed these limits, demonstrating electrically excited acoustic modes into the hundreds of GHz, with the highest frequency being 210 GHz. The ultimate limit of these resonators remains an open question, urging further study towards understanding the ultimate frequency limits, with implications for lower frequency applications. In this work, we probe these limits with a periodically poled lithium niobate resonator leveraging sub-100 nm films for strong resonances detectable up to our measurement limit of 220 GHz.

papers.title: Acoustic-plate-Mode Excitation Using Particular Resonator Structures and piezo-Orientations
papers.abstract: Research on piezo-coupling of plate modes in lithium niobate (LN) dates back many years. Recently, advances in transferring submicron crystalline layers onto Si substrates have enabled LN membranes for a wide range of RF resonators and filters. Mass production of XBARs operating at 5-7 GHz has been reported. YBARs and SH0-mode devices show record-large passbands. Here, we systematically explore all acoustic plate modes with particular structures and piezo-orientations. Six novel LN thin-film resonators are presented for high-frequency large-bandwidth filter applications. Vertical electrodes (VE) are included to achieve a more uniform horizontal electric field. Resonators using e111 (LLSAW), e112 (TFSAW), e113 (TCSAW), e131 (A1 XBAR), e332 (SH1 YBAR), and e333 (FBAR) are widely reported; resonators using e113 and e313 (A0) require a high thickness-to-width ratio of LN for strong coupling, compared with e131 and e331, complicating design and fabrication; resonators using e133 (S1) and e311 (S0) have smaller coupling than e111 (S0) and e333 (S1). We also study all remaining acoustic modes using specific exyz with particular structures

sessions.title: NDE: Advanced Ultrasonic Sensing and Guided Wave Techniques for Industrial Monitoring
sessions.chair: Mauricio Pereira da Cunha, Heechul Yoon

papers.title: Quantitative Evaluation of Adhesion Degradation in Attenuative Coated Pipes Using Zero-Frequency Guided Waves
papers.abstract: Assessing interfacial bonding in composite-metal pipes is challenged by polymer coating damping, which attenuates high-frequency signals. To overcome this, we utilize the nonlinear self-interaction of guided waves to excite zero-frequency waves (ZFW). ZFW shows an exceptionally low attenuation coefficient, enabling long-range transmission in attenuative media. A spatially cumulative ZFW was excited by satisfying group velocity matching and evaluated using a 3D finite element model with a nonlinear cohesive interface. Experiments utilized a high-power ultrasonic system and a phase-inversion strategy to isolate the ZFW. Results demonstrate ZFW displacement is highly sensitive to interfacial stiffness. A derived calibration curve reveals a monotonic relationship with bonding strength, showing exceptional sensitivity at near-zero stiffness typical of kissing bonds. This validates the ZFW method for early-stage debonding detection in hybrid systems.

papers.title: A Lightweight Guided Wavefield Prediction Model for Irregular Defects Based on the Born Scattering Approximation
papers.abstract: Ultrasonic guided waves are vital for structural health monitoring, yet predicting scattering and phase distortion from irregular defects remains computationally demanding. This study proposes a lightweight Born-Inspired Surrogate Network (BIS-Net) for rapid, high-precision frequency-domain wavefield prediction. Utilizing the first-order Born approximation, BIS-Net directly maps squared slowness perturbations to the array scattering response matrix, bypassing the direct solution of partial differential equations during inference. The architecture features a FieldEncoder for multi-scale spatial mapping, a SensorSampler for discrete local feature extraction, and a BilinearHead for symmetric transmit-receive interactions. Validation on a 10 mm aluminum plate using the A0 mode showed high agreement with real experimental data, achieving complex and amplitude correlations of 0.87 and 0.95, respectively. Furthermore, substituting numerical forward operators with BIS-Net in inversion imaging tests yielded a 0.91 correlation in defect reconstruction. These results demonstrate the model's significant potential for efficient, quantitative defect imaging.

papers.title: Interfacial Stiffness Estimation of Cu-Cu Hybrid Bonding in HBM via Phase-Sensitive Ultrasonic Analysis Under Echo Overlap
papers.abstract: Scanning acoustic microscopy (SAM) is widely used for semiconductor inspection; however, in high-bandwidth memory (HBM), ultrathin multilayer stacks induce severe temporal overlap of echoes, fundamentally limiting conventional time-of-flight (ToF)-based interface isolation. In particular, Cu–Cu hybrid bonding interfaces—including weak or kissing bonds—exhibit minimal amplitude contrast, making them difficult to evaluate using A-line amplitude or ToF metrics. This work addresses the echo-overlap regime by modeling the Cu–Cu bonding interface as an effective stiffness and proposing a phase-sensitive evaluation framework that does not rely on explicit echo separation.

papers.title: Pressure-Robust Gas Flowmeters Enabled by Polymer-Integrated PMUT Arrays
papers.abstract: Piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducers (PMUTs) are promising for compact ultrasonic gas flowmeters, but pressure variations can affect resonance frequency and damping, reducing measurement stability. This work investigates 9-channel AlSc30%N PMUT arrays under gas pressure up to 4 bar and evaluates the impact of Parylene-C polymer integration. Devices are characterized using impedance measurements, comparing uncoated arrays with 5 µm and 10 µm coated arrays. Uncoated devices show strong pressure dependence, with frequency shifts up to 50 kHz (1–2.5 bar) and Q-factor reduction from ~100 to 10. Polymer integration significantly stabilizes performance. With 5 µm coating, the resonance shifts to 280 kHz and varies only by 10 kHz (1–4 bar), with Q-factor decreasing from 45 to 35. With 10 µm coating, the resonance shifts to 310 kHz with only 7 kHz variation and Q decreasing from 35 to 28. These results demonstrate that polymer integration reduces frequency drift and suppresses Q-factor degradation, enabling stable PMUT operation for gas flowmeter applications.

papers.title: Aperture-Dependent Doppler Observability of Pipeline Leakage Jets Under Strong Wall Clutter Using a CFD-Ultrasound Digital Twin
papers.abstract: This work presents a CFD-ultrasound digital twin framework for Doppler visualization of small-aperture pipeline leakage jets under strong wall clutter. A pressurized pipe model with 3, 5, and 10 mm leakage apertures was simulated in COMSOL, and the resulting velocity vectors near the leakage region were mapped to moving scatterers for Field II echo simulation. A dense static scatterer layer with approximately 30 dB higher amplitude than the fluid scatterers was added to represent strong pipe-wall clutter. High-rate slow-time echo ensembles were generated using a 5 MHz, 128-element linear array and processed by delay-and-sum beamforming, wall filtering, and Kasai autocorrelation. The Doppler-active area increased from 98.7 mm² to 167.1mm² and 341.5mm² for the 3, 5, and 10 mm apertures, respectively, while the integrated Doppler-response index increased from 1147.3 to 1903.5 and 3987.8. These results demonstrate aperture-dependent Doppler signatures of leakage jets and provide a simulation basis for ultrasound-based leak localization and aperture assessment.

papers.title: A Global MPPT Algorithm for Multi-RX Ultrasound-Powered Implants Achieving Directional Robustness and upto 6.53x Power Enhancement
papers.abstract: Ultrasound enables wireless powering of µm–mm scale implants deep in the brain. This work presents a robust global maximum power point tracking (MPPT) method for multi-receiver (multi-RX) piezoelectric transducer (PT) arrays. The algorithm is scalable and independent of parameters such as phase misalignment, bias-flip efficiency, open-circuit voltage, and resonance frequency. We also introduce a fully integrated synchronized switch harvesting on capacitors rectifier with top-plate switching and cooperative shared capacitors (CoFlip-SSHC). It supports 740 kHz operation without sacrificing area or efficiency. To enable miniaturization, only four on-chip capacitors are used for rectifying a 4-RX PT array, regardless of phase differences, and are shared with an on-chip multi-VCR switched-capacitor DC–DC converter. Fabricated in a 180 nm HV-BCD process and tested in water, the chip harvests up to 10.45 mW from a 4-RX PT array (2×2×1 mm³ per element), achieving 6.53× higher power than a full-bridge rectifier. The MPPT reaches 97.5% peak tracking efficiency with a simulated speed of 675.7 ns.

sessions.title: MIM: AI-Enabled Freehand 3D Ultrasound Reconstruction§

papers.title: Freehand 3D Photoacoustic and Ultrasound Reconstruction via Deep Sequential Motion Estimation
papers.abstract: Photoacoustic and ultrasound (PAUS) imaging provides structural US and vascular contrast, but is typically limited to 2D imaging with restricted field of view. Freehand 3D imaging is promising, yet requires accurate probe trajectory estimation without external trackers. This study proposes a tracker free freehand 3D PAUS framework using image based deep learning motion estimation. A scan sequence is acquired using a custom probe fiber holder with a gel pad to reduce skin motion, enabling flexible trajectories. For motion estimation, we develop a sequence modeling network, windowed bi directional cross attention with Mamba (wBCAM), which predicts 6-DoF probe motion from consecutive B mode frames. Frame pairs are encoded into local tokens and refined via windowed cross attention with Mamba based global memory. On US and PAUS datasets, the method achieves a local frame error of 0.0837 mm, a global frame error of 7.0491 mm, and a trajectory correlation of 99.64%. It improves motion accuracy and reduces drift, maintaining stable estimation over long sequences. PA frames are aligned in 3D space using the estimated motion, demonstrating feasibility of tracker free 3D PAUS imaging.

papers.title: Volume Measurement of Full-Shape Thyroid Using Multi-View 3D Ultrasound Reconstruction and Fusion Methods
papers.abstract: This study proposes a multi-view fusion imaging framework for full-shape thyroid volume measurement using freehand 3D ultrasound. Left and right thyroid-lobe ultrasound sequences were acquired for each subject and reconstructed into 3D volumes using electromagnetic tracking information. The reconstructed volumes were segmented with nnU-Net and post-processed to remove reconstruction artifacts. To construct the full-shape thyroid volume, an isthmus-guided constraint was proposed, using the isthmus region as a structural anchor for generalized ICP registration with centroid initialization. The aligned masks were then fused into a unified voxel grid. Validation on an independent cohort of 11 patients with paired 3D ultrasound and CT data showed good agreement with CT volume measurements, with Pearson r = 0.904 and ICC = 0.910. Compared with the calibrated ellipsoid method, the proposed framework achieved lower MAE and MAPE (2.94 ml vs 3.67 ml; 23.11% vs 31.37%). Isthmus-guided registration also showed small surface discrepancy in the isthmus region, with Chamfer = 0.262 mm and HD95 = 0.757 mm.

papers.title: A Freehand Ultrasound System for 3D Imaging of the Human Hip
papers.abstract: Femoroacetabular impingement syndrome (FAIS) is a leading cause of hip pain. Currently, diagnosis and pre-operative planning rely on computed tomography (CT). However, this increases surgical wait time and cost while exposing patients to ionizing radiation. Our study investigates whether this CT can be replaced by freehand 3D ultrasound imaging. Our system applies 3D tracking to a point-of-care ultrasound probe to localize images in 3D space. A convolutional neural network-based segmentation model extracts bone surfaces from B-mode images. These segments, combined with tracking data, form a point cloud to which a 3D surface mesh is fit. The system was tested in N=4 cadaveric hips and N=2 healthy participant hips and is currently in a clinical trial of N=50 patients with FAIS. RMS error was used to assess CT and ultrasound 3D mesh agreement (0.3-0.6mm) and mesh repeatability (0.57mm) across 3D ultrasound scans. Freehand ultrasound imaging can achieve bone surface reconstruction with submillimeter 3D agreement to CT. As clinically significant bone deformities associated with FAIS are ≥2 mm in prominence, freehand ultrasound is a viable alternative to CT in FAIS assessment.

papers.title: Automatic 3D Ultrasound Shape Completion Method for Intraoperative Lumbar Surgical Navigation
papers.abstract: This study is developed an automatic shape completion method for 3D ultrasound images based on preoperative CT images, enabling rapid intraoperative reconstruction of complete 3D structures of lumbar spine. This strategy preserved the pose information inside ultrasound while reducing modality-induced alignment errors. As a result, the method can rapidly produce a more shape-specific and geometrically consistent 3D lumbar model, demonstrating its potential for application in surgical navigation.

papers.title: Improved Volumetric Ultrasound Imaging Using a Transformer-Based Neural Network and a Virtual Large Synthetic Aperture Matrix Array Transducer
papers.abstract: Fully sampled matrix array transducers offer flexibility on beam transmission and beamforming for volumetric ultrasound imaging, however, they typically have a small aperture that limits resolution and field-of-view for deep-region imaging. Increasing the aperture size requires additional transducer channels that increases system cost, or techniques such as micro beamforming and row-column array that introduce grating lobe artefacts. In addition, some applications may provide limited acoustic windows (cardiac/cranial ultrasound) that limit probe aperture size. Here we aim to improve the overall quality of volumetric ultrasound imaging with a U-shaped transformer-based neural network (UNETR). We also propose an experimental method to build a virtual large aperture matrix array to support the network training. Our method increases NCC by 13%, SSIM by 4.5%, and PSNR by 4.8 dB on ex-vivo ultrasound volumes compared to a speckle filter, indicating the potential of improving volumetric imaging quality with small-aperture transducers.

papers.title: Segmentation Guided Iterative Pose Refinement for Freehand 3D Ultrasound Reconstruction
papers.abstract: This work addresses pose estimation for freehand 3D ultrasound reconstruction, where insufficient use of volumetric information can cause anatomical distortion. We propose GCE-Net, a segmentation-guided iterative pose refinement framework that jointly exploits frame-level and volumetric information. Multiscale local features are extracted from ultrasound images and segmentation maps, then spatially assembled into a 3D volume using an initial baseline pose. The reconstructed volume is built with trilinear splatting and occupancy-aware 3D convolutions. By slicing the volume according to the current pose, the network obtains pose-aligned global context and Z-axis positional encoding, which are fused with local features to predict residual relative poses. Iterative updates progressively refine slice positions. Qualitative and quantitative results show that GCE-Net improves trajectory alignment, reduces accumulated drift. Ablation results further indicate that predictions converge through iterative refinement, demonstrating the effectiveness of segmentation-guided local appearance and volumetric position-aware context for robust freehand 3D ultrasound reconstruction.

sessions.title: MTC: Musculoskeletal & Bone QUS

papers.title: High-Frequency Quantitative Ultrasound to Monitor Tendon Microstructure in a Murine Model of Patellar tendinopathy
papers.abstract: Patellar tendinopathy is characterized by collagen disruption and matrix degeneration. Longitudinal assessment of these microstructural changes remains challenging due to the limitations of biopsy and conventional imaging. This study evaluates high-frequency (60 MHz) quantitative ultrasound (QUS) as a noninvasive tool to detect and monitor these changes in a murine model. Twenty-five mice received collagenase injections in the right patellar tendon with contralateral saline controls and were assessed at 7, 14, and 28 days. The tissue backscatter coefficient was estimated, from which the parameters effective scatterer diameter (ESD) and acoustic concentration (EAC) were computed, along with tendon thickness and histological scoring. Significant differences in ESD, tendon thickness, and histology were observed at 7 days when comparing collagenase-treated with control tendons; no differences at later time points. Longitudinally, EAC and histological score differed at the 7 day timepoint compared to 14 and 28 days post-injection. These findings demonstrate the sensitivity of QUS to tendinopathy-related microstructural changes and its potential for noninvasive longitudinal monitoring.

papers.title: Volumetric Nakagami Distribution for Tissue Characterization of Multifidus Muscle in Subjects with Myofascial Pain
papers.abstract: This abstract presents a 3D quantitative ultrasound method using the Nakagami distribution to characterize multifidus muscle tissue in subjects with myofascial pain. The study addresses the need for an objective imaging biomarker because myofascial pain is usually diagnosed by manual palpation, which is subjective. Using a 6 MHz row-column array transducer, volumetric ultrasound images of the multifidus muscles were collected from 91 subjects, including 161 MP-positive and 171 MP-negative diagnostic units. The main imaging feature was the median Nakagami-m value calculated from the ultrasound envelope signal within the multifidus muscle. Statistical analysis used cluster bootstrap methods to account for repeated exams from the same participants. The results showed that Nakagami-m distinguish MP-positive from MP-negative cases while conventional B-mode intensity performed poorly. The difference between these two methods was statistically significant. The study suggests that volumetric Nakagami imaging may detect microstructural tissue changes in the multifidus muscle that are not visible in standard B-mode ultrasound.

papers.title: Surface Acoustic Waves for Noninvasive Detection of in situ Tibial Stress Fractures
papers.abstract: This work presents a noninvasive method for early detection of tibial stress fractures (TSF) using surface acoustic waves (SAW). A compact (~3 cm) acoustic device was developed using a PDMS wedge to efficiently excite SAWs along cortical bone with a 2.25 MHz excitation, enabling transmission and sensing through the skin. Experiments in four cadaveric lower limbs evaluated two conditions: controlled cortical cuts of increasing depth to simulate fractures, and cyclic mechanical loading (~1,200 N, 8 mm displacement, up to 10,000 cycles) to induce fatigue. MicroCT imaging was used to assess accumulated microdamage, with SAW measurements taken periodically during loading. Results showed a linear relationship between SAW signal delay and cut depth, with sensitivity to defects as small as ~0.5 mm, exceeding typical X-ray resolution. Fatigue testing demonstrated decreasing signal coherence with increasing damage, correlating with microCT findings. This approach offers a portable, radiation-free tool for monitoring bone health and detecting early-stage stress injuries, with ongoing work focused on miniaturization and clinical translation.

papers.title: Backscatter Anisotropy As a Biomarker for Patellar Tendon injury: Preliminary Evaluation of test-Retest Repeatability
papers.abstract: Patellar tendon injury disrupts the tendon’s fibrous microstructure. Quantitative ultrasound backscatter anisotropy is sensitive to fiber orientation and remodeling, motivating its evaluation as a tendon biomarker. In this IRB approved study, we assessed test–retest repeatability of mean backscatter power difference (mBSPD) in the patellar tendon. Eleven participants with prior unilateral ACL reconstruction or patellar tendinopathy were scanned twice within 7 days using a research ultrasound system with multi‑angle beam steering. Raw IQ data were acquired across long‑ and short‑axis views, and mBSPD was computed relative to an isotropic phantom. Parametric maps were segmented by two raters, with agreement assessed using Dice–Sørensen coefficients and repeatability evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients. Interrater agreement was high, within‑trial repeatability was excellent, and between‑trial repeatability was good. mBSPD was higher in long‑ versus short‑axis imaging and in uninvolved compared with involved tendons, consistent with greater microstructural organization.

papers.title: Improved Repeatability of Cortical Bone Microstructure Estimation in Ultrasound with Coherence-Selective f-K Beamforming
papers.abstract: We investigate the impact of coherence-selective frequency-wavenumber beamforming on the repeatability of cortical bone microstructure estimation in quantitative ultrasound. Accurate identification of cortical interfaces is essential for stable backscatter-based measurements, yet conventional delay-and-sum beamforming is sensitive to speckle noise and acquisition variability. By enhancing coherent reflections, the proposed method improves interface identification and reduces variability in quantitative estimates. Validation was performed on in vivo tibia measurements from healthy subjects with repeated acquisitions and multi-angle imaging. While no significant differences were observed in mean porosity and pore size estimates, the proposed method significantly reduced standard deviation and coefficient of variation, indicating improved repeatability. These results demonstrate that coherence-selective beamforming stabilizes microstructure estimation and enhances the robustness of quantitative ultrasound for bone assessment.

papers.title: Virtual Aperture Method for Estimating Cortical Bone Thickness and Speed of Sound in Humans
papers.abstract: Osteoporosis reduces cortical bone thickness and weakens bone microstructure, increasing fracture risk. This work presents a pulse-echo ultrasound method for estimating cortical thickness and speed of sound that implicitly accounts for refraction without explicit modeling. Transmit focusing creates virtual point sources on the bone surface, while shifted receive apertures form virtual receivers. Thickness and speed of sound are estimated by maximizing signal coherence. Validation was performed using simulations, a curved bone-mimicking phantom, and five human volunteers. In simulations, errors remained below 2% across varying thicknesses (1–10 mm), tilts (0°–30°), curvatures, and heterogeneous conditions with 10% porosity. Phantom experiments produced thickness estimates of 4.83 ± 0.08 mm and speed of sound estimates of 3025 ± 47 m/s, both within 3.4% of reference values. Human measurements also showed good agreement with CT (e.g., dCT = 3.71 mm, dUS = 3.92 ± 0.29 mm, within 5.4%). These results demonstrate the virtual aperture method as a promising non-invasive bedside technique for cortical bone assessment.

sessions.title: MSR: Counting the minutes

papers.title: Sequence Optimization for continuous, High Frame rate, and Long Data Acquisitions on a Verasonics Platform
papers.abstract: The ultrasound community has seen the rise in popularity of highly demanding imaging acquisition sequences, such as those for super-resolution imaging (SRUS) and functional ultrasound (fUS), which push the boundary of hardware limits. However, errors in sequence programming can lead to corrupted RF channel data, inaccurate timing(s), and reduced data throughput, which impacts the performance of these modalities. Critically, these errors can be subtle, often stemming from race conditions between hardware and software sequencers around direct memory access (DMA) events, which are difficult to diagnose and hidden by beamforming. In this presentation, we detail the fundamentals of the hardware and software sequencers of the Verasonics NXT research ultrasound scanner, highlighting some common pitfalls in sequence design and strategies to mitigate these errors. We include example Verasonics sequences for SRUS and fUS imaging for synchronous, asychronous, and concurrent acquisitions, which will be made publicly available on a Git repository for dissemination to the ultrasound research community.

papers.title: Superharmonic ULM Detects More low-Velocity Vessels Than SVD-Based ULM in Vivo
papers.abstract: The sensitivity of Ultrasound Localization Microscopy (ULM) to low-velocity vasculature relies on the robustness of the microbubble-tissue separation. Superharmonic (SpH) imaging potentially addresses the limitations of SVD-filtered ULM by leveraging nonlinear microbubble physics to separate the signals in the frequency domain. Simultaneous 2D SpH and 2D SVD-filtered B-mode images of internal kidneys (n = 7) were acquired continuously for 200 s at a frame rate of 400 Hz in anesthetized, freely breathing rodents. Slow-flow sensitivity was quantified in manually segmented kidney regions. Results demonstrate that SpH ULM retains high slow-flow sensitivity compared to conventional SVD-filtered ULM, with future applications in detecting slow-flowing glomerular units in the kidney.

papers.title: Matrix Whitening for Parameter-Less Clutter Suppression in Single Capillary Ultrasound Localization Microscopy
papers.abstract: The visualization of slow-moving microvasculature via Ultrasound Localization Microscopy (ULM) is often hindered by the difficulty of separating stationary tissue from blood flow. While Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) is the current standard for clutter filtering, its reliance on manual eigenvalue cutoff selection lacks physical intuition and risks suppressing low-velocity signals. This study introduces a parameter-less alternative using spatiotemporal whitening and Zero-phase Component Analysis (ZCA) to normalize eigen subspaces. By imaging 8-week-old mice with a 16 MHz linear array, we compared ZCA against traditional SVD (removing 20 eigenvalues). Results demonstrate that ZCA-processed maps significantly outperform SVD by reducing false tracks at skull-tissue interfaces and recovering 50% more capillaries. Furthermore, ZCA produced dwell time distributions that align more accurately with literature-standard distributions. Matrix whitening provides a superior, automated method for microvascular enhancement, specifically improving the detection and analysis of single-capillary dynamics.

papers.title: Super Resolution Cellular Imaging Using Nonlinear Ultrasound Scanning Microscopy
papers.abstract: Gas vesicles (GVs) are emerging as protein-based ultrasound contrast agents that enable deep-tissue cellular imaging, overcoming the limits of light. However, current GV imaging is diffraction-limited to ~100 μm resolution at 15 MHz, far above the 10–30 μm needed for single-cell imaging. Here, we introduce nonlinear ultrasound scanning microscopy, achieving 26 μm lateral resolution at 15 MHz. This method combines sub-wavelength GV excitation with dense line-by-line scanning, modifying a cross amplitude modulation sequence to reach λUS/15 (~6.5 μm) lateral precision using a standard array. We validated performance using U87 glioblastoma cells expressing GVs embedded in agarose. Single cells served as point targets, showing a resolution of 35 μm for µxAM versus 107 μm for conventional xAM. µxAM could resolve cells spaced 45 μm apart (<λUS/2), which xAM could not. In vivo imaging of GV-expressing brain tumors in mice confirmed these results, with Fourier line correlation measuring 26 μm resolution. This work demonstrates the first non-destructive super-resolution cellular ultrasound imaging, advancing GV technology toward true single-cell resolution in deep tissue.

papers.title: Localization Microscopy in the Channel Data Domain
papers.abstract: In Ultrasound Localization Microscopy (ULM) vessels are reconstructed by tracking peaks across image frames. A limitation of using image data for detection and tracking is that valuable information from the channel data is lost in beamforming and envelope detection. This can make it difficult to distinguish bubbles from clutter, especially for weak bubbles in the presence of beamforming artefacts such as grating lobes. We present a method that performs ULM directly on the channel data by fitting a set of micro bubble positions and intensities using a differentiable simulator to reproduce the measured channel data. The simulator includes relevant aspects of the ultrasound physics such as attenuation, the element directivity and the transmit waveform.
