Our method extends to 3D localization microscopy and arbitrary transducer geometries, which we demonstrate using under-sampled matrix array transducer with diverging lenses (pitch>3λ, aperture 93x71mm). Our method is able to reconstruct low flow vessels that are missing in traditional ULM reconstruction. The results show that ULM in the channel data domain is possible and can reveal small vasculature that remains hidden otherwise.

papers.title: ULM for Quantitative Monitoring of Microvascular Clot Dissolution Before and After Thrombolytic Therapy
papers.abstract: Microvascular obstructions are associated with poor clinical outcomes and are difficult to study with conventional imaging. This work presents an ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) approach to monitor flow in microvascular clot obstruction conditions, before and after thrombolytic treatment. Using an ultrasound-compatible platform with physiological blood and fibrin clots embedded in microchannels, this method enables quantitative, single-vessel analysis of clot dynamics. Clots were introduced into microvascular phantoms, and microbubbles with a dedicated ULM algorithm were used to measure flow velocities. Thrombolysis will be evaluated using tissue plasminogen activator (tPA), ultrasound with microbubbles, and their combination. ULM successfully visualized and quantified flow in obstruction scenarios, showing elevated velocities near clots and reduced microbubble tracking. After tPA treatment, clot volume decreased, flow area increased and velocity profiles normalized, indicating restoration of laminar flow. Using this platform, ULM captured tPA-induced restoration of blood flow in individual small vessels, establishing a framework for therapy comparison and optimization.

sessions.title: MPA: Signal Processing and Deep Learing for Photoacoustic Imaging

papers.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Quantitative Assessment of Bone Microstructure from Photoacoustic Signals
papers.abstract: Accurate bone assessment is vital for fracture screening, but traditional methods face radiation or resolution trade-offs. Photoacoustic (PA) detection offers high-fidelity characterization, yet decoding signals remains difficult due to bone's complex poroelasticity. We propose Biot-PINN, a physics-informed neural network integrating Biot's theory into a U-Net to invert porosity from 128-channel PA signals. By embedding governing equations into the loss function, the model ensures physical consistency. Validated via k-Wave simulations and ex vivo bovine experiments, Biot-PINN achieved 96% and 97% accuracy, respectively. Results demonstrate that constraining the solution space with Biot's theory enhances accuracy and interpretability, offering a high-precision methodology for clinical skeletal health assessment.

papers.title: Real-Time Closed-Loop Control of Medical Microrobots Enabled by Deep Learning-Based Photoacoustic Tracking and Coded Excitation
papers.abstract: This work presents a real-time, photoacoustic (PA)-guided closed-loop control platform for medical microrobots operating under tissue. A 10 Hz (100 ms) loop integrates time-multiplexed US/PA acquisition, GPU beamforming, microrobot localization (deep learning vs. thresholding), and 8-coil magnetic actuation to avoid imaging–actuation interference. A YOLO-derived detector is fine-tuned on curated PA data (excluding the test robot to probe generalization). To enable compact illumination with low-energy VCSELs, the system compares single-pulse excitation to length‑7 Barker-coded excitation with matched filtering. Experiments steer a 300 µm spiral robot along a ~1.6 mm figure‑of‑8 at 20 mm depth (467 ± 114 µm/s). Compared to an optical reference, US-only threshold tracking misses >91% of detections, while PA thresholding cuts misses to 17.4% (RMS 62 ± 16 µm) and DL tracking to 16.9% (RMS 67 ± 15 µm). Barker coding boosts PA SNR from 42.9 dB to 50.5 dB (~7 dB), supporting deeper-penetrating, more portable PA microrobotics.

papers.title: Phase-Coded Single-Pixel Photoacoustic Reconstruction for Prior-Guided 3D Vascular Imaging
papers.abstract: Single-Pixel photoacoustic imaging offers a compact, low-cost route to 3D reconstruction, but limited spatial diversity produces correlated voxel responses and an ill-conditioned inverse problem. This work proposes a prior-guided phase-coded reconstruction framework in which a constrained phase mask placed before the receiver introduces state-dependent wavefront modulation without additional acquisition channels. Eight coded measurements are obtained by translating the mask among discrete states, and flat-reference calibration suppresses common-mode signal components while preserving modulation-dependent information. In k-Wave 3D vascular phantoms, phase coding reduced system-response row correlation from 0.2556 to 0.0838 and increased effective rank from 0.0782 to 0.4735 compared with the no-mask single-receiver baseline. With strong anatomical support, SNR increased from 8.29 to 11.50 dB, CNR from 0.53 to 9.31 dB, correlation from 0.3298 to 0.6418, and Dice score from 0.4056 to 0.6886. These results demonstrate that phase-coded measurements improve conditioning and reconstruction quality in prior-guided single-Pixel 3D vascular photoacoustic imaging.

papers.title: Nonlinear Photoacoustic Imaging for Tensile Force Measurement Using Dual-Pulse Excitation
papers.abstract: We propose a dual-pulse nonlinear photoacoustic tomography (PAT) method for real-time tensile force measurement. Two nanosecond laser pulses with controllable delay generate a nonlinear photoacoustic (PA) response by probing thermal relaxation. A model links the nonlinear signal increment and decay to tensile force via stress-dependent Grueneisen parameter and thermal diffusivity. Experiments on a tungsten wire under calibrated loading were performed using a synchronized dual-laser system (0~200 ns delay) with single-element and 128-channel array detection. The nonlinear PA signal shows delay-dependent decay and strong correlation with tensile force. The extracted amplitude parameter exhibits high linearity (R²≈0.99), while the relaxation rate increases with load. Nonlinear PAT imaging improves contrast and enables real-time tracking of tensile variation, demonstrating feasibility for quantitative biomechanical sensing.

papers.title: Filtered Delay Coherent-Gaussian-Weighted Multiply-and-Sum Beamformer for PLD-Based Reflection Mode Photoacoustic Imaging: Experimental Results
papers.abstract: The low optical fluence of pulsed laser diode (PLD)-based photoacoustic imaging (PAI) limits image quality by reducing SNR and introducing artifacts. To address this, we propose a novel beamformer, Filtered Delay Coherent-Gaussian-Weighted Multiply-and-Sum (F-DCGwMAS), which integrates coherence-adaptive Gaussian weighting directly within the F-DMAS framework to enhance noise suppression, contrast, and resolution. The method was experimentally validated on chicken breast tissue with three ink-filled capillary targets (0.7 mm diameter) at depths of 4-11 mm using a 128-element linear array and 905 nm PLD excitation (18 µJ and 21 µJ). Results demonstrate that F-DCGwMAS consistently outperforms DAS, F-DMAS, and F-DMAS+CF in both contrast ratio (CR) and SNR. At 18 µJ, CR improvements of up to ~138% and SNR gains up to ~63% over DAS were achieved, with additional improvements over other methods. Similar trends were observed at 21 µJ, confirming robust performance across energy levels. These findings highlight F-DCGwMAS as an effective approach for improving image quality in low-SNR, PLD-based PAI systems.

papers.title: Acoustic Scattering Encoding for super-Resolution Microvascular Optoacoustic Imaging
papers.abstract: This work presents a new approach to achieve super-resolution in localization optoacoustic tomography (LOT) while reducing hardware complexity. Traditional LOT methods rely on dense detector arrays and complex systems to track sparse absorbers in blood, limiting scalability. Here, we introduce acoustic scattering as an alternative encoding mechanism, allowing spatial information to be captured in time-domain signals using minimal hardware. The method uses an acoustically dispersive medium to encode signals, enabling accurate localization of absorbers with even a single detector. A self-calibrated forward model reconstructs these signals without prior knowledge of the scattering field. The approach is tested with a limited-aperture setup in both phantom and in vivo experiments. Results show high-precision localization and vascular imaging resolution comparable to conventional LOT. Signal-to-noise ratio remains strong even with one detector. Overall, the method simplifies system design and lowers costs while maintaining performance, making super-resolution optoacoustic imaging more accessible and scalable.

sessions.title: SPT: Ultrasound Neural Stimulation and Guidance - Enabling Technologies - II

papers.topicName: Spotlight Session: Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Devices & Applications
papers.title: Artificial Hibernation by Combining Ultrasound with Genetics
papers.abstract: This study presents a sonogenetics-based approach for inducing artificial hibernation through noninvasive and cell-type-specific neuromodulation. The ultrasound-sensitive ion channel TRPV1 was expressed in excitatory neurons of the preoptic area (POA), a hypothalamic region involved in thermoregulation, using stereotaxic AAV delivery in mice. A wearable ultrasound device enabled repeated transcranial stimulation of the POA. Physiological responses were evaluated using infrared thermography of brown adipose tissue temperature (TBAT) and indirect calorimetry measurements of metabolic activity (VO2, VCO2). Sonogenetic stimulation induced robust and reversible hypothermic and hypometabolic states. Compared with ultrasound neuromodulation alone, TRPV1-mediated sonogenetics produced significant temperature reduction at lower acoustic pressures, indicating reduced activation thresholds. These findings demonstrate that sonogenetics enables genetically targeted control of thermoregulatory circuits and may support development of therapeutic hypometabolic strategies.

papers.topicName: Spotlight Session: Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Devices & Applications
papers.title: Towards an Earpiece for Dry Ultrasonic Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation
papers.abstract: Ultrasound (US)-based auricular vagus nerve stimulation (aVNS) is an emerging noninvasive neuromodulation modality for therapeutic and well-being applications. However, existing systems often remain bulky and require wet coupling media. We present a wearable US stimulation system combining a personalized, dry-coupled earpiece with a battery-powered, wirelessly controlled US probe. The earpiece integrates a 2 MHz piezoelectric transducer fully encapsulated in Humimic material for anatomical fit and stable coupling without externally applied gel. Hydrophone measurements of the encapsulated earpiece in water yield a peak rarefactional pressure of 0.24 MPa at 15 mm under 15 V unipolar excitation. Fully dry, in-ear pulse-echo acquisitions demonstrate acoustic transmission under realistic wearing conditions. These results establish the integration of a personalized dry acoustic interface with wearable stimulation electronics, providing a platform for investigating US-based aVNS. Future studies will assess functional outcomes, including heart rate variability and pupillary responses during stimulation.

papers.topicName: Spotlight Session: Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Devices & Applications
papers.title: A Head-Mounted Acousto-Optic Platform for Single-Neuron Imaging During Focused Ultrasound Neuromodulation in Freely Behaving Mice
papers.abstract: Focused ultrasound (FUS) is a powerful tool for noninvasive neuromodulation, yet its cellular mechanisms remain poorly understood due to a lack of platforms for simultaneous stimulation and high-resolution recording in mobile subjects. We developed a novel, lightweight (2.2 g) head-mounted acousto-optic system that enables longitudinal tracking of single-neuron calcium dynamics during FUS in freely behaving mice.The system integrates a miniaturized microscope, GRIN lens, and a 3.2 MHz ring transducer. In mice (n=10) expressing GCaMP6s, we targeted the preoptic area (POA) using FUS (1 MPa, 50% duty cycle, 10 Hz PRF). Single-neuron signals were recorded alongside core temperature and oxygen consumption (VO2). Results showed a decrease in temperature (−1.6 ± 0.3 °C ) and VO2 (−19.7 ± 3.8%) following stimulation. We identified a stable population of ultrasound-responsive neurons (approx. 20% of the field of view) whose calcium dynamics strongly correlated with these physiological changes. These findings reveal a functionally defined neuronal population recruited by FUS and establish a versatile platform to elucidate the cellular-level mechanisms of ultrasound neuromodulation.

papers.topicName: Spotlight Session: Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Devices & Applications
papers.title: TuFFlex: a Tunable-Focus Flexible Ultrasound Device for Adaptive Transcranial Stimulation
papers.abstract: A Tunable-Focus Flexible Ultrasound Device (TuFFlex) is a tunable-focus flexible ultrasound device for adaptive transcranial stimulation. It addresses the fixed-focus limitation of conventional transcranial focused ultrasound, which often requires lenses, standoff changes, or multiple transducers to target cortical and subcortical regions. TuFFlex uses a 55-mm-diameter, 650-kHz circular aperture with a mini-motor-actuated perimeter-control mechanism. Peripheral 3D-printed anchors and tensioning tethers adjust the global curvature, enabling curvature-dependent focal reconfiguration. Multiple active elements are connected by serpentine electrodes to form a mechanically flexible unified aperture. k-Wave simulations showed focal-depth tuning from approximately 30 to 90 mm. At a representative 30-mm radius condition, the simulated field produced 1.52 MPa peak pressure, 1.54 W/m² intensity, 2.02/1.99 mm lateral FWHM, 6.31 mm axial FWHM, and −16 dB peak sidelobe level, indicating a confined focus with limited off-target energy.

sessions.title: MIS: AI for Ultrasound Diagnosis & Clinical Decision Support

papers.title: ZAGNet: Zone-Aware Graph Aggregation Network for Patient-Level Lung Ultrasound Diagnosis
papers.abstract: Lung ultrasound (LUS) diagnosis requires integrating findings across multiple anatomical zones, often under incomplete acquisition. We propose ZAGNet, a zone-aware graph neural network for patient-level LUS classification. Frame-level detections of consolidation and pleural effusion are temporally linked into tracklets and represented as nodes with spatial and confidence features. Nodes are connected using an anatomical adjacency map, and message passing aggregates inter-zone context. A global node produces patient-level predictions, enabling flexible handling of variable and missing zones. Evaluated on a multi-center dataset of 714 subjects (20,256 video loops), ZAGNet achieved AUC 0.803 for consolidation and 0.893 for pleural effusion, outperforming max (0.677/0.804) and mean pooling (0.674/0.815). Results show that graph-based aggregation captures inter-zone dependencies and supports robust patient-level LUS assessment.

papers.title: Generalizable Ultrasound Optic Nerve Sheath Segmentation with Physiology-Aware Quality Control
papers.abstract: B-mode ultrasound measurement of the Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter (ONSD) is widely used for non-invasive intracranial pressure assessment, but deep learning (DL) segmentation models often lack generalization across devices and fail to ensure anatomical plausibility. Conventional metrics such as Dice can mask errors that lead to clinically unreliable results. This study evaluates a DL segmentation pipeline on an external dataset and introduces a physiology-aware Quality Control (QC) algorithm for automated screening. The pipeline combines YOLO-based ROI detection with U-Net multiclass segmentation. Trained on a multi-device dataset, it was tested without fine-tuning on 6291 external images. The QC classifier evaluates structural and anatomical features to categorize masks as Complete, Partial, or Absent. Results show 75.7% Complete, 23.5% Partial, and 0.8% Absent masks. The QC module effectively identifies anatomically implausible outputs, complementing traditional metrics and improving clinical reliability of ONSD estimation.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Based Ultrasound Analysis for Glucose Classification in Flowing Blood
papers.abstract: Achieving non-invasive, real-time glucose monitoring continues to be a significant hurdle in diabetes management. To address this, our research introduces a novel ultrasound-driven deep learning framework that pairs a 27 MHz single-element ultrasonic transducer with a convolutional neural network (CNN). We collected acoustic data from circulating, modified blood samples spanning 30 different glucose levels, varying between 0 and 250 mg/dL. These raw signals were transformed into spectrograms via Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) and then processed by a three-layer CNN. When classifying the 30 distinct glucose levels, the system yielded an accuracy of 88–90% in a narrow tube (0.7 mm outer diameter) and 98–99% in a broader tube (3.0 mm outer diameter). Furthermore, the model attained up to 100% accuracy when categorizing the data into five diagnostic groups. Ultimately, these findings validate the viability of needle-free, ultrasound-based glucose tracking and underscore its strong promise for future continuous monitoring systems.

papers.title: Automatic Vessel Segmentation and Event Detection in Compression Ultrasound for Deep Vein Thrombosis Assessment
papers.abstract: Compression ultrasound is the standard method for diagnosing deep vein thrombosis (DVT), but its reliability depends on operator expertise. To support AI-assisted diagnosis, we propose an uncertainty-aware vessel tracking framework for compression ultrasound. B-mode movies were acquired using a clinical scanner (ARIETTA 850, FUJIFILM) with a 7-MHz linear probe. A total of 738 datasets were collected, including 650 negative cases and 88 positive cases with proximal or distal DVT, and divided into training, validation, and test sets at a ratio of 5:1:1. The method combines U-Net-based vessel segmentation, temporal tracking of arteries and veins, and uncertainty estimation using Monte Carlo dropout. By tracking vessels across about 100 frames over three compression cycles, the framework captures compression-induced changes in vessel morphology and quantifies prediction reliability. In DVT-positive cases, uncertainty in thrombus regions (0.761) was higher than that in arteries (0.370, 0.515) and negative veins (0.476). These results suggest that temporal vessel dynamics and uncertainty features can improve the robustness and clinical reliability of AI-based DVT diagnosis.

papers.title: Carotid Plaque Volume Extraction for Freehand 3D Ultrasound Images Using a Multi-View Segmentation Approach
papers.abstract: The automatic detection of the 3D morphology of carotid plaques is crucial for the vulnerability assessment.This study proposes a multi-view automatic segmentation framework to achieve accurate 3D plaque volume extraction from freehand ultrasound images. Specifically, a dual-branch pre-trained nnU-Net framework was proposed for multi-view carotid plaque segmentation. The method performed cross-view geometric alignment to reproject longitudinal features into the transverse space, and introduced 3D cross-attention on the shared representation to enable voxel-level cross-view feature interaction.The model achieves a Dice coefficient of 0.81±0.01, IoU of 0.69±0.14, and a median 95% Hausdorff distance of 3.6 pixels. It achieves lower relative volume error (RVE=0.21±0.25) compared with cross-sectional (0.23±0.38) and longitudinal views (0.28±0.53). By integrating complementary information from cross-sectional and longitudinal perspectives, the proposed method provides more accurate and robust 3D structural characterization of carotid plaques.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Based Ultrasound Urodynamic Studies for Bladder Pressure Estimation
papers.abstract: Urodynamic studies (UDS) are the clinical gold standard for evaluating lower urinary tract dysfunction but require invasive catheter-based measurements of vesical pressure (Pves), abdominal pressure (Pabd), and detrusor pressure (Pdet). We developed a deep learning-based ultrasound UDS workflow to noninvasively estimate all three pressure signals. High-frame-rate ultrasound data were acquired during bladder filling from 29 patients undergoing clinical UDS. The ultrasound workflow included bladder wall imaging, acoustic radiation force excitation, and tracking of Lamb wave-induced bladder wall displacement. Modified transfer-learning ResNet-50 regression models were trained using displacement plots and bladder features to estimate Pves, Pabd, and Pdet, with leave-one-subject-out testing. The model showed strong agreement with UDS measurements, with mean RMSE values of 8.34, 4.54, and 5.66 cmH₂O for Pves, Pabd, and Pdet, respectively. Pves, Pabd, and Pdet achieved PCC/ICC values of 0.85/0.83, 0.64/0.62, and 0.90/0.86, respectively. Ultrasound-derived BOOI and BCI also showed strong agreement with UDS-derived indices, with ICC values of 0.86 and 0.96

sessions.title: AFF: High Frequency Filters

papers.title: Bandwidth-Reconfigurable LL-SAW Filters for N77/N78 Bands
papers.abstract: This work presents a bandwidth-reconfigurable longitudinal leaky surface acoustic wave (LL-SAW) filter platform targeting 5G NR N77/N78 C-band operation. The proposed approach achieves intrinsic bandwidth reconfigurability by reconfiguring the IDT polarity and finger connectivity within an IDT period. All devices are implemented on a single X-cut LiNbO3/SiO2/SiC wafer while maintaining the same in-plane angle α. Finite-element simulations reveal that α-optimized LL-SAW modes provide large k2eff, and that modified-polarity IDTs enable tunable k2eff for controlled bandwidth. Two ladder-type filters (F1 and F2) with distinct bandwidth targets are designed and fabricated to cover the N77 and N78 bands. Measurements confirm discrete bandwidth states: F1 achieves a 17.6% fractional bandwidth (FBW) at 3.698 GHz, whereas F2 provides narrower 7.3% FBW at 3.520 GHz. These results provide a scalable and integration-friendly solution for future multi-band and multi-bandwidth acoustic RF front ends.
keywords: longitudinal leaky surface acoustic wave (LL-SAW) filters

papers.title: Longitudinal Frame Structure for Suppressing Finite-Length-Induced Spurious Responses in XBARs
papers.abstract: Laterally excited shear mode bulk acoustic wave resonators (XBARs) are promising for next-generation RF filters, but their performance depends on stable confinement of the resonant mode excited by interdigital transducers (IDTs). As the IDT pitch is reduced, longitudinal confinement deteriorates and longitudinal leakage becomes significant. To address this issue, we propose a Longitudinal Frame Structure (LFS), formed adjacent to the outermost IDTs, as an acoustic confinement structure for suppressing longitudinal leakage. The LFS modifies the boundary condition for acoustic waves propagating longitudinally, is compatible with existing lateral confinement structures, and can be introduced without additional fabrication steps. Finite element simulations using a finite-length resonator model showed that the LFS reduces acoustic loss and spurious responses, bringing the electrical characteristics closer to an ideal periodic boundary model. Displacement analysis showed that the LFS stabilizes the longitudinal mode profile over a frequency range. These results demonstrate that the proposed LFS is an novel and effective longitudinal confinement structure for improving XBAR performance.

papers.title: Enabling High Q and Spurious-Free Response in Ultrawideband HAL SAW Resonator Using Hammer Head with Metal Overlay
papers.abstract: The hetero acoustic layer (HAL) surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonator employing 11°YX-LiNbO3(LN) on Quartz or Glass shows large electromechanical coupling coefficient (k2>30%), good temperature stability and out-of-band spurious-free characteristic. However, the transverse modes (TMs) inevitably arise in such ultrawideband devices due to a highly convex slowness curve. Several approaches were proposed to suppress TMs such as the piston mode using hammer head and apodization. However, in ultrawideband resonators, the former can hardly suppress strong TMs while the latter faces severe Q degradation. On the other hand, the study of ultrawideband TMs suppression is usually limited to experiments. The objective of this work is to comprehensively study the TMs suppression in ultrawideband SAW resonators, and achieve spurious free characteristic without sacrificing Q. Last, a general design guideline for spurious modes suppression without Q degradation will be established after experimental verification.

papers.title: A Novel Cascaded FBAR Based on Sputtered Al0.7Sc0.3N with High Electromechanical Coupling Coefficient of 19.5% at 10.8 GHz
papers.abstract: This work aims to develop a sputtering-only cascaded FBAR technology that utilizes highly Sc-doped AlScN films with suppressed abnormally oriented grains (AOGs), enabling the realization of Ku-band FBARs with high electromechanical coupling (k^2). A bottom floating electrode is utilized to minimize the thickness of the bottom electrode layer, while the thickness of the piezoelectric layer is increased to enhance the piezoelectric response. Notably, an additional 30 nm AlN seed layer is introduced on the bottom electrode to suppress the generation of AOGs and control residual stress for the AlScN deposited subsequently. The shape of the top electrode is optimized to a trapezoidal shape to avoid lateral spurious modes. Meanwhile, simulations are performed to determine the gap length between two top electrodes, and the value that minimizes spurious modes is found. Finally, an AlScN cascaded FBAR operating at 10.76 GHz with k^2 of 19.5% and maximum quality factor Q of 126 was fabricated, which demonstrates a record high k^2 compared to all other AlScN based FBARs operating in a similar frequency range, making it suitable for next-generation wireless communications.

papers.title: Hybrid Filter Using XBAR and IPD Technologies for 5G/6G Large Bandwidth Applications
papers.abstract: RF filters demand wider bandwidth and higher selectivity as mobile communications evolve. To overcome the bandwidth limitations of acoustic filters and the insufficient frequency selectivity of IPD filters, hybrid filters are widely investigated. However, existing inductor and acoustic series topologies exhibit limited flexibility, struggling to balance bandwidth and out-of-band rejection. This work proposes a hybrid filter integrating acoustic resonators and IPDs, synthesized via a quasi-elliptic topology with a multi-transmission-zero (TZ) tuning mechanism. The filter forms a quasi-elliptic response by shunting an XBAR with an inductor and cascading it with a matching network for bandwidth expansion. Furthermore, three topological modifications are incorporated to enhance the out-of-band rejection and frequency selectivity. The optimized filter shows a center frequency of 3.66 GHz, a bandwidth of 0.94 GHz. The 3 dB/10 dB shape factor is improved from 0.638 to 0.776, with stopband rejections exceeding 41 dB and 62 dB. This scheme successfully combines the high-Q of acoustic resonators and the flexibility of lumped elements, showing great potential for 5G RF front-ends.

papers.title: 12.6 GHz Solidly Mounted S1 Mode Resonator Based on LiNbO3/W/SiO2/SiC Substrate
papers.abstract: To enable 5G/6G communications above 10 GHz, acoustic resonators must overcome low phase velocity (~4000 m/s). Several methods have been proposed to build high frequency resonators. FBARs and Lamb wave devices based on suspended piezoelectric films offer high frequency but suffer from insufficient structural stability. Longitudinal leaky surface acoustic wave (LL SAW) exhibits high velocity, yet its Q value degrades rapidly with frequency due to energy leakage. We propose a solidly mounted S1 mode resonator with a simple, stable structure consisting of a SiC substrate, a tungsten layer, a LiNbO3 film, and top electrodes. With the LiNbO3 thickness (hₚ) fixed at 150 nm, the S₁ mode exhibits a resonant frequency (fᵣ) significantly higher than those of other modes. The introduced tungsten layer substantially reduces energy leakage and thereby enhances Q. The fabricated S1 resonator shows fr = 12.6 GHz, Qmax = 254, and k2 = 8.4%. These results demonstrate that the proposed S₁ resonator not only offers structural stability but also achieves high frequency and reasonably high Q, indicating its potential for operation above 10 GHz.

sessions.title: MEL: Advanced Wave Physics and Multi-Transducer Instrumentation

papers.title: Exploiting Shear Wave Reflections for Elasticity Quantification in Confined Microfluidic Channels
papers.abstract: Quantifying extracellular matrix stiffness inside microfluidic platforms is essential for organ-on-chip mechanobiology, drug screening, and tumor microenvironment studies, yet no reliable in-channel elastography method currently exists. Rigid channel walls in microfluidic systems distort shear-wave propagation, and conventional analytical models fail to recover the true tissue elasticity. To address this gap, we propose a single-element reflected shear wave (R-SW) elastography framework for small-sample geometries, combined with size-specific machine learning (ML) to decouple boundary artifacts and directly quantify the intrinsic stiffness of materials confined in microchannels. Results demonstrate that the proposed setup can successfully capture shear wave reflections within microchannels. Our ML models are validated against simulations with strong predictive performance (R² > 0.99). With experimental data, the models eliminated geometry-induced boundary artifacts and yielded consistent elasticity values with MSEs as low as 0.112. This combined R-SW and ML approach provides a practical, robust route to non-invasive stiffness quantification in microchannel environments.

papers.title: Shear Wave Velocity Estimation in 3D Magnetomotive Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Magnetomotive ultrasound (MMUS) relies on magnetic excitation of embedded nanoparticles to induce tissue displacement, enabling mechanical characterization through shear wave tracking. However, conventional MMUS is largely restricted to 2D imaging, limiting the assessment of complex wave propagation; here, we propose 3D MMUS for volumetric analysis. Experiments were performed in tissue-mimicking phantoms (8% PVA, 3% cellulose) containing a 5 mg inclusion of MnFe₂O₄ nanoparticles. Data were acquired using a 2.5 MHz matrix array probe (3072 elements; Vermon) connected to Verasonics systems, enabling high-rate volumetric imaging. Magnetic excitation was generated by a custom coil producing fields up to 300 mT. Shear waves were visualized over a 40×40×50 mm volume, yielding a velocity of 3.25±1.8 m/s (R²=0.79), in agreement with clinical elastography (3.0±0.4 m/s). The 3D approach enabled improved visualization of wave propagation and reduced dependence on imaging plane selection, supporting more robust volumetric stiffness estimation.

papers.title: Improved Point Shear Wave elastography with Coherent Multi-Transducer Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Shear wave elastography (SWE) enables quantitative assessment of tissue mechanical properties through shear wave (SW) speed estimation. However, accuracy depends on displacement tracking quality, which is limited by inherent ultrasound (US) constraints, including low and anisotropic spatial resolution, limited signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and view-dependent artifacts. Coherent multi transducer ultrasound (CoMTUS) overcomes these limitations by coherently combining data from multiple probes to form a large effective aperture, improving SNR and spatial resolution. SW propagation was tracked using high-frame-rate diverging wave (DW) imaging at 10 kHz pulse repetition frequency. For CoMTUS, 2 transmission events occured, yielding a 5 kHz frame rate. This was compared with single probe US setup, where one probe imaged by compounding 5 DWs, yielding a 2 kHz frame rate. CoMTUS improves tracking quality at a higher frame rate, resulting in more stable and precise SW speed estimation with reduced bias and variance. Overall, CoMTUS improves SWE performance and enables multi-directional excitation, which is particularly advantageous for deeper regions and anisotropic media.

papers.title: Coplanar Dual-Probe Ultrafast Ultrasound Reveals the Importance of Full Vectorial Tissue Velocity for Robust Shear Wave Speed Estimation
papers.abstract: Conventional shear wave elastography typically tracks only the axial tissue velocity which assumes purely lateral propagation and axial polarization due to axially-exerted acoustic radiation forces. However, shear waves are inherently vectorial. Their propagation through inhomogeneous media induces diffraction, refraction, and reflection. Tracking the polarization directions as shear waves evolve ensures the pure shear wave assumption for accurate shear wave speed (SWS) estimation. This study aims to investigate full vectorial shear wave propagation and its impact on SWS estimation by coplanar dual-probe ultrafast ultrasound.

papers.title: Fast Volumetric Elastography Using Plane Wave ARFI Push Pulses
papers.abstract: Acoustic radiation force impulse (ARFI) imaging is an elastography method that uses acoustic push pulses to displace tissue, which is then visualized through displacement images. The contrast in these images is due to variations in tissue stiffness, with stiffer tissue experiencing less displacement. Although conventional ARFI is valuable, one limitation is that it uses a series of focused push pulses to sequentially interrogate tissue lateral locations. Between these pushes, time must be allotted for displacement tracking and thermal recovery. This makes volumetric ARFI challenging, especially for a large field of view. To address this, we demonstrate a single plane wave push pulse to induce motion throughout an entire field of view, and we pair this with a Bayesian displacement estimator to overcome the low SNR from the plane wave push pulse. The primary motivation for this work is to provide volumetric elastography to a robotic system that will be used for autonomous prostate resection.

papers.title: Improving Resolution, Accuracy, and Stability of Ultrasound Strain Imaging Using Hyper-Beam Incoherent Plane-Wave Compounding
papers.abstract: Quasi-static ultrasound strain imaging estimates tissue strain from tracked displacement, and its performance depends strongly on displacement accuracy and spatial resolution. In conventional normalized cross-correlation (NCC)-based tracking, limited image resolution, sidelobe artifacts, and speckle decorrelation can degrade NCC peak stability and reduce strain estimation accuracy. In this work, we improve strain imaging using hyper-beam incoherent plane-wave compounding (HB-ICPWC). By providing a narrower mainlobe, better sidelobe suppression, and improved speckle preservation during motion, HB-ICPWC enables more stable tracking and improves the resolution, accuracy, and robustness of NCC-based strain imaging.

papers.title: Four-Dimensional Sequential Elastography for Ocular Tissue Using 2D Matrix Array
papers.abstract: This study presents a sequential excitation 4D shear wave elastography (SWE) method for volumetric assessment of ocular tissue mechanical properties. Using a 2D matrix array (1024 elements) with a standard 256-channel system via 4-to-1 multiplexing, the approach avoids the need for costly fully-connected hardware. The method divides a 32×32 matrix into four subpanels and applies a swept-cross compounding strategy to reduce inter-panel gap artifacts and improve elevational resolution. A 4D directional filter enables direction-resolved shear wave analysis, and a distance-weighted averaging technique improves local wave speed estimation. Validation using wire targets and in vivo rabbit cornea showed improved elevational resolution (from 0.84 mm to 0.35 mm at 10 mm depth). In rabbit eyes, shear wave velocity increased with intraocular pressure: from 5.03 m/s (normal) to 12.45 m/s at 55 mmHg, demonstrating strong pressure sensitivity. This framework offers a cost-effective, accessible solution for high-quality 4D elastography applicable to ocular biomechanics and anisotropy assessment.

sessions.title: MIM: AI, Foundation Models & Learning-based Reconstruction

papers.title: Filter-US: a Physics-Informed Video to Frame Filtering Pipeline for Deep Learning-Based Ultrasound Image Analysis
papers.abstract: Deep learning (DL) for ultrasound (US) image analysis is often limited by the availability of large, high-quality annotated datasets. Converting US videos into frame-level datasets is a common workaround, but introduces substantial variability due to probe motion, inconsistent acoustic coupling, and acquisition artifacts. Treating all frames equally incorporates low-quality samples that corrupt supervision and degrade model performance. Despite this, systematic approaches for identifying and prioritizing diagnostically reliable frames remain underexplored. This study aims to address this gap by developing a reliability-driven framework for curating high-quality training data from ultrasound videos, enabling more robust DL model development under limited data while mitigating the impact of label noise. The proposed approach is validated on a COVID-19 classification task using lung ultrasound data, demonstrating consistent performance gains over unfiltered and randomly sampled datasets.

papers.title: Ultrasound Operator Guidance via Deep Latent Space Action Planning
papers.abstract: Ultrasound imaging is highly operator dependent, motivating guidance methods that assist users navigate to predefined anatomical views. Existing approaches rely on one-shot predictions or learned models, which are sensitive to domain shift and limited in generalization to patient-specific targets. We propose a general framework that formulates probe navigation as a planning problem over empirically observed image–action transitions, enabling arbitrary goals such as standardized or patient-specific views with real-time guidance. The method encodes the live and target view in a compact latent space capturing relevant anatomy. Image–action dynamics are inferred from prior acquisitions and queried via nearest-neighbor search to identify transitions relevant to the current state. Candidate action trajectories are explored and evaluated by their likelihood of reaching the target, and the first action of the most likely trajectory is proposed to the user. We validate the approach on a carotid ultrasound dataset of over 200,000 images with probe motion data. The method achieves a promising 82% target view success rate over an eight-step planning horizon without visual feedback.

papers.title: AI-Based Multi-View Echocardiographic Image Synthesis Using Dynamic Shape Control
papers.abstract: AI-based approaches have improved echocardiographic workflows but remain limited by the lack of large annotated datasets, making synthetic data a promising alternative. However, most methods focus on specific views, lacking other standard or unconventional ones. To address this, we propose a novel framework for shape-controlled synthesis of multi-view echocardiographic sequences. The pipeline includes 2 modules: dynamic heart cross-sections are first extracted and then translated into ultrasound-like sequences using a two-stage AI approach. Stage 1 uses an unpaired translation model to generate realistic frames, while Stage 2 improves temporal coherence via video reconstruction. Using this framework, we generated a dataset of 6 views from 1,000 dynamic meshes derived from a statistical shape model. Evaluation of anatomical fidelity, image quality, and motion, including blinded clinician A/B studies, showed high realism in the generated frames. Although video remains more challenging, Stage 2 improved motion consistency. Overall, limitations are mainly related to mesh motion rather than the framework itself, with future work focusing on improved dynamics and additional views.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Network Architecture Search for Accelerated Ultrasound Beamforming
papers.abstract: Deep learning (DL) based beamforming accelerators can be used to improve image quality and increase the effective frame rate in medical ultrasound (US) applications. However, their performance varies significantly across different anatomical regions, imaging depths, and acquisition conditions. Beamforming accelerators trained on a specific US use case generally perform poorly on other use cases and on data acquired from other subject cohorts. Often, a single model is not optimal across all scenarios. To address this, we propose a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework that dynamically selects the most suitable reconstruction model based on clinically derived quality criteria.

papers.title: Physics Guided Multi-Scale Wavelet-Based Deep Learning Approach for Enhanced Cortical Visualisation in Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: Medical ultrasound (US) imaging commonly employs Delay-and-Sum (DAS) beamforming due to its computational simplicity. However, portable point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) systems often suffer from reduced image quality caused by hardware and computational limitations, resulting in low contrast, increased noise, and poor visualization of musculoskeletal (MSK) structures. To address these challenges, we propose a deep learning (DL) framework for improving MSK US images acquired using clinical POCUS probes. The proposed approach enhances structural details and tissue contrast while preserving clinically relevant anatomical information, making it suitable for real-time integration into portable US systems.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Latent Diffusion Models for Ultrasound Thyroid Nodule Synthesis
papers.abstract: Deep learning in thyroid ultrasound (US) is limited not only by dataset size but also by poor representation of diagnostically important phenotypes. This is especially relevant for thyroid nodules, as only about 5–10% are malignant, creating severe class imbalance unless datasets are intentionally enriched. We propose a physics-guided counterfactual synthesis framework combining a Physics-Informed variational autoencoder (VAE) with conditional latent diffusion for localized benign-to-malignant and malignant-to-benign nodule generation. The VAE models Nakagami-based speckle statistics and depth-dependent attenuation, while a physics-guided acoustic renderer recombines these components during reconstruction. Conditional diffusion performs ROI-guided class transformation while preserving surrounding anatomy. The framework was evaluated on TN5000 using 4,500 training images and 500 held-out real test images. Physics-LDM augmentation achieved 89.20% accuracy and 93.82% AUC, compared with 88.40% 93.10% for the real-only baseline and 85.60% 91.76% for weighted oversampling, supporting physics-guided counterfactual synthesis for enriching limited US datasets.

papers.title: A Frozen V-JEPA 2.1 Latent World Model for Offline Evaluation of A4CH Ultrasound Probe Guidance
papers.abstract: This work evaluates a frozen V-JEPA 2.1 video foundation model as a 6-DoF motion-conditioned latent world model for apical four-chamber cardiac ultrasound. A lightweight cross-attention predictor, selected via controlled ablation, predicts next-frame latent tokens from A4CH B-mode sequences paired with electromagnetic probe tracking. The model achieves stable multi-step latent prediction, outperforms an ImageNet-21k ViT-L/16 control on replay and action-attention metrics, and matches real-world rankings of candidate probe-guidance policies on held-out test sessions with narrower confidence intervals than the control. Motion-stratified analyses further support ranking robustness across probe-motion regimes, suggesting frozen-JEPA latent prediction as a promising offline evaluation tool for cardiac ultrasound probe guidance.

papers.title: Cognitive Sampling for Motion Estimation in Ultrasound Using Temporally-Consistent Diffusion
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce a cognitive ultrasound pipeline that uses the variance between motion estimates on different diffusion posterior samples as the information target for selecting upcoming scan lines. We propose a novel history-aware diffusion posterior sampling algorithm to generate varied yet temporally-consistent video samples, eliminating the need for a specialized motion estimation method. As our pipeline is compatible with any motion estimation technique and as the information target is defined in the output space of the downstream task, the proposed cognitive acquisition scheme is easy to integrate, and guarantees alignment of the estimated uncertainties with the downstream tasks.

papers.title: PLAX Guide: an Interactive Real-Time Guidance System for PLAX View Acquisition
papers.abstract: The Parasternal Long-Axis (PLAX) view is a clinically significant echocardiographic perspective, but its consistent acquisition remains challenging. The PLAX guide is a real-time guidance system designed to assist users in obtaining the standard PLAX view. It continuously analyzes each frame using dual-head classification along two complementary axes: four proximity classes, which indicate the distance from the optimal PLAX view, and three tilt classes, offering actionable directional guidance to adjust the probe orientation and facilitate the sequential acquisition of the optimal view. It delivers actionable, real-time feedback through a designed graphical user interface to guide the acquisition of the standard PLAX view position. We propose a lightweight dual-head CNN architecture for the simultaneous classification of proximity and tilt. Experimental results demonstrate that it achieves an F1-score of 0.79 (k = 0.90) for proximity classification and 0.77 (k = 0.75) for tilt classification while maintaining real-time inference with only 0.85M parameters. In a pilot clinical study, AI-guided acquisition improved mean PLAX image quality by 6.8%, demonstrating clinical feasibility.

sessions.title: MIS: AI & Data‑Driven Methods

papers.title: A Hybrid Deep Learning Classification Model for Ultrasound Tomography
papers.abstract: Ultrasound tomography (USCT) provides reflection and sound speed (SOS) images that contain complementary information, including local texture and global structural features. This work proposes a hybrid deep learning framework that leverages modality-specific inductive bias by applying convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to reflection images and vision transformers (ViTs) to SOS images. Four architectures (joint CNN, joint ViT, CNN+ViT, and ViT+CNN) were evaluated on simulation and in vivo breast datasets using multi-class classification. Features extracted from each modality were fused for final prediction. The proposed hybrid model achieved the highest accuracy across both datasets, with relative improvements of 5.6% on simulation data and 10.6% on in vivo data. Results demonstrate that combining CNN and transformer backbones improves classification performance by effectively exploiting complementary characteristics of USCT data.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Based Pulse-Echo Monitoring of Ultrasound-Induced Bubbles Using a Dual-Element Transducer
papers.abstract: This work proposes a designed dual-element ultrasound transducer combined with a lightweight deep-learning classifier for pulse-echo monitoring of ultrasound-induced bubbles in tissue, supporting stable operation of ultrasound-induced optical clearing microscopy (US-OCM). A 30 MHz monitoring element was mounted concentrically within a 3 MHz HIFU element, sharing focal distance and imaging plane. The 30 MHz element receives echo signals reflected from acoustic bubbles, and the network is trained on the resulting pulse-echo RF signal patterns. Each signal was paired with its Hilbert envelope and provided to a lightweight 1D CNN as a two-channel input. The model achieved 96.0% accuracy and 98.6% recall via 5-fold cross-validation. TensorRT FP16 optimization further reduced inference time to about 70.5 us per sample, a level suitable for deployment on embedded systems.

papers.title: Ultrasound-Specific Foundation Models Improve Perceptual Metrics for Ultrasound Image Evaluation and Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) is often used as an automated metric for evaluation of image similarity, utilizing a pre-trained backbone model to compare images in feature space. It is widely used in computer vision applications that require image generation such as generative models and image reconstruction. Typically, ImageNet-based or general-purpose radiology models are used as the backbone for LPIPS. Here, we challenge the idea that such backbones can extract semantic meaning from B-mode images by composing a benchmark of classification, segmentation, and reconstruction tasks. We find that ultrasound backbones overwhelmingly outperform general purpose radiology models and in most cases also outperform ImageNet models, challenging the mainstream usage of these models in ultrasound projects. We will open-source our benchmark and code and welcome the contribution of additional ultrasound backbones.

papers.title: You Are What You Eat: Ultrasound Data Representation As the Driving Force Behind Deep Learning Classification Performance
papers.abstract: Most deep learning (DL) studies in ultrasound propose novel architectures for B-mode images without questioning this representation, largely because open-source ultrasound datasets are almost exclusively distributed in this format. Yet B-mode is just the human-readable endpoint of the ultrasound pipeline, where beamformer choice reshapes texture, while earlier stages such as IQ data preserve information lost downstream. We show that optimizing data representation can yield greater gains than optimizing the network itself. We provide a large-scale, systematic evaluation across two preprocessing axes: input representation (IQ vs B-mode) and beamforming method (DAS, DAS+PCF, DAS+SCF, IMAP-1, IMAP-2), for multiple 2D and 2D+time architectures under identical training conditions.

papers.title: Multimodal Vision–Language Models for Automated Fast Ultrasound Instruction Generation
papers.abstract: FAST exams are essential for detecting free fluid in critical care, yet reliable image acquisition is highly operator-dependent, limiting its use in prehospital, remote, and low resource settings. Advances in AI and multimodal large language models create an opportunity to shift US from an expert-driven skill to a guided, accessible process. We propose a real-time multimodal AI coaching system that enables novice users to perform complete, diagnostically adequate FAST exams. Untrained US users performed FAST exams with verbal guidance using a standardized transcript and tracked the US video, audio guidance, and synchronized 6-DoF probe motion tracking. AI models generated step-by-step scanning instructions from US videos, which were quantitatively compared to expert guidance using text embedding similarity across multiple acquisitions. This study demonstrates that multimodal large language models can effectively interpret US video and generate clinically meaningful scanning guidance, with performance significantly enhanced through domain-specific fine-tuning. These findings support the feasibility of real-time AI-assisted US coaching systems, particularly in non-expert settings.
keywords: Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma

papers.title: Multi-feature, Non-Invasive Acoustic Detection of Metallic Biopsy Markers in the IQ Domain of Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: Post-biopsy re-localization typically uses metallic markers imaged via X-ray or CT, causing radiation exposure and often requiring invasive wire localization. Ultrasound is non-invasive but operator-dependent and struggles to isolate metal echoes near bone or echogenic tissue. We propose a multi-feature framework detecting metallic markers in the ultrasound IQ domain via four acoustic traits: hyperechogenicity, comet-tail reverberation, echo-filled shadowing, and phase coherence. Candidate pixels are selected by Z-score thresholding and described by seven features (autocorrelation periodicity, axial persistence, comb-pattern similarity, shadow decay, relative brightness, phase variance, lateral A-line consistency), linearly combined with grid-searched weights into a per-pixel score. On a phantom and three ex-vivo cases (wing, drumette, leg) with screw, needle, and clip, the method achieved Dist 0.7 ± 0.6 mm, IoU 0.34 ± 0.26, FPR 0.006 ± 0.009, far surpassing a hyperechogenicity-only baseline (IoU 0.03, FPR 0.15). This establishes IQ-domain multi-feature acoustic detection as a reproducible, non-invasive approach for biopsy marker localization.

papers.title: A Large-Scale Ultrasound Channel Dataset Initiative for End-to-End Foundation Model Training
papers.abstract: Foundation models trained on large standardized datasets have transformed medical imaging modalities like CT and MRI, but ultrasound has not yet seen the same progress. Openly sharing channel data has been hard due to limited hardware access, fragmented standards, and high storage costs. Many existing datasets are restricted to single tasks and lack the scale needed for foundation model training. This work introduces a large-scale open dataset initiative for end-to-end foundation model training directly from ultrasound channel data. We target ≥20,000 acquisitions spanning in-vivo, ex-vivo, phantom, and simulated data, with annotations for image reconstruction, flow estimation, motion tracking, quantitative imaging, and interpretation. A unified format built on open software ensures consistent representation across heterogeneous sources, and the dataset is released under CC BY 4.0 for academic and commercial use. Built with hospitals, universities, researchers, and industry, the initiative covers data collection, curation and is hosted publicly on Hugging Face to enable the community and accelerate the next generation of breakthroughs in ultrasound imaging.

papers.title: Synthetic Ultrasound Images via Diffusion Models Based on Attenuation Dynamics
papers.abstract: Micro-ultrasound (micro-US) is an advanced imaging technique that operates at higher frequencies—typically 29 MHz or above—than conventional ultrasound, offering 3–4 times greater resolution. It is particularly effective in detecting prostate cancer, potentially providing real-time imaging quality comparable to that of MRI. With the growing use of deep learning in medical image segmentation, accurate prostate delineation has become crucial for guiding biopsies and supporting disease diagnosis. However, segmenting micro-US images remains challenging due to imaging artifacts and the indistinct boundaries between the prostate, bladder, and surrounding tissues.

papers.title: Deep Regression of Amniotic Fluid Index from Single-Quadrant Ultrasound: an Ablation Study on Architecture, Pretraining, and Depth Fusion
papers.abstract: We present a direct CNN regression approach for estimating Amniotic Fluid Index (AFI) from single-quadrant ultrasound panels, bypassing segmentation. From 443 third-trimester GE Voluson E10 scans (222 patients), we extracted 878 expert-annotated panels (AFI 0-11.6 cm) via paired symmetric cropping with OCR-guided inpainting. We ablated three backbones (DenseNet121, ResNet50, InceptionV3), two pretraining strategies (ImageNet vs RadImageNet), and depth fusion via FiLM, using stratified 5-fold cross-validation with L1 loss. DenseNet121 with ImageNet achieved MAE 0.864 cm, R2 0.683, Pearson r 0.828, a threefold reduction over prior segmentation work (MAE 2.67 cm). Counterintuitively, RadImageNet underperformed ImageNet (MAE 1.386), suggesting its corpus underrepresents obstetric ultrasound. FiLM depth fusion provided no benefit, indicating scale information is already implicit in single-quadrant content. Optimal-threshold pocket detection reached balanced accuracy of 0.91 and F1 of 0.95. Direct regression with natural-image pretraining is a strong default for AFI estimation.

papers.title: Quantum-State Variational Consensus Fusion for Multi-Rater Ultrasound Delineation
papers.abstract: This work presents QUAFUSE, a training-free quantum-state variational framework for consensus fusion of multi-rater ultrasound delineations. Unlike classical voting or reliability-based fusion, QUAFUSE encodes foreground evidence from multiple annotators in a normalized quantum state, enabling globally coupled evidence updates, nonlocal ambiguity resolution, and boundary-aware refinement without model training. The method combines annotator agreement, spatial coherence, and boundary sharpening in a variational objective before decoding the fused mask. Evaluated on a 30-case clinical abdominal ultrasound cohort (15 liver, 15 kidney) with three junior-radiologist annotations and a senior expert reference, QUAFUSE produced contours closer to the expert than majority voting, SIMPLE, and iSTAPLE, with the strongest gains in low-agreement regions. On liver cases, it improved DSC by 4.4 points and reduced HD95 and ASSD by 49% and 54%, supporting its novelty, clinical relevance, and efficiency for ambiguity-aware consensus estimation.

papers.title: Ultrasound Radiofrequency Signals Improve SAM-Based Semantic Segmentation of Breast Tumors
papers.abstract: Breast ultrasound tumor segmentation remains challenging because benign and malignant high-grade lesions may show similar B-mode appearances. This work proposes a radiofrequency (RF)-signal-guided SAM-based framework for breast tumor semantic segmentation. Instead of relying only on envelope-derived B-mode images, RF signals are converted into color-coded RF images to preserve polarity-, frequency-, and phase-related tissue information. The framework combines a SAM-derived ViT branch for global structural representation, a CNN branch for RF-sensitive local feature extraction, and cross-branch attention for multi-modal fusion. In addition, wavelet spectral features around point prompts are used to estimate the benign or malignant category of the prompted lesion region, enabling semantic mask prediction with both boundary and category information. The method was evaluated on an in-house high-grade BI-RADS breast RF dataset and the public OASBUD dataset. With one-point prompts, it achieved Dice scores of 73.32% and 75.62%, respectively; with nine-point prompts, Dice increased to 81.29% and 81.00%. RF-image input consistently outperformed B-mode input.

papers.title: Deep Learning Classification of Prostate Cancer Cells from Beamformed Radiofrequency Ultrasound Without Image Formation
papers.abstract: Ultrasound cell classification typically relies on B-mode images or quantitative ultrasound maps, both of which introduce information bottlenecks through envelope detection or model-dependent spectral fitting. This study demonstrates that a one-dimensional residual network (ResNet1D) trained end-to-end on beamformed radiofrequency signals, without image formation, can classify PC3-FLU and PC3-PIP prostate cancer cell lines with 92.4% accuracy, MCC of 0.849, and ROC-AUC of 0.976 across five nested cross-validation folds. Cell suspensions were loaded in wells within a 1.5% agarose phantom and imaged using a Vevo 2100 system. The model produced 243 errors out of 3,200 predictions, with narrow confidence intervals indicating high reproducibility. These results establish that discriminative biological information is encoded in the beamformed RF signal in ways recoverable by end-to-end deep learning, supporting extension of this framework to therapy-response monitoring.

sessions.title: MIS: Organ & Disease Detection / Classification

papers.title: Boundary-Aware Active Learning with Adaptive Uncertainty Calibration for Abdominal Ultrasound Segmentation
papers.abstract: Precise segmentation of boundary in abdominal ultrasound is vital but limited by high annotation costs. While Active Learning (AL) helps, conventional strategies fail due to spatial imbalance (boundaries comprise <5% of an image) and network miscalibration, resulting in incorrect estimation of boundary uncertainty. We propose Boundary-Aware AL with Dual-Level Adaptive Calibration (DLAC). We restrict uncertainty computation to organ boundary zones to eliminate background bias. To fix overconfidence, DLAC operates at two levels: class-level (inherent anatomical difficulty) and sample-level (adjusting for individual image complexity). Experiments on a patient-split abdominal dataset (liver, kidney, etc.) showed exceptional efficiency. With only 20% of the labels, our method achieved a 94.14% Dice and a 19.07 HD95. At a 40% budget, performance reached 96.04% Dice. By restricting uncertainty estimation to edge zones and calibrating confidence, our approach effectively extracts informative samples, reducing clinical annotation burdens while surpassing advanced methods.

papers.title: Hierarchical Analysis of B-Mode Ultrasound for Detection of Invasion in Follicular Thyroid Lesions
papers.abstract: Differentiation of follicular-derived thyroid lesions remains challenging in ultrasound, as malignancy is defined by capsular and/or vascular invasion, which cannot be directly assessed in B-mode imaging. A hierarchical, multiscale analysis of B-mode ultrasound images was proposed to identify features reflecting tumor microstructure and local boundary disruptions. A total of 171 lesions (342 images) with histopathological reference were analyzed. Global, local, and texture features were extracted. The perimeter-to-area ratio (P/A) achieved AUC up to 0.804 for differentiation of FA vs FTC and PDTC. Local boundary analysis enabled detection of focal capsule disruptions; for FA vs HCC, AUC reached 0.806. Kullback–Leibler divergence (AUC 0.731) differentiated PTC from FTC and HCC. The results demonstrate that diagnostically relevant information is multiscale and linked to local boundary complexity and tumor microarchitecture, supporting improved characterization beyond conventional risk stratification.

papers.title: Enhancing Cancer Localization Through System Identification: a Multiparametric Ultrasound Approach to Prostate Cancer Detection
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer represents one of the most prevalent malignancies affecting the male population worldwide. Prior investigations employing multi-parametric ultrasound have demonstrated considerable promise for the diagnosis of clinically significant prostate cancer. However, these studies have not incorporated system identification (SI) features within their deep learning (DL) predictive models. Contrast ultrasound dispersion imaging by identification of the input/output dilution system between adjacent voxels has been extensively utilized for the localization of cancer-associated angiogenesis in prostate lesions through contrast enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) following intravenous administration of an ultrasound contrast agent bolus. Using registered histopathological results as ground truth, the present study investigates the added diagnostic value to simulated targeted biopsy of malignant lesions conferred by integration of SI features within a dedicated DL predictive model on a dataset of 330 prostate cancer patients. An increase of 2.6% in the effective cross-validated AUROC and 10% in average effective specificity for thresholds corresponding to 80-84% sensitivity was observed.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Differential Diagnosis System for Lymphoma Based on CEUS Spatial Heterogeneity Analysis
papers.abstract: Contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) helps evaluate lymph node microvascular perfusion, but differentiating lymphoma from reactive hyperplasia remains challenging due to lesion drift and spatial heterogeneity. This study proposes an automated diagnostic framework integrating deep learning-based lesion tracking, spatially resolved perfusion quantification, and interpretable machine learning. A YOLOv11m detector with IoU-based continuity tracking enables robust lymph node localization and ROI extraction in CEUS videos. Each ROI is divided into an 8×8 grid to capture local perfusion heterogeneity via time-intensity curve (TIC) analysis. Nine hemodynamic parameters are extracted per grid, followed by feature selection and SMOTE balancing. Among multiple classifiers, the RBF SVM achieves the best performance: accuracy 0.71, sensitivity 0.80 for lymphoma, specificity 0.67, and weighted F1-score 0.72, outperforming global TIC analysis. SHAP analysis enhances interpretability. The system demonstrates automated, objective differential diagnosis of lymph node diseases, with potential for AI-assisted ultrasound.

papers.title: Multi-Feature-Based Classification of Lung Ultrasound B-Lines for Differentiating Pulmonary Edema and Fibrosis
papers.abstract: B-lines in lung ultrasound indicate interstitial syndrome but show similar patterns across different pathologies, making differential diagnosis challenging. This study proposes a multi-parametric radiofrequency (RF) analysis framework combined with machine learning to distinguish pulmonary edema from fibrosis. RF data from tissue-mimicking phantoms and rabbit models were analyzed, and seven features were extracted. Group differences were evaluated using independent t-tests. Classification was performed using decision tree (DT), support vector machine (SVM), and K-nearest neighbors (KNN). All features showed significant differences. In phantom data, KNN and SVM achieved the highest AUC (0.907), followed by DT (0.897). In vivo, KNN (0.888) and SVM (0.887) outperformed DT (0.849). SVM achieved the highest sensitivity (0.948), while DT showed higher specificity (0.675).

papers.title: A Quantitative Method of the Lung Injury Based on the Estimation of Lung Injury Depth via Phase Reversal Detection with Ultrasound RF Signals
papers.abstract: Quantitative lung ultrasound (LUS) currently relies on indirect B-line artifacts, lacking critical morphological information such as lesion depth. This study introduces a novel quantitative method based on RF signal phase reversal analysis to measure pulmonary lesion depth, establishing a direct acoustic biomarker for clinical diagnosis. Theoretically, ultrasonic waves undergo a 180° phase reversal upon reflection at the interface between lung lesions and alveolar air. Our algorithm identifies lesion boundaries by detecting this phase reversal in backscattered RF signals. The method was validated through three experiments: phantom studies with controlled depths (3-8 mm), an acute lung injury (ALI) model monitoring progression via oleic acid injection, and a chronic pulmonary fibrosis model induced by paraquat, correlated with biochemical SP-A levels. Results demonstrated high precision and robustness: phantom measurements showed a strong linear correlation (R² > 0.9) with actual depths. In the ALI model, the method successfully tracked increasing lesion depth over 60 minutes, and in the fibrosis model, depth measurements consistently tracked with serum SP-A concentrations.

papers.title: Wearable Ultrasound Patch with Physics-Guided Deep Learning for Continuous Monitoring of Post-Surgical Pneumothorax Recovery
papers.abstract: Pneumothorax is a common complication after thoracic surgery, requiring continuous monitoring to guide lung re-expansion and chest tube management. Although ultrasound is highly sensitive for pneumothorax detection, handheld examinations are limited by intermittent use and subjective interpretation of M-mode images. We developed a 5 MHz wearable ultrasound patch with a physics-guided deep learning framework for longitudinal monitoring of pneumothorax recovery. A clinical study enrolled 20 post-thoracic surgery patients, with 5 additional CT-guided procedure-related pneumothorax cases for validation. The patch continuously acquired bilateral intercostal M-mode signals, capturing transitions from the barcode sign to the seashore sign. A two-stage ResNet-18 model used three physical indicators—High Frequency Fraction, Fractal Dimension, and Temporal Centroid—to quantify severity and track recovery. The system achieved AUCs of 0.96 for pneumothorax detection and 0.87 for severity assessment, with an overall accuracy of 81.4%. Predicted severity scores correlated with CT-based volumes (r = 0.81), supporting the feasibility of continuous monitoring with the wearable ultrasound patch.

papers.title: A-Mode-Based 3D Bladder Volume Estimation via Multi-Channel Wall Detection Without Image Formation
papers.abstract: Accurate bladder volume estimation is essential for monitoring and managing lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS). This study proposes an A-mode-based framework that detects bladder wall locations from multi-channel A-line signals and reconstructs them as 3D coordinates for direct volume estimation without image formation. A patient-specific 3D simulation environment was constructed using CT segmentation data combined with Field II-based ultrasound simulation, to evaluate the feasibility of the proposed method. Anatomical regions including bladder, urine, fat, and muscle were segmented, and tissue-specific acoustic properties were assigned to model reflection and attenuation at boundaries. Multi-channel RF signals were generated using an 8×8 convex A-mode array. Simulation results demonstrated that the proposed A-mode-based method achieved a mean error of 22.5% and a median error of 15.4% across a bladder volume range of 100–600 mL. Notably, by reconstructing bladder wall coordinates directly in 3D space without relying on ellipsoidal assumptions, the proposed framework enables volume estimation for irregular bladder geometries.

papers.title: Optical Navigation-Assisted Ultrasound Fusion for Intraoperative Virtual MRI in Brain Tumor Resection
papers.abstract: We propose an optical navigation–assisted, ultrasound-driven framework for generating intraoperative synthetic MRI during brain tumor resection. By integrating multimodal co-temporal association and unimodal multi-temporal deformation updating, our method dynamically aligns preoperative MRI with real-time brain anatomy, compensating for brain shift and tissue loss. A deformation propagation network estimates 3D displacements from ultrasound, while optical tracking ensures global spatial consistency. Multi-temporal self-correction refines the cross-modal deformation field to produce anatomically accurate virtual MRI. Experiments on phantoms and cadaveric heads show a target registration error of 2.8 ± 0.3 mm, demonstrating reliable, continuous navigation comparable to preoperative alignment—overcoming key limitations of conventional IOUS–MRI fusion.

sessions.title: MTC: Tumor Characterization, Vasculature & Blood Dynamics

papers.title: Quantitative Ultrasound Analysis of 3D ABVS Volume Data in Breast Lesions Using Spatial Entropy and Statistical Models
papers.abstract: Background & Objective: ABVS provides extensive 3D views but lacks quantitative metrics. We integrated a Siemens ABVS probe with a Verasonics platform to acquire 3D volumetric data for enhanced lesion differentiation. Methods: 75 patients (41 benign, 34 malignant) were analyzed via dual-zone speckle analysis. A novel Spatial Distribution Shannon Entropy (SDSE) quantified lesion core heterogeneity, while peritumoral margins were evaluated using Nakagami and Homodynamic K-distributions. This hybrid strategy combines entropy-based sensitivity in the core with statistical robustness at the boundary. Results: Malignant lesions showed significantly higher complexity. SDSE identified core irregularities missed by conventional models, while Nakagami/K-parameters tracked marginal infiltration. Combining these zone-specific features markedly improved classification accuracy compared to global or single-parameter methods. Conclusion: Dual-zone speckle analysis is a robust framework for 3D breast differentiation, enhancing diagnostic precision in automated ABVS clinical workflows.

papers.title: Lesion and Perilesional-Tissue Quantitative Ultrasound for Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis in Breast Cancer
papers.abstract: Prior studies have shown that quantitative ultrasound (QUS) of breast lesions provides microstructural information useful for breast cancer assessment. Breast cancer may also cause microstructural changes in surrounding perilesional tissue. This study evaluates whether lesion and perilesional-tissue QUS parameters can predict axillary lymph node metastasis to support preoperative decision-making.

papers.title: High-Frequency Ultrasound Attenuation Imaging for in Vivo Mouse Tumor Characterization
papers.abstract: This study proposes a high-frequency (35 MHz) array-based attenuation imaging framework for in vivo tumor characterization in mice. RF data were beamformed and analyzed using frequency-domain methods, with attenuation estimated from the depth-dependent decay of band-limited power. Phantom experiments demonstrated accurate differentiation of attenuation coefficients with varying scatterer concentrations. In vivo imaging of 4T1 tumors revealed spatial variations in tissue attenuation overlaid on B-mode images. The results demonstrate that high-frequency attenuation imaging enables improved spatial resolution and provides a feasible quantitative tool for tumor characterization in small animal models.

papers.title: Envelope Statistics for Characterizing Shear-Rate-Dependent Red Blood Cell Aggregation
papers.abstract: Red blood cell aggregation under low shear affects hemorheology, microcirculation, and thrombosis. Ultrasound can noninvasively monitor backscatter from red blood cell suspensions, but conventional BSC and spectral-slope metrics may miss aggregation-induced scatterer heterogeneity. This study evaluated shear-rate-dependent aggregation in Couette flow using envelope statistics. Human red blood cell suspensions were prepared at hematocrit 0.4 in PBS with 29% OptiPrep and 2.88 g/dL dextran 500. Shear rates of 100, 10, and 1 s⁻¹ were generated in a 2-mm-gap Couette system. After stabilization, 5000 RF signals were acquired using a 30-MHz focused transducer. Hilbert-transform envelopes were analyzed using the Generalized Nakagami distribution to calculate m and s from depth-shifted ROIs. At 10 and 100 s⁻¹, GN parameters indicated random-medium scattering, consistent with estimated red blood cell density within the ultrasonic PSF. At 1 s⁻¹, m and s suggested structural contributions, with depth-dependent trends differing from the beam profile. These results suggest that envelope statistics can reflect spatial variations in aggregation within the flow channel.

papers.title: 3D Clutter Filter Wave Imaging for Pulse Wave Velocity Estimation
papers.abstract: Ultrasound-based pulse wave imaging enables non-invasive estimation of pulse wave velocity (PWV), a key indicator of vascular stiffness. Conventional methods rely on tissue motion estimation followed by velocity computation, whereas clutter-filtering-based approaches allow direct tracking of the wavefront without explicit motion estimation. While this method has been extended to 3D for applications in the myocardium, extending it to vascular imaging remains essential due to the inherently three-dimensional nature of arterial motion and the impact of out-of-plane effects on accuracy. In this work, we aim to extend this approach to 3D imaging of the common carotid artery. The proposed framework applies temporal high-pass filtering, envelope detection, spatiotemporal smoothing, and acceleration-based arrival time estimation to compute PWV from time-of-flight analysis. Simulation results demonstrate accurate PWV estimation, supporting the feasibility of the method.

papers.title: Effect of Venous Flow Velocity Distribution on Ultrasonic Backscatter Characteristics and Attenuation Coefficient of Blood
papers.abstract: In quantitative ultrasound (QUS) studies of blood, QUS parameters such as backscatter characteristics, attenuation coefficients, and the degree of red blood cell (RBC) aggregation are usually estimated within a region of interest (ROI). However, venous flow is typically laminar and produces a shear rate distribution that may cause ROI-dependent differences in parameters. This study investigates the effects of measurement position and analysis range on these parameters. RF signals were acquired from the dorsal hand vein of a healthy subject in their 20s using a 40-MHz ultrasound probe. The acoustic focus was set at five positions within the vessel. The backscattered power spectra were calculated from the RF signals. The attenuation coefficients were estimated around the center of the vessel and across the vessel lumen. The backscattered power spectra were higher at the central region, suggesting that the shear rate distribution affects the backscatter characteristics. The attenuation coefficient estimated around the center of the vessel was higher than that estimated across the vessel lumen. This study demonstrated that blood flow causes ROI-dependent differences in QUS parameters.

papers.title: Tumor Vasculature Characterization Using Multiple Scattering and Novel RMT-Based Metrics (ΔQC and R²)
papers.abstract: This study introduces new quantitative ultrasound metrics to characterize tumor vasculature using multiple scattering. Previous work showed that Scattering Mean Free Path (SMFP) can distinguish tumor from healthy tissue, while Random Matrix Theory (RMT) parameters reflect microbubble concentration. Here, the authors propose two new parameters, ΔQC and R², to improve vascular assessment. Their performance is evaluated alongside Scattering Mean Free Path (SMFP), maximum probability (λ_max), and expected value (E) using k-Wave simulations, gelatin phantoms, and in vivo rat fibrosarcoma models. Results showed SMFP and λ_max detect large vessel density changes but miss smaller differences, while E is insensitive. ΔQC demonstrated consistent sensitivity to vessel density and robustness to bubble concentration, making it a strong new metric. In phantoms, lower vessel density increased SMFP, ΔQC, and λ_max. In vivo, SMFP correlated strongly with vascular changes and ground truth (r = −0.87), even revealing necrosis-related vascular reduction. Overall, SMFP and ΔQC provide improved, structure-sensitive measures of tumor vasculature.

sessions.title: MTC: Tissue Phantoms & Advanced Biological Modeling

papers.title: Ultrasound-Based Monitoring of Drug-Release Dynamics in Gelatin-Magnesium Gallate Hydrogels via Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Hydrogel-based drug delivery systems enable controlled and localized therapeutics through tunable release behavior; however, conventional chromatographic and spectroscopic analyses are invasive and end-point based, limiting continuous monitoring. Although ultrasound can non-destructively probe structural changes, the resulting acoustic signals are subtle and difficult to interpret.
