This study presents a non-invasive platform integrating ultrasound with machine learning to decode acoustic signals and continuously monitor drug release from a Gelatin-Magnesium Gallate (GMG) hydrogel. Backscattered signals were acquired over time (0–360 min) using a 5 MHz transducer under in vitro, ex vivo, and HIFU-stimulated conditions, and time-gated signals from the hydrogel region were analyzed. Machine learning models (CNN-BiLSTM, CNN-BiGRU, and Vision Transformer) tracked temporal acoustic changes, with CNN-BiGRU achieving 100% accuracy and CNN-BiLSTM achieving 99.7%, while the Vision Transformer showed lower accuracy (60.44%–85.55%). These results demonstrate that machine learning enables accurate interpretation of ultrasound signals for continuous monitoring of drug release dynamics.

papers.title: Frequency-Dependent QUS Characterisation of the IEC Tissue Phantom As a Route to Customise Properties for Disease Specific Research
papers.abstract: The IEC standard is an agar-based tissue mimic (TMM) used to replicate echogenic response in ultrasound imaging and allow quantitative comparison between commercial systems [1]. While researchers have quantified behaviour (speed of sound, attenuation and backscatter coefficient (BSC), reproducibility), the contributions of each scattering agent (nominal diameters 37, 3 and 0.3 µm) are not determined against imaging frequency. In addition, model-based BSC estimation assumes particle sphericity, uniform distribution in a fluid, and absence of other contributors. To improve utility of the IEC TMM we investigated each scatterer diameter at two bandwidths: 5-8 MHz, 19-27 MHz to establish quantitative data for TMM customisation.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Based Digital Reference Phantom for Quantitative Ultrasound Analysis
papers.abstract: Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) has shown clinical promise in tissue characterization but traditionally requires calibration with a physical phantom, limiting clinical portability and workflow efficiency. This work proposes a deep learning-based digital reference phantom to extract the reference power spectrum, enabling calibration without a physical phantom during analysis. Paired radiofrequency ultrasound data were acquired from three tissue-mimicking phantoms and a well-characterized reference phantom. Power spectra were extracted using a 2D Hamming-windowed short-time Fourier transform. A U-Net was then trained to extract the reference power spectrum from target data. Backscatter coefficient (BSC) was computed from the output spectrum and compared with BSC computed using the physical reference phantom. The digital phantom achieved a mean sample-level BSC error of 2.3 ± 1.5%, RMSE of 2.94 ± 1.08 dB and near-zero mean bias of +0.075 dB, showing good agreement between the digital and physical phantom estimates. These results are promising for more flexible and portable quantitative ultrasound by removing the session-by-session dependence on physical reference phantom calibration.

papers.title: A Dual Framework for Characterizing Complex Tissues Using Quantitative Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Traditional ultrasound fails in complex media because multiple scattering disrupts the linearity between time and distance. Quantitative Ultrasound offers an alternative by using the diffusive regime to characterize tissues. The diffusion constant (D) is a key metric here as it correlates with scatterer density, a marker for diseases like edema, fibrosis, and tumors. While prior work validated D with direct tissue contact, this study evaluates its accuracy when an intervening layer like the abdominal wall is present. We compared two methods, Incoherent Backscattering (IBS) and enhanced Coherent Backscattering (eCBS), using simulations and experiments. Results show that while IBS allows for longer temporal measurements, it suffers from far-field diffraction. Gaussian beamforming corrects this by numerically refocusing the probe on the medium surface. Conversely, eCBS is resilient to phase aberrations due to its use of plane waves, though it is limited by a short temporal coherence window and angular resolution. This dual-method framework bridges the gap between models and clinical reality, enabling stable tissue monitoring through anatomical barriers.

papers.title: Experimental Characterization of Random Media for Lung Quantitative Ultrasound Using Incoherent Backscattering
papers.abstract: Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) is a promising approach for lung tissue characterization, but clinical translation requires controlled validation using phantoms with known scattering microstructure. This study develops i) gelatin-based air-bubble phantoms which undergo micro-CT to provide ground-truth for bubble distributions and ii) agar-based Orgasol® particle phantoms with controlled scatterer properties. Backscattered radio-frequency data are acquired using full synthetic aperture scheme at varying insonification frequencies and the spatial growth of the incoherent backscattered intensity is used to estimate the diffusion constant (D), for each phantom. Bubble phantoms show a strong relationship between D and micro-CT-derived bubble content where, D decreases with the bubble count. Orgasol® phantoms show decreasing D trends with increasing particle diameter and concentration, and higher-frequency acquisitions produce lower D values, consistent with stronger scattering. Particle diameter has a larger impact on D than concentration under the tested conditions. Together, these results demonstrate a controlled phantom-based framework for validating lung QUS biomarkers.

papers.title: Improving Biophantoms Backscattering Parameters with Total Variation Regularization
papers.abstract: This study evaluates the Structure Factor Model adapted for two scatterer types (SFM2) to estimate scan-plane maps of nuclear and cellular radius and volume fraction in dense JC cell-pellet biophantoms. Unlike prior work that fitted BSCs averaged across ROIs, this approach estimates parameters spatially using nonlinear least-squares optimization with isotropic total variation regularization. Eleven scan planes from 10 JC cell pellets were analyzed using BSCs measured from 25-55 MHz with a 40 MHz transducer. Four TV-based configurations were compared, including cases with radius and/or volume-fraction separation constraints. Relative to unregularized estimates, TV regularization reduced spatial fluctuations in the parameter maps. The resulting distributions were less sparse and more concentrated than the unregularized estimates. Adding radius and/or volume-fraction separation constraints shifted some estimates closer to histology-derived reference values, although variability increased in some cases. These results describe the effect of total variation regularization and simple physical constraints on SFM2-derived microstructure maps from cell-pellet BSC data.

sessions.title: MCA: Engineering and characterization of advanced ultrasound contrast agents

papers.title: Evaluating Acoustic Stability of Monodisperse Microbubbles via Acoustic Attenuation Spectrum Under High/Low-Pressure Excitations
papers.abstract: Lipid shedding under acoustic exposure and its effect on shell properties remain unexplored. This work aims to use acoustic attenuation spectrum of monodisperse microbubbles (MDMBs) under low- and high-pressure excitations to evaluate how acoustic parameters affect shell elasticity and compare the acoustic stability of MDMBs across PEG chain lengths. Under high PNP, fMR (frequency of maximum attenuation) remained constant, suggesting unchanged bubble size since high PNP oscillations approximate shell-free bubbles. However, under low PNP, fMR shifted for both types, with a notably smaller shift for PEG2k MDMBs than for PEG5k, indicating that shell viscoelasticity changed during repeated high PNP excitations. Using MDMBs with DPPE-PEG5k as an example, relative elasticity increased progressively with higher PNP and more pulse numbers, suggesting that acoustic parameters induce the shedding of PEG chains from the shell, leading to an increase in shell elasticity. Under repeated high PNP excitations, MDMBs with DPPE-PEG5k exhibited significantly greater elasticity changes than MDMBs with DPPE-PEG2k, showing that the acoustic stability of MDMBs depends heavily on the PEG chain length.

papers.title: High-Pressure Extrusion-Based Scalable Production of Sub-Micron/Nano Ultrasound Contrast Agents for in Vivo Imaging Applications
papers.abstract: This work presents a scalable high-pressure extrusion platform for producing sub-micron/nano ultrasound contrast agents. Unlike conventional syringe-based mini-extrusion, the proposed method enables higher throughput bubble formation under dual-gas pressurization. Systematic variation of lipid concentration showed clear effects on bubble yield, size, and acoustic response, while maintaining stable surface charge. The optimized formulation demonstrated strong nonlinear ultrasound contrast and signal persistence in vitro, along with sustained in vivo liver contrast enhancement persisting for up to 70 minutes. Overall, the study demonstrates a scalable approach for producing stable sub-micron/nano contrast agents suitable for effective ultrasound imaging.

papers.title: Ultrasound-Induced Dynamics of Phase-Change Contrast Agents in Synthetic Cystic Fibrosis Mucus: Toward Pulmonary Drug Delivery and Mucus Rheology Assessment
papers.abstract: The viscoelastic properties of cystic fibrosis airway mucus can limit treatment effectiveness, yet standard rheology methods often struggle to assess these variations non-invasively. This study examines the potential of ultrasound phase-change contrast agents (PCCAs) to serve as sensors for their local mechanical environment. Using a 1.1 MHz focused transducer and optical monitoring, lipid-shelled PCCAs were tested in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) and 1–3% polyethylene oxide (PEO) solutions that mimic mucus. The results indicate that the vaporization threshold (P50) increases with medium concentration, with 3% PEO requiring significantly higher pressure than PBS (~905 vs ~493 kPa). Additionally, post-vaporization stable cavitation doses (SCD) showed different acoustic patterns depending on the concentration, with higher PEO levels exhibiting more stable signals across a range of pressures. These observations suggest that both the activation of PCCAs and their subsequent acoustic emissions are influenced by the surrounding medium. This supports the possibility of using PCCAs as acoustic reporters to help characterize mucus properties and guide ultrasound-assisted therapies.

papers.title: Effect of Pulsing Parameters and Acoustic Pressure on Cavitation Activity of Nanobubbles Characterized by Power Spectral Density Analysis
papers.abstract: Focused ultrasound (FUS) combined with nanobubbles (NBs) enables cavitation-based therapies including sonoporation and tumor disruption. Unlike microbubbles, NBs can extravasate into tumor interstitium, enabling extracellular and intracellular cavitation. Effective application requires precise control over stable and inertial cavitation dose (SCD, ICD). While duty cycle (DC) is commonly used to describe pulsing protocols, the independent contributions of burst length (BL) and burst period (BP) remain poorly understood. This study systematically characterizes SCD and ICD of lipid-shelled NBs across nine pulsing conditions (BL=0.1–30ms, BP=50–500ms) at 1.0 and 2.0 MPa using power spectral density analysis. BL governs an efficiency-dose tradeoff: shorter BL yields higher normalized ICD but lower cumulative dose. Conditions sharing identical DC produced markedly different SCD and ICD, demonstrating DC alone cannot predict cavitation behavior. These findings provide a framework for rational pulsing parameter selection in NB-mediated FUS.

papers.title: Scaled Fabrication of Octafluoropropane phase-Change Contrast Agents via Direct Emulsification
papers.abstract: This study demonstrates a direct emulsification technique to produce octafluoropropane phase change contrast agents (PCCA) at a 16-fold greater scale than traditional microbubble condensation methods while maintaining comparable acoustic and physical properties. PCCA were fabricated via direct emulsification at scale and characterized via nanoparticle tracking analysis and the probability of cavitation. These results demonstrate the feasibility of direct emulsification for scaled manufacture of PCCA, towards commercialization for future applications in ultrasound imaging and therapy.

papers.title: Activation and Imaging of High-Boiling-Point Nanodroplets with a Linear Array Transducer
papers.abstract: Perfluorohexane (PFH) nanodroplets are high-boiling-point phase-change contrast agents that offer stable, repeatable vaporization but are difficult to activate with diagnostic ultrasound transducers. We developed a custom interleaved imaging and activation sequence on a 15-MHz linear array and systematically evaluated PFH nanodroplet vaporization as a function of voltage, frequency, pulse length, and duty cycle. We identified reliable activation conditions at 17.9 MHz and demonstrated a clear voltage-cycle tradeoff governing the threshold. These results establish a practical excitation window for controlled PFH nanodroplet vaporization on a clinically relevant platform, supporting future applications in targeted contrast-enhanced imaging.

papers.title: Effects of Frequency, Pressure, and Additional Cavitation Nuclei on the Activation Threshold of Phase Change Contrast Agents
papers.abstract: This study aims to better understand the effects of pressure, frequency, and presence of local cavitation nuclei on acoustic droplet vaporization (ADV) of low-boiling point phase change contrast agents (PCCAs). Transducers with frequencies of 0.5, 1, 5, and 7.5 MHz were tested with a range of peak negative pressures. B-mode images were obtained and analyzed using binary analysis to determine the presence of microbubbles (defined as the fractional bright region). Results indicate that higher frequencies required increased pressures to induce acoustic droplet vaporization. Moreover, combining microbubbles to PCCAs at a 1:20 ratio enabled the PCCAs to undergo ADV at lower pressures.

papers.title: Mechanical Filtration Alters Nanobubble Lipid Shell Integrity and Compromises Acoustic Stability
papers.abstract: Lipid-coated nanobubbles (NBs) are ultrasound contrast agents whose acoustic behavior depends on shell composition and size. Syringe filtration is commonly used for size isolation, but its effect on shell integrity remains unexamined. This study determines whether the loss of acoustic activity in filtered NBs stems from size reduction alone or lipid shell disruption, by comparing syringe-filtered NBs to centrifuge-isolated NBs (icNBs) of equivalent size. NBs were passed through 0.45µm filters (PVDF, glass fiber/PVDF, SFCA) and characterized by resonant mass measurement, dynamic light scattering, and optical density, with echogenicity assessed at 21MHz. All filtered samples showed reduced size and optical density, membrane debris indicated significant lipid loss, and no measurable ultrasound signal was produced. icNBs, isolated at 450g without membrane contact, maintained shell integrity and produced detectable signal at elevated concentrations. These results demonstrate that shell disruption, not size reduction, accounts for the loss of acoustic activity in filtered NBs, with significant implications for NB preparation in contrast-enhanced ultrasound applications.

sessions.title: MBE: Brain, Neurons, Microbubbles, Cells II

papers.title: Factors Influencing Delayed Intercellular Calcium Waves Induced by Directly FUS-Activated Cells
papers.abstract: Delayed intracellular calcium transients triggered by directly FUS-activated cells complicates ultrasound neuromodulation and impedes efficiency. This study aims to characterize these delayed calcium transients and to explore the influencing factors. Real-time responses of HEK293T to a single continuous wave (1.0 MHz, 5–300 ms, 0.3–0.45 MPa) was monitored. PI and Fluo-4 indicated membrane permeability and time-lapse Ca²⁺ changes (ΔF/F₀). Cells were classified as directly activated (ΔF/F₀≥0.2, ΔF(PI) < 0.5 within 2 s post-FUS) or delayed (same criteria thereafter). Within 2-s post FUS, Fluo-4 increased rapidly in directly FUS-activated cells. From 2 to 30 s, a calcium wave spread concentrically from these cells to neighbors. Propagation velocity was constant within 200 μm from the epicenter and declined slightly beyond. Velocity increased with peak amplitude and proportion of directly FUS-activated cells, but decreased with longer time to peak in those cells. Gad, 2 APB, and BAPTA significantly reduced the propagation velocity, indicating that mechanosensitive ion channels and intracellular calcium release are critical in delayed activated cell response.

papers.title: 10 MHz Focused Ultrasound Restores Spike Output During Strong Depolarising States While Suppressing Near-Threshold Firing
papers.abstract: Focused ultrasound (FUS) is a non-invasive neuromodulation modality with potential for spatially precise, miniaturised neural interfaces, but intracellular effects at higher frequencies remain poorly defined. We investigated how 10 MHz FUS modulates excitability and spike generation in CA1 pyramidal neurons using whole-cell current-clamp recordings in acute mouse hippocampal slices. Responses were assessed during depolarising current injection with within-cell comparisons between control and FUS conditions. FUS produced state-dependent effects: near firing threshold, it hyperpolarised the membrane and suppressed spiking, whereas during stronger suprathreshold input (>200 pA above threshold), it enhanced firing. In neurons approaching depolarisation block, FUS restored spike output. Passive membrane resistance was unchanged (p=0.199), while spike amplitude increased and action potentials narrowed, indicating modulation of active conductances. Peak focal ΔT was ~0.7 °C. These findings provide intracellular evidence that high-frequency FUS enables excitability-state-dependent neuromodulation and supports spatially selective neural modulation and implantable ultrasonic technologies.

papers.title: Toward Understanding the Molecular Mechanisms of Ultrasound-Induced Neuronal Activation
papers.abstract: The biophysical mechanisms underlying ultrasound-activated neurons remain unclear. This study aims to identify key mechanosensitive ion channels and downstream signaling axes through transcriptomic analysis. Neurons were stimulated with a single continuous wave (1.0 MHz, 5 ms, 0.37 MPa) and divided into three groups: controls (without FUS stimulation), and those collected 10 min and 2 h after stimulation. RNA-seq analysis with DESeq2 and GO/KEGG enrichment was performed. A total of 1802 and 2260 differentially expressed genes were identified at 10 min and 2 h post exposure, respectively. GO based screening revealed that Piezo1, ASIC1, and TRPC1 were upregulated at 2 h, and KEGG enrichment highlighted focal adhesion, actin cytoskeleton regulation, and axon guidance. Downstream analysis revealed engagement of a Piezo1 initiated mechanotransduction cascade and the calcineurin–NFAT signaling axis. These results indicate that a Piezo1–FAK/Src–ROCK2/Rac1 mechanical cascade and a TRPC–PPP3CA–NFATC2 calcium signaling axis jointly drive the transcriptional remodeling of cortical neurons in response to ultrasound.

papers.title: Ultrasonic Mechanotransduction for Tumor Physical Microenvironment Normalization
papers.abstract: Increased matrix stiffness in the tumor microenvironment contributes to tumor progression. Previously, using a multimodal shear wave elasticity measurement system, we have demonstrated that combining mechanosensor inhibitors with ultrasound treatment could normalize matrix stiffness. In this study, we applied a focused ultrasound system to uncover the underlying mechanism and bioeffects of ultrasound in this therapeutic strategy. We found that cellular contractility, DNA damage response, and cell migration were the key factors in regulating ultrasound-assisted matrix stiffness normalization.

papers.title: Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound Neuromodulation: a Histological Safety Assessment in the Rodent Brain
papers.abstract: Transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) is a non-invasive neuromodulation method that can target deep brain structures with millimeter precision. When paired with microbubbles (MB), it enables enhanced imaging and potential closed-loop neuromodulation, but the safety of this combination is not well defined due to possible mechanical bioeffects. We assessed histological safety of 1 MHz tFUS with MB in awake, head-fixed mice by varying pressure (180–300 kPa), duty cycle (DC; 25–75%), and sonication duration (SD; 4.5–54 s) while targeting the primary motor cortex (M1) with a focused transducer and concurrent functional ultrasound imaging. Brain tissue was analyzed using H&E for hemorrhage and Fluoro-Jade C (FJC) for neuronal degeneration. Results show a clear parameter-dependent effect. At MI = 0.3, consistent damage was observed across conditions. At MI = 0.26, damage occurred in ~50% of animals at 75% DC and 54 s SD, but not at lower parameters. No damage was seen at lower MI across all DCs and SDs. These findings indicate that safety depends on interacting acoustic parameters, defining preliminary safe operating ranges for MB-enhanced tFUS neuromodulation.

papers.title: Understanding Cavitation Effects at Preclinically and Clinically Relevant Frequencies
papers.abstract: Focused ultrasound (FUS) blood-brain barrier (BBB) opening (FUS-BBBO) describes the safe and transient relaxation of the BBB due to FUS mechanical stresses mediated by the administered microbubbles. Clinical translation for treatment of neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD) requires decreasing the center frequency in order to account for the skull attenuation. Both phantom and mouse studies were performed. A spherical, single-element transducer (H204-06, Sonic Concepts) was driven at 0.5 MHz or 1.5 MHz with the same otherwise parameters: MI = 0.4, PL = 10 ms, PRF = 2 Hz. Lipid-shelled polydisperse microbubbles were used and passive cavitation detection was assessed at Fc = 3.5 MHz (CS84-SU, Olympus) and Fc = 7.5 MHz (V320, Olympus). Passive cavitation reveals ultraharmonic and inertial cavitation significantly drove the cavitation dose differences between the two frequencies with 7x and 29x increase, respectively.

sessions.title: MTH: Advances in Transcranial Ultrasound: Modeling, Correction, and Therapeutic Guidance

papers.title: Simulation Pipeline for Successful neuronavigation-Guided FUS-BBBO in DIPG Patients
papers.abstract: FUS and microbubbles allow the blood-brain barrier opening non-invasively, transiently and safely, enabling targeted drug delivery into DIPG tumors. However, the tumor is located at the pons/brainstem, a deep region limiting the FUS transducer placement due to the oblique incidence at the occipital bone. Accurate transcranial simulations are critical for excellent prediction. Our simulation pipeline includes realistic clinical limitations to predict focal deviations. Simulation pipeline on k-Wave: 51 linear and angular positioning errors cases within [-10,0,10] mm and [-10,-5,0,5,10]°, 40 cases of coupling imperfections by varying the active coupling diameter within [105,95,85,75,65,55,45,35] mm. FUS-BBBO setup: 250-kHz FUS (0.2-MPa-PNP, PRF 2 Hz, PL 10 ms) for 2 min, 10 μL/kg Definity microbubbles IV, PAM with Vantage 256. Post-FUS gadolinium CE-T1-MRI for BBBO assessment. CE-T1-MRI showed BBBO along the simulated focus. The FUS beam undesirably crossed a burr hole due to a positioning error, with focal deviation predicted by simulation. This study demonstrates the reliability of the employed simulation pipeline for prediction of BBBO on DIPG patients.

papers.title: Linking Skull Transmission and Thalamic Ultrasound Stimulation to Cortical ECoG Responses
papers.abstract: Transcranial focused ultrasound has shown potential to noninvasively stimulate deep neural circuits. However, its effectiveness is limited by complex interactions among acoustic propagation, skull-induced attenuation, and neurovascular coupling. Therefore, US parameter selection critically influences the characteristics of the acoustic field at the cortical target. The thalamus plays a central role in regulating cortical activity through thalamocortical pathways with direct projections to the somatosensory cortex (S1). This study aims to investigate how stimulating thalamic regions, under varying US conditions, modulates S1 activities in a non-human primate (NHP).

papers.title: Design and Evaluation of Compact Guiding Cones for Flexible and Efficient Transcranial Focused Ultrasound Delivery
papers.abstract: Transcranial focused ultrasound using single-element transducers offers a simple and cost-effective approach for neuromodulation. With a fixed focus we can target only one location in the brain. Multi-channel/element approaches provide focus control. Water-filled cones are commonly used to ensure acoustic coupling between the transducer and skull. The shape and length of the cone can influence the acoustic field and change the target location in the brain. We evaluated the use of different cones with single element transducers to provide target area control with single element transducers. Hydrophone measurements were performed following transmission through an ex vivo non-human primate skull (NHP) to evaluate cone-induced changes in the acoustic field.

papers.title: Inverse Angular Spectrum Method for Estimating Hair-Induced Focal Attenuation via Dual-Transmit/Receive Transcranial Focused Ultrasound
papers.abstract: This study proposes an RF echo-based framework using the inverse angular spectrum method (inverse ASM) to estimate hair-induced focal attenuation in focused ultrasound. RF acoustic feedback signals were acquired from 32 channels of a 256-element circular transducer. A processing workflow including echo-window selection, channel weighting, multi-angle signal integration, and phase correction was implemented to stabilize the reconstructed complex field for inverse ASM estimation. Plastic-sphere experiments were performed under long-hair, short-hair, and no-hair conditions, and hydrophone measurements were used as the reference. Compared with direct reconstruction, the proposed processing reduced MAE from 286.04 to 159.83 and MAPE from 48.56% to 27.62%. The percentage of cases within the ±20% agreement band increased from 8.33% to 45.83%, and Pearson’s correlation coefficient improved from 0.490 to 0.790. These results suggest that RF-based inverse ASM estimation may provide an indirect indicator for hair-induced focal attenuation.

papers.title: Impact of Brain Heterogeneity on Transcranial Ultrasound Wavefields
papers.abstract: Transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) models typically assume homogeneous bulk modulus and density, despite evidence from magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) that brain tissue exhibits strong mechanical heterogeneity. While shear-modulus variability is well established, small spatial variations in compressional properties can significantly affect wave propagation, pressure, and strain fields. This work hypothesizes that structured heterogeneity in bulk modulus, aligned with known shear heterogeneity, can distort tFUS targeting. An in-silico model based on a mixed finite element method is developed, where heterogeneous bulk modulus fields are generated by statistically transforming MRE-derived maps, and anisotropy is incorporated using diffusion tensor imaging (DTI). A phase-conjugation approach enables accurate focusing through a hemispherical transducer array. Simulations reveal reproducible off-target hotspots, with strain magnitudes reaching up to 50% of the focal peak and shifted by about 0.4 cm. These findings indicate that neglecting compressional heterogeneity may lead to underestimation of off-target exposure and focal misalignment in tFUS.

papers.title: Ultrasound Tomography Guided Phase Correction for Transcranial Focused Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Transcranial focused ultrasound (TcFUS) delivers acoustic energy through the skull to selected brain targets for therapeutic applications. Skull acoustic mismatch and heterogeneity reduce focal pressure, broaden the focus, and shift energy from the target. CT/MRI-based aberration correction requires additional imaging and co-registration, increasing cost and radiation exposure. We propose a machine learning-augmented ring-array framework for skull sound speed (SS) estimation and phase-corrected TcFUS focusing. Reflection data identify the skull boundary to generate mask features, while transmission data estimate skull SS. Multi-static waveforms are converted to magnitude, phase, and group-delay features, which together with CT-derived SS maps train a U-Net for supervised 3D SS regression. Predicted SS maps drive a virtual-source simulation to compute inter-element delays for coherent focusing. Evaluated via k-Wave simulations on a public head CT dataset, the framework restored focal pressure and localization close to ground-truth CT-based correction, demonstrating effective TcFUS aberration correction without CT/MRI planning.

papers.title: Optimizing Transducer Array Element Size for Phase Aberration Correction in Transabdominal Histotripsy
papers.abstract: Phase aberration from heterogeneous abdominal tissues limits the efficacy and accuracy of transabdominal histotripsy. Correcting this requires subdividing the transducer aperture into a phased array. This study evaluated how element size affects aberration correction performance. Histotripsy focusing through the human abdomen was simulated using the k-Wave Toolbox for a transducer similar to the Histosonics Edison® system. The aperture was divided into arrays with element sizes ranging from 17.2λ to 1.1λ. Aberration correction with the smallest elements (1.1λ) increased focal pressure by an average of 51% (range: 21–123%). Larger elements of 4.6λ, 9.2λ, and 17.2λ achieved increases of 47%, 39%, and 1%, respectively. These findings suggest that element sizes around 5λ can provide near-optimal correction while reducing system cost and complexity compared to smaller elements. This simulation approach may also help optimize phased array design in other therapeutic ultrasound applications, reducing fabrication time and cost.

papers.title: Functional Ultrasound (fUS) Imaging of Displacement-guided Focused Ultrasound (DgFUS) Neuromodulation in Transgenically and Ototoxically Deafened Mouse Models
papers.abstract: Displacement-guided focused ultrasound (DgFUS) can modulate neuronal activity in the central (CNS) and peripheral nervous system (PNS) while simultaneously mapping FUS-induced displacement. Although DgFUS can elicit local hemodynamic changes, the evoked responses may be influenced by the indirect activation via an auditory pathway, which has not yet been studied at a length. In this study, we utilized a transgenic deafened mouse model and performed functional ultrasound (fUS) imaging to monitor hemodynamics simultaneously with either DgFUS or auditory stimulation. The objectives of this study were to image and quantify audible tone-evoked and DgFUS-evoked hemodynamic responses in the deafened and normal-hearing mice.

sessions.title: TPM: Piezoelectric and Other Materials, Devices and Applications

papers.title: High-Temperature Ultrasonic Transducers Based on PIN-PZ-PT 1-3 Piezocomposites
papers.abstract: The developed PIN-PZ-PT ceramics exhibit a TC of 346 °C and a d33 of 435 pC/N, demonstrating excellent thermal stability with only an 10.2% variation in d33 up to 300 °C. The fabricated 1-3 composite transducer operates effectively with a 2.5 MHz center frequency and a 30% -6 dB bandwidth. Crucially, the transducer maintains exceptional operational stability across the entire 25-300 °C range, showing <12% total variation in center frequency, bandwidth, and pulse-echo amplitude. These results indicate that the proposed material and composite design strategy effectively resolves the performance-stability trade-off, offering a viable pathway for high-temperature ultrasonic transducer.

papers.title: Dynamics of a Refractive Index Change Region Induced by 100-MHz-Range Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Microbubble ejection induced by ultrasound in water at frequencies in the 100-MHz-range was observed using the schlieren technique. When the transducer was faced downward, acoustic streaming was observed and the front of the acoustic streaming exhibited a lower grayscale in the schlieren image than the surrounding area, indicating a refractive index change. On the other hand, with an initial propagation speed of less than 21 mm/s, the low-grayscale region gradually slowed to a static state while continuing to form an arch-shaped region more than 15 mm away from the transducer surface. The propagation speed and refractive index change were confirmed to be correlated with the number of burst cycles and the applied voltage. this refractive index change area could be potentially utilized in light path manipulation device, ultrasound cleaning and ultrasound-assist chemical processing.

papers.title: Round Robin Evaluation of Length Extensional k33 and Width Extensional Mode k33 Modes in Generation I PMN-PT Single Crystals
papers.abstract: In September 2024, the five year process of updating the IEEE Standard 1859TM-2017 (IEEE Standard for Relaxor-Based Single Crystals for Transducer and Actuator Applications) began. In addition to updating existing data on length extensional <001>-poled PMN-PT, new properties are being added such as the width extensional mode coupling factor k33'. The PiezoStandard Committee embarked on a round robin evaluation of k33 and k33' using samples from multiple manufacturers for all three types of <001>-poled PMN-PT. Twelve institutions voluntarily participated, representing academia, industry and government. Sample fixtures robust enough to withstand the rigors of shipping worldwide that did not impact the measurement were developed. Instrument calibration procedures, analysis methods and recording processes were established to ensure uniformity of reporting. Statistical analyses were conducted to identify any biases based on a specific sample or a particular institution’s measurement and exclude outlying data. An analysis comparing the material properties from the k33 and k33' samples to the existing values in IEEE Standard 1859TM-2017 and suggested revisions will be presented.

papers.title: Design, Fabrication, and Acoustic Field Optimization of a Wearable Linear Array for Ultrasound Monitoring of Deep Vein Thrombosis
papers.abstract: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) remains underdiagnosed due to the intermittent nature of standard Duplex ultrasound, motivating continuous monitoring solutions. We present the optimized design and initial validation of a wearable ultrasound patch for automated DVT detection. A 32-element, 5 MHz linear array was first modeled using finite element simulations and fabricated with a 2×3 cm footprint suitable for placement over the popliteal vein. Initial results revealed pronounced sidelobes in both simulated pressure fields and experimental B-mode imaging. To address this, a second-generation design incorporated finer pitch, dual matching layers, an optimized kerf pattern, and an acoustic lens, increasing the element count to 64 while maintaining the same aperture. Simulations demonstrated improved beam coherence, enhanced main lobe intensity, and effective sidelobe suppression. These results highlight the importance of acoustic stack and aperture optimization in wearable ultrasound systems. Ongoing work focuses on fabrication of the optimized design and integration with automated clot detection algorithms for continuous bedside monitoring

papers.title: Solderable Brass Spacer Elements for Thickness Compensation of Piezoelectric Transducers in Hybrid Arrays
papers.abstract: This work addresses the challenge of height mismatches in hybrid arrays (HAs), which integrate piezoelectric and CMUT/PMUT transducers for advanced imaging modalities. Height mismatches, caused by differences in transducer technology or frequency, hinder close-pitch integration and reliable electrical contact. To resolve this, laser-micromachined brass spacer elements were developed to compensate for thickness differences while serving as ground electrodes. A HA with piezoelectric and CMUT elements was assembled using soldered brass spacers on a PCB, and its acoustic performance was evaluated. Results showed successful electrical contact without added capacitance or resistance. Spacer-integrated arrays exhibited a resonance frequency of 8 MHz with a bandwidth of 6.0 MHz, while non-spacer variants had broader bandwidths (13.5 MHz) but lower sensitivity (-5.9 dB). These findings demonstrate that brass spacers effectively enable reliable integration of hybrid arrays without degrading acoustic performance, paving the way for scalable, high-performance designs.

papers.title: Toward a Selection Framework for Couplants in Wearable Ultrasound: Preliminary Comparison of Dry and Hydrogel-Based Interfaces
papers.abstract: This study presents a preliminary screening framework for selecting couplants for wearable and flexible ultrasound systems. Because wearable ultrasound requires stable acoustic coupling during prolonged use and body motion, dry, hydrogel, and soft interface materials were compared against conventional ultrasound gel. Candidate couplants included Aqualene dry couplant, lab-fabricated AMPS and AMPS+PVP hydrogels, AG625 hydrogel, Liveo™ SSCT, Liveo™ MG 7-9800, and Liveo™ MG 7-9900. Using a 10-MHz probe, each material was evaluated by B-mode phantom and in vivo muscle imaging under matched settings. Conventional gel showed the highest CNR (2.107), while Liveo™ SSCT showed the strongest performance among wearable candidates (1.992), followed by AMPS+PVP (1.864), Gel-Dry-Gel (1.689), AG625 (1.660), and AMPS (1.238). Dry and MG 7 materials showed limited visibility or reverberation. These results highlight the need to balance image quality with retention, conformability, and skin stability.

papers.title: Lead-Free Flexible KNbO₃ Actuator on Titanium Foil with Stable Long-Term Electromechanical Performance
papers.abstract: This work presents a lead-free flexible KNbO3 piezoelectric actuator integrated on a 40 μm-thick titanium foil for flexible transducer applications. A KN / SrTiO3 / TiO2 / Ti multilayer structure was fabricated using a sequential hydrothermal process. The TiO2 layer and SrTiO3 intermediate layer were introduced to promote stable KN film growth on the metallic foil. The crystalline phase, cross-sectional structure, and elemental distribution were confirmed by X-ray diffraction, focused ion beam imaging, and energy-dispersive spectroscopy. The KN film showed a strong piezoelectric response with a measured d33 of approximately 119 pm/V. A cantilever-type actuator was further fabricated to evaluate voltage-driven displacement and long-term electromechanical stability. Under 10 V excitation at the fundamental resonant frequency of 442 Hz, the actuator exhibited a clear displacement response with a stable peak-to-peak displacement of approximately 30 μm over 60 minutes. These results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating lead-free KN films on flexible titanium foils for durable and environmentally friendly piezoelectric transducer applications.

papers.title: Quantifying and Optimizing Acoustic Energy Delivery in Multilayer Interfaces for Ultrasonic Thin-Film Processing
papers.abstract: Structural defects in thin-film energy materials—including dislocations, stacking faults, and grain boundaries—act as centers for non-radiative recombination and limit device efficiency. beyond traditional passivation strategies, post-treatment approaches can further improve crystallinity and reduce defect density. High-power ultrasound has been shown to induce acoustic softening in metals, promoting dislocation mobility and annihilation [1]. Given the ductile nature of metals, we hypothesize that ultrasonic treatment can facilitate defect recovery in thin films with Pugh’s ratio < 0.57. This approach requires efficient acoustic energy transfer, governed by acoustic impedance matching at interfaces and by attenuation in the coupling layer. Therefore, the objective is to identify coupling configurations that minimize interfacial losses and maximize energy delivery in the transducer-couplant-glass substrate system.

sessions.title: TTT: Therapeutic Transducers and Applications

papers.title: Evaluation of Common Ultrasound Phantom Gels for Use in Solid Coupled Histotripsy
papers.abstract: Histotripsy is an emerging therapeutic ultrasound ablation method. This study evaluates common ultrasound phantoms for use as solid coupling representing a novel approach to histotripsy therapy. To determine this, characterization experiments were conducted on seven gels to determine speed of sound, acoustic impedance and acoustic attenuation. Preliminary results show that commercially available gels and oil-based gels are promising candidates and require further characterization.

papers.title: Novel Solid-Phase Coupling Approach for Focused Histotripsy Transducers
papers.abstract: Histotripsy is a non-invasive ultrasound-based therapy for targeted tissue ablation via microbubble cavitation. Current procedures couple the acoustic field of the histotripsy transducer to the skin surface via a bath of degassed water. The bath set-up presents challenges as it is bulky, requires extensive provision of degassed water, and is subject to leakage during procedures. Further, mismatches between the acoustic impedances of water and tissue lead to shifts in the focal region that complicate initial targeting. This paper presents a novel design of a coupling system using a simulation-grade gel insert as the primary medium. This approach allows for a more maneuverable histotripsy alternative to accommodate varying patient anatomies and facilitate implementation in a clinical setting. A wire targeting test assessed the modular set-up relative to the conventional water bath. Some clutter was noted in the nearfield that coincided with interfacial locations for the insert. However, these artifacts did not obscure assessment of the focal zone. Both trials visualized the wire successfully with comparable intensities at 53 mm, the focal length for the histotripsy transducer.

papers.title: The Effect of Insulin Dose on in Vivo Effects in Sequential Ultrasound Irradiation
papers.abstract: Sonophoresis is a minimally invasive technique for the transdermal delivery of biomolecular drugs. Conventional sonophoresis relies on randomly generated cavitation by kHz-band ultrasound, resulting in limited efficiency. The sequential irradiation method (SIM), which sequentially applies kHz- and MHz-band ultrasound, has been proposed to improve drug delivery efficiency; however, the relationship between drug dose and in vivo efficacy remains unclear. This study evaluated the efficacy of SIM by administering insulin at different doses in mice. Insulin was retained on the mouse abdomen and delivered using sequential ultrasound irradiation, and blood glucose levels were measured as an indicator of pharmacological effect. The results showed that SIM reduced blood glucose levels. The 100-fold dose produced greater in vivo efficacy than conventional injection. These results suggested that increasing the drug dose in the SIM performed pharmacological effects equivalent to injection. Therefore, SIM represents a promising needle-free alternative for the administration of biomolecular drugs.

papers.title: Rotational Dual-Frequency Therapeutic Transducer for Imaging-Guided Intravascular Sonothrombolysis
papers.abstract: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) can progress to life-threatening pulmonary embolism (PE), which is associated with a sudden mortality rate of over 20%. Current clinical approaches, including pharmacological thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy, are constrained by hemorrhagic complications and limited performance in treating retracted clots. Catheter-based ultrasound thrombolysis has emerged as a promising option by locally delivering acoustic energy to the thrombus; however, most existing devices still require further improvement in clot lysis efficiency and fully integrated therapeutic and imaging functions. Here, we introduce a miniaturized intravascular ultrasound system integrating 750 kHz and 900 kHz dual-frequency therapeutic transducers, which can decrease the cavitation threshold, guided by a 50 MHz imaging transducer. Combined with a wedge-matching layer and rotational design, the system enables dual-frequency excitation, efficient treatment, and high-resolution 360° B-mode imaging for image-guided intravenous sonothrombolysis.

papers.title: Topological-Charge-Dependent Cavitation and Thrombolysis Using Miniaturized Vortex Ultrasound Arrays
papers.abstract: Vortex ultrasound enables acoustic-field control through helical phase and topological charge (TC), but TC-dependent microbubble cavitation remains unclear. This study developed a miniaturized 3 × 3 PZT-5A vortex ultrasound array with eight active elements driven by programmed phase delays to generate TC1, TC2, and TC3 modes. Simulations, electrical/acoustic characterization, and pressure–phase mapping confirmed controllable vortex-field formation. Under matched peak pressure, microbubble cavitation was measured by passive cavitation detection and quantified as stable and inertial cavitation doses from harmonic/ultraharmonic and broadband emissions. TC1 showed the lowest cavitation threshold, whereas higher TCs enhanced post-threshold cavitation. TC2 produced the strongest stable cavitation at high pressure, while TC3 generated the strongest inertial cavitation and the greatest microbubble-assisted clot mass loss. These results show that TC control can regulate cavitation and improve vortex-ultrasound-mediated thrombolysis.

papers.title: Influence of Acoustic Frequency on ND Vaporization and Cavitation
papers.abstract: This study investigates how single- and dual-frequency ultrasound excitation affects ND vaporization, stable cavitation, and inertial cavitation thresholds. A miniaturized forward-looking PMN-PT transducer was developed with a 500 kHz center frequency, 2 × 2 mm aperture, and alumina–epoxy matching layer. NDs with a perfluorocarbon core and lipid shell were exposed to 500 kHz, 5 MHz, and 10 MHz ultrasound bursts. Acoustic emissions were recorded by hydrophone and analyzed spectrally, with stable cavitation dose calculated from harmonic/ultraharmonic bands and inertial cavitation dose from broadband emissions. At 500 kHz and 5 MHz, vaporization and stable cavitation occurred near similar thresholds of ~0.9–0.95 MPa. At 10 MHz, vaporization, stable cavitation, and inertial cavitation appeared at distinct thresholds of ~1.7, ~3.3, and ~3.9 MPa, respectively. These results show that acoustic frequency governs ND activation dynamics and can tune vaporization and cavitation behavior for therapeutic ultrasound applications.

sessions.title: ADS: Device Simulation and Synethesis

papers.title: Separated Hierarchical Cascade Technique with Accelerated Schur-Complement Construction for Lossless SAW Simulation
papers.abstract: The hierarchical cascade technique (HCT) is widely used for finite-element simulation of periodic SAW devices. In conventional HCT, the physical domain and PML are assembled into a single unit cell, forcing complex-arithmetic Schur-complement construction even when the physical domain is lossless. This work proposes a separated HCT (SHCT) that vertically decomposes each unit cell into upper physical-domain and lower PML subblocks. The decomposition reduces the Schur-complement cost through smaller matrices, and for lossless devices further enables real-arithmetic construction with a theoretical cost ratio approaching 4:1. On a 2D TCSAW resonator with 455 electrode pairs, SHCT reduces single-frequency runtime from 22 s to 14 s (36 %) and 401-point sweep time from 12 372 s to 5 252 s (58 %). The lateral PML Schur-complement cost is reduced by 33 % through size reduction, and the physical-domain cost by 61 % through real-arithmetic treatment. The admittance responses obtained by SHCT and conventional HCT are identical.

papers.title: Direct Extraction of k15² in Piezoelectric Films Using LFE-Type HBAR
papers.abstract: Modern wireless communication systems require wideband acoustic filters and piezoelectric materials with high electromechanical coupling. Recently, laterally excited bulk acoustic resonators (XBARs) have attracted attention as a new BAW technology based on lateral-field-excited (LFE) coupling. Conventional HBARs, consisting of a piezoelectric film sandwiched between electrodes on a substrate, allow convenient evaluation of TFE coupling coefficients such as k33², but cannot directly determine the shear-mode coupling k15² relevant to XBARs. This work proposes direct extraction of k15² using an LFE-type HBAR, where a piezoelectric thin film is bonded to a substrate and electrodes are formed only on the top surface. When the electrode spacing is much larger than the film thickness, the device can be approximated as a pure thickness-shear resonator. The conversion loss is interpreted using a semi-analytical model with geometry-dependent electric-field amplitudes. The model was validated by 2D FEM analysis and experiments on multiple LiNbO3-on-Si substrates. The extracted k15² agreed well with reported bulk values, demonstrating a practical characterization method for XBAR materials.

papers.title: Synthesis of Bridge-T Filters with Multiple Network Realizations
papers.abstract: AW ladder filters typically require a kt2 of twice the FBW. In wideband designs, such high kt2 values degrade the quality factor. BridgeT (BT) topologies relieve this constraint by introducing parallel signal paths, enabling equivalent filtering responses with reduced kt2 requirements. Rather than replacing ladder networks, BT filters provide a complementary solution that expands the design space for broadband applications. However, their synthesis remains challenging: classical element extraction techniques often fail because additional circuit elements are inherently required, without providing guidance on their number or placement. As a result, designers frequently resort to trial and error methods. Moreover, a single filtering function can admit multiple physically distinct BT realizations. The attached figure shows how the same filtering function can be realized through multiple topologies simultaneously. This work presents a coupling matrix (CM) methodology to determine this information. As a proof of concept, a LPF is fabricated using the bottom-right circuit.

papers.title: An Improved Q-Circle Centering Method for Quality Factor Calculation of Acoustic Resonators
papers.abstract: This paper improves the currently widely used method for calculating quality factor (Bode-Q) of acoustic resonators based on S-parameters. The original method, proposed at IUS 2008, requires the Q-circle to be centered on the Smith Chart because the calculation necessitates d|S11|/dω to be approximately zero. To center the Q-circle, the conventional method relies on empirical trial and error to determine the reference impedance. This paper adopts the geometric mean of the series and parallel resonant impedances as the port reference impedance. It can be theoretically proven that the proposed method achieves perfect centering of the Q-circle on the Smith chart. Consequently, the improved method is theoretically rigorous, and the calculation procedure for Bode-Q is further standardized.

papers.title: Theoretical and Experimental Analysis of SAW-on-Poi Sensitivity to Structural Parameter Dispersion
papers.abstract: POI have unlock SAW fiter performances. The dispersion of all the structure parameters must be accounted when design a SAW on POI. The influence of all the constitutive parameters on typical resonators figures of merit is studied.

papers.title: Generalized Transformation Matrix for Direct Bandpass Numerical Synthesis of Acoustic Wave Filter Topologies
papers.abstract: Numerical coupling-matrix reconfiguration techniques have emerged as an effective alternative to classical analytical synthesis for exploring unconventional filter topologies. These methods rely on congruent transformations between canonical and target coupling matrices via a transformation matrix Q, whose diagonal structure preserves source and load terminations. However, this formulation becomes restrictive in the direct bandpass domain in the presence of frequency-variant source–load couplings (FVCs). This work introduces a generalized transformation matrix Qg that enables preservation of the termination matrix under FVC conditions. The formulation incorporates a termination matrix, explicitly included in the numerical optimization through an extended cost function. The approach is validated through the synthesis of unconventional acoustic-wave filter topologies, with resulting coupling matrices mapped to nodal and hybrid BVD-based implementations. Results demonstrate an expanded design space for direct bandpass numerical synthesis.

papers.title: Spurious Signal Control for SAW Devices on Poi Substrates
papers.abstract: various POI layer combinations favors spurious contributions degrading the spectral purity of the final device. Even if the Si-base orientation is selected to limit the excitation of guided waves above the fundamental shear mode, the acoustoelectric energy radiated by the surface at given frequencies can be partially trapped in the POI layers and confined enough to sign on the IDT response. This work is devoted to explain the related physical mechanisms and to propose a POI stack optimization process to suppress the spurious contributions, preserving the figures of merit of the fundamental shear mode used for the filtering function.

sessions.title: PAT: Acoustic Tweezers & Particle Manipulation II

papers.title: A Spatial Displacement Correlation Function for Identifying Strong Resonances in Coupled Vibrations of Acoustic Wave Resonators
papers.abstract: Spurious modes are a persistent problem in acoustic wave resonator design, degrading performance and complicating tuning. Existing identification methods rely on subjective mode shape inspection or computationally expensive energy calculations. We introduce a spatial displacement correlation function — a single scalar computed from the vibration field — that directly pinpoints strong resonances as sharp peaks. The method requires no subjective judgment or heavy computation. Applied to a quartz crystal plate using Mindlin's plate theory, the correlation function clearly identifies the optimal design points where thickness-shear resonance dominates and flexural coupling is minimized. The computed correlation peaks align exactly with known frequency spectra, while flexural modes yield distinctly smaller amplitudes. This approach transforms resonance identification from a qualitative art into a quantitative, automatable step. It enables rapid parametric optimization of resonator geometry, material selection, and layer design, and extends naturally to MEMS, FBAR, SAW, and other emerging acoustic wave devices.

papers.title: Elastic Constant Measurement and Crystal Orientation Estimation of Fe-Based and Cu-Based Superelastic Alloys Using Resonant Acoustic Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Large-scale infrastructure requires high seismic resilience provided by superelastic alloys (SEAs). As SEA performance depends on crystal orientation, 100% inspection is required. Conventional methods like EBSD are difficult on-site for large materials. This study proposes rapid evaluation using Resonant Acoustic Spectroscopy (RAS). We combine impact RAS with a pre-calculated frequency database. A hammer strike excites resonance modes, captured by a 40 kHz microphone and analyzed in under 10 seconds. For small specimens, a three-point support method ensures ideal free-vibration. Modes are identified via laser Doppler interferometry. Orientation is estimated by matching frequencies against a database calculated via the Rayleigh-Ritz method. Results for single-crystal Fe-Mn-Al-Ni showed high precision with a 0.7% RMS error. Increasing Mn content decreases C11, raising Zener anisotropy. For 17 Cu-based samples, RAS estimates matched EBSD results within a few percent error. This method simultaneously evaluates orientation and material integrity, offering a rapid, cost-effective alternative for 100% inspection of structural SEAs.

papers.title: Ultrasonic Phenakistoscope Based on Static Transmissive Metasurfaces
papers.abstract: Acoustic metasurfaces can manipulate acoustic wavefronts for tasks like focusing and holography, but most are static and limited to a single function. Inspired by the phenakistoscope, this work introduces an ultrasonic version that rapidly switches between different acoustic fields at 40 kHz. It uses a rotating disk containing multiple metasurfaces, each designed for a specific function using labyrinthine unit cells that control phase delays. A stepper motor and Arduino rotate the disk, while a transducer array emits timed pulses so only one metasurface is active at a time. By adjusting pulse timing and frequency, different acoustic outputs (such as focal points or holographic letters) are generated in sequence. Instead of slow microphone scans, water surface disturbances visualize the dynamic fields in real time. This system offers a low-cost, simple way to create fast, programmable ultrasonic “animations.”

papers.title: Deformable Soft Collimator for Dynamic Shaping of Acoustic Fields
papers.abstract: Acoustic metasurfaces have been proposed as an alternative to electronic phased arrays for dynamic acoustic field manipulation. However, their reliance on sophisticated microstructures (e.g., Helmholtz resonators and coiled spaces) typically results in a narrow operating bandwidth, acoustic impedance mismatch, high acoustic attenuation, or complex, costly fabrication. To circumvent these limitations, we propose a deformable soft collimator (DSCo) that achieves dynamic acoustic field manipulation via mechanical deformation of soft materials.

papers.title: High-Precision Acoustic Focusing via Holographic Interdigital Transducers for Manipulating Microparticles and Droplets
papers.abstract: Surface acoustic waves are widely used in communications, sensing, and microfluidics.However, their anisotropic behavior causes energy flow to differ from the wave direction, making precise velocity characterization essential. This study combines experiments and finite element simulations on 128°Y-cut lithium niobate to map phase velocity using slowness curves, enabling accurate visualization of wave propagation.The results indicate that even minor changes in electrode geometry significantly affect acoustic energy focusing. By leveraging the anisotropic velocity profile, optimized holographic interdigital transducers are designed to precisely control energy flow. Experiments with micro-particles (2 μm and 5 μm) and droplet deformation confirm improved acoustic radiation force manipulation.This approach achieves a narrower focal region (78 μm FWHM) compared to conventional circular IDTs, enhancing energy confinement. Overall, the work enables more precise acoustic control, benefiting microfluidic applications such as particle separation and droplet manipulation in biomedical.

sessions.title: NAS: Acoustic Sensors II

papers.title: Experimental Validation of a Volumetric Vascular Access Guidance System Using Hydrophone-Synthesized Sensor Emulation
papers.abstract: We experimentally validate a multi-sensor photoacoustic tracking system for which a prior simulation study demonstrated sub-millimeter IV tool-tip localization. To avoid fabricating each candidate sensor geometry, we emulate a 2x2 mm square sensor by raster-scanning a 0.4 mm needle hydrophone over a 5x5 grid and summing the waveforms, yielding the aggregate response of the target aperture. Using a bare-fiber photoacoustic source in a water tank and a four-sensor layout surrounding a 4x2 cm US probe footprint, we characterize tracking accuracy across 20 source positions in the elevational YZ plane, the plane most relevant to IV needle insertion. Sub-millimeter 3D error is achieved at 18 of 20 positions (mean 0.112 ± 0.083 mm) across the 2-5 cm depth range relevant to central venous access. Two shallow lateral points fail at elevated errors (3.2 and 20.1 mm), traced to TOF-detection breakdown at ~70° incidence, well outside the sensor's simulated 20° FOV half-angle. These results validate the simulated design in its intended operating range and quantify a concrete FOV limit guiding future sensor geometry refinement.

papers.title: Low-Profile Hydrophone Based on Capacitive Micromachined Ultrasonic Transducer (CMUT) for Extreme high-Power Acoustic Sensing
papers.abstract: Conventional hydrophones based on lead zirconate titanate (PZT) ceramics and polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) films suffer from Curie-temperature-limited depolarization and thermal instability, rendering commercial devices unreliable within minutes under high-power exposure. This study presents a low-profile six-channel capacitive micromachined ultrasonic transducer (CMUT) hydrophone engineered for extreme high-power environments, wherein electrostatic transduction provides intrinsic insensitivity to thermal degradation. A 15 MHz CMUT array was fabricated via silicon wafer bonding with thermal robustness validated by laser Doppler vibrometer confirming less than 2% degradation at 180 °C. Hybrid multilayer protection comprising conformal Parylene-C, polymer encapsulation, and a stainless-steel chassis ensures durability under combined thermal and fluidic loading. Operated in collapse mode, the device detected acoustic signals at 400 kHz—well below the 15 MHz resonance frequency—without external preamplifier. Both waveform morphology and time-of-flight stability were preserved following one hour at 100 W, conditions under which commercial hydrophones universally fail.

papers.title: Surface Plasmon Resonance Sensor for Wireless Detection of Ultrasonic Waves
papers.abstract: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensors, which detect refractive index changes at the sensor surface, are promising candidates for future ultrasound receivers due to their non-resonant characteristics and simple wireless structure, enabling highly reproducible fabrication. Using a small glass prism coated with a bilayer metal film, we developed an SPR sensor that exhibits stable performance for over one year. In this study, the feasibility of the SPR sensor as a standard ultrasound receiver in the MHz range was evaluated by examining its linearity and comparing measured ultrasonic waveforms with those obtained from a calibrated needle-type ultrasonic sensor. Based on the pressure dependence of the refractive index of water, we theoretically estimated the effect of sound pressure on changes in light reflectance. These reflectance changes indicated that nonlinearity in ultrasonic measurements is negligible. Furthermore, the ultrasonic waveforms and frequency characteristics measured using the SPR sensor and the needle-type sensor showed good agreement.

papers.title: SAWR Sensor Configuration to Measure Static Strain, Dynamic Strain & Temperature
papers.abstract: Static/dynamic strain and temperature are important sensing measurands for industrial high-temperature/harsh-environment (HT/HE) applications including metallurgy, power generation, aerospace, and automotive. Surface acoustic wave resonator (SAWR) sensors can meet the demands of HT/HEs. In this work, a three langasite SAWR sensor configuration (SA, SB, and SC) that can simultaneously measure static/dynamic strain and temperature in HT/HEs was designed, implemented and tested on a Kovar beam. SA (parallel to the beam length) and SB were rigidly mounted orthogonal to each other using a glass solder. The setup was heat-cycled from room temperature to 300°C and tested with varying levels of static/dynamic strain. SA and SB differentially responded to static strain ranging from 2.1 to 29.6 με, SA measured dynamic strain from 5.5 to 16.2 με at 500 Hz, and SC measured temperature only. The data indicates that the setup responds to static strain, dynamic strain, and temperature, offering the capability of measuring simultaneous changes in all three measurands.

papers.title: Design of Nonperiodic Microphone Arrays for Ultrasonic Bathroom Monitoring via Ray-Tracing Simulation and Exploratory Search
papers.abstract: For a case involving 16 microphones, a trade-off exists: expanding the array aperture improves the resolution, whereas narrow, nonperiodic spacing suppresses the grating lobes. Additionally, physical constraints such as a sensor with a diameter of 5 mm and a central speaker aperture must be satisfied. Hence, a logarithmic spiral was adopted. Its dense center prevents artifacts, whereas its expanded periphery maintains a high resolution. Using this model, an exploratory grid search over three parameters and multi-stage screening were performed to derive an effective 16-element layout. The array was evaluated in a virtual bathroom. Its low computational cost enables a rapid evaluation that requires only 1 min per localization on a standard PC. Simulations show that the explored logarithmic spiral configuration reduced the peak sidelobe level from -4.93 to -8.68 dB compared with the conventional grid. the mean absolute error was approximately 0.18 m, which is sufficiently small to distinguish between standing, sitting, and falling postures. This result indicataes that the proposed array minimizes the effect of artifacts and achieves high localization accuracy.

papers.title: Synthesis of Sharp Cutoff Directivity for Airborne Ultrasonic Transducer
papers.abstract: Airborne ultrasonic sensors sometimes suffered from unwanted detection of object. This problem was usually caused by the slow cutoff characteristics or sidelobes in the directivity of transducers. In this study, the authors tried to synthesize a directivity pattern with rectangular shape by designing the vibration distribution on the radiation surface of transducer. We adopted an aluminum alloy disk of 30 mm in diameter and thin annular piezo-ceramic element bonded each other. After a number of simulations, we have reached a design to obtain the far-field directivity close to the rectangular pattern. A bending vibration with two nodal circles at 41.0 kHz was selected. The signal level in the main beam changed only 15%, and attenuated rapidly outside of the beam. Sidelobe was not observed.

papers.title: Toward Ku-Band Surface Acoustic Wave Delay Lines on AlScN-on-Diamond with Decoupled Phase and Group Velocities
papers.abstract: This work presents the first surface acoustic wave (SAW) acoustic delay line (ADL) on an AlScN-on-Diamond platform, scaling ADL operation into the Ku-band. High-frequency ADLs face a fundamental conflict: high phase velocity (vp) is needed to relax the IDT pitch, while low group velocity (vg) preserves delay density. On weakly dispersive platforms, the two scale together. AlScN-on-Diamond resolves this by combining diamond's exceptional acoustic velocity, low loss, and high thermal conductivity with the strong piezoelectricity of sputter-deposited AlScN, producing a strongly dispersive Sezawa branch in which vp exceeds 9 km/s while vg stays close to conventional-platform values. Sezawa-mode ADLs on a 200 nm Al0.7Sc0.3N on polycrystalline diamond stack achieve a 9.55 GHz center frequency with 1.05% FBW, propagation loss of 0.094 dB/λ, and QPL of 465. The extracted vp/vg of about 1.6 provides direct experimental evidence of engineered dispersion. Frequency scalability is further shown by a Sezawa ADL at 16.5 GHz with 0.7% FBW, establishing AlScN-on-Diamond as a uniquely scalable, low-loss platform for Ku-band and beyond acoustic delay elements.

sessions.title: NUA: Underwater Acoustics

papers.title: Development of a Wideband Cymbal Array Hydrophones and its Experimental Evaluation
papers.abstract: Cymbal transducers have been widely utilized in underwater transmitting arrays; however, their application in receiving arrays has received relatively limited attention. For effective use as a hydrophone, a cymbal transducer must exhibit both high sensitivity and a broad frequency bandwidth. However, the bandwidth of a single cymbal hydrophone is inherently limited. To address this challenge, this study proposes a new design rule for wideband cymbal array hydrophones that achieve both high receiving voltage sensitivity (RVS) and broad bandwidth in the low-frequency region. This study provides a systematic design framework for cymbal-based underwater acoustic sensors that effectively overcomes the trade-off between sensitivity and bandwidth. The proposed approach is expected to be applicable to the development of a wide range of underwater acoustic sensing systems.

papers.title: An Align-and-Stack Algorithm for Improving SNR in Airborne Sonar
papers.abstract: This work addresses the challenge of low signal-to-noise ratio in airborne sonar imaging, where multi-frame averaging is often degraded by motion-induced misalignment. It proposes an align-and-stack framework that estimates and compensates for inter-frame motion prior to averaging, enabling improved image reconstruction. Through simulation, the approach demonstrates enhanced image quality compared to naive averaging, highlighting the importance of motion correction for effective SNR improvement in airborne sonar systems.

papers.title: Spatially Adaptive Underwater Wireless Acoustic Power Transfer System
papers.abstract: This work develops a spatially adaptive underwater acoustic power transfer (UAPT) system that uses a phased array transducer (PAT) and receiver feedback to wirelessly power non-stationary underwater devices (nodes) such as sensors and unmanned vehicles. Unlike existing UAPT systems, which largely rely on static beamforming and assume a fixed, well-aligned receiver, the proposed system dynamically tracks a moving node by exploiting spatial variations in harvested power across multiple piezoelectric receivers on the node. These variations provide closed-loop feedback that continuously updates PAT element phases to maintain focal alignment as the node moves. PAT design is informed by analytical and multiphysics models of acoustic propagation and transducer behavior. Experimental characterization is expected to demonstrate continuous power delivery to a mobile node, validating spatially adaptive UAPT for non-stationary underwater applications.

sessions.title: Student Paper Finalists
MEL: Cardiovascular and Pulmonary Mechanics

papers.title: Carotid Artery Mechanical Properties Comparison Between Healthy Subjects and Patients with Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection (SCAD)
papers.abstract: In this study, we employ noninvasive arterial elastography techniques to estimate the mechanical properties of the in vivo human common carotid artery (CCA) wall in individuals with SCAD.

papers.title: Ultrasound-Derived Carotid Diameter Waveform Measurement: Comparison of Longitudinal and Transverse Cine Acquisitions
papers.abstract: Accurate estimation of arterial diameter dynamics from ultrasound is essential for vascular biomechanics, yet extraction from B-mode cine is sensitive to acquisition variability, and the impact of imaging orientation remains unclear. This study quantitatively compares longitudinal and transverse cine approaches for estimating carotid diameter change. Ultrasound cine data from 21 subjects (N = 42 arteries) were acquired in both views with repeated acquisitions. Representative cardiac cycles were extracted, and repeatability was evaluated using structural similarity index (SSIM) and normalized dynamic time warping (nDTW). Agreement with manually annotated reference diameter change (Δ) was assessed using correlation and Bland–Altman analysis. Longitudinal cine demonstrated significantly higher SSIM and lower nDTW (p < 0.01), indicating superior repeatability. It also showed strong agreement with reference (r ≈ 0.98) with minimal bias, whereas transverse cine exhibited lower correlation, greater variability, and systematic overestimation. These results indicate that longitudinal imaging provides more reliable and accurate estimation of arterial diameter dynamics.

papers.title: A Dynamic Diaphragm Phantom for Ultrasound-Based Respiratory Monitoring of Ventilated Patients
papers.abstract: Respiratory monitoring and ventilator management currently rely on indirect parameters such as airflow and pressure, which do not capture diaphragm mechanics. This work presents a low-cost, modular, and fully programmable dynamic diaphragm phantom designed for ultrasound-based respiratory monitoring and device evaluation. The phantom consists of multilayer structures representing anatomical tissues, fabricated using PVA-C for acoustic and mechanical property matching, with Orgasol additives for controlled scattering, and an ex vivo diaphragm layer. Physiologically relevant diaphragm motion and thickening are generated using orthogonally arranged linear actuators with real-time control and automated calibration. B-mode ultrasound imaging demonstrates clear visualization of rib structures and diaphragm boundaries, enabling extraction of clinically relevant metrics such as diaphragm thickness. The proposed platform provides a versatile and reproducible testbed for ultrasound system validation outside clinical settings.

papers.title: Monitoring of Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia Repair with Shear Wave Elasticity Imaging
papers.abstract: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) often requires patch repair for large defects, but commonly used materials like small intestinal submucosa (SIS) can degrade rapidly, increasing the risk of repair failure and reherniation. Hybrid patches combining SIS with biodegradable polymers such as poly(glycerol dodecanedioate) (PGD) may improve structural support. This study establishes ultrasound shear wave elasticity imaging (SWEI) as a non-invasive method to assess diaphragm mechanical integrity and detect early reherniation risk. In a rat model, CDH defects were repaired with SIS or SIS+PGD, with a control group included. SWEI was used at 1 and 4 months to measure diaphragm shear modulus, alongside excursion analysis. Results showed no significant changes in diaphragm excursion. However, SWEI revealed increased stiffness over time in the SIS-only group, while the SIS+PGD group remained stable. These findings, consistent with tensile testing, suggest that stiffness increases reflect tissue remodeling due to SIS degradation and may indicate higher reherniation risk. SWEI demonstrates promise as a tool for monitoring repair outcomes and enabling earlier clinical intervention.

papers.title: A Dual-Site Ultrafast Ultrasound Platform for Central and Peripheral Arterial Mechanics and Hemodynamics: a Feasibility Study in Vivo
papers.abstract: PWI+ (pulse wave imaging coupled with vector flow imaging), an ultrafast ultrasound technique for arterial characterization, was extended to a dual-site configuration to characterize both central (carotid) and peripheral (brachial) arterial stiffness, blood pressure, and blood flow, within a single ultrasound session. Using a custom mechanical arm and probe holder for peripheral scans, the brachial artery and carotid artery (freehand) were imaged within one minute with a plane wave coherent compounding sequence. In a healthy young male (27 y.o), carotid PWV was 4.50 m/s, PP = 32 mmHg, and PSV was 97 cm/s. For the brachial artery, PWV was 6.69 m/s, PP = 45 mmHg, and PSV was 51 cm/s. Pulse pressure amplification (PPA) was found to be 1.41, which was consistent with values expected for young adults. These preliminary results showcase the feasibility of dual-site PWI+ for comprehensive vascular characterization, enabling simultaneous local and systemic biomarkers.

papers.title: Guided-Wave Foundation Model for Arterial Dispersion Ultrasound Vibrometry (ADUV)
papers.abstract: Acoustic Dispersion Ultrasound Vibrometry (ADUV) infers arterial stiffness from guided-wave dispersion, but inversion relies on simplifying assumptions that limit in vivo accuracy. We pre-train a convolutional joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) on ~4,400 finite-element-simulated arterial waveguides spanning shear modulus G, inner radius IR, and wall thickness WT, then transfer the frozen encoder to in vivo recordings (10 cardiac stages × 256 × 144 spatiotemporal points). Linear probes on simulations estimate G, IR, and WT at R² = 0.99, 0.95, and 0.99. In vivo, they reconstruct the phase velocity F(1,1) dispersion mode partially (Pearson r = 0.23 [0.14–0.31] linear; 0.32 [0.21–0.49] non-linear MLP), indicating the embeddings encode dispersion-related physics. A stage-attention pool over the frozen encoder classifies cardiovascular health with AUROC = 0.79 [0.74–0.84], rising to 0.83 [0.80–0.87] with low-rank adaptation (LoRA, r = 8) fine-tuning, evaluated under subject-level bootstrap. To our knowledge, this is the first foundation model for guided-wave vascular elastography, and motivates scaling pre-training and in vivo cohorts.

sessions.title: MIM: Advanced beamforming & Reconstruction

papers.title: Optimal Signal-to-Noise Ratios and Frame Rates for Ultrasound Imaging Using Plane and Spherical Wave Emissions
papers.abstract: Optimizing imaging for the best possible signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and frame rate entails adjusting the transmit voltage, element number, and focus under the restrictions enforced by the FDA for ultrasound safety. In synthetic aperture imaging (SAI), a spherical wave is emitted by a number of elements, and in plane wave imaging (PWI) the full aperture is used. It is hypothesized that SAI sequences can give the highest frame rate for the same or better SNR than normal focused imaging and PWI. The SNR was simulated for a10 MHz linear array for both SAI and PWI with different transmit voltages. The SNR was measured using a Verasonics scanner. Probe heating was measured on a Test Phantom . There is close correspondence between measured and simulated responses. PWI attains a better SNR for 50 and 100 volts than SAI. SAI has a probe temperature below the 10 oC threshold even for fprf=15 kHz, whereas the PWI sequence breaks the limit and is only below for 5 kHz for 50 volts. So for high frame rates PWI cannot be maintained above 5 kHz or the voltage and, thus, SNR must be reduced. For SAI both frame rate and SNR is maintained at 15 kHz, making it the best choice for fast imaging.

papers.title: Sparse Delta Integration Method for Calculation of Spatiotemporal Pressure Fields of Arbitrary Ultrasound Transducer Geometries
papers.abstract: Accurate ultrasound pressure-field simulation is critical for probe design, imaging workflows and therapy development, but existing methods are too slow for large apertures or high sampling rates. We present the Sparse Delta Integration (SDI) method for fast far-field Spatial Impulse Response (SIR) computation.
