Transducer geometries are modelled by subdividing elements into small rectangular patches; SDI reformulates each trapezoidal SIR as eight weighted temporal delta events, independent of field point, reconstructed by integration. Implemented in PyField, a Python/Numba framework, SDI achieves 10x–130x speedups over FIELD II with negligible error (MSE ~ 0.001–0.01%). Gains are greatest for large apertures, high sampling rates, and distant field points. A hybrid Naïve-SDI strategy covers cases where the naïve method remains preferable. By decoupling cost from trapezoid width, SDI enables vectorization and future GPU acceleration, benefiting downstream applications of SIR computation such as RF simulation, beamforming, and imaging workflows.

papers.title: Feasibility Study of Helical Acquisition for Ultrasound Computed Tomography
papers.abstract: Ultrasound Computed Tomography (USCT) is a promising imaging technique. In X-ray CT, helical acquisition was introduced into clinical use in 1989, enabling faster acquisition, reduced radiation exposure and minimized breathing artifacts. A modern approach for this acquisition method is needed for USCT, evaluating Full-Waveform Inversion (FWI) reconstruction under this acquisition. Reconstruction of helical USCT requires accurate approximation of the projections within a given reconstruction plane. This approximation was performed using two interpolation methods: nearest-neighbor interpolation and linear interpolation. For evaluation, a PVA phantom was constructed. Compared with the reference, nearest interpolation yielded the following results for MAE and SSIM inside the ROI: 3.64 m/s and 0.9949; and for linear interpolation: 3.82 m/s and 0.9945. Compared with the standard slice-by-slice, the data and time savings acquisition for a helical pitch of 10.24 mm are 62.2%, enabling more efficient acquisition of large volumes.

papers.title: Reducing Spectral Oscillations for Robust Reference Frequency–Based Ultrasound Attenuation Coefficient Estimation in Harmonic Imaging
papers.abstract: Ultrasound attenuation coefficient estimation (ACE) is a promising tool for quantifying liver fat. The reference frequency method (RFM) enables system-independent ACE without a calibrated phantom but is limited by oscillations in frequency power ratio decay curves caused by interference in backscattered signals. To address this, we propose an approach that leverages incoherence across multiple frequencies and steering angles to suppress these oscillations and improve robustness. Our method reconstructs I/Q data from different steered angle and frequency transmissions and averages the resulting frequency power ratio decay curves to stabilize the attenuation estimate. Validation was performed using a calibrated tissue phantom and an in vivo study with three patients, with MRI proton density fat fraction (PDFF) serving as a reference for trend assessment. Results demonstrate that the proposed method improves the linearity of the decay curve (R² = 0.99 vs. 0.89 for conventional RFM) and yields more accurate attenuation estimates in the phantom. In vivo, the method also reduces measurement variability, indicating enhanced robustness.

papers.title: A Plane-Wave Travel-Time Framework for Robust Sound Speed Inversion and Refraction-Aware Beamforming in Layered Media
papers.abstract: Conventional ultrasound imaging assumes a uniform speed of sound (SoS), leading to phase aberrations and degraded image quality in heterogeneous media. Existing SoS inversion methods often neglect refraction and depend on accurate initial guesses, limiting robustness. This work proposes a computationally efficient, refraction-aware plane-wave travel-time framework for layered media. By decomposing travel time into horizontal and vertical components, a 2D map is constructed from separable 1D vectors, improving efficiency. The SoS profile is iteratively optimized using common middle angle (CMA)-based time-shift correction to enhance beamforming accuracy. Simulation results show high accuracy with a relative error of 0.98% and robustness to initial SoS (1500–1600 m/s). In vivo experiments on human liver data acquired with a Verasonics system demonstrate consistent SoS estimation (1596±1.34 m/s). Compared to conventional beamforming, the proposed method significantly improves spatial resolution in ultrasound microvessel imaging (UMI).

papers.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Stable Ultrasound Wave Propagation Modeling
papers.abstract: Accurate acoustic wave propagation modeling is essential for ultrasound imaging and applications including aberration correction and speed-of-sound (SoS) estimation. Conventional solvers such as k-Wave provide high-fidelity results but require grid-based discretization and high computational cost, limiting their use in learning-based frameworks. This study proposes a physics-informed neural network (PINN) that models acoustic pressure as a continuous function for mesh-free evaluation. To improve stability for high-frequency wavefields, a scaled wave equation and normalized coordinates are introduced. Two early-time wavefield snapshots from short pre-propagation are used as supervised constraints for directional plane-wave transmission. The model is trained using collocation points constrained by the wave equation via automatic differentiation. Results show agreement with k-Wave simulations in homogeneous and heterogeneous media, capturing reflection, transmission, and refraction. The method shows stable convergence and reduced error, supporting its potential as a mesh-free forward solver for SoS reconstruction and ultrasound image correction.

papers.title: Phase and Amplitude Correction for Plane Wave Transmission Through the Skull in Transcranial Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: Plane wave imaging enables ultrafast acquisition for high frame-rate imaging and improved Doppler applications, but transcranial use is limited by the skull, whose heterogeneous density and speed of sound (SoS) distort both the phase and amplitude of the transmitted wavefront. The resulting loss of coherence prevents a true plane wave from being maintained inside the brain thereby degrading image quality. This work investigates whether phase correction alone, or phase correction combined with amplitude correction, is required to reconstruct a coherent plane wave in the brain through the skull. Full-wave simulations were performed for an 80-element, 2.5-MHz phased array transducer transmitting a plane wave through a skull model derived from a microCT scan of a human temporal skull specimen (19.53 μm/voxel). We can demonstrate the uniformity of the plane wave transmission after correction, thus proving that both phase and amplitude correction is required to achieve plane wave transmission.

papers.title: Physics-Constrained Data-Driven Transcranial Ultrasound Full Waveform Inversion with Realistic 3D Acoustic Simulation
papers.abstract: Transcranial ultrasound imaging is limited by skull-induced acoustic aberrations, including refraction, reflection, scattering, diffraction, attenuation, and mode conversion, which distort wavefronts and degrade intracranial reconstruction. Unlike conventional B-mode imaging, advanced ultrasound tomography systems use transmitted acoustic waves and full or adaptive waveform inversion (FWI/AWI) to reconstruct quantitative tissue properties. However, FWI/AWI remains difficult: FWI is prone to skull-induced cycle skipping, while AWI is sensitive to amplitude loss and waveform distortion. However, many data-driven transcranial FWI methods remain limited to simplified 2D or slice-based simulations, while existing 3D studies are largely physics-based or require prior skull models. Here, we combine realistic 3D skull modeling with physics-consistent learning to bridge the simulation-to-measurement gap.

papers.title: CardiacSim: Interactive Echocardiography Simulation from Cardiac CT Mesh
papers.abstract: Acquiring diagnostic echocardiographic views requires years of hands-on training, yet no open simulator can generate realistic ultrasound images interactively from patient-specific CT anatomy at arbitrary transducer orientations. Existing approaches are expensive both financially and computationally. This work introduces CardiacSim, a hybrid simulator that takes a segmented cardiac CT mesh, synthesises anatomy-consistent pseudo B-mode echocardiography at any transducer pose, and targets deep learning refinement toward clinical realism.

papers.title: In-Vivo Musculoskeletal Ultrasound Full Waveform Inversion with Multi-Constraint Regularization
papers.abstract: Frequency-domain full waveform inversion (FDFWI) enables high-resolution ultrasound tomography but becomes highly nonconvex in musculoskeletal imaging due to strong sound-speed contrast, limited low-frequency data, and imperfect initial models, often causing cycle skipping and nonphysical updates in bone regions. We propose a multi-constraint FDFWI framework integrating a phase-derived travel-time guidance term with physics-based feasibility constraints. The phase-based objective maps phase discrepancies to travel-time residuals, reshaping the misfit from periodic to approximately quadratic and stabilizing early iterations. A lower-bound sound-speed constraint (1400 m/s) prevents nonphysical collapse, while a monotonic update constraint suppresses erroneous gradient directions in bone regions. The combined objective enables a transition from low-wavenumber stabilization to high-resolution refinement. Numerical experiments demonstrate improved convergence stability and reconstruction accuracy, particularly at cortical–soft tissue interfaces, with minimal computational overhead.

papers.title: Rapid Contrast-Free Super Resolution Ultrasound for Volumetric Assessment of Glioblastoma Microvascular Heterogeneity
papers.abstract: Microvascular remodeling is a key pathological feature of glioblastoma and is closely associated with tumor proliferation, invasion, and therapeutic response. Although ultrasound localization microscopy enables microvascular imaging beyond the diffraction limit, conventional approaches mainly rely on microbubbles, which limits rapid, repeatable, and clinical translation. This study aims to develop a contrast-free rapid super resolution ultrasound imaging method by exploiting the spatiotemporal characteristics of intrinsic blood flow scattering signals, termed clusters of scatterers (CS). By reconstructing glioblastoma microvascular and extracting volumetric vascular parameters without microbubbles, the proposed method provides a potential tool for non-invasive evaluation of tumor vascular phenotypes and treatment response.

sessions.title: MIS: AI in Echocardiography

papers.title: Deep Learning-Based Venous Gas Emboli Detection in Echocardiograms: a Multi-Source Large-Scale Validation
papers.abstract: Decompression sickness (DCS) can occur when divers experience rapid pressure changes, causing bubbles to form in tissues and the bloodstream. Venous gas emboli (VGE), detected via ultrasound, are commonly used as a surrogate marker of the risk of DCS but are typically graded manually, making assessment subjective and time-intensive. To streamline analysis, deep learning models were developed for automated VGE detection, and the best-performing model was tested across multiple cohorts. Echocardiography videos were collected from three retrospective datasets (n=805, 176, 91) and one prospective study (n=236) in a controlled hyperbaric chamber dives. Human experts graded VGE using the Eftedal–Brubakk (EB) scale, while a pre-trained Faster R-CNN ResNet-50 model detected VGE without prior exposure to these cohorts. Given the absence of observed VGE in pre-dive recordings, baseline values were approximated using AI-derived measurements. Subtracting pre-dive AI detections from post-dive values improved classification accuracy. This study provides large-scale, multi-source validation of automated VGE detection for binary EB classification using retrospective and prospective data.

papers.title: Cardiac Chamber Segmentation in Post-Dive Echocardiography: an Initial Evaluation of End-to-End Vs Prompt-Based Methods Across Low- and High-Burden Venous Gas Emboli
papers.abstract: Venous gas emboli (VGE) are used as a surrogate for decompression sickness risk, but most automated methods ignore cardiac context. Chamber segmentation is needed to localize VGE and detect paradoxical embolization linked to neurological outcomes. This study compares fully supervised models with prompt-based foundation models (SAM2/SAM3 and its medical varient MedSAM2) for four-chamber segmentation under low- and high-burden VGE. Ground truth masks were derived from post-dive echocardiograms. VGE were graded (Eftedal-Brubakk (EB) ordinal scale, 0–5) and grouped as low (≤2) or high (≥3). A total of 133 images were used for training and 97 for testing. Semi-automatic approaches included first-frame prompting (MedSAM2) and per-image prompting (SAM2/SAM3). Performance was assessed using Dice and IoU. U-Net++ performed best (0.85/0.75), followed by U-Net (0.83/0.73) and nnU-Net (0.80/0.70). Prompt-based methods were less accurate overall, though per-image prompting (SAM3: 0.76/0.63) outperformed propagation. While supervised models achieved highest accuracy, prompt-based methods offer a practical trade-off by reducing annotation effort and training time.

papers.title: On the Relationship Between inter-Rater Agreement in Venous Gas Emboli Grading and Echocardiography Video Quality
papers.abstract: Venous gas emboli (VGE) detected by echocardiography are widely used as a surrogate endpoint for decompression sickness. VGE burden is graded by trained raters using the Eftedal-Brubakk ordinal scale (EB 0–5). Assessing VGE is inherently subjective, and no objective standards exist to assess rater performance or training level. This study tested the hypothesis that inter-rater agreement is correlated with video quality. Two deidentified post-dive echocardiography datasets (N=1534, N=225) were analyzed. Video quality was quantified using a validated machine-learning metric (Q). Videos were stratified by Q into quartiles. Inter-rater reliability on the EB scale across these groups was evaluated and compared using quadratic weighted kappa. Logistic regression evaluated if video quality predicted disagreement. Rater disagreement in VGE grading was not explained by video quality alone. Among videos with EB>=1 video quality emerges as a contributing factor. A hypothesis is that poor video quality may bias agreement rates as graders often default to EB 0. Agreement rate alone is not enough to evaluate a rater's competency; weighted kappa is a better measure for evaluating rater ability.

papers.title: EchoWMANet: Dual-View Motion-Aware Echocardiography Video Learning for Automated Myocardial Infarction Diagnosis
papers.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) remains a leading cause of death globally, and echocardiography plays a crucial role in diagnosing MI through wall motion abnormalities. However, manual interpretation is subjective, often missing subtle impairments. While deep learning has shown potential for automating MI screening, current methods only extract a few static frames from videos, missing critical temporal dynamic information. This work introduces EchoWMANet, a dual-view echocardiographic video classification network designed to address these limitations. EchoWMANet captures spatiotemporal motion patterns and uses cross-view fusion to extract robust patient-level features for MI prediction. The model employs a shared ResNet encoder with two branches for myocardial morphology and wall-motion pattern extraction, integrating features from both A2C and A4C views. Experiments on the HMC-QU dataset achieved an AUC of 0.8194, accuracy of 0.8077, F1 score of 0.8649, precision of 0.8421, and sensitivity of 0.8889, demonstrating the model’s effectiveness for automated MI diagnosis.

papers.title: Impact of Spatial Context on Deep Learning-Based RWMA Detection in Echocardiography
papers.abstract: This study systematically evaluates how different levels of spatial context affect the performance of DL models for automated RWMA detection. Specifically, we investigate the impact of five input configurations derived from short-axis mitral valve view echocardiographic images: (1) full image, (2) left ventricular (LV) wall, (3) dilated LV wall, (4) combined LV wall and LV region, and (5) dilated LV wall + LV region. Dilation was used to incorporate peri-myocardial context potentially relevant to RWMA detection. Six models were evaluated, including convolutional networks (ResNet34, DenseNet121), transformer-based architectures (Swin-Tiny), and recent hybrid models (ConvNeXt-Tiny, MedViT-Small, MedKAN). Across six DL models, input spatial context substantially influenced classification performance and diagnostic trade-offs. Compared with full-image input, ROI-focused representations generally improved specificity, F1-score, and AUC, but showed different sensitivity-specificity trade-offs. Using only the LV wall achieved strong overall discrimination, with AUC values ranging from 86.14% to 95.07%, and produced the smallest average sensitivity-specificity gap of 2.52%.

papers.title: AI-Empowered Real-Time Declutter Method Enhances Diagnostic Confidence in Echocardiography
papers.abstract: Clutter artifacts in echocardiography degrade myocardial visualization and diagnostic confidence, especially in patients with poor acoustic windows. We propose a native-AI real-time declutter framework that combines offline model generation using a computationally intensive tissue-sensing declutter algorithm with deployment in the real-time imaging pipeline. The method integrates aperture-domain wavefront coherence and image-domain cardiac tissue characteristics to estimate artifact-versus-tissue distribution, enabling clutter suppression while preserving tissue integrity. In 84 patients scanned on an ultrasound research system, AI-decluttered images were compared with original images by two experienced experts using near-field clutter suppression, intracavitary clutter suppression, myocardial structure enhancement, myocardial structural integrity, and contrast resolution. Generalized contrast-to-noise ratio was used as an objective measure of tissue-clutter separability. Results showed clear improvements in clutter suppression, contrast, myocardial border delineation, and structural visualization, supporting improved diagnostic confidence in echocardiography.

papers.title: Sparse Multi-Phase Cardiac Sampling for Myocardial Infarction Detection in Echocardiography
papers.abstract: This study evaluates the effect of sparse multi-phase inputs, including end-systole (ES), end-diastole (ED), and an intermediate frame (mid), on MI detection from short axis echocardiography. Specifically, we investigate the impact of cardiac phase selection on MI detection using multiple input configurations derived from short-axis echocardiographic images. Three phase-based representations are considered: (1) single-phase input using ES, (2) dual-phase input combining ES and ED, and (3) sparse multi-phase input incorporating ES, an intermediate frame, and ED. Four DL models, including MedKAN, MedViT-Small, DenseNet121, and ConvNeXt-Tiny, are evaluated to assess the robustness of the findings across different network architectures. Experimental results indicate that the sparse multi-phase configuration consistently achieved superior performance, with ES+mid+ED yielding higher AUC, sensitivity, and F1-score across most models. The gains were consistent across architectures, indicating that performance improvements are driven by input representation.

papers.title: Development and Comparison of Deep Learning-Based Clutter Filters in Echocardiography
papers.abstract: Acoustic clutter such as rib and near‑field reverberations degrades transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), limiting diagnosis and automated analysis. Classical suppression methods struggle with the non‑stationary nature of these artifacts, motivating learning‑based alternatives. This work presents a deep‑learning clutter‑reduction pipeline trained entirely on realistic simulated TTE and evaluates its transfer to clinical data. Using 837 paired clean/cluttered sequences, a framework combining a Recurrent Attention Model with a Contextual Autoencoder was trained using multiscale reconstruction, attention, and perceptual losses. Performance was compared with an attention‑gated 3D U‑Net on simulated tests and 20 in‑vivo studies. Both performed well in simulation, but perceptual‑loss training reduced blurring and preserved speckle. On clinical data, the proposed attention‑based model showed superior robustness and generalization. These results highlight the value of attention mechanisms, perceptually informed objectives, and high‑fidelity simulation for improving clinical transfer of deep‑learning clutter suppression.

papers.title: Evaluation of a YOLOv8-Based Tricuspid Valve State Detection Model on a Benchmark Post-Dive Echocardiogram Dataset for Cardiac Cycle Tracking
papers.abstract: Venous gas emboli (VGE) detected on post-dive transthoracic echocardiography are commonly used as a marker of decompression stress. Frame-based VGE quantification requires accurate identification of late ventricular diastole (LVD) frames, which traditionally relies on manual or intensity-based methods. Recent deep learning approaches using tricuspid valve state detection have been proposed to facilitate cardiac cycle identification but lack evaluation on benchmarked datasets. In this study, a pre-trained YOLOv8-based tricuspid valve state detection model was evaluated using 20 post-dive apical four-chamber echocardiogram videos previously analyzed in a benchmark LVD selection study. Frames were manually annotated to identify closed–closed valve indices. Performance was assessed using LVD detection per cardiac cycle and frame-level comparison of closed-valve clusters against ground truth. LVD detection per cardiac cycle achieved a sensitivity of 0.689 ± 0.036 and specificity of 0.994 ± 0.001, while closed-valve cluster detection demonstrated higher agreement with sensitivity of 0.946 ± 0.071 and specificity of 0.992 ± 0.009.

papers.title: An Automated Pipeline for Fetal Cardiac Functionality Assessment Using Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) affects 1% of births worldwide and is the leading cause of infant death from non-communicable diseases. Survival exceeds 90% in high-income countries but remains critically low in Low- and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs), where cardiac imaging expertise is limited. Fetal cardiac assessment via Doppler echocardiography is manual, time-intensive, and operator-dependent. This study presents the first automated deep learning pipeline estimating fetal Doppler parameters: Myocardial Performance Index (MPI), E/A ratio, Cardiac Output (CO), Depth of M, and mechanical PR interval (mPR). A Faster R-CNN on 3,800 Mitral Valve Doppler cycles estimates MPI, E/A, Depth of M, and mPR; an EfficientNet estimates Left Ventricular Outflow Tract (LVOT) diameter; a second Faster R-CNN estimates velocity-time integral (VTI) for CO. Validation shows — mitral valve F1: 0.894, VTI F1: 0.954, and LVOT diameter Mean Absolute Error (MAE): 0.047 cm. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first unified pipeline to automate fetal cardiac Doppler assessment end-to-end, supporting the clinician's workflow with meaningful implications for global prenatal care.

papers.title: Fetal Cardiac Standard Plane Classification Using Lightweight CNN and ViT Models - a Comparative Study
papers.abstract: Identifying fetal cardiac standard planes accurately is critical for early detection of congenital heart abnormalities. Building models that are both accurate and lightweight remains a challenge for clinical use. This study compares a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and a Vision Transformer (ViT) for classifying fetal cardiac planes across five categories: 4Ch, 3VV, Left Ventricular Outflow Tract (LVOT), Right Ventricular Outflow Tract (RVOT), and Others, using 9,600 ultrasound images split 70/15/15 for training, validation, and testing. The CNN, a modified LPCSonoNet reduced from 4.3M to 1.5M parameters, was trained using AdamW and ReduceLROnPlateau. The ViT used convolutional patch embedding across 1M–6M configurations with cosine annealing. The CNN achieved 95.93% accuracy at 1.64×10⁻³s, outperforming the best ViT (3.85M) at 90.49% and 6.30×10⁻³s — a gap of 5.4 percentage points at nearly four times the speed. These results confirm the lightweight CNN as the stronger choice for clinical deployment, while highlighting ViTs as a worthwhile direction for future work in automated fetal cardiac diagnosis.

sessions.title: MTC: Renal, Reproductive & Specialized Tissue Characterization

papers.title: Power-Law Modeling of Frequency-Dependent Attenuation in Murine Kidney Disease: an Ex Vivo Study
papers.abstract: This study presents a power-law modeling framework to estimate frequency-dependent ultrasound attenuation for tissue characterization in murine kidney disease. Unlike conventional linear approaches, the proposed method captures nonlinear attenuation behavior using parameters α₀ and η. The framework, incorporating spatial regularization and multi-band analysis, demonstrated high repeatability in phantom experiments (R = 0.99). Applied to ex vivo murine kidneys, the method revealed significant differences (p < 0.01) in attenuation parameters between control, mild, and moderate disease groups, indicating sensitivity to microstructural changes. A multi-class linear SVM achieved 68.2% classification accuracy, with strong discrimination for control and mild cases but reduced performance for moderate disease. Overall, the results support the potential of frequency-dependent attenuation parameters as biomarkers for kidney disease assessment, with future work aimed at improving intermediate-stage classification and validating the approach in larger cohorts.

papers.title: In Vivo Ultrasound Speckle Statistics in the Rhesus Macaque Cervix Throughout Gestation
papers.abstract: Our goal is to develop ultrasound biomarkers that help predict delivery timing by monitoring cervical microstructure. We investigate first-order speckle statistics as a lens into cervical remodeling. Twenty-one pregnant Rhesus macaques were analyzed. Transrectal ultrasound exams with a custom linear array transducer were performed for longitudinal views of the cervix at 4, 16, 21, 22, and 23 weeks of gestation. Parameters of the Nakagami and homodyned K distributions were estimated from envelope signals acquired at beam angles from -10 to 10 degrees. The steering angle dependence of these parameters was also analyzed to investigate changes in microstructural alignment. Although median speckle statistics parameters increased over gestation, inter-subject variability was greater than any trend. Median steering angle dependence of speckle statistics were greater in vivo at all measured times compared to a reference phantom, suggesting that aligned microstructure was detected in the cervix. This study establishes baselines of speckle statistics metrics and their variability in the macaque cervix, representing an important step in developing noninvasive biomarkers of preterm birth.

papers.title: Sensitivity of Quantitative Ultrasound Vitreous Echodensity Measurements to Region of Interest Selection
papers.abstract: Vision Degrading Myodesopsia (VDM) reduces contrast sensitivity (CS) and visual quality-of-life due to symptomatic vitreous opacities. While quantitative ultrasound (QUS) metrics correlate with CS, standard variable-ROI approaches introduce spatial sampling bias that confounds measurements. We evaluated the sensitivity of QUS parameters to ROI perturbations and validated a standardized "Fixed ROI" method. We imaged 39 eyes (15-MHz system, 100 frames/scan) to compute mean amplitude (M) and percentage filled by echodensities (P50) from log-compressed envelopes. We analyzed QUS sensitivity to ROI shifts (axial: 1 mm; sector: 5º) and compared these to a fixed ROI standardized to the 87th percentile of variable-ROI areas. Perturbation analysis demonstrated that high-floater cases (P50 > 5%) are significantly more sensitive to ROI variation than low-floater cases. Our fixed ROI method reduced the coefficient of variation of M by 45.5% ± 22.4% in representative high-floater cases. By standardizing spatial sampling, the fixed ROI method facilitates improved, quantitative VDM evaluation.

papers.title: Deep Learning on Raw Ultrasound Data for Detection of Placenta-Mediated Diseases
papers.abstract: Placental dysfunction plays a key role in a wide range of adverse pregnancy outcomes. Placental dysfunction is typically manifested by changes in placental microstructure which may be subtle to be captured by conventional ultrasound. One promising alternative is quantitative ultrasound. However, this technique is still facing challenges due to model-based assumptions and calibration requirements. In this work, we present the application of deep learning to raw ultrasound data for identification of adverse pregnancy conditions. We have used raw radio-frequency ultrasound scans from a set of ex vivo placentas collected from control subjects and subjects associated with preeclampsia and/or small for gestational age conditions. Using a 1D convolutional neural network, the model achieved 72% mean testing accuracy and mean precision of 0.73 over 5 groups of random subjects excluded from training set. Overall, this method demonstrated potential of ultrasound RF based analysis as a reference-free reliable approach for detecting complicated pregnancy conditions.

papers.title: Quantitative Renal Ultrasound Texture Analysis for Assessing Tissue Response After Pediatric Renal Angioplasty
papers.abstract: Quantitative ultrasound texture analysis enables objective assessment of spatial gray-level patterns within B-mode images and may detect subtle tissue-level changes beyond visual interpretation. This study evaluated renal ultrasound texture features as markers of parenchymal response after pediatric renal angioplasty. Pediatric patients with renal artery stenosis who underwent angioplasty and had comparable pre- and post-procedural renal B-mode ultrasound images were included. Renal parenchymal regions of interest were analyzed using texture analysis software. Extracted features included first-order histogram, gray-level co-occurrence matrix, and run-length matrix parameters reflecting echogenicity, gray-level organization, homogeneity, and uniformity. Eight patients undergoing 10 angioplasty procedures were analyzed. Several texture features changed after angioplasty, including GLCM correlation, inverse difference moment, sum average, mean brightness, and long-run emphasis. These findings support B-mode ultrasound texture analysis as a feasible, objective tool for quantifying renal echotexture changes after intervention.

papers.title: Q-Gland: Quantitative Glandular Tissue Characterization for Ultrasound-Based GTC Assessment
papers.abstract: Glandular tissue component (GTC) has recently emerged as a potential imaging biomarker, as a higher proportion of glandular tissue is associated with increased breast cancer risk. While mammography has limitations in assessing tissue composition, ultrasound is increasingly utilized for GTC evaluation. However, current assessment is primarily based on visual estimation by clinicians, leading to operator dependency and variability. Although recent deep learning approaches have attempted automated quantification, they are typically trained on normal breast data without lesions, limiting their robustness in real clinical scenarios. To address these limitations, this study aims to develop a lesion-robust and objective ultrasound-based GTC quantification framework by leveraging tissue-specific statistical characteristics derived from spectral, echo, and texture analyses.

sessions.title: MBB: Beam Design

papers.title: Decreasing the depth-of-Field in Array Focusing Using Null Subtraction Imaging with Applications for Passive Cavitation Detection
papers.abstract: Passive cavitation detection (PCD) is essential for monitoring therapeutic ultrasound, but its axial resolution is physically limited by the depth-of-field (DOF) of focused receiver arrays. For common parameters (5 MHz, f-number = 2), this results in a poor axial resolution of ~8.7 mm, hindering precise localization of cavitation events.This study evaluates the use of Null Subtraction Imaging (NSI), a nonlinear beamformer, to overcome this limitation. Using an L9-4 array and a Verasonics Vantage system, researchers mapped receive beam characteristics by moving a wire target through focal points at 12, 22, and 32 mm (f-numbers of 1.25, 2.25, and 3.28, respectively). NSI performance was compared to conventional delay-and-sum (DAS) beamforming while adjusting a DC offset parameter (0.1 to 1.0). Results demonstrated that NSI significantly reduces axial DOF as the DC offset decreases. At a 12 mm focus, NSI (offset 0.1) reduced the DOF to 1.6 mm, compared to 6.1 mm with DAS. This trend remained consistent across all tested f-numbers. By narrowing both lateral beamwidth and axial DOF, NSI provides a superior method for localizing cavitation.

papers.title: Synthesis of 0th-Order Bessel Beams with a Sparse Array for Shear-Wave Super-Resolution Ultrasound
papers.abstract: A recently proposed super-resolution imaging technique modulates the point spread function of an imaging system with a focused shear wave generated remotely by the acoustic radiation force of a focused 0th-order Bessel beam. All experimental implementations reported so far have relied on fixed-focus annular transducers, which limit beamforming flexibility and prevent volumetric scanning. In this work, we report about the synthesis of focused 0th-order Bessel beams with a two-dimensional sparse array. A 256-element, 3.7 MHz spiral array with 50%-Tukey density tapering was used to synthesize Bessel beams with scaling parameters α ∈ [1200, 2400] m⁻¹ and focal depths F ∈ [10, 30] mm. Well-defined pressure rings were obtained over a wide range of geometries, with ring diameters between 1.4 mm and 8.9 mm, ring lengths between 1.9 mm and 37.1 mm, and ring-to-axis pressure ratios between 2.7 dB and 24.1 dB. Sparse arrays can replace annular transducers as electronically reconfigurable and steerable generators of Bessel fields for shear-wave super-resolution imaging, while keeping channel count and hardware complexity compatible with existing research scanners.

papers.title: Beamforming with Axial Intensity Control Using Angular Spectrum Method
papers.abstract: Beamforming plays a critical role in determining diagnostic ultrasound imaging quality. Conventional beamforming prescribes the apodization and delay at each element to generate a beam. Traditional beamforming specifies a beam’s focal depth and direction, but the axial intensity of the beam is not a design parameter. A relatively large depth of field (DoF) can be achieved with a small aperture, but at the expense of beam width and energy. The traditional approach struggles to balance DoF and penetration, limiting design flexibility.

papers.title: On the Trade-Off Between Resolution and Grating Lobes in Wearable Multi-Probe Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Wearable ultrasound systems are fundamentally limited by the restricted aperture of a single probe. Multi-probe configurations with diverging wave (DW) transmission offer a promising solution, yet imaging performance remains sensitive to probe placement due to the lack of analytical design principles. We propose a geometric DW-based framework parameterizing each transducer by radial distance (R) and orientation angle (θ), from which closed-form expressions for lateral resolution and grating lobe conditions are derived for a dual-probe setup, revealing that θ_1 and θ_2 are the primary design parameters. The model reveals a fundamental trade-off: increasing angular separation improves resolution through synthetic aperture expansion but simultaneously introduces grating lobes. Field II simulations confirm that while a wide-angle configuration achieves the narrowest beamwidth (0.006°), it suffers from CNR degradation (0.824), whereas the optimal configuration achieves a superior CNR of 1.242 while preserving resolution. This framework provides a generalizable foundation for hardware-level optimization in wearable multi-probe ultrasound systems.

papers.title: Windowed Integrated Sidelobe Level for Beamforming-Consistent Characterization of Ultrasound Pressure Fields
papers.abstract: Beam steering in phased array ultrasound introduces structured off-axis energy beyond the main lobe, which, for unfocused transmissions, appears as extended trains of delayed pulses propagating in unintended directions. Hydrophone-based pressure maps typically quantify sidelobes using peak sidelobe level (PSL) or integrated sidelobe level (ISL). However, PSL captures only a single maximum off-axis amplitude, while ISL aggregates total sidelobe energy without accounting for its temporal distribution. Both metrics are therefore limited for unfocused wavefields. We propose a windowed ISL formulation that aligns pressure field evaluation with the temporal and spatial integration of delay-and-sum beamforming, where the method applies a sliding window defined by the effective temporal aperture of the system. Based on hydrophone measurements, all methods agree for the main lobe and small steering angles (~15°), while significant deviations arise at larger angles (~30°), where sidelobe representations diverge. The proposed metric yields distinct differences in dB contour patterns, reflecting receive beamforming effects in pressure field characterization

papers.title: An Analytical Framework for Patterned Acoustic Fields from Diagnostic Arrays
papers.abstract: While field patterning has been explored in holography (e.g., acoustic tweezers), achievable design parameters remain less studied, particularly for US arrays with controllable amplitude and phase. To address this, we present an analytical framework for acoustic field design.

papers.title: Coherence-Regularized Bayesian Beamforming with Subspace Spatial Filtering for Matrix Array Imaging Using Separable Hybrid Transmissions
papers.abstract: Real-time 4D ultrasound with 2D matrix arrays faces severe cable constraints. Sub-aperture processing (SAP) with ASICs mitigates this but increases effective pitch, inducing severe grating/side lobes that degrade contrast and resolution. We propose a coherence-regularized iterative maximum a posteriori (CRiMAP) beamformer to overcome this. CRiMAP integrates three components: (1) A low-complexity reduced-rank Capon (RRC) prior replaces delay-and-sum (DAS) to provide a purified signal subspace. (2) A local-SNR-driven generalized coherence factor (GCF) is embedded into the Bayesian variance update, preserving tissue speckle while strictly suppressing lobe-dominated regions. (3) Interference variance is rigorously updated using the residual between raw data and the estimated signal. Evaluated on a 64×24 array (4×4 SAP) in biplane imaging, CRiMAP outperforms standard methods. It increases contrast ratio by 17.2 dB over DAS and 7.9 dB over conventional iMAP, and improves spatial resolution by 18.3% (gCNR=0.87). Despite a modest speckle SNR trade-off, CRiMAP profoundly eliminates intracystic clutter, demonstrating immense potential for clinical SAP-based matrix imaging.

sessions.title: MCA: Microbubble physics, modeling, and imaging

papers.title: Controlling Surface Tension of Monodisperse Microbubble via Multi-Gas Core to Enhance Subharmonic Response
papers.abstract: Subharmonic response of microbubbles to ultrasound is promising for theranostic applications. Numerical calculations show that near buckling bubbles with low surface tension exhibit a low subharmonic threshold. This work aimed to produce monodisperse microbubbles (MDMBs) with tunable CO2 content in multi-gas (CO2 and C3F8) cores to control initial surface tension to enhance the subharmonic response. MDMBs with varying CO2 fractions (0%, 50%, 80%) in multi-gas cores were formed in a flow-focusing microfluidic chip. Pressure-dependent attenuation spectra were measured to characterize bubble state and calculate surface tension. Subharmonic responses were measured over 70–120 kPa peak negative pressures (PNPs) to determine the PNP threshold and subharmonic amplitude. Results showed that higher CO2 fractions reduced surface tension from 30 to 13 mN and shifted bubbles towards a buckling state. This reduction lowered the PNP threshold for subharmonic generation and significantly increased the subharmonic amplitude. These findings demonstrate that increasing CO2 fractions in the multi-gas core to reduce surface tension is an effective strategy for improving subharmonic response.

papers.title: On Factors Affecting Optimal Incident Acoustic Output for Subharmonic Aided Pressure Estimation
papers.abstract: Subharmonic Aided Pressure Estimation (SHAPE) utilizes subharmonic signals of ultrasound contrast agents during their growth stage to estimate hydrostatic pressure. Commercial SHAPE implementation requires identifying the optimal incident acoustic output (IAO) for pressure estimation, but the impact of tissue-induced attenuation and aberration, transmit parameter variations, and signal processing on the optimization process remains underexplored. This in vitro study investigates how these factors may impact optimal IAO selection for pressure estimation.

papers.title: Acoustic and Physical Stability of PVA Vs SonoVue Microbubbles Under Repeated Focused Ultrasound Exposure
papers.abstract: MBs-mediated cavitation enables FUS-induced BBB opening, but conventional lipid-shelled MBs such as SonoVue show limited stability and rapid clearance, restricting sustained exposure. This study compares the acoustic behavior, cavitation dynamics, and stability of PVA MBs versus SV under repeated low-mechanical index sonication. Experiments were conducted in a tissue-mimicking phantom using clinically relevant MB concentrations (5×10⁷ MB/mL). Sonication (1.5 MHz, 0.1–0.7 MPa, 10% duty cycle) was applied in four sequential runs, while cavitation activity was monitored via passive cavitation detection and quantified as stable, inertial, and ultraharmonic doses. SV exhibited increasing inertial activity and decreasing stability over time, indicating progressive disruption, especially at higher pressures. In contrast, PVA MBs maintained more stable cavitation emissions and showed greater resistance to ultrasound-induced degradation. Microscopy confirmed slower, pressure-dependent depletion of PVA MBs. Overall, PVA MBs demonstrate superior acoustic and physical stability, supporting their potential for prolonged and controlled BBB modulation and FUS-mediated therapeutic delivery.

papers.title: Post-Activation Shell Stiffening Shifts Microbubble Resonance: a Potential Source of Clinical Variability
papers.abstract: Ultrasound contrast agents are widely used in diagnostic and therapeutic ultrasound, but their acoustic response is often assumed to remain stable after activation. This study investigated whether post-activation shell evolution alters the resonance behavior of agitation-fabricated, size-isolated lipid microbubbles despite stable size and concentration. Microbubbles with a mean diameter of 3.6 µm were monitored for 48 h using broadband attenuation spectroscopy at 7 kPa, with size and concentration independently measured by Coulter counter. Although the size distribution remained consistent and total concentration varied by no more than 7%, the resonance frequency shifted markedly from ~3.6 MHz at 5 min post-activation to 10.6 MHz within a few hours, stabilizing between 2 and 24 h. The decoupling between size and resonance suggests progressive shell stiffening, likely associated with limited gas dissolution, lipid repacking, and transition toward a more condensed shell state. These findings indicate that injections from the same activated vial at different times may exhibit different acoustic responses, with implications for reproducibility and protocol consistency.

papers.title: Real-Time 3D Contrast Imaging Using DC-Biased Row Column Arrays and Amplitude Modulation
papers.abstract: Contrast ultrasound imaging uses microbubble agents injected into the bloodstream to enhance the visualization of blood flow and blood vessels. 3D contrast-enhanced ultrasound imaging (CEUS) allows for better visualization of vessels in 3D, however row-column-array-based 3D CEUS methods like tilted plane-wave (TPW) imaging require minimal motion over volume compounding. Here, we propose a strategy that uses DC-biased RCAs, also called Top-Orthogonal-Bottom-Electrode (TOBE) arrays, with a fast synthetic aperture 3D imaging method (Walking uFORCES) that is modified for amplitude modulation. We show how this strategy is able to obtain 3D CEUS volumes at real-time rates, transmit-receive focused everywhere and with improved robustness to motion.

papers.title: Memory Effects in Fractional Kelvin–Voigt Microbubble Models: Advantages in Describing Transients and Capturing Strong Nonlinearities
papers.abstract: The study of microbubble dynamics is central to ultrasound imaging. This study aims to reveal the significant advantages of the fractional Kelvin–Voigt(FKV) model over the Kelvin–Voigt(KV) model by examining both transient establishment processes of microbubbles and complex nonlinear behavior. The research has found that the advantages of the FKV model are primarily twofold: 1. Accurate depiction of transient memory effects: This shows that the FKV model can describe the history dependence of bubble oscillations, whereas the KV model reduces this to an instantaneous steady state. 2. Ability to capture strong nonlinear behavior: The stronger the nonlinearity, the more pronounced the advantage of the fractional model.

papers.title: Spectral Fingerprinting of Gas-Filled Scattering Agents Using 200 MHz Acoustic Flow Cytometry: Resolving Lipid-Shelled Nanobubble Scattering Mechanisms with Experimental Evidence
papers.abstract: Single-particle acoustic flow cytometry at 200 MHz was used to compare the spectral fingerprints of lipid-shelled nanobubbles (NBs), microbubbles (MBs), and protein-shelled gas vesicles (GV-ST, GV-WT). Quantitative ultrasound analysis showed that NBs and MBs had similar per-particle echogenicity by MBF, while both bubble types were ~5 dB more echogenic than the GVs. NBs also exhibited a less negative spectral slope than MBs, consistent with a near-buckled shell state that shifts the time-averaged response closer to zero. In contrast, GVs showed positive spectral slope and in-phase scattering, consistent with more Rayleigh-like rigid-shell behavior. These results provide experimental evidence that lipid-shelled bubbles and protein-shelled gas bodies scatter through distinct physical mechanisms and that spectral parameters can serve as a mechanistic single-particle fingerprint for gas-filled agent classification.

sessions.title: MBF: Clinical and Preclinical Applications of Doppler Ultrasound and Microvascular Imaging

papers.title: Optimization and Development of the Doppler-Enabled MICROBEAD Device Into a Clinically Translatable Biopsy Marker
papers.abstract: Doppler-enabled breast biopsy markers are a promising replacement for B-mode biopsy markers in the treatment of metastatic axillary lymph nodes. Preliminary tests of the MICROBEAD marker have shown distinguishable Doppler signal in an in situ porcine environment. To optimize Doppler signal for varied transducers, 1 mL syringes were filled with surfactant solution and polyethylene particles with diameter ranges of 45-75, 75-90, and 125-150 µm and scanned with C1-6, 9L, and ML6-15 transducers on a GE LE9 system. The original plastic capsule was upgraded to more rugged 1.4 mm diameter glass capsules with better biocompatibility. Capsules were filled with 125-150 µm particles, sealed, and evaluated monthly by massing and Doppler scans. The 45-75, 75-90, and 125-150 µm particles showed the most signal at frequencies of 8.3, 5.0, and 3.1 MHz, respectively. The glass capsules exhibited strong Doppler signal over multiple months, supporting device longevity. These results show the importance of matching particle sizes to Doppler transmit wavelengths and portray the ability of the design to be tuned to a specific transducer.

papers.title: Quantitative Ultrasound Microflow Imaging for Grading Diagnosis and Early Monitoring of Infantile Hemangioma
papers.abstract: Objective To investigate the value of ultrasound microflow imaging (MFI) and quantitative microvascular parameters in grading infantile hemangioma (IH) and monitoring early treatment response. Methods Fifty-two children with IH underwent MFI and color Doppler flow imaging (CDFI). Lesions were graded G1–G5 based on CDFI blood-flow signals. MFI parameters, including vascular ratio (VR), number of vessels (NV), number of branch points (NB), and microvascular fractal dimension (mvFD), were compared among grades and followed after treatment. Results MFI showed clearer tiny vessels and higher spatial resolution than CDFI. VR, NV, NB, and mvFD differed significantly among grades and distinguished any two grades. After treatment, MFI showed reduced vascular density and complexity, with decreases in NV, NB, VR, and mvFD and increased VBR. Conclusion MFI quantification can objectively assess IH microvascularity, differentiate IH grades, and support early treatment-response monitoring.

papers.title: Quantifying Doppler Twinkling in Polymethyl Methacrylate Markers Using Channel-Level Signal Features
papers.abstract: Polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) biopsy markers use color Doppler twinkling to enhance ultrasound detection; however, conventional Doppler metrics often fail to distinguish true twinkling from coherent backscatter, especially at low signal levels. This study explores channel-level feature extraction to capture phase instability and decorrelation. Three samples were evaluated: metal (no twinkling) and PMMA with strong and low twinkling (LT). Doppler RF data were acquired using L7-4 and L11-4v transducers (4 MHz, 12°, PRF 2.5–3.0 kHz; 14 pulses, 20 frames). Two configurations were used: gel-pad coupling (L7-4) and water-tank suspension (L11-4v). Beamformed data were demodulated to IQ and high-pass filtered (100 Hz). Lag-one normalized autocorrelation features (x1,x2) were computed to quantify phase shift and decorrelation. Feature distributions showed clear separation: metal at low values, LT intermediate, and twinkling highest. L7-4 produced compact, well-separated clusters, while L11-4v showed broader distributions. These features enable robust differentiation of twinkling signatures across transducers, supporting quantitative ultrasound detection.

papers.title: From Minutes to Seconds: Fast Envelope Extraction of Ultrafast Doppler Spectrograms in the Neonatal Brain
papers.abstract: This abstract introduces a fast method for extracting Doppler spectrogram envelopes from neonatal brain ultrafast ultrasound. Conventional pixel-by-pixel binarization and thresholding approaches are computationally impractical for full-brain mapping (~5 min per acquisition). The proposed spectral-moment-based method computes envelopes simultaneously across all pixels by defining the envelope as a z-score-parameterized confidence interval around the mean Doppler frequency, derived from the power spectral density. Validated on 30 healthy neonates using a Verasonics Vantage 256, the optimal z-score converged to z ≈ 2.63–2.93 across large, medium, and small vessels. The method showed excellent agreement with ground-truth envelopes (r = 0.987, slope = 0.93) and reduced computation from 5 minutes to 10 seconds — a 30× speedup enabling practical full-brain cerebrovascular hemodynamic assessment.

papers.title: Dual-Aperture Ultrasound Vector Flow Imaging and Wall Shear Stress Mapping in an Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Phantom
papers.abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) surveillance is primarily based on ultrasound diameter measurement, but diameter provides limited information on local hemodynamic disturbance. Biomarkers such as wall shear stress (WSS), oscillatory flow, and recirculation may support functional AAA assessment, yet quantitative vector flow and WSS mapping are challenging at abdominal-aorta depths because of limited aperture, weak blood signal, and poor lateral-flow sensitivity. This study uses two angled ultrasound transducers to increase effective aperture and expand Doppler interrogation-angle range for deep AAA flow imaging. A wall-less tissue-mimicking phantom with an idealized AAA-like channel was perfused with blood-mimicking fluid under pulsatile flow. Dual-angle Doppler acquisition, extended-aperture beamforming, and clutter suppression were used to reconstruct 2D vector flow and estimate WSS along the segmented lumen boundary. The method visualized pulsatile flow, recirculation within the aneurysm sac, and reduced WSS in the dilated region, demonstrating feasibility for ultrasound-based VFI and WSS mapping beyond diameter-only AAA assessment.

papers.title: Null Subtraction Imaging for Functional Ultrasound Evaluation in Trembler-J Mice, Model of the Neurodegenerative Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease
papers.abstract: Functional ultrasound imaging (fUS) allows the evaluation of cerebral blood volume (CBV) dynamics. Trembler-J (TrJ) mice, a model of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, exhibit impaired neurovascular responses to vibrissae stimulation compared with wild-type (WT) mice. In this work, we evaluate whether Null Subtraction Imaging (NSI), a nonlinear beamforming technique with enhanced spatial resolution, can characterize fUS responses in WT and TrJ mice by comparing its performance to conventional delay-and-sum (DAS). fUS acquisitions were performed in WT and TrJ mice (n=4 per group). fUS responses were assessed using significant pixel-wise correlation between CBV signal and the stimulation pattern (p<0.001), and the CBV ON–OFF amplitude computed from 20 s averages within stimulation ON and OFF periods. NSI showed higher temporal noise than DAS, yielding lower correlation values, but preserved CBV dynamics. NSI estimates CBV changes that are more closely associated with activated vessels, providing larger CBV ON–OFF amplitude differences with respect to DAS. This result highlights the potential of NSI for fUS studies.

papers.title: Optimization of a Sparse 2D Ultrasound Array for Autonomous Transcranial Doppler Emboli Monitoring
papers.abstract: Conventional Transcranial Doppler (TCD) is limited to short-term clinical use because slight probe or patient motion can shift the target artery outside the beam, restricting continuous monitoring. To address this limitation, a 16-element sparse 2D ultrasound array (2DTCD) was proposed capable of volumetric beam steering for autonomous cerebral blood flow localization and emboli detection. Active sparse element distributions, element size, and kerf spacing were optimized in Field II simulations using Peak Side Lobe Level (PSLL), steering accuracy, and beamwidth over ±15° steering angles and 20–70 mm focal depths. The optimal design employed a 2 × 2 mm element size and 1.45 mm kerf spacing, achieving 9.64 ± 4.43 dB PSLL and 2.39 ± 0.27 mm beamwidth. A 3D pulsatile flow simulation further demonstrated flow localization through volumetric velocity scanning, Power M-mode, and Doppler spectrograms, supporting autonomous cerebral blood flow and emboli monitoring.

papers.title: 4D Non-Invasive Functional Ultrasound Imaging Reveals Functional Network Disruption in Mice with Alzheimer’s Disease
papers.abstract: High-resolution, brain-wide imaging of network dynamics is essential for diagnosing and monitoring neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's Disease (AD). Current neuroimaging techniques are limited in spatiotemporal resolution, preventing the capture of transient, network-wide dynamics. Here, we propose a non-invasive 4D functional ultrasound imaging (fUSI) approach to map brain hemodynamics, functional connectivity, and network-level organization. WT and AD mice were imaged volumetrically and transcranially. Cerebral blood flow (CBF), resting state connectivity analysis, and graph theory metrics were calculated. Global efficiency decreased by 5.3% and local by 3.8% compared to WT. Across all other metrics, AD mice showed higher values in cortical regions (+1.1% to +16.3%) but lower values in subcortical regions (-1.1% to -14.8%), except betweenness, which was 40.3% lower cortically and 9.9% lower subcortically in AD, indicating network restructuring. These results reveal cortical hyperconnectivity and subcortical hypoconnectivity in AD, demonstrating that 4D fUSI can capture brain-wide network restructuring inaccessible to conventional neuroimaging.

papers.title: Functional Sure for Ultrahigh-Resolution Cerebral Blood Volume Mapping and Single-Vessel Level Analysis via Doppler-power-weighting-Based Contrast Enhancement
papers.abstract: Functional ultrasound has traditionally relied on ultrasound localization microscopy to achieve super-resolution; however, its dependence on exogenous contrast agents limits its applicability for non-invasive and longitudinal studies. While super-resolution ultrasound imaging of erythrocytes (SURE) has demonstrated effectiveness in structural mapping and flow velocity estimation, its potential for dynamic functional imaging remains unexplored. This work extends the SURE framework to functional imaging and introduces an improved SURE (iSURE) with a Doppler-power-weighting-based contrast-enhancement strategy to enhance localization fidelity, improve cerebral blood volume (CBV) mapping accuracy, and enable functional analysis at the single-vessel level.

papers.title: Improving the Contrast of Super-Resolution Ultrasound Imaging of the Erythrocytes by Hyper-beamformation
papers.abstract: Super-resolution ultrasound imaging of erythrocytes (SURE) enables contrast-free, toward real-time super-resolution microvascular imaging. However, compared to ultrasound localization microscopy and power Doppler imaging, SURE typically exhibits suboptimal vessel-to-background contrast. This limitation arises from a high rate of peak misdetection, as noise fluctuations frequently exceed the detection threshold. To address this issue, hyper-beamformation (HBF) was integrated into the SURE framework to enhance image contrast. In vivo experiments demonstrate that this approach significantly improves microvessel visualization by providing a cleaner background.

papers.title: Contrast-Free Phase-Resolved Myocardial Microvascular Imaging in Beating Hearts
papers.abstract: Direct visualization of myocardial microcirculation remains challenging because of rapid cardiac motion, small vessel size, and the limited spatiotemporal resolution of conventional perfusion imaging. Conventional myocardial perfusion methods mainly provide tissue-level or temporally averaged perfusion information. Ultrasound localization microscopy can visualize microvascular structures, but it requires contrast agents and long trajectory accumulation, and myocardial ULM is often limited to relatively stable diastolic phases, making full-cycle phase-resolved imaging difficult. We developed phase-resolved myocardial microvascular imaging, a contrast-free dynamic ultrafast Doppler framework for imaging myocardial microvascular flow in beating hearts. Results show strong correlations between diastolic microvascular metrics and flowmeter-measured coronary perfusion, highlighting the potential of the proposed framework for evaluating myocaridal microcirucation without the need for contrast agents.

sessions.title: MSR: The sound of brain mapping

papers.title: Contrast-Free Transcranial Super-Resolution Ultrasound Imaging of Human Brain Using Robust Principal Component Analysis
papers.abstract: Super-resolution ultrasound (SRUS) imaging is a powerful approach for visualizing fine vasculature in the brain with high sensitivity. While many SRUS techniques rely on contrast microbubbles to provide strong sparse point scatterers in the vasculature bed, contrast-free SRUS is of increasing interest as it avoids contrast administration. However, in the absence of contrast agents, extraction of blood-flow-related signals becomes significantly more challenging due to skull attenuation and the weaker scattering of red blood cells (RBCs) compared to contrast agents. The objective of this work is to develop a processing pipeline for highly-sensitive estimation of sparse RBC-related signals and subsequent reconstruction of cerebral vasculature in a contrast-free setting. We propose Robust Principal Component Analysis (RPCA) for separating blood-flow-related signals from tissue clutter in ultrafast ultrasound data acquired without contrast agents. The sparse component is then processed using a ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM)-inspired tracking pipeline to reconstruct super-resolved vasculature.

papers.title: Volumetric Rat Brain Sure Imaging
papers.abstract: Super-resolution ultrasound imaging using erythrocytes (SURE) enables contrast-free visualization of microvascular networks, but its extension to volumetric imaging remains limited. This study demonstrates 3D SURE in the rat brain using a row-column array and synthetic aperture acquisition with only 80 receive elements. Microvascular maps and local vessel diameters were reconstructed from short acquisitions (20 s), revealing a dense vascular network and resolving vessel segments smaller than half the acoustic wavelength (λ/2 = 51.3 μm, λ = 102.6 μm). Results were consistent across multiple segments from a single acquisition. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of rapid, high-resolution, contrast-free 3D brain imaging using SURE.

papers.title: Functional Sure Imaging
papers.abstract: Super-resolution ultrasound imaging using erythrocytes (SURE) enables contrast-free visualization of microvascular networks, but its ability to detect functional changes in the microvasculature remains limited. This study evaluates SURE for detecting stimulus-evoked blood flow changes in the rat brain during whisker stimulation. Activation maps reveal localized increases in vascular signal in somatosensory regions, and analysis of selected vessels shows significantly stronger responses in activated vessels compared to controls (P<0.05). Although signal changes are small (0.3–0.8%), they are stimulus-locked and consistent across cycles. These results demonstrate that SURE can detect functional microvascular responses without contrast agents, supporting its potential for high-resolution functional brain imaging.

papers.title: Toward Ultrafast Transcranial Ultrasound Localization Microscopy: Transferable Aberration Correction Across Sparse-Angle Acquisitions and Scatterer-Varying Media
papers.abstract: Transcranial ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) requires long-sequence ultrafast acquisition, but skull-induced aberration degrades focusing and localization. This study evaluates whether a transcranial aberration correction law, derived once from fully sampled multi-angle plane-wave RF data using optimization-based beamforming, can be reused in acquisition and medium conditions relevant to ULM. Simulations used a 192-element linear array, a skull layer, and a heterogeneous soft-tissue medium with strong scatterers. A correction law estimated from 121 plane waves was directly transferred to five-angle compounding, single-angle acquisition, and a mixed scenario with single-angle imaging plus random medium fluctuations and scatterer-position changes. The pre-calibrated law improved focusing, reduced clutter, and retained visible correction benefits across all tested cases. FWHM improved by up to 75%, supporting pre-calibrated transcranial aberration correction as a practical route toward ultrafast ULM without per-frame full-angle optimization.

papers.title: Self-Inspired Learning for Denoising in Nonlinear Ultrasound Localization Microscopy
papers.abstract: Nonlinear ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) leverages the acoustic nonlinear properties of microbubbles (MBs) as the physical basis to distinguish them from tissue and noise. In practice, however, achieving complete extraction of MB nonlinear signals without spatiotemporal filtering remains a significant challenge. Recent work has reported another approach for extracting MBs from background clutter by adopting nonlinear coherence operator. Self-supervised denoising is appropriate for ultrasound lacking ground truth. In this work, by tailoring the denoising process to the specific characteristics of MB nonlinear imaging, a self-inspired module achieves the targeted enhancement of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). This module potentially further enhances MB extraction in nonlinear ULM and angiographic performance within the microvasculature.

papers.title: Deep-Learning Based super-Resolution Functional Ultrasound Imaging in Rat Brains
papers.abstract: Functional ultrasound (fUS) exploits the neurovascular coupling to detect neural activity. But its spatial resolution remains constrained by the diffraction limit. To overcome this constraint, functional ultrasound localization microscopy (fULM) combines fUS with ULM; this approach requires repeated stimulation and data accumulation. Recently, deep learning methods have been introduced to reconstruct ULM images from contrast-free power Doppler data. However, the spatial resolution of contrast-free power Doppler is insufficient to identify microvasculature. In this study, we adapted the methodology by incorporating gradient fluctuation characteristics of red blood cells and an uncertainty-driven loss function into the deep-learning model to enhance microvascular imaging for transient super-resolution functional ultrasound imaging (SR-fUS).

papers.title: 3D Ultrasound Localization Microscopy for Visualization and Quantification of Intraocular Pressure in Posterior Ocular Microvessels Using a 256-Element Matrix Array
papers.abstract: This study demonstrates the feasibility of 3D ULM for imaging posterior ocular microvasculature by combining sound-speed-corrected beamforming with angular-domain spatial similarity enhancement to improve microbubble (MB) signal quality. A 3D framework was also developed to quantify vessel density and mean flow velocity across varying intraocular pressure (IOP) levels.In an in vivo rabbit study, 16,000 volumes were acquired using plane-wave imaging with a 256-element 2D array. The proposed processing pipeline enhanced MB resolution and contrast, enabling improved visualization of microvessels. Quantitative analysis was performed within a fixed 3D region of interest across different IOP conditions.The method successfully resolved posterior ocular microvessels and demonstrated sensitivity to IOP-induced changes. Vessel density decreased markedly with increasing IOP (from ~17% at 15 mmHg to ~4% at 45 mmHg), while mean flow velocity showed a moderate decline at lower IOPs followed by a more pronounced reduction at higher pressures.

papers.title: Transcranial Ultrafast Doppler and Ultrasound Localization Microscopy in Rats After EDTA-Treated Acoustic Transparency
papers.abstract: Ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) enables cerebral microvascular imaging by localizing circulating microbubbles, but transcranial applications are limited by skull-induced attenuation, scattering, and wavefront distortion. This study evaluates EDTA-treated acoustic transparency for transcranial ultrafast Doppler imaging and ULM in rats. The rat skull was exposed and locally treated with EDTA for 10 min. Pre- and post-treatment power Doppler imaging was performed to assess transcranial blood-flow visibility. After tail-vein injection of ultrasound contrast agents, ULM data were acquired, and microbubble signals were localized and accumulated to reconstruct the microvascular map. Acquisitions used 15 MHz, 1000-Hz PRF, and 9 compounded plane waves from −11° to 11°. After EDTA treatment, Doppler signals were enhanced, and more vascular structures became visible. The CNR increased from 4.19 to 4.82, corresponding to a 15.2% improvement. These preliminary results suggest that EDTA-treated acoustic transparency enhances transcranial Doppler visibility and microbubble detectability, indicating potential for microbubble-based transcranial vascular imaging without craniotomy.

sessions.title: TMU: Micromachined Ultrasonic Transducers

papers.title: Transferred Single Crystalline PMN-PZT Thin Film Based 2D row-Column PMUT Array for real-Time Ultrasonic 3D fingerprints/Vein Imaging
papers.abstract: Piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducers (PMUTs) are promising for ultrasonic fingerprint and vein recognition owing to their compact size and low power consumption. However, their performance is limited by the piezoelectric quality of thin films directly deposited on Si, while heteroepitaxial buffer layers restrict electrode design and increase parasitic resistance. Here, we developed a two-dimensional row-column PMUT array using a transferred single-crystal PMN-PZT thin film. The PMN-PZT was grown on a perovskite substrate and transferred to Si via metal-metal diffusion bonding and sacrificial layer etching. This process enabled orthogonally arranged identical top and bottom electrodes, improving electrical symmetry and design flexibility. The transferred film showed superior crystalline and ferroelectric properties, with a rocking-curve FWHM of 0.19° and remanent polarization of 34 μC/cm², compared with 0.95° and 21 μC/cm² for directly grown films. Consequently, the PMUT achieved a dynamic displacement of 60 nm/V at 12 MHz, nearly 10 times higher than a directly grown PMN-PZT device, while reducing pressure variation by minimizing parasitic resistance mismatch.

papers.title: Broadband AlScN PMUT Row-Column-Addressed Array Based on Front-Side Sacrificial-Layer Etching for Real-Time 3-D Imaging
papers.abstract: This work presents a broadband piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducer (PMUT) based on a front-side sacrificial-layer etching process. By adopting a thin membrane-type structure with reduced effective membrane mass and applying PDMS encapsulation for acoustic loading and damping, the PMUT achieves a broadband frequency response. A 32 × 32 row-column array was fabricated and characterized. The device shows a center frequency of 5.582 MHz and a displacement sensitivity of 3.01 nm/V in air, while the resonance shifts to 2.986 MHz after PDMS encapsulation. In receiving experiments, the PMUT exhibits a short ringing duration and a fractional bandwidth of 69.7%. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed thin-membrane PMUT design for broadband ultrasound imaging applications.

papers.title: Adaptive Optical Ultrasound Detection via Polymer-Tuned Integrated Photonic Transducers
papers.abstract: Integrated photonic ultrasound transducers (IPUTs) combine silicon photonics with micromachined membrane structures, offering compact, CMOS compatible optical detectors. However, their mechanical properties are fixed after fabrication, limiting application specific tuning. This work demonstrates a post fabrication polymer coating strategy that enables deterministic control of resonance frequency, bandwidth, and sensitivity without modifying the underlying photonic design. Mach–Zehnder IPUTs coated with 17.4 μm Altuglas P10 show a resonance shift from 1 MHz to 4 MHz and a Q factor reduction from 10 to 3, enabling broader band operation. Experiments and a viscoelastic, prestress aware multiphysics model agree within 1.7% in transfer function amplitude. Thickness dependent simulations (0–100 μm) reveal a transition from membrane dominated motion to hybrid elastic wave modes beyond ~50 μm. These results establish polymer coatings as a scalable, CMOS compatible mechanism for post fabrication tuning of micromachined optical ultrasound transducers.

papers.title: A Compact Photoacoustic Sensing Probe Using Surface-Micromachined Optical Ultrasound Transducer (SMOUT)
papers.abstract: In this paper, we report an innovative compact photoacoustic (PA) sensing probe based on a surface-micromachined optical ultrasound transducer (SMOUT). Owing to its excellent optical transparency, the excitation light can propagate through the SMOUT to the target, enabling the use of a single optical fiber for both excitation and reception. In addition, the SMOUT provides high acoustic sensitivity, high optical uniformity, and excellent operation stability. For demonstration, a prototype PA sensing probe using the SMOUT has been designed, fabricated, and experimentally characterized. Red-dye solutions with different concentrations and a piece of black tape embedded at various depths in biological tissue are used as sensing targets, and the probe performance is validated by the experimental results. Overall, the compact and sensitive SMOUT-based probe shows strong potential for a wide range of PA sensing applications, and its uniform mass production makes it amenable to be arranged into 1-D and 2-D planar or spherical arrays for imaging applications.

papers.title: High-Performance,Ultra-Thin and Intrinsically Flexible PMUT Array by SOI Process
papers.abstract: Flexible ultrasound is key to monitoring, detection and robotics. Compared with PZT, PMUTs offer miniaturized, low-power, CMOS-compatible integration. Yet flexible PMUTs trade performance for deformability: hybrid substrates improve bending but limit radius and density; polymer substrates add compliance but suppress vibration and output through low modulus and high damping.We present a high-performance, flexible PMUT array on an ultra-thin silicon substrate. Controlled thinning lowers bending stiffness while preserving silicon’s low-loss mechanical/acoustic properties. The SOI-compatible array is 11.6 μm thick, tested by LDV, impedance analyzer and microphone.After thinning, acoustic responses remain stable, showing reduced bending stiffness without impaired transduction. The device works at a 10 mm bending radius, with 85.5 kHz resonance, 2.97 μm displacement at 10 Vp-p and 133.5 dB SPL at 2 cm under 25 Vp-p. Unlike polymer-supported PMUTs, ultra-thin silicon retains low loss while enabling flexibility, reducing dissipation and damping, improving energy conversion and supporting high-performance flexible ultrasonic systems.

papers.title: A Geometry-Programmable Flexible PMUT Array for Airborne Sensing of Non-Planar Obstacles
papers.abstract: Conventional rigid airborne ultrasonic arrays have fixed aperture geometries and element normals, limiting directional response and effective field of view. Here, we present a 16-channel flexible PMUT array operating at 80 kHz that combines low-frequency air-coupled sensing, multichannel integration, and mechanical flexibility. Array bending changes element positions and local transmit/receive normals, redistributing channel responses and tuning the effective field of view. Deformation can enhance echoes from selected directions, while channel-wise echo distributions provide directional information. Simulations and experiments confirm angular-mismatch-induced echo attenuation and demonstrate improved sensing of large-azimuth targets. This work establishes a flexible PMUT architecture for low-frequency, wide-angle airborne obstacle sensing.

papers.title: Frequency-Dependent Phase Gradients in Globally Excited PMUT Arrays for Passive Beamforming and Sensing
papers.abstract: Active beam steering in PMUT arrays typically requires complex phase-shifting electronics. This study investigates frequency-dependent spatial phase gradients in globally excited arrays as an alternative mechanism for acoustic wave manipulation. A 4×4 ScAlN PMUT array was fabricated and characterized. To analytically formulate phase dispersion, a modified Mason equivalent circuit incorporating self and mutual radiation impedance matrices was developed. A 3D finite element method (FEM) model was built to analyze fluid-coupled acoustic interactions. Under uniform global AC excitation, the full-field spatial phase response was mapped via Laser Doppler Vibrometry (LDV). Analytical and FEM models predicted that high mechanical Q-factors interact with mutual acoustic coupling to generate deterministic phase delays. LDV measurements confirmed that the array produces an orderly spatial phase gradient shifting dynamically with excitation frequency. Heavy fluid loading disrupts this gradient due to increased acoustic damping. Intentionally designing such gradients enables passive beamforming and acoustic tweezers, while fluid-induced phase disruption provides a metric for liquid sensing.

papers.title: Exact Conductance-Shape Fitting and Background Subtraction for Automated BVD Characterization
papers.abstract: Impedance spectroscopy of PMUTs and CMUTs is commonly interpreted with the Butterworth-Van Dyke (BVD) circuit, but direct nonlinear fitting of the complex impedance can be difficult because the resonance depends on coupled parameters and because background conductance distorts extraction. This work presents an automated conductance-based pipeline that fits the exact normalized shape of G = Re{Y} around series resonance. From the fitted peak height, series resonance frequency, and FWHM, the method extracts Rm, Q, Lm, and Cm, while low-frequency susceptance provides the effective shunt capacitance. Background conductance is estimated from the off-peak regions, subtracted before fitting, and used to estimate effective shunt loss tangent. Synthetic validation with prescribed backgrounds and Monte Carlo noise shows unbiased recovery in the noiseless case and strong robustness under noise. The method also provides reliable starting values for more advanced BVD models.

papers.title: Reconfigurable Piezoelectric Micromachined Ultrasonic Transducer (pMUT) Array for Photoacoustic Imaging
papers.abstract: Piezoelectric micromachined ultrasound transducers (pMUTs) are widely applied in photoacoustic imaging (PAI) for their advantages, but traditional fixed-channel pMUT arrays increase optimization costs by requiring new fabrication for different configurations. This study develops a reconfigurable pMUT array to solve this issue, tests its performance, and conducts preliminary PAI experiments. The array’s pMUT cells use a PZT piezoelectric layer and other functional layers; each channel contains 24 devices of 8 sizes, with reconfigurability achieved by adjusting flexible printed circuit board (FPCB) positions. PAI experiments adopted single-channel raster scanning and circular array modes. Pulse-echo tests show the pMUT channels have an average 100% -6 dB bandwidth and 4.7 MHz peak frequency. PAI experiments successfully imaged pencil leads, producing 3D and 2D images. Ongoing work aims to enhance resolution by reducing FPCB size and increasing array density, with the array offering a flexible, cost-effective PAI solution.

papers.title: Large Aperture PVD PZT PMUT 1D Arrays for Medical Imaging
papers.abstract: This work presents the acoustic characterization of a 9.6 mm x 6.4 mm, 48-channel Piezoelectric Micromachined Ultrasonic Transducer (PMUT) array. The device features a 2 µm PZT film on a 4 µm polysilicon membrane, with 100 µm cavities and a 135 µm pitch.
