Initial characterization involved impedance and phase measurements of all 48 channels using a Keysight E4990A analyzer. Butterworth-Van Dyke (BVD) curve fitting was applied to extract the electromechanical coupling coefficient (Kt2) and evaluate array uniformity. For performance testing, the array was encapsulated in Sylgard 184 PDMS and tested under immersion. The transmit (TX) response was measured using a needle hydrophone 2 cm away, driven by a 20 Vpp square wave to determine the TX transfer function against DC bias. The receive (RX) sensitivity was characterized using an Olympus 5072PR impulse generator and transducer. Finally, the array was integrated with a Verasonics Vantage system via a bias tee network to evaluate imaging performance on a 040GSE ultrasonic phantom.

sessions.title: AHF: High Frequency Devices

papers.title: Periodically Poled Lithium Tantalate Bulk Acoustic Wave Resonators for Frequency Range 3 (FR3)
papers.abstract: The growing demand for high-frequency and wideband RF filters in 5G or 6G communication systems requires advanced resonator technologies. However, further increases in operating frequency often degrade device performance due to frequency-dependent deterioration of physical and electrical properties, such as excessively thinned electrodes and piezoelectric films. Periodic polarity BAW resonators with higher order vibration modes can have higher resonant frequencies than conventional single layer BAW resonators. Periodic polarity BAW resonators can have improved frequency characteristics with thicker electrode and piezoelectric films than conventional single layer BAW resonators. In this study, we fabricated 4-layer LT BAW resonators and investigated the characteristics of those resonators via a vector network analyzer. The keff^2 is about 15% and Q values at resonant and anti-resonant frequencies are around 140. These results validate the effectiveness of high-order vibration modes in periodically poled LT BAW resonators and indicate their strong potential for high-frequency, wideband RF filters applications in FR3.

papers.title: Technological Considerations in Matching an Acoustic Wave Ladder Filter to a Dispersive Impedance
papers.abstract: The synthesis of filters is often carried out under the assumption that both the source and load terminations are constant impedances. However, in most practical BAW and SAW filter designs, this assumption does not hold, as filters are typically required to be matched to real devices with frequency-dependent complex impedances (Z_L(f)). This work analyzes how a direct synthesis method for designing general Chebyshev filters terminated with a Z_L(f) at one port affects the technology of an AW ladder filter. A dispersive impedance extracted from an RF front-end module is used to match the filter at different locations on the Smith chart to evaluate the impact on the AW technology and determine the most area-efficient region.

papers.title: Relaxing Resonator Coupling Requirements in a Wideband Ku-Band Acoustic Filter Using Reflection-Coefficient Phase-Controlled Synthesis
papers.abstract: This paper presents a reflection-coefficient phase-controlled synthesis method to relax resonator coupling requirements for wideband Ku-band acoustic filters. By leveraging phase tuning via non-resonating nodes (NS/NL) and external inductive compensation within a ladder topology, the proposed method significantly reduces the effective electromechanical coupling (keff2) demand on AlScN bulk acoustic wave (BAW) resonators. Unlike conventional ladder synthesis, which requires a keff2 up to 45%, the proposed design confines the requirement for all resonators to 20%, addressing a key limitation of AlScN technology. Simulation results demonstrate that the synthesized Ku-band filter achieves a 17.1% fractional bandwidth and superior impedance matching with significantly reduced S11 ripple compared to the reference design. This approach enables the realization of high-performance, wideband RF filters suitable for satellite front-ends using practical low-coupling resonators.

papers.title: Analysis of thickness-Shear Mode Resonance Properties of Piezoelectric Substrates with Periodic Void Structure
papers.abstract: Recent advancements have necessitated high-performance acoustic wave filters. A laterally-excited bulk-wave resonator (XBAR), with an aluminum interdigital transducer (Al-IDT) on a LiNbO3 (LN) thin plate, operates in the thickness-shear mode (TSM) and achieves a large electromechanical coupling factor K2. However, the freestanding LN thin plate structures are mechanically fragile. Studies have reported a bonded structure with periodic voids, exhibiting resonance properties similar to A1-mode Lamb wave. In this study, the resonance properties of the TSM of a bonded structure with periodic voids were analyzed using the finite element method. In the analytical model, an infinite-period Al-IDT was assumed on a bonded structure with periodic voids. A void was placed on the surface of the support substrate between adjacent electrodes. We investigated the effects of the void width-to-pitch ratio (w/p) and the support substrate. When SiO2 and AT90°X-quartz were used, the spurious responses were suppressed. As w/p increased, the resonance properties approached those of a single LN thin plate. When SiO2 was used at w/p=0.9, the bonded structure achieved a K2eff of 35.6% and a YR of 85 dB.

papers.title: Singular Value Decomposition Methods to Analyze the Impact of Layer Sensitivity on Figures of Merit in CRF BAW Devices
papers.abstract: This work presents an efficient methodology to evaluate the impact of individual layer variations on the key figures of merit (FoM) of SMR BAW filter performance. Using a global sensitivity representation of the filter response, Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) is applied to extract orthogonal modes that capture how groups of layers jointly influence device behavior. The dominant modes provide clear ranking of sensitivity contributions, enabling identification of the most critical layers and coupled layer groups. The approach is demonstrated on a 4th-order coupled resonator filter (CRF), evaluating sensitivity across center frequency, insertion loss, bandwidth, and return loss. The results identify critical layers for specific performance metrics and highlight candidates for frequency trimming during manufacturing. This framework supports robust tolerance definition, improving production yield, stability, and next-generation BAW filter performance.

papers.title: Flexible Transversal BAW Filters with Intrinsic Phase Cancellation
papers.abstract: Transversal electroacoustic filters form the response as the sum of several acoustic-resonator paths. Unlike ladder networks, they provide independent control of transmission-zero placement, impedance and resonant frequency, enabling wideband, multi-band and channelized responses with no dependence on resonator k2e. Their main implementation drawback is the 180º phase shift required between positive- and negative-sign paths, typically provided by a balun. This component increases loss, footprint and complexity in compact BAW front-ends. This work presents a balun-free transversal framework for achieving flexible advanced responses.

papers.title: Size Reduced Multilayer Piezoelectric Substrate Device
papers.abstract: Acoustic filter performance has a critical impact on overall RF module performance. A Multilayer Piezoelectric Substrate (MPS), in which a thin piezoelectric layer is bonded to a substrate, has been studied to improve Q, k², and TCF. MPS demonstrates excellent electrical performance; however, compared with standard SAW and TCSAW devices, the device size required to achieve the same impedance is increased due to the smaller static capacitance. The size of an acoustic filter is important for both tight floor planning and cost per die. For size reduction, high-mass-loading IDT electrodes have been applied to reduce acoustic wave velocity and increase the reflectivity of IDT fingers, thereby shortening the resonator length and reducing the number of reflector fingers. However, simply increasing IDT mass loading on MPS significantly increases energy leakage loss in the transverse direction. To mitigate this leakage loss, a 3D periodic FEM study was performed. The optimized structure achieves comparable performance to the finest TF-SAW devices while being 30% smaller than conventional TF-SAW designs.

sessions.title: ATF: Thin Film SAW Devices

papers.title: Propagation-Angle-Dependent Influence of PnCs on SH-SAW and LL-SAW Transmission in X-Cut LiNbO3/SiO2/SiC Delay Lines
papers.abstract: Surface acoustic wave devices on thin-film LiNbO3 are attractive for high-frequency applications because of their high phase velocity and large electromechanical coupling. On X-cut LiNbO3/SiO2/SiC, the in-plane propagation angle strongly affects the modal mixture of SH-SAW and LL-SAW. In this work, finite-element simulations are used to study circular-hole phononic crystal delay lines with identical geometry at representative mixed, LL-SAW-favored, and SH-SAW-favored angles. By comparing their transmission responses with reference delay lines without PnCs and analyzing displacement fields, we show that PnC-induced transmission loss is highly angle dependent. The results reveal selective suppression in different frequency regions and provide guidance for modal filtering and spurious-mode management.

papers.title: Theoretical and Experimental Study on the Nonlinear Behavior of SAW Propagation in Metal Thin-Film/Piezoelectric Substrate Structures
papers.abstract: In recent years, as telecommunications capacity has increased, the problem of intermodulation in surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices caused by material nonlinearity has become more apparent. Empirical evidence suggests that metal thin-film electrodes formed on piezoelectric substrates generate larger nonlinear waves than predicted using bulk nonlinear constants. Therefore, expressing the effective nonlinear constants of thin-film metal electrodes formed on a piezoelectric substrate in the form of correction factors for the bulk nonlinear constants is extremely important. To achieve the above objectives, we first established a rigorous theory in closed-form that enables quantitative analysis of the generation of second- and third-harmonic SAW waves on metal thin films deposited on piezoelectric substrates. Next, we measured the absolute values of the amplitude distributions of the second and third harmonics actually generated using the laser probe method. We analyzed the experimental results using the theory and determined the correction factors (multipliers) for the bulk nonlinear constants of the metal thin-film materials.
keywords: Correction factor for the bulk nonlinear constants

papers.title: High-Power n28F+n20 Duplexer Using Bonded-Wafer TCSAW with Dielectric Overcoat
papers.abstract: The authors combine buried‑electrode TCSAW with bonded wafer to improve power handling and design an n28F+n20 duplexer, using low‑cut LN for its large SH‑SAW k²eff. PE thickness is optimized considering frequency sensitivity, high‑order modes position & strength, and heat dissipation. Cut angle, IDT and TC thickness are tuned to suppress Rayleigh‑mode over a wide frequency range. IDT duty factor is tailored to enlarge k²eff and reflection. We use 170°YX-LN, set IDT thickness to normalized to ~9%. Thermal simulation shows clear improvement over regular TCSAW device. The flip chip CSP package achieves compact die and chip sizes of 1400×1000 and 1600×1200 μm², respectively. Frequency uniformity of bonded‑wafer TCSAW are slightly worse than that of regular TCSAW, particularly near the wafer edge, due to abnormal bonding. Except for several ripples near the Rx high channel, the S‑parameters are almost identical. The duplexers show typical IL of 2.2 dB for Tx and 2.4 dB for Rx, and isolation better than 55 dB. TCF test shows an improvement of 5 ppm/K at fs, owing to CTE compensation. Power handling test at 55°C under 5G-NR CP-OFDM signal shows enhancement of 2 dB.

papers.title: Low-loss, High Shape-Factor Filter Based on Optimized POI-SAW Resonators
papers.abstract: We adopt POI SAW technology and demonstrate a low-loss, high shape factor n50 filter. To accurately model POI SAW resonators, we modify the coupling-of-modes (COM) model by introducing frequency dependent Q loss and velocity. 3D FEM simulations are performed to investigate the influence of IDT tilt angle and rotation angle on device performance. Structural parameters (cut angle, IDT thickness and duty factor.) are optimized considering proper k2eff, frequency sensitivity, resistance, and transverse slowness curvature etc. In fabrication, the thin films are etched to prevent cracks from occurring during packaging stages such as bumping and dicing. The fabricated n50 filter achieves a high shape factor of BW15/BW2.5 <1.1, with typical insertion loss of 2 dB, and rejection better than 40 dB in GPS and sub 3 GHz cellular bands. Using a trimming process, the unilateral frequency uniformity is controlled within ±1 MHz, ensuring high yield. Measured TCF values are 14 and –9 ppm/K on the left and right roll-off sides, respectively. With low loss, high shape factor, and good TCF, this n50 filter is well suited for integration into 5G wireless devices.

papers.title: Buried-Electrode Surface Acoustic Wave: a High Velocity Mode for High Power UHB Applications
papers.abstract: This contribution addresses the design and manufacturing of Buried-Electrode Surface Acoustic Wave (BESAW) atop Piezoelectric-On-Insulator (POI) substrates operating above 3 GHz. The BESAW on POI exhibits an atypical vibration mainly located in the electrode of the grating. Its phase velocity well in excess of 10 km.s-1 is enabling the above frequency operation using I-line lithography for the production of industrial SAW filters. Radiation losses in the substrate are minimized using optimal grating dimensions. Mode operation is explained. First demonstration is reported with figures of Merit. Solution will be presented for their improvement.

papers.title: Design of Single Rayleigh Mode SAW Resonators Based on ScAlN Multilayer Structure
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a single-Rayleigh-mode surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonator based on a ScAlN/Mo/Au/SiO₂/Si multilayer POI structure. Au‑Au bonding technology was employed to transfer high‑quality ScAlN thin films and integrate an Au layer into the multilayer structure. Exploiting the Au layer with ultra-low acoustic velocity, this design facilitates the dissipation of high‑order mode energy within the layer rather than reflection back to the piezoelectric layer, effectively suppressing spurious responses. Finite element method (FEM) simulations using COMSOL were employed to optimize the layer thicknesses. The fabricated device (λ = 1.2 μm) exhibits an excellent single-mode characteristic.

papers.title: Transverse Mode Dispersion and Cut-Off in SH-SAW Strip Waveguides on X-Cut LNOI
papers.abstract: We map the transverse-mode dispersion of guided shear-horizontal surface acoustic waves (SH-SAW) on X-cut Y-propagating thin-film lithium niobate on insulator (LNOI) strip waveguides. Devices with five waveguide widths (W = 30, 15, 8, 4, 2 μm) are fabricated on commercial LNOI and characterized by VNA S-parameter measurements. At W = 30 μm, three transverse-mode orders—fundamental, 2nd-, and 3rd-order SH-SAW—are resolved within the IDT passband. As W decreases, higher-order modes cut off first and fall below the noise floor; at W = 8 μm only the fundamental survives, and at W ≤ 4 μm the fundamental itself is cut off. 3D finite-element analysis confirms that each mode evolves from well-confined to leaky as W decreases through its cut-off, with higher-order modes cutting off at larger W than the fundamental. These results establish the W-dependent cut-off hierarchy of guided SH-SAW modes on X-cut LNOI and identify the single-mode regime for transverse-mode-engineered acoustic devices.

papers.title: Hybridizable Discontinuous Galerkin Discretization for Hierarchical Cascading Surface Acoustic Wave Devices Simulation
papers.abstract: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) filters are key RF front-end components in 5G systems, but accurate simulation of multilayer TCSAW and IHP-SAW devices remains costly for conventional FEM-HCT solvers due to globally coupled volume unknowns and refined meshes near thin interfaces. This work proposes a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin hierarchical cascade technique (HDG-HCT). HDG locally eliminates element-interior displacement and electric-potential unknowns by static condensation, leaving only face-trace unknowns globally coupled through numerical fluxes and embedded into HCT. For a 2D TCSAW resonator over 401 frequency points, HDG-HCT reproduces the FEM-HCT admittance spectrum without observable resonance shift. A fourth-order HDG model reduces runtime from 183.3 to 29 min, achieving a 6.3× speedup with frequency error below 0.06%. On a 27-element coarse mesh, runtime further decreases to 4.6 min with 1443 trace DoFs, yielding 86% fewer unknowns and a 40× speedup while keeping frequency error below 0.12%. For an IHP-SAW with an 80 nm SiO₂ layer, HDG reduces the field-profile error to 0.008 ppm, versus 431–564 ppm for FEM.
keywords: hybridizable discontinuous galerkin， hierarchical cascade technique

papers.title: Guided SAW Mode Imaging of Phononic Integrated Circuit Components via Laser Doppler Vibrometry
papers.abstract: Laser Doppler vibrometry is used to directly image guided surface acoustic wave mode behavior in ScAlN-on-SiC phononic integrated circuit components, including spirals and splitters, providing the first experimental validation of simulated displacement field distributions across a PnIC component library. The resulting displacement field maps identify loss mechanisms at critical junctions and bends, offering a direct experimental reference for numerically guided component optimization.

sessions.title: QUASOS Challenge Poster Session

papers.topicName: Technical Challenge: Quantitative Ultrasound Estimation of Attenuation and Speed-of-Sound
papers.title: Coherence-Based Estimation of Sound Speed and Attenuation from RF Ultrasound Data
papers.abstract: Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) aims to characterize tissue microstructure by estimating acoustic parameters such as sound speed and attenuation from raw radiofrequency (RF) channel data, thereby improving image quality and diagnostic value. In practice, however, these estimates are often affected by tissue layers, aberration, and noise, which can reduce lesion detectability. In this work, we explore a framework for estimating variations in sound speed and attenuation directly from RF ultrasound data. The approach is guided by signal coherence and is designed with an emphasis on robustness and stable performance.

papers.topicName: Technical Challenge: Quantitative Ultrasound Estimation of Attenuation and Speed-of-Sound
papers.title: Differentiable Beamforming for Sound Speed Estimation Using SVD-Based Phase Coherence
papers.abstract: Sound-speed (SoS) distribution is a quantitative acoustic property that can serve as both a tissue biomarker and a prior for aberration correction. This work introduces singular-value-decomposition-based phase error (SVDPE) within a differentiable beamforming framework to estimate SoS maps directly from full-matrix RF data provided by the QUASOS challenge. The SoS map was parameterized as 2D map. For the given map, transmit and receive delays were computed by straight-ray slowness integration and applied in delay-and-sum beamforming. SVDPE was evaluated patch-wise using sliding transmit subapertures of 20 events with 25% overlap across 128 transmits, then minimized with anisotropic total-variation regularization after constant-speed initialization. Across datasets from Groups A, C, and D, the estimated SoS maps showed group-dependent patterns consistent with expected phantom structures. Homogeneous Group A produced uniform maps, Group C showed broader SoS variation in highly attenuating multilayer media, and Group D recovered layer and circular-inclusion differences corresponding well with B-mode images.

papers.topicName: Technical Challenge: Quantitative Ultrasound Estimation of Attenuation and Speed-of-Sound
papers.title: Dual-Branch Implicit Neural Representation for High-Resolution Sound Speed Mapping in Pulse-Echo Ultrasound
papers.abstract: This work introduces a dual-branch implicit neural representation (DB-INR) network for fast and high-resolution sound speed mapping in pulse-echo ultrasound. On the QUASOS challenge dataset, this approach produced sound speed maps with fewer stripe-like artifacts than grid-based optimization and remained stable at higher grid density.

papers.topicName: Technical Challenge: Quantitative Ultrasound Estimation of Attenuation and Speed-of-Sound
papers.title: The Challenges and Rewards of Generating the Quantitative Ultrasound Estimation of Attenuation and Speed-Of-Sound (QUASOS) Challenge Data
papers.abstract: The Quantitative Ultrasound estimation of Attenuation and Speed-Of-Sound (QUASOS) Challenge was created to provide a standardized and rigorous benchmark for evaluating quantitative ultrasound (QUS) methods for estimating tissue attenuation and speed of sound, addressing persistent errors caused by intervening tissues. The organizers generated a large, diverse dataset using carefully calibrated physical phantoms and realistic full-wave simulations, including both aberrated and unaberrated conditions with two clinical transducers. In total, 1,554 randomized datasets were released without training labels to encourage fair algorithm comparison. The challenge attracted broad international participation from academia, industry, and government, highlighting strong global interest in QUS validation. Despite the complexity and stress of data generation, the effort was deemed rewarding, producing a valuable open dataset expected to support future QUS research and method development.

papers.topicName: Technical Challenge: Quantitative Ultrasound Estimation of Attenuation and Speed-of-Sound
papers.title: Adaptive, Automated Optimization of Attenuation Calculations in Tissues with High Variance of Complexity
papers.abstract: Acoustic attenuation coefficient estimation via conventional spectral log-difference methods suffers from resolution-stability trade-offs and depth-dependent biases. This study proposes an adaptive QUS framework combining frequency-matched multistatic beamforming with dynamic spectral window optimization to improve attenuation mapping across diverse tissue morphologies. The two-stage pipeline first stabilizes beamformed channel data across transducer geometries, then selects optimal window sizes based on local signal statistics. Evaluated on the QUASOS Challenge dataset, the adaptive approach yielded visual consistency of attenuation maps compared to conventional fixed-parameter methods. Full quantitative validation against ground truth is planned upon final dataset release.

papers.topicName: Technical Challenge: Quantitative Ultrasound Estimation of Attenuation and Speed-of-Sound
papers.title: Speed of Sound Mapping Using Common mid-Angle Echo Phase shift: QUASOS Results
papers.abstract: This contribution to the QUASOS challenge investigates speed of sound (SoS) reconstruction using an echo phase shift-based approach: echoes are probed with collimated transmit (Tx) and receive (Rx) beams for a multitude of angle combinations, and echo phase shift determined between angle pairs sharing the same mid-angle. SoS is reconstructed via the pseudo-inverse of a linear ray-based forward model. To improve accuracy, the method was combined with an automatic beamforming SoS selection, and an automatic identification of depth-dependent center frequency. While this method works well in the simulation group D despite typical interference-related artifacts below inclusions, the physical examples A are challenging due to strong attenuation leading to excessive noise, and group C was hard to analyze because the surface aberrators lead to random echo phase shift values at depth.

papers.topicName: Technical Challenge: Quantitative Ultrasound Estimation of Attenuation and Speed-of-Sound
papers.title: Ultrasound Attenuation Estimation via Ensemble Reference Averaging and Self Contrastive Learning
papers.abstract: For the QUASOS Challenge, we propose a pipeline combining conventional attenuation estimation methods with different references and parameters with a zero-shot deep learning framework. To mitigate reference-side speckle, we compute log-spectral differences against an ensemble of 10 independent homogeneous references. A global Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) filter is then applied to suppress uncorrelated noise. Diverse attenuation maps are generated by varying parameters. These initial estimates are refined using a Self-Contrastive Learning network that encodes features into distinct "clean" and "noise" latent spaces, decoding exclusively from the clean space. Optimized via a self-supervised, test-time training (TTT) loop, this framework disentangles physical attenuation gradients from speckle artifacts without ground-truth labels. Preliminary evaluations demonstrate improved homogeneity in uniform regions with on reference dataset.

papers.topicName: Technical Challenge: Quantitative Ultrasound Estimation of Attenuation and Speed-of-Sound
papers.title: Physics-Based Optimization of the speed-of-Sound in pulse-Echo mode: Sneaking Through Local minima
papers.abstract: We propose a new Speed of Sound (SOS) estimation method based on the optimization of wave focusing in heterogeneous media. Our approach exploits a wave propagation model that goes beyond the straight-ray approximation and fully encompasses refraction and diffraction effects. In particular, we study the local minima of the cost function and propose techniques to avoid or suppress them, such as the separation of the SOS map into an axial profile and a residual map and a Lagrangian relaxation of the resulting constraints. The use of an advanced propagation model combined with such optimization techniques enables the measurement of SOS variations of more than 100 m/s with a spatial resolution of a few wavelengths.
keywords: Physics-based optimization of the speed-of-sound in pulse-echo mode: Sneaking through local minima

papers.topicName: Technical Challenge: Quantitative Ultrasound Estimation of Attenuation and Speed-of-Sound
papers.title: Accurate Pulse-Echo Speed-of-Sound Estimation for the QUASOS Challenge
papers.abstract: Knowledge of the tissue SoS both improves image quality and serves as a biomarker for health, and it is critical to estimate the SoS using the same pulse-echo paradigm as conventional ultrasound. One overlooked effect in pulse-echo SoS estimation arises from the array lens, where SoS mismatch between the lens and medium can lead to ToF errors and, consequently, reduced estimation accuracy. Given homogeneous SoS reference phantoms, we estimated the lens SoS and thickness of the L7-4 and L11-5 arrays by minimizing SoS estimation variance across depth. Using this lens information, we then adopted a segment-then-estimate approach to generate SoS maps for the challenge data. We observed consistent SoS minima across depth when the lens was appropriately modelled, while the uncorrected loss only converged to the reference SoS at lower imaging depths. Overall, our work highlights the importance of modelling the array lens for maximizing SoS estimation accuracy, as accuracy is essential when using the SoS as a biomarker for tissue diagnostics.

papers.topicName: Technical Challenge: Quantitative Ultrasound Estimation of Attenuation and Speed-of-Sound
papers.title: Attenuation Coefficient Estimation Using Enhanced Reference Frequency Method with Homomorphic Filtering: the 2026 QUASOS Challenge
papers.abstract: characterization and quantitative ultrasound (QUS). While the Reference Frequency Method (RFM) offers a system-independent approach to ACE, it often suffers from spectral oscillations due to multiple-scatterer interference, leading to significant estimation variance. This study proposes an enhanced RFM integrated with homomorphic filtering to provide stable and accurate specific attenuation estimates.

papers.topicName: Technical Challenge: Quantitative Ultrasound Estimation of Attenuation and Speed-of-Sound
papers.title: Coherence-Anchored Spatial-Domain Reconstruction of Speed-of-Sound from Full-Matrix Pulse-Echo Ultrasound Data
papers.abstract: A GPU-accelerated spatial-domain reconstruction (SDR) pipeline is submitted to the 2026 QUASOS challenge for pulse-echo speed-of-sound (SoS) imaging from full-matrix-capture data. Three plane waves at 0° and ±20° are beamformed, ZNCC-tracked between 0°-anchored pairs, and inverted by an ℓ1-data ADMM with multi-angle anisotropic total-variation regularization on a 0.30 mm grid. Two extensions address known SDR failure modes: a per-column 2-D cumulative-mean coherence-factor anchor that constrains absolute SoS at every lateral coordinate using axial CF maximization, energy-balanced against the τ rows; and a depth-Hessian re-conditioning of the anchor block that restores the data Hessian's diagonal at depth without enlarging the prior. Beamforming, tracking, CF sweep, and ADMM run fully on the GPU in OpenCL; the full evaluable challenge batch reconstructs in ≈2.5 h on two consumer GPUs. SoS maps for every evaluable dataset across both probes and all groups have been submitted; quantitative ranking is deferred to the organisers' evaluation.

papers.topicName: Technical Challenge: Quantitative Ultrasound Estimation of Attenuation and Speed-of-Sound
papers.title: Constrained 2D ADMM for Robust Attenuation Estimation in Pulse-Echo Quantitative Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) attenuation estimation is widely used for tissue characterization but remains sensitive to spectral noise, limited window size, and spatial inconsistency. We propose a two-dimensional constrained ADMM (2D C-ADMM) framework for attenuation estimation using normalized power spectra with reference phantom calibration. RF data are reconstructed into B-mode images via total focusing method (TFM) beamforming, and local spectra are estimated using windowing and multi-taper spectral estimation to improve robustness to noise. The problem is formulated as a global inverse model, enforcing spatial consistency through 2D regularization across depth and lateral directions. The method is evaluated on multiple QUASOS challenge datasets. For datasets with visible inclusions, CNR ranges from 0.35 to 0.55, while more challenging cases show lower contrast (CNR ≈ 0.05 to 0.1). ROI analysis yields consistent attenuation estimates with mean values of 0.10–0.7 dB/cm/MHz and variance on the order of 10⁻³, demonstrating stable performance.

papers.topicName: Technical Challenge: Quantitative Ultrasound Estimation of Attenuation and Speed-of-Sound
papers.title: Learning Speed-of-Sound via Physically Consistent RF Reconstruction and Image-Domain Constraints in Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: Most conventional beamforming methods in Ultrasound (US), including plane wave and focused imaging, assume a constant and homogeneous speed of sound (SoS). In reality, SoS varies across tissues due to differences in composition and density. This mismatch degrades image quality, causing blurring, speckle decorrelation, reduced lesion visibility, and other aberrations. Accurate SoS estimation improves beamforming, supports downstream tasks such as speckle tracking, quantitative US, and tissue characterization, and enables adaptive beamforming and aberration correction. In this work, we estimate SoS from full transmit RF data by jointly standardizing image- and RF-domain representations into a geometrically consistent form.

sessions.title: MEL: Clinical Oncology and Reproductive Organ Imaging

papers.title: Can Erectile Dysfunction Evaluation Be Performed Using Ultrasound Imaging Without an Intracavernosal Injection of a Vasoactive Agent?
papers.abstract: This study investigated the use of microflow Doppler (cSMI and mSMI) and shear wave elastography (SWE) as novel techniques for evaluating erectile dysfunction (ED) in subjects undergoing penile ultrasound pre and post intracavernosal injection (ICI) of a vasoactive agent to compare the ultrasound results to observe if similar findings can be found pre and post injection. The results are encouraging indicating that the use of mSMI and SWE in a no injection examination (i.e., in the flaccid penis) may be a way to indicate ED. The mSMI and SWE imaging modes may be able to identify characteristics consistent with ED in the flaccid penis facilitating clinical practice for providers and improving patient experience.

papers.title: Investigating intratumoural Variations in Bladder Tumour Stiffness Using Vibrational Shear Wave elastography (VSWE) and its Relationship with Stromal Collagen Architecture
papers.abstract: The presented work sought to investigate the underlying contribution collagen to spatial variations in tumour stiffness in bladder cancer models models utilising a vibration-based shear wave elastography (VSWE) method to quantify the biomechanical properties of tumours together with histological interrogation. VSWE and picrosirius red histology images of tumours were segmented into three subregions core, inner rim, and outer rim, for shear wave speed (SWS) and collagen analysis within regions. VSWE imaging revealed differences in spatial distribution of SWS measurements across different subregions, with histological analysis showing differences in total collagen correlating with mean SWS measurements within the subregions.

papers.title: Growing Indenter Anisotropy Imaging (GIAnI) Enables in Vivo Differentiation of Malignant and Benign Breast Masses
papers.abstract: Breast tumors and surrounding tissue differ in structural organization between benign and malignant cases, producing variations in shear elastic anisotropy that may serve as a diagnostic biomarker. Growing Indenter Anisotropy Imaging (GIAnI) is a novel ultrasound elastography technique that enables two-dimensional (2D) point-wise imaging of shear anisotropy using paired confocal acoustic radiation force excitations, where the sum of absolute differences (SAD) between the resulting displacement profiles spatially resolves anisotropy. We hypothesize that GIAnI-derived 2D shear anisotropy can differentiate malignant from benign breast masses in vivo. GIAnI imaging was performed in 54 women with BI-RADS 4–5 breast masses (38 benign, 16 malignant). Tumor and background regions were delineated to extract tumor SAD, background SAD, and the tumor-to-background SAD ratio. The tumor-to-background ratio significantly differentiated malignant from benign lesions (p < 0.05) and achieved an AUC of 0.79 (IQR 0.71–0.86). These results demonstrate that GIAnI provides clinically relevant 2D anisotropy imaging and supports its potential as a noninvasive tool for characterizing breast masses.

papers.title: Correlation of 4T1 and CT26 Tumor Volume with Ultrasound Shear Wave Elastography
papers.abstract: B-mode ultrasound (US), radiofrequency data, and shear wave elastography (SWE) offer a noninvasive, accessible approach to longitudinally track tumor growth and tissue mechanical properties. This study aimed to quantify tumor mechanical properties across two tumor types with distinct immune phenotypes to support development of predictive biomarkers for immunotherapy efficacy. 5 BALB/c mice per murine cancer cell line (CT26 and 4T1) were implanted with bilateral flank tumors. Functional imaging was performed on days 10, 13/14, and 15/18. SWE US imaging was conducted using a 29 MHz probe on the Fujifilm VisualSonics F2 system. 4T1 tumors exhibited more rapid growth than CT26 tumors and maintained higher stiffness across all timepoints (Panel C, D), with final mean stiffness values of 46.5 ± 3.46 kPa versus 28.66 ± 3.34 kPa (p = 0.001). Tumor volume and stiffness showed a statistically significant, moderate positive linear correlation (Panel E, F; 4T1: r = 0.52, p = 0.003; CT26: r = 0.638, p = 0.0001). This method highlights the potential of using SWE to provide complementary insights into tumor dynamics during treatment.

papers.title: ARFI Displacement Imaging for Ex Vivo Mechanical Characterization of Brain Metastases in a 4T1 Breast Cancer Mouse Model
papers.abstract: Tissue viscoelasticity provides information beyond elasticity, with viscosity reflecting tissue composition, fluidity, and microstructural remodeling. Existing shear wave–based methods often require large spatial averaging and are limited in heterogeneous tissues, while Viscoelastic Response ultrasound requires computationally intensive pixel-wise model fitting. This study develops a machine-learning pipeline to estimate inclusion-to-background elasticity and viscosity ratios directly from ARFI-derived on-axis temporal and velocity features, enabling automated viscoelastic mapping without pixel-wise mechanical model fitting.

sessions.title: MIM: Clinical AI - Segmentation & Diagnostic Applications

papers.title: foundation model, lung ultrasound, pseudo-mask refinement, Segment Anything Model, semi-supervised learning
papers.abstract: Lung ultrasound (LUS) enables real-time pulmonary assessment using reverberation artifacts such as A-lines, B-lines, and consolidation. However, LUS biomarker segmentation remains challenging due to the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and artifact-driven characteristics, which make accurate annotation difficult and limit the availability of labeled data. We propose BM-SAM, a semi-supervised pseudo-mask refinement framework based on a mean teacher–student model. Coarse pseudo-masks generated by the teacher are refined using a SAM-based refiner that exploits foundation model priors. The refined pseudo-masks, weighted by IoU-based confidence, supervise the student model, while the teacher is updated through an exponential moving average (EMA). Additionally, patch-wise augmentation based on uncertainty maps is applied to improve training stability. Experiments on 100 LUS images demonstrate that BM-SAM outperforms CNN-based, semi-supervised, and SAM-based methods, achieving the highest IoU (0.76) and mDice (0.86), with improved segmentation accuracy and stable convergence.

papers.title: Workflow-Oriented Deep Learning for Standard-View Recognition and Multi-Organ Segmentation in Upper Abdominal Ultrasound
papers.abstract: This study evaluates a workflow-oriented deep learning pipeline for upper abdominal ultrasound, using standard-view recognition as an upstream quality-gating step before multi-organ segmentation. A retrospective dataset was built from real-world examination videos acquired with commercial ultrasound systems. Among 521 videos, 465 were eligible, yielding 5,535 expert-reviewed images representing 12 standard views of the liver, gallbladder, pancreas, and spleen. A nested subset of 4,255 standard-view images was manually annotated for visible organs, including the liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, and right kidney. ResNeSt-50 was trained for 12-class standard-view recognition, and HRNet-W48 for multiclass semantic segmentation, with all splits performed at the case level. On the held-out test set, standard-view recognition achieved 97.00% accuracy, 97.08% precision, 97.00% recall, and 99.70% specificity. Segmentation achieved high IoU for the liver, gallbladder, and right kidney, moderate IoU for the spleen, and lower IoU for the pancreas. These results support the feasibility of view-gated analysis for more stable downstream ultrasound image interpretation.

papers.title: Feasibility of AI-Assisted Fracture Detection on Volumetric Ultrasound
papers.abstract: X-ray is the standard of care for suspected extremity fractures in the emergency department, yet most cases are negative, contributing to radiology backlog, wait times, and cost. Bedside ultrasound may enable faster fracture assessment. This study evaluated the feasibility of AI-assisted fracture detection on volumetric ultrasound of the wrist. A YOLO model was trained to detect fractures in 2D sagittal slices from 3D wrist ultrasound scans acquired with a custom probe and beamformer. In an IRB-approved study, scans were collected from 130 subjects and annotated by experts with reference to available x-ray data. The model was trained on 80 subjects and tested on 50 subjects. A multi-reader, multi-case (MRMC) study was performed with nine physicians with novice or fellowship-level ultrasound experience. Combining physician and AI predictions increased specificity while maintaining similar sensitivity as the fellowship-trained cohort. Combined predictions improved AUC significantly, suggesting that AI trained on a limited dataset can approach physician-level performance and may improve ultrasound-based fracture detection as a decision-support tool.

papers.title: Deep Learning Based on Dual-Modality Ultrasound Videos for Superficial Lymphadenopathy: a Multicenter Study
papers.abstract: Background, Motivation and Objective Superficial lymphadenopathy (LA) diagnosis remains challenging due to imaging feature overlap. Prior studies lack multicenter validation. We aimed to develop a deep learning model using dual-modality ultrasound videos for accurate LA diagnosis. Statement of Contribution/Methods A deep learning model (DMUVL-DiagNet) was trained on retrospective dual-modality videos (n=1616) from five hospitals for two tasks: benign vs. malignant (Task I) and lymphoma vs. metastasis (Task II). External validation used prospective videos (n=454) and static images (n=1956). An eight-radiologist reader study assessed AI assistance. Results/Discussion In 4026 patients, the model achieved AUCs of 0.905-0.949 (Task I) and 0.870-0.907 (Task II), outperforming average radiologists. AI assistance improved junior radiologists' AUC from 0.716 to 0.876 (Task I) and 0.579 to 0.772 (Task II) (P<0.01), reaching senior-level performance. The model shows strong generalizability and clinical promise.

papers.title: HMUVL-Net: a Hierarchical Multimodal Ultrasound Video Network for Lymphadenopathy Diagnosis
papers.abstract: This study presents HMUVL-Net, a hierarchical multimodal ultrasound video network for lymphadenopathy diagnosis. The framework integrates B-mode ultrasound, color Doppler flow imaging, strain elastography, contrast-enhanced ultrasound, and clinical data to support stepwise clinical decision-making. Representative video frames are selected using HOG descriptors and grayscale variation, while a CNN-Transformer-Mamba backbone captures local texture, global spatial context, and temporal dynamics. A mixture-of-experts module separates shared and modality-specific features, allowing inference when advanced modalities are unavailable, and a clinical-prior-guided gating module adaptively weights modalities across diagnostic stages. The model was evaluated on 200,880 key-frame images from 8,087 patients across eight centers and 11 scanner manufacturers. HMUVL-Net achieved strong performance for benign/malignant differentiation, subtype classification, and metastatic origin prediction, and improved radiologist performance in a 300-case reader study. These results suggest potential for noninvasive, consistent, and stepwise LA diagnosis.

papers.title: Ultrasound Image Classification via Mask-Guided Learning for Standardized Liver Cancer Screening
papers.abstract: Standardized liver ultrasound acquisition for national liver cancer screening is highly operator-dependent. This study proposes a mask-guided gate ResNet (MGG-ResNet) that incorporates liver segmentation masks to improve standard scan plane classification. The liver mask is decomposed into inner, boundary, and outer regions, and mask-derived features are converted into sigmoid gating signals to modulate ResNet feature maps. Using 10,873 images from 10 standard scan planes and one non-defined class, MGG-ResNet achieved 73.91% accuracy and 73.10% macro-F1. It improved accuracy/macro-F1 by 3.43%/4.11% over image+mask ResNet-34 and by 6.20%/6.88% over image-only ResNet-34. Grad-CAM showed attention to clinically relevant anatomical structures, supporting robust real-time QA for liver ultrasound screening.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal Deep Learning for Thyroid Nodule Classification Using Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Accurate thyroid nodule classification is challenging due to inter-reader variability and limited performance of single-modality ultrasound (US). Integrating B-mode, shear wave elastography (SWE), and color Doppler (CD) provides complementary structural, stiffness, and vascular information, but most deep learning (DL) methods fail to fully exploit multimodal data or account for varying modality reliability. We propose an uncertainty-aware multimodal DL framework for robust thyroid nodule classification. Each modality is processed by an independent network with a pretrained MobileNetV2 backbone and lightweight head using depth-wise separable convolutions, mixed pooling, and self-attention to capture local and global features. Modality-specific malignancy probabilities are fused using an uncertainty-aware strategy based on Monte Carlo Dropout, assigning higher weights to more confident predictions. Evaluated on 422 patients with fivefold cross-validation, the method achieved 95% accuracy, 98% sensitivity, and AUC of 0.97, outperforming single modalities and conventional fusion. It surpassed existing networks with low complexity, enabling near real-time, robust clinical deployment.

papers.title: Diffusion-Based Anomaly Detection for Unsupervised Carotid Plaque Segmentation in Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of mortality, with carotid plaque being a major risk factor for stroke. Ultrasound is widely used for carotid assessment but is affected by operator dependency and image variability. This study introduces an unsupervised, reconstruction-based framework for annotation-free carotid plaque detection and segmentation using a denoising diffusion implicit model (DDIM). The model is trained exclusively on healthy carotid ultrasound images to learn the characteristics of normal vascular tissue. During inference, reconstructed images are compared with the input to generate residual maps that highlight abnormal regions. Evaluated on longitudinal carotid ultrasound images, the proposed framework achieved a Dice score of 0.801, an IoU of 0.684, and a pixel accuracy of 0.914, while demonstrating clear separation between plaque and normal tissue. These findings demonstrate the potential of DDIM-based reconstruction for accurate, annotation-free plaque detection and segmentation, reducing reliance on manually labelled pathological data and supporting scalable automated carotid assessment.

papers.title: Respiration-Anchored and Self-Measurement-Aware Foundation Model Adaptation for Inferior Vena Cava Segmentation
papers.abstract: Dynamic ultrasound requires stable Inferior Vena Cava (IVC) lumen segmentation for respiratory diameter tracking and collapse-index estimation, but direct use of promptable foundation models is limited by respiration-induced shape changes, weak boundaries, and unstable measurements. We propose a respiration-anchor guided and self-measurement-aware weakly supervised framework based on MedSAM2. First-frame red-line cues are converted into point and box prompts to generate coarse masks M0(t). The initial diameter curve D0(t) is used to locate maximum, minimum, and intermediate respiration-anchor windows. Conservative second-pass prompts are built from temporal-consensus cores, robust boxes, center positive points, and exterior negative points. A measurement-aware prompt genetic algorithm optimizes prompts using cue consistency, temporal consistency, diameter smoothness, area stability, and measurement-success rate, producing final masks M1(t), diameter extrema, and collapse-index estimates. The proposed method achieves the best average Dice score of 0.885, outperforming MedSAM2, nnU-Net, SAM2, USFM, and TransUNet.

sessions.title: MIS: Beamforming & Array Processing

papers.title: Volumetric transcranial Ultrasound of the Human Brain Using a Matrix Array – a Pilot Study
papers.abstract: Conventional transcranial Doppler (TCD) and color Doppler (TCCD) are limited by operator dependence and a restriction to 1D or single 2D planes, which necessitates careful manual probe positioning. Volumetric transcranial ultrasound mitigates these constraints by enabling comprehensive 3D duplex imaging. This study demonstrates the in vivo feasibility of volumetric B-mode and power Doppler imaging through the temporal acoustic window of the human brain using a matrix array. To achieve this, volumetric imaging sequences were developed on a Verasonics Vantage NXT 256 system equipped with a multiplexed 2 MHz matrix-array probe. Initial results demonstrated that the B-mode volumes delineated key anatomical landmarks across multiple slices, including the third ventricle and thalami. Concurrently, the volumetric power Doppler resolved blood flow signals near the skull base and within the midbrain region, highlighting the clinical potential of volumetric transcranial ultrasound.

papers.title: SIMD-Accelerated Simulation of Ultrasound Fields for Large Scale Arrays
papers.abstract: FieldII has long been the standard for transducer simulation in array and image sequence work. It approximates surface integrals by subdividing transducers into finite 'physical elements' and representing scattering media as individual scatterers. In linear acoustics, each element and scatterer can be calculated independently, making the process highly parallelizable for Single-Instruction-Multiple-Data (SIMD) computing. Modern CPUs and GPUs are designed with SIMD in mind. While FieldII has parallel capabilities, it doesn't fully exploit modern computing devices. We present an open-source alternative leveraging GPU parallelism and SIMD-accelerated CPUs, with C-compatible bindings for integration beyond MATLAB.

papers.title: An Open-Source Pulse Sequencing Toolkit for Utilizing Row Column Arrays on Vantage Ultrasound Research Platforms for Streamlined 2D and 3D Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: Row Column Arrays (RCAs), including Bias-sensitive RCAs, enable volumetric ultrasound imaging with far fewer channels than fully addressed 2D arrays. However, the absence of standardized software tooling limits adoption. We present an open-source MATLAB framework to streamline 2D and 3D imaging with (bias-sensitive) RCAs on the Verasonics Vantage (NXT) 256, designed so a novice user can begin imaging within a single day. The framework interfaces with the Verasonics MATLAB API and a custom biasing electronics API. An open-source GPU beamformer enables real-time reconstruction, and a boilerplate system lets users define custom imaging sequences with minimal effort. Validated across three institutions, the framework supports 10+ imaging schemes including TPW, VLS, and FORCES, with real-time GPU beamforming at 5.5 vol/s over 3.8 million points. Full documentation and user guides accompany the release, providing the ultrasound community with a robust, extensible, and beginner-friendly toolkit for RCA imaging on the Verasonics platform.

papers.title: High-Spatiotemporal Resolution 3D Ultrasound Imaging Using a Multi-Scale Deep Learning Framework
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) ultrasound imaging with matrix transducers is valuable for cardiovascular assessment but suffers from a trade‑off between volume rate and image quality. Multi‑angle coherent compounding improves resolution but reduces temporal resolution and increases hardware cost. To address this, we propose MS²RE‑Net, a two‑stage deep learning framework that reconstructs high‑quality 3D vascular volumes from single‑angle transmission data. Validation on simulated, in‑vitro and in‑vivo datasets shows that MS²RE‑Net preserves fine anatomical details (e.g., plaque boundaries, residual lumens). It achieves a robust PSNR of 27.51 ± 3.08 dB in‑vivo with stable metric distribution. Notably, its image quality is equivalent to 6×6 or 7×7 coherent compounding, while providing a 24.6× processing speed‑up. This work enables real‑time, high‑fidelity 3D dynamic imaging on low‑channel systems, lowering hardware barriers without compromising diagnostic precision.

papers.title: Assessing Encoder Design for Sparse-to-Dense Ultrasound RF Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Sparse ultrasound RF acquisition can reduce data transfer and hardware burden, but missing receive-channel data can degrade RF reconstruction and introduce beamforming artifacts. This work studies how encoder design affects sparse-to-dense RF interpolation in a standard U-Net-style framework. Two encoders were compared: CAFormer, a hybrid encoder with convolutional and token-mixing components, and HGNetV2, a purely convolutional encoder. Both were tailored to the RF input dimensions and trained using 2560 RF samples with a 9:1 train-test split. A randomized decimation strategy sampled rates from ×2 to ×8 during training, making these rates in-distribution, while ×9 to ×13 were held out as more challenging out-of-distribution cases. Reconstruction quality was evaluated using SSIM between predicted and reference RF data. HGNetV2 and CAFormer performed similarly for ×2 to ×8, with average SSIM values of approximately 0.966 and 0.963. For ×9 to ×13, CAFormer achieved higher average SSIM, approximately 0.955 compared with 0.923 for HGNetV2, and showed better preservation of structures with fewer grating-lobe artifacts.

papers.title: A Compound Multi-Angle Diverging Wave Imaging Method Based on Variable-Angle Transducers
papers.abstract: Background & Objective: Cerebral hemodynamics robustly map neuronal activity. To overcome the narrow field of view (FOV) of conventional Doppler ultrasound, we propose a variable-angle transducer compound multi-angle diverging wave imaging method for real-time, wide-FOV monitoring of cerebral blood volume (CBV) dynamics. Methods: First, subarray 1 is activated individually. Using its geometric center as the origin, it transmits diverging waves at steering angles ranging from -30° to 30° (in 10° increments) and records the corresponding backscattered echoes locally. Subarray 2 then repeats this process. The final wide-FOV image is generated by spatially compounding these independent echoes. Global signal intensity at point (X, Z) fuses local signals R_{S1} and R_{S2}: I(X, Z) = c_1 * R_{S1}(X, Z) + c_2 * R_{S2}(X, Z). Results: Using the Field II platform, we simulated the scanning of a digital vascular branch phantom by dual 7 MHz phased arrays. This yielded wide-FOV B-mode and Power Doppler images, validating the method's efficacy in expanding FOV and tracking hemodynamics, and establishing a solid foundation for future physical phantom and in vivo studies.

papers.title: Diverging Beam Synthetic Aperture Technique for Convex Arrays in the Fourier Domain (ω–k) Algorithm : Preliminary Results
papers.abstract: Beamforming is fundamental to ultrasound imaging, with Delay-and-Sum (DAS) being the most commonly used time-domain approach. However, DAS is computationally intensive. The Fourier-domain (Omega–Wavenumber) algorithm offers an efficient alternative, reducing computational burden while improving image quality, as demonstrated in focused and plane-wave imaging. This study aims to develop and evaluate an ω–k beamforming method for diverging beam synthetic aperture imaging using a convex array, and to compare its performance with DAS in terms of contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), resolution, and computational efficiency. The proposed method adapts the ω–k algorithm to account for the curved geometry of a convex transducer. Ultrasound images reconstructed using ω–k algorithm were compared with DAS. At 40 mm depth, axial/lateral resolutions were 53.98/99.94 mm (DAS) and 56.2/87.80 mm (ω–k), respectively. The ω–k approach showed improved contrast, with CR of 0.865 and CNR of 5 dB versus 0.353 and 2.59 dB for DAS. Additionally, computation time in MATLAB was reduced from ~256 s (DAS) to ~4 s (ω–k), achieving ~50× speed improvement.

papers.title: ACCU-Net: Angle-Conditioned and Coordinate-Aware Attention U-Net for Single-Angle Plane-Wave Image Reconstruction
papers.abstract: To address the trade-off between image quality and frame rate in plane-wave imaging, we propose an Angle-Conditioned and Coordinate-aware attention U-Net (ACCU-Net), a physics-informed network operating on B-mode images. The model integrates 3 components: (1) FiLM-based angle conditioning, where steering angles are encoded via a multi-layer perceptron and injected into feature maps; (2) spatial coordinate encoding using normalized axial and lateral maps to model spatially variant degradation; and (3) an ultrasound-specific perceptual loss based on a pretrained Ultrasound Foundation Model (USFM). On cyst phantoms, ACCU-Net achieves CR: 2.70 dB, gCNR: 0.643, PSNR: 21.19 dB, and SSIM: 0.579, outperforming U-Net in CR, PSNR, and SSIM. On point-target data, ACCU-Net improves PSNR from 19.40 dB to 19.78 dB and SSIM from 0.433 to 0.457, with sharper targets and better recovery in deep lateral regions. Across datasets, ACCU-Net produces speckle patterns closer to the CPWC reference, demonstrating the effectiveness of incorporating angle, spatial, and ultrasound-specific priors for single-angle reconstruction.

papers.title: RF- and Image-Supervised Neural Network for Channel Interpolation in Sparse Array Ultrasound
papers.abstract: In wireless and handheld ultrasound, the receive channel count largely determines the front-end hardware complexity. A sparse receive array reduces the number of channels, but the enlarged effective pitch breaks the spatial Nyquist criterion and increases grating-lobe energy in the B-mode. This work proposes RF channel interpolation supervised in the RF and image domains to mitigate these effects. The method employs a two-stage network. Stage 1 reconstructs missing RF channels and interleaves them into full 128-channel data, while Stage 2 maps the reconstructed RF to a plane-wave B-mode image. RF supervision enforces data fidelity, while image-domain supervision directly targets image quality. Stage 2 is pretrained and frozen, enabling image-domain supervision through beamforming backpropagation. The loss combines RF and image terms with a weight ratio from gradient analysis. Experiments on in vivo data from the CUBDL dataset show that the proposed method outperforms cubic spline interpolation and a branched CNN baseline at decimation factors of 2 and 4, improving RF NRMSE and image SSIM while reducing grating-lobe artifact power to the full-array reference level.

papers.title: Low‑Bitrate Transmission of Pre‑Beamforming Ultrasound Radiofrequency Data Using Deep Autoencoder
papers.abstract: The growth in channel count and sampling rates of ultrasound systems (driven by ultrafast and 3‑D imaging) has raised pre‑beamforming data rates. In high‑channel‑count scanners, this throughput becomes a bottleneck for transmission, storage, and real-time operation. While most compression methods target beamformed- or image-domain data, the pre-beamforming domain remains underexplored. This work proposes a hardware-aware deep-learning compression framework operating directly on pre-beamforming data, enabling low-bitrate transmission with minimal signal degradation.

papers.title: Quantization of IQ Channel Data for Plane-Wave Fourier-Domain Beamforming
papers.abstract: Fourier-domain beamforming (FDB) is a highly efficient approach to plane-wave (PW) image reconstruction, but it needs to access an entire 2D channel data frame at once to take advantage of the FFT algorithm. To reduce the cost of probe-to-beamformer data transfers, we propose to compress complex-valued IQ channel data using a simple quantization scheme that involves a small fixed codebook and a dynamic scaling factor updated at every snapshot of an array probe aperture during data acquisition. Our PICMUS-based results demonstrate that FDB can produce high-quality images after receiving only 4/4 bits per real/imaginary parts of each data sample. While this work is motivated by the FDB needs, our quantization scheme is also applicable in the case of delay-and-sum (DAS) beamforming.

sessions.title: MTC: Liver & Prostate QUS

papers.title: Reproducible Quantitative Ultrasound (QUS) Characterization of Steatosis-Grade Phantoms Using Robot-Assisted Acquisition: Implications for MASLD Diagnostic Thresholds
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease affects approximately 30% of the U.S. population and is a leading cause of chronic liver disease worldwide. Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) techniques can objectively quantify hepatic steatosis. Tissue-mimicking phantoms provide a controlled, grade-specific acoustic reference for QUS calibration across MASLD severity. We fabricated agarose-gel, tissue-mimicking phantoms and acquired images in B-mode and raw RF signals using Farino Cobot robotic arm and obtained three replicate scans per phantom. From each scan, we extracted attenuation coefficient (AC), backscatter coefficient (BSC), and Nakagami parameter (m). Results demonstrated a monotonic increase in AC, BSC, and Nakagami m with increasing oil volume fraction, which is consistent with theoretical acoustic predictions. These findings suggest that the proposed phantom platform produces acoustically distinct, grade-dependent QUS signatures and supports its use as a calibration standard for MASLD imaging. Robotic-assisted acquisition further enhances reproducibility, enabling reliable detection of subtle acoustic variations.

papers.title: The Confounding Role of Transducer Frequency When Using H-Scan Ultrasound Imaging for the Preclinical Assessment of Liver Steatosis
papers.abstract: H-scan ultrasound (US) imaging is used to estimate relative scatterer size and is fundamentally impacted by transducer frequency: lower frequencies offer depth but poor resolution and higher frequencies give better resolution but limited penetration and greater attenuation. This study used four different US transducers (15 to 40 MHz) to perform H-scan frequency imaging on mice with and without diet-induced liver steatosis. H-scan frequency was significantly higher for steatotic livers using lower frequency probes (p < 0.01) but reversed at higher frequencies where control livers showed higher values (p < 0.01). Differences likely result from increased attenuation and loss of spectral content at high frequencies. Overall, these results reveal that tissue characterization using H-scan US is transmit frequency-dependent and multiscale.

papers.title: 3D Dynamic Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound (DCE-US) with AI-Assisted Segmentation for Liver Lesion Characterization
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional dynamic contrast-enhanced ultrasound (3D DCE-US) enables volumetric tumor perfusion assessment but is vulnerable to respiratory motion artifacts, compromising time-intensity curve (TIC) analysis. This study investigates an AI-assisted pipeline combining 3D motion compensation and MedSAM2-based autosegmentation to improve perfusion quantification in liver lesions. Paired 3D B-mode and CEUS sequences were acquired from four patients using a Philips EPIQ system with an X6-1 matrix transducer. A cross-correlation algorithm tracked lesion displacement across volumetric frames, and the resulting 3D bounding box was passed to MedSAM2 for slice-by-slice autosegmentation to extract TICs. MedSAM2-assisted segmentation outperformed manual VOI delineation across all participants, with mean R² improving from 0.835 ± 0.057 to 0.922 ± 0.011, and motion-compensated parametric maps showed reduced boundary artifacts. Future work will incorporate deep learning-based non-rigid deformable registration to capture breathing-induced tumor shape changes and assess longitudinal perfusion analysis.

papers.title: Improved B-mode-Based Attenuation Coefficient Estimation for Steatosis Grading: a Comparative Study with Histology and FibroScan
papers.abstract: Accurate steatosis grading is critical for managing non-alcoholic fatty liver disease. While FibroScan’s controlled attenuation parameter is a clinical standard, it lacks B-mode imaging, which limits its diagnostic capabilities. B-mode-based attenuation coefficient estimation (ACE) offers integrated anatomical guidance. However, in clinical settings, spectral distortion arising from averaging A-lines with heterogeneous tissue layer thicknesses compromises the accuracy and precision of ACE, leading to unreliable steatosis grading. Here, our objective is to demonstrate that an improved ACE framework can provide superior grading performance compared to both the traditional reference frequency method (RFM) and FibroScan, using histology results as the gold standard. The proposed method achieved superior diagnostic performance with AUC values of 0.973, 0.996, and 0.998 for detecting S1+, S2+, and S3 stages, respectively, and showed a strong positive correlation between the ACE and steatosis grades. Statistical analysis revealed extreme significance (p < 0.001) across nearly all stages, indicating higher sensitivity in monitoring disease progression.

papers.title: Backscatter Coefficient Estimated Jointly with Total Attenuation Versus Hepatorenal Index for Liver Fat Quantification in Vivo
papers.abstract: This study evaluates two ultrasound-based measures of liver echogenicity for in vivo liver fat quantification: the hepatorenal index (HRI) and the backscatter coefficient (BSC) estimated jointly with total attenuation using a 2-degrees-of-freedom approach. In 46 volunteers with suspected metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, both biomarkers were compared with automated histological steatosis percentage area and histological steatosis grade. The logarithm of BSC showed higher correlation with steatosis percentage area than HRI in this cohort. Both biomarkers increased with histological grade, but BSC showed statistically significant differences between more grade pairs than HRI, except between G2 and G3. These results indicate that jointly estimated BSC is associated with histological measures of steatosis and may provide an alternative to HRI for liver fat assessment.

papers.title: Unsupervised Prostate Cancer Characterization in a Mouse Model Using Temporal Enhanced Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Fast, accurate, and noninvasive cancer detection remains an unmet need. Conventional B-mode ultrasound is real-time and accessible, but often shows limited contrast between tumors and surrounding heterogeneous soft tissues. This study investigates Temporal Enhanced Ultrasound (TeUS) for unsupervised tumor characterization in a mouse prostate cancer xenograft model. PSMA-positive PC3 PIP cells were inoculated subcutaneously in mice, and 100 TeUS frames were acquired per mouse at 625 Hz using a Verasonics Vantage 256 system with an L22-14 vX linear array probe. Eleven physics-informed temporal and spectral features were extracted and clustered using a four-cluster Gaussian mixture model. Performance was evaluated by tumor cluster fraction and tumor-to-non-tumor enrichment ratio. Across seven mice, the tumor-associated cluster occupied 54.5 ± 10.9% of the tumor ROI, with an enrichment ratio of 1.50 ± 0.35. Representative results showed limited B-mode contrast but clear TeUS-GMM spatial differences near the tumor. These findings suggest that TeUS captures tumor-associated temporal signatures beyond B-mode imaging and may support rapid, label-free cancer monitoring.

sessions.title: MBB: Coherence, Aberration Correction, and Adaptive Beamforming

papers.title: Subspace Projection Beamforming for Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: Ultrasound beamforming is commonly performed using delay-and-sum (DAS); however, its spatial resolution and contrast are limited. Minimum variance (MV) beamforming improves image quality but suffers from sensitivity to covariance estimation errors and numerical instability. Eigenspace-based MV methods have been proposed to enhance robustness. In this study, we propose a subspace projection approach that applies eigenvalue decomposition (EVD) directly to element-space signals and reconstructs the data within a dominant subspace prior to beamforming. Unlike conventional methods, the proposed approach operates in the data space and does not require matrix inversion. The method was evaluated using phantom and in vivo carotid data. The contrast of a cyst phantom improved from 30.0 dB (DAS) to 47.4 dB. In vivo results showed reduced lumen artifacts and improved visualization of vessel wall structures, demonstrating stable and effective performance.

papers.title: Low-Complexity Clutter Suppression in AFB Using DAX–PCF Hybrid Weighting
papers.abstract: Acoustic-field beamforming (AFB) enables portable ultrasound imaging but suffers from clutter, degraded contrast, and limited speckle fidelity. Coherence-based methods such as GCF and PCF improve image quality but introduce trade-offs between clutter suppression and speckle preservation. This work proposes a hybrid coherence weighting framework combining dual-apodization with cross-correlation (DAX) and phase coherence factor (PCF). Dual receive apodizations generate two channel signals, and lateral normalized cross-correlation (NCC) derives DAX weighting for suppressing incoherent clutter. A weighted fusion strategy integrates DAX and PCF to balance amplitude and phase coherence. The method was evaluated using carotid ultrasound data and compared with AFB, GCF, NSC, SLSC, CF, SCF, and PCF. Results show balanced performance with contrast of ~27–28 dB, CNR of ~2.2, and background SNR of ~5. Compared with DAX and PCF alone, it improves structural visibility while preserving speckle. The proposed approach provides effective clutter suppression with low computational complexity and is suitable for real-time AFB-based vascular imaging.

papers.title: Assessment of Advanced Aberration Correction Methods Across SNR Conditions
papers.abstract: Ultrasound image quality is degraded by tissue-induced speed-of-sound (SoS) variations that cause wavefront aberrations, particularly under the constant SoS assumption in conventional beamforming. Advanced methods such as DBUA and IMPACT exploit full synthetic aperture (FSA) data to mitigate these effects; however, FSA inherently suffers from low channel SNR due to reduced transmit energy, making SoS and phase estimation susceptible to noise. This study investigates the robustness of DBUA and IMPACT across SNR levels from −20 to 20 dB using both phantom and in vivo datasets, with image quality assessed via off-axis energy and spatial resolution (FWHM). Results show that DBUA consistently outperforms IMPACT and DAS, particularly in lateral resolution and sidelobe suppression, although its performance degrades at very low SNR (<6 dB). While both DBUA and IMPACT achieve comparable improvements in axial resolution, DBUA provides significantly better lateral resolution. Overall, DBUA demonstrates greater robustness under moderate-to-low noise conditions, supported by both quantitative phantom results and qualitative in vivo observations.

papers.title: Dynamic Apodization Beamformer Based on Channel Partial Correlation for Dark Region Artifacts Elimination
papers.abstract: Coherence factor (CF) based methods can effectively improve ultrasound image contrast. Unfortunately, they have inherent problems in terms of dark-region artifacts and speckle distortion. In this study, we found that the possible reason for the CF beamformer excessively suppress incoherent signals is that the uniformly weight was used in the whole array signal. Inspired by this, we propose a dynamic apodization beamformer based on channel partial correlation (DA-CPC) to solve the dark-region artifacts problem in CF-based methods. Finally, we use the experiment resolution datasets of PICMUS challenge to evaluate the performance of DA-CPC. The imaging results of experiment resolution datasets shows that compared to traditional CF, the proposed DA-CPC beamformer not only significantly improves the resolution of point targets, but also maintains a good contrast close to CF. More importantly, the black-region artifacts were successfully eliminated in the imaging results of DA-CPC. We believe that this method will also helpful for other CF-based methods, particularly in the case of black-region artifacts problem.

papers.title: Aperture-Domain Characterization of Ultrasound Wavefront Distortions Using Coherence Noise Suppression and Aberration Correction
papers.abstract: This study investigated how two sources of ultrasound image degradation: wavefront aberration and coherence noise (reverberation, multipath scattering) affect image quality, and determined the best way to correct for both. We applied two algorithms, DBUA (aberration correction) and ADMIRE (clutter suppression), individually and in combination on phantom and rat abdomen datasets. We found that applying aberration correction first, followed by clutter suppression (DBUA->ADMIRE), produced the best image quality across all metrics. The reverse order (ADMIRE->DBUA) actually worsened results, because ADMIRE disrupts the phase information that DBUA needs to function correctly. The key takeaway is that aberration correction should precede coherence noise suppression in ultrasound imaging pipelines.

papers.title: Adaptive Inter-Angle Coherence Weighting for High-Frame-Rate Cerebral Blood Flow Imaging
papers.abstract: Background, Motivation, and Objective Cerebral hemodynamic monitoring relies on high-frame-rate plane-wave imaging; however, traditional linear spatial compounding fails to suppress incoherent noise and sidelobes in complex cranial environments. This degrades the contrast of fine microvasculature, and cranial clutter obscures deep-seated vessels, creating a trade-off between artifact suppression and temporal resolution. Statement of Contribution/Methods C57BL/6J mice underwent cranial window surgery. Data were acquired using an L22-14vX transducer (five-angle plane-wave imaging, 500 Hz). Following spatio-temporal SVD filtering, an adaptive nonlinear weighting map was constructed based on energy coherence and phase consistency across the five steering angles. Results/Discussion The proposed method effectively removes noise, revealing distinct microvascular networks and improving deep-vessel sensitivity. Quantitative analysis shows contrast increased from 31 dB to 56 dB (80.6% enhancement) over linear compounding, demonstrating that angular coherence significantly improves blood flow imaging quality.

papers.title: SVD-Based Joint Angular-Element Coherence Factor for Plane-Wave Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: Coherent plane-wave compounding (CPWC) enables high-frame-rate ultrasound imaging, but residual sidelobes and incoherent clutter remain when delay-aligned channel data are not phase-consistent. Existing coherence-factor-based methods mainly measure direct channel similarity and may over-suppress structured but useful echo components. This study proposes a singular value decomposition-based coherence factor (SVD-CF) that adaptively identifies informative coherent components. At each image pixel, delay-aligned complex data from multiple transmissions are arranged into an angle-by-element matrix and decomposed by SVD into orthogonal coherent components. A pixel-wise angular-element coherence weight is computed from the singular-value energy distribution and component-wise coherence, and applied during CPWC. SVD-CF was evaluated using simulated data and compared with delay-and-sum (DAS), coherence factor (CF), and united coherence factor (UCF) weighting. Results show SVD-CF suppresses background artifacts while preserving speckle better than CF and UCF, indicating SVD-CF provides an effective way to use angular-element coherence information in multi-angle plane-wave imaging.

papers.title: Angle-Dependent Bounded Refocusing for Axial-Lobe Suppression in Coherent Plane-Wave Compounding
papers.abstract: Coherent plane-wave compounding (CPWC) enables high-frame-rate ultrasound imaging, but off-axis reflectors can cause element-dependent transmit-time errors that create axial lobes at incorrect depths. These artifacts may brighten anechoic vessels or cysts and reduce contrast. Angle-dependent transmit apodization (ADTA) suppresses them by muting elements with large delay errors, but reduces effective aperture and SNR. This work proposes angle-dependent bounded-refocus CPWC, which partially corrects transmit delays toward angle-dependent reference points shifted along the steering ray while keeping all elements active. Correction strength is limited by βmax, and reference spacing is controlled by g. The method was evaluated using k-Wave simulations with seven plane waves, CIRS phantom data, and in vivo carotid data. In simulation, vessel contrast improved from 18.2 dB with CPWC and 22.9 dB with ADTA to 28.8 dB. Phantom and in vivo experiments also showed contrast improvement while preserving surrounding tissue signals better than ADTA. Overall, bounded refocusing reduces axial-lobe contamination without transmit-aperture loss, suggesting value for vessel-focused Doppler imaging.

papers.title: Aperture-Adaptive Scaled Wiener Postfilter for Second-Stage Synthetic Aperture Sequential Beamforming
papers.abstract: Synthetic aperture sequential beamforming (SASB) is attractive for portable ultrasound systems because it improves lateral resolution without storing full-channel RF data. However, finite apertures can make the ideal synthetic aperture exceed available low-resolution lines, especially for off-axis pixels, causing aperture truncation, asymmetric apodization, and elevated sidelobes. CF weighting effectively suppresses these artifacts but tends to over-suppress speckle, whereas Wiener postfiltering is more robust but less suppressive. To balance artifact suppression and speckle preservation, this work investigates an aperture-adaptive scaled Wiener postfilter for second-stage SASB (SASB-aScW). At each image point, aperture descriptors were computed to adaptively tune the scaling factor. Field II simulations based on an L7-4 linear array compared SASB, SASB-CF, SASB-aScW, and SASB-Wiener using an off-axis point target and a two-cyst phantom. SASB-aScW improved CR, gCNR, and background sSNR compared with CF, and provided higher CR than Wiener filtering with lower sSNR. These results suggest that aperture-aware postfiltering provides a practical trade-off for finite-aperture SASB.

papers.title: A Hybrid Beamforming Approach for Plane-Wave Ultrasound Imaging Using Das and Eigenspace MVDR
papers.abstract: Plane-wave imaging enables high-frame-rate ultrasound imaging; however, it often results in reduced image quality, particularly in terms of contrast and resolution. Multi-angle coherent compounding improves image quality through coherent summation, but it increases computational complexity and reduces temporal resolution. A hybrid beamforming architecture is developed in this work by integrating delay-and-sum (DAS) beamforming with eigenspace-based minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) beamforming.
