papers.title: SonarForge AI: an Accessible Ultrasound Field and Imaging Design Tool for Rapid Transducer Prototyping Using Rayleigh-Based Modeling
papers.abstract: We present SonarForge AI, an AI-built ultrasound simulation platform designed to improve accessibility and interpretability in transducer design and imaging physics. Established tools such as Field II, k-Wave, OnScale, and PiezoCAD enable high-fidelity modeling but require significant expertise and are not optimized for intuitive, goal-driven workflows. SonarForge AI introduces a plain-language interface where users specify imaging objectives (e.g., resolving 2 mm targets at 5 cm depth) and receive immediate feedback through beam profiles, resolution estimates, impedance predictions, and synthetic B-mode visualizations. The platform leverages simplified Rayleigh-based coherent summation under linear acoustic assumptions to generate real-time outputs. A dual-mode interface supports both novice users and experts by combining guided interpretation with explicit equations and assumptions. SonarForge AI serves as an educational and rapid prototyping tool while establishing a pathway toward validation against established ultrasound simulation frameworks.

sessions.title: ASN: AlScN BAW Devices

papers.title: Vertically Integrated BAW Delay Line with input/Output Matched Transducers As a low-Loss Filter for GHz Frequencies
papers.abstract: Low-loss micro-acoustic filters operating at 5-7 GHz are in high demand for 5G smartphones. They are often realized as ladder circuits of resonators or coupled resonator filters (CRFs). The third option—unidirectional transducers in a delay line (DL) configuration—is nearly forgotten. S. Ballandras [1] reminded us of this approach. Here, we exploit this idea to implement a short BAW delay line with well-matched transducers. A BAW transducer becomes unidirectional when bounded on one side by a vacuum. If properly matched, its passband is ~0.9 K, not K2/2 << 0.9 K, as in ladder filters, enabling wideband filter design on AlN layers. These layers can be vertically integrated, further reducing filter size.

papers.title: Two-Layer Polarization Inverted SiScAlN/ScAlN Film SMRs Operating in Second Overtone Mode
papers.abstract: Polarization inverted film BAW resonators can strongly excite overtone mode resonances, which have the capacity to exhibit higher resonance frequencies and larger device volumes than standard single-layer BAW resonators without any degradation in resonance performance. Therefore, overtone mode BAW resonators with multilayer polarization inverted film will be identified as a potential solution for next-generation RF filter applications operating at high frequencies. In this study, the two-layer polarization inverted film SMRs were fabricated by stacking the ScAlN and SiScAlN layers, grown using an RF magnetron sputtering. The (0002) ScAlN or SiScAlN peak, indicating the (0001) orientation, was observed in the XRD patterns for the SiScAlN/ScAlN and ScAlN/SiScAlN film SMRs. The strong second overtone mode resonance was observed at ~6 GHz in both SMRs. The keff2 values of the SiScAlN/ScAlN film SMR and the ScAlN/SiScAlN film SMR were approximately 7.8 % and 6.6 %, respectively.

papers.title: Theoretical Modelling of a Unidirectional Hybrid BAW/SAW Transducer Based on Phased Piezoelectric Pillar Arrays
papers.abstract: This work presents a theoretical model of a unidirectional hybrid BAW/SAW transducer based on phase-controlled AlScN piezoelectric pillar arrays on a non-piezoelectric sapphire substrate. Localized thickness-mode BAW vibrations in individual pillars are converted into SAWs propagating in the substrate. To suppress bidirectional radiation, a single-phase unit cell is proposed, consisting of one actively driven pillar and three passive pillars with floating top electrodes separated by an effective lambda/4 spacing. Piezoelectric coupling induces phase-shifted electric potentials in the passive pillars, enabling constructive acoustic interference in the desired direction and destructive interference in the opposite direction without multi-phase RF excitation. FEM simulations were performed to evaluate the electromechanical response, displacement fields, acoustic power flow, and transmission characteristics. A three-port delay-line model with a 65-pillar AlScN array and two IDT output ports confirms asymmetric S21/S31 transmission and directional SAW excitation. The concept is promising for acoustic delay lines, sensors, and piezo-MEMS.

papers.title: Single-Ended Ku-Band Lattice BAW Filter Using a Phase-Flip Network
papers.abstract: Ku-band RF front-ends require compact filters with low-loss passband and strong out-of-band rejection. Lattice BAW filters are promising but have a four-port differential structure that cannot directly adapt to single-ended systems, requiring baluns that increase volume and insertion loss. This study designs a high-performance lattice BAW filter for single-ended Ku-band RF front-ends. The resonators use a two-layer Al₀.₈Sc₀.₂N periodically poled (P3F) stack to match the uplink band. A second-order LC-LC network at the output provides a 180° phase flip, enabling balun-free single-ended operation. By analyzing its frequency response, this phase-flip network naturally generates a deep transmission zero in the downlink band, allowing removal of a shunt resonator conventionally dedicated to downlink rejection. Simulation results show operation in the 14–14.5 GHz uplink with 1 GHz 3-dB bandwidth, minimum insertion loss below 1.4 dB, return loss better than 14.5 dB, and downlink rejection >30 dB from 10–13 GHz. The proposed phase-flip lattice topology is a promising compact, balun-free solution for Ku-band RF front-ends.

papers.title: Energy Storage and Power Dissipation Analysis for Enhanced Power Handling in CRF BAW Filters
papers.abstract: Further reduction of BAW filter size requires architectures capable of concentrating multiple resonant functions in a limited volume. Coupled Resonator Filter (CRF) structures address this need by exploiting vertically coupled acoustic modes in multilayer stacks, which may include more than 20 material layers. As the stack becomes denser, however, the relationship between the modal response, the spatial distribution of acoustic energy and the resulting power dissipation becomes less straightforward. This is particularly relevant because thermal stress and power-handling degradation are among the main constraints in highly miniaturized filters. Here, we study how volume reduction affects power handling by resolving the energy and loss mechanisms throughout the stack. The proposed analysis quantifies, for each layer and frequency point, both stored energy and dissipated power, enabling the layers that dominate the effective quality factor and passband losses to be identified.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Accelerated Forward Simulation and Inverse Thickness Design of P3F BAW Resonators
papers.abstract: This work presents a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) framework for accelerated forward simulation and inverse thickness design of ultra-high-frequency Periodically Polarity-Inverted Piezoelectric Film (P3F) Bulk Acoustic Wave (BAW) resonators. It addresses trial-and-error design based on repeated Mason-model or finite-element simulations, especially above 10 GHz where polarity inversion and Q-enhancement microstructures increase complexity. The forward branch combines a Mason baseline, physics priors, and neural residual learning, so the network corrects impedance spectra rather than generating them from scratch. The inverse branch maps target fs, fp, Qs, Qp, and kt² to electrode and piezoelectric-layer thicknesses. Comparisons with ADS data, COMSOL 2D microstructure-enhanced data, Mason baseline, and NN prediction show close agreement with the enhanced response. Training curves show MSE below 0.01 and R² approaching unity, supporting target-metric-driven thickness prediction and spectral verification.

sessions.title: NDE: General NDE Methods and Acoustic Imaging and Microscopy

papers.title: Underwater Ultrasound Heartbeat Estimation Using Quadrature Phase Processing and Variational Autoencoder
papers.abstract: Drowning in residential bathtubs is a serious public health risk. Conventional monitoring—wearables, cameras, and microwave radar—faces limitations due to discomfort, privacy concerns, or cost. This study proposes a contactless heartbeat estimation system using underwater ultrasound and deep learning. Two identical transducers—one for transmission, one for reception—are submerged in water. The key novelty is quadrature (I/Q) multi-channel sampling: by pairing I- and Q-channel samples offset by one quarter-wavelength in depth, at least one component always retains sensitivity to chest-wall micro-displacements regardless of carrier phase. After band-pass filtering and cross-correlation, 64 channels are extracted over a 7.7 cm span and fed into a variational autoencoder (VAE) trained on ECG-derived triangular-wave labels with binary cross-entropy loss. Two male subjects were evaluated at 20 and 50 cm via leave-one-out cross-validation. At 20 cm, the system achieved an F1 score of 81.1%, heartbeat interval RMSE of 52.61 ms, and heart rate error of 4.57 bpm, demonstrating strong potential for non-contact vital monitoring and drowning prevention in residential bathtubs.

papers.title: Liquid Level Estimation Without Baseline Data Using Multi-Frequency Guided Waves in a Partially Immersed Waveguide
papers.abstract: Reliable liquid-level measurement is essential for process stability, safety, and product quality in industrial tanks. However, conventional methods often require calibration or baseline data, limiting their use in in-service environments. To overcome this limitation, this study proposes a baseline-free liquid-level estimation method using multi-frequency guided waves in a partially immersed plate waveguide. A 1-mm-thick aluminum plate was used to excite the A0 mode in a pulse-echo configuration. When partially immersed, the A0 mode is converted into quasi-Scholte (QS) modes, leading to propagation distances that vary with immersion length. Guided-wave signals were measured from 490 to 510 kHz, where the QS mode group velocity showed a near-linear dependence on frequency. Using multi-frequency arrival times, the liquid level was directly estimated without baseline data. Simulations and experiments confirmed delayed arrival times with increasing immersion length, and the estimated liquid levels agreed well with actual values, with a mean relative error of 2.17%.

papers.title: Nondestructive Inspection of Concrete Structures by Combining Rapid Screening and Pinpointed Auto-Frequency-Adaptive High-Resolution 3D Ultrasonic Imaging
papers.abstract: A hybrid inspection scheme combining real-time 2D ultrasonic phased-array (PA) screening with pinpointed, high-resolution 3D auto-frequency-adaptive PA imaging is proposed for aging concrete structures. Its feasibility is experimentally demonstrated, enabling efficient evaluation of internal defects in highly attenuative, diverse concrete materials. Furthermore, we conducted a fundamental study on the introduction of augmented reality (AR) for 3D imaging results to facilitate on-site practical application.

papers.title: High Quality Ultrasound Imaging with Limited Sensors via Compressive Sensing Based Deconvolution
papers.abstract: Ultrasound imaging in non-destructive testing commonly uses the Total Focusing Method (TFM), but its resolution is limited because it ignores the system’s spatial impulse response (SIR). Incorporating SIR can improve resolution. While MMSE beamforming enhances resolution by minimizing mean square error, it does not effectively suppress noise. This work extends MMSE by integrating prior statistical information—specifically the sparsity of scattering targets—into the formulation, enabling both denoising and improved imaging with fewer array elements. The imaging model is expressed as a linear system y = Po + e, where measurements depend on a propagation matrix derived from transmit/receive SIRs. Exploiting sparsity, the image is reconstructed by minimizing a combined least-squares and L1 regularization cost function. Simulations with a 16-element array and noisy data (20 dB SNR) show that, compared to TFM and MMSE, the proposed method achieves better resolution, contrast, and overall image quality.

papers.title: Memory-Efficient IQ-Domain Volumetric Refocusing for Scanning Acoustic Microscopy
papers.abstract: High-frequency scanning acoustic microscopy (SAM) enables non-destructive inspection of internal microstructures, but its limited depth of field causes blurring in volumetric imaging. This study proposes a memory-efficient IQ-domain 3D VSSA-CFW framework for scalable volumetric refocusing in SAM. RF signals acquired at 1 GSPS were converted to complex IQ data by quadrature demodulation and filtering, reducing data volume by 85%. Carrier phase rotation was applied to compensate for delay-induced phase shifts and preserve RF-equivalent beamforming. The method was validated using a 39 MHz focused transducer, a 20 μm tungsten wire phantom, and an RP2040 IC package. CUDA-based GPU parallelization assigned each voxel to one thread. Compared with RF-domain reconstruction, the proposed method reduced memory usage by 4.5× and transfer time by over 60%. It achieved a lateral FWHM of 37.98 μm with 3 dB noise reduction, and improved IC bonding-wire visibility, increasing gCNR from 0.7994 to 0.8797.

papers.title: An extensive study of the use of high frequency ultrasonics from 50MHz up to 175MHz on very high accuracy sratigraphies simulation of Byzantine frescoes and icons of all the periods
papers.abstract: A few teams in the scientific community are using high frequency ultrasonics in the various fields of nondestructive testing/examination. Especially in the field of cultural heritage objects, which is a demand for the non-destructive reveal of the internal structure of the cultural heritage objects. One of the most demanding is the non-destructive tomography of the paint layers of frescoes and icons and in general paintings, supporting the decision on authenticity, and eventual effort of exact copies of fake creations, historical documentations and reveal of ancient techniques of creation. The inner structure of such kind of stratigraphist evolves in the various layers, many materials organic and inorganic ones even including metals and grainy, subjected to destruction if the coherence with the binding medium of the pigment is breakdown.

sessions.title: NMC: Acoustic Sensors and Material and Defect Characterization

papers.title: Ultrasound Characterization of Hydrogel Under Stress for intraoral Imaging
papers.abstract: High frequency ultrasound imaging of periodontal tissues is emerging as a promising non-invasive technique for visualizing soft tissues of the oral cavity such as gingival structures and assessing periodontal diseases. For intraoral applications, a dedicated semi-solid hydrogel cap has been designed to conform to the probe geometry and maintain contact with the tissue. The aim of this work is to characterize the mechanical and acoustic behaviour of the hydrogel under stress and evaluate its influence on B-mode intraoral images performed with a dedicated 20MHz probe.

papers.title: A Finite-Difference Simulation Framework for Ultrasonic Crystal Orientation Fabric Estimation in Ice: Timing Methodology, Forward Model Selection, and the Cram´er–Rao Accuracy Limit
papers.abstract: A 2-D finite-difference elastodynamic simulation framework is presented for evaluating crystal orientation fabric (COF) estimation in glacial ice cores. COF (the preferential alignment of ice grains under sustained loading) causes azimuthal P-wave velocity variation measurable by rotating a transducer around a cylindrical specimen. The framework compares three forward models (bulk harmonic C1, path-traced C2, Fresnel-weighted C3) across three acquisition geometries: pulse-echo reflection, opposed pitch-catch, and chord-family multistatic transmission. C2 achieves residuals of 14-18% in reflection and opposed transmission versus approximately 25% for C1; C3 provides no benefit. In chord-family transmission all three models are equivalent. Cramer-Rao bound analysis gives a 1.7-2.2 degree orientation accuracy floor for C2, consistent across 1-5 MHz, providing the first principled accuracy benchmark for ultrasonic COF estimation on ice cores.

papers.title: Ultrasound Imaging of Porosity in Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymers
papers.abstract: Porosity is a critical manufacturing defect in carbon‑fiber‑reinforced polymers (CFRP), particularly in aerospace applications, where it reduces mechanical performance and reliability. Conventional ultrasonic testing provides mainly averaged information based on signal attenuation and scattering, offering limited insight into the spatial distribution of voids. This work explores the potential of advanced ultrasonic imaging using a 2D matrix array probe and FMC/TFM with refraction correction to achieve porosity characterization at the level of individual voids. Three‑dimensional ultrasonic images are compared with X‑ray computed tomography data, demonstrating that porous regions and some individual voids can be identified. The results indicate that ultrasonic imaging may offer a promising path toward more informative porosity assessment in CFRP.

papers.title: Experimental Calibration and Validation of COMSOL-Based Acoustic Reflection Modeling in Air-Filled Channels for Active Sensing Applications
papers.abstract: Accurate modeling of acoustic wave propagation and reflection is essential for active sensing systems, such as respiratory monitoring based on airway acoustics. However, quantitative agreement between simulation and measurement remains limited, particularly for transient responses in confined geometries. This work presents a calibration framework that aligns COMSOL-based acoustic simulations with experimental measurements in air-filled channels. A controlled platform consisting of a speaker-microphone front-end coupled to a sealed cylindrical pipe (length ≈ 41 cm, diameter 2.5 cm) was developed to generate and capture burst acoustic reflections. A corresponding multiphysics COMSOL model replicates the system geometry and boundary conditions. Calibration is achieved by tuning the equivalent normal velocity boundary using measured acoustic pressure. Results show strong agreement in both time and amplitude domains, with the first reflected burst observed at ~2.4 ms, corresponding to an ~82 cm round-trip distance. A calibrated velocity of ~0.03 m/s produces ~3 Pa peak-to-peak pressure, matching measurements (~97.5 dB).

sessions.title: MEL: Machine Learning and Optimization in Elastography

papers.title: ROBUST: Regularized Optimization-Based Ultrasound Shear Wave Speed Estimation from Time-to-Peak Maps
papers.abstract: Estimation of shear wave speed (SWS) in ultrasound elastography using time-to-peak (TTP) analysis is highly sensitive to displacement tracking noise, resulting in unreliable maps and potential boundary distortion under post-processing. We propose ROBUST (Regularized Optimization-Based Ultrasound SWS from TTP), a model-based framework that reconstructs SWS by analytically optimizing a cost function enforcing a physically consistent relationship between TTP differences and inter-pixel spatial distances, with axial and lateral regularization. The proposed method was evaluated on phantom data acquired using a Verasonics Vantage NXT system. Compared with conventional TTP-based reconstruction, ROBUST yields more spatially consistent SWS maps while preserving stiffness boundaries. These characteristics support improved reliability of quantitative elastography for assessing tissue stiffness heterogeneity.

papers.title: Bi-Planar Structure-Preserving Variational Particle Velocity Cleaning for Robust Shear Wave Speed Estimation
papers.abstract: We propose a sequential bi-planar variational cleaning technique for particle velocity fields in ultrasound shear wave elastography (SWE) to improve shear wave speed (SWS) reconstruction. Existing filtering approaches reduce noise but do not explicitly preserve wavefield structure, often blurring wavefronts and distorting motion fidelity. The proposed method enforces data fidelity while penalizing first- and second-order variations, suppressing noise and tracking artifacts without degrading shear wavefronts. The cost function is optimized using ADMM and applied sequentially across x-t (lateral-temporal) and z-t (axial-temporal) planes on Loupas-tracked, directional-filtered particle velocity data, with the output used for correlation-based SWS reconstruction. The technique produces less noisy SWS maps with improved spatial consistency. Progressive cleaning (x-t → x-t & z-t) enhances inclusion visibility and boundary delineation. These results demonstrate improved elasticity contrast and more robust SWS reconstruction, supporting improved lesion delineation and diagnostic confidence in clinical SWE.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Viscoelastic Imaging: Toward Real-Time 3D Elastography
papers.abstract: Volumetric viscoelastic imaging from conventional 2D ultrasound would unlock real-time, spatially resolved characterization of tissue. Full-waveform inversion is able to recover these out-of-plane viscoelasticity images from typical shear-wave acquisitions, yet it can take hours per image. Our ultimate goal is to use deep learning to bridge this gap by reconstructing 3D viscoelasticity from 2D ultrasound in real time. Toward this goal, we develop a two-stage deep learning pipeline. We first use a Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) network to predict viscoelastic parameters from a single shear-wave acquisition. Validation is performed on 5 ex vivo pig livers, where shear modulus agrees within 3% of two classical methods and viscosity within 12%. We then extend the FNO with a decoder to reconstruct 2D out-of-plane maps from multiple line acquisitions, a proof of concept toward 3D viscoelastic imaging, on an in silico phantom at 15 dB SNR. Our maps achieve 3 to 5 times lower error than full-waveform inversion and structural similarity above 0.99 (compared to 0.85-0.93), in 5 milliseconds rather than 30 minutes.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Estimation of Mechanical Anisotropy from ARFI Displacements Acquired at Arbitrary Angles
papers.abstract: Mechanical anisotropy, quantified as the shear moduli ratio (SMR = μL/μT), is a diagnostically relevant biomarker in structured tissues like muscle, kidney, and breast tumors. However, conventional ARFI-based assessment requires precise transducer alignment with the tissue's axis of symmetry — often clinically infeasible when fiber orientation is unknown. This study presents a machine learning framework to predict SMR from ARFI peak displacements at arbitrary angles. A simulation dataset (LS-DYNA FEM + Field II; SMR = 0.90–4.90) trained a hybrid MLP–Gaussian process regression model using 4, 5, or 6 angles (≥20° separation), with the 5-angle model yielding the best accuracy-stability balance (most predictions within ±20% error). Applied to murine breast tumor data, background SMRs (0.9–1.2) indicated near-isotropic tissue while tumor SMRs (3.5–5.04) reflected pronounced anisotropy consistent with tumor microstructure. These results demonstrate the feasibility of alignment-free, ARFI-based anisotropy estimation, with potential extension to SWEI-based approaches.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based On-Axis Estimation of Elasticity and Viscosity Ratios from ARFI-Derived Displacement Features
papers.abstract: This study develops a machine-learning pipeline for on-axis estimation of inclusion-to-background elasticity ratio (ER) and viscosity ratio (VR) from ARFI-derived displacement features. Existing off-axis shear-wave methods often require spatial averaging and are limited in heterogeneous tissues, while Viscoelastic Response (VisR) ultrasound requires computationally intensive pixel-wise model fitting. LS-DYNA and Field II simulations generated 550 inclusion cases with varied focal depths, geometries, sizes, and ER/VR contrasts. An MLP classifier first identified inclusion masks from ARFI features, followed by a dilated Conv1D model that predicted A-line-level ER and VR using temporal/velocity feature ratios and imaging parameters. In held-out simulations, ER and VR errors were mostly below 15% across geometries. Experimental testing in a chicken-breast inclusion embedded in gelatin produced coherent ER/VR maps with clear inclusion boundaries and background values near unity. These findings support automated viscoelastic mapping without pixel-wise mechanical model fitting, with future application to breast cancer treatment monitoring.

papers.title: Deep Learning–Based Recovery of On-Axis ARFI Displacement from Off-Axis Shear Wave Motion for High-Frame-Rate Elastography
papers.abstract: There is a need to improve the frame rate of acoustic radiation force impulse (ARFI) imaging for high-motion organs such as the heart. Combining ARFI with shear wave elastography imaging (SWEI) can enhance lesion detection, but separate acquisitions may cause spatial misalignment and increased thermal exposure. This study proposes generating ARFI displacement images from shear wave–induced displacement using a convolutional neural network (CNN), enabling high-frame-rate ARFI. The CNN estimates on-axis ARFI displacement from off-axis shear wave displacement by regressing normalized patches to corresponding noise-free ARFI patches from an 81×49 field of view. Training used ~1M simulated patches across multiple noise levels and material conditions. Noise-free ARFI served as ground truth for denoising and correcting displacement underestimation. The model was tested on experimental phantom data. The model achieved comparable or improved contrast-to-noise ratio while reducing ARF pushes by 50 times.

papers.title: Patch-Based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) Estimation of Elasticity and Viscosity in Heterogeneous Media from Shear-Wave Motion Features
papers.abstract: This study develops a patch-based convolutional neural network (CNN) to estimate shear modulus and viscosity maps in heterogeneous media from ARF-induced shear-wave motion features. Current viscoelasticity methods may ignore viscosity, require homogeneous regions, or fail when shear waves are distorted by inclusions and boundaries. The CNN input was a 12×36×15 patch representing a 3×9 mm axial–lateral region, with feature channels derived from peak displacement ratio, peak velocity ratio, and time-to-peak displacement across five lateral shifts. Patches were generated with 0.25-mm axial overlap, and overlapping predictions were averaged. Training and testing used 182,187 simulated patches from 90 homogeneous and 43 heterogeneous materials with shear modulus of 0.3–37 kPa and viscosity of 0.1–5.6 Pa·s. Predicted elasticity and viscosity maps reconstructed the inclusion contrast across geometries, with errors of 22.9±15.0% and 26.5±44.8% for elasticity and viscosity, respectively. These results support patch-based CNN estimation for spatial viscoelasticity mapping without explicit dispersion fitting or homogeneous-region assumptions.

sessions.title: MIM: Freehand 3D Ultrasound & Clinical Translation (8 posters)

papers.title: Evaluating Individual Predisposition to Decompression Sickness Risk After independent, Identical Dive Exposures Using two-Dimensional Echocardiography
papers.abstract: This work evaluated the day-to-day risk of decompression sickness (DCS) for individuals conducting identical SCUBA dive exposures. SCUBA diving can induce bubble formation, which may lead to DCS injury. We used echocardiography to characterize post-dive bubble formation in 33 individuals that completed the same dive profile six independent times (198 dives total). Bubble presence in the ultrasound recordings was graded on an ordinal scale and the peak was identified over a two-hour observation period. The median absolute deviation (MAD) of peak grades per participant was calculated and compared against the MAD for a random permutation of the dataset. We found the MAD to be larger for the random permutations than the original dataset (p<0.05), which was bootstrapped over 1000 iterations. Separately, a mixed-effects model was used to calculate the intra-class coefficient, which was found to be 0.6. Both findings indicate that participants tended to produce individually consistent VGE presence after identical, independent dive exposures. Further, some divers consistently produced high VGE presence, and likely may be at a higher predisposition to decompression stress and DCS.

papers.title: Freehand 3D Thyroid Ultrasound Reconstruction with Feature- and Frequency-Guided Motion Estimation and Anatomical Segmentation
papers.abstract: This study proposes a deep learning-based sensorless freehand 3D thyroid ultrasound reconstruction framework consisting of a motion tracking branch, an anatomical segmentation branch, and a visualization phase. In the motion tracking branch, FFME-Net estimates 6-DoF inter-frame motion by combining encoder features, feature differences, and Fourier-domain low-frequency differences with ConvLSTM-based temporal modeling. The estimated relative motion vectors are accumulated for 3D ultrasound volume reconstruction. In the visualization phase, DL-driven segmentations of the thyroid gland, carotid artery, and nodules are overlaid onto the reconstructed 3D volume. Experimental results showed improved motion estimation performance compared with baseline methods, with relative translation and rotation errors of 0.0458 mm and 0.0171°, respectively, and local, global, and final frame errors of 0.0973 mm, 5.9707 mm, and 9.1297 mm. By combining the estimated scan motions with the segmentation results, the proposed framework reconstructs 3D thyroid ultrasound volumes and visualizes target anatomical structures.

papers.title: Initial Clinical Experience Using H-Scan Ultrasound Imaging for Early Detection of Cancer Response to transarterial chemoembolization in Liver
papers.abstract: Early evaluation of liver metastasis response to transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) is challenging. This study assessed H-scan ultrasound (US) imaging for monitoring microstructural tumor changes post-TACE in 17 metastatic melanoma patients. Patients were scanned before, and at 1–2 and 4–8 weeks after TACE. Tumor-to-parenchyma ratios (TPR) for intensity and heterogeneity from B-scan and H-scan US images were tracked. While most TPRs showed no significant differences between viable and nonviable tumors, baseline heterogeneity TPRs from H-scan US differed significantly (p < 0.001). Nonviable tumors showed a significant decrease in heterogeneity based on TPRs over time (p = 0.02). These results suggest TPRs of H-scan heterogeneity may help differentiate viable from nonviable tumors and monitor post-TACE response.

papers.title: Direct Myocardial Microvascular Imaging with intra-Cardiac Echocardiography
papers.abstract: Direct myocardial microvasculature assessment in vivo remains challenging due to limitations in spatial resolution of current cardiac imaging modalities. Contrast-enhanced intracardiac echocardiography (CE-ICE) combined with ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) may offer a promising method to directly visualize myocardial microvasculature with potential intraprocedural applications, such as ablation monitoring before and after electrophysiological ablation. This capability could help evaluate microvascular flow alterations associated with lesion formation and improve assessment of treatment efficacy. Here, we present the first proof-of-concept feasibility study of CE-ICE ULM in an ex vivo porcine heart model.

papers.title: EchoRoute: Visual-Prompt-Guided Soft Routing for Multi-Item Echocardiography Report Retrieval
papers.abstract: EchoRoute is a visual-prompt-guided framework for multi-item echocardiography report retrieval. Echocardiography interpretation requires integrating multiple visual items such as views, imaging modes, cine loops, still images, and Doppler data, but this process is labor-intensive and reader-dependent. EchoRoute addresses this by projecting visual items and reports into a shared embedding space and learning exam-level representations through global contrastive alignment. To capture local visual-textual correspondence without item-level expert labels, it uses appearance-based view-mode prompts and relaxed optimal transport to generate soft routing weights. These weights guide biomarker alignment by connecting numeric values and clinical criteria with relevant visual item combinations while reducing noise from irrelevant images. Experiments show that routing, compositional biomarker alignment, biomarker prediction, joint fine-tuning, and recovery-ready training each improve performance. The full model achieved R@1/5/10 of 15.80/43.20/67.10% and an MRR of 0.294, demonstrating effective and interpretable hierarchical prompt-guided alignment.

papers.title: Sparsity Adaptive Coarse to Fine Framework for Freehand 3D Ultrasound Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Tracked freehand 3D ultrasound reconstruction enables real-time, cost-effective volumetric imaging without ionizing radiation, but practical scenarios with probe motion and limited sampling make reconstruction from sparse data challenging. We propose a sparsity-adaptive, coarse-to-fine multi-resolution fusion strategy that directly addresses sampling sparsity. Data is acquired using an Atracsys FusionTrack 500 and Clarius C3HD with synchronized imaging and tracking. Sampling sparsity is quantified via an inter-frame gap metric computed using AABB from consecutive frames, with the maximum gap (Gm) representing worst-case sparsity. This is used to adaptively set voxel resolution such that gaps correspond to two pixels, ensuring sufficient overlap while limiting smoothing via a threshold. Reconstruction is performed using a PNN scheme, with voxel resolution progressively refined toward the native resolution. Validation on a wire phantom shows improved robustness under sparse sampling compared to a PlusToolkit reconstruction baseline.

papers.title: Mesh Localization Using Ultrasound Shear Wave Elastography and Deep Learning-Based Segmentation
papers.abstract: Surgical mesh is widely used in soft-tissue reinforcement procedures, such as hernia repair. However, surgical mesh, particularly legacy implants without magnetic material, is difficult to visualize with traditional imaging modalities and challenging to monitor postoperatively. Our hypothesis for this work was that ultrasound shear wave elastography (SWE) could be a useful tool for localizing and assessing the mesh after implantation, as the meshes provide mechanical contrast with soft tissues. Although accurate localization is challenging due to tissue heterogeneity and various anatomically stiff structures, such as tendons and scar tissue, resulting false positives. This study proposes a deep learning (DL)-based segmentation framework, combined with SWE, to improve mesh localization.

papers.title: A Blind-Sweep Ultrasound Pipeline for Automated Liver Fat Assessment
papers.abstract: Liver fat disease is common, but scalable screening is limited by the need for expert ultrasound acquisition and interpretation. This study develops a blind-sweep ultrasound pipeline for automated liver fat assessment using right-upper-quadrant volume sweep imaging (VSI), which can be acquired by minimally trained operators. Data from 112 patients, including 1456 videos with liver annotations and paired reference liver fat measurements, were evaluated through three stages: liver frame detection, liver segmentation, and patient-level fat estimation. U-Net, TinyUSFM, USFM, and DINOv2 were benchmarked, with inference latency and computational cost profiled for deployment. DINOv2 achieved the best liver detection performance, while TinyUSFM produced the strongest segmentation results. A DINOv2-based regressor achieved the best fat estimation performance. Overall, results show that automated VSI liver analysis should be optimized as a connected pipeline balancing accuracy, recall, estimation error, speed, and computational cost.

sessions.title: MIM: Novel US Systems & Wearables

papers.title: Fetal Monitoring for high-Risk Pregnancies Using a Wearable Ultrasound Patch
papers.abstract: Ultrasonography is a cornerstone of fetal monitoring, but it requires specialized sonographers and is limited to providing snapshot evaluations at discrete intervals. Here we report a wearable ultrasound patch (UPatch) for continuous and autonomous fetal monitoring. The UPatch can acquire anatomical structures and blood flow velocities, demonstrating high agreement with a handheld clinical ultrasound device on 62 pregnancies. Real-time image segmentation allows autonomous tracking of target vessels and thus the acquisition of continuous blood flow spectra during fetal and maternal movements without a sonographer. Continuous monitoring data for 1–3 h from 52 pregnant women aligned with stratified perinatal conditions, including healthy, small for gestational age, large for gestational age, gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia, and gestational hypertension. Additionally, integration with a miniaturized circuit could enable fully wireless operation and greater patient mobility. The UPatch could provide evidence of fetal complications in high-risk pregnancies, expanding prenatal-care capabilities.

papers.title: Birefringence Compensation in LiNbO3 Transparent Ultrasound Transducer for Two-Photon Imaging
papers.abstract: Transparent ultrasound transducers enable simultaneous optical imaging and acoustic stimulation, allowing two-photon imaging of neural activity during ultrasound stimulation. However, 36° Y-cut lithium niobate (LiNbO₃) exhibits intrinsic birefringence that splits light into ordinary and extraordinary rays, causing image duplication and optical distortion that degrade image quality. We present a birefringence compensation approach using a dual-layer LiNbO₃ configuration, where a second layer rotated 180° about the surface normal cancels lateral beam displacement and recombines the rays. Compared to polarization filtering, which reduces optical throughput by ~50%, the proposed method suppresses image duplication while preserving higher optical intensity. Experiments show ~10 µm image displacement with a single layer, while the dual-layer configuration eliminates duplication and achieves approximately twice the average pixel intensity compared to polarization filtering.

papers.title: Image-Based Calibration for Tracked Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Tracked ultrasound requires calibration of the rigid transformation between tracker and image coordinates for applications such as freehand 3D ultrasound, image-guided intervention, and coherent multi-view reconstruction. This work presents an image-based calibration framework that estimates the full 6-DOF transform directly from tracked beamformed data using a continuous sweep over a standard phantom, avoiding calibration-target segmentation, phantom localization, and specialized phantom geometry. A P4-2 transducer was swept over an ATS 539 phantom while transmitting 0 degrees plane waves at 400 Hz with synchronized optical tracking. Frame pairs separated by about 1 mm were reconstructed on a common grid, and calibration was recovered by minimizing a differentiable similarity-matrix loss. Compared with an N-wire benchmark, the proposed method achieved a mean wire-line residual of 0.58 mm versus 1.84 mm, while also improving feature definition in coherent lateral reconstructions and slice-to-slice consistency in elevational volumetric sweeps.

papers.title: Hardware-Aware Feature Extraction for Wearable Ultrasound Systems: a Case Study in Hand Gesture Recognition
papers.abstract: Wearable ultrasound systems (WUSs) are a promising unobtrusive human-machine interface for robotics and prosthetics. Movement tracking relies on detecting signal variations caused by muscle and tendon motion. This poses major challenges for feature detection and extraction (FE), which must be robust to anatomy, coupling, motion, and signal quality while meeting strict limits on computation, power, memory, and data bandwidth. Yet, the embedded efficiency and reliability of FE approaches remain insufficiently investigated. This work addresses this challenge through a hardware-aware case study using four 4 MHz A-mode forearm transducers for eight-gesture recognition. The results show that compact architectures retain task-relevant ultrasound information under wearable constraints. Autoencoder-based FE with two-stage semi-supervised training outperforms the investigated alternatives, demonstrating a pathway toward low-power, real-time wearable ultrasound interfaces. More broadly, signal processing in WUSs should be co-designed through a full-stack, data-driven approach that jointly considers application, ultrasonic sensing, and embedded hardware.

papers.title: Comparison of Hybrid Array Design Strategies for Wearable Ultrasound Devices
papers.abstract: Wearable ultrasound systems offer a platform for continuous vital monitoring but are limited by small footprints and hardware constraints. Hybrid Arrays (HA), which separate transmit (TX) and receive (RX) circuitries, can enhance signal-to-noise ratios but often suffer from degraded beamforming. This study compares HA designs - Laterally Separated Array (LSA) and Interleaved Array (IA) - against a conventional Uniform Array (UA) within a 3x6 mm^2 footprint. Using a commercial linear-array probe and a tissue phantom, imaging performance was evaluated by measuring Contrast Ratio (CR) relative to lateral misalignment. Results show the UA achieved the highest peak CR (34.1 dB) but is incompatible with HA hardware requirements. Between the hybrid designs, the LSA (24.6 dB) significantly outperformed the IA (16.2 dB). Furthermore, the LSA demonstrated superior robustness to misalignment (2.5 dB/mm degradation) compared to the IA (1.5 dB/mm with lower absolute performance), which suffered from larger effective TX pitch. The study concludes that the LSA strategy provides the optimal trade-off for compact wearable ultrasound implementations.

papers.title: Energy Efficient Implementations of Mismatched Filtering for Wearable Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Wearable ultrasound enables continuous, non-invasive physiological monitoring but is limited by strict power budgets, making efficient on-device signal processing critical. This work investigates the energy–accuracy trade-off of matched filtering (MF) on a heterogeneous MCU with an integrated neural processing unit (NPU). MF is implemented in time- and frequency-domain on an ARM Cortex M55 and Ethos-U55 to test the hypothesis that NPU-based processing improves energy efficiency at comparable accuracy. CPU-based MF uses ARM CMSIS convolution and real-valued Fast Fourier Transformation (RFFT), while NPU models are implemented in TensorFlow Lite, requiring custom (R)FFT models due to limited NPU operator support. Energy, runtime, and normalized mean squared error (NMSE) are evaluated on a pre-recorded ultrasound signal. The results show that NPU-based MF reduces energy consumption by up to 28% while maintaining accuracy at higher bit-depths, although frequency-domain models suffer from accumulated quantization errors. These findings highlight the potential of NPUs for energy-efficient ultrasound signal processing on edge devices.

papers.title: Development and Characterization of a Wearable Ultrasound Patch for Post-Operative ECMO Monitoring
papers.abstract: This work presents a wearable ultrasound patch for continuous post-operative monitoring of ECMO cannulas, addressing dislodgement risks that visual inspection may miss. The patch comprises three layers: a chitosan-acrylamide hydrogel, a flexible elastomer membrane, and a bioadhesive layer enabling skin adhesion via hydrogen bonding, electrostatic, and covalent amide interactions. Acoustic characterization used a through-transmission technique to measure sound speed through the hydrogel. Results compared bare and elastomer-encased hydrogels over 24 hours: bare hydrogels lost about 30.95% thickness with 5.77% sound speed increase due to dehydration, while encapsulated hydrogels showed no thickness loss and only 0.55% sound speed change. Although differences did not reach statistical significance due to limited sample size, large effect sizes suggest elastomer encapsulation effectively preserves hydrogel structural and acoustic properties. Future studies with larger cohorts are needed to confirm significance and assess longer-term stability.

papers.title: A Compact Mechatronic Ultrasound Wearable for Active Neonatal Cardiac Screening
papers.abstract: This work presents a miniaturized robotic ultrasound system for neonatal cardiac image acquisition. The platform combines a conventional full-aperture clinical ultrasound probe, a two-degree-of-freedom programmable gimbal, and a compact imaging/compute backend in a body-mounted form factor. The system provides real-time B-mode and color imaging, programmable probe sweeping, and a complete control interface for image acquisition. Bench testing demonstrated sub-0.1° repeatability for both motion axes, and an IRB-approved clinical feasibility study acquired diagnostically useful neonatal cardiac ultrasound images from more than 10 infants. These results support the system as a hardware and data-collection foundation for future automated CHD screening.

papers.title: Evaluating Posture Invariance of Real-Time Sonomyographic Control
papers.abstract: Wearable sonomyography (SMG) captures depth-resolved muscle deformation, offering a promising alternative to electromyography for prosthetic control. However, maintaining stable control across varying arm positions remains a challenge. We present SonoGlide, an integrated regression-based SMG and Glide control framework designed for intuitive, posture-tolerant, multi-DoF proportional control. Continuous 2-DoF signals were generated from ultrasound M-mode data. Offline analysis included six participants (two with limb loss); real-time Fitts’ Law evaluation was performed on three able-bodied participants in neutral and shoulder positions. Intensity-weighted mean depth features were extracted to train linear regression models for wrist flexion, extension, pronation, and supination. SonoGlide achieved a mean offline F1-score of 91.70 ± 9.22%. In real-time tests, completion rates reached 100%, with path efficiency up to 0.85 and throughput up to 0.44. Completion times improved across trials (e.g., 8.32s to 5.45s), remaining stable across arm positions. Results support SonoGlide’s robustness for intuitive, proportional, and position-invariant prosthetic control.

sessions.title: MIS: Dynamic & Time-Resolved Monitoring

papers.title: Simultaneous Catheter Trajectory Estimation and Vascular Mapping via Deep Learning of RF Signal Sequences from a Sparse Intravascular Ultrasound Array
papers.abstract: This study proposes a deep-learning framework to simultaneously estimate catheter trajectory and reconstruct a 3D vascular map using RF signal sequences from a sparse IVUS array. A neural network analyzes inter-frame time delays and phase shifts of echoes to estimate catheter displacement without external tracking. Multi-frame RF data are then integrated along the estimated trajectory to generate a wider-field map beyond a single frame. Simulation results (4 mm vessel model, 32 elements, 20 MHz) showed accurate trajectory estimation with a mean error of 0.33 mm and successful visualization of vessel-like structures. The method demonstrates potential for radiation-free navigation in microvascular interventions.

papers.title: 2D/3D Tissue Motion Compensation/Characterization Using Top-Orthogonal to Bottom-Electrode (TOBE) Arrays with Recursive Aperture-Decoded Ultrasound Imaging (READI)
papers.abstract: TOBE arrays can image large volumes outside the shadow of the aperture across multiple planes of the Fast Orthogonal Row-Column Electronic Scanning (FORCES) sequence. These volumes are susceptible to motion artifacts due to aperture encoding, preventing accurate tissue measurements and boundary identification under live conditions. READI is a beamforming technique for FORCES that enables characterization and compensation for tissue motion. This is tested by imaging a beating-heart phantom compressed by a servo at 120 BPM. READI successfully recovers chamber wall thickness and boundary sharpness compared to the static case and accurately measures wall velocity over multiple heartbeats. These results enable the use of TOBE arrays for dynamic tissue characterization over large volumes.

papers.title: Microbubble Tracking for Super Resolution Ultrasound Using a Spatio-Temporal Aware Neural Tracker with a Latent Ode Prior
papers.abstract: Super-resolution ultrasound (SR-US) leverages microbubbles (MB) to achieve sub-diffraction resolution of vascular structures through robust tracking. However, high acquisition rates and frame dropping to alleviate motion artifacts lead to non-uniform temporal spacing and sparse localizations. Traditional trackers struggle with missing frames, resulting in trajectory drift and identity switching. We propose TrajMB-ODE, a continuous time framework that propagates MB states through temporal gaps. TrajMB-ODE uses a variational autoencoder to encode motion history, kinematic priors, and spatio-temporal cues into a latent state. A neural ODE continuously evolves this latent state, learning autonomous dynamics with a spatio-temporal gate regulating updates to prevent occlusion-driven drift. The evolved state is mapped back to MB positions for track continuation through data association. Preliminary results using a modified Piepenbrock model for nonlinear flow show high tracking accuracy with RMSEs of 6.28-6.75 microns for simple/complex motion and 6.72-7.42 microns for track crossing and frame dropping. Phantom validation is underway to confirm performance in high density environments.

papers.title: Quantifying Motor Unit Velocities and Their Reproducibility in Human Skeletal Muscle Using Ultrafast Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Ultrafast ultrasound enables detection of individual motor units (MUs) by capturing the localised tissue motion induced by MU activation. However, prior studies have mainly reported MU activity in normalised units, limiting physiological interpretation. This study quantified absolute tissue velocities of individual MUs during voluntary contractions and evaluated their reproducibility. Ultrafast ultrasound and high-density surface electromyography were recorded simultaneously in the tibialis anterior of ten subjects during isometric contractions at 10% and 30% of maximum voluntary contraction. MU discharge times were used to extract MU-specific mechanical responses via spike-triggered averaging. Mean peak MU velocities were 60 ± 50 µm/s at 10% and 59 ± 46 µm/s at 30%, corresponding to displacements below the axial imaging resolution and requiring sub-pixel motion estimation. Reproducibility analysis showed a velocity difference of 23 ± 33 µm/s across repetitions. These findings demonstrate both the sensitivity of ultrafast ultrasound and the challenges of measuring sub-pixel tissue motion in vivo.

papers.title: Towards Realtime Interface Tracking Using Wearable M-Mode Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Applications of wearable ultrasound include using devices for prosthetic control and muscle force prediction. A difficulty exists in extracting the muscle boundary and tracking muscle deformation over time. Time Delay Spectrometry (TDS) was proposed as a low complexity hardware system that uses chirp excitation and encodes depths of scatters as different frequencies [1]. Since the information is in the frequency domain, time frequency analysis can be employed to extract muscle boundaries. Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) [2] is a data driven approach that decomposes a signal into intrinsic mode functions (IMF). These IMFs can be analyzed using the Hilbert-Huang transform and their instantaneous frequency (IF) extracted. This abstract explores the use of EMD on TDS data and compares it to spectral centroid (SC) approach tracking technique.

papers.title: Wearable Ultrasound Patch for Real-Time Breathing Monitoring: a New Tool for Enhancing Intraoperative Respiratory Safety
papers.abstract: Current clinical respiratory monitors like capnography lack sensitivity to regional changes and are prone to displacement. This study introduces a novel wearable ultrasound patch(5 MHz PZT) positioned at the Zone of Apposition(ZOA) for continuous, non-invasive breathing monitoring. We enrolled 49 intubated patients under controlled ventilation at various tidal volume(TV) levels. Three parameters—Pleural Elapsed Time, Pleural Absent Time, and Pleural Ratio(PR)—were extracted. Using each patient's first breath as a baseline, we calculated relative changes(∆PR and ∆TV). Results showed a strong correlation between ∆PR and ∆TV(ρ=0.8338). Leave-One-Subject-Out cross-validation (LOSO-CV) yielded rho = 0.881 and RMSE = 0.18, confirming robust cross-subject performance.This novel method directly monitors the changes of tidal volume thus remaining unaffected by factors such as mouth breathing, airway secretions, or sensor displacement. These findings confirm this wearable ultrasound patch as a robust tool for intraoperative respiratory monitoring, offering a reliable and innovative alternative to enhance patient safety during anesthesia.

papers.title: An ADC-Free Wearable Ultrasound System for Continuous Bladder Volume Monitoring
papers.abstract: Bladder volume monitoring is essential for managing lower urinary tract dysfunctions, yet current solutions rely on invasive catheters or bulky ultrasound systems requiring high-speed ADCs and trained operators, precluding continuous wearable use. Recent wearable ultrasound approaches enable multi-point A-mode sensing but still depend on full RF digitization, adding power and hardware overhead. This work presents a compact, low-power alternative that eliminates conventional ADCs entirely, instead employing an event-driven, comparator-based architecture to extract time-of-flight directly — demonstrating that accurate bladder monitoring is achievable with a fundamentally simpler hardware path suited for continuous wear.

sessions.title: MIS: Vascular Imaging & Monitoring

papers.title: Enhancing transcranial Blood Flow Imaging Using a Time Reversal Mirror – a Preliminary Study
papers.abstract: Transcranial ultrasound of cerebral blood flow is fundamentally limited by skull-induced attenuation, phase aberration, and scattering, which degrade Doppler sensitivity. This preliminary study introduces a time reversal (TR) mirror-based approach to overcome these physical barriers. By leveraging the reciprocity of wave propagation, the method focuses more acoustic energy onto targeted intracranial flow regions, thereby strengthening backscattered echoes. The proposed TR method uses blood flow signals as guide sources for adaptive enhancement. It was evaluated via k-Wave numerical simulations using a digital skull phantom and a ring-array transducer. Doppler signals were acquired, time-reversed, and re-transmitted to automatically focus on specific flow regions. A dedicated reconstruction algorithm then generated the enhanced blood flow images. The TR approach effectively compensated for skull-induced aberrations and attenuation, increasing the blood-flow-to-tissue contrast ratio to 3.48, compared to 2.33 for conventional Doppler.

papers.title: Ultrasound-Based Semi-Supervised Vulnerable Plaque Classification Using an Improved UniMatch and Tabular Foundation Model with Interpretable Features
papers.abstract: This study addresses the challenge of limited annotated data for automatic carotid plaque analysis in ultrasound. We improve an UniMatch-based semi-supervised segmentation model by integrating a flexible information block and multi-scale deep supervision with pyramid consistency loss, boosting segmentation performance by up to 8% on multicenter data. For classification, we design a multi-round sampling-with-replacement semi-supervised strategy for the TabPFN tabular foundation model to generate reliable pseudo-labels, fully leveraging abundant unlabeled data. This approach uncovers seven interpretable features, including plaque burden, geometry, and shape, and improves vulnerable plaque classification by over 10%. This method offers a promising, interpretable solution for automated stroke risk assessment.

papers.title: Low-Frequency Chirp-Coded Diverging-Wave Imaging with Sound-Speed Correction for Transcranial Deep-Vessel Super-Resolution
papers.abstract: Low-frequency ultrasound improves transcranial penetration, but skull attenuation and wavefront aberration weaken deep echoes and introduce phase distortion, limiting deep-vessel super-resolution imaging. We evaluated low-frequency Chirp-coded diverging-wave imaging with sound-speed correction using transcranial point targets. Experiments used a Verasonics Vantage system, a 64-element P4-2v probe, a 3D-printed resin skull phantom, and a Gammex Sono403 phantom. Single-pulse and 8-μs, 2.25-MHz-bandwidth Chirp-coded transmissions, both centered at 2.5 MHz, were compared with four-angle diverging-wave compounding. Chirp echoes were pulse-compressed before reconstruction. Skull sound speed was estimated from head waves, and skull boundaries were extracted using Dijkstra’s algorithm to compute a transcranial delay field for global phase correction. Chirp pulse compression increased deep RF envelopes, with SNR/CNR gains of 6.22/2.52 dB in the deep ROI and ~20 mm greater detection depth, while maintaining a maximum main-axis mechanical index (MI) of 0.133. Sound-speed correction improved point-target focusing and reduced mean axial localization error by ~2.62 mm.

papers.title: Femoral Artery Bifurcation Detection from Free-Hand Ultrasound Sweeps with Deep Learning
papers.abstract: Hemorrhage is the leading preventable cause of death in trauma. Resuscitative Endovascular Balloon Occlusion of the Aorta (REBOA) requires rapid, accurate common femoral artery (CFA) access which is challenging in austere settings. We present a hybrid automated femoral artery bifurcation detection framework using deep-learning object detection and signal processing on freehand ultrasound sweeps. A single-stage detector localized femoral artery and vein per frame; low-confidence arterial detections were filtered and temporal bounding-box area changes identified bifurcation frames. We trained and evaluated models on 573 videos (176,475 frames) from 204 patients across three EDs, annotated by two vascular sonographers. In 5-fold cross-validation our method achieved mean accuracy 86.5 ± 4.7%, outperforming a 2D CNN classifier at 72.3 ± 4.5%. These results demonstrate feasibility of automated CFA localization to guide REBOA and other CFA-dependent procedures for less-trained users.

papers.title: SPADA: A Robust Algorithm for Ultrasound B-Mode Image-Based Sub-Pixel Arterial Diameter Tracking Towards Continuous Non-Invasive BP Measurement
papers.abstract: Ultrasound can enable continuous, non-invasive blood pressure (BP) measurement. For accurate BP monitoring, precise arterial diameter tracking is crucial. However, current ultrasound-based diameter tracking methods rely on raw data, inaccessible on most clinical systems, while B-mode-based tracking lacks required accuracy. This work hypothesizes that sub-pixel precision can overcome these limitations and introduces the deterministic SPADA (Sub-Pixel Arterial Diameter Analysis) algorithm for B-mode images. SPADA estimates the vessel center and applies radial scanline profiling. Gaussian fitting of the second derivative profiles enables sub-pixel wall localization beyond the sampling limit. Validation on simulated B-mode images showed low bias (-0.044 ± 0.017 mm) and tight limits of agreement (0.012 to 0.072 mm). In vivo, SPADA reconstructed physiologically plausible diameter waveforms from video sequences. In comparison, manually annotated waveforms showed high intra-observer variability. Both simulated and in-vivo results demonstrate SPADA as an accurate algorithm, enabling sub-pixel diameter estimation from standard B-mode images, which facilitates BP measurement.

papers.title: Hankel-Matrix-Based Sparse Compounding for Enhancing Twinkling Artifact Signals in Low Sensitivity Doppler Imaging
papers.abstract: Twinkling artifact (TA) is a Doppler imaging phenomenon characterized by rapid color fluctuations and can serve as a potential Doppler biomarker for biopsy markers associated with microcalcifications (MCs). However, TA visibility is highly dependent on acoustic energy sensitivity and becomes weak under low-transmit-voltage or off-focus conditions. This study proposes Hankel-matrix-based sparse compounding (HMSC) to enhance weak TA signals in low-sensitivity Doppler imaging. Ensemble-direction IQ signals are embedded into Hankel matrices using varying temporal segments, window lengths, and neighboring spatial pixels. Singular value decomposition estimates the dominant left singular subspace, and projection errors are used to quantify ensemble variations and spatiotemporal inconsistencies. Robust principal component analysis then isolates sparse TA-related components, which are compounded to generate a TA-enhanced image. Phantom and in vivo results show that HMSC improves TA visualization, increases SNR and CNR, and enhances weak MC-related TA signals compared with conventional IIR filtering.

papers.title: High Frequency Ultrasound Microvascular Imaging for Assessing the Neovascularization in Tenosynovitis
papers.abstract: Tenosynovitis is an inflammatory tendon sheath disorder associated with pain and pathological neovascularization. Conventional ultrasound has limited sensitivity to microvascular changes, while ultrasound localization microscopy provides super-resolution imaging but requires microbubble contrast agents, limiting clinical use. We propose a contrast-free super-resolution high-frequency ultrasound method to visualize peritendinous microvasculature. The approach uses ultrafast imaging, clutter filtering, and erythrocyte-based flow tracking to reconstruct vascular networks without contrast agents. This enables high-resolution, non-invasive assessment of microvascular changes and provides a tool for evaluating disease activity and treatment response in tenosynovitis

sessions.title: MTC: Bone, Skull & Neural Tissue Characterization

papers.title: Dependence of Piezoelectric Signal on Ultrasound Signal Propagated Through Cancellous Bone
papers.abstract: The piezoelectric signal generated in cancellous bone by ultrasound irradiation can largely depend on the ultrasound signal propagated through the bone. In this study, the piezoelectric and ultrasound signals were simultaneously observed, and the dependence of the piezoelectric signal on the ultrasound signal was investigated. The simultaneous observation was performed using a piezoelectric cell (PE-cell). The PE-cell is an ultrasound sensor, in which a cancellous bone specimen is set as a piezoelectric element. In the modified PE-cell, a receiving device for the ultrasound signal propagated through the cancellous bone specimen was added. Ultrasound pulse waves at 1, 2, and 3 MHz were radiated to the PE-cell. In both the piezoelectric and ultrasound signals, two waves could be observed. The two waves in the ultrasound signal corresponded to "fast and slow waves" which propagate mainly in the trabecular and pore parts. It was considered that the former and later waves of the piezoelectric signal were contributed to the fast and slow waves, respectively. Both amplitude ratios of the former and later piezoelectric waves to the fast and slow waves increased with frequency.

papers.title: 3D-Printed Subject-Specific Human Skull Acoustic Phantom Using PLA-CaCO3 Composites
papers.abstract: We present a cost-effective, 3D-printed acoustic phantom that trying to replicate subject-specific human skull acoustics for transcranial ultrasound testing. By combining a tunable PLA-CaCO₃ composite with FDM micro-architectures, we decouple bulk acoustic impedance (adjusted via CaCO₃ doping) from local porosity (controlled through infill patterns). At 30% CaCO₃, the composite achieves a density of 1.42 g/cm³, sound speed of 1944 m/s, and impedance of 2.76 MRayl. Critically, the FDM approach faithfully reproduces micro‑CT-derived trabecular diploë structures, surpassing homogeneous cast phantoms in anatomical realism. Although impedance remains below that of human cortical bone (4–6 MRayl), this prototype validates on‑demand printing of patient‑specific porous cranial acoustics. The platform offers an accessible, realistic testbed for developing transcranial therapies and imaging, with future work targeting impedance optimization and direct acoustic propagation validation.

papers.title: Ultrasound Elastography-Based Spatial Quantification of Mechanical Heterogeneity for Intraoperative Assessment of Peripheral Nerve Injury
papers.abstract: Accurate intraoperative delineation of peripheral nerve injury remains challenging due to spatially heterogeneous structural remodeling. This work investigates shear-wave elastography (SWE) for spatially resolved quantification of mechanical properties and introduces a centerline-based framework for extracting continuous stiffness profiles. Ex vivo porcine nerve specimens were imaged using SWE, and color-encoded data were converted to quantitative shear wave velocity (SWV) values through calibrated mapping. Spatial sampling along the nerve axis enabled reconstruction of continuous SWV profiles spanning proximal, lesion, and distal regions. Injured regions exhibited elevated SWV relative to surrounding tissue, with profiles revealing localized stiffness gradients and transitions corresponding to lesion boundaries. This approach enables reproducible quantification of mechanical heterogeneity and extends elastography beyond qualitative imaging toward spatially resolved tissue characterization. These findings support SWE-derived spatial profiling as a potential tool for intraoperative assessment of peripheral nerve injury.

papers.title: Phase aberration-Corrected Ultrasound Imaging Through bone-Mimicking Plates
papers.abstract: Generally, skull aberration correction utilizes the backscattered echoes from individual microbubbles. In this study, an alternative “skull aware” approach is proposed. First, the local thickness and velocity of the aberrating structure are estimated. Then, taking into account refraction through this structure, delay-and-sum beamforming is performed to obtain a spatially-resolved image. Ultrasound data were acquired from four dense bone-mimicking plates and three porous bone-mimicking plates with 30% air content, with thicknesses of 2, 4, and 6 mm. A verasonics vantage NXT research ultrasound system equipped with a 2.8 MHz linear array probe was used to scan each plate using single-element transmission acquisitions. A phantom containing 100 µm diameter wires was positioned behind the aberrating plates. The ultrasound wave speed within the plates was estimated using a refraction-corrected autofocusing approach combined with the spatial coherence of RF signals. Plate thickness was measured directly from the reconstructed ultrasound images. The wire phantom was imaged using three-layer homogeneous refraction-corrected beamforming for aberration correction.

papers.title: High-Resolution, Specimen-Specific Speed-of-Sound Mapping in Human Skull
papers.abstract: Accurate, high-resolution skull SoS maps are desirable for transcranial ultrasound research but are currently unavailable. This study proposes a method for high-resolution, specimen-specific SoS mapping with improved accuracy over empirical HU-SoS mapping. The method integrates through-transmission ultrasound with high-resolution micro-CT. Ultrasound measurements were performed using a 1 MHz single-element transducer and an aligned capsule hydrophone, with 2D raster scanning to obtain a low-resolution SoS map. The same specimen was scanned using micro-CT to resolve skull microarchitecture, including trabecular structure and diploë porosity. The proposed method significantly outperformed empirical HU-SoS mapping, providing a powerful tool for studying skull acoustic properties and aberration correction techniques.

papers.title: Evaluation of Microstructural Anisotropy and age-Related Variation in Quantitative Ultrasound in the Neonatal Brain
papers.abstract: Despite substantial efforts to ultrasonically-characterize brain tissue ex-vivo, in vivo quantitative ultrasound (QUS) imaging remains elusive due to the brain’s structural macro- and micro-structural complexity and its variation with age. This study evaluated anisotropy-related and age-related variations in QUS features in the thalamus of healthy babies. Anisotropy was assessed by comparing coronal and sagittal views, and coronal measurements were compared between newborns and infants. In neonates, ESS and AC did not differ significantly between time points in either view. After averaging across time points, ESS was significantly higher in the sagittal than in the coronal view. AC also differed significantly between views. These findings suggest microstructural anisotropy, as expected in thalamic gray matter. Coronal comparisons between newborns and infants, acquired with different scanners, showed a significant difference only for AC, while ESS showed no detectable age-related difference.

sessions.title: MSD: Advanced Ultrasound Technologies and Applications

papers.title: 3D contrast-Free Super Resolution Microvasculature Imaging of Tumor Through the Concentric Rotational Scanning Approach
papers.abstract: High-frequency ultrasound (HFUS) lacks 2D array transducers for real-time 3D imaging, making mechanical linear scanning common but limited by inter-frame gaps and slow speed. This study proposes a concentric rotational scanning approach using a 40 MHz transducer with synchronized motor control. A 180° rotation captures a full cylindrical volume, and 2D data are reconstructed into 3D images via polar-to-Cartesian interpolation. Phantom and in vivo tumor experiments demonstrate accurate reconstruction and clear microvascular visualization, indicating improved spatial continuity and imaging efficiency over conventional linear scanning.

papers.title: An Optimized Ultrasound Helmet for Human whole-Brain 3D Ultrasound Localization Microscopy (ULM)
papers.abstract: We propose an analytical framework to optimize ultrasound helmet designs, using a geometric approach and Snell’s law to model wave reflections. A 3112-element helmet (1 MHz, 10 cm radius) was designed, split into hexagonal/pentagonal pads. Simulations show improved resolution and reduced grating lobes with randomized multilens pads, enhancing pressure homogeneity, especially in cortical areas, making it promising for whole-brain 3D Ultrasound Localization Microscopy.

papers.title: Tool-Tip Tissue-Awareness (T3A) – a Non-Contact Photoacoustic Beacon for Surgical Safety: a Feasibility Study
papers.abstract: We present Tool-Tip Tissue Awareness (T3A), a novel non-contact photoacoustic guidance paradigm for continuous intraoperative sensing. Unlike conventional ultrasound or photoacoustic imaging, which require visual interpretation and may interrupt workflow, T3A provides real-time, intuitive feedback on the presence of target tissue using an active photoacoustic beacon. A compact multi-mode fiber integrated with a tunable pulsed laser delivers localized excitation near the surgical tool tip, while a laser Doppler vibrometer (LDV) remotely detects the generated signals at a standoff distance of ~7 cm. Adaptive threshold-based processing enables robust beacon localization, and a GPU-accelerated pipeline converts detection events into low-latency (<30 ms) auditory feedback for immediate operator awareness. Phantom experiments demonstrate reliable detection with high contrast and consistent localization. These results establish feasibility of a signal-driven sensing approach that complements or bypasses image-based guidance, offering a scalable path toward real-time, non-contact surgical safety systems.

papers.title: A Handheld Dual Motor Scanner with Three Degrees of Freedom for Photoacoustic Imaging of Curved Surfaces
papers.abstract: Photoacoustic imaging on curved or irregular tissue surfaces is limited by unstable probe-tissue coupling, inconsistent scanning trajectories, and poor repeatability during manual operation. This work presents a surface-adaptive handheld 3-DOF dual-motor scanner for repeatable photoacoustic imaging on nonplanar targets. The scanner uses a motorized X-axis for linear scanning, a motorized Y-axis for probe angle adjustment, and a spring-based passive Z-axis with a 5 mm compliant displacement range to compensate local surface variations and maintain contact. The prototype is designed for integration with an existing photoacoustic acquisition platform equipped with a linear-array ultrasound probe. Preliminary handheld imaging visualized vascular targets, confirming the feasibility of the imaging configuration. The proposed scanner provides controllable probe motion and adaptive contact, supporting future quantitative evaluation on flat and curved phantoms and three-dimensional reconstruction.

papers.title: Smart Ultrasound-Based Non-Invasive ICP Monitoring Through Multi-Layer Skull Echo Features and AR-Guided Visualization
papers.abstract: Intraoperative ultrasound (iUS) helps localize brain tumors and assess resection extent, but speckle noise, acoustic shadowing, hyperechoic artifacts, and resection-induced tissue changes make automated boundary identification challenging. We developed a deep learning workflow to detect four structures in intraoperative 3D brain ultrasound: tumor, resection cavity, sulci, and falx cerebri. A total of 17,362 annotated 2D slices were extracted from 69 3D B-mode volumes of 23 patients in the public RESECT and RESECT-SEG datasets, covering before-, during-, and after-resection stages. A YOLOv8 model was trained for multiclass detection, and a cross-slice consistency check flagged continuous or discontinuous detections. In slice-level internal validation, the model achieved an mAP50 of 92% and mAP50-95 of 73%, with confusion-matrix diagonal values of 0.91, 0.88, 0.84, and 0.84 for tumor, resection cavity, sulci, and falx cerebri, respectively. These results demonstrate the preliminary feasibility of YOLOv8 for multi-structure detection in iUS. Because a slice-level data split was used, cross-patient generalization requires confirmation through patient-level validation.

papers.title: Near-Eye Motorized Led Fixation for Controlled Lateral Rectus B-Mode Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: This project presents a near-eye, motorized LED fixation system for obtaining B-mode ultrasound images of the lateral rectus (LR) muscle. The goal is to image the LR of the right eye at controlled horizontal gaze angles while avoiding obstruction of the left viewing eye by the ultrasound probe. The system uses calibrated LED positions to guide gaze from −40° to +40° in 10° steps, allowing the LR to be visualized across different contraction states. The acquired LR images can be segmented to quantify region properties, including muscle thickness and mean pixel intensity, and to compare these measurements across gaze positions. Future work will focus on improving synchronization between the LED sequence and ultrasound acquisition, selecting efficient video key frames, and improving the robustness and alignment stability of the motorized setup.

papers.title: Real-Time, Sensor-Free Transducer Surface Temperature Monitoring Using an H-Bridge Transceiver with an Active Clamp
papers.abstract: We present a real-time ultrasound transducer temperature (TP) tracking approach using an H-bridge transceiver with an active clamp. Unlike T/R switches, transducer elements stay connected to the receiver during transmit for direct reception of the transmit signal. The active clamp provides a low-impedance path to ground at high-voltage transmit, then turns off to pass the full reflected signal. Since piezoelectric properties are TP-dependent, the received transmit signal’s vary with TP, enabling thermal monitoring without external sensors. Experiments used 2 different transducers in a water bath with slow and rapid TP changes. Probes were driven at 20 V, 4-cycle waveforms at 3.3 and 7.8 MHz. The transmit signal was then averaged across 64 channels and phase determined vs. time. Probes surface TP was measured with an infrared thermometer. Phase inverse vs. TP showed strong correlation: Pearson r=0.97 for slow and r=0.90 for rapid changes. Lower r likely reflects reduced infrared accuracy under rapid changes, not a technique limitation. This method enables real-time transducer TP monitoring and safety thresholds that halt transmission at critical TP, protecting system and patient

papers.title: Phase-Shift Beam Steering for CMUT Transcranial Focused Ultrasound Arrays
papers.abstract: Clinical implementation of transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) for blood-brain barrier (BBB)opening systems typically use digital pulse drive signals and true time delay (TTD) architectures. This approach requires accurate time delays and can generate undesired nonlinearities and harmonic distortion complicating microbubble harmonics detection especially for CMUT arrays. Considering typical 10ms long, CW like therapy signals, this study proposes and validates phase-shift beam steering of long pure tone bursts as a functionally equivalent, electronically simpler alternative with less nonlinearity to drive CMUT modules for BBB opening.

papers.title: Volumetric Topology Optimization for Arbitrary 3D Beam Shaping in Transcranial Acoustic Holography
papers.abstract: Transcranial focused ultrasound is limited by skull aberrations and by the geometric complexity of deep-brain targets. 3D-printed acoustic holograms offer an economical alternative to dense phased arrays, but conventional design relies on the thin-element approximation and planar (single-plane) loss functions, yielding elongated needle foci or unintentionally apodized lenses. We introduce Volumetric Gradient Descent (VGD), a fully differentiable multiplane scheme built on the heterogeneous angular spectrum approach that records pressure at every slice within a 3D region of interest and directly optimizes lens thickness. Three formulations are demonstrated through a patient-specific skull at 1 MHz: an anisotropic 3D-Gaussian cigar focus (FWHM 2.12 × 13.28 mm) for tract-like targets; an l = 1 acoustic vortex with a persistent on-axis null; and an energy-maximization formulation reaching 2.01 mm lateral FWHM (~1.34 λ) near the diffraction limit. VGD enables anatomy-matched 3D beam shaping

papers.title: Conformal Acoustic Holography for Enhanced Transcranial Therapeutic Ultrasound
papers.abstract: This research develops personalized, skull-conforming acoustic holographic lenses (AHLs) for noninvasive transcranial ultrasound therapy, including neuromodulation and blood-brain barrier opening.
