The key innovation encodes patient-specific wavefront corrections into 3D-printed lens geometry, with elastomeric coupling layers that conform to cranial anatomy while minimizing impedance mismatch. Validation using ex vivo skulls confirms accurate volumetric ultrasound field control across complex surfaces. The scalable framework supports clinical transcranial focused ultrasound applications, with future work extending toward multi-hologram architectures for enhanced volumetric control.

sessions.title: MPA: Novel Techniques for Signal Processing in Photoacoustic Imaging

papers.title: Viscoelastic Characterization of Biological Tissues via Photoacoustic Damped Oscillation Modeling
papers.abstract: Conventional photoacoustic (PA) oversimplify tissues as elastic, ignoring viscous damping and hindering decoupled quantification of Young’s modulus (E) and viscosity coefficient (η). This work integrated the Kelvin-Voigt relation into the thermoelastic wave equation. Finite element method (FEM) simulated the full multi-physics cascade in viscoelastic absorbers and parametric sweeps analyzed modulation effects. Experimentally, a PA platform validated the method using graded agarose phantoms and ex vivo tissues. Simulations reveal that E governs the frequency-domain, η dominates time-domain attenuation behavior with minimal frequency influence. Elasticity-independent indicators (peak attenuation coefficient, peak attenuation time, number of oscillation peaks, and peak attenuation rate) were identified for η quantification. Phantom experiments confirmed fc increases monotonically with agar concentration (modulating E), while attenuation accelerates with castor oil concentration (modulating η). Ex-vivo studies verified the method distinguishes high-elasticity tissues (lean meat, chicken heart) from high-viscosity tissues (fat, liver) via unique time-frequency signatures.

papers.title: Anharmonic DFT Simulation of NIR Spectra for Wavelength Optimization in Vibrational Photoacoustic Imaging
papers.abstract: Vibrational photoacoustic (VPA) imaging enables label-free tissue contrast via molecular overtone absorptions. However, inconsistent empirical data for lipid and collagen wavelength selection limits diagnostic precision. This study establishes a first-principles computational framework to resolve these discrepancies.A hierarchical approach was developed, combining Boltzmann-weighted harmonic DFT on full structures with anharmonic calculations (GVPT2) on model systems to predict NIR spectra. Results matched experimental spectra of porcine adipose and rat tail tendon. GVPT2 predicted lipid CH2​ overtones at 1729 and 1175 nm, while the collagen NH overtone was predicted at 1499 nm.Ex vivo VPA imaging validated these findings, achieving high contrast (2.74-fold for lipid at 1210 nm; 1.86-fold for collagen at 1499 nm) and orthogonal discrimination without spectral unmixing. Application to skin tissues revealed significantly elevated collagen and reduced lipid in SCC compared to normal skin, aligning with tumor-associated desmoplasia. This study provides a rigorous theoretical basis for wavelength optimization in clinical VPA diagnostics.

papers.title: Patch-Based Sub-Aperture Pixel-Wise Correlation for Artifact Suppression in Linear Array Based Photoacoustic Imaging
papers.abstract: Linear array photoacoustic imaging (PAI) suffers from restricted angular coverage and background noise, especially under hardware multiplexing constraints. Conventional coherence methods like Coherence Factor (CF) reduce artifacts but often inadvertently attenuate valid absorber signals. This work proposes a novel Patch-Based Sub-aperture Pixel-Wise Correlation (PS-PWC) framework to suppress background artifacts while strictly preserving the amplitude and geometry of actual absorbers. PS-PWC utilizes spatial correlation across overlapping sub-apertures. Acquired RF data are divided using a sliding window, followed by Delay-and-Sum (DAS) beamforming per sub-aperture. Local pixel patches are compared to a mean reference using normalized cross-correlation. Positive correlations form a spatial coherence map, from which an active contour model generates a binary mask applied to the full-aperture DAS image.
keywords: Patch-Based Sub-aperture Pixel-Wise Correlation for Artifact Suppression in Linear Array based Photoacoustic Imaging

papers.title: Phase-Stabilized Iterative Coherence Factor (PS-iCF) Beamforming for High Contrast Photoacoustic Imaging
papers.abstract: Photoacoustic (PA) imaging often operates at restricted optical energy levels for safety reasons, which can lead to low SNR and reduced image contrast. Conventional delay-and-sum (DAS) beamforming suffers from high sidelobes, while coherence-based methods such as the coherence factor (CF) provide only modest improvements. The iterative coherence factor (iCF) has recently been introduced to enhance coherent signal components; however, it does not explicitly enforce phase consistency. In this work, we propose a Phase-Stabilized Iterative Coherence Factor (PS-iCF) beamformer that incorporates a phase stability constraint to suppress incoherent contributions and improve image contrast under low-fluence conditions.

papers.title: Data-Driven Optical Fluence Compensation for Low-Power Photoacoustic Imaging
papers.abstract: Photoacoustic (PA) imaging is limited by laser safety constraints that restrict the maximum optical fluence delivered to tissue. While higher fluence improves signal amplitude and contrast, it cannot be used in vivo. As a result, low-fluence imaging often suffers from reduced contrast and poor visualization of vascular structures. In this work, we propose a data-driven framework to compensate for low-fluence PA signals by learning a mapping from low- to high-fluence acquisitions. The goal is to recover high-contrast image quality while maintaining safe optical exposure for in vivo imaging.

papers.title: Investigating the Impact of Gold Nanoparticle Size and Clustering on Cellular Pa Imaging
papers.abstract: Gold nanoparticles are commonly used as contrast agents for photoacoustic imaging due to their tunable spectral properties and strong absorbance. Gold nanospheres demonstrate great biostability, making them a popular choice for cell tracking applications. However, their ability to be imaged at longer wavelengths is a result of random clustering that occurs after being endocytosed by cells, leading to unpredictable signals. Hyperbranched gold nanoconstructs are an emerging platform that exhibit black-body like absorbance and maintain consistent photoacoustic signal throughout the cell labeling process. Here, we aim to investigate the influence of gold nanoparticle shape and size on cell uptake preferences and PA signal generation to develop a platform that can be used to inform future cell tracking applications.

sessions.title: MSR: At the turning point-spread-function

papers.title: STCLNet: a Lightweight Spatiotemporal Context Localization Network for Efficient High-Concentration Ultrasound Localization Microscopy
papers.abstract: Ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) enables super-resolution vascular imaging beyond the acoustic diffraction limit. Temporal information can improve microbubble localization performance under high-concentration conditions, which is important for shortening acquisition time in practical ULM. However, existing temporal localization networks usually adopt multi-frame input but single-frame output, resulting in inefficient temporal information utilization and increased processing burden for the large amount of data involved in ULM. The objective of this work is to develop a more efficient temporal localization network for ULM that can exploit temporal information more effectively while maintaining low model complexity.

papers.title: Quantitative Classification of Targeted Microbubble Behavior in Ultrasound Molecular Imaging
papers.abstract: Ultrasound molecular imaging (UMI) uses targeted microbubble contrast agents to noninvasively image disease-specific vascular biomarkers. However, current protocols can take up to 30 minutes and often assume stable adhesion, overlooking transient attachment and detachment. Although RPCA-based methods can nondestructively separate bound and free microbubble signals, they are limited to population-level analysis. We developed a multistage MATLAB pipeline that extends RPCA decomposition for single-bubble detection, localization, tracking, and behavioral classification. Beamformed k-Wave simulations and in vitro data from an integrin-incubated channel were processed using SVD prefiltering, RPCA decomposition, and Kalman filter tracking. Bubbles were classified as free, bound, transiently attached, or detached. Simulation results agreed with ground truth across all states, validating the pipeline. In vitro results from eight experiments showed a ~40% increase in bound fraction by 6 minutes, stabilizing through 14 minutes, while the free fraction decreased by ~45%, consistent with optical observations. This work enables nondestructive, time-resolved analysis for quantitative UMI.

papers.title: Deconvolution and Differentiated Tracking for Plane-Wave Super-Resolution Imaging Using Erythrocytes
papers.abstract: Super-resolution ultrasound imaging using erythrocytes (SURE) is a promising technique for contrast-agent-free, high-resolution vascular imaging within seconds. In this work, we investigate the feasibility of plane-wave-based SURE (PW-SURE) for in vivo microvascular density mapping and flow visualization. In vivo rat-kidney data were acquired on a Verasonics platform using a 15-MHz, 128-element linear array. Plane-wave data were first beamformed, compounded, and demodulated into IQ data. The IQ data were then processed by motion correction, SVD clutter filtering, and deconvolution. Erythrocyte-related signals were localized with an overlapping patch-based detector, and the localized positions were accumulated to form super-resolved density maps. For flow estimation, localization-based tracking was used mainly in small and medium vessels, while direct speckle-based tracking was used in larger vessels. Using 3 s of in vivo data, PW-SURE produced renal density and directional velocity maps with sharper vascular boundaries than power Doppler. Representative density profiles showed an average FWHM of 45.9 μm for PW-SURE, compared with 180.8 μm for PD.

papers.title: Selective Nonlinear Microbubble Detection for Super-Resolution Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: Ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) enables visualization of microvascular structures beyond the diffraction limit through localization of individual microbubbles (MBs). However, most current approaches model MBs as broadband scatterers despite their strongly size-dependent resonance behaviour. Clinical MBs are polydisperse, with nonlinear responses that vary with transmit frequency and acoustic pressure, affecting detectability and localization accuracy. A better understanding of frequency-dependent microbubble dynamics could enable improved contrast specificity and adaptive imaging strategies. This study investigates the relationship between bubble diameter, transmit frequency, and mechanical index (MI) using multi-pulse imaging, with the aim of enabling selective microbubble detection for ULM.

papers.title: Development of Advanced Ultrasound Flow Imaging: from Vector Flow Imaging to Microvascular Super-Resolution
papers.abstract: This study presents a contrast-free super-resolution imaging (SRI) and Doppler-based vector flow imaging (VFI) that employs multi-directional diverging wave transmissions (Tx) and an SVD clutter filter. Vector velocity can be reconstructed using least square from estimated velocity components. By compounding data from multiple angles, SRI is implemented via localizing the centroid of erythrocyte cluster with radiality preprocessing after SVD filtering and interpolation. Both high and low pulse repetition frequency (PRF) are utilized for velocity component estimation and de-aliasing. A convex probe was used to scan abdominal vessels. After de-aliasing, the VFI results were superimposed on the SRI map. For a large vessel, the estimated velocities from VFI were compared to those from PW. The mean velocity was 19.44 cm/s for PW, and 21.9±2.6 cm/s for VFI after de-aliasing. Vessels at different levels of the renal vasculature can be visualized, where the VFI arrows were superimposed on it. Combining SRI with VFI allows processing steps reuse, enabling efficient development of clinical system for simultaneous quantification and super-resolution of flow in different vessel sizes.

papers.title: Simulation-Trained Deep Learning for Microbubble Localization: Toward Clinical Translation of Ultrasound Super-Resolution Imaging
papers.abstract: Ultrasound Localization Microscopy (ULM) enables super-resolution vascular imaging by localizing individual microbubbles across thousands of frames. Deep learning approaches have shown promise for microbubble localization; however, they typically require large annotated training datasets that are unavailable for in vivo scenarios. Moreover, most existing studies rely on research-grade open platforms, leaving a significant gap toward clinical translation with commercially available systems. This work aims to establish a simulation-to-clinical transfer pathway for deep learning ULM, where a network trained solely on simulated data is directly applied to in vivo data from a commercial scanner, without manual annotation or research platforms.

papers.title: Multi-Stage Motion Correction with Complex-Valued Optimization
papers.abstract: Multi-stage motion correction for super-resolution ultrasound was developed to reduce tissue-motion artifacts from pulsatility and breathing. The pipeline combines rigid Lucas-Kanade correction, B-mode optimization, motion-error detection and repair, and complex-valued IQ optimization. It was evaluated on transcutaneous rat-kidney super-resolution and contrast-free power-Doppler datasets, plus simulation. Compared with intensity-based imregdemons and Transverse-Oscillation methods, the proposed approach improved vessel recovery, reduced residual tissue signal, and achieved lower simulated motion error while running substantially faster than imregdemons.

papers.title: Localization Strategies for Superharmonic ULM Using a Single Frame of Complex Data
papers.abstract: Ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) employs microbubble (MB) contrast agents, ultrafast acquisition of large B-Mode image sets (~10^5), filtering, localization, and tracking of MB responses, and accumulation of MB trajectories. The need for spatiotemporal filtering may be removed by using a dual-frequency transducer and isolating the 4th-order harmonic MB response. In this work, we develop a MB localization strategy using a single frame of simulated complex 4th-order harmonic beamformed data acquired with a diverging-wave transmit (DWT) and multiple receive apodizations for several point scatterer positions. Our localization approach tracked changes in absolute and relative complex magnitude and phase across a quadrant of four focal coordinates nearest the PSF maximum magnitude. Localization error was taken as the L2-norm between the estimated and ground truth locations of each point scatterer. The localization error across all points was less than 100 µm and typically increased with range and focal angle. This novel single-frame localization strategy has the potential to offer robust, real-time ULM in limited-aperture contexts (i.e., transcranial or cardiac ultrasound).

papers.title: Detecting Flow Perturbations in Bioprinted Microvasculature Using Volumetric ULM
papers.abstract: Bioprinted liver constructs require perfusable microvascular networks with controlled flow, yet lack volumetric, high-resolution functional validation. Here, bioprinted vascular channels serve as a controlled platform for volumetric ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM). An omega-shaped channel (~500 µm) was fabricated using an acellular bioink. Microbubbles (1:2000) were perfused, and volumetric ULM (~250 volumes/s) enabled super-resolved density and velocity mapping, compared with computational fluid dynamics (CFD). ULM resolved 3D geometry and detected fabrication-induced deviations, including constrictions and outlet narrowing. Velocity mapping showed coherent flow with localized acceleration, though measured increase (1.7×) was lower than CFD prediction (2.4×), indicating viscous effects and geometric variability. These results demonstrate that volumetric ULM enables sensitive detection of structural and flow deviations for validating bioprinted vascular constructs.

sessions.title: MTN: Brain and cancer theranostics

papers.title: Acoustic Distance-Based Correction of Optical Tracking Errors for Transcranial Focused Ultrasound Neuromodulation
papers.abstract: Optical tracking–based neuronavigation is commonly used to guide transcranial focused ultrasound (FUS), but inherent tracking errors of several millimeters can compromise targeting accuracy. This work proposes a fully acoustic correction method that leverages element-to-skull distances from a 128-element spherical FUS array to refine the tracked position. In simulation, optical tracking error was modeled by applying rigid transforms with pseudo-random translational and rotational perturbations to the array's position relative to a CT-derived skull. A grid search over six degrees of freedom identified the correction that best matched element–skull distances to their expected ground truth values. A cascaded two-round refinement further improved accuracy. Results demonstrated significant reductions in both translational and rotational errors, bringing multi-millimeter tracking errors below one millimeter. In practice, the required distance measurements could be obtained from pulse-echo time-of-flight data already available on large hemispherical therapeutic arrays, making this a potential low-cost augmentation to existing optical tracking workflows.

papers.title: MRI-Free CT-Ultrasound Skull Registration Using a Dual-Mode CMUT tFUS/Imaging Arrays
papers.abstract: Transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) requires accurate skull-to-array registration for phase-aberration correction, but conventional CT-to-MRI workflows add time, cost, and MRI dependence. Prior CT-US methods used iterative closest point (ICP) alignment between sparse pulse-echo skull reflections and CT surfaces, which can be sensitive to pose and noise. We propose an MRI-free CT-US framework using a hemispherical CMUT dome that fuses sparse tFUS pulse-echo with localized high-frequency US-Cross imaging. The simulated system includes a 128-element CMUT pulse-echo array on a 15-cm-radius dome and a secondary 3.5-MHz CMUT imaging layer. Skull/scalp surfaces were segmented from 3D head CT data and imported into Field II. Beamformed images were processed by Canny edge detection to extract two orthogonal skull contours. ICP used pulse-echo points alone or a fused point set combining pulse-echo echoes with US-Cross contours. Twenty-five translated (±1 cm) and rotated (±5°) poses were evaluated with added pulse-echo noise. Fusion improved mean displacement error from 1.41 to 0.33 mm at 0.5-mm noise, from 3.74 to 0.82 mm at 1.0-mm noise, and from 9.58 to 4.05 mm at 2.0-mm noise.

papers.title: Volumetric Ultrasound Displacement Tracking for Monitoring Transcranial Ultrasound Neuromodulation
papers.abstract: Focused ultrasound neuromodulation enables noninvasive brain stimulation, but the link between induced tissue motion and neural response is not well understood. This work uses high-frame-rate volumetric ultrasound to track microscale displacements during 1 MHz transcranial stimulation in vivo in mice. Displacements were measured using co-aligned plane-wave imaging and an adaptive normalized cross-correlation algorithm applied to 3D+t data. The results show displacement fields consistent with acoustic radiation force, including a superimposed standing wave pattern, and transient oscillations at the 500 Hz pulse repetition frequency. Peak displacements of approximately 1.5–3.5 µm were observed in the focal region, followed by steady-state behavior and relaxation after stimulation. These findings demonstrate that high-frame-rate displacement tracking can directly resolve localized mechanical effects of neuromodulation, offering a powerful approach for mapping and optimizing ultrasound-based brain stimulation.

papers.title: Multi-Parametric Machine Learning Prediction of ultrasound-Mediated blood-Brain Barrier Opening in Diffuse Midline Glioma Patients
papers.abstract: In this study, we demonstrate the feasibility and accuracy of predicting focused ultrasound-mediated blood-brain barrier opening (FUS-BBBO) success or failure based on ultrasound-derived data and prior to contrast-enhanced MRI confirmation, in a pediatric Diffuse Midline Glioma population. We derive metrics from passive acoustic mapping (PAM), B-mode, and acoustic simulations, and train a logistic regression classifier model to distinguish successful from failed FUS-BBBO procedures based on acoustic cavitation, microbubble localization, and transducer-skull coupling information. We assess the model's classification ability using receiver operating characteristics (ROC) analysis, and apply it on new, unseen data obtained from recent FUS-BBBO sessions. We demonstrate high classification ability with areas under the ROC curve up to 0.95 using a 4-parameter classifier. Predictions on new data also show high accuracy, with over 85% accurate predictions. Overall, this is the first study using clinically derived ultrasound-based data to predict FUS-BBBO outcomes, paving the way towards reduced reliance on contrast-enhanced MRI for treatment evaluation.

papers.title: Cell-Guided Cavitation Nucleation Using Phase-Change Nanoparticles for Drug Delivery in Glioma Models
papers.abstract: Cell-guided cavitation using phase-change nanoparticles offers a targeted alternative to conventional microbubbles in focused ultrasound (FUS) therapy. Here, macrophages deliver PLGA–PEG nanoparticles encapsulating curcumin and PFOB, enabling localized cavitation nucleation and drug release. The nanoparticles (240–320 nm, 16–25% loading) showed high macrophage uptake (92.4% vs. 13.8% control). Upon FUS exposure, PFOB underwent acoustic droplet vaporization, generating cavitation nuclei detectable via ultrasound imaging. In GL261 co-cultures, this triggered localized drug release and ~50% tumor cell reduction, with enhanced cavitation confirmed by passive detection. In vivo, macrophages accumulated at glioma sites (~240% increase), enabling tumor-localized cavitation and acoustic emissions post-FUS. This platform integrates immune targeting, responsive cavitation nuclei, and real-time monitoring, enabling controlled, feedback-guided drug delivery without relying on microbubbles.

papers.title: Sparse-Channel Cavitation Imaging via Deep Learning-Based Channel Interpolation for Portable Blood-Brain Barrier Opening
papers.abstract: Blood-brain barrier opening (BBBO) with microbubble cavitation is promising for drug delivery in neurological diseases, but safe treatment requires real-time cavitation monitoring. Power cavitation imaging (PCI) maps acoustic power from microbubble activity, yet conventional PCI needs full-channel arrays, limiting portable use. This study developed a residual U-Net to reconstruct 128-channel data from sparse 16, 32, or 64 channel inputs. Its multi-branch first layer combines 3×3 local convolutions with 3×128 full-aperture lateral convolutions to capture inter-channel correlations. Reconstructed data were beamformed to form PCI images. The model was trained with Field-II simulations and phantom data and tested on mouse in vivo BBBO data. PCI quality improved in all settings: in vivo PSNR increased by 18.15, 16.68, and 8.24 dB, and SSIM by 0.4645, 0.3059, and 0.0433 for 16, 32, and 64 channels. Gains were larger in PCI than IQ images, indicating channel coherence is critical. Zero-padded U-Net inputs performed better than linear interpolation, suggesting that pre-interpolation may hinder correlation learning. The results support reduced-channel, portable PCI for BBBO monitoring.

sessions.title: TMI: Ultrasonic Transducers for Biomedical Imaging

papers.title: A Wearable Ultrasound Patch for Dual-Plane Imaging of Superficial Tissues
papers.abstract: Continuous monitoring of superficial tissues requires multi-plane imaging for complete anatomical characterization. Conventional ultrasound relies on probe manipulation, leading to operator dependence and temporal mismatch. This work presents a wearable ultrasound patch enabling simultaneous dual-plane imaging. To address bandwidth limitations in high-frequency arrays, a three-layer acoustic matching structure was designed to improve impedance transition and acoustic transmission.Two perpendicular 64-element linear arrays (8.5 MHz, 0.2 mm pitch) were integrated on a flexible printed circuit board (FPCB). Based on the KLM model and binomial method, the target acoustic impedances were 14.8, 4.2, and 1.9 MRayl. A high-impedance composite (15.3 MRayl) was developed for the first matching layer.The fabricated patch has a thickness of 1.4 mm and achieves a −6 dB fractional bandwidth of 72%. The proposed design improves bandwidth performance and enables compact dual-plane imaging, showing potential for carotid blood flow and muscle monitoring.

papers.title: Fabrication and Integration of a 10 MHz 2D Ultrasound Array on a Polyimide Flexible Substrate for Hybrid Ultrasound-Gamma Imaging
papers.abstract: This work presents a 10 MHz 2D ultrasound array integrated with an interposer-free polyimide-based flexible interconnect for hybrid ultrasound–gamma imaging. Such systems require high-density interconnects while minimizing gamma-ray attenuation, which is challenging with conventional interposer-based structures. An 80-element PZT-5A array (64 active) with a 300 μm pitch was designed and integrated with a multilayer polyimide substrate. A 30 μm polyimide layer with two metal layers was fabricated using photolithography and via formation. For the second metal layer, 45° tilted e-beam deposition improved step coverage along via sidewalls, followed by wet etching to minimize substrate damage. Solder-ball bonding was used to enhance interconnect reliability. Electrical impedance and phase measurements confirmed proper connectivity and resonance, while pulse-echo results validated acoustic performance. Using 8 elements, 1 mm wire-target imaging was demonstrated, confirming system functionality. This approach provides a compact and scalable solution for high-frequency 2D arrays, enabling real-time imaging in endoscopic systems with potential for intraoperative cancer localization.

papers.title: A Side Looking, High-Frequency, Ultrasound Probe for Intraoperative Arthroscopic Guidance
papers.abstract: Arthroscopy is a minimally invasive orthopedic procedure performed through small incisions, requiring compact imaging tools. We present a rigid, 6.35 mm diameter cylindrical ultrasound probe with a 288-element, 27 MHz side-looking array for intraoperative guidance. This work addresses the challenge of high-density interconnect and signal routing within the probe’s constrained circular cross-section. The design employs a nested stack of hemicylindrical thin flexible PCBs with 100 μm pitch and 9 um thick traces. A novel fabrication approach enables reliable wire bonding to the traces by electroplating 60 μm of copper at trace terminations, followed by dicing to expose cross-sectional bonding pads. Using 18 μm aluminum wirebonds, robust electrical connections were achieved. The resulting structure demonstrated >20 μm pad spacing with no electrical failures once fully formed. This architecture supports high element counts in a compact form factor compatible with arthroscopy, while providing space for an acoustic backing layer and central lumen for additional features. The approach shows strong potential for high-frequency ultrasound endoscopes in minimally invasive surgery.

papers.title: AI-Enhanced Dual-Probe Ultrasound for Point-of-Care Multidepth Imaging
papers.abstract: Existing portable ultrasound systems require manual probe repositioning, limiting their utility for continuous, unattended point-of-care monitoring. We present a back-to-back dual-probe patch integrating a 3.5 MHz sector phased array and a 7 MHz linear array in a shared backing layer with matched 220 µm pitch. A dual-branch convolutional neural network reconstructs pseudo fully-sampled apertures from 64-channel sparse acquisitions for each frequency independently, suppressing grating lobe artifacts caused by stretchable interconnect constraints. Beamforming and multimode reconstruction run in real time on the UltraVision portable platform. The system enables deep organ surveillance and high-resolution superficial tissue assessment from a single substrate without operator repositioning.

papers.title: H-Array Transducer for 4D Tissue Harmonic Echocardiography
papers.abstract: 4D transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) is a real-time, low-cost alternative to cardiac MR but lacks the spatial and temporal resolution needed for accurate 4D flow assessment. This work proposes an “H-Array” transducer that transmits at the fundamental frequency and receives higher-order harmonics from tissue and microbubbles, enabling high-volume-rate 4D imaging and improved sensitivity. The design also allows flexible selection of imaging planes, supporting techniques like EchoPIV for flow and strain analysis. The prototype includes one 32-element transmit array and two orthogonal 32-element receive arrays (96 elements total), using 2-2 PZT composites targeting 2 MHz transmit and 4 MHz receive. Cylindrical lenses broaden the field of view. Measurements show good element uniformity, widened beam profiles, and successful harmonic imaging of a wire phantom with ~5° resolution, demonstrating feasibility and potential for enhanced cardiac imaging.

papers.title: A 2.5 MHz 32 X 32 Rectangular Boundary Array for 3D Imaging
papers.abstract: Row-column arrays (RCAs) enable 3D imaging with reduced channel counts but suffer from limited field of view due to constrained beam steering. To address this, a 2.5 MHz 32×32 rectangular boundary array (RBA) is proposed to improve steering capability and expand imaging coverage. In this design, edge columns are used for transmit and edge rows for receive, forming an effective aperture through the 2D convolution of transmit and receive elements. This produces broad k-space coverage with minimal gaps, supporting improved spatial resolution. The array was fabricated from CTS 3203HD material, integrated with a custom flex circuit, and interfaced with a Verasonics system. Full synthetic aperture data from 124 elements was acquired and beamformed offline in MATLAB. Imaging of wire targets demonstrated clear visualization, with a measured −6 dB angular resolution of 2.1° at 40 mm depth. These results confirm feasibility for 3D imaging, with future work targeting phantom studies and real-time implementation.

papers.title: Development of a Hybrid 32-Element PZT and 64-Element CMUT Stacked Array for Acoustic Angiography
papers.abstract: Acoustic angiography (AA) is a minimally invasive technique for imaging microvasculature using microbubble contrast agents. In AA, microbubbles are excited at low frequencies (<5 MHz), generating high-frequency superharmonic signals that enable high-resolution imaging. Conventional piezoelectric arrays lack the bandwidth to efficiently support both transmit and receive operations across these frequency ranges, often necessitating dual-array configurations with limited flexibility. While CMUT arrays provide broader bandwidth, they can introduce transmit-generated harmonics that degrade microbubble signal fidelity. To address these challenges, we propose a stacked PZT–CMUT array with spectrally separated transmit and receive bands. We developed a hybrid array comprising a 32-element PZT array (1.7 MHz) bonded to a 64-element CMUT array (6.4 MHz), along with scalable packaging strategies. This approach demonstrates improved acoustic performance and enhanced signal fidelity for acoustic angiography.

papers.title: Handheld 4,096-Element 2D Array for Interventional Liver Guidance
papers.abstract: Real-time ultrasound guidance offers a cost-effective, non-ionizing alternative to CT and MRI for interventional liver procedures, provided it maintains high spatial resolution and volumetric acquisition. To address this application, we are developing a handheld 4,096-element 2D ultrasound array with an 83.2 mm x 16 mm active aperture. The device employs a modular architecture consisting of two FPGA/power boards and four HDI ASIC boards. The design integrates over 15,000 high-voltage switches and local preamplifiers to implement a multiplexing scheme that interfaces the large array with a 1,024-channel system beamformer. The locally integrated FPGA controllers enable real-time configuration of the ASIC switch settings, while the local power generation provides all the required supplies for the ASICs and locally integrated preamps from a single 5V supply. Preliminary validation of the electronics shows that the FPGA and power circuits are functional, and initial image results are promising.

papers.title: A 1-3 Composite High-Frequency Imaging Transducer for Intravascular Plaque Imaging
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, with atherosclerosis serving as the underlying cause of many acute coronary syndromes. Plaque rupture is closely associated with lesion vulnerability, which is determined by both structural and compositional features, including fibrous cap thickness, lipid-rich necrotic core, and calcification. However, accurate differentiation of plaque components, particularly the lipid core, fibrous cap, and surrounding vessel wall, remains challenging because of their small dimensions, complex geometry, and sometimes limited acoustic contrast. Among these features, a thin fibrous cap is one of the most important indicators of vulnerable plaque. Therefore, high-resolution intravascular imaging is essential for identifying plaque morphology, evaluating lesion vulnerability, and guiding future catheter-based diagnosis and therapy. In this work, a 50 MHz 1-3 composite PMN-PT transducer was designed, fabricated, and characterized for in-vitro and ex-vivo intravascular plaque imaging.

sessions.title: NAF: Acoustic Microfluidics and Structural Health Monitoring

papers.title: Focused Ultrasound Modulation of Glymphatic‑Like Transport in a Microfluidic Brain‑Mimetic Platform
papers.abstract: The glymphatic system regulates cerebrospinal fluid–interstitial fluid exchange and solute clearance in the brain, and its dysfunction has been linked to multiple neurological disorders. Although low-intensity focused ultrasound (FUS) can enhance perivascular fluid transport, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear due to limited in vivo control and the absence of active in vitro models. This work introduces the Sono-NeuroFlux-Chip, a FUS-enabled glymphatic-on-chip platform for controlled study of glymphatic-like transport in brain-mimetic environments. The PDMS microfluidic device was fabricated using stereolithography-assisted soft lithography and acoustically matched to the ultrasound focal zone for uniform stimulation. Dimensional verification and leak testing confirmed device integrity. Application of FUS (0.65 MHz, 0.3 MPa, 7% duty cycle) significantly enhanced tracer transport versus controls (p = 0.00023), establishing the platform’s capability.

papers.title: Accelerated Biofabrication of ADSC Spheroids via Acoustofluidic Platform for Boosting Proangiogenic Potential in Stem Cells
papers.abstract: 3D human adipose-derived stem cell (ADSC) spheroids enhance regenerative factor secretion and viability, yet traditional ULA methods are slow. We developed an acoustofluidic platform using a 2-MHz FUS transducer and PDMS microchannels to drive rapid, non-contact cell aggregation via acoustic streaming. Optimal conditions (400 kPa, 300 s) yielded uniform spheroids (451.1 ± 48.1 μm), achieving assembly approximately 1,100 times faster than the 3-day ULA method while maintaining high viability. At Day 1, FUS-assembled spheroids showed significantly higher VEGF (3.2 ± 0.9-fold) and HGF (4.6 ± 0.5-fold) expression than controls. By Day 3, sustained upregulation of VEGF (3.3 ± 0.8-fold) and HGF (2.9 ± 0.6-fold) persisted. This scalable strategy rapidly produces functional ADSC spheroids with enhanced pro-angiogenic potential, offering a high-throughput solution for regenerative medicine and wound healing applications.

papers.title: Ultrasound Manipulation of Microbubbles on THP-1 Macrophages to Modulate Molecular Markers
papers.abstract: Macrophages play a key role in tumor eradication following immunotherapy, dynamically shifting between pro- and anti-tumor phenotypes in response to cytokines. IFN-γ and TNF-𝛼 are key drivers of anti-tumor polarization, so we investigated if acoustic microbubble (MB) manipulation could induce inflammatory signaling in macrophages and modulate cytokine expression. 1x10^6 macrophages were seeded into each well across two 6-well plates. In test conditions, 1×10^8 MBs were added, wells were sealed with parafilm, and inverted to promote MB contact with adherent cells. Samples were exposed to 1 MHz ultrasound on our optimized platform for 2 or 4 minutes (40% duty cycle, 20 Vpp). Supernatants were collected at 0, 2, and 4 hours post-stimulation, and ELISAs quantified IFN-γ and TNF-α. TNF-α levels increased following 2 minutes of MB oscillation, peaking at 4 hours post-stimulation (10 to 68 pg/mL). These findings suggest that brief MB-mediated mechanical stimulation can trigger cytokine release associated with anti-tumor macrophage activation, providing a foundation for noninvasive strategies to enhance immunotherapy response.

papers.title: Ultrasonic Guided Wave piezopolymer Interdigital Transducers for the Detection of micro-Notch in Large Aluminum Panels
papers.abstract: Detecting microdefects and monitoring their progression in aluminium panels is a challenging problem in large structures (typical lengths of several meters), given the need to maintain low transducer density and robustness to environmental stresses. These requirements are important for guided-wave structural health monitoring systems for the aerospace sector. The objective of this work is to design InterDigital Transducers capable of detecting a micro-notch in an area 1 m x 0.7 m of a larger aluminium panel. An integrated design of the IDT in transmission and the receiver on the same piezopolymer film is described. The IDT operate with an A0 mode at 550 kHz. The paper will report the full investigation results with the detection of the micro-notch at orientations 0°,45° and 90° with respect to the incident beam, in the range 0 – 350mm using the pulse echo and pitch and catch modes. The main outcome of this work is the possibility to use piezopolymer IDTs for covering a range of 700mm for the detection of microdefects with a signal to noise ratio better than 6dB for all cases.

papers.title: Ultrasonic Guided Wave Signatures of Identically Shaped Metal-Loss Defects and Surface Deposits
papers.abstract: Ultrasonic guided waves are widely used for structural health monitoring. While most studies focus on material-removal defects (metal loss), surface deposits (material-addition anomalies) also perturb wave propagation. Clarifying their distinct responses is essential to avoid misinterpretation. A controlled experiment compared three conditions: an intact baseline, a 1.8 mm paraffin surface deposit, and a 1.8 mm metal-loss defect of identical geometry. Multi-channel signals were acquired, analyzing A0 wave packets via time-domain, frequency-domain, and imaging approaches. Despite identical geometries, responses differ markedly. Metal-loss defects produce localized scattering (amplitudes up to 2.8x baseline) and high-contrast indications. Conversely, deposits produce weaker, distributed perturbations (amplitude ~0.7x metal-loss response) and diffuse images. While envelope widths are similar, deposits cause stronger high-frequency attenuation (26.6% reduction) due to added-mass and viscoelastic damping. Consequently, metal-loss imaging methods should not be directly applied to deposit detection.

sessions.title: NPA: Photoacoustics and Industrial NDE

papers.title: Temporal Hadamard Multiplexing for Laser Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Temporal Hadamard Multiplexing can improve the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of laser ultrasound signals, more than regular averaging, without an increase in acquisition time or additional prior knowledge. Multiple sequences of different laser pulse combinations are sent with a chosen time delay between subsequent pulses according to the chosen Hadamard matrix. This leads to the recording of multiple sequences of different superimposed ultrasound signals that after being demultiplexed will result in a single ultrasound signal that has a higher SNR than obtained via regular averaging. We tested temporal Hadamard multiplexing using simulated data. Comparing the resulting signals after regular averaging and Hadamard demultiplexing shows a better SNR for the Hadamard demultiplexed signal. The observed improvement in SNR is in line with its theoretical prediction.

papers.title: Ultrasound-Guided Refraction Correction for Photoacoustic Oxygen Saturation Mapping in Bone-Mimicking Media
papers.abstract: Oxygen saturation (sO₂) of blood in bone is critical for monitoring bone metabolism, yet non-invasive quantification remains challenging. Photoacoustic (PA) imaging enables sO₂ mapping in soft tissue by unmixing wavelength-dependent optical absorption spectra of blood chromophores, but its application in bone is limited by speed-of-sound (SoS) mismatch, causing refraction-induced distortions and inaccurate reconstructions under uniform SoS assumptions. We propose an ultrasound-guided refraction correction method using US-derived bone interfaces and layer-wise SoS as priors for PA reconstruction. Simulations with a PMMA bone-mimicking model show that refraction correction significantly improves image quality, restoring vessel focus at the correct depth with stronger PA signal intensity and ensuring unmixing originates from true vessel regions. While mean sO₂ remains unaffected, spatial blurring under uniform SoS inflates variance; refraction correction reduces standard deviation from 9.3%–15.0% to 0.3%–0.4%, improving sO₂ quantification reliability.

papers.title: Narrowband Photoacoustic Lamb Wave Generation via Slit-Patterned CSNP-PDMS Transmitters
papers.abstract: Photoacoustic (PA) generation using CSNP-PDMS composites enables efficient, non-contact structural health monitoring (SHM). However, unpatterned transmitters yield broadband signals, causing multi-modal interference. This study proposes slit-patterned CSNP-PDMS transmitters to generate tunable, narrowband Lamb waves via spatial filtering. Transmitters were designed with periodic slit pitches satisfying constructive interference for the fundamental antisymmetric (A0) mode at 350, 450, and 550 kHz. Fabricated on an aluminum plate, they were excited by a low-energy pulsed Nd:YAG laser (<70 mJ). Transient out-of-plane surface velocities were measured using a laser Doppler vibrometer. Experiments validated a ~10-18 dB signal-to-noise ratio improvement over bare metal. Unlike broadband bulk patches, the slit-patterned arrays constrained acoustic energy into narrow bands (<50% fractional bandwidth) with dominant peaks at the targeted frequencies. This allowed clear temporal isolation of A0 wave packets, offering a structurally simple yet highly effective method to enhance signal reliability for advanced non-contact SHM.

papers.title: Long-Distance Ultrasonic Echo Reception Using a Laser-Deflection-Based Photoacoustic Probe with Pulse Compression
papers.abstract: This study evaluates pulse-compression-based long-distance ultrasonic echo reception using a laser-deflection-based photoacoustic probe. In a water-tank experiment with a propagation distance of 1020 mm, matched-filter processing was applied to received ultrasonic signals. The results showed that pulse compression improved the signal-to-noise ratio from 33.15 dB to 47.07 dB and enabled separate detection of echoes from the upper and lower surfaces of a 10 mm acrylic target. These findings indicate that the proposed approach can improve weak echo detectability while maintaining axial resolution in long-distance underwater ultrasonic measurements.

papers.title: Flat Ultrasonic Channels for Broadband Through-Metal Communications
papers.abstract: Ultrasonic waves can transmit data through metallic barriers where electromagnetic solutions fail. However, existing ultrasonic channels are highly resonant, which limits their coherence bandwidth for broadband communications. This work designs and experimentally validates an ultrasonic stack that suppresses these mechanical resonances. Using 5 MHz piezoelectric transducers bonded to opposite sides of a 3 mm aluminum wall, we show via 1D analytical and 3D finite-element models that the resonances arise from internal reflections within the stack and cannot be removed by conventional backing. We introduce a graded filled-epoxy fronting layer integrated into the metal surface that minimizes reflections through gradient impedance matching and attenuation. Multiple epoxy formulations and micromachined patterns are evaluated and characterized with a vector network analyzer. The optimized stack reduces frequency-response ripple from over 30 dB to under 3 dB across the 3 to 20 MHz range. An OFDM communication link demonstrates the resulting throughput gains, enabling high-rate data transfer for sealed pressure vessels, nuclear waste canisters, and EMI-shielded electronics.

sessions.title: PMUT Competition
MEL: Viscoelasticity, Muscle Mechanics, and Anisotropy

papers.title: Viscoelastic Parameter Analysis Based on S- Transform and KVFD Model
papers.abstract: Conventional dispersion estimation methods suffer from limited bandwidth and high noise sensitivity, hindering accurate extraction of viscoelastic parameters. Here we propose an integrated approach: first, the generalized Stockwell transform combined with slant wavenumber analysis (GST‑SFK) is used to obtain broadband shear wave phase velocity dispersion curves. Then, the KVFD (Kelvin‑Voigt fractional derivative) viscoelastic model is fitted to the dispersion curves to directly estimate elasticity, viscosity, and fractional order. The method was validated on finite‑difference simulated viscoelastic phantoms, tissue‑mimicking phantoms, and ex vivo plaque data. Results show that GST‑SFK expands the usable bandwidth by more than a factor of two (up to 2000 Hz in phantoms and 900 Hz in tissues). With the KVFD model, the root‑mean‑square percentage error of the estimated viscoelastic parameters is below 5%. The framework is robust against noise, requires only a few spatial points, and is suitable for limited‑field‑of‑view applications such as plaque imaging. This technique offers a powerful tool for quantitative viscoelastic characterization of soft tissues.

papers.title: Characterization of in situ Soft Tissue Mechanics During Ballistic Relevant Impacts Using High Frame Rate Elastography
papers.abstract: his work evaluates high-frame-rate ultrasound for measuring soft tissue mechanics during high-rate impacts such as ballistic trauma, where conventional methods lack sufficient temporal resolution or soft tissue contrast. Using a Verasonics system operating up to 10,000 frames per second, tissue motion was captured during externally driven impacts, which produce primarily lateral displacement. The approach was validated in tissue-mimicking phantoms with embedded markers by comparing ultrasound-derived motion to high-speed X-ray measurements, then applied to a cadaveric porcine model under behind-armor blunt trauma conditions. Custom displacement tracking methods were developed to handle lateral motion. Results show the ability to resolve organ-scale deformation, quantify internal strain, and observe relative motion between structures such as the abdominal wall and liver. A rate-dependent slip boundary effect was observed at higher projectile velocities. This technique enables direct, high-resolution measurement of internal tissue dynamics during rapid loading, providing a new tool for injury biomechanics research.

papers.title: Nonlinear Acoustic Radiation Force Modeling Enhances QVisR Viscoelastic Modulus Estimates
papers.abstract: Quantiative Viscoelastic Response (QVisR) ultrasound is an on-axis elastography method which uses machine learning models to estimate viscoelastic parameters from acoustic radiation force (ARF) displacement data. QVisR models are trained on simulated ARF data using Field II acoustic simulations of the acoustic point spread function (PSF) to generate body forces in finite element method simulations of Kelvin-Voigt materials. Field II simulates linear acoustic propagation; however, ultrasound is nonlinear, particularly at high pressure amplitudes. We investigate using nonlinear acoustic simulations of ARF PSFs in k-Wave for training QVisR machine learning models. We observe improved QVisR prediction accuracy in calibrated phantom acquisitions using k-Wave-trained models.

papers.title: Investigating Single-Probe Rotational Shear Wave Elastography Configuration for Improved Shear Vertical Wave Detection in Transversely Isotropic Phantoms
papers.abstract: Rotational Shear Wave Elastography (SWE) enables characterization of anisotropic tissues such as skeletal muscle, but shear vertical (SV) waves remain difficult to detect, limiting estimation of tensile anisotropy. SV detectability depends on its projection onto the imaging beam, which varies with fiber orientation and acquisition geometry. This study compared phantom and probe tilting strategies (15° and 25°) using rotational SWE on a stretched PVA phantom. SH and SV waves were extracted, and SV detection was quantified using SNR and mapped against a theoretical projection model. Results showed that SV detection is more reliable when projection exceeds 53%, with higher SNR in this region. Lower tilts yielded higher SNR, while higher tilts increased SV detection rate. Phantom tilt at 25° performed best, combining high detection and high SNR, whereas probe tilt at 15° performed worst. Overall, a trade-off exists between detectability and signal quality, with phantom tilt outperforming probe tilt, suggesting tissue orientation is more effective than acquisition geometry.

papers.title: Quantification of Paraspinal Muscle Mechanical Asymmetries in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis Participants Using Viscoelastic Response Imaging (VisR) Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS), a spinal deformity affecting 1%-4% of adolescents, has been hypothesized to result from a vicious cycle involving asymmetrical stresses and spine growth. Muscle mechanical properties are hypothesized to contribute to this cycle. This study used Viscoelastic Response (VisR) ultrasound imaging to assess the multifidus, longissimus, and iliocostalis muscles in six AIS participants with moderate spinal curvature. Relative elasticity (RE) was measured, and anisotropy was quantified as a material anisotropy index (MAI), defined as the difference over the sum of RE measurements from transverse and longitudinal transducer orientations. Analysis detected significant MAI differences, showing a measurable side-specific asymmetry in the multifidus muscle. These preliminary findings suggest that VisR-based measurements can identify mechanical property asymmetries in paraspinal muscles, offering a new path to understand scoliosis development.

papers.title: Prediction of Shear Elastic Modulus in the Presence of Viscosity Using Double-Profile Intersection Ultrasound (DoPIo)
papers.abstract: Double Profile Intersection (DoPIo) ultrasound estimates shear elastic modulus (G) by applying an acoustic radiation force (ARF) excitation and tracking on axis tissue displacements using two simultaneous beams with different focal configurations. The intersection time of resulting displacement profiles (t_int) has been empirically related to G. Existing DoPIo models were developed using purely elastic materials, despite the viscoelastic nature of biological tissue. In this study, DoPIo data were simulated using a Kelvin–Voigt material model spanning physiologically relevant ranges of G and shear viscosity (η). Displacement-derived features, t_int and time to peak (ttp), were used to evaluate three weighted total least squares models: a single variable model fit using elastic data, a single variable model fit using viscoelastic data, and a viscoelastic multivariable model incorporating both features. Results demonstrate that η results in G underestimation in the original model, while the multivariable model improved G estimation, yielding a more accurate and biologically relevant DoPIo framework for tissue elasticity imaging.

sessions.title: MIM: Functional Imaging

papers.title: Functional Ultrasound Imaging Revealed Early Functional Alterations in Cln3-/- Mice
papers.abstract: CLN3 disease causes early vision loss, but dysfunction in the central visual pathways has been underexplored. This study uses functional ultrasound (fUS) imaging to examine visually evoked responses in young wild-type and Cln3 knockout mice under intact-skull conditions. Activation was quantified across the visual cortex, thalamus, and midbrain, and histological analysis measured SCMAS accumulation as a marker of pathological burden. Cln3 knockout mice exhibited pathway-dependent functional alterations, suggesting potential compensatory mechanisms. This work highlights the use of fUS for studying early functional changes in neurodegenerative disease.

papers.title: Automatic Boundary Detection with Signed Distance Function Supervision for Wall Shear Stress Estimation
papers.abstract: Stroke risk is linked to carotid Wall Shear Stress (WSS), a hemodynamic driver of plaque formation and rupture. Ultrasound enables cost-effective, real-time WSS mapping, but requires precise vessel wall segmentation, typically relying on labor-intensive manual delineation, limiting clinical adoption. Deep learning solutions have been explored, but it remains unclear whether they provide sufficient boundary accuracy for reliable WSS estimation. We propose a dual-stage transfer learning approach with signed distance function (SDF) regression to improve boundary accuracy under limited data. Predicted segmentation masks are used to estimate WSS from velocity gradients, with velocity fields obtained via transverse oscillation vector flow imaging using an interleaved synthetic aperture sequence. We assessed whether fully automatic WSS estimation is statistically equivalent to manual measurements. No significant differences were found between manual and automatic WSS (paired t-test), and strong agreement was observed (r ≥ 0.96), supporting automatic, operator-independent WSS estimation and its potential for clinical adoption.

papers.title: Comparison of 4D Vector Flow Imaging Strategies with a Handheld 128+128 Row-Column Addressed CMUT Array Probe
papers.abstract: This study evaluates three 4D vector flow imaging (VFI) strategies using a 128+128 row-column addressed CMUT array probe to capture multidirectional flow. The approaches include pseudo-3D slice-by-slice imaging, conventional orthogonal plane-wave (OPW) volumetric imaging, and a novel subgroup-OPW method designed to improve estimation accuracy. A custom 14 MHz CMUT array was integrated with custom-designed electronics enabling orthogonal transmit-receive operation and flexible aperture selection. Experiments were conducted on a pulsatile tube flow phantom with retrospective time-gating for synchronization. For the pseudo-3D approach, a model-based iterative reconstruction (MBIR) algorithm was used to recover a continuous 4D flow field from sparsely acquired slices. Results show that MBIR enables smooth and consistent volumetric flow reconstruction despite limited sampling, while OPW-based methods provide direct volumetric velocity estimation. Overall, the results demonstrate the feasibility of RC-based 4D VFI and highlight trade-offs between sampling efficiency, temporal resolution, and estimation accuracy.

papers.title: Doppler Twinkling Artifact for Long-Term Biopsy Marker Visibility in Lymph Nodes in a Longitudinal Animal Model Study
papers.abstract: Biopsy marker identification is critical for tracking breast lesions and metastatic lymph nodes (LNs) during treatment. PMMA markers produce Doppler twinkling that enhances ultrasound detection. This study evaluated effects of marker type, LN location, and transducer on long-term twinkling visibility. Eight Yucatan minipigs underwent bilateral LN targeting at primary inguinal, secondary inguinal, and popliteal sites. Baseline imaging preceded CFA/KLH-induced lymphadenopathy, with follow-up over 6 months. Four marker types (PMMA, Pmesh, Q, SoB) were placed. Twinkling was scored (0–4) using L2-9, ML4-20, and L6-24 transducers. An ordinal mixed-effects model was applied. Twinkling score was significantly influenced by transducer, LN location, node volume, and time. Transducer choice was the strongest predictor: L2-9 showed near-maximal detection (~95–100%), ML4-20 remained high (~85–98%), while L6-24 declined to <20% by 6 months. Marker type had a smaller effect. These findings show transducer selection is key to maintaining consistent twinkling visibility.

papers.title: Temporal Decoupling of Cerebral Blood Volume and Oxygenation Dynamics Using High-Speed Functional Ultrasound and Photoacoustic Imaging
papers.abstract: Cerebral blood volume (CBV) and oxygen saturation (sO2) are two key hemodynamic parameters that reflect distinct physiological processes. Understanding their interplay at high spatiotemporal resolution can provide new insights into neurovascular coupling mechanisms. However, current functional ultrasound (fUS) and photoacoustic (PA) approaches, although capable of imaging CBV and sO2 separately, are limited to temporal resolutions of >3 seconds/rame and may miss critical transient hemodynamic events. To overcome this limitation, we developed a high-speed fUS–PA system with a 100 Hz laser and an optimized acquisition sequence, achieving 0.41 seconds/frame—an 8-fold improvement over the current state of the art. Using this system, we studied CBV and sO2 dynamics in mice under brief electrical stimulation and observed temporal decoupling: sO2 decreased prior to the CBV increase, followed by a rapid rise due to the inflow of oxygenated blood. Notably, these fast, decoupled dynamics were undetectable at lower frame rates, demonstrating that high-speed fUS–PA enables in vivo observation of rapid neurovascular coupling and opens new opportunities for studying transient hemodynamics.

papers.title: High Volume-Rate 3D Echocardiography Using Multiplexed Single 256-Channel System
papers.abstract: 3D cardiac electromechanical activation mapping requires high volume-rate single-heartbeat imaging. Current systems use four synchronized scanners (1024 channels), limiting clinical adoption. We demonstrate feasibility using a single 256-channel Vantage with a 1024-element 32×32 matrix array (3.5 MHz, 0.3 mm pitch) via UTA 1024-MUX. Five diverging wave virtual sources (VS) transmit on all 1024 elements; receive data is multiplexed across four 256-element panels (100 vol/s at 2000 Hz PRF). Four MUX strategies were compared on a CIRS phantom at two depths and two VS configurations. DAS beamforming with coherent compounding was performed on GPU. Full TX achieved 5-10 dB lower sidelobes than sub-aperture TX (FWHM 1.57-1.77 vs 1.96 mm). VS position 1 maintained uniform resolution across depth (1.4-1.8 mm); position 2 degraded at depth (2.75 mm). In vivo imaging in a healthy volunteer visualized all four chambers, and normalized cross-correlation produced displacement estimates with consistent cardiac motion patterns. Multiplexed 3D imaging on a single system is feasible for cardiac EM assessment. Ongoing work includes axial strain and flow estimation.

papers.title: GPU-Accelerated Robust Smoothing of Ultrasound Vector Flow Fields
papers.abstract: Ultrasound vector flow imaging provides multidimensional blood flow estimation but suffers from noise, outliers, and missing data due to decorrelation and low signal-to-noise ratio. Regularization methods such the discrete cosine transform (DCT) based smoothing effectively recover coherent flow fields, but their iterative spectral formulation is computationally expensive and limits real-time use. In this work, we propose a fully GPU-accelerated version of this method, enabling fast and practical regularization of vector flow data for real-time ultrasound imaging.

papers.title: Tomographic Imaging of Piezoelectric Polarization in Fibrous Biological Tissues Using an Ultrasound Array Probe
papers.abstract: Fibrous biological tissues such as tendons exhibit piezoelectricity. The acoustically stimulated electromagnetic (ASEM) method enables detection of such responses using ultrasound. The purpose of this study is to acquire ASEM tomographic images simultaneously with conventional B-mode images using an ultrasound array probe, allowing spatial mapping of piezoelectric signals. Ultrasound pulses were irradiated to bovine Achilles tendon samples embedded in agar, and the induced electric field was detected by differential antennas. The signal location was determined from the ultrasound focus (lateral) and the ASEM signal delay time (depth), and the resulting ASEM map was superimposed onto the B-mode image. Clear signals were observed in the tendon region when the antenna was aligned parallel to the fiber orientation, whereas weaker signals were obtained for the orthogonal orientation. These results are consistent with the expected piezoelectric response of uniaxially symmetric fibrous tissues. In this paper, we also demonstrate the feasibility of ASEM imaging for visualizing tendons in the human wrist.

papers.title: Lightweight U-Net-Based Movement Intention Decoder for Functional Ultrasound Brain-Machine Interfaces
papers.abstract: This study presents a lightweight U‑Net‑based framework for movement intention decoding in functional ultrasound brain‑machine interfaces (fUS‑BMI). Compared with the PCA+LDA baseline used by Griggs et al. (2023), our model integrates a U‑Net backbone, AdaBoost discriminative enhancement, and DBSCAN clustering for trial‑level robust fusion. Circular soft labels encode directional geometry for the eight‑direction task, and online incremental retraining handles cross‑session drift. On the public fUS dataset, binary decoding achieved 90.9% accuracy (Kappa 0.817), while eight‑direction decoding reached 53.1% (Kappa 0.465), substantially outperforming PCA+LDA (43.2%), MLP, CNN, and ViT. Ablation showed AdaBoost and DBSCAN provide complementary gains, and online retraining is critical for maintaining performance across sessions. The results demonstrate that a compact deep learning model can enhance fUS‑BMI decoding under limited data.

sessions.title: MIM: Multimodality Imaging

papers.title: Detailed and Realistic CT-Based Intracardiac Echo Simulations
papers.abstract: A CT-based simulation framework for intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) is presented to generate annotated data to support algorithm development. The method combines CT-derived anatomical models with full-wave acoustic simulation using k-Wave, mapping Hounsfield units to acoustic properties and refining them with cardiac segmentations. Myocardial fiber orientation is incorporated to model anisotropic backscatter, improving tissue realism. A probe model replicating the clinical ICE VeriSight Pro (Philips) catheter enables realistic image acquisition and reconstruction. Validation against phantom data showed high technical accuracy, while comparison with patient data demonstrated realistic anatomical structures and imaging artifacts. The framework generates flexible, anatomically accurate ICE images with improved physical interpretability compared to existing methods, supporting the development of machine learning algorithms and training tools in environments with limited annotated datasets.

papers.title: Experimental Demonstration of Barker Coded Excitation in MAET with Magnetic Field Measurements
papers.abstract: Magneto-acousto-electrical tomography (MAET) is a hybrid imaging modality that provides conductivity-related information through the interaction of ultrasound-induced particle motion with a static magnetic field. This study experimentally evaluates 7-bit and 13-bit Barker coded excitation in MAET with coil-based magnetic field measurements. The experiments are performed under a 1.5 T static magnetic field using a 16-element linear phased array transducer, low-Q receiver coils, and a two-stage amplifier with 82.6 dB total gain. A 1 MHz sinusoidal carrier is phase modulated according to each Barker sequence, and the received signals are processed by matched filtering for pulse compression. Compared with conventional single-cycle excitation, the 7-bit and 13-bit Barker codes improve the SNR by 11.85 dB and 14.67 dB, respectively. Both codes yield a full width at half maximum of 2.4 mm, equal to that of single-cycle excitation, with peak sidelobe levels of -14.82 dB and -20.44 dB. These results demonstrate improved signal detectability while preserving axial resolution.

papers.title: Real-Time Multimodal Ultrasound Fusion Imaging for Precise Percutaneous Navigation in the High-Risk Perihilar Region: Technical Feasibility and Clinical Validation
papers.abstract: This study evaluates a real-time multimodal image fusion (CT/MRI/PET-US) to overcome the inherent acoustic limitations of conventional ultrasound in the complex perihilar region. Visualization and spatial targeting are severely restricted here by isoechoic tissues, acoustic shadowing, and dense vasculature. Using real-time electromagnetic tracking, preoperative 3D datasets were dynamically synchronized with live ultrasound to navigate percutaneous biopsies in 9 high-risk patients contraindicated for standard biopsy. Validation demonstrated a 100% technical success rate in spatial registration and targeting, with zero major complications. By leveraging internal anatomical landmarks, the system dynamically projected high-resolution targets onto the sonographic field. This enabled safe navigation through narrow vascular windows to strike extreme micro-lesions (e.g., 4x6 mm). This high-precision navigation altered clinical pathways in 33.3% of patients, preventing unnecessary radical resections and validating the critical value of fusion in enhancing spatial accuracy for interventional ultrasound.

papers.title: A Feasibility Study for Trans-Cortical Focused-Ultrasound Acousto-Electric Imaging via an Acoustic Coupler
papers.abstract: Focused ultrasound acousto-electric imaging (FUS-AEI) enables the non-invasive measurement of cerebral current density distributions. However, acoustic impedance mismatch at the skull-transducer interface reduces focal energy and degrades signal quality. This study introduces a hydrogel matching layer designed to conform to skull geometry, mitigate impedance mismatch, and enhance FUS-AEI signals at a low mechanical index. Utilizing a biocompatible sodium alginate base, glycerol was added in concentrations up to 30% by weight to systematically tune the coupler's density and speed of sound toward a target acoustic impedance of 3.11 MRayl. Testing with a 1.1 mm bovine femur cortical slice revealed that the optimal 30% glycerol coupler successfully enhanced through-bone energy delivery by 20.4%. Despite this increase in energy transmission, the actual AEI signal gain was limited to 5.63%. This limitation is attributed to phase aberration, which induces main lobe broadening and a spatial shift of the focal peak during the fixed acquisition window. Ongoing work will focus on phase aberration correction to fully characterize and optimize through-bone AEI signals.

papers.title: Adaptive Ultrasound and Photoacoustic Imaging for Deformed Arthritic Finger Joints via Robotics and Deep Learning
papers.abstract: An adaptive robotic ultrasound (US) and photoacoustic (PA) imaging system is presented for automated imaging of deformed arthritic finger joints. The system integrates a robotic arm, an RGB-D camera for joint localization, and deep learning (DL) models for real-time image-based feedback. An initial sagittal scan is performed to estimate the finger boundary, from which tilt angle and midpoint height are predicted. The robot is then adjusted to optimal alignment (0° tilt, 1 cm height) and a second scan is acquired. DL-based waypoint planning enables cross-sectional scanning, followed by real-time visual servoing that continuously refines lateral position and boundary alignment. Experiments on a test subject with simulated deformation demonstrated improved imaging performance. After adaptation, tilt and height errors were reduced to −0.4±4.6° and 0.0±0.2 cm, respectively. Median bone–soft tissue contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) increased from 1.3 dB to 2.6 dB (p=0.02), and bone signal-to-noise ratio improved from 24.2 dB to 31.9 dB (p<0.01). The results demonstrate the feasibility of adaptive, closed-loop US/PA imaging for anatomically variable joints.

papers.title: A Simulation Study of Transcranial Acoustoelectric Brain Imaging Using Multi-Electrode Current Source Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Direct mapping of neuronal currents is essential to understand brain function and diagnose neurological disorders. Transcranial acoustoelectric brain imaging (tABI) is a noninvasive modality that uses acoustic pressure to interact with neuronal currents through the skull. A multi-electrode current source reconstruction method based on a scalar potential AE formulation was recently introduced and validated in a cube phantom. Here, we evaluate the feasibility of tABI with multi-electrode current source density (CSD) reconstruction using simulations in a realistic human brain model prior to experimental validation.

papers.title: Linking SUMOylation to Tumor Structure and Function Using Multiparametric Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: SUMOylation regulates tumor progression via transcription factors and angiogenesis pathways like HIF-1α, yet non-invasive approaches linking SUMOylation activity to tumor structure and function are lacking. We hypothesize that SUMOylation inhibition alters tumor perfusion, vascular flow, and tissue mechanics detectable by ultrasound. A20 tumor-bearing mice received vehicle, radiation, SB-4826 (SUMOylation inhibitor), or combination treatment, assessed via multiparametric ultrasound: quantitative ultrasound (QUS), Power Doppler (PD), contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS), and shear wave elastography (SWE). All groups reduced tumor burden, strongest in the combination group. QUS detected structural heterogeneity shifts; PD and CEUS showed treatment-dependent vascular changes; CEUS TIC analysis revealed reduced MB wash-in in SB-4826 tumors (0.5 vs. 1.5 a.u./s). SWE showed increased stiffness post-treatment, indicating microenvironment remodeling. Next steps include longitudinal imaging and correlating biomarkers with SUMOylation, establishing a framework linking molecular regulation to tumor phenotype.

papers.title: Adaptive Scanning Pattern Planning for Anatomical Map Registration in non-Contact Photoacoustic Imaging System
papers.abstract: Non-contact photoacoustic imaging (nc-PAI) enables visualization of anatomical structures without surface contact, allowing free access of surgical tools during intervention. However, imaging time scales linearly with scanning points, and increasing detector channels remains challenging. We propose a particle filtering-based method that dynamically optimizes scanning patterns to accelerate registration between pre-operative volumes and intra-operative frames. The algorithm iteratively samples scanning points, updates particle probabilities based on measurement-prediction similarity, and selects the next imaging region to maximize inter-particle discrimination. In preliminary phantom validation, successful convergence cases achieved <1mm translation error and <4° rotation error within 10 iterations—up to 27 times faster than dense scanning. Further work is ongoing to improve convergence robustness across varying initial conditions.

sessions.title: MIS: Image Quality Enhancement

papers.title: Deep Coherence Disentanglement: One-Shot Ultrasound Image Denoising by Pyramid Self-Contrastive Learning
papers.abstract: We propose Deep Coherence Disentanglement (DCD) for one-shot ultrasound denoising. Ultrasound imaging is degraded by electronic, speckle, and side lobe noise. Conventional coherence factors rely on predefined noise assumptions, while deep learning denoising suffers from domain shift and high pretraining costs. DCD addresses these by combining physical coherence priors with deep representation capacity. DCD creates noisy pairs through shuffled sub-aperture transmissions and encodes coherence and incoherence features from sub-aperture IQ signals into separate pyramid latent spaces. Clean images are decoded from the coherence space while discarding incoherent components. Pyramid self-contrastive learning maximizes/minimizes similarity between coherence/incoherence feature spaces. A self-supervised swapping loop enables one-shot test-time training, eliminating domain shift and labeled data dependency. Simulations and in vivo cardiac and abdominal results show significant improvements in SNR, PSNR, CNR, gCNR, and SSIM. Feature distribution analysis confirms effective disentanglement of coherence/incoherence components, enabling more reliable anatomical visualization.

papers.title: A Novel Wavelet-Based Differential Periodogram Strategy Towards Effective Crosstalk Suppression in PMUT-Based Imaging
papers.abstract: Before image reconstruction, signals often require pre-processing to suppress unwanted contributions like crosstalk - a strong early-time signal contribution. Traditional calibration considers subtraction of measurements with and without the reflector present, but this is cumbersome and can distort images due to medium variability. A new strategy that avoids calibration is proposed in this work by using a differential periodogram derived from the Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT), enabling effective crosstalk suppression in PMUT-based imaging.

papers.title: Tunable B-Mode Despeckling via Image Saliency and Adaptive Stochastic Resampling
papers.abstract: A defining characteristic of ultrasound images is speckle. Despeckling filters act to reduce this speckle for increased interpretabiltiy of images, but it can be challenging to design these filters for high despeckling while maintaining image resolution. We propose a new image processing framework for depeckling based on image saliency and adaptive stochastic resampling. First, we generate a saliency map of the image. We then convert the saliency map into a probability for pixel resampling. A despeckled image can then be formed by accumulating from only the resampled pixels. Moreover, this method is tunable by controlling the saliency to probability function. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework both in vitro and in vivo. Our framework preserved image resolution (<0.03 mm resolution difference) after despeckling compared to the original image (<0.03 mm resolution difference) and resulted in improved gCNR values for contrast targets. Overall, our pure image processing despeckling framework is tunable by an operator, while still maintaining the image resolution of the unfiltered B-mode image.

papers.title: Deep Learning Based Clinical Tissue Harmonic Imaging Using Raw IQ Channel Data from a Single Transmission
papers.abstract: We propose a signal-domain deep-learning method for generating PIHI-like tissue harmonic images from single-transmit raw fundamental IQ channel data. Using 30,000 paired 1D fundamental and PIHI IQ channel signals from volunteer MSK scans, a lightweight 1D U-Net was trained with magnitude, phase, and STFT-based losses. After beamforming, the model-generated harmonic image showed closer agreement with reference PIHI than high-pass-filtered THI, with higher SSIM and PSNR, suggesting a potential route to harmonic imaging without frame rate reduction using a deep-learning-based signal-domain solution.

papers.title: Enhancing Ultrasound Imaging with Extended Coded Excitation via Chirp Predistortion and Decoupled Transmit-Receive Architecture
papers.abstract: Conventional systems, using the same elements for transmission (TX) and reception (RX), are limited by mode-switching, constraining signal length to avoid dead zones. Hybrid arrays (HAs), which separate TX and RX elements, enable continuous imaging with arbitrary signal lengths, overcoming this limitation. We hypothesize that adapting transmission signals in long-signal systems using HAs can enhance bandwidth (BW) and SNR. Two modulation schemes were tested: amplitude modulation (AM), which shapes signal amplitude, and sweep modulation (SM), which redistributes chirp frequency to emphasize weaker components. A 1 ms chirp (1–20 MHz) was measured in water using a piezoelectric transducer and hydrophone. In a second setup (1ms Chirp 1-6MHz), a HA with a piezoelectric TX and CMUT RX was aligned with a tissue phantom. Reflections from the phantom wall were processed using mismatched filtering. Results showed BW doubled to over 200% (A), with SM exhibiting 7 dB less loss than AM. SM also improved SNR by 3 dB compared to the original chirp (B). These findings highlight the potential of HAs with predistorted long signals for real-time ultrasound imaging.

papers.title: Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) Implementation for Receive Apodization Towards Improved Image Quality for Ultrasound Beamforming
papers.abstract: This work investigates ant colony optimization (ACO) for receive apodization in ultrasound beamforming. ACO is an evolutionary method where candidate solutions are guided by reinforced pheromone trails from previous high-performing solutions. It optimizes a discretized 128-element receive-weight vector, a high-dimensional, non-separable problem because each weight affects coherent summation across the aperture. After delay alignment, each vector is applied directly to receive-channel data, without modifying acquisition or transmission. The method was evaluated on single plane-wave simulated cyst data generated with MUST (+12, +6, -6, and -12 dB targets) and in-vitro cyst data acquired with Verasonics Vantage 256. Compared with DAS, ACO moved reconstructed cyst responses closer to target contrast in all simulated cases, reducing target error by 3.6%, 7.7%, 14.0%, and 15.5%. In vitro, it slightly improved the hyperechoic cyst response and reduced the +6 dB cyst target error by 18.3%. Results suggest ACO improves contrast recovery by reshaping the effective receive aperture to reduce sidelobe and clutter leakage. Main challenges are objective-function bias and computational cost.
