papers.title: Beyond Int16: Half-Precision Data for Enhanced Low-SNR Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: With the advancements in ultrasound (US) RF signal quality and dynamic range, the int16 datatype for storing RF data has become limiting. This is especially true when digital signal conditioning after the A/D adds extra bits of resolution through bandpass filtering and/or decimation. The Vantage NXT system uses a multi-rate filter after the A/D converters that processes data with 22 bits of dynamic range. With int16 storage, the LSBs from the filter output must be discarded, even though they contain additional information. Adding more bits to represent the RF data would address this limitation but would increase memory requirements and data transfer time. Increasing the dynamic range without increasing bit-width can instead be achieved using floating-point representation (float16, or ‘half’ datatype). In this work, we evaluate the benefits of float16 compared to int16 for storing RF data during flash-angled plane wave B-mode imaging.

papers.title: Incoherent Compounding Strategies for Ultrafast Imaging of Cardiac Structures
papers.abstract: Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) is an ultrasound-based imaging modality in which a transducer is introduced directly into the heart, offering increased procedural flexibility and patient comfort compared to transesophageal echocardiography (TEE). This work focuses on enhancing the image quality of ultrafast imaging sequences of the heart, applicable to both 2D and 3D ICE systems. Adapting to the dynamic environment in cardiac interventions and provide a high temporal resolution effectively restricts the available insonification time for any given region, thereby limiting the number of transmit events that can be combined in the compounding algorithm. To address this limitation, we compare the application of incoherent compounding strategies, including spatial and frequency compounding, which are known to improve contrast and signal-to-noise ratio in ultrasound imaging by reducing coherent noise. In addition, an adaptive weighting scheme for frequency compounding is proposed, where the contribution of different frequency bands is optimized as a function of imaging depth and angle. The proposed methods are evaluated on both phantom and in vivo datasets.

papers.title: Deep Bayesian Refocus
papers.abstract: The full array response matrix, or multistatic dataset, contains individual element responses and allows for synthetic aperture focusing, retrospective transmit beamforming, and sharper lateral resolution than focused transmit sequences. In REFoCUS the multistatic dataset is recovered from a set of arbitrary transmits through inversion of the frequency domain forward model. In this work, we expand on this through the introduction of a probabilistic generative model to approximate the true posterior distribution, offering a much richer modeling of the joint multistatic prior statistics across all frequencies and elements. This enables sampling of plausible measurement-consistent multistatic sets from a strongly reduced set of acquisitions.

papers.title: IQ Demodulation As a Spatial Frequency Selector in Ultrafast Ice Imaging: Implications for Aliasing
papers.abstract: IQ demodulation and bandpass filtering are standard components of ultrasound beamforming. However, their influence on spatial sampling and aliasing has received limited attention. We investigate how demodulation frequency and filtering bandwidth affect image formation in ultrafast intracardiac echocardiography (ICE), where miniaturized arrays impose trade-offs between element pitch, aperture size, and field of view, particularly near steering limits. Due to the coupling of temporal and spatial domains, a selected temporal frequency band directly maps to a spatial frequency band. If this exceeds the array’s spatial sampling limit, aliasing occurs, leading to grating-lobe-like artifacts. This can be interpreted as a receive-side extension of the spatial Nyquist constraint d ≤ λ/2. We demonstrate these effects in vivo: higher-frequency demodulation within the system bandwidth leads to artifacts and phase wrapping, while lower-frequency settings improve localization and preserve phase coherence. These results show that demodulation and filtering act as spatial frequency selectors, enabling a trade-off between resolution and aliasing in ultrafast imaging.

sessions.title: MTC: Advanced Signal Processing, Speed-of-Sound & Nonlinearity Estimation

papers.title: Local Dispersion Analysis Based on Wavelet Transform for Soft Tissue Viscoelastic Inversion
papers.abstract: Ultrasonic shear wave elastography is widely used for non-invasive evaluation of biological tissue mechanical properties. However, traditional methods mainly focus on tissue elasticity and ignore viscous dispersion, leading to inaccurate viscoelastic parameter inversion. Existing dispersion estimation methods have low local spatial resolution and large errors in heterogeneous media. Therefore, this work proposes a local dispersion analysis method based on continuous wavelet transform, achieving high-precision dispersion curve reconstruction and viscoelastic parameter inversion through time-frequency decomposition and cross-correlation phase difference estimation.

papers.title: High-Resolution Amplitude-Based Reflection-Mode Sound Speed Mapping
papers.abstract: The tissue’s speed of sound (SoS) is a promising diagnostic marker for, e.g., cancer or liver disease. The phase shift of echoes when acquired with varying transmit/receive steering angles allows spatially resolved mapping of the SoS using handheld ultrasound but is inherently limited by the trade-off between angular and spatial resolution of echo acquisition. In this study we demonstrate that it is possible to resolve phase aberrations far below the resolution of the echoes, by inverting a forward model that relates the acquired echo amplitudes for all angle combinations to the aberration profiles for each angle. We show in a phantom study that this not only leads to highly resolved SoS maps, but in addition reduces artefactual noise due to short-scale aberrations. Preliminary results confirm the feasibility in real tissue.

papers.title: Unrolled Proximal Gradient Descent Algorithm for Attenuation Coefficient Estimation (PI- ACE): a Self-Supervised Physics-Informed Method for Quantitative Ultrasound
papers.abstract: We present PI-ACE, a self-supervised, physics-informed framework for attenuation coefficient estimation (ACE). The method formulates ACE as a maximum a posteriori problem and solves it using an unrolled proximal gradient descent approach, where the proximal operator is replaced with a learnable neural network. This design enables subject-specific adaptation while maintaining physical consistency, eliminating the need for manual parameter tuning. The model is trained using a data-consistency loss without ground truth labels and implemented with a U-Net across multiple unrolled iterations. Evaluated on simulated homogeneous and heterogeneous phantoms, PI-ACE achieves improved accuracy compared to maximum likelihood methods while demonstrating substantially improved robustness to noise and enhanced boundary delineation.

papers.title: Latent Space Separation with a Disentangled Autoencoder for Local B/a Imaging
papers.abstract: This work evaluates deep learning methods for estimating local B/A maps from cumulative B/A maps obtained with the depletion method. The conventional linear inversion assumes that cumulative values are depth averages of local values, which may introduce bias when nonlinear effects are present in heterogeneous media. A U-Net and a disentangled autoencoder were trained on k-Wave simulations with different B/A spatial configurations and evaluated on both simulated data and out-of-distribution physical phantom data. Results showed that the autoencoder had lower errors beneath inclusions, while both DL methods performed similarly to or better than linear inversion in layered cases. These findings indicate that latent-space separation can be useful for local B/A reconstruction.

papers.title: Improving B/A Imaging with a Multi-Energy Level Regression Strategy
papers.abstract: This work proposes multi-energy-level regression (MLR) to improve B/A imaging when hydrophone pressure-scaling measurements are uncertain. The depletion method estimates B/A from fundamental-band changes between two pressure levels, but it is sensitive to errors in the true low- and high-pressure scaling factor. MLR instead uses multiple drive levels and a nonlinear fundamental-band pressure model. Reference phantom data with known attenuation and Gol’dberg number estimate the optimal pressure-scaling axis, and sample data estimate the sample Gol’dberg number and B/A. The method was tested in matched simulations and physical phantoms with characterized sample/reference B/A values of 6.8 and 6.7. Simulations used 20 pressure levels and compared no scaling noise with 4% added noise; phantom data used hydrophone-measured scaling factors. In simulations, only one DM pair shifted less from baseline than MLR under noise. In phantoms, DM estimates showed high variability: the modal DM shifted 14.5% from simulation and the mean over all DM pairs shifted 43%, while MLR shifted 5.3%. These results suggest MLR reduces sensitivity to pressure-calibration uncertainty in B/A imaging.

sessions.title: MBB: Deep Beamforming and Image Reconstruction Methods

papers.title: DeconvNet: Unifying Beamforming and Deconvolution for Plane-Wave Imaging
papers.abstract: Plane-wave (PW) imaging enables ultrafast ultrasound acquisition but suffers from low image quality due to the lack of transmit focusing. Coherent plane-wave compounding (CPWC) improves imaging performance but relies on delay-and-sum beamforming, an approximate adjoint operator that leads to blurred tissue reflectivity function (TRF) estimates. Conventional methods separate beamforming and deconvolution as sequential steps, limiting image quality and temporal resolution. To address this trade-off, this study proposes DeconvNet, an end-to-end deep learning framework that unifies beamforming and deconvolution in a single network to directly map single-PW RF data into high-quality deconvolved TRF outputs. Evaluated on the PICMUS dataset, DeconvNet achieved a −6 dB FWHM of 0.8 mm, outperforming single-PW by 1.88× and CPWC by 1.25×. Carotid imaging results show a CNR of 3.76 dB, exceeding CPWC by 0.34 dB and single-PW by 1.44 dB. DeconvNet effectively sharpens the PSF, improves resolution and contrast, and recovers a more realistic TRF, achieving CPWC-level image quality from a single transmission with real-time efficiency.

papers.title: Hybrid Beam Pixel-Based Focusing for Ultrafast High-Frequency Phased-Array Imaging
papers.abstract: Hybrid Beam Pixel-Based Focusing (HbPBF) is a new ultrafast imaging approach for high-frequency phased-array ultrasound. The technique combines bidirectional pixel-based focusing and unified pixel-based beamforming to improve image quality across depth while maintaining high-frame-rate capability. The method uses a depth-dependent transition between delay models, adapts beam boundaries and weighting for phased-array sector imaging, and reduces reconstruction cost by beamforming only a subset of receive lines per transmit to reduce hardware cost. HbPBF was evaluated at 30 MHz against focused imaging and diverging-wave imaging using simulations, wire-target measurements, phantom measurements of contrast and signal-to-noise performance, and in vivo wrist imaging. Results showed that HbPBF improved performance relative to diverging-wave imaging, especially at greater depths, while preserving high frame rate capability and reducing signal leakage into low-intensity regions. These findings suggest HbPBF is a practical alternative for high-frequency ultrafast B-mode imaging.

papers.title: Physics-Informed RF-Domain Learning for Beamforming in Coherent Multi-Transducer Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Coherent multi-transducer ultrasound (CoMTUS) expands the effective aperture and can improve field of view and spatial resolution, but combining multiple transmit–receive datasets over a discontinuous aperture is challenging for conventional delay-and-sum (DAS) beamforming. This work presents a physics-informed RF-domain learning approach for CoMTUS beamforming using a 2-D U-Net operating directly on element-wise delayed-RF data, with a post-reconstruction model on DAS envelope images used as reference. Models were trained on Field II simulations generated from photo-based echogenicity maps and evaluated against DAS on simulated, in vitro, and in vivo data. The physics-informed model achieved the lowest intensity adjusted mean absolute error, best point-target resolution, and improved sidelobe suppression with reduced noise floor. It also produced improved feature delineation and clearest point targets in in vitro CIRS phantom test, and produced sharper in vivo gallbladder boundaries, although with some contrast reduction. These results indicate that physics-informed RF-domain learning beamformer is a more effective method to exploit the CoMTUS aperture than DAS.

papers.title: Plane-Wave Compounding Based on f-K Migration and Fourier Ptychographic Spectrum Stitching
papers.abstract: Plane-wave (PW) imaging provides ultrahigh frame rates and is widely used in cardiovascular imaging, microvascular imaging. However, single-angle PW imaging suffers from limited lateral resolution, elevated sidelobes, and poor visualization of weak scatterers due to the lack of transmit focusing. Coherent PW compounding improves image quality by coherently summing multiple angles, but it does not fully exploit the complementary spectral information among different steering angles. Fourier ptychography (FP) offers a promising strategy for expanding spectral support through multi-angle spectrum stitching and overlap-region updating. This work aims to combine f-k domain beamforming, FP spectrum stitching, and frequency-domain sign coherence factor (FDSCF) weighting to improve lateral resolution while suppressing sidelobes.

papers.title: Differentiable Paraxial Full-Waveform Inversion for Fast Through-Transmission Speed-of-Sound Imaging
papers.abstract: In through-transmission ultrasound tomography, speed-of-sound (SoS) is traditionally reconstructed by back-projecting travel time delays, which is computationally efficient but lacks accuracy. In contrast, full waveform inversion (FWI) can deliver SoS images with high detail but at the cost of very long computation times. In this research we propose differentiable paraxial FWI, which allows for a massive improvement of performance and brings FWI based ultrasound tomography closer to a real-time modality, which is regarded as crucial for clinical adaptation. We propose a split-step wave solver implemented in JAX to leverage hardware acceleration. This enables an efficient auto-differentiation without the need for computationally expensive wavefield simulations. The approach was tested on numerical SoS phantoms for an imaging geometry consisting of a ring of 8 linear arrays. SoS map reconstruction took 1 minute on a portable system using a readily available mobile GPU. Compared to a baseline straight-ray travel-time reconstruction, the paraxial-based reconstruction shows more detail and a significantly improved resolution. Future work will focus on validating the method in vitro.

papers.title: Plane-Wave Image Reconstruction in Fourier Domain Using IQ Channel Data
papers.abstract: Fourier-domain beamforming (FDB) can reconstruct plane-wave ultrasound images at a much lower computational cost compared to the conventional delay-and-sum (DAS) approach. Note that the latter can handle both raw radio-frequency (RF) and in-phase/quadrature (IQ) channel data. As IQ beamforming is often preferable (e.g., baseband data processing), we investigate a simple extension of RF-based FDB to handle IQ signals. Based on the PICMUS experimental data, we demonstrate that IQ-based FDB produces high-quality B-mode images as anticipated.

sessions.title: MPA: Biomedical Applications of Photoacoustic Imaging

papers.title: Enhancing Minimally Invasive Neurosurgical Guidance Using Coherent Multi-Transducer Photoacoustic Imaging
papers.abstract: Photoacoustic (PA) imaging provides optical contrast with ultrasonic resolution and can visualize critical intracranial structures, but transcranial PA imaging is limited by skull-induced aberration, attenuation, reverberation and restricted acoustic windows. This study evaluates a coherent multi-transducer PA imaging approach combining internal PA excitation with multi-transducer ultrasound reception to improve endonasal neurosurgical guidance. Two-dimensional k-Wave simulations were performed using a CT-based human head model. Internal PA excitation was modelled as a point source at the pituitary gland, and four phased arrays positioned at ocular and temporal acoustic windows received the ultrasound signals. Images were reconstructed using conventional delay-and-sum (DAS) and aberration-corrected DAS, with time reversal as a benchmark. Multi-transducer reception improved target visibility, while aberration correction reduced artifacts and sidelobes and enhanced focusing. Aberration-corrected coherent multi-transducer imaging achieved the best performance, demonstrating its potential to improve transcranial image quality for minimally invasive neurosurgical guidance.

papers.title: A Multimodal copolymer-in-Oil Phantom for Photoacoustic Imaging Quality assurance: inter-Platform Performance Evaluation
papers.abstract: Photoacoustic imaging (PAI) is advancing toward clinical translation, yet standardized quality assurance (QA) tools remain limited. Inspired by established ultrasound QA practices, we present a multimodal phantom based on styrene–ethylene/butylene–styrene (SEBS) in mineral oil for the quantitative assessment of key imaging metrics. SEBS is a stable tissue-mimicking material recently validated in a multicenter study by the International Photoacoustic Standardisation Consortium. The phantom integrates three modules: (i) spectral sensitivity analysis using vessels with CuSO₄ solution for hemoglobin-like absorption; (ii) imaging depth; and (iii) spatial resolution. Three PAI/US platforms (AcousticX, Vevo 2100, and Vevo F2) were evaluated. Results show superior lateral resolution for Vevo systems, while the lower-frequency LED-based platform showed greater penetration depth. SNR decreased with depth across all systems, and strong linearity between the PA signal and CuSO₄ concentration was observed. PAI spectral measurements agreed with expected CuSO₄ absorption (r > 0.96). This SEBS-based phantom provides a robust tool for standardized QA and cross-platform evaluation.

papers.title: Longitudinal US/Pa Tracking of Live-Cell Migration in 3D Hydrogel Systems
papers.abstract: Inflammatory environments are frequently characterized by dysregulated cell migration, which plays a critical role in impaired tissue repair. Consequently, the ability to monitor cellular migratory behavior is essential for understanding and evaluating regenerative processes under such conditions. US/PA imaging provide a noninvasive, longitudinal approach for tracking cell dynamics in real time. In this study, we investigate the behavior of nanoparticle-labeled macrophages within 3D hydrogel constructs using a custom-designed, gas-permeable, sterile in vitro US/PA imaging platform. This system enables continuous monitoring of live-cell activity while maintaining physiologically relevant conditions. Key findings demonstrate distinct migration patterns across hydrogels with varying porosity and characterize the infiltration of surface-seeded cells into the scaffold interior. Collectively, this platform establishes a foundation for advanced in vitro live-cell imaging studies and provides critical insights to guide future in vivo applications aimed at tracking cellular behavior in inflammatory environments.

papers.title: Photoacoustic-Guided Clutter Filtering for Ultrafast Power Doppler Microvascular Imaging
papers.abstract: Ultrafast power Doppler microvascular imaging provides a safe, low-cost approach for visualizing microvascular perfusion, but weak slow-flow signals are often obscured by dominant tissue clutter with overlapping spatiotemporal features. This study proposes a photoacoustic-guided clutter filtering method that incorporates vascular priors from co-registered single-wavelength photoacoustic images into Doppler signal decomposition. The Doppler ensemble is formulated as a Casorati matrix and decomposed into low-rank tissue clutter and sparse blood-flow components using nuclear-norm and weighted row-sparsity regularization. Sparsity weights derived from the photoacoustic image assign lower penalties to vessel-like regions, preserving slow microvascular flow while suppressing background clutter. Simulations using k-Wave and Field II data showed that the proposed method preserved vascular continuity better than Butterworth, SVD, block-wise SVD, and stable rPCA filters. The method achieved the best CNR-SNR balance and the highest connectivity, signal-to-clutter ratio, contrast ratio, and clutter rejection ratio, indicating improved preservation of weak slow flow and enhanced image quality.

papers.title: Quantitative Association of Photoacoustic Nanoparticle Distributions with Thermal Response in Magnetic Hyperthermia
papers.abstract: This study evaluates the relationship between photoacoustic imaging (PAI)-derived nanoparticle distributions and thermal response during magnetic hyperthermia (MH). Manganese ferrite nanoparticles were intratumorally injected into LNCaP tumors in five mice and imaged using a combined ultrasound/PA system. MH was induced using an alternating magnetic field, while surface temperature was monitored via infrared thermography. Reconstructed PA volumes were processed by combining depth-resolved axial slices into projections, which were spatially aligned with thermal maps. Correlation analysis showed a maximum Pearson coefficient (r = 0.64) at depths 13.8% below the tumor surface. The highest correlation was obtained using 70 stacked slices, corresponding to a large fraction of the tumor volume. Three mice reached hyperthermic conditions (>41 °C), and cumulative thermal dose (CEM43) correlated with nanoparticle distribution. These results support the use of PAI for predicting thermal response in MH.

papers.title: Micro-Ultrasound and Photoacoustic Imaging for Picosecond Infra-Red Laser Assisted Intra-Tumor Injections
papers.abstract: This study evaluates Picosecond Infra-Red Laser (PIRL)-assisted intratumoral injections guided by micro-ultrasound (micro-US) and photoacoustic imaging (PAI) in DU-145 prostate cancer xenografts in mice. PIRL selectively vaporizes tissue water, creating lesions with cavities at the center that can be used for localized drug deposition, potentially improving drug diffusion and reducing backflow during intratumoral dye delivery. For ablation, a sapphire fiber was inserted into tumors and operated at 0.9 mJ/pulse for 120 min under micro-US guidance. For dye delivery, 50 µL methylene blue was administered through an automated 7-step injection array, with cavities created at each site using 0.25 mJ/pulse for 45 s before injection. Volumetric PAI assessed post-injection dye distribution. Micro-US clearly visualized the PIRL fiber, cavitation clouds, and post-ablation hypoechoic cavities. Histology confirmed a ~1 mm cavity surrounded by coagulation. PAI demonstrated successful intratumoral dye distribution in 3D tumor volumes. These results show that PIRL combined with micro-US and PAI enables tumor ablation and targeted dye delivery.

sessions.title: MSD: Research and Open-source platforms

papers.title: Highly Modular Large Channel Count Ultrafast Ultrasound Research Platform for Both Imaging and Therapy
papers.abstract: Affordable and compact large-channel-count ultrasound systems are needed for volumetric ultrafast ultrasound imaging research, especially with the growing use of fully populated 2D matrix arrays. Although 2D matrix arrays can provide the highest volumetric imaging rates, they typically require 1024 or more independent ultrasound channels, making existing high-channel-count systems prohibitively expensive for most ultrasound imaging researchers. To address this limitation, we initiated the development of a highly modular, large-channel-count ultrafast ultrasound research platform that reduces the total system cost to less than 70,000 USD while also supporting therapeutic ultrasound applications through arbitrary waveform generation (AWG) capability.

papers.title: Ultrasound Imaging System Based on Capacitive Micromachined Ultrasonic Transducer Array for Continuous Monitoring in Small Animal Research
papers.abstract: Continuous ultrasound imaging of small animals enables non-invasive, real-time assessment of biological responses essential for evaluating disease progression and therapeutic interventions. However, conventional imaging systems employ bulky PUTs that obstruct access to the animal and limit compatibility with concurrent experimental procedures. Here, a miniaturized ultrasound imaging system with a CMUT array is developed for seamless integration with a surgical bed. This enables unobstructed surgical access during imaging and supports versatile in vivo experiments. A surgical bed comprising a 1D CMUT array operating at 7 MHz was integrated with an oil-filled chamber and a TPX acoustic window. Imaging of mouse abdominal organs and real-time visualization of a needle injection were successful over 3 hours of continuous operation. The proposed system offers a compact, high-performance imaging solution that enables real-time monitoring of internal structures while maintaining full spatial access. This capability facilitates multimodal experimental protocols in preclinical research, enabling comprehensive studies on the effects of various treatments.

papers.title: Ultrasound Research Scanners - Which Metrics Need improvement?
papers.abstract: Contemporary ultrasound imaging techniques can produce high-quality 2D and 3D images, derive various properties of the interrogated tissues, such as elasticity and speed of sound, and uncover microvascular structure through super-resolution imaging. These goals place high demands on the ultrasound research scanners used to develop new imaging methods. This work presents a quantitative comparison between three research scanners.

papers.title: Scanning System for Abdominal Us Tomography
papers.abstract: Ultrasound tomography (UST) has previously been used for breast imaging; this project aims to extend that capability to the abdomen using a semicircular array geometry. A full synthetic aperture (FSA) dataset is acquired by moving two transducers around an arc, then processed via full waveform inversion (FWI) to reconstruct SoS images. Simulations using the open-source Stride library compared 180° vs. 360° array coverage and element counts of 32, 64, 128, and 192. Two FWI starting models were tested: a uniform 1540 m/s and a bone-informed model generated by a neural network. Results showed 360° coverage outperformed 180°, higher element counts improved resolution, and the bone-informed starting model consistently produced superior reconstructions. A physical prototype was also built using a 250° track on an 80/20 frame, with stepper motors driving a 2.25 MHz piston transducer and a P4-2v transducer. The system was successfully integrated with a Verasonics scanner and tested on an abdominal phantom. Experimental reconstructions are forthcoming. Together, the simulation and hardware results mark meaningful progress toward a clinically deployable abdominal UST scanner.

papers.title: U-Sonic: An Open-Source 8-Channel Ultrasound Transmit IP in a 130 nm RISC-V SoC
papers.abstract: Miniaturized ultrasound (US) front-ends require synchronized multi-element TX with programmable bursts, aperture selection, and damping control. Existing research ASICs achieve high channel counts but are closed and difficult to reuse, commercial HV pulser ICs offer mainly register-level control, and MCU-based pulsers are typically single-channel with limited synchronization. We present an open-source TX peripheral for a RISC-V US SoC, spanning RTL, open EDA, and open PDK integration. The SoC core configures up to 16 pulser cores through a memory-mapped Open Bus Interface. Each core supports single- or dual-frequency bursts, programmable period, duty cycle, burst length, polarity, and an optional inverted stop pulse for damping, with 10 ns timing resolution at 100 MHz. A shared control register enables simultaneous start/stop and clock-gating for synchronized multi-channel excitation. The IP was verified in Verilator against a Python golden model, validated on an Intel DE10-Lite FPGA, and implemented in IHP SG13 130 nm using Yosys and OpenROAD. RTL, drivers, verification, and physical design scripts are released under permissive licenses.

papers.title: Ultraportable Ultrasound Platform for Edge Processors and GPUs
papers.abstract: The emergence of AI-enabled mobile processors creates an opportunity to rethink ultraportable ultrasound architectures. This work aims to enable AFE-to-mobile processor connectivity to study software-defined ultrasound processing in edge processors or GPUs. We present an ultraportable ultrasound platform that interfaces AFEs to mobile processors using commodity USB-C and MIPI links for raw or processed data. The system could support simultaneous data rates of 5 Gbps (USB-C) and 6 Gbps (MIPI), achieving an aggregate throughput of 10~11 Gbps. For a 32-channel AFE operating at 25 MS/s with 12-bit resolution and a 64-channel transmitter, the raw data rate reaches 9.6 Gbps. With digital demodulation and decimation enable >2× data reduction, supporting real-time software beamforming on mobile GPUs or edge processors. The platform supports up to 64 receive and 128 transmit channels within a compact form factor for ultraportable and wearable applications. Experimental validation demonstrates feasible high-speed data transfer for future GPU-centric beamforming in handheld systems. Traditional DAS beamformer can also be implemented.

papers.title: Open-Source, High-Throughput, Scalable Backplane Link Architecture for High-End Wearable Ultrasound Probes
papers.abstract: Wireless wearable US (WUS) probes are increasingly limited by data bandwidth between acquisition electronics and the radio. Recent 32-channel Wi-Fi-based WUS report 55 Mbps radio capability, but FPGA-to-MCU SPI readout stays below 35 Mbps, limiting frame rate. We present an open-source WUS interface that removes this bottleneck via a low-resource multi-wire SPI readout IP, orchestration firmware, and a co-designed power stage. The IP connects an FPGA to a SiLabs SiWG917 MCU on the same SPI pins in two modes: conventional full-duplex SPI for AFE and pulser configuration, and multi-wire half-duplex readout for high-throughput FPGA-to-MCU transfer. A FSM switches automatically between programming and acquisition. Raw US data are read from the FPGA buffer at 80 Mbps via DMA and streamed over UDP at up to 55 Mbps. Implemented on an AMD Kria K26 FPGA, the IP uses 71 LUTs/97 FFs, <1 mW logic power, supports standard SPI fallback, and reaches 80/160 Mbps in dual/quad mode. In a SoA WUS probe, it saturates the 55 Mbps Wi-Fi payload (+57% BW), enabling >250 Hz raw 32-channel B-mode and >2 kHz synthetic Doppler PRF in a sub-1 W battery-powered probe.

sessions.title: TES: Front-end Electronics and Integrated Ultrasound Systems

papers.title: A Step Towards Vertical Integration of Integrated Circuits Underneath a 2D Ultrasound Transducer Array
papers.abstract: In 2D ultrasound arrays, application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) must be pitch-matched to the transducer above, and conventional planar integration limits the circuit area per element. Existing solutions such as redistribution layers introduce parasitic coupling. We propose orienting ASICs with their active face perpendicular to the transducer, decoupling circuit area from transducer dimensions. Here, we demonstrate the fabrication of side-wall contacts on a chip using planar processes. Chips from a TSMC 180nm BCD wafer with aluminum interconnects were diced along their active plane to expose the interconnect pattern on the vertical face, enabling side contacts when the chip is oriented vertically. Through CMOS post-processing, Transfer Length Method (TLM) pad structures were deposited to contact the exposed aluminum and the BCD silicon substrate for reference. Kelvin 4-point probe measurements confirmed current flow through the aluminum interconnects, and the extracted contact resistance was consistent with literature values. These results demonstrate the feasibility of side-wall contacts on CMOS chips for vertical integration of transceivers under 2D ultrasound arrays.

papers.title: Arbitrary Biasing of Electrostrictive Row-Column Ultrasound Arrays
papers.abstract: This work presents novel biasing electronics for electrostrictive row-column ultrasound arrays (RCAs). Unlike conventional RCAs, electrostrictive relaxor-based RCAs require an applied electric field to exhibit piezoelectric behavior, and that behavior scales with the magnitude and polarity of the bias voltage — enabling more sophisticated imaging strategies. Existing biasing systems are limited to 4-state architectures, restricting their flexibility. To overcome this, the authors developed a distributed, amplified DAC system with 256 channels of DC bias, each microcontroller-controlled with 4096 programmable voltage states per channel. The design delivers 14-bit resolution from 0–250V with buffered outputs to handle low-impedance transducers, integrated with a Verasonics ultrasound platform. The electronics achieve a switching rise time under 20 μs and a slew rate of 12.5 V/μs, enabling advanced techniques such as transmit/receive apodization and SPARC beam steering in full 3D volumes — capabilities not possible with prior biasing architectures.

papers.title: Implementation of Multi-FPGA Architecture of Scalable Airborne Dual Transmit/ Receive Ultrasound Phased Array Synchronization and Self-Registration
papers.abstract: Scalable airborne ultrasound phased arrays demand thousand-channel apertures, but master–slave FPGA architectures impose central bandwidth bottlenecks. We propose a distributed multi-FPGA receiver where each board uses an independent USB 3.0 link, synchronized via a shared 10.24 MHz reference clock and open-drain wired-OR trigger bus with handshake-free, deterministic alignment. Each T/R module hosts 128 channels in 32 ADC clusters with analog multiplexing, supporting three modes: sparse-aperture (1 MSPS/channel), full-aperture (142.9 kSPS/sensor), and coherent-averaging (10 dB SNR gain). At 40 kHz and 20 cm, the physics-limited PRF reaches 855 Hz; an 800-channel frame transfers in 490 µs within the 1.17 ms receive window, confirming USB is no longer the bottleneck. Modes 1–2 sustain 855 FPS, Mode 3 delivers 85.5 FPS. The architecture scales linearly, and integrated self-registration enables real-time element-position calibration, sharpening the PSF and enhancing imaging resolution.

papers.title: Charge-Recycling Driving Scheme for Power-Efficient Therapeutic CMUT Ultrasound Transmitters
papers.abstract: Therapeutic ultrasound systems require high power to deliver focused energy, but conventional transmitters suffer from low efficiency, causing heat and power issues that hinder mobile or implantable applications. This work addresses these barriers by introducing an adiabatic charging scheme designed for Capacitive Micromachined Ultrasonic Transducers (CMUTs). While typical CMUT driving involves repetitive charging and discharging that wastes energy, our method recycles charge by transferring it between four transducer arrays operating at 0°, 90°, 180°, and 270° phases. By coordinating these phases through specialized switch logic, we significantly minimize power dissipation. Experimental validation using a CM5 linear CMUT array at 2.5 MHz demonstrated a reduction in power consumption from 1,111 mW to 340 mW—a 69.4% improvement, closely approaching the theoretical 75% limit. Further 2D scanning at a 31-mm depth aligned with Field II simulations, and the scheme's efficacy was successfully extended to Fresnel acoustic lenses for ring-type CMUT arrays. This approach proves the feasibility of highly efficient, compact therapeutic ultrasound platforms.

papers.title: Enhanced Acoustic Transmission and Resolution in Intracranial Ultrasound Neuromodulation Using Titanium-Encapsulated Transducers: a Simulation Study
papers.abstract: Ultrasound enables non-invasive neuromodulation with high spatiotemporal precision. However, transcranial ultrasound (TUS) suffers from skull-induced attenuation and aberration, which result in limited resolution. In contrast, intracranial ultrasound (IUS), with transducers implanted epidurally, bypasses skull-induced distortions, enabling stable, reproducible transducer positioning—ideal for chronic closed-loop neuromodulation. Nevertheless, IUS requires hermetic and biocompatible encapsulation, but its effects on acoustic fields remain unclear. To quantify IUS advantages on acoustic transmission, we modeled TUS and IUS using finite-element simulations, incorporating all anatomical layers for both configurations. The results demonstrate that titanium encapsulation can be suitable for acoustic transmission, with up to two-fold higher pressure compared with TUS. Furthermore, IUS enables the use of higher frequencies, which are key parameters to improve spatial selectivity in ultrasound neuromodulation applications.

papers.title: A 5-Channel Closed-Loop Multi-Level CMOS Pulser for Wideband PMUT Synthetic Aperture Imaging
papers.abstract: Wideband Piezoelectric Micromachined Ultrasonic Transducers (PMUTs) are vital for balancing penetration depth and axial resolution in cardiovascular monitoring. However, maximizing their broadband potential requires specialized multi-level, frequency-tunable pulsers. To address this, we present a custom 5-channel multi-level pulser IC designed to drive wideband PMUT arrays. This work demonstrates the highly integrated pulser's capability in enabling synthetic aperture imaging (SAI) of screw phantoms, paving the way for scalable, high-resolution wearable ultrasound systems.

papers.title: Impact of Ground Bounce in Row-Column-Addressed and Linear CMUT Arrays
papers.abstract: Ground bounce in row-column-addressed (RCA) and linear CMUT arrays is investigated as an array-level mechanism affecting terminal voltage and electrical crosstalk. SPICE models of the transmit, receive, and return networks were developed using BVD equivalent circuits for the CMUT elements and representative return-network values from a prototype probe. The models were validated using scaled measurements on 16-element linear arrays, where substrate and passive-element voltages were monitored during emission. The validated models were used to predict ground-bounce effects in larger RCA and linear array configurations. The results show that finite return-network impedance can induce coupling to passive elements, while decoupling-network design strongly affects terminal voltage during both transmit and receive. Optimized decoupling substantially reduced simulated transmit crosstalk. The results demonstrate the value of circuit models for guiding return-network design and reducing crosstalk in CMUT arrays.

sessions.title: SPT: Ultrasound Neural Stimulation and Guidance

papers.topicName: Spotlight Session: Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Devices & Applications
papers.title: Design and Verification of a Compact 4-Channel Ultrasound Excitation System for Wearable Low Intensity Stimulation
papers.abstract: Ultrasound neuromodulation offers high spatial-temporal precision, yet existing systems often lack the integration required for wearable applications. We present a compact, 4-channel integrated excitation system featuring independent frequency, phase, and amplitude control. Coordinated by an STM32 MCU, the architecture integrates AD9833 signal generation and high-voltage amplification, delivering a stable ±60 V output and 10 W per channel. Custom flexible transducers with optimized impedance matching were developed to ensure robust electromechanical coupling. System characterization at 348 kHz confirmed excellent channel consistency.With ±60 V excitation and a 2000 Hz PRF, a single channel generated 220 kPa acoustic pressure.Acoustic field mapping validated focusing performance: in the X-Y plane, the simulated lateral FWHM was 4.61 mm, while the experimental result was 5.33 mm. In the X-Z plane, the simulated and experimental axial FWHMs were 9.52 mm and 13.93 mm, respectively. This integrated platform demonstrates a robust, high-fidelity solution for targeted wearable ultrasound neuromodulation.

papers.topicName: Spotlight Session: Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Devices & Applications
papers.title: Skull-Channel-Adaptive POSP-NLFM for Standing-Wave Mitigation in Transcranial Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) is promising for neuromodulation, but acoustic transmission through the skull is affected by frequency-selective attenuation, reflection, and multipath effects. Fixed-frequency continuous wave (CW) can reinforce skull-mediated interference, producing standing waves, focal shift, and hotspots that raise thermal accumulation and off-target stimulation risk. LFM broadens bandwidth and can reduce CW interference, but does not compensate the skull-filtered spectrum at the target. To address this source–channel mismatch, we propose a CT-informed skull-channel-adaptive POSP-NLFM waveform. A short broadband probe estimated the target-specific transfer function H(f). Guided by stationary-phase theory, dwell time was shifted toward skull-attenuated bands through sweep-rate control. In k-Wave simulations within 400–600 kHz, H(f) showed a notch near 480 kHz and attenuation at 530–580 kHz. POSP-NLFM reduced focal shift to 1.31 mm versus 2.01 mm for LFM and 1.45 mm for CW, and showed lower ripple than CW over 79.7% of the analyzed axial extent, supporting skull-aware dwell-time control for more stable tFUS.

papers.topicName: Spotlight Session: Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Devices & Applications
papers.title: Effects of isoflurane Depth on transcranial Focused ultrasound-Induced neuromodulation in Mice
papers.abstract: Anesthesia is frequently used in preclinical studies of transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) neuromodulation. Due to the need of animal restraint during the stimulation, isoflurane anesthesia is a commonly used method to achieve this purpose. However, anesthesia itself has a profound effect on the brain which might interfere with the tFUS-induced neuromodulation. To address this, we systematically studied isoflurane anesthesia with varying concentrations while applying single tFUS pulses and using fiber photometry calcium imaging as our neuronal readout. Contrary to our expectations, our findings showed a significant effect of isoflurane anesthesia on tFUS-induced calcium responses, in which the highest calcium peaks induced in response to tFUS pulses were under the highest isoflurane concentration. Our study poses critical questions on the influence of anesthesia on tFUS neuromodulation and highlights the need for a more systematic investigation of the brain state effect on the neuromodulation outcomes.

papers.topicName: Spotlight Session: Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Devices & Applications
papers.title: Conditional Diffusion Models for 3D Transcranial Ultrasound Simulation
papers.abstract: This work develops a conditional diffusion surrogate for fast 3D transcranial ultrasound simulation. Patient-specific planning requires repeated prediction of steady-state wave propagation through heterogeneous skull and brain media, but full-wave Helmholtz solvers are computationally expensive. Deterministic learning-based surrogates can accelerate prediction, but they often oversmooth high-frequency oscillatory wavefields and reduce focal accuracy. To address this limitation, we train a conditional diffusion model with a 3D U-shaped Vision Transformer denoising backbone to map acoustic property volumes and transducer source descriptions to steady-state pressure fields. The method is evaluated on four in-silico datasets: synthetic skull phantoms, anatomical head models with randomized single-element transducer placement, tumor-augmented head models, and randomized activation patterns of a 1024-element hemispherical array. Compared with U-Net and Fourier neural operator baselines, the diffusion model achieves lower wavefield error, energy error, focal position error, and maximum pressure error, showing improved preservation of oscillatory structure and focal localization.

papers.topicName: Spotlight Session: Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Devices & Applications
papers.title: Deep Learning-Based Volumetric Tracer Diffusion Segmentation of Focused Ultrasound Modulated glymphatic Clearance in Rat Brain
papers.abstract: This abstract presents a deep learning framework for volumetric analysis of glymphatic tracer diffusion in ex vivo rat brain fluorescence images after low-intensity tFUS. The study compares control and tFUS groups to evaluate how ultrasound affects tracer transport, showing broader and more extensive tracer distribution in the tFUS condition. To replace manual, time-consuming, and variable tracer annotation, a deep learning-based pipeline has been developed using a densely convolutional spatial attention network. The model processes 128×128 fluorescence slices from 26 rats and achieves overlap scores of 0.52 IoU/0.66 Dice for tFUS and 0.43 IoU/0.58 Dice for control. These results indicate that deep learning can provide fast, consistent, and accurate results for volumetric analysis of tracer diffusion, supporting studies of glymphatic clearance and its potential relevance to brain disorders, including Alzheimer’s disease, and future therapeutic applications.

papers.topicName: Spotlight Session: Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Devices & Applications
papers.title: Optimal Transcranial Focusing Using Broadband Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM)
papers.abstract: Transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) suffers from frequency-dependent skull attenuation that varies by location, yet conventional single-frequency or fixed broadband excitation ignores skull transmission bandwidth, compromising either energy delivery or focal precision. We propose an OFDM-based waveform design framework that treats the focal spectrum as an optimizable parameter. Using 3D full-wave k-Wave simulations of a 32×2 concave array and a CT-derived cadaveric skull, we characterized the focal transfer function (TF) at the temporal lobe via a 25-subcarrier OFDM signal (0.6–3 MHz, 100 kHz spacing) and applied two RMS-normalized weighting strategies: matched (proportional to TF magnitude) and inverse. Matched weighting maximized focusing gain, concentrating energy in efficiently transmitted bands—well suited for high-intensity therapy. Inverse weighting equalized the spectrum, producing a narrower focal zone at lower gain, favorable for low-intensity applications and imaging. Focal shifts remained sub-mm across waveforms. Spectral weighting guided by the skull TF thus enables application-specific control of tFUS focal characteristics within a unified framework.

sessions.title: AME: Modeling and Evaluation Techniques

papers.title: Miniaturized Helical Antenna for High-Temperature Vibration Sensor Applications
papers.abstract: In cutting edge industrial and power generation environments, sensors are needed to monitor mechanical vibrations that can operate at often extreme high temperatures (HT). Such environments limit the use of wired and/or active sensing components, making a passive and wireless langasite (LGS) surface acoustic wave resonator (SAWR)-based sensor system a very attractive solution. In this work, wireless, passive vibration sensing was obtained from room temperature (RT) to 500°C using an integrated sensing system made up of a miniaturized helical antenna and an LGS SAWR-based vibration sensor using a test setup including a mechanical shaker and custom furnace door. The antenna length was used to reduce the mismatch between the SAWR and the antenna without the use of any additional matching component. Wireless vibration sensing data was obtained from 14.5” away up to 14gs, in the 100Hz to 500Hz range, and over the entire temperature range up to 500°C. The results show a consistent wirelessly measured acceleration sensor system response over the entire temperature range, demonstrating the feasibility of this system for HT HE vibration sensor applications.

papers.title: FEM Modeling of Nonlinear Harmonics in Capacitors and SAW Devices on Lithium Tantalate Substrate
papers.abstract: Nonlinearity generation in lithium tantalate (LT) surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices is a hot topic in the industry, as the power density in high-frequency RF system is increasing. An accurate model that can predict such harmonics is necessary to understand device physics and to mitigate such effects. The current work employs full physics in piezoelectric solids, independently measured nonlinear material constants, and a 3D finite element model to predict nonlinear harmonics in LT SAW devices and capacitors. Both capacitors and SAW devices were fabricated on 42YX LT substrate. FEM models based on full nonlinear piezoelectric physics were developed to predict the harmonics measured in these devices, and there is good correlation between the model and the measurement. The findings of this study include: (1) a full physics nonlinear FEM model can be developed to predict harmonics on SAW despite the computational challenges; (2) the referenced independent nonlinear constants of LT are valid; (3) harmonics generation on LT42 SAW depends on the direction of the input power; (4) the physical origin of this direction dependence.

papers.title: Evaluation of Droplet Generation by a Surface Acoustic Wave Device for micro-Sized Particle Loading
papers.abstract: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices generate elastic waves on a substrate by applying high-frequency voltage to interdigital transducers. A key advantage is highly directional droplet ejection, enabling applications such as medical nebulizers and fragrance sprayers. However, conventional SAW systems are limited to droplets of only a few micrometers, restricting deliverable material size. To overcome this, we fabricated a SAW device via lift-off with an aluminum film exceeding 1 µm for stable high-power excitation. A 1 wt% fluorescent particle suspension containing 20, 50, and 100 µm diameter particles was supplied via syringe needle, and droplet dynamics were recorded by high-speed camera at 800 mA. High-speed camera observations demonstrated a previously unreported behavior distinct from jetting or atomization, which we term "secondary droplets," featuring simultaneous generation of fine droplets below 10 µm and larger droplets near 200 µm . Particle loading per droplet decreased with increasing particle diameter. These results suggest that secondary droplets can transport microscale solids, indicating potential applications such as artificial pollination.

papers.title: Spectrum Prediction of Surface Acoustic Wave Resonators Based on Multi-Resolution Wavelet Analysis and Ensemble Learning
papers.abstract: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators are essential in RF front-ends, yet conventional design relies on expensive finite element simulations. Recent machine learning surrogates using vector fitting suffer from limitations: global error minimization prioritizes the main resonance, degrading spurious peak predictions, and forcibly fitting spurious modes triggers "pole explosion." This work develops a wavelet-based surrogate using Extremely Randomized Trees (ExtraTrees) to decouple the main resonance from spurious peaks via wavelet decomposition, while a parallel branch predicts quality factors and resonance frequencies. Validated on thousands of measured resonators, the model accurately predicts full-band Y₁₁ spectra including spurious peaks without compromising the main resonance, addressing high-order pole instability and enabling fast inverse design of RF micro-acoustic devices.
keywords: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonator，wavelet transform，ensemble learning

papers.title: A Method of Evaluating TCF of Piezoelectric Thin Layer Without Depending on TCF of Substrate in HBAR
papers.abstract: The temperature coefficient of frequency (TCF) of piezoelectric thin film is important parameter to design SAW filters and BAW filters with high temperature stability. In general, accurate evaluation of the intrinsic TCF of piezoelectric layer requires the fabrication of free-standing resonators (FBAR) through substrate removal. However, this conventional method requires etching process, resulting in substantial times and cost for evaluation. In this study, we propose a new method to evaluate the TCF of piezoelectric layer using substrate-supported-film resonators (HBAR). Broad but smooth resonance-antiresonance peaks directly reflecting piezoelectric film properties can be obtained by gating the electromagnetic signal in (0 sec.) using window function and eliminating an acoustic multiple reflection signal. Using this feature, we experimentally extracted TCF of two samples each with AlN and ZnO thin films in the range of 25 −120 °C. For AlN thin films, the extracted TCF values were -32 and -34 ppm/°C. ZnO thin films exhibited TCF values of -51 and -67 ppm/°C.

papers.title: Non-Contact Evaluation of Shear Wave Properties of Bulk Crystal Plate
papers.abstract: This study proposes a novel, non-destructive method for measuring in-plane shear wave velocity anisotropy in bulk single crystals. Conventionally, this required direct transducer bonding or complex LSAW analysis. Inspired by non-contact SAW measurement and lateral electric field excitation, the authors developed a configuration using two finger electrodes placed near a specimen coated with a c-axis oriented piezoelectric thin film. This setup excites shear waves via k15 coupling induced by a lateral electric field, enabling easy evaluation of velocity distributions without physical contact. To validate the method, a ZnO film was fabricated on an AT-cut quartz plate. The shear waves propagate through the substrate and reflect from the back surface. By performing a VNA-based S11 IFFT, the time-domain impulse response is obtained to estimate velocity. Results showed a thickness-shear resonance at 230 MHz and a distinct round-trip peak at ~300 ns. By rotating the substrate, the researchers characterized two shear wave types derived from the c44 and c66 constants. This technique provides an efficient tool for mapping the acoustic properties.

papers.title: Spectral-Element Accelerated Hierarchical Cascading Simulation of Surface Acoustic Wave Devices
papers.abstract: Numerical dispersion accumulated over multiple acoustic wavelengths limits accurate resonance and antiresonance prediction in high-frequency surface acoustic wave (SAW) simulation. This work presents a GLL spectral-element hierarchical cascade technique (GLL-SEM-HCT) to improve phase accuracy and efficiency. The coupled piezoelectric displacement–potential fields are expanded by high-order Lagrange polynomials on Gauss–Lobatto–Legendre nodes, yielding a diagonal mass matrix through quadrature collocation. The SEM period block is then reduced to port degrees of freedom through a Schur complement and incorporated into the HCT cascade. Dispersion analysis shows that SEM-N4/N6 reduces phase-velocity errors by several orders of magnitude compared with FEM-p2 at comparable DoFs, with SEM-N6 approaching machine precision. For a 2D TCSAW resonator over 401 frequency points, SEM-HCT reproduces the FEM-HCT admittance response. Compared with the 183 min FEM-HCT baseline, SEM-N6-HCT reduces runtime to 18 min, achieving a 9.9× speedup with 0.06% peak-frequency shift, while SEM-N4-HCT reaches 5 min, giving a 35.9× speedup with 0.11% deviation.
keywords: spectral element method， hierarchical cascade technique

sessions.title: NSP: Signal Processing

papers.title: A Spatially Weighted FISTA Approach for 3D Computational Ultrasound Imaging
papers.abstract: This study proposes a spatially weighted FISTA (wFISTA) algorithm for 3D computational ultrasound imaging using a single-element transducer and coded mask. The method aims to overcome the hardware complexity and computational burden of conventional array-based 3D ultrasound systems. k-Wave simulations were performed with a 2.25 MHz single-element transducer in water, and RF signals were acquired over multiple rotations. A spatial weighting matrix was generated from an initial back-projection estimate to emphasize strong-response regions during sparse recovery. Compared with conventional compressed sensing algorithms, wFISTA improved reconstruction fidelity, suppressed background noise, and reduced processing time. In 2D point-target simulations, it achieved an axial FWHM of approximately 85 ± 5 μm and required only 12.00 s for reconstruction. In 3D “IUS” phantom imaging, wFISTA preserved volumetric structures across depth planes while reducing reconstruction time by approximately 83%, demonstrating its potential for fast and high-fidelity coded-mask ultrasound imaging.

papers.title: Open-Source Multichannel Arbitrary Waveform Generator for Multiple-Input and Multiple-Output (MIMO) Ultrasound Research
papers.abstract: This work presents an open-source, scalable arbitrary waveform generation system for MIMO ultrasound research, implemented on a Xilinx ZCU216 RFSoC with 8 simultaneous DAC channels controllable via a Python interface. The system introduces no significant nonlinearities, supports signal durations of up to 10 ms, and enables reliable transmitter separation via matched filtering, all within a single-FPGA setup that substantially reduces integration complexity compared to existing platforms.

papers.title: Methodology for Self Compensation of Temperature Effects in Ultrasonic time-of-Flight Using the built-in Delay Line of a Commercial Transducer
papers.abstract: The present study proposes and evaluates the use of the time-of-flight (ToF) in a built-in delay line of a commercial transducer as a reference to self-compensate the effects of temperature fluctuations in the measured ToF in a liquid sample of interest. The work focuses on developing a post-processing methodology to enable relating both ToFs: a moving average is first performed and then a time-lag between the ToFs is identified and corrected. The autocorrelation function helps objectively and quantitatively define the window size for the averaging procedure. Results demonstrate that the Pearson correlation between the ToFs could be increased from 0.27 to 0.80 with the proposed post-processing, thus, a single A-scan can enable both property measurement and temperature compensation. The present abstract focused on showing that the ToFs could be related and no additional elements in the measuring apparatus are needed for the temperature compensation. In the full paper, the self-compensation procedure will be discussed in depth.

papers.title: Pulse Shaping to Mitigate Transducer Ringing
papers.abstract: Ringing of piezoelectric transducers complicates time domain ultrasound measurements by increasing pulse length, narrowing bandwidth, and producing a ‘dead zone’ in the pulse envelope that obscures near-field measurements. Typically, this is minimized using passive, heavily attenuating transducer backings. Our endeavor is to implement an active technique for mitigating ringing, that is adaptable and can be automated. We propose a pulse shaping technique that uses time delay filters from the control systems community, in conjunction with an in-situ system identification step, to cancel transducer vibrations with an engineered signal. We demonstrate several pulse shaping filters in controlled laboratory experiments, and their success points toward possible use in a variety of time-domain applications.

papers.title: Differential Spatial Ultrasound Sensing for Real-Time 3D Human Localization and Height Estimation in Bathrooms
papers.abstract: Bathroom accidents pose serious risks because delayed rescue can be fatal. Privacy concerns and steam preclude visual sensors, while ML-based ultrasound requires site-specific training data. Targeting a single bather, we developed a 3D localization and height estimation system using only physical signal processing. A ceiling-mounted sensor emits a 41.7-kHz DSSS signal, and a 16-channel microphone array captures reflections. Consecutive frames are differenced to remove static clutter; cross-correlation yields range, and delay-and-sum beamforming yields direction, producing 3D candidate points. Our spatiotemporal tracking framework then isolates the dominant dynamic scatterer from ghost reflections to robustly estimate height. In verification, fallen postures in the washing area were estimated at 26.9-42.4 cm, while sitting averaged 109.9 cm. This 70-cm gap provides a clear margin between emergency and normal states without needing environment-specific training. In the bathtub, the system tracked the water surface, yielding 53.7-67.8 cm. These results support environment-independent bathroom monitoring toward reliable accident detection.

sessions.title: NSP: Signal Processing and Industrial Transducers

papers.title: A Study on Fetal Sizing Using Divergent Wave Transmission and Reception via a Multistatic Transducer Array
papers.abstract: This study proposes a fetal body-sizing method using a multistatic transducer array placed across the pregnant abdomen. To overcome the limited field of view of conventional ultrasound probes, spherical divergent pulses are sequentially transmitted from each element, and echoes are received by all elements. Time-of-flight data corresponding to strong specular reflections from the fetal surface are extracted to estimate reflection points and reconstruct the surface geometry. The reconstruction is formulated as an optimization problem combining TOF fitting errors, a smooth surface constraint, and specular reflection constraints. Numerical evaluation is performed as a simplified curve-fitting problem, including analysis of weighting parameters and the effect of a pregnant-abdomen skin model. The results suggest that the proposed method is feasible for estimating fetal surface geometry.

papers.title: A Wearable Doppler Ultrasound Patch for Continuous Superficial Blood Flow Monitoring
papers.abstract: Continuous monitoring of superficial blood flow is important for cardiovascular assessment, vascular function evaluation, and hemodynamic management. Conventional Doppler ultrasound systems are usually bulky, hand-held, and highly dependent on operator skill, which limits their use for long-duration and real-time monitoring. This work presents a patch-based wearable Doppler ultrasound system for continuous superficial blood flow monitoring. The proposed patch integrates a conformal ultrasound transducer structure with Doppler signal acquisition and spectral analysis to improve skin coupling, wearing stability, and real-time flow assessment. Doppler signals from superficial vessels are processed to extract flow-related spectral features, including frequency shift, velocity waveform, and pulsatility information. Preliminary results indicate that the patch can capture blood-flow-related Doppler signals continuously and has the potential to support beat-to-beat hemodynamic monitoring in vascular and cardiovascular applications. This study demonstrates the feasibility of a wearable Doppler ultrasound patch for real-time, continuous, and operator-independent blood flow monitoring.

papers.title: U-Waveformer for Real-Time Ultrasonic RF Noise Cancellation in Needle Guidance
papers.abstract: Everyday settings can overwhelm individuals with sensory sensitivities, particularly those on the autism spectrum, with unpredictable, high-intensity noises that impair communication and cognitive function. To address this, we introduce a deep learning–based real-time audio noise attenuation framework that combines a de-noising auto-encoder with a U-Net–inspired encoder–decoder architecture. Our method using UrbanSound8K and Freesound datasets learns to suppress disruptive environmental sounds (e.g., vacuum cleaners, sirens, jackhammers) while preserving crucial speech and ambient cues via skip connections that maintain temporal and spectral detail. Evaluated across diverse noise conditions, the algorithm achieves low loss and high speech quality, demonstrating marked reductions in unwanted noises and significant gains in auditory clarity without introducing artifacts. These results validate the framework’s ability to balance noise suppression with signal fidelity, for real-time implementations that could enhance acoustic comfort in classrooms, workplaces, and public spaces.

papers.title: Flexible Magnetostrictive Guided Wave Transducer Based on Fe-Based Amorphous Ribbon and Electromagnetic Bias for Small-Diameter Tubing Monitoring
papers.abstract: Traditional MPTs are limited by the highrigidity of Fe-Co alloys and the bulkiness of permanent magnets. To address the challenges of monitoring small-diameter tubing in confined aerospace andprecision engineering environments, this study developed an integrated, highly flexiblemagnetostrictive patch transducer (MPT). This design utilizes a 20 um-thick 1K101 Fe-based amorphous ribbon (λs ≈ 27ppm) combined with dual-layer flexibleprinted circuits (FPC) to achieve a lightweight, conformal coupling with micro-curvaturesurfaces. The multi-physics electromagnetic–mechanical model results indicate that the DC bias coils generate a magnetic field with non-uniformity below 10% in the patch region, and demonstrate the successful excitation of the L(0, 1) mode in a 4 mm thin-walled tube, confirming its ability to identify reflections from a 20% wall-thickness circumferential notch.Experimentalvalidation using the RITEC RAM-5000 system further verified the feasibility of L(0,1) waveexcitation and reception. This research provides a highly adaptable and engineering-feasiblesolution for the structural health monitoring of complex, small-diameter tubing systems inrestricted spaces.

papers.title: Acoustic Signal from Photostriction in Ferroelectric AlScN Thin Films
papers.abstract: Our work demonstrates that photostriction in ferroelectric AlScN thin films can act as an optical-to-acoustic transduction mechanism with significantly improved strain rate. A modulated laser was used to generate photo-excited carriers, which create a photovoltaic field through BPVE in AlScN. This field couples with the converse piezoelectric effect, producing periodic strain at the modulation frequency. An AlScN photostrictive actuator with a cantilever structure was fabricated. Thermal effects were evaluated and found to be much smaller than the measured displacement magnitude. Our results confirm that the dominant actuation mechanism is non-thermal photostriction. The results suggest a pathway toward optically driven ultrasonic transducers, non-contact signal transmission, and optomechanical microsystems.

sessions.title: MBF: Technical Advances in 3D Doppler, Vector Flow Imaging, Flow Signal Processing

papers.title: 3D Ultrasound Flow Motion Estimation with Sparse Arrays
papers.abstract: Blood flow is a key biomarker for vascular diseases and requires full 3D characterization to capture complex hemodynamics. While matrix arrays enable 3D imaging, their high channel count limits practical use. Sparse arrays reduce hardware complexity while preserving steering and field of view. Although phase-based motion estimation with Transverse Oscillations (TOs) has shown promise for static motion, its application to flow remains largely unexplored. This work presents an experimental investigation of 3D flow estimation using sparse arrays with TOs. A phase-shift–based estimator with TO components introduced via spatial frequency filtering is used for multidirectional velocity estimation. Validation was performed on a 7-mm PVA vessel with steady flow (12 mm/s peak) using a 256-element, 5-MHz spiral sparse array in synthetic aperture mode. Beamforming and compounding yielded a 576 Hz frame rate. Results show accurate recovery of the expected parabolic profile. RMSE values were 17.2, 4.8, and 1.7 mm/s for vx, vy, and vz. These results demonstrate accurate volumetric flow estimation with reduced system complexity.

papers.title: A Novel Coherence Metric for High-Frequency Ultrasound Microflow Imaging with Improved Contrast and Speckle Preservation
papers.abstract: In ultrasound blood flow (BF) imaging, echoes from blood cells are extremely weak, resulting in a low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Consequently, the contrast of BF images is limited. The coherence factor (CF) has been widely used to suppress incoherent noise; however, it also suppresses partially coherent speckle echoes from blood cells, which are the signals of interest. In this study, a coherence metric based on SNR is proposed to enhance BF visualization while preserving speckle information. Unlike CF, whose dynamic range is bounded, the proposed approach allows increased separation between coherent and incoherent components. To avoid excessive suppression of speckle echoes, received signals are integrated across the receive aperture prior to SNR estimation. The method was validated using RF data acquired from a rabbit pup brain with a high-frequency ultrasound system. Compared with DAS and CF, the proposed method improved the structural definition of BF and enhanced visibility in deeper regions. These results demonstrate that the proposed approach provides a more suitable coherence metric for BF imaging, improving contrast while preserving speckle information.

papers.title: Contrast Agent-Free Ultrafast Vector Flow Imaging with Top-Orthogonal to Bottom-Electrode (TOBE) Arrays
papers.abstract: Bias-sensitive RCA-based TOBE arrays can create high-quality 2D images with global transmit-receive focusing using the Hadamard aperture-encoded Fast Orthogonal Row-Column Electronic Scanning (FORCES sequence. Recursive Aperture-Decoded Ultrasound Imaging (READI) is a partial Hadamard-decoding and beamforming method that creates sub-images of the FORCES sequence at much higher frame rates while still capturing the full high-resolution image. A custom-made carotid bifurcation phantom was imaged using a 128-transmit FORCES sequence. READI was applied to form sub-images from 4 transmits each, for an effective frame rate of 875 FPS. This enabled a speckle-tracking correlation-based block-matching algorithm to produce a 2D motion field with flow speeds up to 62 cm/s. Complex flow features such as vortices are detected.

papers.title: Deep Unfolded Recurrent Network for Online Clutter Filtering in Ultrasound Microvascular Imaging
papers.abstract: Ultrasound microvascular imaging allows microvasculature visualization and hemodynamic analysis. Spatiotemporal clutter filtering is the fundamental step for the separation of tissue and blood flow signals. Although online robust principal component analysis (rPCA)-based filtering achieves high-quality separation, its dependence on frame-wise iterative calculations and fine-tuned hyperparameters limits efficiency and clinical practicality. This work proposes a deep unfolded recurrent network to address these challenges.The proposed method encapsulates layer-wise deep unfolded recurrent neural network (RNN) cores to perform framewise online filtering, with the hyperparameters transferred into learnable coefficients. The experimental validations demonstrate that our method significantly improves the computational efficiency by factors of 2.4 over the baseline on the in-vivo datasets, achieving framerates of 189.39 fps. Furthermore, our method also effectively mitigates the sensitivity to the hyperparameters compared to the baseline.

papers.title: 3D Doppler Angle Estimation Using Spectral Symmetry and Matrix Arrays
papers.abstract: Doppler-based velocity estimation requires accurate knowledge of the beam-to-flow angle. Current approaches often rely on algorithms that, especially in 3D, are computationally demanding and hardly feasible in real-time. This work presents a fast and robust procedure for 3D Doppler angle estimation, based on a method, so far limited to 2D, which exploits the symmetry properties of Doppler spectra acquired with a matrix array probe.

papers.title: Phase Linearity-Regularized Robust PCA (PL-rPCA) for Clutter Filtering and Grating-Lobe Suppression in Ultrasound Microvascular Imaging
papers.abstract: Robust PCA (rPCA) has shown its high sensitivity in ultrasound microvascular clutter filtering. However, conventional rPCA filtering typically applies spatial sparsity constraint to blood flow signals without fully exploiting their distinct characteristics in signal magnitude and phase. Under the assumption that the phases of microvascular flows tend to evolve linearly in the slow-time dimension, whereas noise, including grating-lobes exhibits random or discontinuous phases, we propose a Phase Linearity-regularized rPCA (PL-rPCA) method to simultaneously suppressing tissue signals, grating lobes, and background noise.

papers.title: Real-Time 3D Power Doppler with Fast-Orthogonal Row-Column Electronic Scanning (FORCES) Using Top Orthogonal to Bottom Electrode (TOBE) Arrays
papers.abstract: Row-Column Arrays (RCAs) have previously been used for 3D blood flow imaging. However, RCAs lack two-way focusing and demonstrate limited penetration depths and volumetric coverage, often spanning to only a few cubic centimeters. Bias-switchable TOBE arrays with FORCES imaging schemes, however, enable full synthetic two-way focusing via Hadamard-encoded schemes, and extend volumetric coverage beyond the shadow of the aperture, while improving SNR and penetration depth. We propose a real-time 3D PD acquisition and clutter suppression pipeline utilizing FORCES acquisition with TOBE wide-aperture arrays. Our proposed method leverages high-speed FORCES acquisition enabled by TOBE arrays to achieve real-time, wide-aperture 3D PD.

papers.title: Noninvasive Estimation of Intravascular Pressure Difference Using 3D Ultrasound Particle Image Velocimetry
papers.abstract: Arterial stenosis alters local hemodynamics, and the pressure difference across the stenosis is a key indicator of vascular disease severity. Current clinical methods rely on catheter-based measurements, which are invasive, require ionizing, and are unsuitable for routine monitoring. This work proposes a fully noninvasive framework combining 3D ultrasound imaging, 3D particle image velocimetry (PIV), and the unsteady Bernoulli equation to estimate intravascular pressure differences across a stenosed vessel, validated against a CFD reference. A 3D simulation pipeline modeled blood flow in a 60% stenosed cylindrical vessel embedded in a tissue-mimicking volume seeded with scatterers. Scatterer motion was updated by a CFD pulsatile flow dataset providing ground-truth velocity and pressure fields. RF data were demodulated and delay-and-sum beamformed into 3D B-mode volumes. Displacements were estimated via 3D PIV, and the proximal-to-distal pressure difference was reconstructed by integrating convective and unsteady terms of the Bernoulli equation. Results demonstrate the feasibility of noninvasive pressure estimation using 3D ultrasound PIV.

papers.title: Reynolds Number Based Vessel Simulator (RUBUS): a Vessel Simulation Tool for Performance Benchmarking in Ultrahigh Resolution Ultrafast Doppler and Ultrasound Localization Microscopy
papers.abstract: Ultrasound-based blood flow imaging is limited by hard-to-control experimental factors, complex vascular geometries, and the lack of ground truth, making it difficult to develop and evaluate emerging methods. This challenge is further increased by the need for large-scale datasets that are difficult to acquire in vivo. To address this, we propose Reynolds number based vessel simulator (RUBS), a novel simulator that models complex vascular architectures and turbulent flow, providing a flexible and realistic platform for blood-flow simulation and method development.

papers.title: Transcranial Functional Ultrasound Imaging Detects Neurovascular Networks Engaged by Median Nerve and Focused Ultrasound Stimulation in non-Human Primates
papers.abstract: Noninvasive mapping of brain networks is essential for understanding responses to sensory input and targeted stimulation. Focused ultrasound stimulation (FUS) can access localized and deep targets, but interpreting its effects requires visualization of engaged neurovascular networks. Here, we evaluated transcranial functional ultrasound imaging (fUS) for detecting stimulus-evoked neurovascular activity in anesthetized macaques. Median nerve stimulation, confirmed by thumb twitch, validated somatosensory network detection and evoked robust %ΔCBV responses in areas 3a/3b and S1, with activity also in M1, PMd, and deeper sensorimotor regions. Separately, transcranial FUS was delivered with a coaxially aligned 0.5-MHz transducer while parameters were varied. FUS evoked CBV responses beyond the focus, engaging a medial thalamic-hypothalamic-limbic network including cingulate and posterior medial/PCC regions. Duty cycle changes modulated network components, indicating parameter-dependent responses. Together, these findings show that transcranial fUS can map sensorimotor and FUS-evoked neurovascular networks in non-human primates, a critical translational step toward human applications.
